intro.heading: Is there anybody near here who has actually taught this course?
paragraphs: That is the real question, and the honest answer in Al Rashidiya is: probably not, and it does not matter as much as you think. The district sits between Dubai International Airport, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Hamar, and it has no secondary school of its own. Its Diploma students travel north to the Garhoud cluster or east towards Mirdif, and the nearest IB continuum option is Uptown International School. That is the whole local pool before you start narrowing by subject.

Then narrow it. The IB accounts for around seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on a UK curriculum, so Diploma cohorts here are smaller than British-curriculum ones to begin with. Of a Diploma cohort, a minority take physics. Of those, a minority take it at Higher Level. The population of adults who have taught Higher Level physics through to a final examination and who also happen to live fifteen minutes from the airport tunnel is a number you could probably count on one hand, and the chances that one of them is free at 5.30pm on a Tuesday are poor.

This is the part most tutoring pages avoid saying. Instead of pretending the local pool is deep, we match on the course. Lessons for Al Rashidiya families are delivered one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen because they have taught the current Physics guide rather than because they live nearby. Home visits are a service offered only in India; nobody is driving to an address in the UAE for a physics lesson, and on a subject this narrow that constraint buys you more than it costs you.

There is a second scarcity problem worth naming, which is that physics tutoring is frequently sold by people who last taught an older syllabus. The current course is organised into five themes, A to E, with Higher Level extensions running through each, and the assessment has changed shape from what a tutor trained a decade ago will remember. A tutor working from the previous structure will teach content that is still physics and still waste a student's revision time, and the student will not know it is happening.

None of this means a local tutor is a bad person or a bad teacher. It means the subject is narrow and the district is small, and those two facts together make distance the wrong filter to apply first.

So this page is built as a test you can run. What is actually in the course now. What the components are and where marks leave. What the scientific investigation asks for and when it has to start. Six questions that separate someone who has taught this from someone who has read about it. And the market rates in dirhams, each attributed, so you can tell whether the quote in front of you is reasonable.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.programmesIntro: Physics problems rarely begin in the Diploma. They begin where the mathematics was left incomplete. These are the stages we cover either side of DP physics for students in this part of Dubai.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Available at Standard and Higher Level. The current course is built around five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level extensions inside each. Assessment is written papers plus the scientific investigation, which carries twenty per cent. Confirm the current structure and weightings with your school's IB coordinator before planning around them.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Rashidiya student sitting DP physics is most likely enrolled in the Garhoud or Mirdif clusters, where Diploma cohorts are small by Dubai standards. Small cohorts mean a single physics teacher often carries both levels, which is excellent for continuity and leaves very little slack if a student falls behind in Theme D. That is the specific gap one-to-one support fills here.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D, with physics taught inside an integrated sciences course in most schools rather than as a separate subject. MYP builds investigation design and evaluation skills that transfer well to the Diploma investigation, and builds considerably less of the algebraic fluency that Diploma physics assumes from the first week of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP physics step is the commonest reason a strong middle-school scientist struggles in DP1 locally. The content is manageable; the algebra is not, because rearranging a formula with three variables under time pressure was never drilled. A short bridging block in the summer before DP1 fixes more of this than a term of content teaching afterwards.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into Diploma Physics
programmes.description: The crossing most Dubai students make, because UK-curriculum schools dominate enrolment. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 leave a student well drilled in recall and standard calculations, and short on the Diploma's demand for derivation, for reasoning from a model, and for handling uncertainty in data properly rather than quoting a value.
programmes.countryNote: A student moving from a British-curriculum school in Mirdif or Al Qusais into a Diploma Programme in Al Garhoud is a routine local case. The three things that reliably need building in that first term are uncertainty and error analysis, graph linearisation, and the confidence to manipulate an equation symbolically instead of substituting numbers immediately.

programmes.name: Engineering and physical science routes
programmes.description: What Higher Level physics is usually for. Engineering, physics and several medicine-adjacent routes commonly expect it, typically alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches rather than Applications and Interpretation. Requirements vary by university and change between admission cycles, so the only reliable method is reading the specific course page for the specific institution.
programmes.countryNote: Check requirements directly with each university your child is considering, including UAE institutions, rather than relying on a summary. IB Gram does not perform or accelerate Ministry of Education equivalency, and no verified IB points threshold for equivalency is published on ministry sources, so ask moe.gov.ae or your school registrar for that rather than any tutoring page.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.subjectsIntro: Physics marks leave from a small number of identifiable places. These are the areas Al Rashidiya families ask about, written so you can match a tutor's claim against the course your child is actually sitting.

subjects.name: Theme A: space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, circular motion and, at Higher Level, rotational dynamics and relativity. Students lose marks by treating problems as formula lookups rather than as free-body diagrams, and the fix is a drawing habit enforced weekly rather than a new explanation.

subjects.name: Theme B: the particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, the kinetic model and thermodynamics with the Higher Level extensions. The recurring loss is confusing heat and temperature in extended-response answers, and failing to state the assumptions a model rests on when the question asks for them.

subjects.name: Theme C: wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, travelling waves, standing waves, resonance, superposition and diffraction, with simple harmonic motion treated far more formally at Higher Level. Phase relationships are where students who can do the algebra still lose marks, because the physical picture never formed.

subjects.name: Theme D: fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, induction and circuits. This is the theme that most often breaks a Higher Level student, because it demands holding three analogous field models in mind at once and not mixing their equations under pressure.

subjects.name: Theme E: nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear binding, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and, at Higher Level, deeper quantum and particle content. Marks here are often the cheapest on the paper, because the questions are structured and the content is finite, yet it is the theme students revise last.

subjects.name: Higher Level extensions
subjects.description: The additional depth running through every theme rather than sitting in a separate block. A tutor who teaches Standard Level content and adds a few harder questions is not teaching Higher Level, and the difference shows up in extended-response marks rather than in recall.

subjects.name: Uncertainty, error and data analysis
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, significant figures, and the graph work that turns a relationship into a straight line. Examined inside the papers and central to the investigation, and almost never taught properly at IGCSE, which is why it dominates early DP1 tutoring.

subjects.name: Graph linearisation and gradient interpretation
subjects.description: Rearranging a relationship so a plot is linear, then reading physics out of a gradient and an intercept. It is a mechanical skill with a high mark yield across both papers and the investigation, and it responds to six worked examples rather than to a lecture.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An independent piece of experimental or data-based physics carrying twenty per cent of the final grade, assessed against published criteria. A tutor may teach the criteria, question a draft and point out an unsupported claim. A tutor may not write, draft or complete any part of it.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: Writing to the command term, stating assumptions, referring to a named law rather than describing it vaguely, and answering the question that was set. A term of weekly correction on this moves marks without covering a single new piece of content.

subjects.name: Mathematics support for physics
subjects.description: Logarithms, trigonometry, small-angle approximations, vectors and rearrangement. Students on Applications and Interpretation frequently need this more than they need physics teaching, and separating the two diagnoses the real problem rather than treating the symptom.

subjects.name: IGCSE physics foundations
subjects.description: Where a DP1 problem usually started. Circuits, moments, and the habit of substituting numbers before rearranging are the three things most often carried forward from 0625 or 4PH1 and most often worth three sessions of unpicking.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of finding a Higher Level physics specialist near here
paragraphs: Work it through rather than taking it on trust. Dubai has 227 private schools as of 2024-25, of which the International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly seven per cent of student enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on a UK curriculum. Al Rashidiya contains none of them; its Diploma students travel to the Garhoud or Mirdif clusters. Within a Diploma cohort, physics is a minority choice, and within physics, Higher Level is a minority again.

Now add the constraint that actually bites. You need not merely a physics graduate but somebody who has taught the current guide, with its five themes and its Higher Level extensions, through to a final examination, and who is free at the hour your child is home from a Mirdif bus route. Each condition cuts the pool by a large factor, and the conditions multiply rather than add.

The usual commercial response is to blur the distinction and send whoever is available. A physics graduate is not a physics teacher; a physics teacher who last taught the previous syllabus is teaching a course your child is not sitting; and a general science tutor is not a Higher Level physicist. All three will fill the hour, and the student will not be able to tell you which one they had.

Our response is to widen the pool rather than lower the bar. Matching on the course and teaching one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time means the question becomes who has taught this guide, not who lives within twenty minutes of the airport tunnel. For a subject this narrow, that is not a compromise. It is the only way a family in this district gets a genuine specialist at all.

sections.heading: What is actually in the course your child is sitting
paragraphs: The current IB Physics course is organised into five themes rather than the topic-and-option structure some tutors will remember, and the Higher Level material runs through the themes rather than sitting in a separate block at the end. That structural point matters when you are judging a tutor, because it is the first thing somebody working from an older syllabus gets wrong.

The table sets the themes out with what each one demands and where students typically lose marks. Read it with your child's current grade in mind. A student scoring well on Themes A and B and poorly on D is not a weak physicist; they have hit the theme that requires holding gravitational, electric and magnetic field models apart without merging their equations, and that is a specific, teachable problem rather than a general one.

Across all five themes the same two skills decide the extended-response marks: stating the assumptions a model rests on, and answering the command term that was actually used. A student who writes everything they know about fields in response to a question asking them to explain one thing is losing marks they already earned by learning the content.

Confirm the current structure and theme content with your school's IB coordinator before planning around it. Subject guides are revised, and a tutoring page is not a syllabus. We also do not reproduce or supply IB subject guides; those belong to the IB and reach you properly through the school.

sections.heading: The components, and where a physics grade is actually decided
paragraphs: Physics is assessed through written papers plus the scientific investigation, which carries twenty per cent of the final grade. Paper 1 is split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and that second section is the one families overlook most consistently, because it rewards a skill rather than knowledge.

The distribution of tutoring effort that works is counter-intuitive. Families ask for more content because the content feels like the problem. The marks, though, cluster around technique: reading uncertainty properly, linearising a relationship so a gradient means something, stating the assumption behind a model, and writing to the command term. All four are mechanical, all four respond to weekly correction, and none of them requires covering new physics.

Data analysis deserves singling out. A student who can propagate percentage uncertainty through a calculation and justify the number of significant figures in an answer is collecting marks across every paper and setting themselves up for the investigation at the same time. A student who quotes an uncertainty because the textbook did is losing the same marks repeatedly without ever being told why.

Confirm weightings, durations and the current component structure with your school's IB coordinator rather than from any third-party page, this one included. The pattern in the table is reliable; the precise percentages are the school's to give you.

One further habit decides more marks than any single topic, and it is almost free to build. Physics examiners award credit for a stated assumption, a named law and a visible step, so a student who writes "assuming air resistance is negligible" or "by conservation of momentum" before the arithmetic keeps marks that a student working silently loses the moment a number goes astray. That is behaviour rather than knowledge. It is corrected weekly for a term and then it is permanent, which makes it the single best use of a recurring slot early in DP1.

sections.heading: Six questions that prove a tutor has taught this course
paragraphs: A parent with no physics can still test a physics tutor, because the answers to these questions are either specific or evasive and the difference is audible. Run them on the trial lesson rather than beforehand, with your child in the room and a past question open.

The first three are about the course. Which themes does the current guide run, and what sits in Theme D? What does the Higher Level extension add inside a theme rather than at the end? What does the data-analysis section of Paper 1 actually ask a student to do? Somebody who has taught this answers each in a sentence. Somebody working from an older syllabus hesitates, or describes options and a Paper 3 that the current structure does not have.

The second three are about teaching. Where do your students lose marks in Theme C, and what do you do about it? What will you refuse to do with my child's investigation? What will you send me after each lesson? The third of these is the most revealing, because a tutor who writes a specific note every week has to actually know what happened in the lesson.

Ignore examiner claims unless they can be evidenced. Examiner status is asserted loosely in this market and is often used to imply access to marking standards or boundaries that nobody has. What you can verify is the teaching, in forty minutes, with a past question in front of your child.

sections.heading: The maths problem hiding inside a physics problem
paragraphs: A large share of Diploma physics difficulty is not physics. It is algebra that was never made automatic, trigonometry held loosely, logarithms half remembered, and the habit of substituting numbers immediately instead of rearranging symbolically. A tutor who treats every wrong answer as a physics gap will teach content for a term and move nothing.

The mathematics course a student is taking makes this predictable. Analysis and Approaches builds the symbolic fluency physics assumes; Applications and Interpretation is a serious course but routes that fluency differently, and a physics student on AI frequently needs explicit algebra support that nobody has flagged. Neither course is wrong, and the two produce different physics students.

The diagnosis is quick. Give the student a standard physics problem and watch what they do in the first ten seconds. If they rearrange the equation before substituting, the physics is the issue. If they put numbers in straight away and get stuck when a quantity is unknown, the algebra is the issue, and three sessions on rearrangement will do more than ten on fields.

Say the maths course when you contact us. It changes the shortlist, because a tutor comfortable teaching the algebra alongside the physics is a different person from one who assumes it is already there.

There is one mathematical skill neither course supplies, and it is worth knowing about before you hear a tutor claim otherwise. Uncertainty propagation, significant-figure justification and the reasoning behind quoting a result to a particular precision are not taught in Analysis and Approaches or in Applications and Interpretation. They belong to physics, they appear in the papers and in the investigation, and every DP1 student arrives without them. A tutor who assumes that ground is covered has mistaken what a mathematics course does, and your child will lose the same marks every week until somebody notices.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the twenty per cent nobody plans for
paragraphs: The investigation carries twenty per cent of the physics grade and is assessed against published criteria. Almost everything that determines the mark is decided before any writing happens, in the choice of research question. A question with too little physics in it has no route to the higher bands no matter how carefully the report is written, and no tutor can retrofit depth into a thin question in the final fortnight.

Cheap to protect, expensive to rescue. Four sessions early in DP1 cover what the criteria reward, how to choose a question with real physics and measurable variables, how to handle uncertainty honestly rather than decoratively, and how to reflect on a method's limitations in a way the criteria recognise. Buying help in the last three weeks costs more, arrives at exam-year rates, and cannot change the question.

The boundary is absolute and this is the place in physics tutoring where the market behaves worst. A tutor may explain the criteria, model method on a different investigation, ask questions about the student's own draft and point out where a conclusion is not supported by the data. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of the submission. One page in the researched competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is a malpractice route and the student carries the finding.

A parent can police this without reading the physics. Ask to see the feedback. If it reads as sentences your child could paste into the report, the line has been crossed. If it reads as questions they have to go and answer, it has not.
bullets: The research question decides the mark ceiling more than the writing does

sections.heading: What the market charges for Higher Level science, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: This section exists because the physics quote a family receives is usually at the top of the Dubai range and nobody explains why. The reason is scarcity rather than effort: there are fewer people who can teach Higher Level physics than who can teach Standard Level maths, and the market prices that.

Look at the travel premium first, because it is the clearest thing on the table. In-home one to one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. The gap is a car journey. In this corridor it is a car journey through Algeria Street or the Garhoud interchange between 3pm and 6pm, and it is worth asking what else the same money buys. Spent on scarcity instead of on travel, it buys a genuine Higher Level specialist rather than whichever physics teacher lives nearest.

The rest of the bands, each read on the provider's own public page: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour for budget online tutoring, Tutopiya's published panel starts lower, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai table runs AED 200 to 450 and above for specialists, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages seen locally sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours.

None of those is an IB Gram rate and we publish no rate card on these pages. What the table is for is calibration: if you are quoted below the qualified-tutor band for Higher Level physics, ask what you are actually getting, and if you are quoted above the premium band, ask what justifies it.

sections.heading: Practical work, and why a tutor in the room is not the answer
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how a physics student is supported online when physics involves apparatus. The answer is that the apparatus is the school's job and always was. Your child's laboratory work, equipment, safety supervision and recorded data come from the school, and no tutor in a Dubai villa is bringing an oscilloscope.

What a tutor adds sits either side of the bench. Before: designing a sensible method, identifying which variables need controlling and why, deciding what range of readings will produce a usable graph. After: handling the uncertainty, linearising the relationship, interpreting the gradient, and writing an evaluation that identifies real limitations rather than ritual ones. Both halves are screen work, and a shared screen with the student's own data open is in several respects better than sitting side by side.

The data-analysis section of Paper 1 makes this concrete. It asks students to work with experimental data they did not collect, which is exactly the skill a well-run online session practises. A student who has spent a term interpreting somebody else's results on a shared screen walks into that section with the right habit already formed.

Where physical presence genuinely matters is a student with a diagnosed need requiring hands-on support. In that case we will say so rather than take the booking, and recommend a local provider with a verifiable MoHRE private tuition permit. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes under any circumstances.

The practical setup is worth five minutes of planning. A physics lesson needs a desk, paper, a calculator, the student's own lab notebook and a laptop on a stable surface rather than a phone held in one hand. Graph work and free-body diagrams happen on paper and get held up to the camera, which works perfectly well and works better if the camera is not moving. Households in this corridor are busy in the early evening, so a door that closes is worth more to the hour than anything else a family can provide.

sections.heading: Starting, and the availability we will be honest about
paragraphs: Send four things: the level, Standard or Higher; which themes the school has covered so far; the mathematics course your child is taking; and a photograph of a marked paper or test. Those four turn matching from guesswork into a short list. The mathematics course is the one families leave out and the one that most often explains the problem.

The trial lesson is free, runs about forty minutes on a past question, and is a lesson rather than a sales call. Afterwards you receive a written read on whether the difficulty is physics, mathematics or technique, with the number of weeks each implies. Nothing is owed if you stop there and no card details are taken.

Higher Level physics is the subject where we most often have to tell a family that nobody suitable is free at the hour they want. Late-evening Gulf Standard Time slots fill first, and a Theme D specialist requested a fortnight before final papers may simply not be available. We will give a realistic match time rather than filling the slot with a general science tutor, because the wrong tutor in the right hour costs a family the fee and the weeks.

What we ask for is limited to what matching needs: level, themes covered, maths course, school if you want its sequence followed, and a contact for scheduling. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs the data we hold and the privacy link on this page sets out what is kept and how to have it removed.

process.title: Say Standard or Higher, and which themes are done
process.description: The level and the school's progress through Themes A to E together tell a specialist where your child is in the course. A student struggling in Theme D needs a different conversation from one struggling in Theme A, and the difference is visible from this answer alone.

process.title: Send a marked paper
process.description: A photograph of a marked test or mock shows a physics specialist the pattern in two minutes: free-body diagrams missing, uncertainty quoted rather than propagated, command terms unanswered, or genuine content gaps in one theme.

process.title: Set the slot from the arrival home
process.description: Garhoud-direction families can usually hold 4.30pm; Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa bus routes need 5.30pm or later. Physics is a poor subject to attempt with a tired student, so build in recovery time rather than optimism.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: Forty minutes on a past question, with your child working and the tutor teaching. Ask the tutor to name what sits in Theme D and what they will refuse to do with the investigation. Then read the written note that follows.

process.title: Review at six lessons against marks
process.description: Against marks on the question types that were going wrong, not against how the lessons felt. If the pattern has not shifted we change the tutor or the approach rather than asking for more time and more money.

faqs.question: Realistically, can I find an IB physics tutor living near Al Rashidiya?
faqs.answer: Probably not one who has taught the current course at Higher Level. Al Rashidiya has no secondary school; Diploma provision sits in the Garhoud and Mirdif clusters, and the IB accounts for roughly seven per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on a UK curriculum. Physics is a minority Diploma choice and Higher Level a minority within that, so the local pool is genuinely tiny before you check who is free at 5.30pm. Matching by course over live video is what makes a real specialist reachable here.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a physics tutor knows the current syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the themes and say what sits inside Theme D. The current guide runs five themes, A to E, with Higher Level extensions inside each rather than in a separate block at the end. Somebody who has taught it answers in a sentence. Somebody working from an older structure describes options and a third paper, which the current arrangement does not have. Then ask what the data-analysis section of Paper 1 demands; the answer separates a teacher of this course from a physics graduate.

faqs.question: Which theme causes the most trouble for Higher Level students?
faqs.answer: Theme D, fields, more often than any other. It asks a student to hold gravitational, electric and magnetic field models in mind simultaneously, keep their equations apart, and reason about potential as well as field strength. Under time pressure the three merge, and an answer that is individually correct for the wrong field earns nothing. It is a specific and teachable problem rather than a sign of general weakness, and a six-to-ten session block on that theme alone is a defensible purchase.

faqs.question: My child understands the physics but keeps getting the numbers wrong. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Usually the algebra, not the physics. Watch what they do in the first ten seconds of a problem: a student who rearranges the equation before substituting has a physics question to answer, while one who puts numbers in immediately and stalls when a quantity is unknown has an algebra problem wearing a physics costume. That pattern is commoner in students taking Applications and Interpretation, which routes mathematical fluency differently from Analysis and Approaches. Three sessions on symbolic rearrangement usually does more than ten on content.

faqs.question: How can physics be tutored online when it involves laboratory work?
faqs.answer: Because the apparatus was always the school's job. Your child's practical work, equipment, safety supervision and recorded data come from the school; no tutor in a Dubai villa is bringing laboratory kit. A tutor's value sits either side of the bench: designing a sensible method and choosing what to control beforehand, then handling uncertainty, linearising the relationship, reading the gradient and writing a real evaluation afterwards. Both halves are screen work, and the data-analysis section of Paper 1 asks for exactly that skill on data a student did not collect.

faqs.question: What does the scientific investigation actually require?
faqs.answer: An independent piece of experimental or data-based physics, assessed against published criteria and carrying twenty per cent of the final grade. The decisive step is the research question: one with too little physics in it has no route to the higher bands however well the report is written. Four sessions early in DP1 on criteria, question choice, honest uncertainty treatment and reflecting on method limits protects that twenty per cent cheaply. Confirm the current criteria and deadlines with your school's IB coordinator, since the school sets the internal timeline.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's physics investigation write-up?
faqs.answer: Only within a firm boundary. A tutor may explain the criteria, model method on a different investigation, ask questions about your child's draft and point out where a conclusion is not supported by the data. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit to completion any part of it. The test a parent can apply without reading the physics is the feedback itself: sentences your child could paste in mean the line has been crossed, questions they must go and answer mean it has not. Decline any offer to produce the work.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level physics a safer choice than Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Safer in workload, and potentially costly in options. Engineering, physics and some medicine-adjacent degrees commonly expect Higher Level physics, often alongside Analysis and Approaches, so dropping to Standard Level in DP1 for comfort can close a route the student later wants. Requirements vary by university and change between admission cycles, so read the specific course page at each institution your child is considering rather than relying on any summary. Make the decision on destination and evidence from marked papers, not on how DP1 feels in November.

faqs.question: Why is an IB physics quote higher than a maths quote in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Scarcity rather than effort. Fewer people can teach Higher Level physics on the current guide than can teach Standard Level mathematics, and the market prices that difference. Published Dubai rates put named IB and IGCSE specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. None of those is an IB Gram price; each was read on the provider's own public page and can be checked there.

faqs.question: Would I be better off paying for an in-home physics tutor instead?
faqs.answer: You would be paying AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor working online, and the difference is a car journey through Algeria Street or the Garhoud interchange between 3pm and 6pm. On a subject as narrow as Higher Level physics, that same premium spent on scarcity rather than travel buys a genuine specialist instead of the nearest available physics teacher. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; those are an India-only service, so the comparison here is between market options rather than between ours.

faqs.question: Which part of the physics course gives the quickest mark improvement?
faqs.answer: Data analysis and uncertainty, by a clear margin. Propagating percentage uncertainty through a calculation, justifying significant figures, and rearranging a relationship so a plot is linear are mechanical skills with a high mark yield across the papers and the investigation at once. Neither IGCSE nor either mathematics course teaches them properly, so almost every DP1 student arrives without them. Six worked examples move more marks than six hours of content teaching, which is why we test for this before anything else.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE Physics 0625 into the Diploma. What needs building first?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order: uncertainty and error analysis, graph linearisation, and the habit of manipulating an equation symbolically before substituting numbers. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 both leave students well drilled in recall and standard calculations and short on all three. A focused block of six to ten sessions in the summer before DP1 removes most of the first-term shock, and it costs considerably less than the remediation block families otherwise buy in November of DP1.

faqs.question: Should we book physics and maths with the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Higher Level physics and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches are both specialisms, and a tutor strong in one is frequently average in the other. The combination is a scheduling convenience rather than a teaching advantage. Where the algebra is genuinely the physics problem, the right answer is a physics tutor who will drill rearrangement for three sessions before resuming content, not a second subject on the invoice. If both subjects truly need help, fix the one blocking a university route first.

faqs.question: You have no Theme D tutor open at our hour. Then what?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a realistic match time rather than putting a general science tutor in a specialist slot. This is the subject where it happens most often: late-evening Gulf Standard Time slots fill first, and a Theme D specialist requested a fortnight before final papers may genuinely not be available. If the wait does not fit your timeline we will tell you that too. A tutor who has not taught this guide will cost the fee and the weeks, and in DP2 the weeks cannot be bought back.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first physics lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of which takes long. The level, Standard or Higher. Which themes the school has covered so far. The mathematics course your child is taking, with its level. And a photograph of a marked test or mock. Those four produce a short list rather than a guess, and the maths course is the item most families omit and the one that most often explains the difficulty. We do not need a photograph of your child or a full grade history; the privacy link explains what is held under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-rashidiya.closingBody: Higher Level physics is narrow enough that the local pool near Al Rashidiya is not a real pool, and no amount of searching by distance changes that. intro.heading: Physics is not a harder version of the other sciences
paragraphs: Parents in Al Safa frequently arrive with a reasonable but misleading model: that chemistry, biology and physics are three versions of the same task at different difficulty levels, and that a student struggling in physics is struggling with science. The three subjects actually fail differently, and physics fails in a way that is specific enough to be worth describing, because the remedy is different from what the model would suggest.

Biology punishes imprecision in language and rewards volume of accurate recall. Chemistry punishes unstated assumptions and dropped signs, and rewards disciplined calculation. Physics does something else: it punishes students who describe what happens when the question asked why, and it makes a student's mathematics visible in a way no other science does. A physics question about a circuit is frequently an algebra question wearing a circuit diagram, and a student whose rearranging is slow will fail it while understanding the physics perfectly.

That has an immediate consequence for how a physics tutor should start. Before any content is taught, the question is what the student's maths course and level are, and how comfortable they are with rearranging, with proportional reasoning and with handling powers of ten. A Higher Level Physics student taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is carrying a structural mismatch that will appear in every paper, and knowing that in Diploma 1 rather than in Diploma 2 changes what can be done about it.

This page therefore compares the things that matter. Physics against chemistry and biology on what each one examines and where each loses marks. Higher Level against Standard Level, including where the extension lands. The two maths courses against the physics content that depends on them. The three ways a family can buy help, with the published rates. And the IGCSE practical a student has just left against the Diploma investigation they are about to meet, because the habits do not transfer.

Al Safa itself is relevant for one reason worth naming. It holds an unusual concentration of secondary provision, with Jumeirah College, Horizon English School, Safa British School and Latifa School for Girls in or beside it and Jumeirah Baccalaureate School alongside. That proximity makes a general tutor easy to find locally and a Higher Level Physics specialist hard, because Higher Level Physics cohorts are spread thin across several schools rather than pooled in one. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses in any case; home visits are a service we provide in India only, and physics here is taught one-to-one over live video in a shared workspace where both people can draw. For a subject built on circuit diagrams, free-body diagrams and graphs, that shared drawing space is the part of the format that matters most.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-safa.subjectsIntro: The physics topics that produce the most work in this cluster, with the specific error in each. Note how many of the errors are mathematical rather than physical.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: Resolving forces and sign conventions on vector quantities. Most lost marks are a sign chosen inconsistently between two lines of working rather than a misunderstanding of the physics involved.

subjects.name: Work, energy and power
subjects.description: Energy accounting questions where one transfer is omitted. Students conserve energy correctly and forget the term that was dissipated, which the mark scheme treats as an incomplete answer.

subjects.name: Momentum and impulse
subjects.description: Collisions in two dimensions, where the momentum components must be handled separately. The physics is usually understood and the component algebra collapses halfway through.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity and latent heat problems with multiple stages. Marks go on students combining stages into one calculation rather than treating them separately, and on temperature units.

subjects.name: Waves and superposition
subjects.description: Path difference and phase relationships. Diagrams are the actual task in many of these questions, and students who answer without drawing lose marks that drawing would have secured.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The single largest source of lost marks across both levels. Potential dividers and internal resistance questions are algebra problems in a circuit diagram, and slow rearranging is fatal under time pressure.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational, electric and magnetic
subjects.description: Proportional reasoning: what happens to a field quantity when a distance doubles. Students who can quote the inverse-square law still answer these wrongly because they compute rather than reason proportionally.

subjects.name: Electromagnetic induction
subjects.description: A Higher Level favourite and a reliable source of explanation-question losses. Answers describe the flux changing rather than explaining why an electromotive force results, which is the mark.

subjects.name: Circular motion and oscillations
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion at Higher Level, with phase, energy and the defining relationship. Losses come from treating it as a formula set rather than as a condition that either holds or does not.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and particle physics
subjects.description: Mass defect and binding energy, where unit conversion between electronvolts and joules costs more marks than the physics. Decay equations lose marks for unbalanced nucleon or charge numbers.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and data analysis
subjects.description: Propagating uncertainty, significant figures and gradient-based analysis. These marks appear in both papers and in the investigation, and they are among the most recoverable in the subject.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: A student-designed investigation marked against criteria. In physics the commonest failures are a research question with no measurable relationship in it and an evaluation that lists equipment limitations without connecting them to the conclusion.

sections.heading: Physics against chemistry and biology
paragraphs: The three Diploma sciences are often chosen on reputation and dropped on experience, which is an expensive way to find out how they differ. They examine different things and they fail in different ways, and a student who is strong in one is not automatically suited to another. For a family in Al Safa still deciding, or reviewing a choice early in Diploma 1, the comparison is worth having properly.

Biology is content-dense and language-precise. The volume of material is the main difficulty and the marks go to named structures, named processes and definitions reproduced accurately. Near-synonyms score nothing. Chemistry is calculation-disciplined: assumptions have to be stated, signs have to be right, units carried, significant figures consistent. Its content volume is lower and its procedural demand is higher.

Physics has the lowest content volume of the three and the highest mathematical dependency. A student can know the whole syllabus and still perform poorly if their algebra is slow, because questions about circuits, fields and oscillations are algebra problems with physical context attached. It also has the sharpest distinction between description and explanation: a physics explanation question wants a mechanism, and an answer that restates the phenomenon in different words earns very little.

The practical implication is that the diagnostic question differs by subject. For biology, is the student learning precisely enough. For chemistry, is the student disciplined enough in calculation. For physics, is the student's mathematics fast enough, and do they know what an explanation is. The table sets this out, and it is also a useful document for a Year 11 student still choosing.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level in Physics
paragraphs: The level decision in Physics is more consequential than in most subjects, because the extension is not simply more of the same material. It adds topics with their own mathematical demands, particularly electromagnetic induction, simple harmonic motion handled properly and fields treated with more rigour. Those are also where the difference between a 5 and a 7 at Higher Level is decided.

A student considering Higher Level Physics should check three things honestly. Whether a university course on their shortlist actually requires it, since engineering and physics degrees commonly specify it and many other courses do not. Whether their mathematics course and level support it, because Higher Level Physics with a Standard Level maths course that avoids algebraic work is a structural mismatch. And whether the total Higher Level load is survivable, since Physics plus two other demanding Higher Levels is a heavy combination that a Year 11 student rarely has the information to judge.

Standard Level Physics is a serious qualification and is accepted by a wide range of courses. A student who takes Standard Level and performs strongly is usually better placed than one who takes Higher Level and cannot handle the extension, and that is worth saying because the cultural pressure in a competitive school cluster runs the other way.

Where a student has already started Higher Level and is struggling, the first question is still diagnostic rather than administrative. Losses concentrated in the Higher Level extension topics indicate a content gap that can be closed with direct teaching. Losses spread across all topics including the Standard Level core usually indicate the mathematical dependency is the real issue, and that needs addressing in maths before it is addressed in physics.

sections.heading: The maths pairing that decides how physics feels
paragraphs: Of all the subject combinations in the Diploma, the one that most determines a student's experience is Physics with their maths course. This is rarely discussed at the point the choices are made, and it produces a predictable pattern of difficulty in Diploma 2 that families then attribute to the physics teaching.

Analysis and Approaches builds exactly the algebraic fluency physics requires: rearranging confidently, handling functions, and in the Higher Level version the calculus that makes several physics relationships make sense rather than merely be memorised. Applications and Interpretation is technology-permitted and statistically weighted, which is valuable in its own right and does not build the same by-hand algebraic speed. Neither course is wrong; the mismatch is specific.

A Higher Level Physics student taking Applications and Interpretation can succeed, and will have to do explicit algebraic work that their maths course is not going to provide. The useful move is to recognise that in the first term and schedule for it, rather than to discover it in a Diploma 2 mock and conclude that physics is the problem. A tutor who audits the maths dependency in the first session is doing the single most useful thing available.

The specific skills to audit are short enough to list. Rearranging a formula with the unknown in a denominator. Proportional reasoning: what happens to a quantity when another doubles, without computing. Handling powers of ten in multiplication and division without a calculator. Reading a gradient from a graph and attaching units to it. A student fluent in those four finds physics calculations straightforward; a student slow in any of them loses marks across every topic in the subject.

sections.heading: Description against explanation, and where the marks go
paragraphs: If there is one sentence worth taking from this page it is that a physics explanation question wants a mechanism. Students answer them with a restatement of the phenomenon, often fluently, and score a fraction of the available marks. This is the dominant loss in Diploma Physics and it has nothing to do with how well the student understands the subject.

A worked example. Asked to explain why an electromotive force is induced when a magnet moves through a coil, a typical answer says that the magnetic flux through the coil changes as the magnet moves. That is a description of the situation the question just described. The mark scheme wants the chain: the flux linkage changes, a changing flux linkage induces an electromotive force, and the magnitude depends on the rate of change. Three steps, each creditable, and the first answer supplied none of them.

The pattern repeats across the syllabus. Asked why the current falls when a resistor is added, students say the resistance is higher. Asked why a satellite stays in orbit, they describe the orbit. Asked why the amplitude decays, they say energy is lost without naming where it went. In each case the student knows the physics and does not know that the question is asking for causation in steps.

The fix is mechanical and quick, which makes it one of the best uses of early sessions. Identify the command term. If it is explain, write a chain with at least one because in it. Count the marks and produce that many distinct steps. Students who adopt this habit gain marks across both papers without learning any new physics, and the gain is usually visible within three or four weeks.

sections.heading: The data booklet, and the equations that are not in it
paragraphs: A data booklet is provided in every Diploma Physics examination, and it contains most of the relationships a student needs plus the constants. Two things follow. There is no value in memorising what the booklet provides, and students waste real hours doing so. And there is substantial value in knowing precisely what it does not provide, because those are the things that must be learned and the list is short enough to be learned properly.

Beyond memorisation, the booklet is a speed skill. Finding the right relationship among several similar ones under time pressure takes seconds for a practised student and a minute for an unpractised one, and a minute a question across a paper is a grade. Practising the search is as legitimate a use of a session as practising the physics, and it is almost never done.

There is a subtler point about selection. Several topics have two or three related expressions in the booklet, and choosing the wrong one produces an answer that looks plausible and is wrong. Knowing which expression applies under which conditions is physics rather than administration, and it is exactly the kind of thing a specialist teaches in a sentence and a textbook takes a page to obscure.

In an online session this is straightforward to practise, since both people can look at the same page and the same question simultaneously. A tutor can watch the student search, time it, and correct the habit. That is a place where a shared screen is at least as good as sitting beside someone, because the search becomes observable rather than invisible.

sections.heading: The Diploma investigation against the IGCSE practical
paragraphs: A student arriving in Diploma Physics from Cambridge 0625 or Edexcel 4PH1 has spent two years doing practical work from a method sheet and answering questions about experiments somebody else designed. The Diploma investigation asks them to design one, which is a different activity requiring a different kind of thinking, and it is where the switchers in this cluster most often struggle.

In physics specifically, the commonest design failure is a research question with no clearly measurable relationship in it. A question that asks how one thing affects another needs a quantity that can be varied, a quantity that can be measured, and an effect large enough for the available apparatus to resolve. Students propose investigations where the predicted effect is smaller than the uncertainty in their measuring instrument, which guarantees inconclusive data however carefully the work is done.

Checking that before the practical rather than after is the highest-value hour a tutor spends on a physics investigation. It is also a legitimate kind of help: asking whether the apparatus can resolve the expected effect is teaching experimental reasoning, not writing the report. The same applies to questioning whether a control is actually controlling anything, which is a question students rarely ask of their own method.

On the evaluation criterion, the pattern matches the other sciences. Students list equipment limitations generically. The descriptor wants a specific limitation connected to the specific conclusion drawn, with a realistic improvement. One sentence of that form outperforms a page of generic regret. And the boundary is firm: a tutor may explain criteria, model an unrelated investigation, question a draft and point at gaps. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit any part of it, and buying a completed internal assessment, which some operators in this market sell, risks the Diploma itself.

sections.heading: Three ways to buy physics help, compared
paragraphs: A family in Al Safa has three realistic options, and they are not interchangeable. The school's own physics provision, which frequently includes a clinic or a revision session at no cost and which a surprising number of households have never asked about. A tuition centre group class, cheaper per hour. And one-to-one work, online or in-home. The right answer depends on the diagnosis rather than on the budget.

Here are the published rates, so any quote has a context. A qualified online subject tutor in Dubai sits at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work is quoted at AED 270 by TutorChase, with Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200-450 and above and BartyED publishing AED 650. Budget online runs AED 33-150, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate and AED 200-500 by independent home tutors, travel included. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600, AED 600-1,200 and AED 1,000-2,000 or more across the three tiers, with packages advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of those are other providers' own published figures.

For physics the scarcity point is sharper than the price point. Higher Level Physics cohorts are spread thinly across the several schools in and around Al Safa rather than pooled, so the local population of people who teach it to examiner depth is very small. Requiring a tutor to be both qualified in it and willing to come to an Al Safa address on a weekday evening removes nearly all of them, and the nearness that Al Safa offers in other respects does not help here.

Our position: no in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, a free trial lesson first, and a fee discussed after the level and the problem are established. If a trial shows that the real bottleneck is maths rather than physics, we will say so, and the right next step may be a maths tutor and the school's own physics clinic rather than anything we sell.

sections.heading: Physics without a laboratory: what online can and cannot do
paragraphs: This objection deserves a straight answer. Laboratory work stays at school, where the apparatus and supervision are. No tutoring arrangement, in-home or online, substitutes for a school physics laboratory, and a provider implying otherwise is overselling something they cannot deliver.

What a tutor works on is the examined part of practical physics, and it is substantial. Variable control and why a particular control matters for a particular measurement. Uncertainty propagation through a calculation. Reading a gradient and attaching units to it. Distinguishing a trend from noise in a results table. Identifying which source of error actually affected the conclusion rather than listing every one that could have. Judging whether apparatus could resolve the effect being investigated. All of those are written skills assessed in both papers and in the investigation.

In practice that is where a large share of recoverable marks sits, because practical reasoning is taught less explicitly than content and students arrive at it with habits formed by prescribed IGCSE practicals. A student who has performed an experiment and cannot write about its limitations precisely is losing marks that have nothing to do with manual skill.

There is also a documentation point that applies to every laboratory session a student attends. Raw data with uncertainties noted rather than rounded values. The apparatus actually used and its precision. Anything that behaved unexpectedly, because that is the raw material of a good evaluation. Any deviation from the planned method. Agreeing in advance what to record converts a laboratory hour into usable evidence, and that conversation is among the most valuable a physics tutor can have.

faqs.question: My child is fine in chemistry and struggling in physics. Why?
faqs.answer: Most often because physics has the highest mathematical dependency of the three sciences and chemistry does not. Questions about circuits, fields and oscillations are algebra problems with physical context attached, so a student whose rearranging is slow or who is uncertain with powers of ten loses marks across every topic while understanding the physics perfectly well. The other common cause is the explanation habit: physics asks why and students answer what. Both are identifiable from a marked script in about twenty minutes.

faqs.question: What does an explanation question actually want in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: A mechanism in steps, with at least one because in it. Asked why an electromotive force is induced when a magnet moves through a coil, a typical answer says the flux through the coil changes, which simply restates the situation the question described. The scheme wants the chain: flux linkage changes, a changing flux linkage induces an electromotive force, and the magnitude depends on the rate of change. Count the marks and produce that many distinct steps. Students who adopt this habit gain marks within weeks.

faqs.question: Does my child's maths course affect how hard physics will be?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it is rarely discussed when the choices are made. Analysis and Approaches builds the by-hand algebraic fluency physics requires, and at Higher Level the calculus that makes several physics relationships comprehensible rather than memorised. Applications and Interpretation is technology-permitted and statistically weighted, which is valuable and does not build the same algebraic speed. Higher Level Physics with Applications and Interpretation can work, and it requires explicit algebra practice the maths course will not provide.

faqs.question: Which is harder, Higher Level Physics or Higher Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: They are hard in different places, which is more useful than a ranking. Chemistry has more content and a higher procedural demand: stated assumptions, correct signs, units carried, consistent significant figures. Physics has less content and a much higher mathematical demand, with the explanation-versus-description distinction sharper than anywhere else in the sciences. A student with strong algebra and a taste for mechanism usually finds physics the better fit; a student who likes thorough procedure often prefers chemistry.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level Physics a problem for engineering applications?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. Engineering and physics degrees commonly specify Higher Level Physics, often alongside a Higher Level maths requirement, while many other courses accept Standard Level or do not require physics at all. The reliable method is to build the university shortlist and read each course's own stated entry requirements, including at UAE universities. Do that in Year 11 while the level choice is still open rather than discovering a requirement in Year 13.

faqs.question: Which physics topics cost Al Safa students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits lead comfortably at both levels, because potential dividers and internal resistance questions are algebra problems in a circuit diagram and slow rearranging is fatal under time pressure. Fields follow, where proportional reasoning is required and students compute instead. Electromagnetic induction is a Higher Level favourite and a reliable source of explanation-question losses. Underneath all of them sits unit and significant-figure discipline, which costs marks in every topic and is among the easiest to recover.

faqs.question: How much of the physics data booklet does my child need to memorise?
faqs.answer: Nothing that is in it, which is more liberating than students expect. The booklet provides most relationships and the constants, so the learning list is only what it omits, and that list is short enough to learn properly. What does need practising is the search: finding the right expression among several similar ones takes seconds for a practised student and a minute for an unpractised one, and knowing which of two related expressions applies under which conditions is physics rather than administration.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor come to our villa in Al Safa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide in India only. Physics sessions here are one-to-one over live video in a shared workspace where both people can draw circuit diagrams, free-body diagrams and graphs. Watching a student search the data booklet on a shared screen is also genuinely useful, because the search becomes observable and correctable in a way it is not when somebody is leafing through a booklet beside you.

faqs.question: How are physics practicals handled if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work stays at school, where the apparatus and supervision are, and no tutoring replaces that. What a tutor works on is the examined part: variable control and why a specific control matters, uncertainty propagation, reading a gradient with units attached, distinguishing trend from noise, identifying which error actually affected the conclusion, and judging whether apparatus can resolve the effect under investigation. Those are written skills assessed in both papers and in the investigation, and most recoverable practical marks sit in them.

faqs.question: What makes a good physics investigation question?
faqs.answer: Three things, and the third is the one students miss. A quantity that can be varied, a quantity that can be measured, and an effect large enough for the available apparatus to resolve. Students regularly propose investigations where the predicted effect is smaller than the uncertainty in their instrument, which guarantees inconclusive data however carefully the work is done. Checking resolution before the practical rather than after is the most valuable hour a tutor can spend on a physics investigation.

faqs.question: What should my child record during a school physics practical?
faqs.answer: More than most students do. Raw data with uncertainties noted rather than rounded values. The apparatus actually used and its precision, since the evaluation depends on it. Anything that behaved unexpectedly, because that is the raw material of a specific rather than generic evaluation. Any deviation from the planned method. Students frequently come back from a laboratory session with data too thin to process properly, and agreeing in advance what to write down turns a laboratory hour into usable evidence.

faqs.question: Is a group physics class at a tuition centre worth considering?
faqs.answer: For broad revision across a cohort moving at a similar pace, sometimes. For the common case it is poor value, because the single most frequent bottleneck in Diploma Physics is one student's mathematics, and a group class cannot address that. Before paying for anything, ask whether your child's school runs a physics clinic. Several schools in and near Al Safa do, it costs nothing, and it is widely underused, which makes it the first thing to try rather than the last.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE Physics into the Diploma. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Two things, both predictable. Explanation questions now demand a mechanism rather than a recalled statement, which is a different kind of writing from the structured recall IGCSE rewards. And the investigation is self-designed rather than worked from a method sheet, so the student has to pose a measurable question for the first time. Both are addressable in the first term if they are identified then. A student who passed IGCSE Physics mainly on recall rather than calculation finds Diploma 1 steeper than expected.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week do families in this area start with?
faqs.answer: One is usual, rising to two in the final term or when the investigation and paper practice both need attention. The constraint is the student's capacity to do the work between sessions rather than the budget: a full paper takes well over an hour to sit and roughly as long again to review properly. A student booked three times a week has no space to produce the evidence those sessions exist to diagnose, and past that point extra contact hours reduce progress rather than adding to it.

faqs.question: What time of day suits a physics session best?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families assume, because quantitative work degrades with tiredness faster than discussion does. Schools in and around Al Safa finish between roughly 2.30pm and 3.15pm and journeys home are short for many students here, so a 4.30pm start is often workable where it would not be further out. For anything calculation-heavy a weekend morning beats a 7pm weekday slot, and online delivery means no tutor's journey needs accommodating in either case.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Physics specialist is available?
faqs.answer: We tell you plainly rather than assigning a general science tutor. Higher Level Physics is among the thinner categories, and it tightens further in exam terms when specialists are fully committed. You get a clear statement that we do not currently have the right person, a realistic estimate of how long a match might take, and a suggestion for the interim, which is sometimes the school's own department or, if the real bottleneck is algebra, a maths tutor instead.

intro.heading: Is there anyone who actually knows this syllabus?
paragraphs: That is the real question behind the search, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Diploma physics is a narrow specialism. The population of people in Dubai who can teach it well is much smaller than the population of people who will accept a booking for it, and the gap between those two groups is where families lose a term. A parent in Al Satwa has no obvious way to tell them apart from a profile page, because every profile says the same words.

So this page hands you the test instead. There are six questions that reliably separate someone who teaches Diploma physics from someone who teaches science and has read the subject guide. They take four minutes to ask, they can be asked in a free trial lesson, and you do not need to know physics yourself to judge the answers — you only need to know what a real answer sounds like, which is what the table further down gives you.

Why it matters so much in this subject: physics at Diploma level is three different competences wearing one name. There is the physics itself — fields, momentum, thermodynamics, quantum ideas. There is the mathematics inside the physics, which is where most capable students actually fail, because they understand the concept and cannot execute the algebra under time pressure. And there is the experimental half: uncertainties, graph linearisation, the language of a method, the scientific investigation that carries a fifth of the grade. A tutor strong in one and weak in the other two will produce a student who sounds knowledgeable and scores a 4.

The second thing a Satwa family needs to know is that the optional and higher-level content differs by school. Schools make choices about what they teach and in what order, and a tutor who is working from a generic course plan rather than from your child's school's sequence will spend February teaching something the class covered in October. Asking which topics the school has already covered, and in what order, is a legitimate first-session question — and a tutor who does not ask it is telling you something.

Al Satwa itself has almost no private schools inside it. Children here travel to Al Safa, Jumeirah, Oud Metha, Al Barsha and Umm Suqeim, and only a subset of those schools runs the IB Diploma at all, since the International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7% of Dubai's private school enrolment against 37% on the UK curriculum. That makes the local pool of Diploma physics specialists thinner still, and it is the practical reason online delivery matters here rather than a marketing reason.

Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one and delivered live online to Al Satwa on Gulf Standard Time, with the first one free so the verification costs you nothing. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The trade is explicit — no person in the room, and a tutor selected for the subject and level rather than for who lives within a twenty-minute drive of Satwa.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-satwa.programmesIntro: Physics does not begin at Diploma level, and a verification conversation is different at each stage. Below is what a tutor should be able to speak about precisely for each programme a Satwa family might be dealing with.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria rather than by examination, with the sciences marked on knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A tutor who can name those criteria and describe what distinguishes a top band from a middle one is working from the actual assessment; one who talks about topics alone is not.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in this district typically travel to Al Safa, Umm Suqeim or Al Barsha. The jump from MYP sciences into Diploma physics is where most of the difficulty appears, because criterion-based marking rewards process while the Diploma rewards precision under timed conditions.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Physics, Standard Level
programmes.description: Two years to the May session, assessed by written papers plus an internal assessment worth 20% of the grade. Standard Level covers the common core without the higher-level extensions. The frequent misdiagnosis here is treating a mathematics problem as a physics problem; many SL students who stall are stalling on algebra and unit handling.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm every IB date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. No IB session or results date is published on this page, because none has been confirmed from the IB itself for this project.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Physics, Higher Level
programmes.description: The same core plus substantial additional higher-level content and a further written paper. Higher Level is where the mathematics becomes genuinely demanding and where a tutor's depth is tested rather than their breadth. A specialist should be able to tell you, without looking it up, which parts of the course exist only at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level physics is a common prerequisite for engineering and physical-science degrees. For UAE university routes, Ministry of Education equivalency should be checked on the authority's own page; no IB points threshold is published here because none has been read on a Ministry of Education source.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE Physics
programmes.description: The usual route into Diploma physics in this part of Dubai, taken as Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Cambridge includes an alternative-to-practical paper for candidates not sitting a laboratory exam, and answering it well is a taught skill rather than a by-product of knowing the physics.
programmes.countryNote: Students arriving at Diploma physics from the Extended tier of 0625 are generally better prepared than those arriving from Core, and the gap shows first in algebraic confidence rather than in content knowledge. A single diagnostic session at the start of DP1 is worth more than a term of remediation in DP2.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-satwa.subjectsIntro: A verification conversation needs something concrete to be about. These are the areas of Diploma physics where a specialist's depth either shows or does not, written as the thing a tutor should be able to discuss without preparation.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: The part students assume they already know from IGCSE and then lose marks on. The difficulty is not the equations; it is resolving forces correctly on an inclined plane and keeping sign conventions consistent through a multi-stage problem. A tutor should be able to name the two or three places candidates habitually drop a negative.

subjects.name: Momentum, impulse and collisions
subjects.description: Conservation arguments are easy to state and hard to apply when a graph of force against time replaces a number. Impulse as the area under a curve is a standard examinable step that students meet unprepared because it sits across physics and graph-reading.

subjects.name: Circular motion and gravitation
subjects.description: Orbital problems combine two equations and one piece of algebra, and that algebra is where most of the loss occurs. Candidates who can state the condition for a circular orbit still fail to derive a period, because the rearrangement was never practised separately.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and the gas laws
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the ideal gas relationships. Marks go missing in unit conversion — kelvin against celsius, grams against kilograms — far more often than in concept. A tutor who drills the conversions explicitly is addressing the actual failure mode.

subjects.name: Waves, interference and standing waves
subjects.description: Path difference and phase arguments require a diagram drawn correctly before any calculation. Students who go straight to a formula get the arithmetic right and the physics wrong. Standing waves on strings and in pipes reward a disciplined approach to boundary conditions.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational, electric and magnetic
subjects.description: The conceptual heart of the course and the place where Higher Level separates from Standard. Potential against field strength, and the sign conventions that follow, are routinely confused. This is the single best topic on which to test a tutor's depth in a trial lesson.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Internal resistance, potential dividers and the behaviour of real cells. Candidates lose marks explaining why a reading changes when a component is altered, because the explanation requires a chain of reasoning rather than a calculation.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy and the photoelectric effect. Students handle the ideas and lose marks on the orders of magnitude and the unit prefixes. Working in electronvolts and converting correctly is a drill, and it is one of the fastest marks to recover.

subjects.name: Uncertainties, errors and graph work

sections.heading: Six questions that separate a physics teacher from a science tutor
paragraphs: Ask these six questions in the free trial lesson. You do not need to know physics to judge the answers; the table gives you what a real answer sounds like and what a weak one sounds like. Four minutes of this will tell you more than any profile page, any review count and any claim about years of experience.

The reason they work is that each one requires knowledge that cannot be acquired by skimming a subject guide. Which content exists only at Higher Level, how the internal assessment criteria are actually worded, what percentage uncertainty does when two quantities are multiplied, which optional topic a school has chosen — these are things a person knows from having taught the course through a full cycle, or does not know at all. Vague confidence is the tell.

The sixth question is the one most parents never think to ask: what has my child's school already covered, and in what order? A tutor who does not want to know this will teach a generic sequence and will eventually spend a session on something the class did two months ago. A tutor who asks it before you do has told you they have worked with Dubai schools and understands that the sequencing varies.

One further note. A tutor may answer a question with an honest 'I would need to check the current guide' and still be excellent, because subject guides are revised and nobody should be confidently quoting a version from three years ago. The distinction to watch for is between somebody who knows where to check and somebody who does not know that there is something to check.
