sections.heading: How Diploma physics is actually assessed
paragraphs: Diploma physics is assessed by written papers plus an internal assessment carrying 20% of the grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Higher Level candidates sit an additional written paper and additional content. The exact component weightings should be confirmed against the current subject guide through your child's IB coordinator, because guides are revised and a stale figure quoted confidently is worse than one checked.

What matters for tutoring is the shape rather than the decimal places. A fifth of the grade is earned before the exam period in a piece of coursework the student produces themselves, which means a fifth of the grade is available to a well-organised student regardless of exam-day nerves. Families who treat the investigation as an administrative chore rather than as a graded component are leaving the most controllable marks on the table.

The written papers split broadly into short-answer and data-analysis work on one side and extended problem-solving on the other. The data-analysis element is why uncertainties and graph work are not an optional extra: they appear in the papers directly and they underpin the investigation as well. A tutor who treats them as a side topic has misread where the marks are.

On dates: UAE schools sit the May session, and this page publishes no specific IB exam or results date because none has been confirmed from the IB itself for this project. Secondary sources circulate windows that do not always agree. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it.

sections.heading: The three ways capable physics students actually fail
paragraphs: A student losing marks in Diploma physics is usually failing in one of three distinct ways, and the remedies are different enough that misdiagnosis wastes a term. The first is mathematical execution. The student understands the physics, states the right relationship, and then loses the question in the algebra — a rearrangement with the unknown in a denominator, a square root taken too early, a sign dropped on an inclined plane. This is the most common failure among students who sound knowledgeable in conversation.

The second is explanation. Physics marks are often awarded for a chain of reasoning: this increases, therefore this decreases, therefore the reading falls. Students who know the answer write the conclusion and skip the chain, and the mark scheme awards the chain. This shows up most in circuits, in thermal physics and in anything involving a changing field. It is a writing problem with a physics subject, and it responds to being shown two or three model answers and then being made to produce the structure repeatedly.

The third is the experimental half. Uncertainties, propagation, linearisation, reading a gradient and stating it with its uncertainty, and the precise language of a method. This is examinable in the written papers and it underpins the internally assessed investigation, so weakness here costs twice. It is also the area where a general science tutor is least likely to be strong, because it is a technique set rather than a body of knowledge.

A good trial lesson should tell you which of the three your child is in. Ask the tutor at the end: which of those three is the problem here, and what is the evidence? A tutor who answers with a specific observation from the hour — the student set up the physics correctly and lost it rearranging, or wrote the right conclusion with no reasoning — has diagnosed. A tutor who says the student needs to practise more has not.
bullets: Mathematical execution: right physics, lost in the algebra
Explanation: the conclusion written without the chain of reasoning

Ask the tutor which of the three it is, and what the evidence was

sections.heading: Uncertainties and graph work: the half nobody tutors
paragraphs: If a family buys only one block of physics support, this is often the one that moves the most marks, and it is the block almost nobody sells. Uncertainty handling appears directly in the data-analysis paper and it underpins the internally assessed investigation, so a student who is weak here loses marks in two places. It is also entirely teachable as technique, which means it improves quickly once addressed.

The content of the block is small and specific. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, and the difference between them. What happens to uncertainty when quantities are added, multiplied, divided or raised to a power. How to choose what to plot so that a relationship becomes a straight line, which is the single most useful analytical move in the whole course. How to draw a line of best fit with maximum and minimum gradients and state the gradient with its uncertainty. How to say, in the mark scheme's language, why a result is or is not consistent with a theoretical value.

Most students arrive at Diploma physics having met none of this properly. IGCSE physics touches error and anomaly but not propagation, and a school's Diploma teaching has to cover a large syllabus in two years, so this part tends to be delivered once and assumed. The consequence is predictable: strong students who can solve a dynamics problem and cannot say whether their own experimental result agrees with the prediction.

Four to six focused sessions will usually complete the set. It is self-contained, which makes it the easiest physics support to buy honestly — the outcome is checkable, because the student either can or cannot propagate an uncertainty through a three-step calculation by the end of it.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The investigation is worth 20% of the physics grade and it is the student's own work. That second sentence is not a disclaimer; it is the whole structure of the thing. IB academic-honesty rules make submitted work that is not the candidate's own a malpractice matter, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on whoever helped. One operator visible in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. A Satwa family should treat that as a reason to walk away rather than as a convenience.

Here is what a tutor may legitimately do. Explain the assessment criteria in the IB's own words. Discuss whether a proposed research question is actually answerable with the equipment the school has, which is where most weak investigations are lost before any data is collected. Model an analysis technique on a completely different dataset. Teach uncertainty propagation and linearisation as technique. Read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning does not follow, where the uncertainty treatment is thin, and where the conclusion claims more than the data supports.

Here is what a tutor may not do: write any part of it, rewrite any part of it, edit it to completion, supply a research question to be adopted wholesale, or produce the analysis. The distinction is between teaching a student to do the work and doing the work. A tutor who offers the second is offering to put your child at risk.

Nor should anyone supply you with board materials. Subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and the correct behaviour is to reference and link the official source rather than host copies. If a provider offers you a folder of IB documents, that tells you how they handle rules generally.

Analysis technique modelled on different data, never on the student's own
Written feedback on a draft the student wrote, and nothing more

sections.heading: What verified physics support costs in this market
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring sites in Dubai publish no price, and the two that do quote US dollars. Here are the AED market bands with the providers who published them, as of October 2026. Budget online tutoring runs roughly AED 33 to 150 an hour, with Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits between AED 150 and 300, Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, Bestimate putting the usual range at AED 180 to 350. The premium named tier starts around AED 500, with BartyED at AED 650.

Diploma physics sits at the upper end of that structure for a straightforward reason: the pool of people who can teach it well is small, and small pools price higher. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support, which is the realistic band for Higher Level physics in DP2. Market packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, though eight sessions at that price is unlikely to be specialist cover.

What the verification questions do is tell you whether you are paying the specialist rate for specialist teaching. That is the actual financial risk in this subject — not overpaying in absolute terms, but paying AED 270 an hour for somebody who knows the topics and cannot teach uncertainty propagation. The questions cost nothing and they can be asked in a free lesson, which makes them the cheapest due diligence available.

A note about the top of the market. Premium rates are sometimes justified by describing a tutor as an examiner. Examiner status means nothing unless it can be evidenced, and it grants no access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. Nobody should be implying otherwise, and a family paying at that level should be able to see what the premium buys in teaching terms.

sections.heading: Permits, examiner claims and what a parent can check
paragraphs: Verification has a regulatory half as well as an academic one, and it is cheap to do. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here, and a site quoting one should be read carefully.

The regulator question is separate. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is ADEK; in Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority; in Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA inspects schools. It does not accredit individual tutors, and 'KHDA-approved physics tutor' is not a real credential. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, claims none, and has no UAE office.

One more thing a Satwa parent should know. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. So an arrangement with your child's own physics teacher, privately, is not something to pursue — treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the exact wording.

sections.heading: If nobody covers the level or topic you need
paragraphs: This is the disclosure no competitor in this market makes, and it is the one a Satwa family most needs. Specialist physics cover is not uniform. Higher Level is thinner than Standard Level. The extension content is thinner than the core. A specific optional topic combined with a specific weekday slot can be thinner still. Pretending otherwise is how a family ends up with a biology graduate teaching Higher Level fields.

The honest options, in order of preference, are these. Wait a short time for the right specialist, which is usually a matter of weeks rather than months and is almost always better than starting with the wrong person. Move the weekly slot, because a different hour opens a different pool and an 18:30 Thursday is not the same market as a 17:00 Monday. Or take a tutor outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time for the same subject and level, which is how online delivery turns a thin local pool into a workable one.

What should not happen is substitution without disclosure. A general science tutor taking a Higher Level physics student because the calendar had a gap is the single most common quiet failure in this market, and it is invisible for about six weeks — long enough for a term to be lost. The verification questions in the first section of this page exist precisely to catch it, and they work whether the tutor comes from here or from anywhere else.

Two final things nobody should be telling you. No tutor can promise a grade, a number of points or an improvement in an externally assessed examination, and a provider claiming it is describing their marketing. And tutoring is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission, or for school progression. Any suggestion otherwise is manufactured urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Making an online physics lesson work from a Satwa apartment
paragraphs: Physics over video works when the writing is visible, and fails when it is not. The subject is conducted in diagrams, derivations and graphs, so a session where the tutor talks and the student listens is a session where nobody can see the sign error. The setup that works is a shared whiteboard the student writes on, or a second camera or phone angled at paper, so that working appears in real time and can be annotated.

In the housing stock typical of Al Satwa — apartments, shared rooms, family life happening in the next room — a few practical choices make a large difference. A wired connection or a position near the router, because a dropped frame during a derivation costs the thread. Headphones, so the room's noise stops mattering. A surface large enough for A4 paper and a calculator, which sounds trivial and is the most common reason a student works on their lap and writes nothing down. And a fixed place, so the setup is not rebuilt every week.

There is an advantage to this format that is specific to physics rather than general. Every annotated derivation and every marked graph is capturable, so the student finishes the year with a growing record of their own corrected work rather than with a memory of a conversation. For a subject where the same algebraic slip recurs across different topics, being able to look back at the last four times it happened is genuinely useful.

Practical work remains the school's to deliver, and nobody should suggest otherwise. What a tutor can do is prepare a student for the laboratory — the method language, the control of variables, the uncertainty estimate before the data is collected — and then work with the data the student actually gathered. That division is honest and it is also where most of the assessed marks sit.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor really knows Diploma physics or just says so?
faqs.answer: Ask six things in the free trial lesson. Which parts of the course exist only at Higher Level. How the internal assessment criteria are worded. What happens to uncertainty when two measured quantities are multiplied. What weighting the internal assessment carries. Which optional or extension topic your child's school teaches. And what the class has covered so far, in what order. A specialist answers the first four without hesitating, asks you the fifth and sixth, and says honestly when they want to check the current guide. Vague confidence on all six is the tell, and it takes four minutes to find.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics a different teaching job from Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Yes, and treating them as the same thing is a common and expensive mistake. Higher Level carries substantial additional content and an extra written paper, and the mathematics becomes genuinely demanding rather than merely fiddly. A tutor comfortable with the Standard Level core may be out of their depth on the extension material, and that will not be visible for several weeks. Ask specifically which content exists only at Higher Level; a specialist names it immediately, and somebody working from a skim of the subject guide talks about depth in general terms.

faqs.question: My son understands the physics and still gets 4s. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of two things. Either he is losing questions in the algebra — a rearrangement with the unknown in a denominator, a dropped sign on an inclined plane, a square root taken a step too early — or he is writing conclusions without the chain of reasoning the mark scheme awards. Both are invisible in conversation, because a student who can explain a concept out loud sounds secure. Both are also fast to fix once named. Ask a tutor at the end of a trial lesson which of the two it is and what the evidence from that hour was.

faqs.question: Why does everyone skip uncertainties, and does it actually cost marks?
faqs.answer: It costs marks twice, which is why it matters. Uncertainty handling appears directly in the data-analysis paper and it underpins the internally assessed investigation worth 20% of the grade. It gets skipped because it is technique rather than content: a school with a large syllabus and two years delivers it once and assumes it. Most students arrive from IGCSE having met anomalies and error but never propagation or linearisation. Four to six focused sessions usually complete the whole set, and the result is checkable — either the student can propagate through a three-step calculation or cannot.

faqs.question: What does linearising a relationship mean and why do tutors go on about it?
faqs.answer: It means choosing what to plot so that a curved relationship becomes a straight line, which turns a hard analysis into a gradient and an intercept. It is the single most useful analytical move in Diploma physics, it appears in the data-analysis paper, and it is usually what separates a strong investigation from a middling one. Students who have not been taught it plot the raw quantities, get a curve, and then have nothing to say about it. It is a short topic with a disproportionate return, and it is squarely in the technique block rather than in the content.

faqs.question: Where does academic honesty draw the line on scientific investigation support?
faqs.answer: The limits are clear once they are written down. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the IB's own words, discuss whether a research question is answerable with the equipment the school has, model an analysis technique on a completely different dataset, teach uncertainty propagation, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion, supply a research question to be adopted wholesale, or produce the analysis. Submitted work that is not the candidate's own is a malpractice matter and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Which part of the investigation goes wrong most often?
faqs.answer: The research question, chosen before any data exists. A question that cannot be answered with the equipment available, or that has no measurable independent variable, or that produces three data points, has already capped the grade before the student walks into the laboratory. That is the cheapest thing in the whole component to get right and the thing least often discussed. A single session testing the question for answerability, before data collection begins, is worth more than several sessions tidying up an analysis built on unusable measurements.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor need to be a current examiner?
faqs.answer: No, and the claim should be treated carefully. Examiner status is only meaningful if it can be evidenced, and it confers no access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased paper content. Nobody should be implying it does. What actually predicts good teaching is depth in the course and the ability to diagnose: naming the extension content, knowing the criteria, teaching uncertainty propagation, and identifying from one hour of work whether a student's problem is algebraic, explanatory or experimental. Ask for that instead, because it can be demonstrated in front of you.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for Higher Level physics support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures as of October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist exam-year support at one hour weekly is AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Higher Level physics sits at the upper end because the pool of people who teach it well is small. Those figures belong to the providers named; here the first lesson is free, so verification costs nothing before anything is priced.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a home in Al Satwa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Sessions for Satwa families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard so derivations and graphs are visible and annotated as they are written. The honest trade-off is that you lose a person in the room and gain a tutor chosen for the level and extension content rather than for who is willing to drive into Satwa at five in the afternoon. In a subject with a pool this thin, that trade is usually worth making.

faqs.question: How do I make an online physics lesson work in a Satwa apartment?
faqs.answer: Three things carry most of it. A fixed place with a surface big enough for A4 paper and a calculator, because a student working on their lap writes nothing down and writing is the whole subject. Headphones, so household noise stops mattering. And either a shared whiteboard the student writes on or a phone angled at the paper, so the tutor sees the working rather than hearing a description of it. A wired connection or a seat near the router helps, because a dropped frame in the middle of a derivation costs the thread.

faqs.question: What time can a physics session start if my child travels to Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Plan 18:00 and you will keep the slot. Al Satwa has almost no secondary schools inside it, and the Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Umm Suqeim runs commonly put a child through the door after 16:30, sometimes after 17:00 on a bad day. A lesson set at 17:00 for that commute slips fifteen minutes one week and half an hour the next, and is abandoned by the third month. For the Al Safa and Jumeirah clusters, 17:15 is realistic. Set it against the latest arrival you have actually seen.

faqs.question: Do private physics tutors in Dubai need a permit, and can I see it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and you can ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. It costs a family nothing. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted to you.

faqs.question: Should I look for a KHDA-approved physics tutor?
faqs.answer: There is no such thing, and the phrase should make you cautious about whoever used it. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai: it inspects schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. It does not accredit individual private tutors. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, claims none, and has no UAE office. The credential that does exist for an individual is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and you can ask to see it.

faqs.question: When are the IB physics exams, and why will nobody tell me a date?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session, and this page deliberately publishes no specific IB exam or results date. The reason is that none has been confirmed from the IB itself for this project — ibo.org blocks automated checking, and secondary sources circulate windows that do not always agree. A date a parent plans around is a date worth getting from the source, so confirm it with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. Any site stating an IB session date confidently without naming where it read it is guessing in public.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level physics specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You get told, and you get the honest options. Higher Level is a thinner pool than Standard Level, the extension content thinner again, and a specific topic combined with a fixed weekday hour is the thinnest combination of all. The choices are a short wait, which is usually weeks rather than months and almost always better than the wrong person; a different weekly slot, because a different hour is a different market; or a specialist outside the UAE working on Gulf Standard Time. What should not happen is a general science tutor taking the booking because the calendar had a gap.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-satwa.closingHeading: Ask the six questions before you pay anybody
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-satwa.closingBody: The hardest part of finding Diploma physics support in Al Satwa is not price and it is not scheduling. It is telling a specialist apart from somebody who has read the subject guide, because both profiles say the same words. The six questions in the first section of this page are the test, they take four minutes, and they can be asked inside a free trial lesson of any tutor in this market including ours. Send your child's level and the school's recent topic order, take the free lesson, ask all six, and ask for the diagnosis in specific terms before you commit to anything. Lessons are one-to-one, live online, on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-sufouh.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Physics at Standard and Higher Level under the current guide, with its five themes and its two-paper structure. Higher Level requests are matched to someone who has taught the deeper field and quantum content rather than only the shared core. All sessions run online.

intro.heading: Work upwards from nothing, not downwards from a quote
paragraphs: Most families in Al Sufouh approach physics tutoring from the wrong end. A quote arrives, it sounds reasonable or it sounds steep, and the decision gets made against that single number. The better sequence is to start at zero and move up only when the free layer runs out, because in Diploma physics the free layer is unusually substantial and most of it goes unused.

What costs nothing: the subject's published assessment criteria, which tell a student exactly what the scientific investigation is marked on; the school's own physics clinic or intervention session, already inside fees that have been paid; the DP coordinator's answer to which level and which school assessment deadlines apply; the student's own last mock paper, sat and left unmarked so that somebody can diagnose it rather than congratulate it; and the official subject documentation the school holds. A family that has used all five of those and still has a problem has a real problem, and is now in a position to buy help precisely rather than generally.

Then the market. Read in October 2026, the Dubai ladder starts lower than parents expect. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to AED 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65, usually delivered by current university students. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted from AED 150 by Unitors for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate placing specialist exam-year support in that band. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500. Those are the market's own published figures, attributed to the providers who publish them, and they are not an IB Gram price list.

The useful question is which rung each job needs. A Standard Level student who has fallen behind on theme A kinematics does not need a AED 650 tutor; the content is in the guide and a competent teacher at AED 200 can close it. A Higher Level student who cannot structure an evaluation on the scientific investigation, or who is losing most of Paper 2 to extended-response questions, is buying judgement rather than explanation, and that is where the specialist band earns its number. Buying the top rung for a bottom-rung problem is the commonest overspend in this catchment, and buying the bottom rung for a top-rung problem is the commonest waste.

IB Gram's delivery position is identical across every UAE page. Tuition for families here is one-to-one online tuition over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service offered only in India. For physics specifically that is less of a compromise than it sounds, because almost all of the examinable work is paper, data and reasoning, and a shared screen holds a graph, a markscheme and a student's working in one visible place.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-sufouh.programmesIntro: Physics appears in three places in the programmes an Al Sufouh family deals with, and the cost of support differs because the assessment differs. The notes below separate them rather than treating science as one continuous subject.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Under the current physics guide the course is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Standard and Higher Level share a core, with Higher Level going further in several themes rather than adding separate option units. Assessment is Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 at forty-four, and the scientific investigation at twenty. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section.
programmes.countryNote: Al Sufouh's Diploma cohort is small, so a single physics set can hold both Standard and Higher Level students, and the Higher Level extension content is often taught in additional sessions rather than in the main timetable. Families here should ask the DP coordinator which level is confirmed and what the school's own internal deadlines are for the investigation, because those dates drive the whole support plan.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP sciences are assessed against four criteria rather than against papers: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is marked out of eight against level descriptors. The inquiring-and-designing and processing-and-evaluating criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma scientific investigation, which is why MYP 5 students who have taken those criteria seriously arrive in DP physics with a real advantage.
programmes.countryNote: In this catchment a student may move from an MYP school in Al Sufouh or Al Barsha into a Diploma at another school entirely. Those students usually arrive with stronger investigation skills and weaker algebraic fluency than their IGCSE-route classmates, and the physics support they need is almost the mirror image.

programmes.name: IGCSE physics into Diploma physics
programmes.description: Students arriving from Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 have met mechanics, electricity, waves and radioactivity in a form that rewards recall and single-step calculation. Diploma physics asks for multi-step reasoning, uncertainty handling and extended explanation, and the gap shows within the first term. The alternative-to-practical experience many IGCSE candidates have is genuinely useful preparation for the Paper 1 data-analysis section.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's UK-curriculum schools account for 37 per cent of private enrolment against 7 per cent for the International Baccalaureate, so the IGCSE-to-Diploma crossover is routine rather than exceptional in Al Sufouh. A family budgeting for the first Diploma year should expect the transition term to need more contact than the terms after it.

programmes.name: The Diploma core alongside physics
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service run alongside the six subjects, and they compete for the same evenings as physics revision. A student writing a physics Extended Essay is doing a piece of independent research on top of the scientific investigation, which is a scheduling problem as much as an academic one. Both must be the student's own work.
programmes.countryNote: Al Sufouh Diploma students typically carry a creativity, activity and service commitment after school, which is one reason an early-evening physics slot often fails and a later online slot succeeds. Planning the physics support calendar around the core deadlines rather than around the subject alone avoids paying for sessions nobody can attend.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-sufouh.subjectsIntro: Physics is the page's subject, but Al Sufouh families rarely buy it in isolation. The entries below name the subjects most often requested alongside it and what each actually demands, because that is what decides whether one tutor or two is the right purchase.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes under the current guide, assessed by two papers and a scientific investigation. The reliable sources of lost marks are uncertainty treatment, graph work where a gradient must be converted into a physical quantity with units, and extended-response questions answered with the right physics in the wrong structure. Higher Level depth in fields and quantum physics is where generalist tutors most often run out.

subjects.name: Physics Paper 1, data-analysis section
subjects.description: The section families forget exists. It presents unfamiliar data and asks for processing, uncertainty handling and interpretation rather than recall. Students who revise only content walk into it unprepared, and it is one of the most trainable parts of the whole course. Three or four sessions on it is high-return work at any rate band.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most commonly paired subject. Physics assumes algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, trigonometry and, at Higher Level, comfort with rates of change. A student who manipulates equations well in a maths lesson and freezes when the same operation appears inside a physics question has a transfer problem, which one tutor can often close in both subjects at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Taken by some physics students, and the pairing is workable but worth examining. Applications assumes technology throughout and spends less time on algebraic manipulation, which is exactly the fluency Higher Level physics leans on. A student on this route taking Higher Level physics usually needs explicit algebra work that the maths course will not supply.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the current science guide's investigation structure and its four assessment criteria, so a student doing well on one investigation usually transfers to the other. The quantitative overlap is in proportional reasoning, significant figures and uncertainty propagation. The content overlap is thinner than families expect, so two subjects usually means two tutors.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paired with physics by students heading towards engineering. The algorithmic reasoning rewards the same stepwise discipline physics demands. Paper technique differs sharply: computer science rewards precise pseudocode convention, and marks are lost describing what a program does instead of tracing what it outputs.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Taken alongside physics in several Dubai Diploma schools. It shares the mechanics vocabulary and the materials content, and it carries its own substantial coursework. Where a student holds physics, design technology and a physics Extended Essay, the constraint is calendar rather than capability and should be planned in Year 12.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The natural sciences are one of the areas of knowledge TOK examines, and physics students are frequently asked to write about them. A tutor can discuss knowledge questions and interrogate an argument's structure. A tutor cannot write the essay or the exhibition commentary, and should state that boundary before any work begins.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in physics
subjects.description: An independent research piece with its own word limit and its own criteria, supervised by a school-appointed supervisor. A tutor may discuss feasibility, question a research question's scope and give feedback on the student's draft. A tutor may not write, draft or complete it, and the student signs any authenticity declaration the school requires.

subjects.name: Arabic and the UAE mandatory subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in every Dubai private school alongside the licensed international curriculum, including IB Diploma schools. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited.

sections.heading: The free layer, exhausted first
paragraphs: Five things an Al Sufouh family can obtain for nothing, in roughly the order of value. First, the DP coordinator's written confirmation of the level your child is entered at and the school's own internal deadlines for the scientific investigation. Those deadlines govern every support plan, and a plan built against a guessed date is a plan that collides with reality in February.

Second, the published assessment criteria for the scientific investigation. The current science guide assesses it on four criteria, each worth six marks for a total of twenty-four: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A student who reads those descriptors before designing an experiment behaves differently from one who reads them after writing it up, and the difference is worth more than several paid hours. The school holds the documentation and will share it.

Third, the school's own physics clinic, intervention group or after-school session. These sit inside fees already paid. A private tutor repeating Thursday's clinic content is being paid to deliver free provision twice, and one email to the subject teacher establishes what is running and whether your child is already on a list. In this catchment that email regularly removes a weekly session from a plan, which at the mid-market band is AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month.

Fourth, one mock paper, sat under timed conditions and deliberately left unmarked. An unmarked paper is diagnostic material; a marked one has usually already been converted into a score and a reassurance. Fifth, the official subject documentation and the specimen material the school holds, which should be read rather than purchased. Nobody should be selling you syllabus documents, past papers or markschemes as downloads: those belong to the IB, and a provider offering a bundle of them as a selling point should be asked where it came from.

sections.heading: The Dubai market from the bottom rung upwards
paragraphs: The table below lists the market in ascending order of price, which is the order a family should read it in rather than the order providers usually present. Every band is attributed to who published it and every figure was read in October 2026. Dubai has no published standard rate for private tuition, so showing who charges what is the only honest way to show cost. None of these is an IB Gram price list.

The bottom rung is more useful than its reputation suggests, within limits. Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 are typically delivered by current university students working from the student's own materials. For a Standard Level student who has missed three weeks of theme A and needs somebody patient to work through the kinematics, that is a sensible purchase and the cheapest route to a solved problem. What the bottom rung cannot do is diagnose: it tends to answer the question asked rather than identify the question that should have been asked.

The middle rung, qualified subject tutors online from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB at Unitors, is where most of the useful work in Diploma physics happens. A teacher who has taught the course can cover a theme properly, mark an extended response against the right expectations and prepare a student for the Paper 1 data-analysis section. For the large majority of physics problems in this catchment, this rung is the correct one.

The top rungs, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for specialists with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and AED 500 to AED 650 and above for premium named tutors with BartyED publishing AED 650, are purchases of judgement rather than explanation. They earn the number on Higher Level fields and quantum content, on structuring an evaluation that reaches the top investigation band, and on Paper 2 extended responses where the physics is right and the answer still scores badly. Buying that rung for a missed-lesson problem is the commonest overspend in Al Sufouh.

sections.heading: Five themes, two papers, and where the time goes
paragraphs: Under the current physics guide the content is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Standard and Higher Level share a core, with Higher Level extending several themes rather than adding separate option units. A tutor who last taught the previous syllabus and has not read the current guide will plan against a structure that no longer exists, which is a question worth asking directly.

Assessment is where the money is best spent. Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent of the grade and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent and holds the extended-response work. The scientific investigation carries twenty. The split matters because it tells you where a marginal hour of tutoring has the most effect: Paper 2 is the largest single component, and extended-response technique is both teachable and frequently untaught.

The data-analysis section of Paper 1 is the most neglected part of the course in this catchment. It presents unfamiliar data and asks for processing, uncertainty treatment and interpretation. Students who revise content alone meet it cold. It is also among the most trainable sections of any Diploma science, because the skills recur: identifying the independent variable, reading a gradient as a physical quantity with units, deciding whether an anomaly is an anomaly, and stating what an uncertainty means for a conclusion. Three or four focused sessions on it is high-return work at any rung.

The commonest Paper 2 failure in this cohort is not wrong physics. It is right physics presented without structure: an answer that states a correct relationship and never applies it to the situation the question built, or that explains two steps of a three-step chain. Fixing that is a writing and sequencing job inside a physics lesson, and it is why the specialist rung exists.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, twenty-four marks, one boundary
paragraphs: The investigation carries twenty per cent of the physics grade and is assessed on four criteria, each worth six marks for a total of twenty-four: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Equal weighting across the four is the fact most students do not act on. They spend their effort on data collection, which sits inside data analysis, and under-serve evaluation, which carries exactly the same six marks and is far easier to improve.

Each criterion rewards something specific. Research design rewards a research question narrow enough to answer and a method whose variables are genuinely controlled. Data analysis rewards correct processing, honest uncertainty treatment and graphs that serve the argument rather than decorate it. Conclusion rewards an answer to the research question that is justified by the data and set against accepted physics. Evaluation rewards identifying the real limitations and proposing improvements that would actually address them.

The evaluation criterion is where marks are most commonly left on the table, and the reason is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. Students write evaluation as apology: a list of things that went wrong, with human error at the top. What the criterion asks for is analysis of which weaknesses materially affected the result and what a better design would do about them. That shift is teachable in two or three sessions and is worth up to six marks of a twenty-four-mark component.

The boundary needs stating before any work starts. A tutor can discuss candidate research questions and say which ones will not generate enough data, question whether a method controls what it claims to control, ask what an uncertainty implies and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, draft, complete or produce the investigation, and should not edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. Where a school requires an authenticity declaration, the candidate signs it. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price, which places a malpractice exposure on the student rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: Practical and laboratory work when the lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the honest objection to online physics tuition and it deserves a direct answer. Hands-on laboratory work belongs to the school. The school has the equipment, the technician support, the safety framework and the supervision requirement, and no tutoring arrangement should attempt to replace it. A tutor who claims to run practicals for a Dubai family is either describing a demonstration or describing something that will not satisfy the school's requirements.

What tutoring can do is everything around the bench. Designing the method before the student reaches the laboratory, so the session in the lab produces usable data rather than a repeat. Choosing the range and the number of repeats. Deciding what to measure and how precisely. Processing the data afterwards: plotting it so the relationship is visible, propagating the uncertainties properly, and deciding whether a point is anomalous or inconvenient. Then writing it up against the four criteria. The laboratory hour is a small fraction of the investigation's work, and almost all the assessed thinking happens either side of it.

For the examined components, a shared screen is often better than a table. The Paper 1 data-analysis section is a paper exercise: the data is printed, the graph is drawn on paper, and the reasoning is written. Working through it with the paper, the markscheme and the student's own attempt visible simultaneously, with the session recorded for revision, is a format that suits the task. The same applies to Paper 2 extended responses, where the useful work is reading what the student wrote and showing where the reasoning chain broke.

IB Gram's position, stated plainly: lessons for UAE families are one-to-one online over live video. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai and does not dispatch tutors to UAE addresses. Home visiting is an India-only service. A family that specifically needs a person in the room should hire locally for that and should still exhaust the free layer and ask the verification questions below before paying anything.
bullets: Laboratory work belongs to the school, with its equipment and supervision
Method design before the lab is what stops a wasted session at the bench
Data processing, uncertainty propagation and write-up are all screen work
Paper 1 data analysis is a paper exercise and suits a shared screen well

sections.heading: Travel premium, Al Sufouh geography and what the extra money buys
paragraphs: A family comparing an in-home quote with an online one in this catchment is comparing two different products at overlapping prices. The published in-home band is AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel. The online specialist band is AED 200 to AED 450 and above. The overlap is almost total, so the comparison is not about money so much as about what the money selects for.

The geography is specific. Al Sufouh is a narrow strip, and a tutor working in-home across New Dubai loses real time to the drive between Knowledge Park, Al Barsha and the Greens. That caps their day at two or three students and it has to be recovered inside the rate. It also makes the arrangement fragile in a way that matters for a two-year course: one closure on Al Sufouh Road and the session is cancelled, shortened or rescheduled, and a Diploma physics plan that loses four sessions a term loses a theme.

What the premium buys is presence, and presence is genuinely valuable in some cases. A student who will not engage with a screen, or a household where supervision rather than teaching is the real requirement, should buy it. What it does not buy is the Higher Level fields and quantum specialist, or the person who has marked a top-band evaluation. Those people are not distributed across Al Sufouh, the Greens and Media City in proportion to demand; they are distributed across the whole market.

Set against the themes themselves, the trade becomes clearer. Physics at Higher Level asks for depth in fields and in quantum physics that a generalist science tutor may never have taught. Restricting the search to driving distance narrows the pool at exactly the point where narrowing hurts most. Removing the travel constraint widens it, and the travel component of the rate, somewhere between AED 50 and AED 150 an hour on published bands, simply stops being charged.

sections.heading: The permit, the claim and the receipt
paragraphs: Three verification steps, all free, and the reason the cheapest end of this market is not always the safest. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Because it is free, a quote itemising a licensing charge should be questioned.

Note what that eligibility list means at the bottom rung of the rate ladder. University students are explicitly eligible, so a tutor charging at the bottom of the band can be entirely legitimate. What is not legitimate is tutoring without the permit, and individuals doing so are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone. A separate rule applies to school staff: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school.

The second step is the claim. IB Gram holds no accreditation from the IB, from Cambridge, from Pearson, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, and claims none. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That is a numbered document. Any provider calling itself approved should produce it. Equally, nobody should be described as an IB examiner unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status should never be presented as access to marking or boundaries.

The third step is the receipt on numbers. Ask where a quoted figure came from and when it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched in this cluster publish no price at all, two quote in US dollars, and one publishes a structured-data price range that contradicts the figure on its own page. Separately, any statistic offered without a sample size, a date and a method should be disregarded, which includes satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and tutor headcounts. None appear on this page for that reason.
bullets: The MoHRE private tuition permit is free of charge and valid for two years
University students are explicitly eligible, so a low rate is not automatically a red flag
No fine schedule is published, so no fine amount should ever be quoted to you
A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a numbered document, not a phrase

sections.heading: Matching the rung to the problem
paragraphs: The practical conclusion of a cheapest-first page is a matching rule rather than a recommendation. Physics problems in this catchment fall into four kinds, and each has a rung that fits it. Confusing them is where money goes.

A missed-content problem, where a student was absent or the teaching moved too fast, needs patience and correct explanation. The budget and mid rungs both do this, and the budget rung does it adequately for Standard Level core content at AED 33 to AED 65 an hour. A coverage problem, where the syllabus is being met but nothing is sticking, needs a teacher who knows the course well enough to sequence it, which is the mid rung from AED 200 for IB.

A technique problem, where the physics is right and the marks are not, needs somebody who knows what the markscheme rewards. That is the specialist rung at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and it is the rung most under-bought in Al Sufouh because the problem is hard to see from a report card. A student scoring five with correct physics is usually losing marks to structure, to incomplete chains, to units and to uncertainty, not to knowledge, and no amount of re-teaching content will move it.

A judgement problem, usually on the investigation's evaluation criterion or on Higher Level fields and quantum questions, is where the top rungs earn their numbers. These are also the shortest engagements: four to six sessions rather than a year. A family that identifies its problem correctly often ends up spending less in total at a higher hourly rate, because the engagement is short and aimed. That is the whole argument of this page compressed into a paragraph.
bullets: Missed content: budget or mid rung, AED 33-300 an hour
No retention despite coverage: mid rung, from AED 200 for IB
Right physics, wrong marks: specialist rung, AED 200-450+
Evaluation and Higher Level depth: top rungs, short and aimed engagements

process.title: Ask the coordinator for level and deadlines in writing
process.description: The DP coordinator can confirm whether your child is entered at Standard or Higher Level and what the school's own internal deadlines are for the scientific investigation. Both are free and both govern the entire support plan. A plan built against a guessed deadline collides with the school's calendar, usually in the worst possible term.

process.title: Read the four investigation criteria before buying anything
process.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. The school holds the documentation. A student who reads the descriptors before designing an experiment behaves differently from one who reads them after writing it up, and that difference is worth more than several paid hours.

process.title: Send one unmarked timed paper
process.description: An unmarked mock is diagnostic material. A marked one has usually already been converted into a score and a reassurance. Send the paper as the student produced it, and the first session can categorise the losses into content, technique, uncertainty and timing rather than counting them.

process.title: Take the free trial on the component that scores worst
process.description: One lesson, one subject, before any payment is taken. Spend it on Paper 2 extended response or on the investigation's evaluation section if that is where the marks go, rather than on comfortable content. The trial exists to test whether this tutor can move the hard thing.

process.title: Pick the rung that matches the problem, then stop
process.description: Missed content is a budget or mid-rung job. Right physics scoring badly is a specialist job. Evaluation structure and Higher Level depth are short, aimed engagements at the top rungs. Identifying the problem correctly often costs less in total at a higher hourly rate, because the engagement ends.

whyPoints.title: Rates presented cheapest first
whyPoints.description: The market ladder on this page runs upward from AED 33 an hour, with each rung attributed to the provider who published it and read in October 2026. Presenting cost in ascending order lets a family stop at the rung that solves their problem rather than starting at the one a brochure opens with.

whyPoints.title: The free layer named before any purchase
whyPoints.description: Published investigation criteria, the DP coordinator's confirmation of level and deadlines, the school's own clinic, one unmarked mock and the official documentation cost nothing. Several Al Sufouh families who use all five find they do not need to buy anything, and saying so is part of giving honest advice.

whyPoints.title: Matched to level and to the current guide
whyPoints.description: Physics is matched to Standard or Higher Level and to a tutor who has taught the current five-theme structure rather than the previous syllabus with its separate options. A tutor planning against a structure that no longer exists will teach material the papers no longer ask for.

whyPoints.title: Investigation support that works to the descriptors
whyPoints.description: Feedback references research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation by name, with their six-mark allocations. Evaluation is where marks are most often left on the table, and it is the criterion most improvable in a short block. The boundary on what a tutor will not do is stated at the first session.

whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is offered only in India. Laboratory work belongs to the school, and no tutoring arrangement here claims otherwise.

whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentage, no star rating, no tutor headcount and no IB examination date appears on this page. IB dates could not be confirmed from the IB's own published source at the time of writing, so session planning here is relative and a family should confirm dates with the school's coordinator.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful thing I can buy for IB physics in Al Sufouh?
faqs.answer: One diagnostic hour built around a mock paper or an investigation draft the student has already produced, sent unmarked in advance. It ends in a written readout categorising the losses into content, technique, uncertainty handling and timing. At the mid-market band that is AED 200 to AED 300 for a single session. Several families stop there, because the readout shows the problem is covered by the school's own clinic or by two hours of work on one component rather than by a term of weekly tuition.

faqs.question: Can a university-student tutor at AED 45 an hour actually help with Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes. If a Standard Level student missed three weeks of theme A and needs patient re-teaching of kinematics, a capable undergraduate working from the student's own materials is a sensible purchase, and MoHRE's permit eligibility explicitly includes university students. What the bottom rung generally cannot do is diagnose: it answers the question asked rather than identifying the question that should have been asked, and it will not mark an extended response against examiner expectations. Those are different jobs at different rates.

faqs.question: How is IB physics assessed, and which component deserves the tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent and holds the extended-response work. The scientific investigation carries twenty. Paper 2 is the largest single component and extended-response technique is both teachable and frequently untaught, so a marginal hour usually pays best there. The Paper 1 data-analysis section is the most neglected part of the course and the most trainable, which makes three or four sessions on it high-return work.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria on the DP physics investigation and what is each worth?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks for a total of twenty-four, together making twenty per cent of the final grade. Equal weighting is the fact students most often fail to act on: effort concentrates on data collection while evaluation, worth exactly the same six marks, is left as an afterthought. Confirm the current descriptors with your school, which holds the documentation, and read them before designing the experiment rather than after writing it up.

faqs.question: Why do students lose so many marks on the evaluation section?
faqs.answer: Because they write it as apology rather than analysis. The habitual version is a list of things that went wrong with human error at the top. What the criterion asks is which weaknesses materially affected the result, how large that effect plausibly was, and what a redesigned method would do about it. That shift is a change of approach rather than a knowledge gain, it is teachable in two or three sessions, and it is worth up to six marks of a twenty-four-mark component that carries a fifth of the grade.

faqs.question: How does online physics tuition handle laboratory work for an Al Sufouh student?
faqs.answer: Laboratory work belongs to the school, which holds the equipment, the technician support and the supervision requirement. Tutoring covers everything either side of the bench: designing the method so the laboratory hour produces usable data, choosing ranges and repeats, then processing the data, propagating uncertainties, deciding whether a point is genuinely anomalous and writing up against the four criteria. The assessed thinking happens mostly before and after the practical, and almost all of it is screen work.

faqs.question: Is a Higher Level physics tutor different from a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is worth asking directly. Standard and Higher Level share a core, and a tutor comfortable with the core can teach Standard Level well. Higher Level extends several themes, with the fields and the nuclear and quantum content being where generalist science tutors most often run out. Specialist rates of AED 200 to AED 450 and above exist largely because that experience is scarcer. For Standard Level core content, paying specialist rates is usually unnecessary.

faqs.question: My child's physics is correct but the marks are low. What am I buying?
faqs.answer: Technique, not content, and that is a specialist purchase rather than a cheap one. A student writing correct physics and scoring in the middle is normally losing marks to incomplete reasoning chains, to answers that state a relationship without applying it to the situation the question built, to dropped units, and to inconsistent precision. Re-teaching content will not move any of that. What moves it is somebody reading what the student actually wrote and showing where the chain broke, repeatedly, against the markscheme.

faqs.question: Does my child need a physics tutor if the school runs a science clinic?
faqs.answer: Often not for the same content. School clinics, intervention groups and after-school science sessions are inside the fees already paid, and a private tutor repeating Thursday's clinic material is delivering free provision a second time. One email to the subject teacher establishes what is running and whether your child is already listed. In this catchment that email regularly removes a weekly paid session, which is AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the mid band. Private support should cover what the school is not covering.

faqs.question: What time can an Al Sufouh Diploma physics session realistically start?
faqs.answer: School days here finish roughly between two o'clock and half past three depending on the school and the phase, and most Diploma students have a creativity, activity and service commitment, a clinic or a fixture afterwards. A student walking home within Al Sufouh can be at a desk by half past four. A household commuting back to Media City, Internet City or Al Barsha is realistically available from six. Online slots run into the evening in Gulf Standard Time and can move post-Iftar during Ramadan.

faqs.question: Is an in-home physics tutor in Al Sufouh worth the published premium?
faqs.answer: The in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel overlaps almost entirely with the online specialist band of AED 200 to AED 450 and above, so the choice is about what the money selects for rather than about the money. Presence is genuinely valuable for a student who will not engage with a screen. What it does not buy is the Higher Level fields and quantum specialist, because those people are distributed across the whole market rather than across New Dubai. IB Gram delivers UAE lessons online only.

faqs.question: Does a physics tutor in Dubai need a permit, and can a teacher tutor my child?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and costs nothing: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Individuals tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. On teachers: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school.

faqs.question: How many sessions does Paper 2 extended response actually take to improve?
faqs.answer: Six to ten in most cases, because it is a habit rather than a fact. The work is repetitive by design: the student writes a response, the tutor reads it against the markscheme, and the two of them locate the step where the reasoning chain stopped. Early sessions usually reveal the same failure repeatedly, which is a good sign rather than a bad one. Paper 2 carries forty-four per cent of the grade, so this is the component where a block of sessions has the largest arithmetic effect.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a physics Extended Essay as well as the investigation?
faqs.answer: Within the same boundary, yes. A tutor can discuss whether a research question is feasible and appropriately scoped, question a method, ask what the data supports, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, draft, complete or produce the essay, and should not edit it until the voice is no longer the student's. The school appoints the Extended Essay supervisor and the student signs any authenticity declaration. A student carrying both plus Higher Level physics has a calendar problem worth planning in Year 12.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level physics specialist is free for our slot?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a timescale, rather than matched with somebody approximate. Higher Level fields and quantum physics is one of the scarcer teaching specialisms in this market. Where no match is free at an Al Sufouh-friendly hour, the realistic options are a tutor in another time zone covering an evening slot in Gulf Standard Time, a short wait with a named date, or one diagnostic hour with a strong generalist to establish precisely what the specialist will be needed for. Disclosure beats a poor match.

faqs.question: Should I buy a bundle of past papers and markschemes from a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: No. Syllabus documents, past papers, markschemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB and to the awarding bodies, and reproducing them as downloads is copyright infringement. For unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. A legitimate tutor references them, cites the official source and links out, and works from material the school already holds. If a provider offers a paper bundle as a selling point, the right question is where it came from and who authorised its distribution.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingHeading: Spend nothing first, then buy the rung that fits
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-sufouh.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB physics tutor in Al Sufouh, work upwards. Get the level and the internal deadlines in writing from the DP coordinator. Read the four investigation criteria. Ask the subject teacher what the school already runs. Have your child sit one timed paper and leave it unmarked. Then book the free trial lesson, one subject, no payment taken beforehand, and use the readout to pick the rung that matches the actual problem. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-twar.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors teaching Diploma physics at Higher and Standard Level to students in Al Twar, Al Qusais and Mirdif, on the current guide, including supervision of the Scientific Investigation.

intro.heading: How many physics hours does an Al Twar family actually need to buy?
paragraphs: Physics is unusual among Diploma subjects in that the spending question has a reasonably definite answer. Most lost marks trace to a short list of repeatable faults: units dropped or converted wrongly, an equation rearranged after substitution rather than before, a vector treated as a scalar, a diagram not drawn, an answer given to an accuracy the data does not support. Each is diagnosable in one session and fixable in three or four. That makes physics a subject where you can plan hours rather than buy them indefinitely.

The second structural fact is the weighting. Paper 2 carries about 44 per cent of the grade, Paper 1 about 36 per cent across its multiple-choice and data-based sections, and the Scientific Investigation about 20 per cent at both Standard and Higher Level. A fifth of the grade therefore sits in one piece of coursework that most families treat as a side project, while the data-based section of Paper 1 is rarely drilled separately in school. Those two facts tell you where hours are worth most before you have spoken to anybody.

Now the prices, with their sources, read in October 2026. IB and IGCSE specialists in Dubai are published at roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 survey agreeing on the band. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Budget and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52. In-home one-to-one, which carries travel inside the rate, is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. BartyED advertises AED 650 at the premium end.

Put the hours and the rates together and you get a budget rather than a commitment. A diagnostic block of four sessions at the specialist band is roughly AED 800 to 1,800. A term of weekly work at the mid band is about AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's monthly estimates. A dated run of ten sessions before the examination series is somewhere between AED 2,000 and 4,500. Those are numbers a household can decide about in advance, which is the entire argument of this page.

One thing to be clear about. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Physics tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for free-body diagrams, graph work and marked past papers. For a subject whose faults are diagnosed by watching the working appear line by line, a shared screen is the natural medium, and it removes the travel premium that a villa district behind Al Qusais otherwise pays.
