dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-twar.programmesIntro: What physics costs depends on which stage your child is at, because the work changes completely between them. These are the four stages for an Al Twar student.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Assessed by two written papers and one Scientific Investigation. Content is organised around space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds depth inside each theme rather than a third paper.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster the spending pattern is predictable: families buy nothing in DP1 autumn, when a weekly hour would be cheapest and most effective, and then buy expensively in DP2 spring. Shifting even a quarter of that spend a year earlier changes the result more than increasing it would.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences before physics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria rather than by paper: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Physics appears as a strand before separating out in the later years at most schools.
programmes.countryNote: An Al Twar student arriving in DP1 physics from MYP usually has good investigation instincts and insufficient calculation volume. That is a cheap gap to close in the summer before DP1, at the budget or mid band, and an expensive one to discover in October.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 give a solid grounding in forces, energy, waves, electricity and radioactivity. Neither covers the vector treatment, calculus-adjacent reasoning or field theory depth that Higher Level physics assumes early.
programmes.countryNote: Students who found Extended IGCSE physics straightforward are frequently advised towards Higher Level, and some should be taking Standard Level. The honest test is whether algebraic rearrangement is automatic, because Higher Level physics offers no time to think about the algebra and the physics at once.

programmes.name: The Scientific Investigation
programmes.description: One independent investigation that the student designs, performs, analyses and writes up, internally assessed and externally moderated, worth about a fifth of the grade at both levels. Uncertainty treatment and the quality of the evaluation drive the mark.
programmes.countryNote: This is where cost and timing interact most sharply. Supervision bought three months out is cheap and effective; bought three days out it cannot legitimately achieve much, because the only remaining help would cross the academic-honesty line. We will not write or complete any part of it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-twar.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely bought alone, and the combinations matter for cost because some overlaps let one tutor do two jobs. These are the subjects Al Twar families pair with it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two papers plus the Scientific Investigation. Marks go in unit handling, in rearranging after substitution, in treating vectors as scalars, and in answers reported to an accuracy the data cannot support.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most valuable pairing. Rearrangement, trigonometry, gradients and calculus all appear in physics questions, and a physics problem is often a maths problem the student did not recognise as one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Workable alongside physics, with more statistical content and technology throughout. Check specific university prerequisites for engineering and physics degrees, because some express a preference for the analytical route.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The usual third science. Energetics and kinetics share proportional and logarithmic reasoning with physics, and students who struggle in both frequently have one underlying mathematical gap rather than two scientific ones.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Less overlap, but the data-based question style is similar enough that practice in one transfers to the other. A cheap way to get value from a single block of data-question coaching.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Chosen alongside physics by engineering-bound students. Algorithmic discipline helps directly with multi-step physics calculations, where most errors are sequencing rather than arithmetic errors.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Shares the modelling and iteration mindset. For students taking both, the investigation and design project habits reinforce each other, which reduces the total supervision needed.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Often neglected by physics students and directly relevant to the investigation, where the evaluation is an argument rather than a list of what went wrong.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive components, each requiring separate practice. Commonly taken in this cluster and commonly tutored too generally to be worth the money.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the essay. Physics offers unusually good material: the status of a model, what counts as evidence, and why a theory can be useful and still be superseded.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A supervised research essay. Physics titles fail on feasibility rather than difficulty: a question that cannot be investigated with school apparatus becomes a literature review with measurements attached.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and data skills
subjects.description: Propagating uncertainty, choosing graph scales, drawing a line of best fit with error bars and judging whether a result supports a claim. Examined in both papers and in the investigation, and rarely drilled separately.

sections.heading: What a physics grade costs in hours, phase by phase
paragraphs: Because the faults in physics are a short list, the hours can be estimated honestly instead of sold open-ended. A diagnostic block is four sessions: enough to see timed work, identify which of the standard faults is present, and say how much further work it needs. A unit and rearrangement repair, once identified, is typically three or four sessions of drilling before the habit sticks. Vector handling is similar. The data-based section of Paper 1 responds to four or five sets of unfamiliar data, which is one short block.

Larger jobs take longer and are still finite. Repairing a Standard Level foundation in a Higher Level student, which is the commonest underlying problem in DP2, is a term of weekly work rather than a block, because the gaps are distributed across several themes. Investigation supervision is five or six sessions spread across months, concentrated at the question stage and the evaluation stage. Full-paper technique before the examination series is eight to twelve sessions with marked timed papers.

Multiply those by the published bands and you have a budget. At the mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, a four-session diagnostic is roughly AED 600 to 1,200; at the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 it is AED 800 to 1,800. A term of weekly mid-band work is AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's monthly estimates. A ten-session examination block is AED 2,000 to 4,500 depending on band. Those are decidable numbers, and a provider who cannot give you an hours estimate for a named fault is asking you to buy time rather than a result.

The table sets this out as jobs rather than as a package. Treat the hour counts as what we would expect rather than a promise, because a student is not a machine and a four-session estimate occasionally turns out to be six. What we will not do is decline to estimate, because that is how an open-ended arrangement becomes a standing cost nobody reviews.

sections.heading: Where the hours actually go in Diploma physics
paragraphs: Mechanics absorbs the most hours in DP1 and the reason is almost always the free-body diagram. Students who do not draw one attempt to reason about forces in their heads, and get the right physics with the wrong signs. Insisting on a diagram before any algebra is a small habit with a large effect, and it is the kind of thing a tutor installs rather than teaches. Three sessions, applied rigorously, and a whole category of error disappears.

Fields are where Higher Level students lose confidence, and the cause is usually not the fields. It is that gravitational, electric and magnetic field questions all assume fluency with inverse-square reasoning, with potential as a scalar against field as a vector, and with graph interpretation, and a student whose mechanics foundation was shaky arrives without that fluency. Buying field tuition for a student with a mechanics problem is the most expensive diagnostic error in this subject.

The data-based section of Paper 1 is the cheapest marks available and the least drilled. Students meet an unfamiliar experiment under time pressure, and describe the table in front of them instead of using it to answer the question asked. Four or five sets of unfamiliar data, marked properly, changes performance on this section inside a month. Schools rarely have time for it because it sits across topics rather than inside one, which is precisely why a tutor should.

Nuclear and quantum content is usually the cheapest part of the course to teach, because it is more modular and less dependent on what came before. A student who is behind in DP2 often does better to secure these themes properly while repairing mechanics in parallel, rather than attempting to rebuild the course in order. That sequencing judgement is itself what a diagnostic session is for, and it is the difference between a term of hours that works and a term that merely happens.

sections.heading: A two-year physics spend that puts the money where it works
paragraphs: The spending pattern in this district is consistent and consistently wrong. Families buy nothing in DP1 autumn, a little in DP1 spring, more in DP2 autumn, and a great deal in DP2 spring at the highest band available. The effectiveness runs in the opposite direction. A weekly hour in DP1 autumn prevents the problem that the DP2 spring block is trying to rescue, and it costs less because there is no urgency premium and no triage.

The strongest argument for front-loading is specific to physics. The faults are habits, and habits take weeks of repetition to change rather than hours of explanation. A student drilled on unit discipline in October has fourteen months of practice reinforcing it before the papers. The same drilling in March has six weeks, which is enough to know the rule and not enough for it to survive the pressure of a timed paper. You are buying time for a habit to form, and that is the one thing money cannot compress.

The second place to concentrate spend is the investigation window, which runs from DP1 summer into DP2 autumn in most schools. A fifth of the grade is decided there, and the supervision that matters is early. Narrowing the research question until the available apparatus can answer it is one session with outsized consequences; everything after that is cheaper because the project is sound.

What deserves less money than it usually gets is the final six weeks. A scoped block of eight to twelve sessions on paper technique is defensible. An open-ended daily arrangement at the premium band is a purchase made out of anxiety, and the honest thing a tutor can tell you at that point is what is still recoverable and what is not. The table sets out the distribution we would recommend, which is deliberately heavier at the start than most families find comfortable.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation, and the cost of leaving it late
paragraphs: A fifth of your child's physics grade comes from one investigation they design, perform, analyse and write up themselves. The economics of supervising it are unusual, because the value of help falls sharply with time rather than rising. Early, a tutor can question a research question until the available apparatus can actually answer it, which is the single highest-value intervention in the component. Late, the only remaining help would be producing work that must be the student's own, and we will not do that at any price.

In physics specifically, two things decide the mark more than the topic does. The first is the uncertainty treatment: whether the student can say how precisely each quantity was measured, propagate that through the calculation, and represent it on a graph with error bars that mean something. The second is the evaluation, where students write apologies listing everything that went wrong instead of judging which weakness actually affected the conclusion, by how much, and in which direction.

Both are teachable in general terms without touching the student's own work, which is what legitimate supervision looks like. A tutor can explain propagation on a worked example of their own, show what a defensible evaluation paragraph does, and then read the student's draft and point out where a claim is not supported by the data in front of it. What a tutor may not do is supply a method, process data the student did not collect, write or rewrite any section, or edit the report to completion.

We state this to students at the first investigation session rather than leaving it in a footnote, because a seventeen-year-old under deadline pressure deserves a clear line rather than an implied one. IB academic-honesty rules make this a malpractice question, and a malpractice finding falls on the student and can reach the whole Diploma. Any service offering to write an investigation is selling a risk dressed as a shortcut, and it is worth remembering that a competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

sections.heading: Group, pair or one-to-one for physics
paragraphs: Physics divides unusually cleanly on this question, which makes it one of the better subjects for reducing cost intelligently. Content teaching and worked examples transfer well to a small group, because a well-chosen example answers the same question for everybody in the room. Fault diagnosis does not transfer at all, because the fault is in one student's working and finding it requires watching that student work.

So the efficient pattern for a cost-conscious Al Twar family is mixed rather than uniform. Use a matched pair or small group for content and worked examples, where the per-student rate falls substantially. Use one-to-one for the diagnostic block and for the investigation, where the whole value is individual. Families who buy one-to-one for everything spend more than they need; families who buy group for everything never find out why their child keeps losing marks.

The condition on the group half of that is strict. The students must be on the same level, working on the same papers, at roughly the same point. A group assembled because three Al Twar families all want physics help will run at the pace of its least prepared member while every family pays, and the Higher Level student in it will learn nothing. Ask who else is in the group, at what level, and what they are working on, before agreeing.

A note on tuition centres, which sit lower again on price. A centre class is structured delivery to a room, which is a legitimate product and not a substitute for diagnosis. Note also that a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

sections.heading: Three places Al Twar families waste physics money
paragraphs: The first is buying field tuition for a mechanics problem. A Higher Level student struggling with gravitational or electric fields very often has an unrepaired mechanics foundation, and teaching fields on top of it produces a student who can quote the inverse-square relationship and still cannot resolve a force. This is the misdiagnosis that costs most in physics, and it persists because the student names the topic they are currently failing rather than the one that caused it. A diagnostic block of four sessions prevents a term of it.

The second is the late investigation purchase. Supervision bought three months before the internal deadline is cheap and decisive; bought in the final fortnight it cannot legitimately achieve much, because the useful interventions have passed and the remaining ones would cross the honesty line. Families spend at the premium band at exactly the moment a tutor can do least, which is a predictable outcome of leaving a component worth a fifth of the grade until last.

The third is paying specialist rates for supervised practice. A tutor at the specialist band watching a student work through problems they could complete alone is an expensive study companion. If the problem is that the work does not get done, the honest answer is a budget-tier tutor, a structured routine, or a conversation that has nothing to do with physics. Separating will not from cannot before booking is the single most useful thing a parent can do with ten minutes.

A fourth, smaller one is worth naming for this district specifically. In-home arrangements in Al Twar carry the travel premium and a hard stop, because the tutor has another appointment across the city. The last ten minutes of a physics session, where a student finally asks about the thing they did not understand two weeks ago, is where a surprising amount of the value sits, and it is the part that gets cut when the car is waiting.

sections.heading: Physics tutor coverage near Al Twar, and the honest fallback
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit, so here is ours. Diploma physics at Standard Level is reasonably well covered by UAE-based tutors. Higher Level physics with a specific need in fields or quantum content is thinner. Investigation supervision with real physics experience is thinner again, and an Extended Essay supervisor in physics is the scarcest of the four. Telling a parent that before they book is worth more than a reassuring sentence that falls apart in week two.

The rule we apply is the same on every UAE page. If a UAE-based tutor covers the subject and level, that is the match, because the school calendar and the time zone already align. If no UAE-based specialist is free for the specific requirement, we say so and offer a tutor from the wider pool working Gulf Standard Time at the same rate band, with the position disclosed before you commit. What we will not do is quietly place a tutor whose availability rather than expertise made them the match.

There is a cost consequence worth stating. The reason a nearby shortlist is expensive is that it is short. In-home physics arrangements in Al Twar draw only on tutors willing to make the drive, and for Higher Level work that list can collapse to one name, at which point the rate reflects availability rather than expertise. Matching on the subject and delivering over video keeps the list long, which is where the price discipline comes from.

The table gives coverage honestly, including the cases where matching takes longer. The time estimates are what we aim for rather than promises, because availability moves week to week and a number that reads well is worth less than a range we can meet.

sections.heading: What an Al Twar parent can establish free before spending anything
paragraphs: Four checks cost nothing and reliably reduce what you need to spend. The first is the school. Your child's IB coordinator will say which component is costing marks, when the internal deadlines for the investigation fall, and when the mocks are. That is the diagnostic information a physics plan should be built on, and buying hours without it is how a family funds the wrong theme for a term.

The second is the fault list in this page. Ask your child to show you a marked paper and look for the pattern yourself: dropped units, rearrangement after substitution, a missing diagram, an answer to four significant figures from two-figure data. You are not marking the physics, you are looking for repetition. A parent who can say which fault recurs has already done the work a first diagnostic session would do, and can buy a shorter block.

The third is the permit, which is free and therefore a clean honesty test. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted at you.

The fourth is the claim check. Nobody offering you private physics tutoring is accredited, approved or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or the IB to do it. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and occupies no UAE premises. Treat any rating, student count or success percentage published without a sample size, a date and a method as decoration: pages in this market show different ratings in different places on the same page. A provider that cannot be accurate about its own arithmetic should not be trusted on diagnosis.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours does a Diploma physics grade actually take?
faqs.answer: More predictably than parents expect, because the faults are a short list. A diagnostic block is four sessions. Repairing unit handling and rearrangement is typically three or four more. Vector discipline is about three. The data-based section of Paper 1 responds to four or five sets of unfamiliar data. A Standard Level foundation repair inside a Higher Level student is a term of weekly work. Full-paper technique before the series is eight to twelve sessions. Any provider unwilling to estimate is asking you to buy time rather than a result.

faqs.question: What does an IB physics tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers: IB and IGCSE specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's survey agreeing; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; budget and university-student tutors from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and up to AED 500 independently; and BartyED at AED 650. None of these is an IB Gram price.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to our home in Al Twar?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram provides no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Physics tuition for an Al Twar family is delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen for free-body diagrams, graph work and marked past papers. For physics that medium suits the diagnosis, because faults are found by watching working appear line by line, and it removes the travel premium a villa district behind Al Qusais otherwise pays twice a week.

faqs.question: My son is failing fields at Higher Level. Do we buy fields tuition?
faqs.answer: Probably not first. Field questions assume fluency with inverse-square reasoning, with potential as a scalar against field as a vector, and with graph interpretation, all of which rest on a secure mechanics foundation. A Higher Level student struggling with fields very often has unrepaired mechanics, and teaching fields on top produces a student who can quote relationships and cannot resolve a force. A four-session diagnostic with timed work establishes which it is, and prevents a term spent on the wrong theme.

faqs.question: Which phase of the two years deserves most of the budget?
faqs.answer: DP1 autumn, which is when almost nobody spends. The faults in physics are habits, and a habit needs months of reinforcement rather than hours of explanation. A student drilled on unit discipline in October has over a year of practice behind it by the papers; the same drilling in March has six weeks, enough to know the rule and not enough for it to survive a timed paper. The second priority is the investigation window, where early question-narrowing decides a fifth of the grade.

faqs.question: How much of the physics grade is the investigation worth?
faqs.answer: About a fifth at both Standard and Higher Level, which makes it the largest single assessment object in the course and the one most families resource last. Paper 2 carries about 44 per cent and Paper 1 about 36 per cent across its multiple-choice and data-based sections. Confirm the exact figures with your child's subject guide or IB coordinator, because assessment detail is revised between guides and the IB publishes the authoritative version rather than any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Can we pay for help finishing the investigation the week before it is due?
faqs.answer: No, and the economics of this component run backwards to most purchases. Early help is cheap and decisive: questioning a research question until the available apparatus can answer it is one session with outsized consequences. Late, the useful interventions have passed and the remaining ones would involve producing work that must be the student's own. We will not write, draft, process data for or complete any part of it. A malpractice finding falls on the student and can reach the whole Diploma.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter get the physics right and the answer wrong?
faqs.answer: Four causes account for most of it, and all are habits rather than knowledge. Units dropped or converted at the wrong point. An equation rearranged after substituting numbers rather than before, which hides a sign error. A vector treated as a scalar, usually because no diagram was drawn. And a final answer reported to a precision the data does not support. Each is diagnosable in one session with timed work and fixable in three or four, which is why a diagnostic block is the right first purchase.

faqs.question: Is group physics tutoring a sensible way to reduce cost?
faqs.answer: For part of the job, yes. Content teaching and worked examples transfer well to a matched pair or small group, because one well-chosen example answers the same question for everybody. Fault diagnosis does not transfer at all, since the fault sits in one student's working. The efficient pattern is mixed: group for content, one-to-one for the diagnostic block and the investigation. The condition is that the group is genuinely matched on level and papers, which is the thing to ask about before agreeing.

faqs.question: Should we drop to Standard Level physics instead of paying for tutoring?
faqs.answer: It is a legitimate question and the school is the right place to ask it, not a tutor with hours to sell. The honest test is whether the Higher Level difficulty is a repairable gap or a consistent ceiling. A student held back by an identifiable fault, such as rearrangement or vector handling, is a repair case. A student for whom the pace of Higher Level is consistently out of reach may do better at Standard Level with a higher grade. A diagnostic block gives you evidence to take into that conversation.

faqs.question: Is a budget tutor ever adequate for Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: For specific jobs, yes. Marking practice sets, drilling recall of definitions and relationships, and keeping work moving between specialist sessions are all tasks a careful tutor at the published budget band of AED 45 to 150 can do properly. What that band rarely buys is diagnosis, which is the ability to identify which of four look-alike faults is present from the first wrong line. Many families get the best result by mixing bands rather than buying entirely at one end.

faqs.question: What is the Paper 1 data-based section and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: It is the part of Paper 1 that presents an unfamiliar experiment and asks the student to interpret the data rather than recall anything. It matters because it is almost never drilled separately in school, since it sits across topics instead of inside one, and because students default to describing the table in front of them rather than using it to answer the question. Four or five sets of unfamiliar data, marked properly, change performance here inside a month. They are the cheapest marks in the course.

faqs.question: Does an in-home physics tutor in Al Twar cost more for a reason?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is travel rather than teaching. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online tutors. A tutor coming to Al Twar from central Dubai at the evening peak spends forty to sixty minutes each way. There is also a quieter cost: the hard stop for their next appointment usually removes the last ten minutes, which in physics is often when the real question finally gets asked.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a physics tutor can diagnose?
faqs.answer: Ask for a timed question in the trial lesson, then watch the thirty seconds after your child gets something wrong. A tutor who re-explains the topic has given you company. A tutor who asks a question designed to establish whether the fault is units, rearrangement order, a vector treated as a scalar or a precision error has given you diagnosis. Then ask what the first four sessions would contain; a named fault and an hours estimate is a plan, while a list of themes is just the syllabus.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take physics and maths together?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and when they can it is genuinely efficient, because a large share of physics losses are mathematical: rearrangement, trigonometry, gradients and standard form. A tutor who sees that treats the cause rather than the symptom. The honest caveat is availability: physics with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in one tutor is a limited match in the UAE-based pool, and we will tell you whether we are offering that or two tutors rather than leaving you to find out.

faqs.question: Is the private tutoring permit expensive for the tutor?
faqs.answer: It costs nothing, which is why asking about it is a useful test. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

intro.heading: Is there anybody near Al Warqa who knows IB Physics properly?
paragraphs: Taken literally, the answer is probably not, and it is worth explaining why rather than arguing with the question. Al Warqa has no IB school inside it. The schools immediately around the community, in Al Warqa'a and Al Qusais, are largely CBSE and British. The nearest IB Diploma teaching sits in Mirdif and Dubai Festival City, twenty to thirty minutes away at pickup time, and teachers at those schools cannot be paid to tutor students enrolled there. So the resident pool of people within a short drive who teach Diploma physics at Higher Level is genuinely tiny.

The second part of the answer is harder and more useful. Knowing physics and knowing this physics course are different things, and the gap widened when the syllabus was revised. The current guide organises content into five themes rather than the old topic-plus-options structure, removes the optional units and the third paper, and replaces the old practical scheme with a single scientific investigation assessed on four criteria. A physicist who last taught the previous version will teach your child content they no longer need and miss the structure they are actually assessed against.

That gives a parent a practical test, and it takes thirty seconds. Ask which theme covers fields, how many papers there are at Higher Level, and what the four investigation criteria are called. A tutor currently teaching this course answers instantly. One who mentions options, or a Paper 3, is describing a syllabus your child is not sitting. That question is worth more than any list of degrees, and it is the one almost nobody asks.

On delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Al Warqa physics lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format is well matched to the work, because most dropped physics marks are in graphs, uncertainties and written explanation, all of which are better addressed with a student's own script on a shared screen and a mark scheme open beside it.

The rest of this page is written so the test can be applied. The five themes and what sits in each. Paper weightings and durations. The content that exists only at Higher Level, which is where a mismatched tutor becomes obvious. The investigation criteria with their mark allocations. Where marks actually go, specifically rather than generally. And an honest account of availability, including how long a Higher Level match usually takes and what happens when nobody suitable is free. Everything here is checkable against the subject guide your child's school works from, and it should be: a tutoring page is not an authority on an IB syllabus, and the school's own documents and the IB coordinator are. What a page like this can usefully do is give a parent the vocabulary to ask better questions, so the first paid hour starts from a diagnosis rather than from a conversation about how physics makes a teenager feel.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-warqa.programmesIntro: Physics support for Al Warqa families spans three stages, and the handover between MYP Sciences and Diploma Physics is where most avoidable difficulty appears. These notes say what each stage assesses.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Available at Higher and Standard Level, with content organised into five themes and assessed by two written papers plus the scientific investigation, which carries twenty per cent. Higher Level includes additional content within each theme rather than separate units, so the depth increases across the whole course rather than in one bolt-on section.
programmes.countryNote: Al Warqa Diploma physicists travel to Mirdif or Festival City, which puts a realistic session at 17:15 or later. Physics tolerates a late start better than mathematics does for recall work, and worse for anything involving unfamiliar derivation, so the slot should be chosen with the week's topic in mind.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria each marked 0 to 8: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. There is no external examination, and the report grade is a conversion from criterion totals rather than a test average.
programmes.countryNote: Criterion B is the direct ancestor of the Diploma investigation's research design criterion, and criterion C of its data analysis. A student with weak B and C in MYP 5 will meet the same weakness in the Diploma investigation eighteen months later, which is the cheapest predictable problem to fix early in this whole subject.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics, as the other route in
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1, tiered Core and Extended in Cambridge, with either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Many Al Warqa students arrive in Diploma Physics from this route rather than from MYP, and the gap is different in character.
programmes.countryNote: An IGCSE Extended candidate arrives with strong recall and calculation and no experience of extended written explanation or of designing an investigation. Four to eight weeks of focused work usually covers it, provided somebody names the gap rather than assuming the transition takes care of itself.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. A student can take Diploma Physics within it, which keeps the subject and its assessment intact while reducing the total load.
programmes.countryNote: Named here because a student struggling with Higher Level Physics inside a full six-subject Diploma has options besides buying more physics hours, including dropping to Standard Level. A tutor who never raises either is selling time rather than advising.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-warqa.subjectsIntro: Physics is one subject and five themes, and a tutor needs to know which theme your child is currently in. These notes name each theme and where marks go inside it.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, with rigid body mechanics and relativity extending the theme at Higher Level. Marks go on free-body diagrams drawn carelessly and on momentum problems where the system is never defined, both of which are habit faults.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, current and circuits. The recurring loss is circuit analysis under time pressure: students who can state Kirchhoff's laws cannot apply them to an unfamiliar network, which is a practice problem rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave models, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with further treatment at Higher Level. Phase relationships and the distinction between intensity and amplitude are where answers go wrong consistently.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential and induction, with substantially more at Higher Level including field and potential gradients. This is the theme where Higher Level depth is most visible, and the one a tutor teaching the old syllabus will organise incorrectly.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Structure of the atom, radioactive decay, fission and fusion, with quantum physics and nuclear binding extended at Higher Level. Decay calculations are straightforward; the extended explanation questions about models and evidence are where marks are lost.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error analysis
subjects.levels: HL and SL, across all themes
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty in gradients. Examined throughout rather than as a topic, which is why students who have never been taught it properly lose marks on every paper rather than in one place.

subjects.name: Graph work and data analysis
subjects.description: Linearising relationships, reading gradients from axis values, error bars and lines of maximum and minimum gradient. The single most reliable source of recoverable marks in the subject, and the one most often treated as a skill students should already have.

subjects.name: Command terms and extended explanation
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, outline, discuss and compare each demand a distinct answer shape. A student who explains when asked to state wastes time; one who states when asked to explain loses the marks entirely. Twenty minutes of teaching and a term of enforcement.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, a single report assessed on four criteria each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The student designs it, runs it, analyses it and writes it. A tutor teaches the criteria and reviews their drafts.

subjects.name: Mathematics for physics
subjects.description: Logarithms, trigonometry, vectors and, for Higher Level, comfort with rearranging multi-variable relationships. Students taking Applications and Interpretation mathematics alongside Higher Level Physics sometimes need explicit support here, and it is rarely identified as the actual problem.

sections.heading: The thirty-second test for whether a tutor knows this syllabus
paragraphs: Ask three questions before anything else. Which theme contains fields? How many written papers are there at Higher Level? What are the four scientific investigation criteria called? Somebody currently teaching this course answers all three without pausing. Somebody who last taught the previous version will reach for topic numbers, mention the optional units, or describe a third paper, and you will have learned in half a minute what a CV would never have told you.

This matters more in physics than in most subjects because the revision was structural rather than cosmetic. Content is now organised into five themes rather than a core plus options. The optional units are gone, and with them the third paper. The old practical scheme, with its separate internal assessment and group project, has been replaced by a single scientific investigation assessed against four criteria worth six marks each. A tutor working from the old structure will spend your money teaching a shape that no longer exists.

The second test is about level. Higher Level physics is not Standard Level with harder questions: additional content sits inside the themes, most visibly in fields, and a tutor comfortable at Standard Level may be genuinely out of their depth at Higher. Ask directly which level they have taught, in which theme, and how recently. A straight answer is worth more than a confident general one.

The third test is about the investigation. Ask what the tutor will not do with it. The right answer arrives immediately and is specific: no design, no data, no analysis, no writing, no editing that changes authorship. A provider who hesitates, or who offers to help produce a report, is offering something that puts an IB registration at risk. Research for these pages found a Dubai provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright, which is malpractice under IB rules and falls on the candidate rather than the seller.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level adds inside each
paragraphs: Theme A, space, time and motion, covers kinematics, forces, momentum and energy, extended at Higher Level into rigid body mechanics and relativity. Theme B, the particulate nature of matter, holds thermal physics, the gas laws and electric circuits. Theme C, wave behaviour, covers simple harmonic motion, wave models, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Theme D, fields, treats gravitational, electric and magnetic fields together with potential and induction. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, covers atomic structure, decay, fission, fusion and quantum ideas.

The structural point for a parent is that Higher Level content sits inside the themes rather than beside them. There is no separate Higher Level section a student can skip to. That changes how support should be sequenced: a Higher Level student weak in theme A mechanics will struggle in theme D fields, because the energy and potential reasoning carries straight across. A tutor who treats the themes as independent modules will produce sessions that each make sense and a student who cannot connect them.

Theme D is where the difference between a competent physicist and a competent IB physics teacher shows most clearly. Fields, potential and induction are taught in many curricula with different emphases and different notation, and the Diploma expects a particular treatment of field and potential gradients and a particular style of explanation. A tutor from another system will teach the physics correctly and the answers wrongly, and the student will not know which part was the problem.

One practical note for Al Warqa families: schools do not all move through the themes in the same order. Before the first session, ask the school which theme is current and which comes next. A tutor consolidating this week's content is worth considerably more than one running a parallel course that arrives at fields three months after the class did.

sections.heading: Papers, weightings and what each one rewards
paragraphs: Both levels sit two written papers plus the investigation. Paper 1 is worth thirty-six per cent and comes in two parts: a multiple-choice section and a data-based and experimental section. Paper 2 is worth forty-four per cent and carries the structured and extended-response questions. The scientific investigation is the remaining twenty per cent. Higher Level papers are longer than Standard Level ones, and the weightings are the same at both levels.

The split matters because the two parts of Paper 1 reward different preparation entirely. The multiple-choice section rewards breadth and speed, and is improved by wide question practice rather than by deep study of any theme. The data-based and experimental section rewards exactly the skills most schools have least time to drill: reading a table, spotting a controlled variable, identifying a source of systematic error, and interpreting a graph that has been linearised.

Paper 2 is where command terms decide the grade. A student who writes a paragraph when asked to state has lost time they needed later in the paper; a student who writes a sentence when asked to explain has lost the marks outright. This is not a knowledge problem and it responds to a term of enforcement rather than to more content. It is also entirely visible on a marked script, which is why two marked papers are the first thing worth sending.

A caution about dates rather than papers. Secondary sources circulate IB examination and results dates, but ibo.org blocks automated access and no IB session date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session. Any specific date your family acts on should come from the school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly, not from a tutoring page, and that includes this one.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the physics grade sits in one report, assessed against four criteria each worth six marks, for twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The student designs the investigation, carries it out, analyses the data and writes the report. Knowing that the four criteria carry equal weight changes how time is spent, because students overwhelmingly over-invest in the practical work and under-invest in evaluation, which is worth exactly as much.

Research design is where most Al Warqa students lose marks, and the cause is almost always scope. A question that cannot produce enough data points, or whose independent variable cannot be varied meaningfully with available equipment, caps the mark before the first measurement is taken. This is also the only criterion that is cheap to fix and impossible to fix late: once the data is collected, a badly scoped question stays badly scoped.

Data analysis rewards correct processing with uncertainties carried through, and graphs that are genuinely interrogated rather than merely drawn. Conclusion rewards an interpretation that engages with accepted physics and with the actual data rather than with what the student hoped to see. Evaluation rewards honest identification of methodological weaknesses and realistic improvements, and it is routinely treated as a closing formality by students who have just spent ten hours on the experiment.

The boundary on support is firm and worth stating in full, because this is the part of the market where providers misbehave. A tutor may teach the four criteria in the examiner's wording, explain what twenty-four marks are made of, question whether a research question can produce analysable data, teach uncertainty propagation and graph technique, and comment on a draft the student has written. No tutor at IB Gram designs an investigation, supplies or processes data, writes a section, or edits until the authorship changes. The report carries the student's own declaration.

sections.heading: Where physics marks actually go in Al Warqa scripts
paragraphs: Uncertainties first, because they are examined everywhere rather than in one place. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products and powers, and uncertainty in a gradient. A student who has never been taught this systematically loses one or two marks on nearly every data question across both papers, and the total is large enough to move a grade while being invisible on any single question.

Graphs second. Gradients measured by counting grid squares rather than reading axis values. Axes without units. Lines of best fit forced through the origin because it feels right. Error bars omitted, or drawn and then ignored when the gradient is extracted. Linearising a relationship so that a straight-line graph can be used at all, which is a specific technique and not an obvious one. All of this is teachable in a handful of sessions and most of it is never taught deliberately.

Command terms third. The extended-response questions on Paper 2 reward a particular shape of answer for each command, and students who have not been shown the difference write what they know rather than what was asked. Explain requires a mechanism; describe requires observable features; outline requires brevity. A term of enforcement with a marked script each week fixes this more reliably than any amount of content revision.

Fourth and least discussed: the mathematics. Higher Level Physics assumes comfort with logarithms, trigonometry and rearranging multi-variable relationships, and a student taking Applications and Interpretation mathematics alongside it sometimes meets a genuine gap. It presents as a physics problem and is not one. Identifying it early saves months of the wrong kind of tutoring, and it is the kind of thing a marked script reveals immediately.

sections.heading: Availability, honestly: how long a physics match actually takes
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics is one of the narrower specialisms in this market, and claiming instant availability would be dishonest. For an Al Warqa family the realistic pattern is this: Standard Level Physics is usually matched within a few days. Higher Level Physics takes a little longer, often up to a week, because the pool of tutors genuinely comfortable with theme D at Higher Level is smaller than the pool who teach physics.

Where a specialist is not free, there are three honest responses and we use all three. Give a date rather than a reassurance, so a family can decide whether to wait. Offer a named alternative where one genuinely helps, such as a Chemistry or Mathematics specialist for a block on uncertainties, graph technique and data analysis, which transfer directly and which many physics students need more than they need theme content. Or decline, which is the right answer when neither applies.

There is a disclosure that belongs here too. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a requirement, the match may be a specialist elsewhere teaching at Gulf Standard Time. That is said before anything is booked rather than discovered later, and it changes nothing about the delivery because the delivery was never going to be in-person in this country. Two competitor pages researched for this project route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without saying so, which is the version of this we are trying not to be.

Finally, the eligibility constraint that reduces apparent supply. A teacher cannot be paid to tutor students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit it explicitly. So the physics teacher at your child's school in Festival City is not an option, however convenient it would be.

sections.heading: How practical physics works when the lessons are online
paragraphs: The question deserves a direct answer rather than reassurance. The practical work for the scientific investigation happens at school, with the school's equipment and under the school's supervision, which is where it belongs and where the student's authorship is visible. Nothing about online tutoring changes that, and no tutor should be involved in collecting the data.

What online support does well is everything around the practical. Pressure-testing the research question before the equipment is booked, so the design can actually produce analysable data. Teaching uncertainty propagation on the student's own measurements. Working through the graph: linearising the relationship, plotting with error bars, extracting a gradient with its uncertainty, and interrogating what the gradient means physically. Then reading the four criteria alongside the student's own draft and asking the questions that produce a real evaluation.

The data-based and experimental section of Paper 1 is, if anything, better taught remotely than in a laboratory. It is a paper exercise: a table, a graph, a described method, and questions about controlled variables, systematic error and interpretation. Working through those with a shared screen and a mark scheme open is precisely the right setting, and it is the section schools have least time to drill because a class of twenty in a laboratory is doing something else.

Where a student genuinely needs hands-on demonstration to understand a concept, the honest position is that online support is a partial fit and the school laboratory is the better place for it. Saying that costs us the occasional enquiry. It is better than taking money for an arrangement that was never going to deliver what the family was imagining, which is a pattern this market has rather too much of.

sections.heading: From MYP Sciences or IGCSE Physics into the Diploma
paragraphs: Two different students arrive in Diploma Physics in Al Warqa, and they need different things. The MYP student has been marked against four criteria, two of which, inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, are direct ancestors of the Diploma investigation's research design and data analysis criteria. If those were weak in MYP 5, they will be weak in the investigation, and that is the single most predictable and cheapest problem to address early in this subject.

The IGCSE student arrives from Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 with a different profile: strong recall, solid calculation, comfortable with structured questions, and no experience of extended written explanation or of designing an investigation from a blank page. Four to eight weeks of focused work usually covers the gap, provided somebody names it. Left unnamed, it shows up as a disappointing first Diploma report that everybody attributes to the course being harder.

A third arrival pattern matters in this community because of the local school mix. Students coming from CBSE physics often have stronger algebraic manipulation and less experience of uncertainty treatment and of writing explanations to a command term. That is a specific, short piece of work, and it is wasted effort to treat it as a general transition difficulty requiring a year of weekly support.

In all three cases the diagnosis comes from marked work rather than from the curriculum the student came from. Two scripts from the first Diploma term show whether the issue is content, uncertainties, graphs, command terms or mathematics, and each of those is a different and much shorter purchase than the open-ended weekly arrangement families usually start with.

whyPoints.description: Uncertainties and graph work are examined across every paper and drilled least at school. A block on propagation, linearising and gradient extraction is usually worth more per hour than any amount of theme revision.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on the investigation
whyPoints.description: We teach the four criteria, pressure-test the research question and comment on the student's own draft. No tutor here designs the investigation, supplies or processes data, writes a section, or edits until authorship changes.

whyPoints.title: No unverified IB dates published
whyPoints.description: ibo.org blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project is confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session; any date you act on should come from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you book
whyPoints.description: Standard Level is usually matched within days, Higher Level can take a week, and theme D at Higher Level is narrower still. You get a date, a named alternative, or an honest decline rather than a reassurance.

whyPoints.title: Online one-to-one, with scripts annotated live
whyPoints.description: Al Warqa physics lessons run one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own graphs and working marked up against a scheme. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: Is there an IB physics tutor near me in Al Warqa who teaches Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Within a short drive, very probably not. Al Warqa has no IB school, the surrounding schools in Al Warqa'a and Al Qusais are largely CBSE and British, and the nearest Diploma physics teaching sits in Mirdif and Festival City twenty to thirty minutes away. Teachers at those schools cannot be paid to tutor their own enrolled students. Matching by level and theme over live video reaches a far deeper pool than any radius drawn around this community, which is why availability rather than distance is the right filter.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a physics tutor knows the current IB syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions. Which theme contains fields? How many written papers are there at Higher Level? What are the four scientific investigation criteria called? A tutor currently teaching this course answers instantly: theme D, two papers, and research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. One who reaches for topic numbers, mentions the optional units, or describes a third paper is describing the previous structure. Thirty seconds of questions tells you more than any list of qualifications.

faqs.question: What are the five themes in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Theme A, space, time and motion, covering kinematics, forces, momentum and energy. Theme B, the particulate nature of matter, covering thermal physics, gas laws and circuits. Theme C, wave behaviour, covering simple harmonic motion, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Theme D, fields, covering gravitational, electric and magnetic fields with potential and induction. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level content sits inside each theme rather than in a separate section, which is why sequencing support matters.

faqs.question: What is the scientific investigation worth on an Al Warqa student's physics grade?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, from a single report assessed against four criteria worth six marks each, for twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Because the four carry equal weight, time should be distributed accordingly, and students almost always over-invest in the practical work and under-invest in evaluation. A badly scoped research question caps the mark before the first measurement, which is why the design conversation has to happen before data collection rather than after.

faqs.question: Where do IB Physics students lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: Uncertainties, because they are examined everywhere rather than as a topic: one or two marks lost on nearly every data question adds up to a grade while remaining invisible on any single answer. Then graph technique, especially gradients counted in grid squares instead of read from axis values, and error bars drawn and then ignored. Then command terms on extended responses, where explain, describe and outline each demand a different answer shape. All three are visible on a marked script within minutes.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Within firm limits. A tutor may teach the four criteria in the examiner's wording, explain what the twenty-four marks are made of, question whether a research question can produce analysable data, teach uncertainty propagation and graph technique on the student's own measurements, and comment on a draft the student has written. No tutor should design the investigation, supply or process data, write a section, or edit until authorship changes. The report carries the student's declaration, and a malpractice finding falls on them.

faqs.question: How does practical physics work if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The practical work stays at school with the school's equipment and supervision, which is where the student's authorship is visible and where it belongs. Online support covers everything around it: pressure-testing the research question before equipment is booked, teaching uncertainty propagation on the student's own data, linearising the relationship and extracting a gradient with its uncertainty, then reading the criteria alongside their draft. The data-based section of Paper 1 is a paper exercise and is arguably better taught on a shared screen than in a laboratory.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Physics need a different tutor from Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is genuinely different rather than merely longer. Additional content sits inside each theme, most visibly in fields, and the papers are longer at the same weightings. The practical consequence for tutoring is that a tutor comfortable at Standard Level may be out of their depth at Higher, particularly in theme D. Ask directly which level they have taught, in which theme, and how recently. A straight answer is worth more than a confident general one about physics.

faqs.question: My child moved from IGCSE Physics and the first Diploma report was poor. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually a predictable gap rather than the course being harder. A Cambridge 0625 Extended or Pearson 4PH1 candidate arrives with strong recall and calculation and no experience of extended written explanation or of designing an investigation from a blank page. Four to eight weeks of focused work normally covers it. Left unnamed, it presents as a general struggle and gets treated with a year of weekly support when what was needed was command-term work and one investigation conversation.

faqs.question: Could the real problem be maths rather than physics?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is rarely identified. Higher Level Physics assumes comfort with logarithms, trigonometry and rearranging multi-variable relationships. A student taking Applications and Interpretation mathematics alongside it sometimes meets a genuine gap that presents as a physics weakness. A marked script shows it quickly: the physics reasoning is sound and the algebra breaks. Treating it as physics means months of the wrong tutoring, which is why the first session should start from scripts rather than from a description.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find a Higher Level physics tutor for an Al Warqa student?
faqs.answer: Standard Level is usually matched within a few days. Higher Level often takes up to a week, and theme D at Higher Level is narrower still. Where nobody suitable is free, you get a date rather than a reassurance, so you can decide whether to wait. Sometimes the better answer is a block on uncertainties, graphs and data analysis with a Chemistry or Mathematics specialist, which transfers directly. Where neither works, declining is the honest response.

faqs.question: Can my child's own physics teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: No. A teacher cannot be paid to provide private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit it explicitly, though the current policy wording should be verified at the source. However convenient it would be, it is not an available option and should not be arranged.

faqs.question: When are the IB Physics exams, and can you tell us the dates?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. Beyond that, we will not publish specific dates, and you should be wary of any page that does. ibo.org returns an error to automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and secondary sources disagree. Get the dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. A wrong date on a tutoring page is the kind of error a family acts on, which makes it worse than no information.

faqs.question: Should we buy weekly physics support or a short technique block?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the marked scripts show. If the content is understood and the losses are in uncertainties, graphs and command terms, a six to eight session technique block is the highest-yield purchase in the subject and has a clear end date. If the content itself is thin, weekly support moving with the school's scheme of work is the right arrangement, and it should start in the first term of Year 12 because Higher Level depth in fields assumes earlier themes are secure.

Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-wasl.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Physics at Standard and Higher Level. Each one works from the 2023 subject guide, marks to published command terms, and can show you a student script annotated the way an examiner reads it. You meet the tutor before you commit to anything.

intro.heading: Physics is where a strong Diploma student first meets a subject that will not reward effort alone
paragraphs: A parent in Al Wasl rarely searches for a physics tutor in September. The search happens in week six or week seven of the Diploma, when the first formal assessment comes back and the number is lower than anything the student saw in Year 11. The student has not stopped working. The subject has changed shape. IGCSE Physics asked for recall, a formula and a substitution. Diploma Physics asks what a quantity means, why a graph has that gradient, and what the uncertainty in the third significant figure does to the conclusion. A student can know every equation in the data booklet and still write a Paper 2 answer that earns two marks out of six.

The 2023 Physics guide, first examined in 2025, organises the course into five themes: A, space, time and motion; B, the particulate nature of matter; C, wave behaviour; D, fields; and E, nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level students take the same five themes with additional content inside each. There is no separate options paper in this guide, which matters for tutoring: the old strategy of sacrificing the option and defending the core no longer exists. Everything is examinable, and the additional Higher Level material sits inside the themes rather than beside them.

The assessment is two written papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 splits into 1A, multiple choice, and 1B, data and practical analysis. Paper 2 is short and extended response. The investigation is worth a fifth of the final grade and is marked by the school against four published criteria, then moderated by the IB. A student who neglects it is capping their grade before they sit a single paper, and this is the single most common pattern we see in Al Wasl households: a capable physicist with a weak investigation, discovered in February of the second year when there is very little room left to move.

Al Wasl sits between Al Safa and Jumeirah, with Al Wasl Road and Al Hadiqa Street carrying most of the local school traffic. Families here feed into Jumeirah College, Horizon English School, Safa British School, Latifa School for Girls and Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, with Dubai College, Raffles World Academy, Emirates International School Jumeirah and Kings' School Dubai all inside a short drive. Those schools between them run both the British route and the IB continuum, so an Al Wasl physics cohort is split: some students sitting Cambridge or Edexcel at 16, others moving through the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma. A physics tutor who does not know which route your child is on will waste the first three lessons finding out.

What we do about it is narrow and specific. A tutor is matched to the theme your child is losing marks in, not to a general science brief. The first session is diagnostic: a past-paper question under timing, marked in front of your child against the actual mark scheme, so you both see whether the problem is the physics, the maths inside the physics, or the way the answer is written. Lessons then run weekly over live video, one tutor, one student, in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to an Al Wasl address; in-home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India, and the comparison table further down this page sets out honestly what that choice costs and buys in Dubai.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-wasl.programmesIntro: Al Wasl families arrive at Diploma Physics from two directions, and a third group never reaches the Diploma at all. Here is what each programme asks of a physics student and what tutoring looks like inside it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics is offered at Standard and Higher Level inside Group 4. Both levels sit Paper 1 and Paper 2 and complete the scientific investigation. Higher Level carries extra content in every theme, longer papers and a higher expectation of algebraic fluency. Students usually take Physics Higher Level alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, because several Higher Level derivations assume calculus the Applications course does not cover in the same way.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Wasl the Diploma physicists mostly come from Jumeirah Baccalaureate School, Raffles World Academy and Emirates International School Jumeirah. Those cohorts are small, which has a consequence parents rarely anticipate: a school may have one Physics Higher Level teacher and six students, so a single clash of personality or pace has nowhere to go inside the school. That is the most common reason an Al Wasl family looks outside it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences in the Middle Years Programme are assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. There is no formula sheet culture and no past-paper bank. Students write investigations from Year 7 onwards, which means a Middle Years student arrives at the Diploma with real experimental habits but often without the algebra speed the Diploma papers demand.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years to Diploma is the gentler of the two routes into Al Wasl physics, and the gap it leaves is numerical rather than conceptual. A Year 11 student from Jumeirah Baccalaureate School can design a fair test and evaluate a method well, then lose six marks on a Paper 2 question because rearranging an equation with three variables under timed conditions has never been drilled. Six to eight weeks of targeted algebra work before Diploma 1 closes most of it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, so a student may take Physics Standard Level without the full Diploma. The subject content and assessment are identical to the Diploma version of that course, including the scientific investigation. Tutoring is the same work: themes, papers, investigation. What differs is the surrounding load, which is usually lighter and leaves more room for weekly physics practice.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is thinly offered in Dubai compared with the Diploma, so an Al Wasl family taking this route is often the only one in their circle doing it. Worth knowing before you plan tutoring around it: a Career-related Programme student sitting Physics Standard Level is examined exactly as a Diploma student is, so nothing about the physics timetable or the investigation deadline is relaxed on their behalf.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-al-wasl.subjectsIntro: A physics problem is rarely only a physics problem. These are the subjects that sit around IB Physics in an Al Wasl timetable and the specific way each one shows up in a physics mark.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, with Higher Level extension inside each rather than as a separate option. Marks are lost most often in fields, where students describe a potential as though it were a force, and in nuclear and quantum, where the arithmetic of binding energy is fine but the explanation of mass defect is not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual partner to Physics Higher Level. Differentiation, integration and the handling of logarithms are the three places where a physics answer stalls for mathematical rather than physical reasons. A student on Analysis and Approaches Standard Level taking Physics Higher Level is the combination that most often needs maths support inside physics lessons.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Perfectly viable alongside Physics Standard Level, and harder work alongside Higher Level. The course is strong on statistics and modelling and lighter on the algebraic manipulation that Higher Level derivations assume. We treat the gap directly rather than pretending it is not there.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the Group 4 investigation structure and the same four assessment criteria, so a student who has learned to design one investigation properly can reuse the skill. Chemistry students taking Physics also benefit from transferable work on uncertainty propagation, which both subjects examine and neither teaches at length.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The common third science in Al Wasl timetables for medicine applicants. Biology trains description and recall; Physics punishes both when they replace explanation. Students holding both often need explicit coaching on the difference between a Biology-style descriptive answer and a Physics answer that must reason from a principle.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Taken by a small number of Al Wasl Diploma students alongside Physics, usually with engineering in mind. The useful overlap is logical decomposition: a student who can trace a program can usually be taught to break a multi-stage Paper 2 question into stages instead of attempting it in one leap.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Another Group 4 subject with a substantial internal component. Students combining it with Physics carry two large coursework loads in the same academic year, and the scheduling of those two deadlines is something we map in the first consultation rather than discovering in term two.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Mechanics content here overlaps with theme A, so force, moment and energy work done for Physics pays twice. The investigation criteria are identical to the Physics ones, which makes it a sensible subject to practise research design on when physics data collection is blocked by lab access.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: A Group 3 and Group 4 subject that can satisfy the science requirement for a student not continuing with Physics beyond Standard Level. Energy, flows and systems thinking carry across; the quantitative demand is lower, which is the point for a student whose strength is argument rather than algebra.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Not a science subject, but physics is the natural source of examples for it: measurement, uncertainty, the status of a model. Diploma students who use their own physics work in Theory of Knowledge essays tend to write sharper ones, and the reverse holds too, because explaining why a model is provisional improves Paper 2 evaluation answers.

sections.heading: What an Al Wasl parent is actually asking when they search for an IB physics tutor
paragraphs: The search phrase is about location; the problem almost never is. An IB physics tutor in Al Wasl is wanted because a specific part of the course has stopped working, and the useful first question is which part. In our Al Wasl enquiries the answer falls into one of four buckets: a content gap in fields or in nuclear and quantum physics; a mathematics gap that only shows up inside physics; a technique gap where the student knows the physics and writes an answer that does not earn the marks; or an investigation that has drifted past its internal deadline. Each of those needs a different tutor and a different number of weeks.

The distinction is worth drawing before you buy anything, because the four problems have very different price tags. A technique gap is often six lessons. A content gap across two themes is a term. A mathematics gap running underneath Higher Level Physics is longer than that and is cheaper to fix in a maths lesson than in a physics one. An investigation three weeks from the school's deadline is urgent, bounded and small. Families who diagnose first spend materially less than families who buy a general weekly slot and hope it lands on the right thing.

This is also why the neighbourhood matters less than the search suggests. A Higher Level Physics specialist who can take apart a fields question is a rare match in any one district of Dubai, and insisting that person also lives within a twenty-minute drive of Al Wasl Road shrinks the pool to whoever is nearby rather than whoever is right. Teaching over live video removes the constraint entirely: your child gets the specialist, and the only local variable left is what time the lesson starts.

So the honest answer to the search is that we do not have a physics tutor who lives in Al Wasl, and we do not think you should want one. What we have is a matching process that starts with your child's last marked paper, identifies which of the four problems you actually have, and puts the right specialist in front of them over video within a few days.
