sections.heading: The five themes of the current Physics guide, and which ones cost Al Wasl students marks
paragraphs: The 2023 Physics guide, first examined in 2025, replaced the old core-plus-option structure with five themes taken by every student. Higher Level content sits inside each theme as additional material rather than in a separate paper. For a tutor this is a real change in strategy: there is no option to triage, and a weakness in one theme is now spread across both written papers instead of being concentrated in one.

In practice the themes are not equally difficult, and the pattern is consistent enough to plan around. Theme A, space, time and motion, is where most students start comfortably, because it extends mechanics they met at 16. Theme B, the particulate nature of matter, is where thermal physics and the gas laws produce arithmetic slips rather than conceptual failure. Theme C, wave behaviour, is largely well taught and well revised. Theme D, fields, is the one that separates grades: gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are taught in sequence and examined together, and students who learned them as three unrelated topics cannot answer a question that crosses between them. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, is last in most schemes of work and therefore the least revised, which is why it so often appears in a student's weakest paper.

The table below is how we triage a new Al Wasl student. We ask for the last two marked assessments, locate the lost marks by theme, and start with whichever theme is both weak and heavily examined. That is almost always D, and the second most common answer is E, for timetable reasons rather than difficulty ones.

One note on sequencing. A student in the second Diploma year who is weak in theme D should not begin with theme E even though E feels more alarming. Fields underpin the quantum material, and six weeks on D usually improves E marks without E being taught at all. Starting with the frightening topic rather than the foundational one is the most common self-directed revision error we see.

sections.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2 and the weightings that decide the final grade
paragraphs: Physics in the current guide is examined by two written papers plus the internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 has two parts: 1A is multiple choice, 1B is a data and practical analysis section. Paper 2 is short and extended response. The investigation carries a fifth of the grade. Higher Level papers are longer and carry additional content, but the proportional split between examination and internal assessment is the same at both levels. Confirm the exact durations and mark totals for your child's session against the subject guide held by their school's IB coordinator, because the guide is the authority and a tutor's recollection is not.

The practical consequence of this structure is that Paper 1B is badly underweighted in most students' revision. It is a data section: graphs, gradients, error bars, uncertainty, a conclusion drawn from numbers the student did not generate. Students revise content for Paper 2 and multiple choice for 1A, then meet 1B with no dedicated practice at all. It is also the part of the examination that most resembles the scientific investigation, so work done for one pays into the other. We treat 1B as a separate skill with its own weekly drill rather than as a sub-section of Paper 1.

The second consequence is about command terms. A Paper 2 question that says state wants one line and gives one mark. A question that says explain wants a causal chain and will not accept a description however accurate. A question that says discuss expects more than one position. Al Wasl students arriving from a British Year 11 are frequently excellent at describing and have never been taught the difference, which is why their marks sit a band below their understanding. This is the fastest improvement available on the whole page: a student who learns to read the command term properly can gain marks within a fortnight without learning any new physics.

The third is timing. Higher Level Paper 2 is long, and students who answer in the order printed spend their freshest forty minutes on questions worth fewer marks. We teach a pass-order strategy, practise it under timing, and review the script for marks lost to running out of time as a separate category from marks lost to not knowing something.

sections.heading: The six physics errors we see most often in this part of Dubai, and what each one is really telling you
paragraphs: Marks lost in physics are diagnosable. After the first marked paper a tutor can usually name the underlying cause from the pattern of errors, and the cause is frequently not the one the student assumes. A student who says they are bad at fields is often a student who cannot rearrange an equation at speed, which looks like a physics problem only because fields questions require three rearrangements where mechanics questions require one.

The first error is the untranslated word problem. The student reads a question, cannot see which principle applies, and writes nothing for four minutes. The cause is not knowledge but a missing habit: they have never been taught to annotate the stem, list the given quantities with units, and name the principle before touching a number. Twenty minutes of explicit instruction and three weeks of enforcement fixes it.

The second is the described answer. The question says explain and the student describes what happens, accurately and at length, without ever saying because. Examiners cannot award explanation marks for description. The third is the lost unit, which costs a mark at a time and is almost always a working-layout problem rather than carelessness: students who write quantities in a column with units attached stop losing them. The fourth is uncertainty treated as decoration, carried into a conclusion that claims a precision the data cannot support. The fifth is the graph drawn without thought about what its gradient physically represents. The sixth, and the most expensive, is the investigation treated as a report to be produced rather than as an inquiry to be designed.

None of this is remedied by more content teaching. A student who has seen theme D twice does not need a third pass; they need a diagnosis, a specific habit installed, and enough marked practice to make the habit survive exam pressure. This is the main reason we insist that written work between lessons comes back marked rather than discussed, because a habit that has not been tested on paper has not been installed.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: a fifth of the grade, four criteria, and the places it goes wrong
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation is an independent piece of experimental work, written up by the student and marked by the school against four published criteria before IB moderation. It is worth a fifth of the Physics grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Your child's school sets the internal deadlines and holds the current criterion descriptors and word limit; ask the IB coordinator for both in writing at the start of the Diploma rather than in February of the second year.

The most expensive failure happens in week one, not week ten. A research question that is too broad cannot be answered with the equipment available, and no amount of good data analysis rescues it. We have read investigations that measured something carefully and well and could not score in the top band for research design because the question asked about a relationship the method could not isolate. A single thirty-minute conversation at the research-question stage is worth more than three sessions at the write-up stage, which is why we push Al Wasl families to book investigation support early and short rather than late and long.

The second failure is evaluation written as apology. Students list what went wrong and promise to be more careful next time. The criterion wants a reasoned assessment of the method's limitations and their effect on the conclusion, with improvements that are specific and would actually work. The third is a conclusion that restates the data rather than interpreting it against accepted physics. The fourth is uncertainty handled correctly in the data table and then forgotten in the final sentence.

What a tutor may do here is bounded, and we would rather state the boundary plainly than leave it vague. A tutor can teach experimental design, interrogate a research question, explain how to propagate an uncertainty, and give feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor must never supply data, never write any portion of the report, and never edit text to the point where the words are no longer the student's. The IB treats breaches of academic honesty as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor. Any provider offering to produce a finished investigation is selling your child a risk they have not been told about.

paragraphs: Most tutoring pages quote an hourly rate, which is the least useful number for planning a household budget. An Al Wasl family does not buy an hour; they buy a term. Those monthly figures come from hourly bands that are worth seeing separately. Budget online tutoring, typically a university student, runs about AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. The useful planning move is to decide the monthly number first and let it determine the format. sections.heading: Online physics lessons against an in-home physics tutor on the Al Wasl corridor
paragraphs: This page targets a phrase parents type, so the honest position comes first: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Al Wasl or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home visiting is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, and we would rather you knew that in paragraph one than in week three. What follows is the case for that choice on its merits, and the places where an in-home tutor genuinely wins.

For a subject like physics the argument is mostly about the tutor pool. A Higher Level fields specialist who can mark to the current guide is uncommon. Requiring that person to be within driving distance of Al Wasl Road at 17:00 on a Tuesday reduces your choice to whoever is nearby and free, which in practice means a general science tutor rather than a physics one. Over video the constraint disappears and the only remaining question is the time of day. For theme D, that trade is not close.

There are practical gains too. A recorded lesson can be replayed the night before a test, which an in-home lesson cannot. Screen-sharing a past paper and annotating the mark scheme live is clearer than two people over one sheet of paper. Graph work, simulations and data analysis are all easier on a shared screen than on a dining table. And a cancelled slot can be moved rather than lost, because nobody has driven anywhere.

The honest counter-case: a younger student who will not sit still without an adult physically present is better served in person, and a household with unreliable connectivity should not pretend otherwise. Al Wasl is well served for fixed-line broadband, so the second rarely applies, and for Diploma-age students the first rarely does either. If your child is twelve and easily distracted, an in-home tutor from a local agency may genuinely suit them better, and we would say so on a call rather than sell you something that will not work.

sections.heading: The regulator, the tutor permit, and what an Al Wasl parent can verify before paying
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. If your child's school is in Dubai, every inspection rating and fee decision that affects them comes from the first of those.

Private tutoring itself is governed separately, by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. u.ae states the permit is granted free of charge for two years, and that eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in u.ae's words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting you an amount is guessing.

Two things follow for a parent in Al Wasl. The permit is free, so a tutor who tells you their fee reflects licensing costs is mistaken. And the permit is a real document you may ask to see. The official application route is the Ministry's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the Ministry's smart app, website and e-services system. Ask any prospective tutor, including ours, whether they hold it, and ask the question before the first paid lesson rather than after.

A note on what we are not. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, by the Ministry of Education, by the International Baccalaureate or by any examination board, and no page on this site should be read as saying otherwise. A Dubai operation with premises and staff needs a Knowledge and Human Development Authority Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific permission issued to a specific address. We do not hold one and we do not operate premises in the UAE. Anyone claiming regulator approval for a tutoring platform should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Starting physics tutoring mid-year, and what happens if the specialist you need is not free
paragraphs: Most Al Wasl physics enquiries arrive mid-term, which is the right time rather than a late one. A student six weeks into a theme they do not understand is a better tutoring prospect than a student in September with no data: there is a marked paper to diagnose from and a specific, recent failure to work on. What changes mid-year is the sequencing. A tutor joining in January works backwards from the school's internal deadlines, not forwards from the start of the syllabus.

The first session is diagnostic and free, and it is a lesson rather than a sales call. Your child brings their two most recent marked assessments and a past-paper question they could not finish. The tutor works the question with them, marks it against the published scheme, and at the end tells you which of the four problem types you have and roughly how many weeks it should take. If the answer is that physics is not the bottleneck, we say that too. We have sent families to a maths tutor instead more than once, because Higher Level Physics marks lost to algebra do not improve with physics teaching.

Availability is where most platforms go quiet, so here is the position stated. Physics Higher Level specialists are our scarcest subject-level match in the UAE, especially for a fixed weekday slot between 16:00 and 18:00 Gulf Standard Time, which is when everybody wants one. If the right specialist is not free at the time you need, we will tell you the actual wait rather than put a general science tutor in the slot. If the wait is longer than a fortnight we will say so and you should consider another provider, because an exam-year student cannot afford to hold a slot open on a promise.

Two further practicalities. Ramadan shifts household routines and many families move physics to a post-Iftar slot for that period; we plan this in advance rather than rescheduling week by week. And if the match is not right, say so after the first or second paid lesson and we will change the tutor rather than ask your child to persist with someone they do not learn from. A physics tutor your child does not want to talk to cannot teach them to explain anything.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Physics tutor cost for a family in Al Wasl?
faqs.answer: There is no single figure, and any page giving you one without asking your child's level is guessing. The Dubai market, read from published provider pages in October 2026, runs about AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and AED 200 to 450 or more for a genuine IB specialist. TutorChase publishes AED 270; BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Those are their rates, not ours. IB Gram quotes your figure after the free diagnostic lesson, because it depends on level, on theme and on how many weeks you actually need.

faqs.question: Which IB Physics theme causes the most trouble for Diploma students?
faqs.answer: Theme D, fields. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are usually taught in sequence and then examined together, so a student who learned them as three separate topics cannot answer a question that crosses between them. The specific error is using field strength and potential interchangeably. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, generates nearly as many lost marks, but for a timetable reason rather than a difficulty one: it is taught last and therefore revised least. If your child is weak in both, start with D, because fields underpin the quantum material and improving D often lifts E marks without E being taught.

faqs.question: Is IB Physics Higher Level much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The difference is less about extra topics and more about algebraic fluency and depth within the same five themes. Higher Level adds content inside each theme rather than as a separate paper, and the papers are longer. In practice the students who struggle at Higher Level are usually not the ones with weak physics intuition but the ones whose equation handling is slow under time pressure. That is why we check the mathematics before assuming the physics is the problem, and why a student on Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation taking Physics Higher Level needs that gap addressed explicitly rather than hoped away.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child with the IB Physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we will state plainly. A tutor can interrogate the research question until it is actually measurable, teach experimental design, explain how to propagate uncertainty, and give feedback on a draft your child has written against the four published criteria. A tutor must never supply data, never produce any part of the report and never edit the text until the words stop being your child's. The IB treats breaches as malpractice and the consequence lands on the student. Any provider offering a finished investigation is selling a risk your child has not been told about.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to our home in Al Wasl?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and recorded so your child can replay it. For Higher Level Physics specifically that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because it means the match is made on which theme your child is losing marks in rather than on who happens to be free and within driving distance of Al Wasl Road at five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: What time can a physics lesson start for a student at Jumeirah College or Horizon English School?
faqs.answer: Most Al Wasl students finishing around 15:15 are home by 15:45, so 16:30 works comfortably on a normal weekday. Two things push it later. After-school sport at the Jumeirah schools often runs to 17:00, which moves the lesson to 18:00. And a sibling in a different year group may finish at a different time, which is why back-to-back slots at 16:00 and 17:15 are a common booking pattern here. Lessons can run as late as 20:00 Gulf Standard Time, and during Ramadan many families move to a post-Iftar slot by arrangement rather than week by week.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but keeps losing marks on Paper 2. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Almost always a command-term problem. A question that says explain requires a causal chain and will not accept a description, however accurate. A question that says state wants one line. Students arriving from a British Year 11 are frequently excellent at describing and have never been taught the distinction, so their marks sit a band below their understanding. This is the fastest improvement available: a fortnight of explicit command-term work on marked past-paper questions typically moves a grade boundary without any new physics being learned. The second candidate is pass-order strategy on a long Higher Level paper.

faqs.question: Why does nobody revise Paper 1B, and does it matter?
faqs.answer: It matters a great deal and it goes unrevised because it does not look like content. Paper 1B is data and practical analysis: graphs, gradients, error bars, uncertainty and a conclusion drawn from numbers the student did not generate. Students revise content for Paper 2 and multiple-choice technique for 1A, then meet 1B cold. It also closely resembles the scientific investigation, so practice pays into a fifth of the grade as well. We drill it as its own weekly skill rather than as a sub-section of Paper 1, which is the single cheapest mark gain on most physics plans.

faqs.question: Does my child need Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches to take Physics Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Schools set their own prerequisites, so check with your child's Diploma coordinator. In practice, several Higher Level Physics derivations assume calculus handled the way Analysis and Approaches handles it, and students taking Physics Higher Level with Applications and Interpretation frequently need maths support delivered inside their physics lessons. That is a workable combination rather than a doomed one, but it needs to be planned for in Diploma 1 rather than discovered in Diploma 2. If the algebra is the bottleneck, a maths tutor is cheaper and faster than more physics teaching.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting physics tutoring ten weeks before the exam session?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for different work than you might expect. Ten weeks is not enough to re-teach two weak themes and should not be spent trying. It is enough to drill paper technique, command terms and Paper 1B data questions, and to make sure revision time is allocated by weighting rather than by comfort. Students at this stage usually gain more from supervised full papers marked against the published scheme than from further content teaching. We would set out that plan in the free first lesson and tell you honestly if the realistic gain looks small.

Ask any tutor to confirm they hold it before the first paid lesson.

The marked work is what lets a tutor diagnose rather than guess, because the pattern of lost marks is visible on the page and a student's own account of the problem is usually inaccurate. The unfinished question gives the tutor something to work live, which is how you find out whether the block is the physics, the algebra inside it, or the way the answer is written. Nothing else is needed and no preparation is required from your child.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Chemistry for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking about rather than assuming. Both subjects sit in Group 4 and share the same four investigation criteria, so one tutor coaching both internal assessments is efficient and coherent. Content teaching is different: a genuine Higher Level Physics specialist is usually not also a Higher Level Chemistry specialist, and a tutor who claims both at Higher Level deserves a question about which they taught longer. For Standard Level across both, a single well-qualified science tutor is often the better value, and we will say which applies in your case.

intro.heading: Why the nearest physics tutor is rarely the right physics tutor
paragraphs: Arabian Ranches sits off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road with the golf club on one side and Al Qudra Road on the other, and the family searching from Alvorada, Hattan, Palmera or Terra Nova almost always types the same thing: a physics tutor, near me. The instinct is sound. The reasoning behind it is not. Physics at Diploma level is one of the narrowest teaching specialisms in the UAE market. The number of people in Dubai who can take a student through electromagnetic induction sign conventions, then switch to uncertainty propagation on a gradient, then mark an extended-response answer the way an examiner reads it, is small. Filtering that already small group by whether they live fifteen minutes away removes most of it.

That is the comparison this page makes, community by community. Arabian Ranches, Arabian Ranches 2, Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon, Remraam, Town Square, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills and Dubai Hills Estate are all within a short drive of each other across the Dubailand belt. They feed overlapping school rosters, they finish the school day within the same half-hour window, and they face the same evening traffic on Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street. A parent in Saheel and a parent in Lila are solving an identical problem, and the honest answer for both is the same.

The schools make this clearer. JESS Arabian Ranches runs the English National Curriculum through IGCSE and then the IB Diploma, so a Ranches family can reach DP Physics without leaving the community. Families a few minutes away reach the Diploma through Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail in Dubai Hills Estate or Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills and GEMS Metropole School in Motor City take the A Level route instead. Four different campuses, four different timetables, one shared shortage: physics teachers with spare capacity in term time.

KHDA inspects every one of those schools annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and publishes the reports. Dubai's private sector carried 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for roughly 7 per cent of that enrolment. That last figure is the one that matters here. IB Physics is a minority course inside a minority curriculum, which is precisely why geography is a poor filter and syllabus fluency is a good one.

IB Gram answers the search honestly. We do not send a tutor to a villa in Arabian Ranches or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. What a Ranches family gets instead is a physics specialist matched to Higher or Standard Level and to the themes your child is behind on, teaching live over video with a shared whiteboard and the past-paper question open on screen. Nothing is driven anywhere, nothing is lost to the Umm Suqeim Road queue at six in the evening, and the pool the tutor is drawn from is the whole pool rather than the residents of three adjoining communities.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.programmesIntro: Arabian Ranches children reach IB Physics by more than one route. Some arrive through JESS at Year 12 after IGCSE, some transfer in from an MYP school in Dubai Hills or The Sustainable City, and a few come from an American campus after AP Physics. The programme notes below describe what each route means for physics specifically.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Physics in the Diploma is built on five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Standard Level runs to 150 taught hours, Higher Level to 240, and the extra ninety hours are where the mathematics thickens. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent and the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. There is no Paper 3 on the current guide.
programmes.countryNote: A Ranches student usually meets DP Physics at JESS Arabian Ranches, inside the community, or at an IB continuum school a short drive away. The practical work and the laboratory sit with the school; a tutor works on the theory, the question technique and the write-up. KHDA publishes the inspection report for each of those campuses, which is the document to read before judging a physics department.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria, each out of eight: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Physics content appears inside integrated science units rather than as a standalone subject until the final years. A student who has never written a controlled-variables table will feel the gap immediately in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Families around Arabian Ranches reach the MYP through Fairgreen International School, Emirates International School Meadows, GEMS International School Al Khail and Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills. MYP 4 and MYP 5 science work is the best preparation available for the Diploma investigation, and it is also where a tutor can close a gap cheaply, before DP1 makes it expensive.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics before the Diploma
programmes.description: Most Ranches students meet physics first as Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1. Cambridge splits into Core and Extended tiers with separate theory papers; Edexcel runs a single tier across two papers. Both stop well short of calculus, which is why the step into DP Physics feels steeper than the step into DP Biology.
programmes.countryNote: JESS Arabian Ranches, Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, GEMS Metropole School in Motor City and South View School in the Remraam direction all run IGCSE physics before their sixth-form routes diverge. A Ranches parent choosing between DP Physics and A Level Physics at Year 11 is really choosing between a themed five-strand course with an investigation and a linear two-year course with practical endorsements.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme science components
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more DP courses with a career-related study, so a student may take DP Physics SL alongside an applied qualification. The physics content and the assessment are identical to the Diploma version; the workload around it differs, which changes how many hours of support make sense each week.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is far less common in Dubai than the full Diploma, and no campus inside Arabian Ranches offers it, so families exploring it are usually looking across the city. The physics teaching requirement does not change: the same five themes, the same Paper 1 and Paper 2, the same 24-mark investigation.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: Physics is the headline here, but a DP physics student rarely needs physics alone. The combinations below are the ones Ranches families ask about most often, with a note on what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Physics HL
subjects.description: Themes A to E at full depth, with Paper 1 running two hours across multiple choice and data analysis, and Paper 2 running two hours thirty. The HL-only material in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics is where most of the extra difficulty lives, along with the expectation that algebra is rearranged without prompting.

subjects.name: Physics SL
subjects.description: The same five themes at reduced depth, with Paper 1 and Paper 2 each running one hour thirty. SL students lose marks less often on the mathematics and more often on explanation questions, where a correct idea is written in the wrong number of steps for the mark allocation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The natural partner to Physics HL. Calculus fluency makes kinematics, simple harmonic motion and induction readable rather than mysterious. Students who take AA SL alongside Physics HL cope; students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside Physics HL usually need the algebra taught twice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy and modelling-led, which suits the data-analysis half of Paper 1B well and the derivation-heavy parts of Paper 2 poorly. A Ranches student on AI who is set on an engineering degree should check the admissions requirement of each named university before Year 12 locks in.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL and SL
subjects.description: The second science in most Ranches science combinations. Chemistry and physics share the same assessment architecture on the 2023 guides, so a student who learns to read command terms properly in one course carries the skill straight into the other, and the two investigations can be planned in the same term.

subjects.name: Biology HL and SL
subjects.description: Often chosen as the third science for medicine applications. Biology rewards precision of vocabulary where physics rewards precision of reasoning, and students who are strong in one are frequently caught out by the other. Statistical tests in Biology overlap with the uncertainty work in Physics 1B.

subjects.name: Computer Science HL and SL
subjects.description: Picked by Ranches students heading towards engineering or software. The internal assessment is a developed solution rather than a laboratory investigation, so a student taking Computer Science and Physics together carries two very different coursework formats in the same academic year.

subjects.name: Design Technology HL and SL
subjects.description: Shares the physics of materials, structures and energy, and leans on the same measurement discipline. Students combining Design Technology with Physics HL get genuine overlap in the mechanics content and almost none in the assessment style, which is worth planning for early.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and essay sit outside subject teaching but consume DP1 and DP2 time in ways that collide with physics deadlines. A tutor can help a student think about scientific knowledge claims clearly; a tutor does not write the essay or the exhibition commentary.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A physics Extended Essay needs a research question narrow enough to be answered with equipment a Dubai school actually owns. Supervision stays with the school supervisor. Tutoring is confined to teaching the underlying physics, discussing method, and giving feedback on the student's own drafts.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.igcseSubjectsIntro: Several Arabian Ranches students arrive at this page a year early, looking for physics support in Year 10 or Year 11 before the Diploma starts. These are the IGCSE physics routes the local schools actually run.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
igcseSubjects.description: Core candidates sit Paper 1 multiple choice and Paper 3 theory; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4. Both tiers then sit either Paper 5, the practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Grades 9 to 1 are available on Extended only, which is the decision Year 10 parents ask about most.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers, untiered. Paper 1 is the longer of the two and carries the larger share of the marks; Paper 2 covers the remaining content in a shorter sitting. There is no practical paper, with experimental skills assessed inside the written questions instead.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
igcseSubjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics taught together for two IGCSE grades rather than three. The physics content is thinner than 0625, which matters for a student who intends to take Physics HL: the gap into DP1 is wider from 0654 than from the separate syllabus.

igcseSubjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Double Award Science 4SD0
igcseSubjects.description: Three biology, chemistry and physics papers at a reduced content load, awarding two grades. Common in Dubai schools that want all students to carry science to 16 without filling the timetable with three separate subjects.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Taken by a minority of Year 11 students and the single best preparation for Physics HL available at IGCSE level. It introduces differentiation and integration early, which removes most of the pain from DP kinematics and simple harmonic motion.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: The standard mathematics route in British-curriculum Dubai schools. Extended tier is effectively a prerequisite for Physics HL in practice, because the graph work and the algebraic rearrangement in Paper 4 are the floor DP Physics builds on.

sections.heading: What an Arabian Ranches parent is actually comparing
paragraphs: The search phrase says location, but the decision underneath it is about three things: who teaches your child, when the lesson can happen, and what it costs. Location only matters because it changes the other three. So the honest way to answer a search for an IB physics tutor in Arabian Ranches is to work out, community by community, how much each of those three actually moves when you cross from Saheel to Lila to Mudon to Town Square.

The answer on teaching quality is that location moves it a great deal, in the wrong direction. Restricting the search to tutors who can be at a Ranches villa by five o'clock removes almost everyone who teaches DP Physics for a living. Restricting it to people who can open a video call at five o'clock removes nobody. That is not a marketing claim; it is arithmetic about the size of the physics teaching population in one emirate.

The answer on timing is that location matters less than the school roster. A JESS student living in Alvorada and a Fairgreen student living in Mudon both finish the academic day inside a predictable window, but the Mudon child spends part of the evening on the road. The answer on cost is the most surprising of the three, and the rate table further down this page shows why: the biggest single variable in a Dubai tutoring quote is not the tutor's qualification. It is whether a car is involved.
bullets: Teaching quality: narrowed sharply by a distance filter
Timing: set by the school run, not by the tutor's postcode
Cost: driven hardest by travel, not by qualification
Continuity: a tutor who moves house does not change your schedule

The last column is the point of the whole exercise: in every row, the number is small, and in several rows it is zero.

Drive times are indicative rather than measured, and they swing with the hour. The approach roads matter more than the kilometres. Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and Al Khail Road absorb the Dubai Hills and Al Barsha traffic badly between five and seven; Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street moves the Mudon and Town Square traffic more freely. A parent planning a weekly slot should build it around the worst evening of the week rather than the best.

Read the table and the conclusion arrives on its own. The communities differ in commute, in campus and in how new the housing is. They do not differ in the thing that decides a physics grade. Every family in the belt is drawing from the same thin local supply of Diploma physics teaching, and every one of them gets a wider choice the moment distance stops being a criterion.

There is one further column a parent should add mentally, which is stability. A tutor hired because they live nearby is a tutor whose availability depends on them continuing to live nearby. Villa leases in the Ranches belt turn over, families relocate between Dubailand and Al Barsha, and a teaching job moves across the city. A weekly slot that survives a change of address is worth more over two years of the Diploma than a slightly shorter drive in the first term, and that is the quiet argument for a delivery model in which nobody has to drive at all.

sections.heading: IB Physics on the 2023 guide: what each paper is worth
paragraphs: Physics in the Diploma was restructured for first assessment in 2025, and a surprising number of parents are still working from the previous shape. The option topics are gone. Paper 3 is gone. The content is organised as five themes, A to E, and the assessment is three components rather than four. Any tutor still talking about Paper 3 options is working from a guide that no longer applies to your child's examination.

Paper 1 is now split into two parts sat together. Paper 1A is multiple choice; Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions drawing on the inquiry and tools skills taught across the course. Paper 2 is short-answer and extended-response. The scientific investigation, written up individually, completes the grade. Higher Level sits longer papers across the same structure rather than extra components.

The weightings below are the ones to plan revision against. Notice that Paper 2 carries more of the grade than Paper 1 at both levels, and that the investigation carries a fifth of everything before a single examination is sat. A DP1 student who treats the investigation as homework has already made the grade harder to reach than it needed to be, and no amount of revision in DP2 recovers that fifth.

Two further features of the current guide change how a Ranches student should prepare. The tools and inquiry strands, covering experimental technique, technology and mathematics, are taught across the whole course rather than as a separate unit, and they are examined inside Paper 1B rather than anywhere obvious. The collaborative sciences project takes roughly ten hours of DP1 and carries no marks of its own, which means it is easy to leave late and expensive to leave late. A tutor working on the current structure plans around both; a tutor working from the previous guide will plan a revision schedule with a component in it that your child will never sit.

sections.heading: Where Arabian Ranches physics students actually lose marks
paragraphs: Across the Dubailand belt the same five problems come up again and again, and none of them is about intelligence. The first is the gradient-versus-area confusion on motion graphs. A student reads a velocity-time graph, knows the words, and still takes the area when the question wants the gradient. The fix is mechanical: label both axes with their units, multiply the units together for the area and divide them for the gradient, and read what comes out.

The second is uncertainty. Paper 1B rewards a student who can convert an absolute uncertainty into a percentage, combine percentages correctly through a multiplication, and draw a maximum and minimum gradient to get an uncertainty on a slope. Most Ranches students have been taught this once and never drilled on it. It is the single most trainable set of marks in the whole course, and it is the first thing a sensible block of tutoring attacks.

The third is direction. Fields, induction and circular motion all depend on sign conventions and on knowing which way a force or a current actually points, and a student who has memorised a rule without understanding it loses the mark every time the geometry is unfamiliar. The fourth is the command term: describe, explain, deduce and determine demand different structures, and a three-mark explanation needs three linked steps, not one good sentence. The fifth is simply arithmetic under pressure, which is why timed practice belongs in the schedule from the start of DP2 rather than from March.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs across the Dubailand belt
paragraphs: Start with what the travel premium buys, because it is the clearest way to read a Dubai tutoring quote. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. The same research puts qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, and EdFlik advertises online sessions from AED 45 to 65 while Tutopiya lists from AED 33 to 52. The difference between the online band and the in-home band is not teaching. It is a car, a driver, and forty minutes of someone's evening.

For a specialist subject the bands shift upwards rather than apart. TutorChase publishes AED 270 an hour, Unitors quotes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and Bestimate puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED's examiner-led tier at AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Those are market figures with the source named, not IB Gram prices, and they were published by the companies and the research service that charge them. What they tell a Ranches parent is simple. Two families can pay the same AED 300 an hour and buy very different things: one buys a physics specialist for sixty minutes, the other buys a generalist for forty minutes plus a drive from Al Barsha. Set against Dubai school fees the context matters too, because KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for 2026-27 under the second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the part of the education budget still moving.

sections.heading: Online lessons against a tutor who drives out to the Ranches
paragraphs: A fair comparison needs the in-home option described properly rather than dismissed. A tutor who comes to the house removes the need for a parent to supervise a screen, works with the student's own textbooks on the table, and reads body language that a video call flattens. For a nine-year-old those advantages are real. For a Diploma physics student they weigh far less, because the material is written, the working is shared on screen anyway, and the student is old enough to run their own session.

Against that sits the cost of distance. The local in-home market quotes AED 180 to 500 an hour because the tutor is paid for the drive as well as the lesson. In practice a tutor serving Arabian Ranches can fit two or three evening visits into the belt, which is why the available pool shrinks to people who already live in Dubailand, Motor City or Dubai Hills Estate. The specialist you want for Physics HL may live in Mirdif, or may not live in the UAE at all.

IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai. That restriction is the whole basis of the comparison in the table below, and it is stated plainly rather than hidden: home tutoring at the door is a service we run only in India, and for UAE families every lesson is delivered live over video. What a Ranches family gains in exchange is the specialist rather than the neighbour, a slot that does not depend on traffic, and a rate that is not carrying a car.

sections.heading: The May session counted backwards from a DP2 physics mock
paragraphs: Dubai IB schools sit the May session, and the useful way to plan is backwards from it rather than forwards from today. The IB publishes its own examination schedule and results dates, and those should be read on ibo.org or confirmed with your school's Diploma coordinator rather than taken from a tutoring page; dates move, and a wrong date on a revision plan is worse than no date. What does not move is the order of events, and the order is what a family can plan against.

For the British board sitting at 16, the published dates make the same point concretely. Cambridge examines International GCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series here, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so which timetable version a family reads matters as much as the date on it. Counting a June sitting backwards is the useful exercise: the papers fall in the first half of June, forecast grades go in before them, and the final entry closed in the spring, several months earlier, on a date the centre prints on the statement of entry. Entries close months before the first paper, not weeks. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with the November 2026 timetable finishing on 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after working from the wrong version. For a Ranches family that is a five-minute check with the school examinations officer. sections.heading: What a physics tutor may and may not do with the investigation
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is a fifth of the physics grade and it is the place where good intentions cause real damage. The report is the student's own work, assessed against four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Twenty-four marks in total, with a limit of 3,000 words. A tutor who understands those criteria can be extremely useful. A tutor who touches the text crosses a line that the IB treats as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student.

What is legitimate is teaching. A tutor can explain what a controlled variable is and why the examiner wants to see it justified. A tutor can show how to propagate an uncertainty through a calculation, how to decide whether a relationship should be linearised, and what an evaluation that scores well actually contains. A tutor can read a draft the student has written and say that the conclusion does not follow from the data. All of that is feedback on the student's work, which is exactly what a school supervisor also provides.

What is not legitimate is writing, rewriting, editing to completion, supplying a research question to be adopted wholesale, or producing data. IB Gram does not do any of those things, and a tutor who offers to is a risk to your child rather than a shortcut. The market contains providers selling finished Internal Assessments outright; one of them lists a price for the service. Treat that as the warning it is. The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and to the Theory of Knowledge essay, where the school supervisor remains in charge throughout.

sections.heading: KHDA, MoHRE and checking a physics tutor is allowed to teach
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The route is a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure should be quoted at you by anyone, including us. For a Ranches parent the practical step is to ask a prospective tutor whether they hold a current private tuition work permit, and to treat a vague answer as an answer. Abu Dhabi adds a further rule worth knowing even in Dubai: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit carries a code of conduct to the same effect.

The schools themselves sit under different authorities depending on the emirate. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, which covers every campus named on this page. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. IB Gram holds no permit, licence or accreditation from any of them, and does not claim one; a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a different thing entirely.

faqs.question: Is there an IB Physics tutor living inside Arabian Ranches itself?
faqs.answer: Possibly one or two, and that is the problem. Diploma physics is a narrow specialism, and Arabian Ranches is a residential community of a few thousand villas rather than a teaching hub. Filtering by residence inside Alvorada, Saheel, Hattan or Palmera reduces the available pool to almost nothing before you have looked at a single qualification. IB Gram matches on the 2023 subject guide and on the level your child sits instead, then delivers the lesson live over video. The tutor's postcode stops being a variable, and the question becomes which specialist is free in your slot.

faqs.question: Would a physics tutor based in Dubai Hills Estate be any better than one further away?
faqs.answer: Not for a Diploma physics student. Dubai Hills Estate is closer to the city's IB cluster and has GEMS International School Al Khail inside it, so the chance of a DP Physics teacher living there is a little higher than in Arabian Ranches 3 or Town Square. A little higher is still very low. Once the lesson runs over video the difference disappears completely, because neither tutor is travelling. What changes the outcome is whether the person has taught themes A to E and worked Paper 2 extended responses, not which exit off Al Khail Road they use.

faqs.question: How does IB Physics Paper 1A differ from Paper 1B on the current syllabus?
faqs.answer: They are two parts of the same sitting with different demands. Paper 1A is multiple choice across the five themes, testing recall and quick reasoning. Paper 1B is data-based and experimental, drawing on the tools and inquiry skills taught through the course: reading graphs, handling uncertainties, judging whether a conclusion is supported. Together they carry 36 per cent of the grade. Most students arrive strong on 1A and weak on 1B, because the data skills are taught once and rarely drilled. That makes Paper 1B the most improvable component in the whole course.

faqs.question: What share of the IB Physics grade does the scientific investigation carry?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Standard and Higher Level. It is an individual report of up to 3,000 words assessed against four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, giving 24 marks in total. Around ten hours of class time is allocated to it. The practical implication for a DP1 student in Arabian Ranches is that a fifth of the grade is decided before the examination hall, and it is the part a family has most control over, because it is written over weeks rather than in two hours under pressure.

faqs.question: Which IB Physics themes cause the most trouble for JESS Arabian Ranches students?
faqs.answer: The pattern across British-curriculum entrants is consistent, and JESS students follow it. Theme D, fields, causes the most difficulty, because gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are taught in parallel and students blur the sign conventions between them. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, comes second, mostly on unit handling between electronvolts and joules. Theme A, space, time and motion, is usually secure in content but leaks marks through graph interpretation. None of this is specific to one campus; it is what happens when IGCSE physics meets Diploma-level reasoning.

faqs.question: Does my child need a school laboratory if physics lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work belongs to the school and stays there. Your child's practical sessions, the equipment for the scientific investigation and the supervision of experiments are all the school's responsibility, whether that is JESS Arabian Ranches, Fairgreen or GEMS International School Al Khail. An online tutor works on the theory, the data handling, the question technique and the written report. No equipment is needed at home. If a tutor suggests otherwise, or offers to supply experimental data, that is a signal to stop rather than to buy.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics HL tutor cost around Arabian Ranches and Mudon?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists between AED 200 and 450 an hour and above, according to Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and BartyED's examiner-led tier at AED 650. In-home visits across Dubai are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the drive is inside the price. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300. Those are other people's figures, named and dated. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page; the free trial and a short consultation establish the plan first.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL sensible if my child is taking Mathematics AI rather than AA?
faqs.answer: It is workable but it costs extra hours. Analysis and Approaches builds the calculus fluency that makes Physics HL kinematics, simple harmonic motion and induction feel routine. Applications and Interpretation is statistics and modelling led, which helps Paper 1B data work and helps far less with derivations. A Ranches student on AI taking Physics HL usually needs the algebraic technique taught alongside the physics rather than assumed. If an engineering degree is the destination, check each named university's own mathematics requirement before Year 12 choices are locked.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics investigation without breaking IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the physics, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, show how to propagate uncertainties, discuss whether a research question is answerable, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite, edit to completion, supply a research question to be adopted or produce data. IB Gram works only on the first side of that line, and says so in writing. Providers selling finished Internal Assessments exist in this market; the risk of using one falls entirely on the student.

faqs.question: How late can an IB Physics session start after the Arabian Ranches school run?
faqs.answer: For a JESS Arabian Ranches student living inside the community, a half past four start is realistic because there is no commute to absorb. From Arabian Ranches 2 or Mudon, five o'clock is more honest. From Town Square, DAMAC Hills or Remraam, half past five to six works better once the Al Qudra Road and Hessa Street traffic is accounted for. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time and the slot is fixed weekly, so the schedule is built around the worst evening of your week rather than the best one.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session should physics revision start?
faqs.answer: Revision proper belongs in the final twelve weeks; the work before that is coverage, not revision. A sensible DP2 plan has the investigation submitted around twenty weeks out, the first untimed past paper done around twelve weeks out, the first timed Paper 2 around eight weeks out, and weekly timed papers in the final fortnight. Confirm the session dates with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org, because published dates change and a revision plan built on a wrong date is worse than one with no dates in it.

faqs.question: Which exam board does Arabian Ranches sit for physics before the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It depends on the campus. British-curriculum schools around the Ranches belt run either Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, with Core and Extended tiers and a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1, which is untiered across two written papers. Some schools use the double-award routes instead, Cambridge 0654 or Edexcel 4SD0. Ask the school examinations officer which syllabus code your child is entered for, because the code decides the past papers that are useful and the ones that waste time.

faqs.question: How do I check an IB Physics tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and expect a straight answer. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. MoHRE lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted amount with suspicion.

faqs.question: My child can do the physics calculations but loses marks on explanations. Why?
faqs.answer: Because explanation marks are awarded per linked step, and a student who understands the idea often writes the conclusion without the chain. A three-mark explain question wants three distinct statements that follow from each other, each one examinable on its own. Describe, explain, deduce and determine all demand different structures, and most students have never been shown the difference explicitly. It is a trainable skill rather than a knowledge gap, and a tutor can usually move those marks within a few weeks by marking the student's own answers against the command term.

faqs.question: Do Arabian Ranches families need to look outside the community for DP Physics at all?
faqs.answer: Not for schooling. JESS Arabian Ranches runs the English National Curriculum through IGCSE and then the IB Diploma inside the community, so a Ranches child can reach DP Physics without a long commute. Families in Arabian Ranches 2 and 3, Mudon, Town Square and Remraam usually do travel, most often towards Fairgreen International School, GEMS International School Al Khail or the Al Barsha South campuses. For tutoring the question is different: nobody needs to look locally, because the lesson arrives over video wherever the specialist happens to live.

Each one has taught the five themes end to end, marked data-based questions, and supervised students through a scientific investigation without touching the student's own writing.

intro.heading: Is there actually anyone near Arabian Ranches 2 who knows DP Physics?
paragraphs: The honest answer is: probably not, and that is the wrong question anyway. Arabian Ranches 2 is a villa community of about a dozen sub-communities — Rosa, Palma, Casa, Camelia, Lila, Azalea, Samara, Yasmin — sitting off Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street in the Dubailand belt. It is residential by design. The chance that a Diploma Programme Physics specialist who has taught Theme D fields at Higher Level happens to live in Palma, be free at 6pm on a Tuesday, and still be free in March when the mocks land, is small. Parents who search for a tutor by proximity are searching a pool of a few dozen people. Parents who search by subject are searching a pool of several thousand.

That matters more in Physics than in almost any other Diploma subject. DP Physics is not one body of knowledge that a competent science graduate can cover. The current guide runs five themes, and the places students lose marks are narrow and technical: sign conventions in gravitational and electric potential, the difference between a tangential velocity and an angular velocity in circular motion, uncertainty propagation in a gradient, and the standing-wave boundary conditions that Paper 2 keeps asking about in slightly different words. A tutor who last taught the old core-and-options structure will teach your child a syllabus that no longer exists.

There is a second problem with the proximity search, and it is specific to this part of Dubai. Arabian Ranches 2 has no metro, and the approach roads — Sheikh Zayed bin Hamdan Al Nahyan Street onto Al Qudra Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road — carry the full Dubailand school run between 2:30pm and 4:30pm. A tutor driving in from Jumeirah or Al Barsha at 4pm is spending close to an hour each way. That travel time is paid for, either in the hourly rate or in the tutor's willingness to hold the slot for eighteen months. Families in Rosa and Palma who have tried in-home arrangements usually describe the same pattern: it works for a term, then the tutor takes a closer client.

So IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE — that service exists only in India. For Arabian Ranches 2 we deliver online IB Physics tuition: one-to-one, live video, a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past papers, and a recording of the session if the student wants to revisit a derivation. What a family gives up is the physical presence of an adult in the villa. What it gets is a tutor chosen because they have taught Theme E quantum physics at Higher Level forty times, rather than because they live in Mudon. On a subject this technical, that trade is not close.

The rest of this page is written to let you judge a Physics tutor rather than trust one. It sets out the five themes and what each one costs students in marks, the full component structure with durations and weightings, the eight questions that separate someone who knows the current guide from someone who knows physics, the boundary rules on the scientific investigation, and a plain table of who can actually teach DP Physics within reach of Arabian Ranches 2.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.programmesIntro: Physics does not begin in DP1. A student in Arabian Ranches 2 arrives at Diploma Physics from one of three places, and each arrival leaves a different gap. These are the programmes we support around the Physics pathway, with what each one means for a family here.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years, 150 taught hours at Standard Level and 240 at Higher Level, built around five themes rather than the old core-plus-options structure. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%. Higher Level adds content inside every theme — rigid body mechanics, special relativity, thermodynamics, induction and quantum physics — so an HL student is not doing SL plus extras at the end.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools overwhelmingly run the May session, and DP Physics students in Arabian Ranches 2 typically start the scientific investigation late in DP1, which collides with the same term's Maths exploration and the Extended Essay first draft. Families here who plan Physics support around the April revision window usually find the investigation has already eaten the autumn. The useful planning unit is the whole of DP1, not the last term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences assessed on four criteria rather than by paper, with physics content distributed across the five years instead of taught as a block. Students are strong on investigation design and inquiry language and comparatively light on algebraic fluency, because MYP Sciences rewards a well-argued method over a fast rearrangement. That is a real strength and a real gap, and both show up in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Several IB continuum schools within the Dubailand school-bus radius run MYP before the Diploma, so a family in Arabian Ranches 2 may have one child in MYP Sciences and another in DP Physics in the same house. The bridging work is almost entirely mathematical: rearranging multi-term equations, handling standard form, and reading a gradient as a physical quantity rather than a number.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the DP entry route
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1, sat at 16 by most British-curriculum students in Dubai before the Diploma split. Extended-tier 0625 covers more than enough content for DP Standard Level, but it assesses recall and single-step calculation, where DP Physics assesses multi-step reasoning with unfamiliar context. The content overlap misleads parents into expecting a smooth entry.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools dominate Dubai by enrolment, so most Arabian Ranches 2 students reaching DP Physics come through IGCSE Physics 0625 rather than MYP. The marks they lose in the first DP1 term are rarely content marks. They are marks for method: stating an assumption, carrying a unit through, and answering the command term that was actually used.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-arabian-ranche.subjectsIntro: Physics is the reason you are on this page, but almost no DP Physics student needs only Physics. These are the subjects we cover around it for Arabian Ranches 2 families, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E under the current guide. Higher Level adds rigid body mechanics and relativity in Theme A, thermodynamics in Theme B, induction in Theme D and quantum physics in Theme E. Paper 2 extended response is where the grade is decided, because it asks for reasoning in an unfamiliar context rather than recall.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion to Physics HL. Differentiation and integration carry straight into kinematics and induction, and trigonometric identities into wave superposition. Students who take Physics HL with Maths AI SL can pass, but they work harder on every algebraic rearrangement in Paper 2.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students who want a quantitative course without the proof-heavy content of Analysis and Approaches. The gap that shows in Physics is manipulation speed, not understanding, and it is closable with targeted algebra drill rather than more physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken alongside Physics by most students aiming at engineering or medicine. Shares the same investigation model and the same uncertainty conventions, so one tutor can carry both data-analysis skillsets. Organic mechanisms and energetics are the usual pressure points.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third science in many Arabian Ranches 2 timetables. Content volume rather than reasoning difficulty is the issue, and students who manage Physics well often under-prepare Biology because it looks easier on the page. Command terms carry very different mark expectations here.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A frequent Group 4 alternative for students who want Physics plus a second technical subject. The internal assessment is a developed product with documentation, which is a different planning problem from a physics investigation, and the deadline usually falls in the same DP1 term.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered by a smaller number of Dubai schools and chosen by students who like the practical side of Physics. The design cycle and the physics investigation share evidence habits: record the decision when you make it, not three weeks later from memory.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A common Group 3 pairing for Physics students aiming at engineering with management. Diagram accuracy and precise definitions carry most of the marks, and students coming from a technical mindset often write too much and label too little.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The written tasks sit in the same DP1 term as the physics investigation, which is why Physics-focused students run out of calendar. Planning both around one timetable is part of what a Physics tutor here ends up doing.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Physics is the easiest subject to write a good TOK essay from and the easiest to write a vague one from. We coach the argument structure and the use of physics as a real-world example; the essay itself stays entirely the student's own composition.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A physics Extended Essay needs a research question narrow enough to answer with equipment a Dubai school actually owns. Supervision here means method review, feasibility checks and feedback on drafts the student has written, within IB academic-honesty rules.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Physics students in Arabian Ranches 2 still carry this load, and it is often the subject nobody plans support for.

sections.heading: What "a physics tutor near me" is really asking, and the honest answer
paragraphs: A parent typing "IB physics tutor in Arabian Ranches 2" into Google is asking three separate questions at once, and conflating them is why the search goes badly. The first is practical: who is close enough to turn up. The second is about competence: who knows the current Diploma Physics guide well enough to be useful at Higher Level. The third is about reliability: who will still be free in eighteen months when it matters. Proximity answers the first question and actively works against the other two.

Here is the arithmetic. Arabian Ranches 2 and the communities immediately around it hold a few thousand households. The subset containing an adult who has taught Diploma Physics at Higher Level is small; the subset of those who are available in the evening, hold a MoHRE private tuition work permit, and are not already committed to two other families is smaller again. Families who insist on a tutor inside the community are usually choosing between a general science graduate and a university student who sat Physics themselves three years ago. Both can help a struggling Standard Level student with Theme A. Neither will reliably move a Higher Level student from a 5 to a 6 on Theme D fields.

The competence question has a sharper edge in Physics than elsewhere because the course changed. The guide now in use restructured the subject into five themes, folded the old options away, replaced the two separate internal assessment pieces with a single scientific investigation, and split Paper 1 into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. A tutor whose mental model is the old core, additional higher level and options structure will cover content your child does not need and skip skills they are assessed on. Ask any candidate to name the five themes. The answer takes four seconds and tells you everything.

So the honest answer to the proximity question is that IB Gram does not place a tutor at a UAE address, and for this subject that is the right design rather than a compromise. Lessons for Arabian Ranches 2 run one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with the whiteboard and the past paper shared on screen. The matching constraint becomes the one that affects the grade: has this tutor taught these five themes, at this level, recently.

sections.heading: The five themes your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Diploma Physics is organised into five themes, each taught at Standard and Higher Level with additional content at Higher Level inside the theme rather than bolted on at the end. Standard Level runs to 150 taught hours and Higher Level to 240. That extra 90 hours is not revision time; it is content, and it is spread across all five themes, which is why an HL student who falls behind in the first term rarely catches up by working harder in the last.

The table below sets out what each theme contains and where students in this cluster most often stall. The stalling points are not guesses. They are the topics that come up in nearly every first consultation with an Arabian Ranches 2 family: circular motion, where students confuse tangential and angular quantities; potential, where the sign convention defeats otherwise strong students; and uncertainty, which is examined in Paper 1B and in the investigation and taught properly in very few classrooms anywhere.

Read the right-hand column as a diagnostic rather than a syllabus summary. If your child's reports say "inconsistent in Physics" and you want to know what that means, the answer is almost always one of these eight rows. A single session spent identifying which one is worth more than a term of general revision, and it is the first thing a competent tutor will do rather than starting at Theme A and working forward.

Confirm the current theme list and the Higher Level additions with your child's Diploma coordinator before building a plan around them. Guides are revised, schools teach themes in different orders, and the IB's own subject pages are the authority. We teach to the school's scheme of work, not to a generic sequence.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: what each one is worth
paragraphs: The component structure is the single most useful thing a parent can understand, because it tells you where effort converts into marks. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and is itself split: Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is a set of data-based and practical questions. Paper 2 carries 44% and is the extended-response paper. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20% and is marked internally against IB criteria before external moderation.

That split changes revision priorities. A student who drills recall is optimising for Paper 1A, which is the smallest and least discriminating part of the grade. Paper 2 is where grades are decided, and Paper 2 rewards something recall does not touch: reading an unfamiliar context, selecting the physics that applies, and writing an argument that answers the command term. A student who can do every derivation in the book and still writes "the force increases" where the paper asked them to explain will lose those marks every time.

Paper 1B is the component almost nobody prepares for deliberately. It tests the handling of real data: reading a graph, finding a gradient, propagating an uncertainty, deciding how many significant figures the final answer deserves. These are learnable in about eight focused sessions, and they transfer directly into the scientific investigation, which is why we usually schedule Paper 1B work in DP1 rather than saving it for revision.
