sections.heading: The data collection window and the Bluewaters evening
paragraphs: Lab windows are typically offered during timetabled lessons, at lunchtime, or after school. For an island family the third option carries a cost that mainland families do not face in the same way: staying an extra hour at a campus in Al Barsha or Emirates Hills means returning across the bridge at the worst time of the evening, and for a student on a school bus it may not be an option at all.

That has a practical consequence worth planning. If after-school lab time is the main route to apparatus access, the family needs a private car arrangement for those specific days, agreed in advance rather than improvised. And the tutoring session on those days should be moved or shortened, because a student who has stayed late and then crossed the bridge is not going to produce good uncertainty work at seven o'clock.

The better pattern, where the school allows it, is concentrating lab access into the timetabled and lunchtime slots and keeping the after-school option in reserve. That requires the student to arrive at each lab session knowing exactly what they are doing, which is precisely what the design sessions before the window are for. Preparation converts lab time into data; its absence converts lab time into exploration.

Ask the IB coordinator two specific questions early: when the window opens and closes, and what access is available outside timetabled lessons. Those answers determine the whole shape of the autumn, and they differ by weeks between the campuses Bluewaters students attend.

sections.heading: Physics at six o'clock: what survives and what does not
paragraphs: A Bluewaters physics student arriving home between four and half past five has limited capacity for a demanding session at six, and physics punishes tiredness more than most subjects because so much of it requires holding several quantities in mind at once.

Habit and drill work survives well. Explain-question structure is the clearest example and also the largest pool of recoverable marks in most scripts: name the quantity that changes, name the relationship, state the direction, state the consequence. That is a four-step pattern, it is mechanical, and a tired student can practise it productively. Equation drill, unit conversion between atomic mass units and joules, and sign convention discipline in kinematics all behave the same way.

What does not survive is anything conceptual on first teaching. Uncertainty propagation requires tracking absolutes and fractionals through several operations. Distinguishing field strength from potential requires holding two similar quantities apart. Gradient uncertainty from best and worst fit lines requires a student to see why two lines are needed at all. Introduce those fresh, which on this island means a weekend morning, and then practise them in the weekday slot.

Full timed papers belong at the weekend without exception, because they need an uninterrupted block and then time to mark against the published mark scheme in the same session. A paper abandoned halfway through at half past seven on a Wednesday teaches a student that they cannot sit a paper, which is both untrue and discouraging.

sections.heading: After-school clinics: use them, and know their limits
paragraphs: Most of the campuses Bluewaters students attend run some form of after-school subject support, and physics departments are often generous with it. A family paying for tutoring should use it, because it is free, it is delivered by the person who will mark the internal component, and it carries information a tutor does not have about what this particular teacher wants.

What a school clinic does well is content questions, lab access and the specific expectations of that department. A teacher explaining why a particular method will not be approved is saving a student weeks. A teacher pointing out that the department's internal deadline is a fortnight earlier than the student assumed is worth more than any session.

What a clinic cannot usually do is sustained one-to-one diagnostic work, because it is a room with several students in it and a teacher who has already taught all day. The specific thing it struggles with is the one that matters most in physics: sitting with one student while they attempt an unfamiliar data-analysis question, watching exactly where they stop, and intervening at that point. That is individual work and it takes the time it takes.

The honest division, then, is to use the clinic for content, access and departmental expectations, and to use paid sessions for the diagnostic work and the uncertainty system. A family doing both well buys fewer tutoring hours than one doing neither, which is the opposite of what most providers would tell you.

sections.heading: Uncertainty: the one skill that pays twice
paragraphs: If a Bluewaters family can buy only a handful of physics hours across two years, they should spend them on uncertainty, scheduled at a weekend when the student is fresh. It is the only part of the course examined in the written papers and assessed inside the internal component, and it is the part schools have least time to teach systematically because it sits across topics rather than inside one.

The content is finite. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, and how each is written. Propagation: add absolutes for sums and differences, add fractionals for products and quotients, multiply fractionals by the power. Error bars plotted from absolute uncertainties. Gradient uncertainty from best and worst lines drawn through those bars. And deciding how many significant figures a result can honestly carry given the precision of the measurements.

The failures are predictable. A result quoted to four significant figures from measurements good to two. Uncertainty propagated through a sum by multiplying fractionals. Error bars drawn and then a gradient taken from the best fit line alone, with no worst line and therefore no gradient uncertainty at all. Each of those costs marks on the Paper 1 data-analysis section and creates a criterion-level problem in the investigation.

Taught as one system it takes three to five focused sessions. Taught piecemeal as topics arise it never quite settles, which is why so many DP2 students can do the physics and cannot say how well they know it. On this island, those three to five sessions belong on weekend mornings in the first term of DP1, before the lab window opens.
bullets: Uncertainty is examined on Paper 1 and assessed inside the investigation
Add absolutes for sums and differences, fractionals for products and quotients
Error bars come from absolute uncertainties, in both directions where relevant

sections.heading: The mock term, when the lab is finished and the papers are not
paragraphs: By the winter of DP2 the investigation is usually written or close to it, the lab window has closed, and the only remaining variable is the written papers. The schedule changes accordingly, and families who do not change it keep paying for investigation-shaped support that has nothing left to work on.

Ask the school for component marks from the mock rather than the grade, because the grade blends three unrelated problems. Clusters of blank or abandoned questions mean theme-specific content gaps, usually fields or quantum physics because they arrive late and abstractly, and those take eight to fifteen hours of teaching in dependency order. Attempted questions marked at half credit across the paper mean explain-question structure, which is three to five hours and the largest recoverable pool.

The most diagnostic single signal is the split between multiple choice and data analysis on Paper 1. A student scoring well on the first and poorly on the second has an uncertainty and graph problem rather than a physics problem, and treating it as physics wastes the term. That is also the pattern that most often appears in students who never had the uncertainty system taught properly in DP1.

The weekend morning becomes the most valuable block at this point, because full timed papers are the highest-return activity available and they need an uninterrupted run plus marking in the same session. The weekday slot narrows to two or three identified themes rather than broad revision, which feels productive and improves very little.

sections.heading: What physics support costs, and which band each part needs
paragraphs: Physics splits cleanly by band, which makes it easier to buy well than most subjects. Equation drill, unit conversion and content catch-up on kinematics or circuits need a competent subject teacher rather than a specialist. Research question design, uncertainty as a system and criterion-level investigation feedback need somebody who has supervised an investigation against the published descriptors.

The Dubai market bands, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, rising to AED 500.

Allocated by job, an efficient two-year plan is roughly three to five specialist hours on uncertainty, four to six on research question design before the window, four to six on criterion-level write-up feedback, three to five qualified hours on explain-question structure, and ten to sixteen qualified hours of timed paper work in the final two terms. That is under forty hours, well targeted, against sixty to seventy for an unreviewed weekly arrangement.

These are market figures and not IB Gram prices. We publish no price list on these pages and start with a free trial lesson instead.

sections.heading: Honesty, regulators and starting
paragraphs: The investigation is a discrete deliverable with a deadline, which makes it the part of physics where the essay-mill end of this market is most active. One operator in our competitor research sells completed internal assessments at AED 3,750. Submitting purchased work is academic malpractice under IB rules and the finding goes against the student rather than the seller.

The legitimate line is clear. A tutor teaches the physics the investigation rests on, explains each criterion and what the descriptors require, interrogates the research question, discusses whether the method and repeats will support an uncertainty, and reads drafts the student wrote. A tutor never writes, rewrites or completes any part of the work, and never generates data. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material.

On regulators: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the Ministry of Education covering Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with no published fine schedule for working without one. IB Gram is not IB authorised, KHDA approved or ADEK approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit and has no UAE office.

To start, send the level, the school, and the four school dates: research question deadline, window open and close, write-up due and internal submission. Add a recent marked script or the investigation draft if one exists. Then take the free trial lesson, run at the day and length intended for the weekly session, with a short written note afterwards. No card is held, nothing renews, and we rematch once at no charge if the fit is wrong.

faqs.question: Can an online physics tutor help when the lab is at school?
faqs.answer: Yes, for most of what is actually assessed. Lab hours cannot be replaced and remain the school's responsibility, but the apparatus work is a smaller share of the marks than families assume. Choosing what to measure and how precisely, deciding range and repeats, propagating uncertainty, plotting error bars, taking a gradient with its uncertainty from best and worst fit lines, and writing an evaluation that names limitations all happen away from the bench. The division is clean, and scheduling follows from it: design before the window, review during, analysis after.

faqs.question: What should we ask the IB coordinator about the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Four dates and one access question. When must the research question be agreed? When does the data collection window open and close? When is the write-up due? And what is the school's internal submission date? Then ask what lab access exists outside timetabled lessons, because for an island family staying after school means crossing the bridge at the worst hour and may not be possible on a school bus. Those answers shape the whole autumn and differ by weeks between the campuses Bluewaters students attend.

faqs.question: Why does the research question matter more than the write-up?
faqs.answer: Because it constrains every criterion that follows. If the expected variation in the dependent variable is smaller than the instrument's precision, the data reads as noise no matter how carefully it is collected, and a flat dataset makes the data-analysis criterion hard and the conclusion criterion nearly impossible. The window then closes and the class moves on. Testing the question before any lab time is used takes one session: what is measured, with what instrument, to what precision, across what range, with how many repeats.

faqs.question: Our son stays after school for lab time. Should we move his session?
faqs.answer: Move it or shorten it on those days. A student who has stayed an extra hour at a campus in Al Barsha or Emirates Hills and then crossed the bridge in evening traffic is not going to produce good uncertainty work at seven o'clock, and a session held anyway teaches very little while costing full price. Agree a private car arrangement for those specific days in advance rather than improvising, and keep the demanding physics work on a weekend morning when he is actually capable of it.

faqs.question: Which physics work can be done in a tired weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Habit and drill work, which fortunately includes the largest recoverable pool. Explain-question structure is a four-step pattern: name the quantity that changes, name the relationship, state the direction, state the consequence. That is mechanical and a tired student practises it productively. Equation drill, unit conversion between atomic mass units and joules, and sign conventions in kinematics behave the same way. What does not survive is first teaching of uncertainty propagation, gradient uncertainty, or the distinction between field strength and potential.

faqs.question: Should we use the school's after-school physics clinic as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a family using both well buys fewer paid hours rather than more. The clinic is free, delivered by the person who will mark the internal component, and carries departmental information a tutor cannot have, such as why a particular method will not be approved or that the internal deadline is a fortnight earlier than assumed. What it struggles with is sustained one-to-one diagnostic work, because it is a room with several students and a teacher who has taught all day. Use it for content, access and expectations.

faqs.question: Why is uncertainty the first thing you teach?
faqs.answer: Because it is the only part of the course assessed twice: examined on the Paper 1 data-analysis section and assessed inside the scientific investigation through the data analysis and evaluation criteria. It is also the part schools have least time to teach systematically, since it sits across topics rather than inside one. Taught as a single system covering absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty plus the propagation rules, it takes three to five focused sessions. Taught piecemeal as topics arise, students reach DP2 able to do physics and unable to quantify it.

faqs.question: What does gradient uncertainty actually require?
faqs.answer: Two lines, not one. Error bars are plotted from the absolute uncertainties in each reading, and the gradient uncertainty comes from drawing both a best-fit line and a worst-fit line through those bars and comparing their gradients. Students routinely draw the error bars, take the gradient of the best-fit line alone, and report no gradient uncertainty at all, which loses the marks the data-analysis section exists to award. It is conceptual the first time and mechanical afterwards, so introduce it fresh and practise it later.

faqs.question: Our daughter's mock physics grade dropped. What should we look at?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for component marks and look specifically at the split between multiple choice and data analysis on Paper 1. Strong multiple choice with weak data analysis is an uncertainty and graph problem, not a physics problem, and treating it as physics wastes the term. Clusters of blank or abandoned questions mean theme-specific content gaps, usually fields or quantum physics, needing eight to fifteen hours in dependency order. Attempted questions at half credit throughout mean explain-question structure, which is three to five hours and the fastest fix available.

faqs.question: Our daughter is choosing between physics at Higher and Standard. Which?
faqs.answer: It is more content and genuinely different content rather than the same material examined harder. The Higher Level extensions across fields, thermal physics and quantum physics add abstraction Standard Level students never meet. The practical implication is that a tutor should be matched to the level actually being taken, since somebody comfortable with Standard Level is not automatically comfortable with the extensions. Check whether the target degree requires Higher Level before committing, because several engineering and physics programmes specify it and the choice is hard to reverse.

faqs.question: Can a tuition centre provide apparatus instead of the school?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth being clear about this because families occasionally assume otherwise. The scientific investigation is the student's own work done with their school's equipment, under their teacher's supervision and within the school's window. Apparatus at a tuition centre is not the school's equipment and using it does not satisfy the school's arrangements. If lab access is genuinely insufficient, that is a conversation with the IB coordinator rather than something a commercial provider can substitute for.

faqs.question: How many physics hours does a two-year plan really need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than a weekly arrangement if they are placed properly. An efficient allocation is three to five specialist hours on uncertainty in early DP1, four to six on research question design before the lab window, four to six on criterion-level write-up feedback, three to five qualified hours on explain-question structure in the autumn of DP2, and ten to sixteen qualified hours of timed paper work in the final two terms. That is under forty hours across two years, against sixty to seventy for an unreviewed weekly session.

faqs.question: Which band should we pay for which physics work?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty as a system, research question design and criterion-level investigation feedback need the specialist band of roughly AED 200-450 an hour, because they require somebody who has supervised an investigation against the published descriptors. Content catch-up on kinematics or circuits, explain-question structure and timed paper marking sit in the qualified band of AED 150-300. Equation and unit-conversion drill can be supervised at the budget band from AED 45. Figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the market rather than presented as our prices.

faqs.question: Do you send a physics tutor to our apartment on Bluewaters?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For physics the online format keeps a shared whiteboard archive of graphs, error bars and gradient work that a student can revise from months later, which matters because the data-analysis section rewards exactly that practice. Independent home tutors do work across the Marina and JBR at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, and for a younger child needing physical presence they can be the better choice.

faqs.question: When do UAE physics candidates sit their papers?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be right, so confirm windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For physics the dates that actually matter are the school's own in any case: research question deadline, data collection window, write-up due date and internal submission. Those govern the year and are the ones to ask for at the first DP1 parents' evening.

intro.heading: Physics is a two-year calendar, and most families meet it in month twenty
paragraphs: Diploma physics is not one long course with an exam at the end. It is a sequence of deadlines, some set by the IB and some set by your child's school, and the grade is largely decided by whether those deadlines were met in a controlled way or in a scramble. Paper 1 and Paper 2 together carry 80 per cent of the final mark. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent, is worth 24 marks across four criteria, and is completed and submitted months before the first paper is opened. By the time most Bur Dubai families start looking for a physics tutor, that 20 per cent has already been banked - well or badly.

This is why the first question we ask is not what topics your child finds difficult. It is which term they are in, and what has already been submitted. A DP1 student in their first term has the whole investigation ahead of them and can be helped with the part of the grade that is most within their control. A DP2 student eight weeks from the papers cannot change the investigation mark at all, and the useful work is entirely different: past papers, the data booklet, uncertainty handling, and the specific places in each theme where marks leak.

The calendar also has a local shape. Bur Dubai schools run mocks in the window between the submission of internal assessment work and the final papers, and a mock script is the single most useful document a physics family will see all year because it is usually a real past paper marked against the real scheme. Dubai's academic year carries other immovable features too - the KHDA-mandated subjects occupying timetable hours, and in some years a Ramadan period with a shortened school day falling inside the revision run-in. Planning tuition without those on the table produces a plan that collapses in week three.

Physics is also the Diploma subject in which the gap between knowing and scoring is widest. Students who can describe a phenomenon fluently lose marks for not quoting a value from the data booklet, for giving an answer to five significant figures when the data supports two, for omitting a unit, for failing to state an assumption, and for treating a six-mark question as a paragraph rather than as six separate marks. None of those are physics problems. All of them are repeatable, teachable habits, and they are what a well-spent hour actually addresses.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram is an online platform, and for every family in the UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For physics this is a real advantage rather than a compromise. A shared screen holds the question, the student's own working, the data booklet and the mark scheme at the same time, annotated together and saved for later. And a Higher Level physics specialist who can read a script for method marks at speed is not necessarily living within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mankhool.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-bur-dubai.programmesIntro: Four points on the physics path through a Bur Dubai school. What a tutor should be doing differs sharply between them, and the difference is the calendar rather than the content.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme year one
programmes.description: The year in which the themes are first taught and in which the Scientific Investigation is normally planned and often carried out. Mechanics and the early parts of Theme A dominate the first term, and students arriving from IGCSE or MYP meet the mathematical demand of physics for the first time. The most valuable tutoring in DP1 is mathematical rather than conceptual: rearranging, logarithms, gradients, and handling units through a calculation.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai schools, DP1 students are typically also settling into Theory of Knowledge, beginning the Extended Essay process and carrying the KHDA-mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies lessons. Physics tuition in DP1 competes for hours with all of that, which is why a single well-placed weekly hour beats an intensive block.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme year two
programmes.description: The remaining themes, the internal deadlines for the investigation where it has not already been submitted, the mocks, and then the papers. The investigation mark is settled early in this year at most schools, after which the whole remaining grade sits in Paper 1 and Paper 2. Revision that is not built on marked past-paper evidence tends to recycle what the student already knows.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit the May session, with November available as the alternative. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so every date should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly rather than taken from any tutoring website.

programmes.name: Higher Level physics
programmes.description: The same five themes taken further, with additional Higher Level content inside each and a longer, harder Paper 1 and Paper 2. The additional material in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics is where Higher Level candidates most often lose ground, partly because it arrives late in DP2 when revision pressure is already high. Planning the final terms so that this content is not met for the first time in April is a genuine strategic decision.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level physics is a common requirement for engineering admission, and students in Dubai often take it alongside Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches. That combination is demanding on time and worth timetabling honestly: two Higher Level quantitative subjects in the same week is the most common cause of a physics grade slipping for reasons unrelated to physics.

programmes.name: Standard Level physics
programmes.description: The core of all five themes without the Higher Level extensions, with shorter papers. Standard Level still carries the same Scientific Investigation worth 20 per cent and the same four criteria, which means the investigation is proportionally the same size of prize for a student with ninety fewer teaching hours. For many Standard Level candidates the investigation is the most efficient place to buy help.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving into Standard Level physics from IGCSE Coordinated or Combined Science - common in the Bur Dubai school cluster - often arrive without having met the mathematical treatment physics requires. Two or three sessions on algebraic rearrangement and gradient interpretation at the start of DP1 saves a term of confusion later.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: The five themes of the current physics guide, plus the skills that cut across all of them. Each entry says what the theme demands and the term in which it typically lands.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, work and energy, momentum, and at Higher Level rigid body mechanics and relativity. Taught first and therefore the content students are furthest from by the time they revise. Momentum and impulse questions are routinely answered with energy methods where energy is not conserved, which is a conceptual error rather than a computational one.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, the kinetic model, and current and circuits. The thermal section is where sign conventions and the difference between heat and temperature cost marks. Circuit questions reward a clear diagram and a stated assumption about internal resistance, and both are frequently omitted.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave model, wave phenomena, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Standing-wave questions require precise language about nodes, antinodes and boundary conditions, and loose description is penalised. Path-difference reasoning in interference is the discriminating skill at the top of the paper.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, with motion in a field, induction and at Higher Level a unified treatment. The analogy between gravitational and electric fields is useful and also the source of the commonest sign error in the whole course. Induction questions need the direction argument stated, not assumed.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear reactions, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and at Higher Level quantum phenomena. Usually taught last, which means it is the least rehearsed content in the final revision window. Mass-energy calculations fail on unit conversion more often than on physics.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and uncertainty bars on a graph with a worst-acceptable-line gradient. This appears in the data-based section of Paper 1 and inside the investigation, and it is the single most reliably under-taught part of the course. Two sessions move it permanently.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing axes that linearise a relationship, extracting a physical quantity from a gradient or intercept, and judging whether a trend supports a proposed relationship. Students who can plot cannot always say what the gradient physically is, and that is the question examiners ask. Central to both the investigation and the data questions.

subjects.name: The data booklet
subjects.description: Not content, but a skill. Knowing where each constant and equation sits, and that a value should be quoted from the booklet rather than recalled approximately, is worth marks on every paper. Students who have not navigated the booklet under time pressure lose minutes they do not have in Paper 2.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique inside physics
subjects.description: Rearranging multi-variable equations, indices and standard form, logarithms where they appear, small-angle work and vector resolution. This is the content of most early DP1 physics difficulty, and it is often misdiagnosed as a physics problem. It is cheaper and faster to fix as mathematics.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: Four criteria - Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion, Evaluation - at 6 marks each for 24 in total. The research question and the method decide the ceiling on all four, which is why help before any data is collected is worth several times help afterwards. A tutor advises and questions; the student designs, collects, analyses and writes every word.

subjects.name: Command terms
subjects.description: State, outline, describe, explain, determine, deduce, discuss, evaluate - each with a defined expected response. A six-mark explain question wants six distinct creditable points, not a well-written paragraph. Explicit command-term work is among the cheapest mark gains available in the subject.

subjects.name: Exam stamina and question triage
subjects.description: Choosing which question to attempt first, deciding when to leave a part and return, and writing enough to earn method marks on a question that will not be finished. These are trainable habits, practised only under full timed conditions, and they are what the final fortnight of a physics run-in should be spent on.

sections.heading: The physics grade, component by component, and when each one closes
paragraphs: Three components make a Diploma physics grade. Paper 1 and Paper 2 together carry 80 per cent and are sat at the end of the course. The Scientific Investigation carries 20 per cent, is worth 24 marks over four criteria, and closes months earlier. Understanding that timing is the difference between buying tutoring that can still change something and buying tutoring that cannot.

Put the investigation first in any plan, because it is the only component where effort translates into marks on a predictable schedule. A DP1 student has the whole thing ahead of them. The four criteria are Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation, at 6 marks each. The research question and the method constrain all four - a question with a weak independent variable or too few data points limits the data analysis, which limits the conclusion, which limits the evaluation. An hour spent interrogating a research question before data collection is worth several hours spent polishing a write-up afterwards.

Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, and the data section is where the uncertainty and graph skills from the investigation pay a second dividend. Paper 2 is extended response, where command terms and mark allocation decide the outcome: a six-mark question wants six creditable points, and students who write one well-argued paragraph routinely score two. Higher Level candidates face longer papers with the additional Higher Level content inside each theme.

What that means practically for a Bur Dubai family is a sequencing rule. In DP1, buy investigation design and mathematical technique. Early in DP2, buy whatever the internal deadlines demand. In the final two terms, buy past-paper diagnosis and technique, and accept that the investigation mark is closed. Families who reverse this order - starting tutoring in the spring of DP2 and asking about the investigation - are asking about a component that has already been banked.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years, term by term, for a physics student
paragraphs: Physics families consistently underestimate how much of the grade is decided before the final revision period. Mapping the two years out term by term makes it obvious, and it also makes clear which term you are currently in and therefore what tuition can still achieve.

The first DP1 term is mechanics and mathematical settling-in. Students arriving from IGCSE Coordinated Science or from MYP meet algebraic physics for the first time, and the difficulty they report as physics is usually mathematics. This is the cheapest term in two years to buy help, because a fortnight of rearranging and unit work removes a problem that would otherwise tax every topic for twenty months. It is also the term in which investigation ideas should first be discussed, long before a school deadline makes it urgent.

The second and third terms add themes and, at most schools, bring the investigation to data collection and a first draft. The internal deadline for that draft is set by the school and not the IB, which parents frequently do not realise - which means it is a date you can ask about and plan around. A student who collects data in the second term has time to repeat a flawed set; a student who collects in the week before the deadline does not, and the Evaluation criterion suffers for it.

DP2 carries the remaining themes, the investigation submission, the mocks and the papers. The mock is the pivot. It is usually a real past paper, so the script is the best evidence a family will get, and the right response to a disappointing mock is a ranked list of mark losses rather than a general increase in revision. The final term should contain no new content at all for a student who is otherwise on track, and we will decline to introduce it: destabilising a nearly-ready candidate in the last fortnight is a known way to lose a grade.

sections.heading: Eight weeks out: what a physics run-in can and cannot do
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most families actually present with, and it is enough to move a grade if it is spent on the right things. It is not enough to re-teach five themes, and a tutor who offers to is either padding the hours or has not thought about it. What eight weeks can do is convert knowledge the student already has into marks the mark scheme will award.

Weeks eight and seven are diagnostic. One full past paper under proper timed conditions, marked hard against the real scheme, and a second shorter data-based section. The output is a list of mark losses ranked by size, and in physics that list is almost always dominated by a small number of recurring mechanical faults rather than by topic ignorance: no unit, a value recalled instead of quoted from the data booklet, five significant figures from two-figure data, an assumption unstated, a six-mark question answered in three creditable points.

Weeks six to three are repair, taken in order of cost. The mechanical faults go first because they are cheap and they recur across every theme - one session on significant figures, units and data booklet navigation can pay back more than three sessions on fields. Then the one or two themes the diagnostic exposed, taught through past-paper questions rather than through notes, so the student meets the content in the form the examiner uses it. A second timed paper in week four checks whether the repair held.

Weeks two and one are technique and stamina only. Full papers, timed, marked, with attention to triage - which question to start, when to leave a part and return, how to write enough on an unfinished question to earn method marks. No new content. A student who meets Theme E for the first time in the final fortnight will not retain it and will lose confidence in the material they did know, and that is a worse trade than leaving the gap.
bullets: Weeks 8-7: one full timed paper, marked hard, mark losses ranked by size

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation against the clock, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is 20 per cent of the physics grade, 24 marks, four criteria at 6 marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. It is also the component with the most generous timeline and the one most often left latest, which is a combination that reliably costs marks.

Research design is won before any apparatus is touched. It needs a research question with a variable that can genuinely be varied across a useful range, a dependent variable that can be measured with a known uncertainty, controlled variables identified and actually controlled, and a method detailed enough for someone else to repeat. The commonest failure is a question that is interesting but not measurable with the equipment available, and it is detectable in a fifteen-minute conversation months before it becomes a problem.

Data analysis and Conclusion depend on the data existing in sufficient quantity and quality - enough values across enough of the range, with repeats, and with uncertainties recorded as they were measured rather than estimated afterwards. A student who collected five points once cannot produce a convincing gradient with uncertainty bars, and no amount of writing fixes that. This is the mechanical reason early data collection matters: it leaves room to repeat a flawed set.

Evaluation is where the most marks are casually given away. It asks for a reasoned assessment of the method's limitations and realistic improvements, specific to what actually happened, and students write generic lists - more repeats, better equipment, human error. A limitation that names a particular source of systematic error in that experiment and explains its effect on the result scores; a generic list does not. On what a tutor may do here: we ask questions, give feedback on the student's own draft, and teach uncertainty and graph technique. We do not design the experiment, process the data or write any part of the report. That boundary protects the student, because an IB academic honesty breach falls on them.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened day and when a Bur Dubai physics session can really happen
paragraphs: A revision plan that ignores the UAE academic calendar fails in practice however good it looks on paper. Two features matter for Bur Dubai families. The first is the school day itself: Dubai private schools carry mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and a minimum advised lesson length of 25 minutes. Those hours are real and they sit in a week that also has to carry six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay.

The second is Ramadan, which in some years falls inside the physics revision window. School days are shortened, routines change, and a family that has committed to a fixed 5pm session will find it does not work. The practical answer is to agree in advance that the slot moves for that period - often to a later post-Iftar time - rather than losing sessions to repeated rescheduling. Families who plan for it keep their hours; families who do not lose three or four weeks of a run-in.

Then there is the ordinary Bur Dubai afternoon. A Diploma student living in Bur Dubai or Karama is frequently at a school across the creek or out towards Al Garhoud, and the return journey at five o'clock is not predictable. A session time that works in October on a quiet day is not the same as one that survives February. Choose the slot against the worst realistic commute, not the best one, because in an eight-week run-in a session lost to traffic is more than a tenth of the plan.

This is also where the online format earns its keep in a way that has nothing to do with teaching quality. The hour does not depend on anyone travelling. A student who gets home at 5.40 instead of 5.10 joins late rather than missing the lesson. During exam season, when sleep and routine matter, a session that reliably happens at the same time each week is worth more than a nominally better tutor whose arrival time varies.

sections.heading: What Diploma physics tuition costs around Bur Dubai, and what the calendar does to the bill
paragraphs: The useful way to think about physics tuition cost is not per hour but per component. The investigation is 20 per cent of the grade and a well-timed six-session block in DP1 touches it. The papers are 80 per cent and an eight-week diagnosed run-in in DP2 touches those. Everything else is optional. Families who buy a standing weekly hour for two years without reference to the calendar spend several times more and do not reliably get a better grade.

With that framing, here is the market. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with in-home one-to-one visits including travel at AED 180 to 350. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which buys homework supervision rather than Higher Level physics. BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Which band is worth paying depends on the component. For DP1 mathematical technique, the mid band is sensible - this is competent teaching of straightforward material and prestige adds nothing. For investigation design and for past-paper diagnosis in DP2, the specialist band earns its premium, because reading a script for method marks and spotting a research question that will cap three criteria are judgement skills rather than knowledge. For technique practice in the final fortnight, almost nothing is worth a premium, because the work is the student's own.

All of these figures are market rates taken from each provider's own published prices as read in October 2026. None are IB Gram prices; we do not publish a rate card on a landing page. We hold no office or centre in the UAE, and we are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, KHDA or any other authority. We also publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor count, because we cannot attach a sample size, a date and a method to any of them.

sections.heading: A physics tutor in a Bur Dubai flat against one-to-one online
paragraphs: Families here ask for a home tutor for reasons worth taking seriously. A tutor in the room is visible, a parent can judge whether the hour was used, and in a flat with younger children it is simpler than a journey. Those are legitimate arguments.

Our position stated before payment rather than after: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai family is one-to-one over live video. We put that on the page because two providers ranking for these searches route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without disclosing where the tutor actually sits, and a family should not discover the delivery model after paying.

For physics specifically, the supply argument is decisive. A teacher who can read a Higher Level script for method marks at speed, who knows where a research question will cap the Evaluation criterion, and who has taught the current guide's Theme D treatment properly is a narrow specialism. The probability that such a person lives within a twenty-minute drive of Al Mankhool and is free at 5pm on a Tuesday is low. Insisting on proximity means accepting a generalist, and in physics the difference between a generalist and a specialist is visible in a single session.

The format itself also suits the subject. Physics work is diagrams, graphs, equations and worked solutions, and a shared screen holds the question, the student's own working, the data booklet and the mark scheme simultaneously, annotated in the tutor's hand and saved for the student to revisit before the next timed paper. Paper passed across a table cannot do that. The market data above shows what the in-home premium buys as well: in-home rates run AED 180 to 500, and the amount above the online band pays for a drive rather than for teaching.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the dates we will not publish
paragraphs: Three things on this page are deliberately absent, and the reasons matter. First, there is no specific IB examination or results date anywhere on it. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, which means no date we could publish would be verified, and a wrong date in a physics revision plan is a date a family acts on. Confirm every session and results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. Any tutoring website quoting you an exact IB date should be asked where it came from.

Second, there is no IB Gram rate card and no claim of accreditation. We are not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge International or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry; we do not hold one and do not describe ourselves as KHDA approved. We hold no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

Third, there is no statistic without its source. Every AED figure names the provider that published it and the month it was read. We publish no satisfaction percentage, star rating or tutor headcount, because we cannot attach a sample size, a date and a method to any of them. Two competitors in this market publish self-asserted star ratings in their structured data that differ from the figure on the visible page, which is a structured-data policy violation as well as a trust problem.

On permits, the position is checkable. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and states a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount should be quoted to you. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise.

process.title: Tell us the term, not the topic
process.description: The first question is which Diploma term your child is in and what has already been submitted. A DP1 student and a DP2 student eight weeks from the papers need completely different work, and the investigation mark is either still open or it is closed. That single answer shapes everything else.

process.title: A free trial, built around real evidence
process.description: One session at no cost with the tutor you would continue with, spent on a past-paper question or on the student's own investigation draft. You get a written note of what was found - the mark losses, or the research-question risk - whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Rank the mark losses before teaching anything
process.description: In DP2 we start with a timed paper marked hard against the real scheme, and we teach in order of marks lost. In physics the top of that list is usually mechanical - units, significant figures, data booklet values, unstated assumptions - rather than a theme the student does not know.

process.title: Fix the hour against the real commute
process.description: Choose a slot that survives February traffic rather than October traffic, and agree in advance that it shifts during Ramadan. Oud Metha and Al Mankhool households can often hold a 4.30pm start; Karama, Deira-side and Al Nahda families are usually better after six. The hour is in Gulf Standard Time.

process.title: Measure with timed papers
process.description: Every two to three weeks, a full paper under proper conditions, marked hard. That is the only honest measure. We report the mark and the error pattern, and if the pattern is not changing we change the tutor or the method rather than selling more hours.

process.title: Stop at the right point
process.description: The final fortnight is the student's own technique practice, and we will say so instead of booking sessions nobody is measuring. We also decline to introduce new content in the last two weeks, because destabilising a nearly-ready candidate is a known way to lose a grade.

whyPoints.title: We plan from the calendar, not from a topic list
whyPoints.description: Which term your child is in determines whether 20 per cent of the grade is still in play. A tutor who starts with a syllabus checklist rather than with what has already been submitted is working on the wrong component, and in DP2 that is an expensive mistake.

whyPoints.title: The investigation taken seriously, early
whyPoints.description: Twenty per cent of the physics grade sits in 24 marks across four criteria, and the research question caps all four. We interrogate the question before any data exists, which is the cheapest high-value hour available in the whole two years.

whyPoints.title: Mechanical marks before content
whyPoints.description: Units, significant figures, data booklet values, stated assumptions and one creditable point per mark recur across every theme. Fixing them is cheap and compounds, and it is routinely skipped in favour of re-teaching a topic the student already half-knows.

whyPoints.title: A hard boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and give feedback on the student's own investigation. We do not design the experiment, process the data or write any part of the report. That boundary is written down because the consequence of crossing it under IB academic honesty rules falls on the student, not on us.

whyPoints.title: No dates we cannot verify
whyPoints.description: There is no IB examination or results date on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so we cite no date we have not been able to confirm, and we tell you to get it from your coordinator. A wrong date in a revision plan is worse than no date.

whyPoints.title: Clear about where the tutor sits
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, stated before payment. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE. The real argument is supply: a Higher Level physics specialist free at 5pm who also lives near Al Mankhool is an unlikely combination.

faqs.question: How much of the IB physics grade is decided before the exams?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent. The Scientific Investigation is worth 24 marks across four criteria and is submitted at a school deadline months before Paper 1 and Paper 2, which together carry the other 80 per cent. That is why the first question we ask is which term your child is in. A DP1 student still has that whole component in front of them. A DP2 student in the spring cannot change it at all, and tutoring hours spent discussing it at that stage are spent on something already banked.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years should physics tutoring start?
faqs.answer: It depends on which component you want to move. For the investigation, DP1 - specifically before any data is collected, because the research question caps all four criteria. For mathematical technique, the first DP1 term, since most early physics difficulty is algebra rather than physics and a fortnight of work there removes a problem that taxes twenty months. For the papers, an eight to twelve week diagnosed run-in in DP2 is enough and is what most families actually need. A standing two-year hour costs several times more without reliably delivering more.

faqs.question: What are the five themes in the current IB physics guide?
faqs.answer: Theme A is space, time and motion - kinematics, forces, energy and momentum. Theme B is the particulate nature of matter, covering thermal physics, the gas laws and electric circuits. Theme C is wave behaviour, including simple harmonic motion, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Theme D is fields, taking gravitational, electric and magnetic fields together. Theme E is nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds further content inside each theme, and Themes D and E usually arrive latest, which is why they are the least rehearsed in revision.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics but lose marks on the papers?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme rewards specific behaviours rather than understanding. The recurring losses are: no unit on an answer, a constant recalled approximately instead of quoted from the data booklet, five significant figures produced from two-figure data, an assumption left unstated, and a six-mark question answered as one well-written paragraph when it wants six distinct creditable points. None of these are content problems. A full paper marked hard against the real scheme usually shows which of them is costing the grade within a single session.

faqs.question: What is the physics investigation marked out of, and on what?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four, across four criteria at six marks each: Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation. That total represents 20 per cent of the final physics grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Research design is decided before any apparatus is touched, Data analysis depends on the quantity and quality of data actually collected, Conclusion can only be as good as that analysis, and Evaluation is written from notes kept during collection. The sequence is why early work on it is worth several times late work.

faqs.question: Where exactly must a tutor stop on the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can interrogate a research question, ask whether a variable can actually be varied and measured enough times, teach uncertainty propagation and graph technique, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor cannot design the experiment, collect or process the data, or write any part of the report. Crossing that line is an academic honesty breach under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the tutor. We put the boundary in writing before any investigation work starts.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Higher and Standard Level physics in practice?
faqs.answer: Higher Level is 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, with additional content inside each of the five themes and longer, harder papers. The Scientific Investigation is the same four criteria and the same 20 per cent at both levels, which means it is proportionally the same prize for a Standard Level student with ninety fewer hours - often making it the most efficient place for a Standard Level candidate to buy help. The Higher Level extensions in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics are the usual ground where Higher candidates lose marks.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions does an eight-week run-in usually need?
faqs.answer: Typically eight to twelve, roughly one or two a week, with full timed papers built in rather than added at the end. Weeks eight and seven go on diagnosis. Weeks six to three repair the mechanical faults first and then the one or two costliest themes. Week four carries a second timed paper to check the repair held. The last fortnight is technique and stamina with nothing new introduced. Buying thirty sessions for an eight-week window buys fatigue rather than marks, and we will say so.

faqs.question: What does IB physics tutoring cost in Dubai, and when is the premium worth it?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026: Bestimate's Dubai table puts IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors. Those are the market, not our prices. The premium is worth paying for investigation design and script diagnosis, which are judgement skills, and not for final-fortnight technique practice, which is the student's own work.

faqs.question: Do you send a physics tutor to our flat in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India. Every lesson for a Bur Dubai family is one-to-one over live video, stated before payment rather than after. For physics the format suits the subject: a shared screen holds the question, the student's own working, the data booklet and the mark scheme at once, annotated live and saved. The stronger argument is supply - a Higher Level physics specialist free at 5pm who also lives near Al Mankhool is an unlikely combination.

faqs.question: Why is uncertainty work so important in IB physics?
faqs.answer: Because it is assessed twice. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and uncertainty bars with a worst-acceptable-line gradient appear in the data-based section of Paper 1 and sit at the heart of the investigation's Data analysis criterion. It is also the most reliably under-taught part of the course, partly because it is taught early and rarely revisited. Two dedicated sessions typically move it permanently, and the return shows up in two separate components rather than one.

faqs.question: Should my child take Higher Level physics and Higher Level maths together?
faqs.answer: It is a common combination for engineering applicants and it is demanding on time rather than on ability. Two Higher Level quantitative subjects in the same week is the most frequent reason a physics grade slips for reasons unrelated to physics: both carry heavy problem sets, both have internal assessment deadlines, and in a Dubai timetable they sit alongside mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies lessons as well as TOK and the Extended Essay. If the combination is needed for admissions, plan the two years rather than discovering the load in DP2.

faqs.question: What should we ask for after the physics mock besides the grade?
faqs.answer: The script, and the mark scheme if the department will release it. Mocks usually use a real past paper, so the losses on that script are the losses likely to recur. A grade tells you where the student stands; the script tells you why, and lets a first tutoring session produce a ranked list of mark losses rather than spending an hour establishing what the department already knew. Ask also which themes had not yet been taught at the time of the mock, so a low mark is not misread as a gap.

faqs.question: How should a physics revision plan handle Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: By agreeing in advance that the session time moves for that period rather than rescheduling week by week. School days are shortened and household routines change, so a fixed 5pm slot that worked in January often will not hold, and families who try to keep it tend to lose three or four weeks of a run-in. A later post-Iftar slot, agreed before the period starts, protects the hours. Dubai timetables also carry the KHDA-mandated subjects throughout, which is part of why Diploma weeks are tighter than families expect.

faqs.question: Why are there no IB session dates anywhere on this page?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the IB directly. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any session or results date we published would be unconfirmed, and a wrong date in a physics revision plan is a date a family acts on. UAE candidates sit the May session, with November as the alternative sitting, and that much is safe to state. For the actual dates, ask your school's IB coordinator or check ibo.org. Any tutoring site quoting you an exact IB date should be asked for its source.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting physics tutoring with only three weeks left?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, with a narrow brief. Three weeks will not repair a theme and should not try. What it can do is drill the mechanical mark-losers - units, significant figures, data booklet navigation, stating assumptions, writing one creditable point per mark - and run two or three full timed papers to build stamina and question triage. That is a real grade effect for a student who knows the content and is leaking marks. If the content genuinely is not there, we will tell you so rather than sell the hours.

If the investigation is still ahead, that is 20 per cent of the grade and the cheapest place to buy help. If the papers are eight weeks away, the work is diagnosis and technique and nothing else. Book the free trial lesson and we will tell you which of those you are in. One hour, no cost, with the tutor you would continue with, spent on a real past-paper question or on the student's own investigation draft, with a written note of what was found. All lessons for Bur Dubai families are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

Each one works through the themes in the order your child's school teaches them, marks written answers against the command terms, and gives feedback on the scientific investigation at the stages where feedback is permitted.

intro.heading: What a Business Bay family is usually asking when they search for an IB Physics tutor
paragraphs: Almost nobody searches for an IB Physics tutor in Business Bay in September. The search happens in week six, after the first unit test on kinematics or on the particulate nature of matter comes back at a 4 when the student has always been a 6 elsewhere. Physics is the subject where a strong student can be working hard, understanding the lessons, and still losing marks in a pattern nobody at home can see. That pattern is diagnosable, and diagnosing it is what the first lesson should be for.

Business Bay is a vertical neighbourhood. Executive Towers, Churchill Towers, the Marasi Drive blocks and the towers along the Dubai Water Canal house a lot of Diploma-age students whose schools are somewhere else entirely: Al Jaddaf, Sobha Hartland, Nad Al Sheba, Al Safa, Al Sufouh, Festival City. A student living above Bay Avenue may be on a school bus for fifty minutes each way. That single fact decides more about Physics tutoring here than anything else, because it decides how much usable study time exists between the school gate and bedtime on a weeknight.

The current IB Physics course is organised into five themes rather than the old topic list, and it is examined through two papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation worth a fifth of the grade. Higher Level is not Standard Level with harder numbers. It is additional content inside every theme, longer papers, and a marked step up in the algebraic fluency the questions assume you already have. Students who coast through SL mechanics on intuition meet a wall in HL fields and in nuclear and quantum physics, where intuition is no help and the mathematics is doing the work.

What a Physics tutor is actually for, in this subject specifically, is three things. The first is command-term discipline: knowing that "state" wants one line and no reasoning, that "explain" wants a mechanism, and that "determine" expects a value with a unit and a visible method. The second is uncertainty and graph work, which carries real marks in Paper 1B and in the IA and which most students have never been taught systematically. The third is past papers under time, marked against the real mark scheme, with the student made to correct their own script rather than watching someone else correct it.

IB Gram delivers all of this to Business Bay as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Physics this is a straightforward advantage rather than a compromise. The pool of people in Dubai who can teach HL fields properly and mark an investigation against the published criteria is small, and it is not distributed by postcode. Online, a family in Business Bay gets the person who knows the syllabus, not the person who can reach the Canal by 5pm.
bullets: Themes A to E, taught in the order your child's school teaches them, not in syllabus order
Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data analysis treated as two different skills, because they are
Scientific investigation feedback mapped to the four assessment criteria and their mark bands
Command terms drilled explicitly: state, outline, explain, determine, deduce, discuss

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-business-bay.programmesIntro: Physics in an IB school does not start in Year 12. The thinking a Diploma physicist needs is built in the Middle Years Programme, and the gap between MYP science and DP Physics is where most of the early Diploma damage happens. These are the programmes we support for Business Bay families, and what each one actually needs.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years, Standard or Higher Level, organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Assessment is two written papers plus one internally assessed scientific investigation. Higher Level adds content within each theme and sits longer papers. Students normally take Physics alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and the maths choice changes how comfortable the Physics feels.
programmes.countryNote: Business Bay students sit Diploma Physics at schools across the central corridor and beyond: the IB continuum at Al Jaddaf, the Diploma at Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba, and schools further out towards Al Sufouh and Festival City. Dubai's private schools are licensed and inspected by KHDA, which publishes inspection reports school by school; check the current rating on KHDA's own site rather than on any agency page, including this one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences assessed against four criteria rather than against content recall: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. MYP marks are criterion levels out of 8, not percentages, which parents routinely misread. The experimental design and data-processing criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma scientific investigation, and a student weak in them at MYP 5 will be weak in the IA two years later.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP transition is the single most requested piece of science tutoring we see from the Downtown and canal-side communities. A Business Bay student moving from MYP 5 science into DP Physics HL has to absorb a new mathematical register and a new assessment language in the same term. Six to eight weeks of bridging work over the summer removes most of that shock and is cheaper than remediation in Year 13.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, transdisciplinary, with no formal external examination. Science appears inside units of inquiry rather than as a timetabled subject. Tutoring at this stage is almost never about physics content; it is about number fluency, measurement, reading a scale, and writing an explanation that answers the question asked. Those are the skills that later show up as marks in Paper 1B uncertainty questions, which is why primary-stage numeracy work is not a detour from physics.
programmes.countryNote: Several Business Bay families have a Diploma student and a primary-age sibling in the same flat, often at different schools in different directions. Where that is the case we schedule the two students back to back on the same evening so the household loses one slot rather than two, which matters more in a two-bedroom tower apartment than it does in a villa community.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-business-bay.subjectsIntro: This is a Physics page, so the grid below is the Physics course itself: the five themes, the investigation, and the two neighbouring subjects whose weakness most often shows up as a Physics problem. Each line says what the theme assesses and where students in Dubai schools most often lose the marks.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces and momentum, work and energy, circular motion, and at HL the rigid-body and relativity extensions. The marks go missing in vector resolution, in sign conventions on deceleration, and in energy questions where students write a formula instead of identifying which energy converted into which.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal energy transfers, the gas laws, the kinetic model, and at HL thermodynamics and entropy. The common failure is temperature-versus-thermal-energy confusion in explanation questions, and unit slips between kelvin and degrees Celsius inside a gas-law calculation that was otherwise correct.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, wave phenomena, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with HL extending the phase and diffraction treatment. Students lose marks describing superposition in words rather than in terms of path difference, and on standing-wave questions where the boundary conditions are never stated.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, magnetic effects of electric currents, motion in electromagnetic fields, and at HL induction and the full field-potential treatment. This is where Higher Level separates from Standard Level most sharply, and where algebraic weakness stops looking like a maths problem and starts costing physics marks.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Structure of the atom, radioactive decay, fission, fusion, and at HL quantum physics and the standard model. Taught late in Year 13 and therefore the theme most often half-learned before the exam. Recall-heavy by comparison with the rest of the course, which makes it the cheapest theme to repair in a short run of lessons.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation (IA)
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: One individual investigation marked out of 24 against four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is the student's own work. A tutor may discuss the physics, question the method, and comment on whether the conclusion is supported by the data. A tutor may not design it, write it or edit it to completion.

subjects.name: Uncertainties, graphs and data analysis
subjects.levels: SL and HL, examined in Paper 1B
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, error bars, lines of best fit and worst-fit gradients, and log-linearisation. Almost no student arrives having been taught this systematically, and it is the single highest-yield block of lessons available in the subject because it pays in Paper 1B and in the IA at once.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.levels: HL and SL, taken alongside Physics
subjects.description: The co-requisite that decides whether HL Physics feels hard or impossible. Logarithms, radians, differentiation of trigonometric functions and confident algebraic rearrangement are assumed, not taught, in Physics lessons. When a Physics problem is really an algebra problem, we say so and fix the algebra.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Frequently taken with Physics by Business Bay students aiming at engineering or medicine. The two subjects share the data-analysis and investigation skill set, so uncertainty work done for Physics pays twice. Where a student is sinking in both, we usually start with the shared skills rather than with either syllabus.

sections.heading: What an IB Physics tutor in Business Bay actually does in the first three lessons
paragraphs: An IB Physics tutor in Business Bay should spend the first lesson diagnosing and almost none of it teaching. The useful opening move is a short mixed set of questions drawn from across the five themes, done out loud with the working visible, so the tutor can see where the student stops: at the physics, at the algebra, at the command term, or at the clock. Those four failures look identical on a report card and need four different responses.

The second lesson should produce a written picture of the pattern. In practice the pattern is rarely exotic. A typical Business Bay Diploma student arrives losing marks in three places at once: resolving vectors in theme A, explaining rather than describing in extended response, and guessing at uncertainty in any question that mentions a gradient. None of those is a knowledge gap. All three are repairable inside six weeks, and all three keep costing marks for two years if nobody names them.

The third lesson is where tutoring stops being general and starts being specific to the school. A student at an IB continuum school in Al Jaddaf and a student at a Diploma school in Sobha Hartland will be on different themes in the same week, with internal investigation deadlines months apart. A tutor who does not ask for the school's scheme of work is teaching a syllabus rather than teaching a student, and the parent is paying for the difference.
bullets: Lesson one: diagnose across themes, do not teach a topic

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level actually adds to each
paragraphs: The current IB Physics course replaced the old topic-and-option structure with five themes, each taught at Standard Level and extended at Higher Level. The practical consequence for a Business Bay parent is that you can no longer tell from a topic title whether your child is doing the SL or the HL version of it. Both levels study fields; only one of them studies induction and the full potential treatment.

The table below sets out what each theme covers and what the Higher Level extension adds, together with the error that costs students the most marks in that theme. It is deliberately specific. A tutor who can tell you that your child's problem is sign convention in theme A rather than "mechanics" is a tutor who can fix it in two lessons.

Note the asymmetry. Themes A and D carry the heaviest Higher Level extensions and the greatest mathematical load, and together they account for most of the HL-versus-SL grade gap we see in Dubai cohorts. Theme E is the lightest extension relative to its examinable content, which is why a student two months out from the May session is usually better served securing theme E than attempting to rebuild theme D from scratch. Confirm the current content of each theme against the subject guide your child's school issues, since the IB revises guides on a published cycle.

One further point about teaching order, which matters more here than it would in a single-school town. Business Bay students are spread across six or seven schools in four directions, and those schools do not teach the themes in the same sequence. One may open Year 12 with theme A and leave fields until the spring; another runs theme B and theme C first so the laboratory work lines up with its own timetable. A tutor who assumes syllabus order will be a term out of step with the class by November. We ask for the school's scheme of work in the first week and follow that, which is why the brief you send us should name the school rather than just the level.
