sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: three different skills on two papers
paragraphs: IB Physics is assessed through two written papers and one internally assessed investigation. The investigation carries a fifth of the grade at both levels. What catches students out is that Paper 1 is really two papers stapled together: a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section that share a time allocation but share almost no skills. Students who revise "Paper 1" as one thing routinely under-prepare the half that is easier to improve.

Paper 1A is multiple choice, no marks for working, and rewards accuracy under time more than depth. Paper 1B is data based: a given experiment, real measurements, and questions about uncertainty, gradients and whether a conclusion is supported. That section is learnable in a way that the rest of the course is not, because the question types repeat. Paper 2 is extended response and is where command terms decide the mark: a question that says "outline" and receives three paragraphs scores the same as one that receives one correct line, and takes six times as long.

The weightings and durations below follow the current subject guide for first assessment under the present syllabus. Treat them as the shape of the assessment rather than as a quotation, and confirm the exact figures against the guide your child's school issues or against the IB's own subject page, since the IB revises both guides and timings on a published cycle.

There is a scheduling consequence to this that affects how we plan lessons for a commuting student. Paper 1B work can be done in short bursts, because the question types are small and self-contained: one gradient, one uncertainty, one evaluation of a stated conclusion. Paper 2 work cannot. A Paper 2 question needs a clear forty minutes and a student who is not already exhausted, which in Business Bay means it belongs in the lesson slot itself rather than in weeknight homework after a fifty-minute bus ride. So we tend to put Paper 2 practice inside the session and leave Paper 1B sets as the work between lessons. That split is not a style preference; it follows directly from what each component demands of a tired student at eight in the evening.

sections.heading: Where Business Bay students actually lose Physics marks
paragraphs: After enough diagnostic lessons the errors stop being individual and start being a short list. The first and largest is command-term failure. Physics mark schemes pay for specific actions, and a student who writes a good explanation to a question that asked them to state a value has produced nothing the examiner can award. This is not a physics weakness at all, which is why it survives years of hard work: the student revises content, the content was never the problem.

The second is uncertainty. Ask a Diploma Physics student to state the percentage uncertainty in a gradient and the room goes quiet far more often than it should. The topic appears in Paper 1B every session and in the IA's data-analysis criterion, so it is the highest-value six lessons available in the subject, and almost nobody arrives having had them. A tutor who starts a Business Bay student on advanced theme D problems before checking uncertainty is leaving easier marks on the table.

The third is specific to commuting students, and it is time. A student on a bus from Business Bay to Al Sufouh and back is losing ninety minutes a day. The realistic consequence is that homework physics gets done late and tired, errors get embedded rather than corrected, and the student arrives at a 7pm lesson already spent. We plan around this by making the lesson itself the hard-thinking slot and keeping between-lesson work to one bounded question set rather than an open revision instruction, which is honest about how much weeknight capacity exists in a tower apartment in term time.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, 24 marks, and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: The Physics internal assessment is one individual scientific investigation, marked out of 24 against four criteria, and it carries a fifth of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Those four criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Students lose most of their IA marks in the last two, because the first two feel like work and the last two feel like filling in a form. They are not: evaluation is where a marker looks for genuine engagement with what went wrong and why.

There is a hard boundary around what help is permitted, and it matters more here than anywhere else on this page. Under IB academic-honesty rules the investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may discuss the physics, question whether a method controls what it claims to control, explain how uncertainty propagates, and say whether a conclusion is supported by the data in front of them. A tutor may not choose the research question, design the method, process the data, draft any section, or edit a draft to completion. IB Gram does not write coursework, and any provider offering to supply a finished investigation is offering your child a malpractice finding.

The practical sequence we use is therefore front-loaded. Most of the value sits before the data exists, in the lesson where the student explains their proposed method out loud and discovers that the variable they planned to control is not actually controlled. Fixing that costs one lesson at the planning stage and is unfixable after the measurements are taken. sections.heading: What a Physics tutor costs in Dubai, and why the specialist band sits where it does
paragraphs: Physics at Higher Level sits at the top of the Dubai tutoring market, and it is worth understanding why before looking at the numbers. The pool of people who can teach theme D properly and mark an investigation against the published criteria is small. Scarcity, not prestige, is what puts specialist IB science at the upper end of the published bands, and it is why the gap between a general science tutor and an HL Physics specialist is wider in this subject than in almost any other.

The figures below are market rates published by other providers and by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are not IB Gram's price list. Reading them from the top down: a premium named or examiner-marketed tutor is advertised at AED 650 by BartyED; the specialist IB and IGCSE band runs roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to 450 and above; a qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; and budget online provision starts far lower, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors.

Two things follow for a Business Bay family. First, the cheapest band and the specialist band are not the same product, and for HL Physics the difference is whether the tutor can mark theme D work at all. Second, the in-home premium is not a quality premium; it is a travel premium, and on a canal-side commute it buys nothing a parent wants. For context on the wider cost picture, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package reported at AED 1.5 billion. Rather than publishing our own rate card, we run a free trial lesson and quote after it. Ask any provider what an hour costs, whether the figure includes VAT, and what the cancellation terms are, in writing, before you book a block.

sections.heading: Online versus an in-home Physics tutor in Business Bay
paragraphs: Parents in Business Bay do search for a home tutor, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. In-home tutoring in Dubai is a real market, priced at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour inclusive of travel according to the figures above, and it suits some families: a younger child who will not sit still at a screen, or a household that wants a visible adult presence during the session. For a Diploma Physics student it is usually the wrong trade.

The reason is pool size. Business Bay is twenty minutes from Downtown on a clear road and considerably more at 6pm on Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road. Any tutor who commits to arriving at a Business Bay tower by 6pm has effectively limited themselves to clients within one short drive, and your child has effectively limited themselves to whoever is inside that radius and free at that hour. For HL Physics that radius may contain nobody who has taught theme D. Online, the constraint disappears and the question becomes who knows the syllabus.

To be explicit: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Business Bay families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing both ways, and the session recorded or the working saved so a student can revisit a derivation they half-followed at 7pm on a school night. sections.heading: The May session, counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session. Working backwards from it is more useful to a Business Bay parent than any calendar of dates, because what matters is which decisions have already closed by the time you notice a problem. By February of Year 13 the subject and level choices are fixed, the investigation is submitted or nearly so, and the only remaining variable is examination technique. A family that starts in February is buying technique; a family that starts in September of Year 12 is buying the grade.

Dates are the part of this subject where agency pages are least reliable, so here is our position plainly. We do not publish IB session or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and we will not restate a date a parent might act on without reading it at source. Ask your child's IB coordinator, who holds the school's confirmed internal and external deadlines, and check ibo.org for the published session windows. For the Cambridge and Pearson qualifications an IB student may sit alongside the Diploma, note that candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, and any UAE page quoting a March exam window is quoting the wrong country's calendar.

What we can give you is the sequence and the lead time, which do not change year to year. The milestones below are the ones families miss, in the order they arrive. Confirm every date against your school's own calendar and the relevant board's live timetable, because provisional timetables are revised and a restated date is a liability rather than a service.

sections.heading: Permits, the regulator, and what a Business Bay parent can actually verify
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, and states a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow that parents are rarely told. The permit is free, so any tutor claiming a fee as a reason for a higher rate is mistaken. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the ministry's words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted as unverified, including the figures that circulate on forums.

The school-level regulator is separate. Dubai's private schools are licensed and inspected by KHDA, Abu Dhabi's by ADEK, Sharjah's by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit; an individual online tutor does not, and neither does IB Gram claim one. We hold no KHDA, ADEK, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership, and you should be sceptical of any tutoring page in this market that says it does.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside Diploma Physics
paragraphs: A Business Bay student taking HL Physics is also taking subjects that have nothing to do with their Diploma choices, and families new to Dubai are often surprised by them. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its published requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

Why this belongs on a Physics page: these subjects occupy timetable hours and generate homework, and a Year 12 student balancing them against HL Physics has less capacity than the Diploma workload alone suggests. There is also a hard content limit to know about. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so tutoring in these subjects follows the school's prescribed material and nothing else. The federal baseline behind all of it is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of the process is short. You tell us the school, the level, the theme currently being taught and the two or three evening slots that actually work from a Business Bay tower in term time. We propose a tutor who teaches that level, and the first lesson is a free trial. The trial exists so you can see whether the tutor can diagnose, which is a different question from whether they are pleasant, and both parent and student should judge it on that.

Sometimes we cannot staff a request immediately. HL Physics in a specific theme, at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, in the fortnight before mocks, is the hardest combination in this subject, and there are weeks when the right person is fully booked. When that happens we say so rather than substituting a general science tutor and hoping. The options we will put to you are a different time slot with the right specialist, a short wait with a date attached, or a named alternative tutor with their actual subject depth described so you can decide. We would rather lose the booking than place the wrong tutor on Higher Level Physics.

One more thing worth saying before you pay anyone, us included. Ask your child's Physics teacher first. Most Dubai schools run subject clinics or support sessions that are already covered by the fees you pay, and a teacher who sees the student daily can often name the problem in one conversation. If that conversation has happened and the gap is still there, tutoring is the right next step, and you will brief us far better for having had it.

process.title: Tell us the syllabus position, not just the subject
process.description: The useful brief is three lines: the school, Standard or Higher Level, and which theme the class is on this week. Add the date of the next assessment and the school's internal investigation deadline if you know them. That is enough to match a Physics tutor properly and to plan the first month of lessons without wasting a session on discovery.

process.title: Free trial lesson, judged on the diagnosis
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing and is deliberately a diagnostic rather than a lesson. The tutor works a mixed set of questions with your child and reports back where the breakdown happens: physics, algebra, command term or timing. Ask for that in writing afterwards. A tutor who cannot tell you which of the four it was has not earned the second lesson.

process.title: Set a pattern that survives a Business Bay term
process.description: One or two sixty-minute lessons a week at a time that works after the school run, usually 6.30pm or later on weeknights, with Saturday mornings as the fallback. Between-lesson work is one bounded question set, not an open revision instruction, because a commuting student has less weeknight capacity than a timetable suggests.

process.title: Track errors by theme, and change the plan on the evidence
process.description: Every marked question set feeds a running error log by theme. After six weeks the log, not an impression, decides where the hours go. If the pattern says theme C uncertainty rather than theme D content, the plan changes. You see the log, so you can see what you are paying for and when it is no longer needed.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by theme, not by subject label
whyPoints.description: A tutor who teaches theme D fields properly is a different person from a general science tutor, and in Higher Level Physics the distinction is the whole product. We match by the level and the content being taught, and if the right specialist is not free we tell you instead of substituting.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty and graph work taught deliberately
whyPoints.description: Data analysis repeats in every Paper 1B and carries a criterion in the investigation, yet almost no student arrives having been taught it systematically. We treat it as its own block of lessons rather than a footnote, because it is the highest-yield work available in the subject.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and give feedback on your child's own investigation. We do not design it, draft it, process its data or edit it to completion, and we will not take the work of a student who asks us to. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, this is a line worth stating in writing.

We publish no success rate, no average score and no star rating, because we cannot produce the underlying data for any of them. Figures without a source are a reason to distrust a page, not to trust it.

The in-home premium in Dubai is a travel cost, and on a central-corridor commute it buys nothing your child's grade will notice.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics tutor in Business Bay actually cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours. Published figures for Dubai put specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate quoting AED 200 to 450 and above. A qualified online subject tutor runs about AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. Budget online provision starts far lower, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Higher Level Physics sits at the upper end because the pool of people who can teach fields and mark an investigation is small. We quote after a free trial lesson rather than publishing a rate card, and you should ask any provider whether the figure includes VAT.

faqs.question: My child is fine at SL Physics but drowning since starting HL. Why the jump?
faqs.answer: Because Higher Level adds content inside every theme and assumes a level of algebraic fluency that Standard Level lets a student get away with not having. The two places it shows first are theme D, fields, where induction and the full potential treatment make the mathematics unavoidable, and theme A, where the rigid-body extension punishes shaky vector work. Nine times in ten the presenting problem is not physics at all; it is rearrangement, logarithms and radians. We diagnose which it is in the trial lesson and, if it is the algebra, we fix the algebra rather than teaching more physics on top of it.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on help with the Physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. The investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may discuss the underlying physics, question whether a proposed method controls what it claims to, teach uncertainty propagation on the student's own measurements, and ask whether a conclusion is genuinely supported by the data. A tutor may not choose the research question, design the method, process the data, draft any section or edit a draft to completion. IB Gram does not write coursework. Any provider offering to supply a finished investigation is offering your child a malpractice finding, which in the IB is an expulsion-level risk.

faqs.question: How much of the Physics grade does the internal assessment carry?
faqs.answer: One fifth, at both Standard and Higher Level, from a single individual scientific investigation marked out of 24. The marks split evenly across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. Most students lose marks in the last two, because conclusion and evaluation feel like paperwork after the experiment is done. They are not. Evaluation is where a marker looks for honest engagement with what limited the experiment and what would realistically improve it. Confirm the current criterion structure against the subject guide your child's school issues, since the IB revises guides on a published cycle.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Paper 1 and Paper 2, and are they revised the same way?
faqs.answer: Both, and no. Paper 1 is two different things sharing a time allocation: section A is multiple choice across all five themes, rewarding speed and accuracy with no marks for working, and section B is data based, asking about uncertainty, gradients and whether a conclusion holds. Section B is learnable because the question types repeat; section A needs timed practice in blocks of twenty. Paper 2 is extended response, and there the deciding factor is command terms. Revising Paper 1 as a single entity is the most common planning error we see, and it under-prepares the half that improves fastest.

faqs.question: Which Physics theme should we repair first if exams are ten weeks away?
faqs.answer: Usually not the one that feels worst. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, is taught last and revised last, so it is typically the thinnest and also the most recall-heavy, which makes it the cheapest marks available in a short run. Theme D is the opposite: heavy, mathematical, and not rebuildable from scratch in ten weeks. Before choosing, we want an error log from marked past papers rather than an impression, because students and parents both routinely misidentify the weakest theme. Two timed papers marked properly will tell you more than six weeks of guessing.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to apartments in Business Bay for Physics lessons?
faqs.answer: Not ours. IB Gram delivers all UAE tutoring one-to-one over live video; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. In-home tutors do exist in Dubai and the market prices them at roughly AED 180 to 500 per hour including travel. For Diploma Physics we think that is the wrong trade, because a tutor committed to reaching a Business Bay tower by 6pm can only serve clients within one short drive, and your child is then choosing from whoever is inside that radius rather than from whoever can teach Higher Level fields.

faqs.question: Does my child need Maths Analysis and Approaches to cope with HL Physics?
faqs.answer: Not formally, but the overlap is real and worth planning for. HL Physics assumes confident algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, radians and comfort with gradients, and Analysis and Approaches builds those more directly than Applications and Interpretation does. Students taking Applications alongside HL Physics can absolutely succeed; they more often need explicit support on the mathematical technique, because Physics lessons use it without teaching it. Ask your child's school which combination their Physics teachers see working, and if the maths is the bottleneck, treat it as a maths problem rather than running more physics past it.

faqs.question: Which schools do Business Bay Physics students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Almost none inside Business Bay itself, which has very little secondary provision. Diploma students commute, mostly to the IB continuum school in Al Jaddaf, the Diploma schools at Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba, and schools further out towards Al Safa, Al Sufouh and Festival City. This matters to a tutor because the school determines the teaching order of the five themes and the date of the internal investigation deadline. We ask for the school name in the first message for that reason. We have no affiliation with any school named on this page.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can a Physics lesson realistically start here?
faqs.answer: Later than most agency pages admit. A Business Bay student bussing to Al Sufouh or Al Safa is often not home before 4.30pm and is not usefully alert at 5pm. Most families in Executive Towers and the canal-side blocks settle on 6.30pm or 7pm on two weeknights, with Saturday morning as the alternative. DIFC households, where working hours run late, more often take 8pm. Students at Sobha Hartland and Nad Al Sheba schools have the shortest commute in this cluster and can genuinely use a 5pm slot. We schedule around the real commute, not an idealised one.

faqs.question: Will a tutor promise my child a specific Physics grade by May?
faqs.answer: No, and you should treat any provider that does so with suspicion. Nobody controls the paper, the cohort, the boundaries or how a student performs on the day, so such a promise is either meaningless or it is a refund policy in disguise, in which case ask for the exact terms in writing before you pay. What can honestly be committed to is specific and checkable: a named diagnosis after the trial lesson, a weekly marked question set, an error log by theme that you can read yourself, and a straight answer when the hours have stopped buying anything. We publish no success rate or average score, because we cannot produce the underlying data for one.

faqs.question: Does the MoHRE private tutor permit apply to an online Physics tutor?
faqs.answer: The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so distrust any amount quoted to you. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold one and under which category.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable to pay my child's class Physics teacher for extra lessons?
faqs.answer: Be careful here. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and verify the current wording against the authority's own policy document before relying on it. The practical answer is that your school's own free support clinics are the right first step and cost nothing, but a paid private arrangement with your child's own teacher is a conversation to have with the school, not with us.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level Physics specialist is available when we need one?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Higher Level Physics at 5pm Gulf Standard Time in the fortnight before mocks is the tightest combination in this subject, and there are weeks when the right person is fully booked. Rather than placing a general science tutor and hoping, we put three options to you: a different time slot with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date attached, or a named alternative tutor whose subject depth we describe honestly so you can judge. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit. Ours does, because the alternative is a wasted month.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB exam and results dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so we will not restate a session or results date that a parent might act on without having read it at source. Your child's IB coordinator holds the school's confirmed internal and external deadlines and is the right person to ask; ibo.org publishes the session windows. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications an IB student may sit alongside the Diploma, note that UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any UAE page quoting a March exam window is quoting the wrong country's calendar.

intro.heading: The physics year, read backwards from the date that matters
paragraphs: Physics in the Diploma is not hard in the way students expect. The content is finite and the mathematics, at Standard Level in particular, is manageable. What catches students out is the shape of the two years: a long first year that feels unhurried, a second year in which the scientific investigation, the mock papers and the final preparation all land inside a few months, and an internal deadline structure set by the school that nobody warned them about.

A City Walk family searching for a physics tutor is almost always inside that compressed stretch. The useful question is therefore not what should my child learn, but what can the time remaining actually deliver. Eight weeks before a mock, the answer is paper technique plus two themes. Eight months before the final session, the answer is different and much larger. Twelve weeks before an investigation deadline, the answer is almost entirely about method and data rather than about content at all.

That is why this page is built as a calendar. It counts the Diploma physics year backwards from the end, names what should already be true at each stage, and sets out what is still fixable at each point and what is not. Nothing in the competitor set does this. Across the pages researched for this project, no provider named a session, a deadline or a results window at all, which is a strange omission given that the calendar is what makes tutoring urgent.

On dates specifically, one caution. Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session, and that is the session a plan should be built around. This page does not publish a specific IB examination or results date, because the IB's own site could not be read directly for this project and a date a parent acts on must be confirmed at source. Your school's IB coordinator holds the internal deadlines, which in practice govern a term far more tightly than the external window does.

One comparison helps, for a household with a second child on a different board. Cambridge and Pearson publish their windows plainly: a candidate here sits Cambridge papers in the June series or the November series, and Pearson International GCSE ran its November 2026 timetable from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in the January that followed. The Diploma calendar is far less visible to a parent than that, which is exactly why the school-set internal deadlines have to be written down somewhere a family can see them.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; that is an India-only service. For physics the online form costs very little, because the lesson is a shared whiteboard with a past paper on screen, and it buys a great deal: a Higher Level physics specialist is a thin pool anywhere, and a pool further thinned by a twenty-minute driving radius around Al Safa Street is thinner still.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-city-walk.programmesIntro: Physics arrives late in the IB continuum, but what happens before it decides how the first term of the Diploma goes. These are the four stages a City Walk student passes through.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria: Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science, each scored out of 8. The design and evaluation criteria are the direct ancestors of the Diploma scientific investigation, and a student who has written them well for five years arrives at the Diploma investigation already competent.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within reach of City Walk run MYP Years 4 and 5 rather than IGCSE. The consequence for physics is a student arriving in Year 12 with strong inquiry skills and, often, less numerical fluency than an IGCSE 0625 student. That gap is identifiable in the first weeks and closable in a term if it is named.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the alternative route in
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Electricity and electromagnetism are the strands that generate the most difficulty and the most lost marks. A student from this route arrives at the Diploma with better equation handling than an MYP student and usually weaker experimental design, which is the mirror image of the MYP profile.
programmes.countryNote: The British-curriculum schools nearest City Walk feed both post-16 routes, so a Year 11 physics student here may be heading for A Level or for Diploma physics. The two need different Year 11 summers: the Diploma route benefits most from work on uncertainty and graphing, which IGCSE barely touches.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Available at Standard and Higher Level, with content organised into themes A to E and assessment split between written papers and the scientific investigation. Higher Level extends several themes substantially and adds depth rather than simply more topics, which is why a Standard Level student moving up mid-course rarely succeeds without a planned catch-up.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai cohorts sit the May session. The internal timetable at a Dubai school typically places the investigation draft in the first half of Year 13 and mock examinations shortly after, so the autumn term of the second year carries most of the load. Confirm all dates with the school's IB coordinator rather than with a tutoring page.

programmes.name: University entry with physics
programmes.description: Engineering, physics and several medical-adjacent programmes commonly expect Higher Level physics or an equivalent, often with a specified grade. The relevant mathematics requirement usually accompanies it, which is why physics and the mathematics route should be chosen together rather than sequentially.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE universities, Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate process from the admission requirement. No sourced IB points threshold for equivalency was available for this page, so verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority rather than relying on any figure found on a tutoring site.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-city-walk.subjectsIntro: Diploma physics content sits in five themes. The notes below name what each covers and where students lose marks, so that a plan written in the final weeks can be written in this vocabulary rather than in whole-subject terms.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extensions
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy, extended at Higher Level into rigid-body mechanics and relativity. Momentum questions lose marks when students treat a collision as an energy problem. Graph-gradient interpretation is tested constantly and practised rarely.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal energy transfers, the greenhouse effect, gas laws and current electricity. The greenhouse content is examined with real precision and revised casually, which is a predictable mark loss. Specific heat capacity calculations lose marks to unit slips rather than to misunderstanding.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extensions
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, the wave model, wave phenomena, standing waves and resonance, and the Doppler effect. Standing-wave questions require a diagram with nodes labelled; students who describe without drawing forfeit marks the mark scheme has allocated to the diagram.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extensions
subjects.description: Gravitational and electromagnetic fields, motion within them, and induction at Higher Level. This is the theme most often half-learned. Field and potential are routinely confused, and the sign conventions in gravitational potential energy questions cost marks for students who understand the physics.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with HL extensions
subjects.description: Atomic structure, radioactive decay, fission, fusion and stellar processes, with quantum content extended at Higher Level. Often taught last and revised least, so it is reliably the weakest theme in a mock. It is also among the most self-containable, which makes it good value late in a plan.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error analysis
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and error bars with a line of worst fit. Examined in Paper 1's data section and central to the investigation. IGCSE barely touches it, so most students arrive with no foundation here at all.

subjects.name: Graphing and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing axes that linearise a relationship, extracting a constant from a gradient, and stating what the intercept means physically. A high-return skill: it appears in the data paper and in the investigation, and it is teachable in two or three focused sessions.

subjects.name: Experimental method and control of variables
subjects.description: Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, choosing a measurable range and justifying repeat readings. The investigation's framing criterion depends almost entirely on this, and a weak choice here caps the later criteria regardless of how well the write-up is executed.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation on a self-chosen research question, marked against published criteria and typically worth a fifth of the final grade. The commonest failure is a question with no measurable independent-variable range, which leaves nothing to analyse and no trend to conclude from.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique
subjects.description: Multiple choice plus a data-based section. Multiple choice rewards elimination and quick estimation rather than full calculation, and the data section rewards uncertainty handling. Both are technique, both are drillable, and both are usually neglected in favour of content revision.

subjects.name: Paper 2 technique
subjects.description: Extended response across the themes. Explain questions want a causal chain, and a student who states the conclusion without the mechanism typically scores one mark of four. This is the single most repairable mark loss in Diploma physics and it responds to two or three sessions of deliberate practice.

sections.heading: The Diploma physics year counted backwards
paragraphs: Work from the end. The final papers sit at the close of the second year, in the May session for Dubai cohorts. Before them comes the school's mock window, usually in the first half of the second year. Before that, the scientific investigation has to be collected, written and submitted to an internal deadline. Before that, the investigation's research question has to be chosen and approved. Every one of those gates is set by the school, not by the IB, and they arrive in that order whether or not anybody has planned for them.

The practical consequence is that the autumn term of the second year carries most of the load, and it is the term in which a family has least spare capacity to react. A student who reaches that term with Themes A to C secure and uncertainty handling competent has a manageable year. A student who reaches it with Theme D half-learned and no experience of error propagation has a difficult one, and the difficulty will be attributed to physics being hard rather than to a schedule.

This is also why the eight-week question has a different answer at different points. Eight weeks before a mock, technique and two themes. Eight weeks before an investigation deadline, method and data, with content almost irrelevant. Eight weeks before the final papers, timed papers and the weakest theme, with nothing new introduced. Treating those three as the same request is the commonest planning error in Diploma science support.

The table below is the year in reverse. It deliberately uses relative windows rather than dates, because no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source and a date a parent acts on must come from the school's IB coordinator or from the IB directly.

sections.heading: Paper 1 and Paper 2: what each one is actually testing
paragraphs: The two written papers reward different things, and a student who revises for both the same way underperforms on at least one. Paper 1 combines multiple choice with a data-based section. Multiple choice is a speed and elimination exercise: full calculation on every item will run a student out of time, and the skill is recognising which option is impossible. The data section is where uncertainty handling, graph reading and gradient interpretation are tested directly.

Paper 2 is extended response across the themes, and it rewards structure. An explain question wants a causal chain: this happens, which causes this, which results in that. A student who writes the final clause alone has given the examiner the conclusion and none of the reasoning, and typically scores one mark out of four on a question they understood completely. Teaching that chain is mechanical, fast and the highest-return intervention available in Diploma physics.

Mark-per-minute arithmetic matters as much here as command-term discipline. If a paper carries roughly one mark a minute, a six-mark question that has consumed fifteen minutes has already cost marks elsewhere whatever it eventually scores. Students almost never calculate this for themselves. A tutor who enforces it with a timer from the first session changes the score on the next timed paper rather than on some distant one.

Confirm durations and weightings against the current subject guide for your child's examination year, because the group 4 guides were revised and an older sibling's experience is not a reliable guide. Your child's physics teacher has the authoritative version.

sections.heading: The order to revise five themes in
paragraphs: Revision order is a scheduling decision and it should not default to the order the themes are printed in. Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, is usually taught last and revised least, which makes it reliably the weakest theme in a mock and also the best value late in a plan: much of it is self-containable and does not depend on earlier themes.

Theme D, fields, is the opposite. It is the theme most often half-learned, because field and potential are easy to conflate and the sign conventions in gravitational potential questions punish students who have understood the physics perfectly well. It also underpins a great deal of Higher Level content, so repairing it early pays forward. A plan that leaves Theme D to the final fortnight has mis-sequenced itself.

Themes A to C generally need consolidation rather than teaching, because they were taught first and have been revisited. The exceptions are momentum, where students default to energy methods, and standing waves, where the mark scheme allocates marks to a labelled diagram that students describe in prose instead. Both are single-session fixes once identified.

Running through all five themes is the uncertainty and graphing layer, which is not a theme at all but is examined in the data section and is central to the investigation. For a student arriving from IGCSE, this is usually the largest single gap and the one least likely to be noticed, because no classroom test has ever asked for it directly.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the deadline that governs it
paragraphs: The investigation is an individual piece of experimental work on a research question the student chooses, marked against published criteria and typically worth around a fifth of the final grade. Those are the only marks in the course that can be earned calmly, with feedback, months before the examination hall. They are also the marks most often thrown away, and almost always for the same reason.

The reason is the research question. A question with no measurable independent-variable range produces no trend, and no trend means the analysis and conclusion criteria cannot score well however carefully the write-up is done. A question requiring equipment the school does not have produces a compromise that undermines the method. A question that is simply a textbook experiment repeated gives the student nothing to evaluate. All three are fixable in one conversation before any data is collected, and unfixable afterwards.

So the sequencing is: interrogate the question, agree the uncertainty treatment and the graphing approach, take a pilot reading, then collect. A student who collects first and thinks about analysis afterwards frequently finds that the data cannot be processed into the graph that would show the relationship, and there is no time to repeat it. That is a scheduling failure rather than a physics failure, and it is the one this page is most concerned with.

The honesty line is absolute here. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the design, point at a passage and say the reasoning does not follow, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write any part of the submission, supply data the student did not collect, or edit the text until the voice is no longer the student's. Crossing that line is academic misconduct under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, up to the loss of the Diploma.

sections.heading: Ramadan, mock season and the Dubai school calendar
paragraphs: A revision plan that ignores the local calendar is a plan the family abandons by week three. Dubai schools run their own mock windows, study-leave periods and internal deadlines, and those are what actually govern a term. Add Ramadan, when the shape of a day changes substantially, and a plan written in generic terms stops working almost immediately.

The practical adjustments are simple once they are acknowledged. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots, which for a Year 13 student is often a better working window than a late afternoon anyway. Around mock weeks, sessions stop being teaching and become paper review. During school study leave, frequency usually increases and session length shortens, because a student revising all day does not benefit from a two-hour lesson in the evening.

School trips, examination leave for a sibling and the long summer break are the other three disruptions worth planning around rather than reacting to. The summer between the two Diploma years is the single most useful block of time available to a physics student, and it is almost always wasted. Two weeks of uncertainty and graphing work in July removes most of the first-term difficulty in Year 13.

None of this is complicated. It requires only that the plan be written with the school's calendar open rather than from a template, which is also why a plan should be a short written document with dates on it rather than a verbal understanding about Tuesdays.

sections.heading: What physics tutoring costs in this market
paragraphs: Physics specialists sit at the upper end of the Dubai market, which is a supply fact rather than a pricing strategy. The researched bands, read in October 2026 and published by the providers named, run as follows. Budget online tutoring advertises from roughly AED 33-150 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly AED 150-300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

Above that, IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate reporting AED 200-450 or more. That is the band a Higher Level physics request usually belongs in, because the pool of people who can teach Theme D properly and mark a data-based paper to the scheme is genuinely small. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650; any claim of current examiner status should be evidenced before it is paid for.

In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, Bestimate reporting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors AED 200-500. Monthly packaging in the market runs near AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and Bestimate's monthly estimate for a specialist exam-year weekly hour is AED 1,000-2,000 or more.

All of the above was published by others and is reproduced so a City Walk parent can check it before any conversation. None of it is an IB Gram price list. IB Gram quotes after the free trial lesson, against a named tutor, a named level and a session length, and the trial happens before any payment or card detail is taken.

sections.heading: Why a physics specialist is reached online rather than driven to
paragraphs: IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, so this is an explanation of the service shape rather than an argument against a competitor's product. In-home tutoring is real, other providers sell it at the rates above, and for a younger student who cannot yet self-manage a session it is the better option. For Diploma physics in City Walk the calculation goes the other way, and sharply.

Consider the actual request. A Year 13 student at Higher Level, losing marks on Paper 1's data section and on Theme D field questions, nine weeks from a mock. The person who fixes that has marked data-based papers and can distinguish a field misconception from a sign-convention error in thirty seconds. The number of such people who will also drive to Al Safa Street for a 5.30pm start on a weekday is small, and the constraint has nothing to do with teaching quality.

Physics also loses very little in the online form. The lesson is a shared whiteboard with a past paper on screen and the student working through it while the tutor watches and interrupts, which is structurally what a good physics lesson is in a room. The session is recorded, which matters here because a worked mechanism chain is exactly the sort of thing a student needs to replay before a timed paper.

The gap between the qualified online band and the in-home band in the published rates is, in large part, the hour that Al Wasl Road takes at five o'clock. That hour is real and a travelling tutor is right to charge for it. The question for a family is what it buys, and for a thin specialism it buys physical presence while costing reach.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can and cannot do
paragraphs: Set expectations properly, because the honest version is more useful than the optimistic one. In eight weeks, with one session a week and work done between, a physics student can reliably automate explain-question structure, fix Paper 1 pacing, build a working competence in uncertainty and graphing, and repair one or two themes to a solid standard. Those are real gains and they show up in the next timed paper rather than in some distant future.

In eight weeks a student cannot learn two years of content, cannot move safely from Standard to Higher Level, and cannot rescue an investigation whose research question produced no measurable trend. If any of those is the actual situation, a provider who says yes is selling a family a term. The right answer is to name what is achievable, do that, and be clear about what is not.

There is a middle category worth naming. Theme D half-learned is repairable in eight weeks and is worth prioritising because so much else rests on it. A complete absence of uncertainty handling is repairable in three or four sessions and transforms the data section. A student who has never sat a full paper under timed conditions will gain marks from doing three, regardless of content. Each of those is specific and each is deliverable.

What makes the difference is starting from a marked paper. A diagnostic, timed and marked to the published scheme, converts eight weeks of good intentions into an ordered list of four things. Without it, the hours get spent on whatever the student feels least confident about, which is rarely where the marks are.

process.title: Name the date and the component
process.description: The useful first message says when the next deadline is and which component is failing. A mock in nine weeks and Paper 1 data questions, or an investigation draft due in three weeks with no data collected. That sentence determines the entire shape of the plan, and it is the difference between a focused block and a general arrangement.

process.title: Diagnostic paper before any hours are committed
process.description: A timed past paper, marked against the published scheme, read theme by theme and component by component. It produces an ordered list of what to fix. This is the step most tutoring arrangements skip, and skipping it is why some run for months without the marks moving.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial with the named tutor
process.description: The first lesson is free, taken with the physics specialist who would teach the course rather than a demonstrator, and no card details are collected beforehand. One trial per student per subject. Afterwards, the test is whether the tutor identified something the school had not already said.

process.title: A written plan counted backwards
process.description: You get a short plan with the school's own dates on it: the mock window, the investigation draft deadline, the study-leave period. The work is sequenced backwards from those rather than forwards from the first lesson, which is what makes a block finish in the right place.

process.title: Marked work every week
process.description: Questions set between sessions come back marked to the scheme with the mark allocation shown, so a student can see that an explain question scored one of four and why. Parents receive that feedback. The number reported is the mark, not an impression of effort or engagement.

process.title: Full papers in the final fortnight
process.description: The block ends with complete papers under timed conditions, because pacing is a separate skill from physics and only improves against a clock. A student who can answer every question but needs two hours for a ninety-minute paper has a timing problem, and that is what the last two weeks exist to solve.

whyPoints.title: The plan runs backwards from your school's dates
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines at a Dubai school govern a Diploma term far more tightly than the external session does. Investigation drafts, mock windows and study leave are what a plan has to fit around, so the plan is written with the school's calendar open rather than from a template, and it has dates on it.

whyPoints.title: Technique before content, because it moves faster
whyPoints.description: Explain-question mechanism chains, Paper 1 elimination and mark-per-minute pacing are mechanical, teachable and show up in the next timed paper. Most revision effort goes to content the student already half-knows. Reordering that is the cheapest improvement available in Diploma physics.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty treated as the real gap it is
whyPoints.description: Students arriving from IGCSE have usually never propagated an uncertainty or drawn a line of worst fit, and no classroom test has told them so. It is examined in the data section and it is central to the investigation, and three or four focused sessions build a working competence.

whyPoints.title: The investigation is sequenced, not polished
whyPoints.description: The research question sets the ceiling, so the first conversation is about measurable range, available equipment and a pilot reading. Feedback on a draft recovers communication marks, which are real and small. Getting the order right is worth more than any amount of work on the write-up.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates published without a source
whyPoints.description: The IB's own site could not be read directly for this project, so no specific examination or results date appears here. Dubai cohorts sit the May session and your school's IB coordinator holds the internal deadlines. Cambridge and Pearson dates elsewhere on this site are sourced and attributed; IB dates are not, and so are not stated.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary is said out loud
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the investigation criteria and give written feedback on the student's own draft. They do not write it, supply data or edit it to completion, and the student is told so in the first session. In a market where one operator sells completed internal assessments, stating this plainly is the point.

faqs.question: My child has a physics mock in eight weeks. What can an IB physics tutor change?
faqs.answer: Realistically: explain-question structure, Paper 1 pacing, a working competence in uncertainty and graphing, and one or two themes repaired to a solid standard. Those gains tend to appear in the next timed paper rather than months later, because they are technique rather than content. What eight weeks cannot do is teach two years of material, move a student between levels safely, or rescue an investigation whose research question produced no measurable trend. The plan should start with a timed diagnostic paper marked to the published scheme, then spend the hours strictly where the marks went.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics but score badly on Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answers give the conclusion without the mechanism. An explain question wants a causal chain: this happens, which causes this, which results in that. A student who writes only the final clause has handed the examiner the result and none of the reasoning, and typically scores one mark of four on a question they understood fully. It is the single most repairable mark loss in Diploma physics and responds to two or three sessions of deliberate practice, enforced afterwards by marking every answer against the scheme rather than for correctness.

faqs.question: What is the data-based section of Paper 1 testing?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty handling, graph reading and gradient interpretation, which is content IGCSE physics barely touches. Students are asked to propagate absolute, fractional or percentage uncertainties through a calculation, draw error bars, fit a line of worst fit and say what a gradient or intercept means physically. Most students arrive at the Diploma with no foundation here and no awareness of the gap, because no classroom test has asked for it directly. Three or four focused sessions usually build a working competence, which makes it one of the better returns on tutoring time.

faqs.question: When does the scientific investigation actually have to be finished?
faqs.answer: The school sets the deadline and it typically falls before the mock window in the second year, with a draft due several weeks earlier and the research question approved late in the first year. Those internal dates govern the term far more tightly than the external session does, so they are the ones a plan should be built around. Ask the subject teacher or IB coordinator for the written internal timeline rather than working from an assumption, and treat the research-question approval date as the real start of the project.

faqs.question: Which physics theme is usually weakest in a Dubai mock?
faqs.answer: Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, because it is generally taught last and revised least. It is also largely self-containable, which makes it good value late in a revision plan. Theme D, fields, is a different problem: it is the theme most often half-learned, with field and potential routinely conflated and gravitational sign conventions costing marks from students who understand the physics. Theme D repays early work because Higher Level material builds on it, so a plan that leaves it to the final fortnight has mis-sequenced itself.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the research question for the investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can and should interrogate it, which is different from supplying it. The right first conversation asks what will be varied, over what range, measured with what, and what the data will look like if the hypothesis is wrong. A question with no measurable range produces no trend, and no trend caps the analysis and conclusion criteria whatever the write-up does. The question has to be the student's own choice; the tutor's job is to stress-test it hard enough that a weak one is rejected before any data is collected.

faqs.question: Will a tutor write or edit my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: No. The boundary is that a tutor teaches the criteria, questions the design, points at a passage and says the reasoning does not follow, and gives written feedback on the student's own draft in the student's own file. A tutor does not write any part of the submission, supply data the student did not collect, or edit the text until the voice is no longer the student's. Crossing that line is academic misconduct under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, up to the loss of the Diploma itself.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is deeper rather than simply broader. Higher Level extends several themes substantially, adds content such as rigid-body mechanics and induction, and asks for more sustained reasoning in extended response. The mathematics demand also rises, which is why the physics and mathematics route choices should be made together. A student moving up mid-course rarely succeeds without a planned catch-up block, because the extension material was taught alongside the shared content rather than appended at the end of it.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor visit homes in City Walk?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; home visits are an India-only service. The practical reason matters here. The person who can fix a Paper 1 data problem and a Theme D misconception is a specialist, and the pool of such people who will also drive to Al Safa Street for a 5.30pm weekday start is small for reasons unrelated to teaching quality. Physics also loses little online, because the lesson is a shared whiteboard with the paper on screen either way.

faqs.question: What does Diploma physics tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Physics specialists sit at the upper end of the market. Budget online tutoring advertises from roughly AED 33-150, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65, which is a weak fit for data-paper technique. A qualified subject tutor online is roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and that is where most Higher Level requests belong. Those are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan and mock weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. During Ramadan sessions shift to post-Iftar slots, which for a Year 13 student is often a better working window than a tired late afternoon. Around mock weeks the sessions stop being new teaching and become paper review. During school study leave, frequency usually rises and session length shortens, because a student revising all day does not benefit from a long evening lesson. A plan written with the school calendar open survives a term; one written from a template does not.

faqs.question: What should my child do with the summer between Year 12 and Year 13?
faqs.answer: It is the most valuable unused block in the whole course. Two weeks of uncertainty and graphing work in July removes most of the first-term difficulty in the second year, because that layer cuts across every theme and is never taught as a topic. Revisiting Theme D at a relaxed pace is the second priority, since Higher Level content leans on it. What is not worth doing is reading ahead through new content, which schools will teach anyway and which the student will meet without context.

faqs.question: How does an online physics lesson actually run?
faqs.answer: The student works and the tutor interrupts. A shared whiteboard both can write on, past papers and mark schemes shared on screen so both are looking at the same question, and a recording afterwards so a worked mechanism chain can be replayed before a timed paper. Questions set between sessions come back marked to the published scheme with the mark allocation shown, and parents receive that written feedback. Sessions sit on Gulf Standard Time around the school day and move after Iftar during Ramadan on request.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB exam dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own site returns an automated-access error, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and a date a parent acts on should not come from a tutoring page. What can be said is that Dubai Diploma cohorts sit the May session, and that the internal deadlines set by your school usually govern the term more tightly than the external window. Ask the IB coordinator for the written internal timeline and check the external dates on the IB's own site.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting physics support in Year 12 rather than waiting?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is cheaper in every sense. One hour a week alongside the course consolidates each theme in the week it is taught, which is when the student has the most context and the least accumulated confusion. It also builds uncertainty and graphing from the first term rather than bolting them on late, and it means Theme D is secure before Higher Level content starts resting on it. A student who reaches the second-year autumn term with Themes A to C solid has a manageable year rather than a difficult one.

A physics specialist for that specific problem will take the free 45-minute trial lesson over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no card details collected beforehand. You then get a written plan counted backwards from your school's own dates, with a diagnostic paper in week one and full timed papers at the end. If the match is wrong it changes at no charge, and when the marks have moved the sensible thing is to stop.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-culture-villag.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IB Physics for families in Culture Village: matched to Higher or Standard Level, experienced with the scientific investigation criteria, and able to teach uncertainty propagation rather than mention it.

intro.heading: The physics is the easy part
paragraphs: Plenty of people can teach mechanics. Fewer can explain why a student's otherwise excellent investigation scored eleven out of twenty-four, and that second capability is what decides an IB physics grade. The internally assessed scientific investigation is worth twenty per cent of the final mark and is assessed on four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Three of those four have very little to do with physics knowledge and everything to do with method.

The same pattern runs through the written papers. Data-based questions present unfamiliar material and reward a student who reads axes, units and uncertainty bars before reading the question. Extended-response questions reward a student who noticed that the command term asked for an explanation and supplied one rather than a description. Calculation questions reward a student who carried units through every stage and did not round an intermediate value. None of that is physics. All of it is marks.

Uncertainties deserve naming separately because they are the clearest example of a scored skill that students treat as bookkeeping. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty. Adding absolute uncertainties for sums and differences. Adding percentage uncertainties for products and quotients. Multiplying percentage uncertainty by the index for a power. Determining a gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines through error bars. Those five rules appear in every series and are routinely half-remembered.

The current physics syllabus is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level covers additional content within those themes and is assessed with longer papers. Paper structures and durations were revised for the current guide, so we work from the subject guide your school holds rather than from a remembered arrangement, and your school's IB coordinator is the authority on it.

No IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unverified exam date is something a family would plan a whole term of revision around. UAE schools sit the main May session. The dates that matter more to a physics plan are internal: the school's deadline for the investigation and its draft stages.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Culture Village or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we operate only in India. For physics specifically, the common objection to online delivery is practical work, and it is worth answering directly: the investigation is designed, analysed and written by the student at school and at home, and what a tutor contributes is design critique, uncertainty treatment and criterion feedback, none of which requires being in the room.

Standard Level students frequently underestimate the investigation precisely because the written content is lighter, which leaves a fifth of the grade exposed.
programmes.countryNote: The pattern we see from Culture Village families is a Standard Level student coping with the content and scoring poorly on the investigation, usually because the evaluation criterion received a paragraph. Since evaluation carries six of the twenty-four marks, that single habit can cost several per cent of the final grade, and it is correctable in two or three sessions if it is caught before the draft is finalised.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed across knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science, each marked out of eight. Integrated sciences in the early years, separating into physics, chemistry and biology later.
programmes.countryNote: Inquiring and designing, and processing and evaluating, map almost directly onto the Diploma investigation's research design and data analysis criteria. A student who learned to control variables, justify a method and discuss anomalies in Year 10 arrives at a twenty per cent component already competent. That is the cheapest physics preparation available and it is bought years before anybody is worried.

programmes.name: The route in from IGCSE physics
programmes.description: Most Culture Village pupils arrive from Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson 4PH1. Both cover mechanics, waves, electricity and atomic physics, and both leave a gap in the mathematical treatment that the Diploma assumes, particularly in vectors, graph analysis and uncertainty.
programmes.countryNote: The specific gap is uncertainty. IGCSE physics touches measurement error lightly; Diploma physics treats uncertainty propagation as an assessed skill across papers and in the investigation. A student entering Year 12 who has never added percentage uncertainties for a product is not behind on physics, they are missing a technique, and it takes a handful of sessions rather than a term.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-culture-villag.subjectsIntro: The IB physics topics Culture Village families ask about, each named with where the marks are actually lost rather than a description of the content.

subjects.name: Kinematics and projectile motion
subjects.description: Displacement, velocity, acceleration, graphs of motion, and projectiles resolved into components. Students lose marks by treating a graph gradient as a number without units, and by resolving a projectile correctly and then using the full velocity in a vertical equation.

subjects.name: Forces, momentum and energy
subjects.description: Newton's laws, free-body diagrams, impulse and momentum conservation, work and energy. The standing failure is an incomplete free-body diagram: a missing normal force or a reaction drawn on the wrong body produces a confident wrong answer that later steps do not reveal.

subjects.name: Rotational dynamics
subjects.description: Torque, moment of inertia, angular momentum and rotational kinetic energy. The mathematical demand here is a step up and it is where Higher Level students most often ask for help, usually because moment of inertia expressions are recalled rather than understood.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and the particulate model
subjects.description: Temperature, internal energy, specific and latent heat, the ideal gas law and kinetic theory. Lost marks cluster in latent heat calculations where a phase change is missed, and in questions asking for a molecular explanation where a macroscopic one is given.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Travelling and standing waves, superposition, interference, diffraction, polarisation and the Doppler effect. Standing wave questions reward a labelled diagram showing nodes and antinodes; a verbal description of the same reasoning scores less.

subjects.name: Electric and magnetic fields
subjects.description: Field strength and potential, Coulomb's law, capacitance, circuits, electromagnetic induction and motor and generator principles. Sign and direction conventions are the reliable loss, particularly in induction questions where the direction of the induced current is asserted rather than derived.

subjects.name: Gravitational fields and orbits
subjects.description: Newton's law of gravitation, field strength, potential and orbital motion. Students confuse field strength with potential and lose marks on energy questions where the sign of gravitational potential energy matters to the argument.

subjects.name: Nuclear physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, half-life, binding energy, mass defect, fission and fusion. Binding energy per nucleon arguments are where the marks are, and most lost marks come from quoting the shape of the curve without using it to answer the question asked.

subjects.name: Quantum physics
subjects.description: The photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality, atomic spectra and energy levels. The photoelectric effect is the classic case where a student describes the observation and never states which part of the classical model it contradicts, which is the explanation the question wanted.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and graphical analysis
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through sums, products and powers, error bars, and gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines. Assessed across the papers and central to the investigation, and routinely half-remembered.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL · 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each for twenty-four in total. Three of the four criteria concern method rather than physics, and evaluation is the one most often reduced to a paragraph.

subjects.name: Data-based questions
subjects.description: Unfamiliar data presented in graphs and tables, with questions about trends, uncertainties and conclusions. The discriminator is reading the axes, units and error bars before reading the question, which is a habit rather than knowledge.
