sections.heading: Uncertainties: the marks almost nobody claims
paragraphs: If a Culture Village family buys one block of physics support, this is the one with the widest return. Uncertainty treatment is assessed across the written papers and sits at the centre of the data analysis and evaluation criteria in the investigation. It is also the part of physics that students most reliably treat as bookkeeping rather than as content, which means the marks are available and unclaimed.

The rules are few and they are rules rather than judgements, which is why they are teachable quickly. Absolute uncertainty is the raw figure. Fractional uncertainty is that figure divided by the measurement, and percentage uncertainty is the fraction expressed as a percentage. For sums and differences, add the absolute uncertainties. For products and quotients, add the percentage uncertainties. For a power, multiply the percentage uncertainty by the index. Five statements, and most students can quote three of them.

Graphical uncertainty is where the higher marks sit and where the teaching is thinnest. A student needs to plot error bars, draw maximum and minimum gradient lines through them, and determine the gradient uncertainty from the difference. That is a procedure, not an insight, and a student who has done it six times does it reliably under exam pressure. A student who has read about it produces a line of best fit and asserts an uncertainty.

The companion habits are unit and significant figure discipline. A final answer whose uncertainty is quoted to three significant figures when the measurement supports one is wrong in a way that costs marks, and an uncertainty stated without the unit of the quantity is incomplete. None of this is difficult. All of it is conventional, and conventional marks are the cheapest marks in any science subject.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade sits here, marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Printing that allocation is the single most useful thing this page can do for a Culture Village parent, because it shows immediately where the work is. Three of the four criteria concern how the investigation was built and interrogated rather than what the physics was.

Research design is the criterion decided before any data exists. It rewards a focused research question, a method capable of answering it, a clear identification of variables, and attention to safety and ethics where relevant. A research question too broad to answer with the available apparatus caps the entire investigation, which is why a design critique before data collection is the highest-value conversation available on this component and the one most frequently skipped.

Data analysis and conclusion are where the physics finally appears, and even here the marks are procedural: processing recorded correctly, uncertainties propagated, graphs appropriate with error bars, and a conclusion that is justified by the data rather than by expectation. Under the conclusion criterion the commonest failure is restating a textbook relationship the data did not actually demonstrate, which is scored against rather than for.

Evaluation is the criterion that costs most marks in practice. Six marks, and students routinely give it a paragraph. It wants the strengths and weaknesses of the method identified specifically, the limitations explained in terms of their effect on the result, and realistic improvements proposed. A modest experiment thoroughly evaluated outscores an impressive one barely discussed, which inverts what most students assume about how a science investigation is judged.

sections.heading: Command terms in physics, and the explanation that was never given
paragraphs: The IB publishes command terms and in physics they produce a recognisable failure. A question says explain and the student describes. The description is accurate, the physics is understood, and the marks are not awarded, because the mark scheme was looking for a causal account and received a sequence of observations. That is the single most common avoidable loss in physics extended-response questions.

The distinction is sharper in physics than in other subjects because the subject offers so many describable phenomena. Take the photoelectric effect. A student can accurately describe that electrons are emitted above a threshold frequency, that intensity affects current and not energy, and that emission is instantaneous. A question asking them to explain why this challenges the classical wave model wants the contradiction stated: a wave model predicts that sufficient intensity should eventually eject electrons at any frequency, and it does not happen. The description earns little; the contradiction earns the marks.

The other high-cost terms are state, which wants no working and gets a page of it, and determine, which wants a value with its supporting reasoning and frequently gets the value alone. Outline and discuss sit at different depths and are not interchangeable. None of this is hard to fix, and the published glossary is the whole curriculum for fixing it.

One session with the glossary and three past extended-response questions typically moves more marks than a month of content review, and the gain transfers to every other subject the student takes, because the same command terms carry the same meanings across the Diploma. For a Culture Village family working to a budget it is among the best returns per hour available, and it is almost never the thing requested.

sections.heading: Where physics marks disappear, topic by topic
paragraphs: Beyond uncertainties and the investigation, physics losses cluster in a short list of named places. They are worth stating specifically, because a tutor who can name them has taught the course, and because a student who has met them once rarely repeats them. Almost all of them are habits of representation rather than gaps in understanding.

Free-body diagrams lead the list. An incomplete diagram, with a missing normal force or a reaction drawn acting on the wrong body, produces a wrong answer that no later step reveals. The fix is procedural: draw every force, label the body it acts on, and check that every force has a partner somewhere in the system. Students who do this on every mechanics question stop losing mechanics marks almost immediately.

Direction and sign conventions are second, and they bite hardest in electromagnetic induction and in gravitational and electric potential. An induced current direction asserted rather than derived from a stated rule, or a gravitational potential energy treated as positive in an energy argument, both convert correct physics into a wrong answer. The habit is to state the convention being used at the top of the answer, which also makes partial credit recoverable.

Third is unit carriage in multi-stage calculations. A student who converts centimetres to metres at step one and forgets at step three produces an answer out by a factor and loses the accuracy mark on correct reasoning. Writing the unit beside every intermediate value is the fix, and it has the useful side effect of making dimensional errors visible before the final line.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level
paragraphs: Both levels cover the same five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level covers additional content within those themes and is assessed with longer papers. The scientific investigation is worth twenty per cent at both levels and is marked against the same four criteria out of twenty-four, which is the fact that most surprises families.

The practical difference at Higher Level is mathematical demand rather than volume alone. Rotational dynamics, the more developed treatment of fields, and the extended quantum and nuclear content all assume comfort with manipulation that a student arriving from IGCSE physics may not have. This is why Higher Level physics and Higher Level mathematics are so often requested together: the physics problem is frequently a mathematics problem wearing a physics question.

The difference that matters for choosing support is availability. Higher Level physics with investigation experience is among the thinnest combinations in the Dubai tutoring market, because it requires both content depth and familiarity with a criterion-marked component. Within a drive of Jaddaf Waterfront that combination is rare; nationally it is reachable. That is the practical argument for online delivery in this subject, stated without decoration.

sections.heading: The practical work question, answered directly
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online physics tuition is practical work, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a deflection. Physics involves apparatus, and a tutor over video has no apparatus. If the question is whether a tutor can run an experiment with your child, the answer is no, and no honest provider should imply otherwise.

What that objection misses is where the marks sit. The scientific investigation is designed, carried out and written by the student, in their school's laboratory and at home, under their teacher's supervision. A tutor's legitimate contribution is design critique before data collection, uncertainty treatment on the data the student gathered, graphing and analysis technique, and criterion-by-criterion feedback on their own draft. None of those four requires anybody to be holding a stopwatch.

The written papers reinforce the point. Practical skills are assessed on paper, through questions about apparatus, variable control, data handling and the evaluation of methods. Those are reading and writing skills applied to physics, and they are taught through worked examples and marked practice, which video delivers identically to a kitchen table. The data-based question in particular is a reading habit and nothing else.

Where a family genuinely wants hands-on support, the honest recommendation is the school. The teacher has the laboratory, the technician support and the duty of supervision, and an investigation is supposed to be supervised by them. A tutor who offered to run practical work alongside that would be duplicating something better provided and potentially complicating the academic honesty position on a component worth twenty per cent.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on a twenty per cent component
paragraphs: Because the investigation is worth twenty per cent and carries a school deadline, this is where pressure concentrates and where the honesty line gets tested. Work submitted for IB assessment must be the student's own. A tutor who writes, completes, substantially rewrites or supplies any part of an investigation creates a malpractice exposure for the candidate, and a finding can cost a Diploma. Providers in this market advertise completed internal assessments at a fixed price; the consequence lands on the student, not the seller.

The legitimate version is also the more useful one, and in physics it is unusually clear. A tutor can critique a research question before data exists, which is the intervention with the largest effect on the final mark. A tutor can check uncertainty propagation on data the student recorded. A tutor can explain what the evaluation criterion rewards and model an evaluation on a different, unrelated experiment, then hand the student's own back untouched. A tutor can teach referencing properly.

Data deserves a specific mention. A tutor must never supply data, adjust a student's data, or suggest that an anomalous point be removed to improve a trend. Anomalies are evaluation material, and a student who discusses an anomaly honestly scores better than one whose data looks suspiciously clean. That is a genuine case where the honest route and the high-scoring route are the same route, which is worth telling a worried student explicitly.

On materials, IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are copyright works. We reference and link them from the organisation's own site rather than reproducing them or supplying them as downloads, and we keep a short session note recording what was covered and whose work was in front of us, which is the document a parent can hand to a school if a question is ever raised.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IB physics tutor before hiring them?
faqs.answer: Two questions. How does a percentage uncertainty propagate through a quantity raised to a power, and how many marks does the evaluation criterion of the scientific investigation carry? The answers are that the percentage uncertainty is multiplied by the index, and that evaluation carries six of twenty-four marks. A tutor who teaches IB physics answers both immediately. A strong general physics tutor answers the first and hesitates on the second, which is exactly where the gap appears before a school deadline.

faqs.question: How much of the IB physics grade is the internal assessment worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Higher and Standard Level, and it is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The detail that matters is that three of those four criteria concern how the investigation was built and interrogated rather than what the physics was. A student can understand the physics thoroughly and score poorly, which is the most common pattern we see from Culture Village families.

faqs.question: Why did my child's physics investigation score badly when the experiment worked?
faqs.answer: Almost always the evaluation criterion. It carries six of the twenty-four marks and students routinely give it a single paragraph. It wants specific strengths and weaknesses of the method, limitations explained in terms of their effect on the result, and realistic improvements. A modest experiment thoroughly evaluated outscores an impressive one barely discussed. The second most common cause is data analysis: raw data presented with correct physics and no uncertainty propagation at all.

faqs.question: What are the uncertainty rules a Diploma physics student must know?
faqs.answer: Five. Absolute uncertainty is the raw figure, usually half the smallest division or the stated instrument figure. Percentage uncertainty is the absolute divided by the measurement. For sums and differences, add the absolute uncertainties. For products and quotients, add the percentage uncertainties. For a power, multiply the percentage uncertainty by the index. Beyond those, gradient uncertainty is found by drawing maximum and minimum lines through the error bars and taking half the difference.

faqs.question: When should a physics tutor get involved with the investigation?
faqs.answer: Before any data is collected, because research design is the criterion that caps everything else. A research question too broad to answer with the available apparatus limits all twenty-four marks and cannot be repaired once data exists. One conversation at the question and design stage is worth more than a dozen sessions on a finished draft. The second useful point is first-draft feedback, criterion by criterion, which is still well before the school's submission deadline.

faqs.question: Can online physics tuition work when the subject involves laboratory work?
faqs.answer: For the components that carry the marks, yes, and the honest limit is worth stating. A tutor over video has no apparatus and cannot run an experiment with your child. The investigation is designed, carried out and written by the student in their school's laboratory under their teacher's supervision. A tutor contributes design critique, uncertainty treatment on the student's own data, graphing and analysis technique, and criterion feedback. Practical skills in the written papers are assessed on paper.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain in a physics question?
faqs.answer: Describe wants an account of what happens; explain wants a causal account of why. This is the largest avoidable loss in physics extended-response questions. Take the photoelectric effect: describing that electrons are emitted above a threshold frequency and that intensity affects current rather than energy is accurate and earns little. Explaining why it challenges the classical wave model requires stating the contradiction, that a wave model predicts sufficient intensity should eventually eject electrons at any frequency and it does not.

faqs.question: Why do free-body diagrams cost so many marks in mechanics?
faqs.answer: Because an incomplete diagram produces a wrong answer that no later step reveals. A missing normal force, or a reaction drawn as acting on the wrong body, propagates silently through the whole calculation. The fix is procedural rather than conceptual: draw every force, label the body each one acts on, and check that every force has a partner somewhere in the system. Students who apply that to every mechanics question usually stop losing mechanics marks within a few weeks.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics mainly harder because of the mathematics?
faqs.answer: Substantially, yes. Both levels cover the same five themes, and Higher Level adds content and depth within them, but the step that students feel is mathematical: rotational dynamics, the more developed treatment of fields, and extended quantum and nuclear content all assume manipulation comfort that a student arriving from IGCSE physics may not have. It is why Higher Level physics and Higher Level mathematics are so frequently requested together, and why a physics difficulty is often a mathematics difficulty.

faqs.question: Why does this page not state the physics paper durations?
faqs.answer: Because paper structures and durations were revised for the current physics guide, and a page restating an arrangement from a previous version would be confidently wrong. Your school holds the subject guide and the IB coordinator can confirm both the paper arrangement and the internal deadline for the investigation. A tutor quoting a structure from an earlier syllabus is a liability rather than an expert, and that is a fair thing to test in a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Should an anomalous data point be removed to improve the trend?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth telling a worried student that the honest route is also the higher-scoring one. Anomalies are evaluation material: a student who identifies an anomaly, considers why it occurred and discusses its effect on the conclusion is doing exactly what the evaluation criterion rewards. Data that looks suspiciously clean invites a different kind of scrutiny. A tutor must never supply data, adjust data, or suggest removing a point, and we state that before any investigation work begins.

faqs.question: What gap do students carry from IGCSE physics into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty treatment, most often. IGCSE physics touches measurement error lightly, while Diploma physics assesses uncertainty propagation across the written papers and places it at the centre of the investigation's data analysis criterion. A student entering Year 12 who has never added percentage uncertainties for a product is not behind on physics; they are missing a technique. It takes a handful of sessions rather than a term, and buying it early serves both the papers and the investigation.

intro.heading: Physics has two deadlines and only one of them is the exam
paragraphs: Diploma physics generates enquiries at two predictable points in the calendar, and they need completely different work. The first is after a student's first full timed paper, usually late in the first year, when a result arrives that does not match the classroom impression. The second is the scientific investigation, whose deadline is set by the school and whose middle requires a laboratory.

The second of those is the one with no slack in it. An essay can be written at midnight. A physics investigation cannot be run at midnight, cannot be repeated once the laboratory timetable has closed, and cannot be rescued by working harder in the final fortnight. Its research question has to be settled while there is still room for a data run to fail, which in practice means a term before submission rather than a month.

The first is the one most often misdiagnosed. A student who understands physics in lessons and scores badly on papers has a technique problem rather than a comprehension problem, and more explanation will not shift it. What shifts it is writing physics in the forms the mark scheme pays for: causal chains in words, units converted before substitution, direction stated on every vector, and method visible rather than held in a calculator.

In DAMAC Hills there is a scheduling constraint on both. Secondary students here generally travel out of the community to school and arrive home after five, so sessions sit late and have to be shorter than a tired student can absorb at length. Sixty minutes twice a week works better than ninety minutes once, which matters more in physics than in most subjects because the work is written and tiring.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For physics the screen is a good working surface: graphs can be plotted and re-scaled live, uncertainty bars added and their effect on a gradient shown immediately, and a student's own data table marked against the criteria while they watch.

Availability is worth stating honestly on a physics page. Higher Level physics is a minority subject inside a Diploma cohort that is itself small, so the pool of tutors who have taught the extensions is thin across the whole emirate rather than in any one community. Where nobody suitable is free, the answer here is a stated wait or a referral rather than a general science tutor presented as a specialist.

subjects.description: Taught first because everything builds on it. Motion graphs, equations of motion, forces, momentum and energy. Marks are lost to direction dropped from a vector and to sign conventions abandoned halfway through a problem rather than to the physics itself.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Usually early to mid first year. Specific heat capacity, latent heat, gas laws and kinetic theory. The reliable loss is unit conversion: temperatures left in Celsius where kelvin is required, volumes in litres where cubic metres are needed, both mechanical and both repeating.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Mid first year, with Higher Level oscillation work later. Phase and path difference questions separate the grades. Diagrams drawn and then never referenced in the written answer lose the analysis marks they were meant to support.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Late first year or early second. Current, potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. The dominant loss is answering an explanation question with a formula where the scheme wants a chain of consequence in words.

subjects.name: Circular motion and gravitation
subjects.description: Second year, with Higher Level extending into potential and escape conditions. Students treat the force providing centripetal acceleration as an additional force, which adds a term and produces an answer that reads as carelessness rather than as a misconception.

subjects.name: Magnetism and induction
subjects.description: Second year, with induction and alternating current at Higher Level. Direction conventions are the whole difficulty: students who have not drilled the hand rules produce correct magnitudes with reversed directions, and the mark goes.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and particle physics
subjects.description: Second year. Radioactive decay, nuclear energy, binding energy and fundamental particles. Energy-mass calculations lose marks to unit choice between joules and electronvolts and to rounding before the final step of a multi-stage answer.

subjects.name: Energy production
subjects.description: Often late and under-prepared because it feels descriptive. Energy sources, efficiency and Sankey diagrams. Efficiency questions still require the calculation to be set out rather than asserted, and the marks here are among the most accessible on the paper.

subjects.name: The option topic
subjects.description: Chosen by the school and taught late, which makes it the content most likely to be thinly covered before mocks. Worth establishing early which option the school teaches, because tutoring matched to the wrong one is wasted entirely.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Spans the second year with a school-set deadline. Marked against published criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with roughly half the marks concerning process and communication rather than the result.

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor in DAMAC Hills is for
paragraphs: An IB physics tutor in DAMAC Hills means one-to-one Diploma physics teaching arranged outside school for a student in the community, and IB Gram provides it live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In a community where the student has already made two journeys and is home after five, removing the tutor's two as well is the practical benefit.

The specific skill a family is buying is diagnosis from a marked script. That is narrower than knowing physics. It means recognising that a four-mark explanation scored two because it named the effect without the mechanism, that a correct calculation lost its last mark to a rounded intermediate value, and that a vector answer was marked down for having no direction. Those judgements come from having taught the course and marked its papers.

The second thing is calendar judgement, which on a physics page means knowing when each piece of work has to happen. The investigation's data collection sits inside the school's laboratory timetable. The option topic is taught late and is therefore thin before mocks. The Higher Level extra paper is first met in a mock unless somebody schedules it earlier. None of that is visible from a school report.

What is not provided is any help producing the investigation. A tutor explains the criteria, questions the variable control, discusses whether the data supports the conclusion, and gives feedback on what the student has written. Writing, completing or producing any part of the report is a malpractice finding against the student, and the deadline pressure that makes it tempting is exactly when it matters most to refuse.

sections.heading: Two years of physics in the order it is taught
paragraphs: Physics is taught in an order and the order matters for intervention timing. Mechanics comes first because the rest of the subject uses its vocabulary and its mathematics. Thermal physics and waves follow. Electricity arrives late in the first year or early in the second. Circular motion, gravitation, magnetism and nuclear physics occupy the second year, with the option topic and energy production often last.

Each stage assumes the one before it in a specific way. Everything after mechanics assumes vector handling and rearrangement. Circuits assume proportional reasoning. Induction assumes magnetic field direction conventions that were introduced earlier and rarely drilled. Nuclear calculations assume unit discipline across joules and electronvolts. None of those dependencies appears on a report, and all of them are checkable in minutes.

The practical consequence is that a weakness is cheapest to fix in the term it is taught and most expensive in the term before the papers. A student struggling with vectors in the first term of the first year has eighteen months in which the problem is still small. The same student discovered at the second-year mock has ten weeks and a syllabus to revise at the same time.

The table sets the sequence against what each stage assumes and what to check before moving past it. It is written to be used during the first Diploma year, when the checks cost nothing more than the five minutes it takes to ask a question and watch the hesitation.

sections.heading: The investigation, counted backwards from the laboratory
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation is the component with the least flexible timeline in physics, because its middle requires apparatus, a room and a slot in the school's timetable. That single fact should drive the planning, and it almost never does: students plan from the submission date backwards through the writing and forget that the data collection has a queue in front of it.

Working backwards properly, the final week is formatting and a criterion check with no physics happening. The fortnight before that is analysis, uncertainty propagation and evaluation. Before that sits the data collection, which needs a booked slot and room for one failure. Before that is the research question, and that is where a block earns most of its value, because an unworkable question discovered during collection cannot be rescued.

Research questions fail in four predictable ways: too broad to answer in the space available, dependent on apparatus the school does not have, involving a variable that cannot practically be controlled, or producing data with so little variation that no conclusion is available. A specialist identifies all four in one conversation, which is why that conversation belongs a term before submission.

Uncertainty is the other thing best handled before the data rather than after. Deciding what will be measured, with what instrument and to what precision, determines the uncertainty that can later be propagated. Students who collect first and think about uncertainty afterwards frequently find they cannot evaluate their own method, which is where a substantial share of the available marks sit.

sections.heading: Term by term: what to fix when
paragraphs: Set against the six terms of the Diploma, physics has an obvious order of work, and following it costs less than any other sequence. The first term of the first year is for explanation structure and unit discipline, because those habits then earn marks on every paper for the remaining eighteen months. It is also the term in which a mathematical weakness can be addressed before it compounds.

The second and third terms of the first year are for content with a first timed paper somewhere inside them. That first paper is the single most informative event of the first year and most students do not sit one. Ninety minutes of a weekend produces a diagnosis that a term of reports does not, and it can be arranged by a parent without any tutor involved.

The first term of the second year belongs to the investigation, whatever the school's precise deadline, and it collides with internal deadlines in other subjects. The second term is mocks and the fortnight of review afterwards. The third is triage, by which point the question is which marks are still reachable rather than which topics remain uncovered.

Against that shape, the common DAMAC Hills pattern — a first enquiry after second-year mock results — arrives at the start of triage. It is workable and a targeted eight-week block does real work there. It is simply more expensive per mark than the same money spent in the first year, which is the argument for a first-year diagnostic even when nothing appears to be wrong.

sections.heading: Before the mock and after it
paragraphs: Physics mocks are treated as weather and should be treated as a measurement that can be prepared for. Preparing for it changes it, and because predicted grades are informed by mock performance, the number matters beyond its diagnostic value. An eight-week block ending at the mock window is better value than the same block starting after it, and almost nobody buys the first version.

What that block should contain is largely determined by which paper types the student has never sat. At Higher Level the extra written paper is the usual answer: it is first met in the mock by most students, which means the mock measures unfamiliarity as much as physics. Attempting it twice before the mock, with marking in between, removes that distortion entirely.

Afterwards, the fortnight of review is the richest information in the course and is usually discarded. The method is to sort every lost mark by cause: content not known, content not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, units or direction, question not attempted. The tally per subject names the next block, and it can be done by a parent and student at a kitchen table in an evening.

The common finding in physics is that mechanical causes dominate, which is good news because they are fast to fix. A student whose largest categories are units, direction and unwritten method does not need a content block; they need three or four weeks of deliberate habit work and some timed practice. That diagnosis is only available from the scripts, which is why they should come out of the bag.

sections.heading: The option topic, and why it is usually thin
paragraphs: Every Diploma physics course includes an option topic chosen by the school, and it is routinely the most thinly covered content in the syllabus for a simple calendar reason: it is taught last, in the term where coursework deadlines and mock revision are already competing for attention. Students arrive at the papers having met it once, briefly.

The first practical step is to establish which option the school teaches, because tutoring matched to the wrong one is entirely wasted. That sounds obvious and it is a real failure: a student can be given weeks of support on an option their school does not cover, because nobody asked and the student assumed all options were taught. The answer is on the course outline the school issued at the start of the Diploma.

The second step is to schedule the option work for the second half of the school's teaching of it, when there is enough content for consolidation to be meaningful, rather than after it has finished. A block arriving after the single pass is doing repair, and repair takes longer than consolidation for the same result.

The third is to accept that in a compressed revision plan the option may be a place where marks are deliberately conceded. That is an uncomfortable recommendation and sometimes the right one: a student six weeks out with a weak option and three weak core topics will gain more from the core topics, because they are examined across more of the paper. Writing that decision down is what makes it a plan rather than an omission.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of physics can do
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most families ask about, and in physics it has a reasonably well-defined best use. It will change explanation structure, install unit and direction discipline, make method visible, and rebuild two or three specific topics. It will not cover the syllabus, and a provider accepting the booking on that basis has made a commercial rather than an educational decision.

Which eight weeks it should be depends entirely on the diagnosis, and the diagnosis comes from the scripts rather than from a conversation. If the losses are mechanical, three weeks on habits and five on two named topics. If the extra Higher Level paper is the problem, it is repeated exposure rather than teaching. If the obstacle is mathematical, the physics content is not where the block should start.

The mathematical case deserves its own note because it is so common. Rearrangement, indices, standard form and gradients run through mechanics, circuits and thermal physics identically, so a student who stalls at the same algebraic step in three topics has one problem rather than three. Twenty minutes of non-calculator manipulation will establish it, and where it is the finding, physics revision never reaches the real obstacle.

The table sets out what each diagnosis implies for the eight weeks, including what the block should state it will not attempt. Writing the omissions down is the part that makes a short block honest, and it is also what stops a student re-reading everything lightly out of guilt instead of drilling anything properly.

sections.heading: What physics support costs, by when you start
paragraphs: The published rates matter less than the starting date, but you need them in front of you to see why. At the university-student end Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, which is a rate that works when there is a year left and the problem is practice rather than diagnosis. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted, which is relevant from DAMAC Hills, where the run out along Hessa Street is long enough that a tutor prices it. A family starting in DP1 can shop anywhere on that list. A family starting eight weeks before the mocks has already lost the bottom two thirds of it.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with local packages advertised around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026, and none is IB Gram's price list.

For physics specifically, the budget band is a poor fit and it is worth saying so directly. A university student who passed physics can supervise homework. Reading a marked Higher Level script and identifying that a four-mark explanation scored two for naming the effect without the mechanism is a different skill, and it is the skill the enquiry is for. Paying the low rate for that work usually means paying twice.

The table arranges cost by starting point rather than by tier, because in physics the starting point determines what the money can reach. A first-year technique block at the qualified band costs a fraction of a second-year triage block at the exam-year band and does more, because the habits it installs then earn marks on every paper for the remaining eighteen months.

sections.heading: Availability, permits and the claims avoided
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is the hardest single match in this market, and that is a structural fact rather than a local one. It is a minority subject inside a Diploma cohort that represents 7% of Dubai private school pupils, so no community in this belt holds a surplus of tutors who have taught the extensions and marked the extended papers. Demand across every school also peaks in the same fortnight after mock results.

The policy here is to state the position rather than conceal it. Where a specialist is free they are proposed within a day with a trial lesson in the same week. Where none is free, the family is told, given a realistic wait and offered a referral. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit, though every provider has one, and concealing it moves the cost onto the student.

On the regulatory side, private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Tutors are not described as examiners without evidence of current status, and examiner status is never presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. No IB session date and no success statistic appears on this page, in both cases because neither could be verified in a form a reader could check.

process.title: Send the level and the marked scripts
process.description: 'Physics HL, first Diploma year, last paper a 4' plus the script itself is enough to decide whether a specialist is available and what the block should target. The scripts show whether the losses are mechanical, mathematical or genuinely about content.

process.title: Establish the option topic and the investigation date
process.description: Two facts from the school's course outline and the Diploma coordinator. Tutoring matched to the wrong option is wasted entirely, and investigation work planned without the laboratory timetable in view tends to discover its data problem too late to fix.

process.title: Diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: A full online session with the proposed specialist, spent sorting the lost marks on a script by cause and running twenty minutes of non-calculator manipulation. It ends with a written count of mechanical against conceptual losses. Nothing is committed.

process.title: Mechanical habits before content
process.description: Where the diagnosis is mixed, the first weeks go to causal-chain writing, unit conversion and visible method, because those transfer across every topic at once and produce a visible change early. Content gaps follow, in order of how often they are examined.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target from session one is measured in writing. If the error log shows the same categories recurring, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes at no cost. In an exam year, making that call at the halfway point saves a month.

whyPoints.title: Planned on the two-year topic order
whyPoints.description: Physics is taught in a sequence and each stage assumes the last. A weakness in vectors or rearrangement is cheap to fix in the term it appears and expensive in the term before the papers, and nothing in a school report flags which dependency has failed.

whyPoints.title: The laboratory treated as the binding date
whyPoints.description: Investigation data collection sits inside the school's laboratory timetable and a failed run needs a slot to repeat it. Counting backwards with that constraint in view is what prevents unusable data being discovered in the fortnight when nothing can be done about it.

whyPoints.title: The option topic established first
whyPoints.description: It is chosen by the school and taught last, which makes it the thinnest content before mocks and the easiest thing to tutor wrongly. Confirming which option the course covers takes one question and prevents weeks of entirely wasted support.

whyPoints.title: The extra Higher Level paper scheduled early
whyPoints.description: Most students meet it for the first time in a mock, so the mock measures unfamiliarity as well as physics. Two attempts before the mock window, with marking in between, removes that distortion and changes a Higher Level profile more than extra content teaching does.

whyPoints.title: Honest about availability
whyPoints.description: Higher Level physics is a minority subject in a small cohort, so the specialist pool is thin across the emirate and tightest after mock results. Families are told, with a realistic wait or a referral, rather than matched to a general science tutor described as a specialist.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled for a student home after five
whyPoints.description: Sixty minutes rather than ninety, from 5.30pm or on a weekend morning, twice a week rather than once. Physics work is written and tiring, and online delivery is what makes the shorter, more frequent pattern practical rather than theoretical.

faqs.question: When should a Diploma physics student start the scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Ten weeks or more before the school deadline, because the middle of it needs a laboratory slot and a failed data run needs another one. Counting backwards: the final week is formatting and a criterion check, the fortnight before is analysis and evaluation, and data collection sits six to eight weeks out with room for one failure. The research question comes before all of that, and an unworkable question discovered during collection cannot be rescued.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor travel to DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For physics the screen is a good surface anyway: graphs can be plotted and re-scaled live, uncertainty bars added and their effect on a gradient shown immediately, and a student's own data table marked against the criteria while they watch it happen.

faqs.question: Why is my child's physics paper mark lower than their classwork suggests?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the written answers are not in the form the mark scheme pays for. An 'explain' question wants a chain — cause, mechanism, effect — and a correct formula earns nothing. Add temperatures left in Celsius where kelvin was needed, a vector given without direction, and method held in a calculator, and a competent student loses a grade's worth of marks mechanically. Sort the losses on the script by cause; the mechanical count is usually larger.

faqs.question: Which physics option topic does my child's school teach?
faqs.answer: Check the course outline the school issued at the start of the Diploma, or ask the teacher. It matters because the option is chosen by the school and tutoring matched to the wrong one is entirely wasted, which does happen when nobody asks and the student assumes all options are covered. The option is also taught last, so it is the thinnest content before mocks and the most likely to need consolidation rather than revision.

faqs.question: How early should the Higher Level extra paper be attempted?
faqs.answer: Early in the second Diploma year, and then again a few weeks later with marking in between. Most students meet it for the first time in a mock, which means the mock measures unfamiliarity as much as physics and produces a mark that misleads everybody. Two attempts beforehand remove the distortion. The skill being tested is partly tolerance for the opening minutes of an unfamiliar problem, and that is built by exposure rather than taught.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write up the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the criteria, explain the mark ceiling attached to each, question the variable control, discuss whether the data supports the conclusion and give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor cannot write, complete or produce any part of it, whatever the deadline. That is an IB academic-honesty rule rather than a preference, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student.

faqs.question: How much of my child's physics difficulty is actually mathematics?
faqs.answer: Often a large share. Rearrangement, indices, standard form and gradients run through mechanics, circuits and thermal physics identically, so a student who stalls at the same algebraic step in three topics has one problem rather than three. Twenty minutes of non-calculator manipulation establishes it: watch for hesitation rather than wrong answers. Where that is the finding, physics topic revision never reaches the real obstacle and the block should start upstream.

faqs.question: Is it better to book a physics block before or after the mocks?
faqs.answer: Before, and almost nobody does. Mocks are a measurement and preparing for a measurement changes it; because predicted grades are informed by mock performance, the number has consequences beyond diagnosis. An eight-week block ending at the mock window costs the same as one starting afterwards and reaches more, particularly at Higher Level where the extra paper can be attempted twice before it counts for anything.

faqs.question: Why is uncertainty handling worth a session of its own?
faqs.answer: Because deciding what to measure, with which instrument and to what precision determines the uncertainty that can later be propagated, and a substantial share of the investigation marks sit in analysis and evaluation. Students who collect data first and consider uncertainty afterwards frequently find they cannot evaluate their own method properly. Planning it before the laboratory slot costs one session and protects marks that cannot be recovered any other way.

faqs.question: What should a first-year physics student do with a bad paper result?
faqs.answer: Treat it as the most useful information of the year and sort it rather than being upset by it. Put every lost mark into a category: content not known, not retrieved under time, command term misread, working not shown, units or direction, question not attempted. If mechanical categories dominate, which in physics they usually do, the fix is three or four weeks of habit work rather than a content block, and it is cheap at that stage of the course.

faqs.question: How thin is Higher Level physics availability in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Thin, and thin everywhere rather than in one community. The IB accounts for 7% of Dubai private school pupils and Higher Level physics is a minority within that, so a school in this belt may have a handful of candidates in a year. Demand also peaks across every school in the same fortnight after mock results. Booking before that fortnight costs nothing to arrange and avoids most of the problem.

faqs.question: Can online physics lessons cover practical skills?
faqs.answer: The examined skills are largely written: variable control, apparatus and precision choice, tabulating data with units in the headings, identifying anomalies, propagating uncertainty and criticising a described method. All of that is teachable on a shared screen with real data, and plotting and re-scaling a graph live is easier there than on paper. Handling apparatus in a school laboratory remains the school's part of the work and no tutor replaces it in any format.

faqs.question: Is a Standard Level physics block shorter than a Higher Level one?
faqs.answer: Usually, because there is less syllabus and one fewer written paper, so a block covers proportionally more of the course in the same time. Standard Level blocks are often technique-led and can lift a grade relatively quickly. Higher Level blocks have to choose between covering extensions and drilling the unfamiliar extra paper, which is why the diagnosis matters more there and why stating the omissions is part of the plan.

faqs.question: What does a physics block cost across a Dubai exam year?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's published monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month and the mid band at AED 600 to 1,200. The hourly figures behind them run from AED 33 to 65 at the university-student end up to AED 650 for premium named tutors, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase at AED 270. All are provider-published market rates read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-damac-hills.closingBody: For an IB physics tutor in DAMAC Hills, the useful first message names the level, attaches the most recent marked scripts, and states the school's investigation deadline and which option topic the course covers. From those it is possible to say how many of the lost marks were mechanical, whether the real obstacle is mathematical, and whether the laboratory timetable still allows a data run to fail once. The trial lesson is a full diagnostic session delivered live online in Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Why IB physics goes wrong, and why it is rarely the topic
paragraphs: Ask a Diploma physics student what the problem is and you will usually get a topic name. Electricity. Thermodynamics. Fields. Occasionally quantum. Ask to see a marked paper and the picture changes: the content was broadly understood, and the marks went on uncertainties handled wrongly, a graph that was never linearised, a definition written in approximately the right words, and working that arrived at an answer without showing the step that carried the credit.

That gap between what students name and what papers penalise is the whole reason a physics specialist is a different purchase from a general science tutor. A capable graduate can explain Newton's laws. Explaining why a particular uncertainty propagates as a percentage rather than an absolute, and what that does to the gradient of a best-fit line, is a different competence — and it is examined directly.

Higher Level makes it sharper, because HL candidates sit a third paper that Standard Level does not. That paper tests experimental technique and data analysis as a skill in its own right: reading an instrument to a sensible precision, spotting that a method cannot answer the question it was set, choosing what to plot so that a relationship becomes a straight line, and saying what a result's limitations are. Schools teach it, but they teach it inside a crowded practical timetable, and a student who missed a few weeks of it rarely recovers the technique from a textbook.

Then there is the mathematics underneath. IB physics assumes algebraic fluency, confident rearrangement, logarithms where exponential relationships appear, and comfort with gradients and intercepts. A student taking Applications and Interpretation maths alongside Physics Higher Level is carrying a real load, because the physics course expects manipulation their maths course does not drill. That combination accounts for a noticeable share of the DAMAC Hills 2 enquiries we see.

The practical side of getting help here is the Al Qudra corridor. DAMAC Hills 2 sits well out, and almost every Diploma student in the community is driven to school in Motor City, Dubai Sports City or deeper into Dubai. A half three finish becomes a 4:45pm arrival home in afternoon traffic, and a tutor who still has to drive out turns that into a half six start. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only — so a session starts when your child is home rather than when the traffic clears.

The pool matters too. The IB is around 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils across 227 schools, spread citywide, and only the final two years sit the Diploma. Physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism within that, so the chance a qualified HL physics teacher lives near DAMAC Hills 2 with a free weekday evening is low. Online matching makes that irrelevant.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.programmesIntro: Physics at each stage of the IB continuum asks for something different, and the useful help changes with it. These are the stages we cover for DAMAC Hills 2 families.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, the physics strand
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is marked against four criteria on a 0-8 scale: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B asks a student to design an investigation with controlled variables, and criterion C asks them to process data and evaluate the method — which is the direct ancestor of Diploma practical work.
programmes.countryNote: DAMAC Hills 2 parents often read a strong criterion A and a weak criterion C as a general science concern. It is not: it is specifically the experimental strand, and it is the one that predicts how a student will cope with Diploma physics. Working criterion by criterion in Years 9 and 10 is the cheapest possible preparation.

programmes.name: Physics Standard Level
programmes.description: Two written papers plus the Internal Assessment at 20% of the grade. The content is broad rather than deep, which means the risk is coverage: a topic taught in a hurried week in Year 12 can quietly stay unlearned until a mock exposes it. Definitions and the correct use of units are examined relentlessly throughout.
programmes.countryNote: SL physics is a common choice for DAMAC Hills 2 students heading into economics, business or life sciences, and it is frequently paired with Applications and Interpretation maths. That pairing works, but the physics course still expects rearrangement and graph work that AI does not emphasise, so the maths underneath needs checking early.

programmes.name: Physics Higher Level
programmes.description: Additional content depth plus a third written paper that tests experimental technique and data analysis directly. The Internal Assessment is still 20%. HL rewards students who can sustain a multi-step argument with units and uncertainties carried correctly through every stage, and penalises those who treat each question as a formula lookup.
programmes.countryNote: This is the level where local specialist supply around DAMAC Hills 2 most often reaches zero. It is also the level that engineering and physical-science degree applications most commonly require, so families frequently need exactly the tutor the neighbourhood cannot provide. Online matching exists for precisely this case.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP to Diploma physics
programmes.description: A real step, and an underestimated one. IGCSE physics rewards recall and single-step calculation; Diploma physics expects derivation, multi-step reasoning and uncertainty treatment. A student with a strong IGCSE grade can be genuinely struggling by November of Year 12, which is the curriculum rather than the student.
programmes.countryNote: The intervention that works is a short block in the summer or early Year 12 on algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, graph interpretation and uncertainty basics. Done then it is inexpensive. Done in February of Year 13 it is a rescue, and the foundations are now carrying two years of content.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: These are the physics topics and components DAMAC Hills 2 students most often need work on, with the specific place marks go in each. Availability varies by level and term and is confirmed at the trial lesson.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: Projectiles, momentum, energy and circular motion. Students usually know the equations and lose marks on sign conventions, on resolving forces in an unfamiliar direction, and on choosing an energy argument where a force argument would have been shorter and safer.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The most commonly named weak topic and often a genuine one. Internal resistance, potential dividers and the behaviour of real components under load. Students can apply Ohm's law and cannot reason about what happens to a circuit when one component changes.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Superposition, standing waves, diffraction and simple harmonic motion. Phase relationships are the recurring difficulty, and diagrams are where credit is won or lost — a correctly labelled wave diagram answers several marks of question on its own.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the kinetic model. The marks here sit in precise definition and in whether a student can explain a temperature change at the level of particles rather than restating the formula they used.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational, electric and magnetic
subjects.description: Field strength versus potential is the distinction students most often blur, and HL questions exploit it directly. Sketching a field pattern correctly and reasoning about work done moving a charge or mass through it is examined repeatedly.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Binding energy, decay, the photoelectric effect and energy levels. The arithmetic with very large and very small numbers in standard form costs students marks independently of whether they understand the physics, which is worth diagnosing separately.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, how each propagates through addition, multiplication and powers, and what that implies about how many significant figures an answer may claim. Examined across every component and taught in a hurry almost everywhere.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing what to plot so a relationship becomes a straight line, then reading physics from the gradient and intercept. This is the single highest-return skill in the course and it is a technique rather than a topic, which is why it responds quickly to one-to-one work.

subjects.name: The practical and data-analysis paper
subjects.description: Reading instruments to sensible precision, identifying a flawed method, selecting controlled variables, evaluating whether data supports a conclusion. A different skill from the content papers, met late in most schools, and worth preparing for separately.

subjects.name: The Physics Internal Assessment
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation assessed against published criteria. Most marks are lost before any data exists: a research question with no measurable variable, too few repeats to say anything about reliability, or a range too narrow to show a relationship.

subjects.name: The maths underneath physics
subjects.description: Algebraic rearrangement, indices, logarithms for exponential relationships, trigonometry for resolving vectors, and gradient reasoning. Students taking Applications and Interpretation maths alongside physics often need this layer taught explicitly.

sections.heading: What each physics component is worth and where marks disappear
paragraphs: Students revise topics; examiners mark components. Organising preparation around the second is what separates a student who knows physics from one who scores it, and the distinction is particularly stark in this subject because so much of the assessment is skill rather than recall.

Every Diploma physics candidate sits written papers plus the Internal Assessment at 20% of the grade. Higher Level adds a third written paper testing experimental technique and data analysis. The loss patterns per component are consistent enough to plan against: the short-answer paper punishes definitions written in approximately the right words; the structured paper rewards visible method and penalises an answer with no working; and the practical paper catches students who have never been taught to evaluate a method rather than execute one.

The most expensive habit across all of them is stopping too early. A physics answer earns marks for the steps, not only the result, and a student who computes mentally and writes one line forfeits credit they had genuinely earned. Changing that is a behaviour change rather than a knowledge gain, it takes a few weeks of marked practice, and it is probably the cheapest grade movement available in the subject.
The table sets the components against their real failure modes. The last column names what to practise, which is almost never the topic the student would have named.

One point about weightings, since parents ask. The exact percentage each paper carries is published in the current subject guide and the school can confirm it, so we do not restate figures here that the IB may revise. What does not change is the shape: the content papers reward precision and visible method, the practical paper rewards evaluation, and the investigation rewards design. Plan against the shape.

sections.heading: Uncertainties and graphs: the part that is not physics content
paragraphs: If there is one section of this page to act on, it is this one. Uncertainty handling and graph linearisation are examined across the whole course, are worth a substantial number of marks, are not conceptually difficult, and are taught in a rush in almost every school because the practical timetable is crowded. That combination makes them the highest-return work available in IB physics.

The specific confusions are predictable. Absolute uncertainty treated as percentage, or the reverse. Uncertainties added when they should be combined as fractions. A final answer quoted to six significant figures when the measurement justified two. An uncertainty on a gradient estimated by eye with no attempt at a maximum and minimum line. Each of those is a single-session fix, and each recurs in every paper until it is fixed.

Linearisation is the other half. Many physics relationships are not straight lines, and the examinable skill is choosing what to plot so that they become one — plotting against the reciprocal, the square, or the logarithm, depending on the relationship — and then reading a physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. Students who have met this only once tend to plot the raw variables, get a curve, and have nothing to say about it.

This also transfers straight into the Internal Assessment, where the processing and evaluation marks depend on exactly these skills. A student who handles uncertainty properly in their investigation is accessing marks that a student with identical data and sloppier analysis cannot. sections.heading: The Internal Assessment is lost at the design stage
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the physics grade comes from an individual investigation, and by the time most students ask for help the marks that mattered have already been decided. Not in the writing. In the fortnight when the research question was chosen and the method was planned.

The recurring design faults are specific. A research question with no genuinely measurable independent variable, so nothing can be varied systematically. A range too narrow for a relationship to show above the noise. Too few repeats to say anything honest about reliability. A controlled variable that was not actually controlled, which the student discovers at the evaluation stage when it is too late to do anything but confess it. None of these is a writing problem and none of them can be fixed by a better conclusion.

A tutor who reads the criteria with the student in week one is therefore worth several who read a draft in week ten. The permitted work is substantial: explaining what each criterion rewards and what it is worth, testing whether a proposed question can be investigated with the equipment available, checking the planned range and repeats will produce analysable data, and giving feedback on the student's own draft against the criteria.

The line is authorship, and it is firm. A tutor may not write any part of the investigation, supply data or calculations, provide a model to adapt, or edit a draft to a finish. The student signs an authorship declaration and the supervisor signs alongside, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice. This search result contains operators selling completed Internal Assessments — one advertises them at AED 3,750 — and buying one risks the whole Diploma rather than one component.

sections.heading: The maths a physics student is assumed to have
paragraphs: This is the hidden prerequisite, and it explains a large share of the physics struggles we diagnose. IB physics assumes a level of algebraic comfort that the course itself does not teach: rearranging an equation with the unknown in the denominator, working with indices and standard form at speed, using logarithms when a relationship is exponential, resolving vectors with trigonometry, and reasoning fluently about gradients and intercepts.

Where this bites hardest is the combination of Physics Higher Level with Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. AI is an excellent course and emphasises modelling, statistics and technology rather than algebraic manipulation, which means a student may be doing well in maths and still lack the specific fluency their physics paper demands. That pairing is common in Dubai schools and it is not a mistake, but it needs the algebra taught explicitly alongside rather than assumed.

The diagnostic consequence is that we look underneath the named topic. A student who says fields are the problem often cannot rearrange the expression confidently enough to see what the question is asking. A student who says the practical paper is impossible often cannot take logarithms of both sides to find a power relationship. Teaching more fields content to the first student, or more experimental theory to the second, misses the layer where the marks are going.

In practice this means a short algebraic block early is one of the best investments a Year 12 physics family can make, and it is cheaper and faster than it sounds. Six to ten focused sessions on rearrangement, indices, logarithms and gradient reasoning changes how every subsequent physics session lands.

sections.heading: Fitting physics into a DAMAC Hills 2 week
paragraphs: Physics is cognitively dense, and the hour it is taught in matters as much as who teaches it. A tired student can read and absorb something; a tired student cannot follow a derivation or hold three variables in mind while rearranging an expression. Booking whichever slot happens to be free is therefore a worse decision in physics than in most subjects.

The clock out here is unforgiving. A school day ending at half three in Motor City or Dubai Sports City means a 4:45pm arrival home in afternoon traffic on Hessa Street and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road; from an inner-city IB school it is closer to five. Because nobody is driving to you, a session can begin at 4:45pm, which for a Year 12 student is often the best hour available. For a Year 13 student the better choice is usually 8pm for ninety minutes, when a full data-analysis question plus marking fits without rushing.

Weekend mornings are the underused option and they suit physics particularly well, because the subject rewards sustained work on one thread rather than scattered half-hours. Two hours on a Friday or Saturday morning during an Internal Assessment term is frequently the most productive block in the week, and it competes with nothing else.

Ramadan needs planning rather than improvising: school days shorten, evenings reorganise around Iftar, and families here typically shift to a late-morning, early-afternoon or post-Iftar slot, or pause part of the month and resume with a heavier block. Prayer times are built into the slot from the start. What we try to avoid is the drift of cancel, reschedule, cancel, which in physics breaks continuity faster than in any other subject because each session builds directly on the last.

sections.heading: What physics tutoring costs in this market
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates, read from provider pages in October 2026. Qualified online subject tutors run AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists run AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai research giving the specialist band as AED 200-450 plus. Budget online tutoring advertises from AED 33-65, with Tutopiya at AED 33-52 and EdFlik at AED 45-65. In-home visits are AED 180-500 including travel. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end.

Physics has a sharper version of the budget-band problem than most subjects, because the thing a cheap generalist cannot do is exactly the thing the marks depend on. Explaining Newton's laws is within reach of many capable graduates. Teaching uncertainty propagation correctly, insisting on a maximum and minimum line through error bars, and knowing what the practical paper rewards is not. A term at AED 50 an hour with somebody who has never marked a data-analysis question is the clearest example of a cheap purchase producing nothing.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for budget tutoring at one hour a week, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour visits.

Read those bands as attribution rather than as a price list of ours: each figure belongs to the provider named beside it, and none of them is an IB Gram price. We publish no rate card on these pages, and the reason sits in the paragraph above - the honest number depends on the level, on the specific gap the marked work exposes, and on the weeks remaining. A family in DAMAC Hills 2 whose daughter is losing marks on uncertainty treatment in the autumn term is buying something quite different from one whose son has a thin fields topic with a term to go, and one advertised figure would misprice both of them. So the trial lesson is free, the diagnostic happens inside it, and the quote comes after the diagnostic rather than before it.

sections.heading: The physics year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session, and planning a physics year backwards from there shows why early help is worth more than late help. The Internal Assessment is worth 20% and is finished long before any exam revision starts. The practical paper, for HL candidates, needs technique built over months rather than crammed.

One honesty note. The IB's own site blocks automated retrieval, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org. We write about the May session as the one UAE schools sit and publish no specific date — get those from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org, which are the only sources worth planning around. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we use them: Cambridge runs June and November series, with the February/March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

The sequence that works: algebraic foundations and uncertainty technique secured early in Year 12, because everything afterwards uses them. Internal Assessment question chosen in the second half of Year 12, while it can still be a good question rather than an available one. Investigation completed to the school's internal deadline. Mocks. Then a final term that is almost entirely paper technique, including dedicated practical-paper work for HL candidates.

The practical consequence for a DAMAC Hills 2 family is that early Year 12 is the best time to start and March of Year 13 is the worst. In March the only remaining lever is technique, which is genuinely worth marks but is smaller than foundations plus the investigation plus technique together.

sections.heading: What we will not claim about physics results
paragraphs: No grade guarantee. Not a 7, not a specific improvement, not a particular paper score. The variables — prior algebra, weeks remaining, whether the Internal Assessment was designed well, whether the student has ever been taught to show working — are not all under a tutor's control, and an offer that ignores that is a sales device.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which means none. No average physics score achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, and no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, occasionally in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never state how any of them was produced.

No regulator or awarding-body claim, and no examiner descriptions. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre anywhere in the UAE, and does not describe its tutors as IB examiners because current examiner status is not something we can evidence. Examiner status also confers no access to marking, boundaries or paper content, whatever anybody implies. We host no IB past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables either; they belong to the IB and we link the official source instead.

What we will give you is a diagnostic verdict. After watching your child work real paper questions, a specialist will say whether the gap is content, the maths underneath, uncertainty technique or the investigation, roughly how long each takes to move, and whether the available time is enough. Sometimes the answer is that it is not, and that concentrating on two of those rather than four is the better plan.
