faqs.question: Why is my child struggling with IB physics when the IGCSE grade was strong?
faqs.answer: Because the step is real. IGCSE physics rewards recall and single-step calculation; Diploma physics expects derivation, multi-step reasoning, uncertainty treatment and graph work. A student with a strong IGCSE result can be genuinely lost by November of Year 12, and that is the curriculum rather than a decline in ability. The effective fix is a short early block on algebraic rearrangement, logarithms, graph interpretation and uncertainty basics, done in the summer or early Year 12 before two years of content gets built on an unstable layer.

faqs.question: What is the Higher Level physics practical paper and how is it prepared for?
faqs.answer: It is the third written paper that only HL candidates sit, and it tests experimental technique and data analysis directly: reading instruments to sensible precision, spotting that a method cannot answer its question, choosing controlled variables, judging whether data supports a conclusion, and linearising a relationship to read physics from a gradient. Schools teach it inside a crowded practical timetable and usually reach it late. It responds well to a separate block of past data-analysis questions, one a week, marked properly rather than discussed.

faqs.question: How much of the IB physics grade is the investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Higher and Standard Level, and most of those marks are decided before any data exists. The recurring design faults are a research question with no measurable independent variable, a range too narrow for a relationship to show above the noise, too few repeats to say anything honest about reliability, and a controlled variable that was not actually controlled. None of those is a writing problem, which is why a tutor reading the criteria with the student in week one is worth several reading a draft in week ten.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's physics Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: With it, substantially; instead of them, not at all. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards and what it is worth, test whether a proposed research question can be investigated with the equipment available, check that the planned range and number of repeats will produce analysable data, and give feedback against the criteria on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply data or calculations, provide a model to adapt, or edit it to a finish. The student signs an authorship declaration.

faqs.question: What are the commonest uncertainty mistakes in IB physics?
faqs.answer: Four, and all are single-session fixes that recur in every paper until fixed. Adding percentage uncertainties where absolutes should be added, for quantities added or subtracted. Adding absolutes where fractional or percentage uncertainties should be combined, for quantities multiplied or divided. Forgetting to multiply the percentage uncertainty by the power when a quantity is raised to one. And quoting a final answer to the calculator's precision rather than the precision the measurement justified. Each is examined across components and each is taught in a hurry almost everywhere.

faqs.question: What does linearising a graph mean and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Many physics relationships are not straight lines, and the examinable skill is choosing what to plot so that they become one — against the reciprocal, the square, or the logarithm, depending on the relationship — and then reading a physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. It matters because it appears in the practical paper, in structured questions, and in the Internal Assessment analysis marks. Students who have met it once tend to plot the raw variables, produce a curve, and have nothing to say about it. It is a technique rather than a topic, so it responds fast.

faqs.question: Does taking AI maths alongside Physics HL cause problems?
faqs.answer: It creates a specific gap worth planning for rather than a problem. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology rather than algebraic manipulation, so a student can be doing well in maths and still lack the rearrangement, index and logarithm fluency their physics paper assumes. The combination is common in Dubai schools and workable, provided the algebra underneath is taught explicitly alongside. Six to ten focused sessions on rearrangement, indices, logarithms and gradient reasoning changes how every later physics session lands.

faqs.question: Is there an HL physics specialist living near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The IB is about 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils spread across the whole emirate, only the final two years sit the Diploma, and Physics at Higher Level is a narrow specialism inside that. The pool of people who have taught it to final grade is small citywide, and most of them are serving school staff whose permit code of conduct bars tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Online matching removes distance from a problem in which distance was never the binding constraint.

faqs.question: What time should a physics session be scheduled out here?
faqs.answer: At an hour the student can still think in, which in physics matters more than most subjects — nobody follows a derivation while tired. For Year 12 that is usually 4:45pm, straight off the Motor City or Dubai Sports City run, a slot that exists only because nobody is driving to you. For Year 13 it is often 8pm for ninety minutes, when a full data-analysis question plus marking fits without rushing. Weekend mornings suit physics particularly well because the subject rewards sustained work on one thread.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor come to our home in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers physics tuition to DAMAC Hills 2 one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from the Al Qudra corridor a real share of that is the drive. For Diploma physics the binding constraint is whether the tutor can teach the practical paper and uncertainty work, which is unrelated to how close they live.

faqs.question: What are DAMAC Hills 2 families paying for IB physics help?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026: qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate giving AED 200-450 plus, budget online from AED 33-65 with Tutopiya and EdFlik, in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel, and BartyED at AED 650 premium. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work. Those belong to the providers named; we quote after the diagnostic.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor ever enough for Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and physics shows why more clearly than most subjects. At AED 33-65 an hour a capable graduate can explain Newton's laws perfectly well. What they generally cannot do is teach uncertainty propagation correctly, insist on maximum and minimum lines through error bars, or tell a student what the practical paper actually rewards — and that is precisely where the marks are going. A term with somebody who has never marked a data-analysis question is the clearest example in this market of a cheap purchase producing nothing at all.

faqs.question: My child has mocks in six weeks. What is worth doing in that time?
faqs.answer: Technique, in a specific order, and nothing else. First, the rule that every step goes on paper, because method marks are being forfeited by a student computing mentally. Second, uncertainty propagation, which is four fixable confusions and recurs in every paper. Third, past structured questions marked properly rather than discussed, with the error pattern deciding the next session. Content gaps larger than a topic or two are not realistically closable in six weeks, and we will say so after the diagnostic rather than imply otherwise.

faqs.question: Would one tutor covering both physics and maths help our Year 13?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in this pairing specifically there is a real argument for it. The algebraic and graphical demands overlap heavily, so one specialist can stop a student treating the two as unrelated and can teach the rearrangement layer once rather than twice. It also lets one person weigh a Physics Internal Assessment deadline against a maths mock instead of two tutors each optimising for their own subject. What we will not do is stretch a tutor across courses they do not genuinely teach to save a second match.

faqs.question: When are IB physics exams for schools near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no specific IB date, and the reason matters: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and we will not put an unverified date in front of a family who will plan around it. Get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. For IGCSE siblings, Cambridge runs June and November series — February/March is offered to India only — and Pearson runs May/June and November.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-deira.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are Diploma Physics specialists: people who teach the 2023 guide, mark against the published criteria, and can tell you within one lesson whether a problem is conceptual, mathematical or a reading-the-question problem. Deira families work with them over live video.

intro.heading: Physics is not one subject, and that is why tuition for it goes wrong
paragraphs: A Deira student who is struggling in IB Physics is almost never struggling with physics as a whole. They are struggling with a specific thing: resolving forces on an incline, the sign convention in a potential-energy problem, reading a gradient off a log-log plot, or writing a conclusion that compares a measured value to an accepted one with a percentage discrepancy rather than the word "close". A general science tutor will respond to "my child is weak in physics" by going back to the beginning. A Diploma Physics specialist will ask to see the last two tests and the mark scheme, and will usually find that the student can do four of the five things the paper asked.

That distinction matters more under the 2023 Physics guide than it did under the old one. The syllabus is now organised as five themes rather than a core-plus-options structure, and the examination has two papers instead of three. Paper 1 arrives in two halves that test genuinely different skills: Paper 1A is multiple choice, Paper 1B is data analysis and experimental method. Paper 2 is short and extended response. A student can be strong on 1A, where a good instinct and a formula sheet carry you a long way, and lose heavily on 1B, where you have to decide what to plot, work out an uncertainty and explain why a line does not pass through the origin. Those are separable skills and they need separable practice.

The other half of the grade problem sits outside the examination hall. The Scientific Investigation is 20% of the final mark, it is worth 24 marks across four criteria, and it is the single component where a Deira student has the most control and typically the least guidance. School physics departments in Dubai are stretched: a teacher running DP1 and DP2 Physics alongside MYP Sciences has limited time to read a twelve-page draft closely and tell a student that the research question is unanswerable with the equipment available. That conversation, early, is worth more marks than any amount of past-paper drilling.

Geography is the reason this page exists. Deira and the surrounding districts — Al Garhoud, Al Mamzar, Hor Al Anz, Al Muteena, Al Qusais, Al Nahda — have no shortage of capable tutors, but they have very few Diploma Physics HL specialists, and the ones who exist are booked by families within a short drive of them. A parent in Hor Al Anz looking for someone who has marked the Scientific Investigation is choosing from whoever happens to be local and free at 5pm, which is a small pool for a narrow subject. Teaching over live video removes the constraint entirely: the question becomes who knows the 2023 guide, not who can reach Al Muteena before Maghrib.

So this page is written from the subject outwards. It sets out the five themes and what each one actually demands, breaks the examination down component by component with weightings and durations, lists where marks are lost topic by topic, explains the four Scientific Investigation criteria and the mark allocation behind each, and states plainly what a tutor is permitted to do with a student's own investigation under IB academic-honesty rules. The cost section quotes what the Dubai market charges, with the source for each band, so you can judge whether a quote you have been given is reasonable.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-deira.programmesIntro: Physics tuition for a Deira family almost always sits inside one of these programmes, and the right starting point depends on which one. programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years, taken at Standard or Higher Level. Content is organised into five themes: Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; and Nuclear and quantum physics. HL students take additional content inside each theme rather than a separate options paper. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the Scientific Investigation at 20%.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai DP cohorts are small by subject. A school with 90 Diploma students may run a single combined SL and HL Physics class, which means HL content gets taught to a room where half the students will never sit it. programmes.description: Physics appears inside integrated or discrete MYP Sciences and is assessed on four criteria — knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science — each marked out of eight against published descriptors rather than a percentage.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP transition is the sharpest step in Dubai physics teaching. MYP criterion C rewards a student who processes data and evaluates it in their own words; Paper 1B rewards a student who can calculate an absolute uncertainty and propagate it. A Deira student arriving in DP1 from MYP5 usually needs six to eight weeks of explicit uncertainty and graphing work before the first DP test is a fair measure of them.

programmes.name: Scientific Investigation supervision
programmes.description: The individual investigation is a single scientific report of up to 3,000 words, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is 20% of the Physics grade at both levels and is marked internally against IB criteria, then moderated.

A Deira student with access to a light gate and a ramp can do excellent work on energy loss; a student planning something that needs a vacuum pump cannot. dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-deira.subjectsIntro: Physics is the reason you are on this page, but Deira families rarely need only one subject. These are the areas a Diploma Physics tutor is most often asked to cover alongside it, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Physics: Theme A — Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces and momentum, work, energy and power, with rigid body mechanics and special relativity added at HL. Marks are lost on sign conventions, on treating momentum as a scalar, and on answers that quote a speed without stating the frame of reference.

subjects.name: Physics: Theme B — The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal energy transfers, the greenhouse effect, the gas laws, current and circuits, with thermodynamics at HL. The recurring error is confusing temperature with internal energy, and circuit questions where students apply a formula before deciding whether components are in series or parallel.

subjects.name: Physics: Theme C — Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, the wave model, wave phenomena, standing waves and resonance, and the Doppler effect. Standing-wave questions reward a student who can count nodes and relate length to wavelength; most marks go on diagrams drawn without labelling the fixed ends.

subjects.name: Physics: Theme D — Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational fields, electric and magnetic fields, motion in electromagnetic fields, with electromagnetic induction at HL. This is the theme Deira students most often name as the point things stopped working, usually because field strength and potential are being used interchangeably.

subjects.name: Physics: Theme E — Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Structure of the atom, radioactive decay, fission, fusion and stellar processes, with quantum physics and nuclear binding energy at HL. Mass defect calculations fail on unit conversion more often than on physics; practising in MeV rather than joules fixes most of it.

subjects.name: Physics: Tools and the data booklet
subjects.description: Experimental technique, uncertainty, graphing and the mathematics the course assumes. Not a theme, but examined throughout Paper 1B. A student who knows where every equation sits in the data booklet saves several minutes a paper, and minutes are marks in Paper 2.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion to Physics HL. Differentiation and integration carry directly into kinematics and induction, so weak calculus shows up as a physics problem. Students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside Physics HL need the algebraic work done deliberately.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken with Physics by most Deira students aiming at engineering or medicine. Shares the same Scientific Investigation structure and the same four assessment criteria, so investigation coaching transfers between the two subjects almost completely.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: The feeder qualification. Paper structures differ between Cambridge and Edexcel, and so does the practical assessment route, so the first question for a Year 11 student in Deira is which syllabus code their school actually entered them for.

subjects.name: Computer Science and Design Technology
subjects.description: Both share the Diploma's internal-assessment rhythm and both are commonly paired with Physics in Dubai schools. A student juggling two internal assessments in the same term needs a plan, not two separate tutors working in isolation.

sections.heading: What a Deira parent is really asking when they search for an IB Physics tutor
paragraphs: The honest answer to the search is that an IB physics tutor in Deira will be teaching your child over live video, not arriving at a building in Al Rigga. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service offered only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because the alternative is a parent discovering it after a phone call. What you get instead is a Diploma Physics specialist chosen from the whole of the matched tutor pool rather than from the handful who could reach Deira by car at 5pm on a Tuesday.

For a subject as narrow as Diploma Physics, that trade is heavily in a Deira family's favour. The pool of tutors who have taught the 2023 guide, marked a Scientific Investigation against the published criteria and seen enough Paper 1B scripts to know which uncertainty errors recur is not large anywhere in the world, and it is certainly not concentrated in one district of old Dubai. Searching locally for a rare specialism produces either a long wait or a compromise: a competent general science tutor who will do a reasonable job on Theme A and guess at Theme E.

There is also a practical argument that only applies to this part of Dubai. The distances between Deira, Al Qusais, Al Nahda and Al Mamzar are short, and the afternoon journey times between them are not. A tutor travelling from Al Garhoud to Hor Al Anz at 3:30pm is in the car for twenty-five minutes each way, and that hour is in the hourly rate whether it is itemised or not. On video the session starts at the agreed minute, the whiteboard history from last week is still there, and a cancelled lesson can be moved to the next evening rather than lost.

What should decide this is the diagnosis, not the format. Book the trial lesson, hand the tutor the last marked physics test and the mark scheme, and listen to what they say about it. A specialist will tell you which of the five themes is actually weak, whether the problem is physics or algebra, and whether Paper 1B is dragging the grade down independently of everything else. If that conversation is vague, the format of the lesson was never the issue.

sections.heading: The five themes of the 2023 IB Physics guide, and what each one demands
paragraphs: The current Physics guide, first taught in 2023, replaced the old core-and-options structure with five themes labelled A to E, taught to both Standard and Higher Level students with additional HL content sitting inside each theme rather than in a separate paper. Running underneath all five is a strand the guide calls the Tools of physics: experimental technique, the use of technology, and the mathematics the course assumes. That strand is not a theme you revise, but it is examined constantly, and it is where a surprising share of the lost marks sit.

The practical consequence for a Deira student is that there is no longer an options paper to carry a weak theme. Under the previous structure a student could be shaky on one area and rescue the grade elsewhere. Now the content of all five themes is examinable in both papers, so a persistent gap in Theme D shows up twice. It also means the sequence a school teaches in matters: a school that leaves Theme E until the final term is asking its students to learn mass-defect calculations during the period they should be practising whole papers.

Below is the theme structure with the HL additions named and the recurring loss point for each. It is worth reading alongside your child's own scheme of work, because the gap between what the guide contains and what has actually been taught by February of DP2 is the single most useful thing a parent can establish before booking anything.

One warning about resources. Plenty of material circulating online is still written against the pre-2023 syllabus, with Paper 3 and the old options in it. A student revising from a question bank built for the previous guide will spend time on content that is no longer assessed and miss the new emphasis on data analysis in Paper 1B. Checking that a tutor is working from the current guide is a reasonable thing to ask in a trial lesson.

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: the assessment structure component by component
paragraphs: IB Physics is examined in two papers at both levels, and the weightings are identical: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade, Paper 2 carries 44%, and the Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20%. The durations differ by level — Higher Level papers are longer because there is more content and the extended-response demand is greater — but the proportions do not. A parent who understands only that is already ahead of most, because it immediately tells you that Paper 2 is where the grade is decided and that the investigation is worth more than a fifth of everything.

The structure inside Paper 1 is where the useful detail lives. Paper 1A is multiple choice. Paper 1B is a set of data-analysis and experimental-method questions built around a given investigation. These reward completely different behaviours. Paper 1A rewards speed, elimination and a sound physical instinct; a student can often get there without a full calculation. Paper 1B rewards exactly the opposite: slow, careful work on uncertainties, gradients, what to plot against what, and whether a systematic error would shift an intercept or a slope. Students who are good at one are frequently poor at the other, and a school report that says "B in physics" hides that completely.

Paper 2 is short and extended response across all five themes. The failure mode here is almost never ignorance. It is command-term discipline and time. A question that says "deduce" is asking for a conclusion with reasoning attached; a student who writes a description gets the description marks and loses the rest. A question worth six marks needs six distinct scoring points, and students routinely make three points very well and then run out of time on the last question because the first one was over-answered. Timed practice with the mark scheme beside the script is the only thing that fixes this, and it is the work a tutor can supervise most usefully.

The table sets out the components with durations and weightings, and names the specific skill each one is testing. Use it to decide where the available tuition hours should go. A Deira student losing four marks a paper on Paper 1B is losing roughly a grade boundary's worth from a component that can be taught in six focused sessions, which is a far better return than another pass through Theme A.

sections.heading: Where IB Physics marks are actually lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: Mark loss in Diploma Physics is remarkably consistent, and almost all of it is diagnosable from two marked papers. The pattern repeats across cohorts and across schools, which is why a specialist can be useful quickly: they are not discovering your child's weaknesses from scratch, they are checking which items from a known list apply. Below is the list as it recurs in Dubai cohorts, in rough order of how much it costs.

The largest single category is command terms. The Diploma uses a defined vocabulary — state, describe, explain, deduce, determine, outline, discuss — and each one specifies a depth of response. A student who answers every question with the same register will systematically under-answer the "explain" questions and over-answer the "state" ones, losing marks at one end and time at the other. This is learnable in a few sessions and it transfers across all five themes at once, which makes it the highest-yield thing to fix first.

Second is unit and prefix discipline. Kilojoules treated as joules, megaelectronvolts treated as electronvolts, centimetres entered into a formula expecting metres: these cost full marks on questions the student understood completely. The repair is mechanical. Every numerical answer gets a unit written before the number is calculated, and every value gets converted on the line it is written down rather than in the student's head.

Third is the uncertainty and graphing cluster that Paper 1B is built on: absolute versus percentage uncertainty, which quantity to plot to get a straight line, what a non-zero intercept implies, and the difference between a systematic and a random error. Fourth, and specific to Theme D, is the conflation of field strength with potential — one a vector measured in newtons per kilogram or newtons per coulomb, the other a scalar energy per unit mass or charge. Fifth is the habit of starting a mechanics question without a free-body diagram, which turns a two-mark resolution into a guess.

None of these are intelligence problems and none of them require a longer course. They require someone to read a marked script carefully, name the specific error, and then set practice that cannot be completed without correcting it. That is the entire method, and it is why the first session with a Deira student is spent on their own papers rather than on a lesson plan written in advance.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation: four criteria, 24 marks, and the honesty line
paragraphs: The individual Scientific Investigation is 20% of the Physics grade at both Standard and Higher Level. It is a single report of up to 3,000 words on an investigation the student designs and carries out, marked by the school against four published criteria and then moderated by the IB. Each criterion carries six marks, for 24 in total. The criteria are the whole of the specification for this component, and a student who has not read them is writing blind.

The most expensive failures happen before any data is collected. A research question that cannot be answered with the equipment actually available, or that has no measurable independent variable, caps every criterion that follows: the design cannot be strong, the data cannot be sufficient, and the conclusion cannot be supported. Thirty minutes spent testing feasibility against the school laboratory's real apparatus is worth more than a week of writing. This is the single most useful thing a tutor can do on this component, and it has to happen early.

Uncertainty is the second cluster. A physics investigation is expected to carry uncertainties through from the instrument to the final result, to show error bars where they are meaningful, and to say something defensible about whether the trend survives them. Students frequently report a gradient to five significant figures from data measured with a ruler, which signals to a moderator that the uncertainty work was not understood. Evaluation then asks for improvements that are specific and physical — a different sensor, a longer run, a controlled variable that was not controlled — rather than the generic "repeat more times".

Now the boundary, stated plainly because it matters more than anything else on this page. Under IB academic-honesty rules the investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, explain what a criterion is asking for, ask questions about a draft, point out that an uncertainty has not been propagated, and model the method on different data. A tutor may not write the report, rewrite sections of it, supply a research question to be submitted as the student's own, or edit a draft into its final form. IB Gram tutors work inside that line and tell the student where it is in the first session. Any service offering a completed investigation is exposing the student to a malpractice finding that can cost them the Diploma.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs in Deira, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the gap rather than the headline rate, because that is the figure that decides the format. Published market rates in Dubai put an in-home one-to-one visit at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour — Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table gives AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. A qualified subject tutor working online sits lower: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The difference between those two bands is not a difference in teaching. It is the car.

In the Deira cluster that premium buys something specific and fairly small. A tutor travelling from Al Garhoud to Hor Al Anz or from Al Qusais into Deira at 3:30pm spends somewhere around fifty minutes in traffic for a sixty-minute lesson. Somebody pays for that hour, and the only question is whether it appears on the invoice as a travel charge or is folded into a higher rate. It also buys a smaller choice of tutor, because the only people who can take the appointment are the ones already close by — which for a subject as narrow as Diploma Physics HL is a real constraint rather than a theoretical one.

The rest of the market sits either side. Budget online tuition, typically delivered by university students, runs from about AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate puts the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 or more. At the top, named and examiner-led tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED quoting AED 650. Monthly packages seen in the market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram's price list. What a Deira family should take from them is a sense of where a quote sits: a Diploma Physics HL specialist quoting AED 120 an hour is probably not a Diploma Physics HL specialist, and one quoting AED 600 is charging a premium you should be able to see the reason for. For IB Gram's own figure, the free trial lesson and the follow-up conversation are the route; the trial is one lesson and does not commit you to a block.

sections.heading: Working backwards from the examination session for a Deira physics student
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May Diploma session, so a DP2 physics student's year runs backwards from there, and the internal deadlines arrive long before the papers do. The Scientific Investigation is normally collected by the school in the first months of DP2, which means the data is gathered in DP1 or the autumn term at the latest. A family that starts thinking about physics support in the spring of DP2 has already passed the point where 20% of the grade could be influenced. Specific IB session and results dates are not published here; confirm them with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, because they are the kind of date a parent acts on.

For IGCSE students in the same household the calendar is different and worth separating. Cambridge International runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and Dubai candidates sit those two. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after consulting the wrong one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Working backwards from a May session, the useful structure for physics is roughly this. Twelve months out, the investigation research question should be tested for feasibility. Nine months out, data collection should be finished and Paper 1B skills should be in regular practice rather than left to revision. Six months out, the first whole Paper 2 should have been sat under timing, because the time-allocation problem only appears at full length. Three months out, practice shifts from topic sets to whole papers marked against the published scheme. Six weeks out, the work is error-pattern repair on the student's own marked scripts, not new content.

Ramadan falls inside this run and reshapes the week rather than pausing it. Dubai school hours shorten, energy drops in the afternoon, and the productive window moves to late evening after Iftar. Deira families routinely move sessions to 9pm or later during Ramadan, which is straightforward for a video lesson and considerably harder for an appointment that depends on someone driving across the city. Planning the shift in advance rather than cancelling four weeks of sessions is what keeps the backwards schedule intact.

sections.heading: KHDA, the Dubai school market, and the mandatory subjects running alongside DP Physics
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. It is worth knowing which body applies to your child's school, because inspection reports and fee decisions come from there and nowhere else. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA or any other regulator, and nobody offering tuition should imply otherwise.

The scale of the market is relevant to why specialist supply is thin. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the International Baccalaureate at 7%. That last figure is the key one for this page: IB is a minority programme in a very large market, so Diploma Physics specialists are a minority within a minority. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for 2026-27 under Dubai's economic incentives package, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three IB — creating 16,846 new places.

Running alongside whatever curriculum a Deira school is licensed for, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. The rules are specific: schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

For a physics student this is a timetable fact with real consequences. Those mandatory periods occupy space in a DP2 week that is already carrying six subjects, an Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and an internal assessment in every science. When a Deira family asks why their child cannot find time to practise Paper 1B, the answer is often visible on the timetable rather than in the student's attitude. A single scheduled session that is protected, short and specific tends to survive that week better than an open-ended plan to revise more.

sections.heading: Tutor permits, verification, and what a Deira parent can check themselves
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity, not an unregulated one. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and u.ae states that it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed and a stated completion time of two working days. That is a short, free, two-day process, which is why a tutor's inability to discuss it is informative. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

There is one more rule a Deira parent should know, because it is occasionally offered as a selling point. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This has been press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK directly if it matters to your decision. Either way, "your child's own teacher, privately" is not something to seek out.

What you can verify yourself, in order: that the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition permit and will say so; that they are working from the 2023 Physics guide rather than the previous one; that they can describe criteria A to D of the Scientific Investigation without looking them up; that they will send written feedback after each session; and that any examiner status claimed can be evidenced. Nobody should be describing themselves as approved by the IB, KHDA or Cambridge, because those approvals are specific things issued to specific entities and a private tutor does not hold them.

faqs.question: How many marks is each paper worth in the current IB Physics course?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade, Paper 2 carries 44%, and the Scientific Investigation carries 20%. Those weightings are the same at Standard and Higher Level; what differs is paper length, with HL Paper 1 running two hours against SL's hour and a half, and HL Paper 2 running two and a half hours against SL's hour and a half. The practical reading is that Paper 2 decides the grade and the investigation is worth more than a fifth of it, so a revision plan weighted entirely towards multiple-choice practice is misallocated from the start.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 1A and Paper 1B in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Paper 1A is multiple choice and Paper 1B is data analysis and experimental method built around a given investigation. They sit inside the same paper and the same time allowance but they test opposite behaviours. Paper 1A rewards speed, elimination and physical instinct, often without a full calculation. Paper 1B rewards slow, careful work on uncertainties, gradients, choice of axes and whether an error is systematic or random. Students are frequently strong on one and weak on the other, and a single grade on a report card hides that completely.

faqs.question: My child in Deira understands physics in class but loses marks in tests. Why?
faqs.answer: That pattern usually points at command terms rather than content. The Diploma specifies response depth through words like state, describe, explain and deduce, and a student who answers everything at the same register under-answers the explain questions and over-answers the state ones. The second common cause is time allocation: three questions answered beautifully and the last one left blank. Both are visible immediately in a marked script and both are fixable in a handful of sessions, which is why the trial lesson is spent reading papers rather than teaching a topic.

faqs.question: Which IB Physics theme do Deira students struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Theme D, Fields, is named more often than any other, and the reason is usually one specific confusion rather than the whole theme. Field strength and potential get used interchangeably, when one is a vector measured in newtons per kilogram or newtons per coulomb and the other is a scalar energy per unit mass or charge. Once that separation is secure, gravitational and electric field questions stop being guesswork. Theme E runs a close second, but there the losses are mostly unit conversion in mass-defect calculations rather than the underlying nuclear physics.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Physics Scientific Investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, explain what each criterion asks for, question a draft, point out that an uncertainty has not been propagated, and demonstrate a method on different data. A tutor may not write or rewrite the report, supply a research question for the student to submit as their own, or edit a draft into its final form. The investigation must be the student's own work. Any service offering a completed investigation puts the student at risk of a malpractice finding that can cost them the Diploma.

faqs.question: How are the 24 marks split across the Physics investigation criteria?
faqs.answer: Four criteria, six marks each. Research design covers the research question, the justified methodology and the controlled variables. Data analysis covers recording, processing and presenting data with uncertainties. Conclusion asks for a result justified by the data and related to accepted physics. Evaluation asks for strengths, limitations and specific realistic improvements. The report runs to a maximum of 3,000 words. Reading those four criteria before choosing a research question is the cheapest marks available on the component, and most students read them after the data is already collected.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to our apartment in Deira?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is offered only in India. Lessons for Deira families are delivered live, one to one, over video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. For Diploma Physics that is an advantage rather than a compromise: the match is made from the whole specialist pool instead of the few tutors who could reach Deira by car at 5pm, and no part of the hourly rate is paying for a journey across the Creek in afternoon traffic.

faqs.question: What does the in-home travel premium actually add to a physics tutor's rate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives AED 180 to 350 for home visits and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500; Unitors publishes online IB tuition from AED 200. The gap is travel time and a locally restricted tutor pool, not better teaching. In the Deira cluster a tutor can spend close to an hour in traffic for a one-hour lesson, and somebody pays for that hour.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week does a Deira DP student usually need?
faqs.answer: One well-targeted session a week is the normal starting point, and it is enough for most students through DP1. Two becomes reasonable in the months before the examination session, or when a student is carrying both a weak component and an unfinished investigation. More than two a week rarely helps, because the limiting factor is the practice the student does between lessons rather than the teaching hours themselves. The useful test after six weeks is whether the specific error pattern in the marked scripts has changed, not whether the student feels more confident.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start physics tuition in the final term before the exams?
faqs.answer: It is late for the investigation, because that work is normally collected by the school months earlier, and 20% of the grade is settled by then. It is not late for the papers. Six to eight weeks of focused work on command terms, timing and the specific error pattern in a student's own marked scripts changes paper performance measurably, because those are mechanical faults rather than knowledge gaps. What does not work in a final term is attempting to reteach all five themes, so a late start has to be ruthless about which component is losing the most.

faqs.question: Which exam sessions do physics students in Dubai actually sit?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB schools sit the May Diploma session. For IGCSE, Cambridge International runs June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, as it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Confirm specific IB dates with your school's coordinator or on ibo.org, and always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

faqs.question: Do physics tutors working with Deira families need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without the permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Deira school teach Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Because KHDA requires it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a DP2 physics student those periods are a real constraint on the week, which is worth seeing on the timetable.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics and Maths AA for a student in Deira?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because the overlap is genuine: differentiation and integration carry directly into kinematics and electromagnetic induction, so weak calculus often presents as a physics problem. A tutor comfortable with both can fix the cause rather than the symptom. The caution is depth. Physics HL and Maths AA HL are each demanding enough that a tutor claiming full command of both should be asked which they have actually taught to Higher Level and for how long, rather than taken on the claim.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan and shortened school hours affect a physics tuition plan?
faqs.answer: They move it rather than pause it. Dubai school hours shorten during Ramadan, afternoon energy drops, and the productive study window shifts to late evening after Iftar. Deira families routinely reschedule sessions to 9pm or later for the month, which a video lesson accommodates easily and an appointment depending on a cross-city drive does not. The mistake is cancelling four weeks outright, because in a DP2 year that is a month of the backwards calendar lost. Agreeing the Ramadan timing in advance keeps the schedule intact.

faqs.question: What should we send a physics tutor before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things, and they are worth more than a long description. First, the last marked physics test or paper with the mark scheme, because the lost marks are the diagnosis. Second, the school's scheme of work or a note of which themes have been taught, so the session addresses what is current rather than a generic order. Third, the school's internal deadline for the Scientific Investigation. With those in hand a trial lesson produces a specific plan; without them it produces a pleasant conversation and a guess.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are physics teachers who work theme by theme and paper by paper rather than chapter by chapter. Each one has taught the current Diploma physics course, with its two written papers and its single scientific investigation, and each can start inside a DIFC family's evening window.

intro.heading: The physics hour a DIFC family actually has
paragraphs: Almost nobody lives and studies inside the same square kilometre in this part of Dubai. DIFC is a working district of towers, serviced apartments and the Gate Village, and the schools its families use sit outside it: Sobha Hartland across the creek, Al Jaddaf a short run down Al Khail, Nad Al Sheba and Meydan to the south, Al Safa and Al Sufouh to the west. The consequence is a timetable problem rather than a teaching problem. A Year 12 physics student is not short of hours in the abstract. They are short of the specific hours between the car arriving home and the point at which nothing useful goes in.

That is why this page is organised around the clock rather than around a subject brochure. Most Dubai secondary timetables release pupils somewhere between 14:45 and 15:30. Add the return leg at the worst part of the afternoon, add a sibling pick-up, add the fifteen minutes of nothing that every teenager needs after a school day, and the first honest start time from a DIFC address is usually 16:45 or later. On a day with swimming, Model United Nations or a Duke of Edinburgh session it is 18:30. A physics plan that ignores this gets abandoned in week three, and the family concludes that tutoring does not work when what failed was the diary.

The subject itself does not forgive a thin week. Diploma physics is assessed through two written papers and one piece of internally assessed work, and the written papers between them carry four fifths of the grade. Paper 1 mixes multiple-choice with a data-based section; Paper 2 is extended response, where a student who understands the physics can still lose a third of the available marks on definitions, units, significant figures and the command term they skimmed. None of that is fixed by reading the textbook again. It is fixed by working through questions with somebody who can see the working as it happens and stop it mid-line.

Online delivery is what makes the narrow window usable. A tutor who has to be driven across Dubai needs the slot to start early enough to be worth the journey, which is exactly the slot a DIFC family does not have. A tutor joining over live video can take 17:00 on Monday, 20:00 on Wednesday and 09:30 on a Saturday morning, and can be a Higher Level physics specialist rather than whoever happens to live within twenty minutes of the Gate Avenue car park. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India, and this page makes the comparison openly rather than hiding it.

What follows is the detail a parent in this district can act on: the realistic session windows school by school, where the physics marks actually sit, the order to repair the five themes in, the four criteria the scientific investigation is marked against, the maths a Higher Level course assumes you already have, what the Dubai market charges in AED per hour and who publishes those figures, and the limits we will not pretend away.

There is no Paper 3 in the current Diploma physics course

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.programmesIntro: Physics does not begin in Year 12. A DIFC family is normally somewhere on a line that runs from middle-school science criteria, through a Year 11 qualification, into the Diploma. These are the four points on that line where tutoring changes the outcome, and what each one asks of a student in this district.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme physics
programmes.description: Two years, five themes, two written papers and one scientific investigation. Higher Level covers the same five themes as Standard Level with additional content and longer papers; the component weightings are identical, so the extra Higher Level load shows up as breadth and as harder algebra rather than as a different exam structure. Students choose physics alongside five other subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service.
programmes.countryNote: In DIFC the practical constraint is subject combination rather than subject choice. A student at a smaller inland campus may find Higher Level physics timetabled against Higher Level economics or against the Arabic class KHDA requires every Dubai private school to run. Where the school cannot resolve the clash, the content a student misses has to be rebuilt outside school hours, and that is the single most common reason a DIFC parent starts looking in October rather than in April.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Integrated sciences until the final years, then separate sciences at many schools. Assessment is criterion-based: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science, each marked out of eight and reported as a level from one to seven. A pupil can be strong on recall and weak on the design criterion and still see a middling overall level that explains nothing.
programmes.countryNote: Several campuses within reach of DIFC run the Middle Years Programme as their lower-secondary route, including the Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf schools. Families moving in from a British system part-way through are the ones who feel the jolt: there is no equivalent of a percentage mark, the criteria are published but rarely explained to parents, and the processing and evaluating criterion is where most new arrivals lose ground in their first reporting cycle.

programmes.name: Year 11 physics before the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge physics 0625 or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE physics 4PH1, taken as a separate science or inside a combined award. Extended or Higher tier is what a Diploma physics course assumes: the circuit theory, the wave vocabulary, the rearranging of formulae and the graph work all reappear in Year 12 at speed and without reteaching. A Core-tier or combined-science background is workable but needs deliberate filling in.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai is a British-curriculum market by weight of enrolment, and most DIFC families arrive at the Diploma through a Year 11 qualification rather than through the Middle Years Programme. That matters for the summer between Year 11 and Year 12. Six weeks spent on mechanics vocabulary, on standard form and on reading a gradient is the cheapest physics support a family in this district will ever buy, because it is bought before anything has gone wrong.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller route that pairs Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where a student takes Diploma physics inside the Career-related Programme, the physics course and its assessment are identical to the full Diploma version; what changes is the surrounding core and the time available for it. Support is therefore the same physics teaching with a different weekly budget around it.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools within easy reach of DIFC offer this route, so most families will never meet it. It is listed here because the ones who do are usually trying to work out whether a physics course taken this way is the same course. It is. The written papers, the five themes and the scientific investigation do not change, and a university reading the transcript sees the same physics grade.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only thing a DIFC family is managing, and it is almost never the only thing that needs attention. These are the courses that sit closest to a Diploma physics timetable, with what each one is actually assessed on rather than what the subject brochure says.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics. Paper 1 combines multiple-choice with a data-based section, Paper 2 is extended response, and the scientific investigation is worth a fifth of the grade. Most lost marks are procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most Higher Level physics students take. Calculus, trigonometric identities, vectors and logarithms all surface inside physics problems before the maths course has covered them, so the two subjects need sequencing together rather than separately. Weak algebraic fluency shows up as physics errors long before it shows up as maths errors.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led, with graphing technology assumed throughout. Perfectly compatible with Standard Level physics and workable with Higher Level, but it leaves gaps in symbolic manipulation that a physics tutor ends up filling. Worth checking against any engineering or physical-science course a student is aiming at, because some programmes name Analysis and Approaches specifically.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken alongside physics by most students heading for engineering or medicine. The energetics, bonding and kinetics content overlaps with physics thinking, and the scientific investigation uses the same four criteria, so a student doing both can prepare one piece of coursework method and apply it twice. The organic sequence is where the time goes.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The other common science pairing in this district, often chosen with Standard Level physics. Biology is marked on the same investigation criteria and the same command terms, which means a student who has learned to answer 'explain' properly in physics gains marks in biology for free. The volume of recall is the differentiator.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Frequently chosen by DIFC students with a finance or technology household around them. The logic and systems content is independent of physics, but the two subjects compete for the same evening hours and the computer science solution has a hard internal deadline, so the two timetables need planning as one.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered at a minority of Dubai campuses. Mechanics, materials and energy content runs close to physics, and students often take both. The design project is substantial and its deadlines rarely line up kindly with the physics investigation, which is the practical reason to map both onto one calendar in September.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece with a supervisor at school. A tutor may discuss the physics, question the research question and ask whether the argument holds; the writing, the data and the final judgement are the student's. Narrowing the question early is the single most useful intervention, and it costs an hour.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects. Science students often find the exhibition harder than the essay because it asks them to argue about knowledge rather than about content. It carries points alongside the Extended Essay, so it is not optional in any practical sense.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. These lessons occupy timetable slots and sometimes clash with science option blocks, which is why they belong in any honest discussion of where a physics hour is going to come from.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.regionsTitle: Where DIFC students actually travel from and to
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.regionsIntro: The useful question in this district is not which areas we cover but what each journey does to an evening. These are the neighbourhoods a DIFC physics student most often commutes into, with the effect each one has on a weekday session.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Ten to fifteen minutes from the Gate Village outside peak, longer on a Sunday afternoon. Two large campuses here, both popular with DIFC families. A pupil leaving at 15:15 is usually home by 15:45, which makes this the easiest commute in the cluster to build a 17:00 physics slot around.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: A straight run along Al Khail or down through Bur Dubai. The continuum school here runs from the early years through the Diploma, so families stay put for a decade. The journey is short but the finish time is later than average, which pushes the first realistic session towards 17:15.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Walking distance in principle, a car journey in practice for most of the year. Students living in Downtown and studying inland face the same return leg as their DIFC neighbours, and the two districts share tutors, timings and the same complaint about the Financial Centre Road slip at four o'clock.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: Dense, residential and increasingly the overflow for DIFC households wanting more floor space. There is no large secondary campus inside Business Bay itself, so almost every family here commutes, which is why online evening slots are taken up faster in this area than anywhere else in the cluster.

regions.name: Meydan and Nad Al Sheba
regions.note: Twenty to twenty-five minutes south, with a British-curriculum campus that feeds a steady number of Diploma students. The drive is clear in the morning and slow coming back, so Nad Al Sheba families more often choose a 17:30 or 18:00 session than a straight-after-school one.

regions.name: Al Quoz and Al Quoz 4
regions.note: Two established campuses plus a newer one, all within a quarter of an hour of DIFC on a good day. The industrial grid around them makes the final approach slower than the distance suggests. Useful to know when a parent is deciding whether a 16:45 start is realistic or merely optimistic.

regions.name: Al Safa and Jumeirah
regions.note: The older British-curriculum belt, with several schools that run Year 11 qualifications before splitting into A Levels or the Diploma. A DIFC student travelling here has a fifteen-minute journey in the morning and a considerably worse one at pick-up, which is the main reason this group books later slots.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and the coast
regions.note: Twenty-five to thirty minutes each way, which is the outer limit most DIFC families will accept for a school run. Students here are usually at selective British campuses and arrive at Diploma physics with strong Year 11 foundations, so support is more often about pace and papers than about gaps.

schoolClusters.city: Inland campuses DIFC families reach in under twenty minutes
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools that make a straight-after-school physics slot possible. All sit within roughly a quarter of an hour of the Gate Village outside the worst of the afternoon, and all run either a Year 11 qualification or the Middle Years Programme into a Diploma or A Level sixth form.

Several of these campuses are selective and well established, so Diploma physics students from them tend to need pace and past-paper discipline rather than foundational repair.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.modesIntro: Four shapes of physics support, chosen by where a student is in the two-year course and by how much of the evening is actually free. All of them run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; none of them involves anybody driving anywhere.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: One 55-minute session a week on a fixed day, tracking the school's own scheme of work rather than a generic syllabus order. The tutor works from the student's class notes and the school's topic list, so the session repairs this week's content while it is still live. This is the shape that suits a Higher Level student who is coping but losing marks in the wrong places.
bullets: Fixed weekday slot between 16:30 and 21:30 Gulf Standard Time

Written note after each session naming the next two priorities

modes.title: Twin sessions before a mock
modes.description: Two shorter sessions a week for four to six weeks ahead of a January or March mock, one on content and one purely on timed questions. The second session is where the marks move, because mock performance in physics is usually a question of exam behaviour rather than of knowledge. Papers are marked against the published mark scheme and the losses are categorised.
bullets: Content session plus a separate timed-paper session each week

modes.title: Scientific investigation clinic
modes.description: A short block of sessions around the internally assessed investigation: narrowing the research question, planning a method that will actually generate analysable data, and then interpreting what came out. The tutor teaches the criteria and asks hard questions about the reasoning. The student designs, collects, analyses and writes; nobody else touches the document.

Feedback is spoken and questioning, never edits typed into the file

modes.title: Holiday and weekend intensives
modes.description: Blocks during the winter and spring breaks and on Saturday mornings, used either to rebuild a theme properly or to buy back the hours a crowded term lost. Dubai school holidays are long enough to make real structural progress, and a student with no school day to recover from can concentrate for ninety minutes rather than fifty-five.

sections.heading: What a DIFC search for physics help is really about
paragraphs: A parent typing 'IB physics tutor in DIFC' is not usually asking a geographical question. They are asking whether anyone who genuinely knows the Diploma physics course can be in the room with their child at half past five on a Tuesday. Proximity is a proxy for availability, and in this district the proxy is a bad one, because the people who live nearest to DIFC are bankers, lawyers and consultants rather than physics teachers. The honest answer is that the specialist exists, is reachable in seconds over live video, and is matched to the paper the student is losing marks on rather than to the postcode on the tenancy contract.

The second thing behind the search is a specific worry. Physics is the subject where a bright student can feel competent and still produce a mediocre mark, and parents notice the gap between the confidence at the kitchen table and the number on the report. That gap is almost always made of procedure: a missing unit, a quantity defined loosely, a graph gradient read without checking the axes, an 'explain' question answered as though it said 'state'. It is diagnosable within one session and fixable within a term, but only by someone reading the student's actual working rather than their final answers.

The third thing is time, and it is the reason the rest of this page is built around a clock. A DIFC household runs on long office hours and a school run that crosses at least one major artery. The question is not whether physics support is a good idea; it is which twenty hours between now and the May session are realistically available, and what the highest-value use of those hours is. Everything below is written to answer that: when a session can start, where the marks sit, what to fix first, and what the Dubai market charges for the same hour delivered three different ways.
bullets: Proximity predicts availability, not subject knowledge
Most physics marks are lost on procedure, not on concepts
The binding constraint in DIFC is the evening, not the budget

sections.heading: The DIFC school run, hour by hour
paragraphs: This is the table nobody in the tutoring market publishes, and it is the one that decides whether a plan survives past October. School finish times in Dubai cluster between 14:45 and 15:30 for secondary, with variation by campus, by year group and by whether the day carries an enrichment block. The return journey is the variable part. The same fifteen-kilometre drive takes eighteen minutes at ten in the morning and forty at four in the afternoon, and the Financial Centre Road and Sheikh Zayed Road slips into DIFC are the slowest part of it.

The figures below are typical rather than official; timetables are set by each school and change by term, so treat them as a planning starting point and confirm against your own child's week. What the table is for is the last column. A family that knows the earliest honest start time stops booking slots that get cancelled, and a tutor who knows it stops offering them. In practice this is the difference between a weekly session that runs for thirty weeks and one that runs for five.

Two patterns show up repeatedly in this cluster. Students at the Sobha Hartland and Al Quoz campuses can usually make a 16:45 or 17:00 start and should take it, because an earlier session leaves the evening free for school homework rather than competing with it. Students travelling back from Al Safa, Al Sufouh or Nad Al Sheba should not attempt a straight-after-school slot at all; 17:45 or 18:00 is a slot that will actually happen, and a session that happens beats a better-timed session that does not.

sections.heading: Where the physics grade actually sits
paragraphs: Diploma physics is assessed through two written papers and one piece of internally assessed work, and the proportions are worth knowing precisely because they tell a family where to spend money. Paper 1 is 36% of the final grade and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 is 44% and is extended response. The scientific investigation is 20%. There is no third paper in the current course, which catches out parents working from an older guide and students revising from second-hand notes.

The structural consequence is that Paper 2 is where the grade is won or lost, and Paper 2 rewards things that are teachable in a one-to-one session. It asks for definitions stated precisely, for quantities with their units, for reasoning set out in steps that a marker can follow, and for command terms obeyed literally. 'State' wants a single line and gets a paragraph. 'Explain' wants a mechanism and gets a description. 'Determine' wants a number with a unit and gets an expression. Each of those is a repeatable error and each one is worth marks every time it occurs.

Paper 1's data-based section is the other place where a strong student underperforms. It presents unfamiliar data and asks for gradients, intercepts, uncertainties and conclusions, and it does not care whether the context has been taught. Students who have only ever analysed data from their own practicals find it disorienting the first time. The remedy is volume: enough unfamiliar data sets, under time, with the uncertainty arithmetic done properly, that the format stops being the obstacle and the physics becomes the only thing left to think about.
