sections.heading: The five themes, and the order to repair them in
paragraphs: The current physics course is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Schools teach them in different orders, which is why a generic revision plan is close to useless and why a tutor needs the school's own topic list before the second session. What does generalise is the order in which a weak student should be repaired, because the themes are not independent and fixing them in the wrong sequence wastes hours.

Space, time and motion comes first regardless of where the school is. It carries the vector work, the graph reading and the energy bookkeeping that every later theme reuses, and a student who is shaky on resolving a vector or on reading a velocity-time gradient will stay shaky in fields and in wave behaviour. Then fields, because electric and gravitational field thinking is the same mathematics twice and students who learn it once learn it cheaply. Wave behaviour third, where the losses are usually vocabulary and diagram convention rather than physics. The particulate nature of matter and the nuclear and quantum theme are the most self-contained and the safest to leave until later, which is also why they are the usual choice for a short pre-exam block.

There is a diagnostic shortcut worth knowing. Ask the student to explain, without notes, what a gradient and an area under a graph represent in three different physics contexts. If they can do that fluently the problem is almost certainly procedural and a term of Paper 2 technique will move the grade. If they cannot, the problem is foundational and the first six weeks belong to space, time and motion whatever the school happens to be teaching. That single question saves a family more money than any discount on an hourly rate.
bullets: Repair order: motion, then fields, then waves, then matter and the quantum theme
Get the school's own topic list before planning anything
Gradient and area fluency is the fastest diagnostic of a foundational gap
Vocabulary and diagram convention, not physics, dominate wave-behaviour losses

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: A fifth of the physics grade comes from one independent investigation, marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. Almost nobody outside the classroom tells parents this, and it changes how the work should be approached. The marks are not awarded for a clever topic or an impressive apparatus. They are awarded for a question narrow enough to answer, data good enough to analyse, a conclusion that follows from the data, and an evaluation that identifies real weaknesses rather than apologising for human error.

The failure mode is almost always criterion A. A student picks something interesting but unbounded, collects data that cannot discriminate between outcomes, and then has nothing to analyse. By the time this is visible the apparatus has been booked, the lab time used and the deadline is weeks away. An hour spent interrogating the research question before any data exists is worth more than ten hours of rescue afterwards, which is why the investigation clinic described above is front-loaded rather than spread across the term.

The boundary on what help is permitted matters here, and we state it plainly rather than leaving it vague. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what uncertainty propagation means, ask whether a conclusion is supported, and point out that an evaluation has not identified a single systematic effect. A tutor may not write, edit or supply any part of the document, choose the research question, or produce the analysis. The student's name on the work has to mean something, and IB academic-honesty rules make the alternative an expulsion risk for the student. Schools in Dubai run originality checks and supervisors sign a declaration; the only safe position is also the only honest one.

table.caption: THE FOUR INVESTIGATION CRITERIA, 24 MARKS IN TOTAL
rows: A focused question, justified method, controlled variables
A question too broad to answer with the data collected
Interrogate the question before any data exists
Teach the arithmetic and the graph choice
A conclusion supported by the data and placed in context
Restating the hypothesis instead of reading the result
Ask whether the data actually supports the claim
Real limitations, their effect, realistic improvements
Generic apologies about human error and timing
Point out that no systematic effect has been identified

sections.heading: The maths underneath Higher Level physics
paragraphs: Higher Level physics assumes a level of algebraic fluency that the maths course has usually not finished delivering. Students meet logarithmic relationships in the nuclear theme, trigonometric resolution in motion, inverse-square behaviour in fields and small-angle approximations in wave behaviour, often weeks or months before the corresponding maths lesson. The result is a student who believes they cannot do physics when what they cannot do is rearrange an equation with three variables under time pressure.

This is the strongest practical argument for pairing physics and maths support rather than treating them as separate purchases. A tutor who can see that a physics error is a logarithm error fixes it in five minutes; a tutor who cannot spends three sessions reteaching radioactive decay to a student whose problem was never radioactive decay. Students taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics feel this most, because that course leans on graphing technology and leaves symbolic manipulation thinner than the physics papers assume.

There is also a route-choice question worth settling early rather than in the middle of Year 13. Analysis and Approaches is the conventional partner for Higher Level physics and is the course some engineering and physical-science programmes name explicitly in their entry requirements. Applications and Interpretation is a perfectly respectable course and suits plenty of students, including many taking Standard Level physics, but a family planning on engineering should read the actual published requirements of the universities on the list rather than relying on what is assumed at the school gate. Requirements differ between institutions and between years, and they are published; checking them takes twenty minutes and prevents a subject change that cannot be undone.

sections.heading: What the drive adds to the bill, and what the Dubai market charges
paragraphs: Start with the part nobody itemises: travel. An in-home tutor crossing Dubai for a 55-minute lesson spends between forty minutes and ninety minutes in the car, and that time is inside the rate whether or not the invoice says so. Published figures bear this out. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, while qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150 to 300. The gap between those two bands is not better teaching. It is a car.

The rest of the market, read from the cheapest end upwards, looks like this. Budget online tutoring, usually university students, advertises from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. Qualified subject tutors online run AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE work from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors occupy AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270. The premium named and examiner tier reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond, where BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are other people's published prices, quoted with their names attached; they are not IB Gram's price list.

For context a DIFC family can use, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Tutoring is the part of the education budget that did move, and it is the part a family controls. One weekly specialist physics session across a Diploma year is a meaningful sum; the same money spent on a generalist in a group of six is usually wasted, because the mark-scheme precision that moves a physics grade cannot be delivered to six students at once. IB Gram's own position is simple: the trial lesson carries no charge, the rate is quoted before anything is booked, and no figure on this page is presented as ours.

Market bands: AED 150-300 qualified online, AED 180-500 in-home, AED 200-450+ specialist
Published monthly packages: AED 799 online, AED 1,599-1,799 in-home

sections.heading: Online delivery, the permit question, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India, and nobody will be sent to a DIFC address. The reason is not reluctance. It is that a tower in DIFC and a physics specialist who has taught the current course are rarely within twenty minutes of each other, and a family that insists on proximity ends up choosing from the handful of tutors who can make the drive rather than from everybody who knows the subject. Over video the shortlist is built on teaching history and on the paper the student is failing.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and the honest position is worth stating because most pages in this market avoid it. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, the application route is MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service through its app, website and e-services system, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published, so no figure is quoted here. Ask any tutor, from any provider, to show their permit.

Three further things we will not say. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB organisation, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here will imply otherwise; a KHDA educational services permit is a specific thing issued to training institutes with premises, and we do not hold one. We have no office, centre or branch in the UAE. And no tutor can guarantee a grade, a point total or a place at a university, because the papers are marked by the board and the boundaries are set after the exam. What a specialist can do is make the next twenty hours count more than the last twenty did, and the first lesson is there so a family can judge that before paying for anything.

process.title: Tell us the week, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps names the school, the year group, whether physics is Higher or Standard Level, and the two or three evening windows that are genuinely free. In this district the diary is the hard constraint, so a tutor is shortlisted against your actual Tuesdays rather than against a vague preference for weekday evenings.

process.title: A free diagnostic lesson of 55 minutes
process.description: No charge and no card details. The tutor works through recent class material and one unfamiliar past-paper question, watching the working rather than the answers. The output is a short written note saying what kind of problem this is: foundational, procedural or simply untaught content the school has not reached yet.

process.title: A plan anchored to the school's topic list
process.description: We ask for the school's own scheme of work or the term's topic list before the second session. Dubai schools teach the five themes in different orders, and a plan built on a generic syllabus sequence will repair content the class covered in September while next week's test goes unprepared.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written note each time
process.description: Every session ends with two or three named priorities and the specific past-paper questions to attempt before the next one. Parents get the note, not a score out of ten. It says what was fixed, what is still wrong and what the student is expected to do unaided in the next seven days.

process.title: Re-plan at the mock, and say so if it is not working
process.description: January and March mocks are the honest checkpoint. The marked paper gets categorised by loss type, the plan changes accordingly, and if the pattern says the tutor is a poor match for this student we say so and move them rather than letting the sessions run on. A changed tutor costs a week; a wrong one costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Matched by paper, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: The shortlist for a DIFC student is built from physics teachers who have taught the current two-paper course, with its single investigation and no Paper 3. Driving distance from the Gate Village does not appear in the criteria, because it has no bearing on whether somebody can teach wave behaviour.

whyPoints.title: Built around a DIFC evening
whyPoints.description: Slots run from 16:30 to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time on weekdays and across weekend mornings. We will tell you which start times are realistic for your school run rather than selling the one that suits us, because a session that gets cancelled three weeks running is worse than no session at all.

whyPoints.title: The investigation handled within the rules
whyPoints.description: Criteria taught, research questions interrogated, uncertainty arithmetic explained, conclusions challenged. Nothing written, edited or supplied. We say this on the page rather than in the small print, because the providers in this market who blur the line are putting the student's diploma at risk, not their own.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the company or rate table that published it, with no invented averages and no statistics without a source. If a page quotes you a market rate without saying whose rate it is, the number is decoration.

whyPoints.title: Limits disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no physics specialist is free in the window you need, we say so and offer the nearest workable alternative rather than putting a generalist in the slot. Specialist availability in a narrow subject at a narrow hour is genuinely finite, and pretending otherwise is how families end up with a tutor who is learning the course alongside the student.

whyPoints.title: One subject teacher, start to finish
whyPoints.description: The same tutor through the term wherever possible, so nobody re-diagnoses the same problem in October and February. Continuity is most of the value in a two-year course, and it is the thing a rotating pool of staff cannot provide however convenient the scheduling looks.

faqs.question: What time can a physics session realistically start if my child finishes school in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: Most Sobha Hartland secondary timetables finish between 15:00 and 15:20, and the drive back into DIFC at that hour runs ten to eighteen minutes. That makes 16:45 the first honest start and 17:00 the slot most families settle on, leaving the rest of the evening for school homework rather than putting the two in competition. Confirm your own child's finish time, because it varies by year group and by whether the day carries an enrichment block. If a 17:00 start keeps slipping, move to 17:30 permanently rather than cancelling weekly; a session that happens beats a better-timed one that does not.

faqs.question: How many evenings a week can a Diploma physics student in DIFC actually give up?
faqs.answer: One, reliably, during a normal term. Two in the six weeks before a mock, and only if one of them is short. A Diploma student is carrying six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and a service commitment, and a DIFC school run already takes an hour of the afternoon. Families who book three weekly sessions in September are usually down to one by November, having paid for the lesson in attrition. The better shape is one fixed weekly session all year plus a short intensive block in the winter break, when there is no school day to recover from and ninety-minute sessions become possible.

faqs.question: Does Diploma physics still have a Paper 3?
faqs.answer: No. The current course is assessed through two written papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade and contains a multiple-choice section and a data-based section; Paper 2 is 44% and is extended response; the investigation is 20%. Parents and students working from an older guide or from inherited revision notes often plan around a third paper that no longer exists, which wastes revision time and distorts the priorities. Check the structure against your school's own documentation at the start of Year 12, and plan the two years around Paper 2, since it carries more of the grade than anything else.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand the physics but score poorly on Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 2 marks how an answer is constructed, not whether the student knows the topic. The usual losses are a command term obeyed loosely, a definition given approximately, a quantity written without its unit, and reasoning compressed so that the marker cannot see the step the mark is attached to. 'Explain' wants a mechanism; 'determine' wants a number with a unit; 'state' wants one line. Each of those is a repeatable error that recurs on every paper until somebody names it. It is fixed by marking the student's own scripts against the published mark scheme and sorting the losses into categories, which usually takes three or four sessions to show up as a grade.

faqs.question: Why does the data-based half of Paper 1 catch out strong DIFC students?
faqs.answer: It presents data the student has never seen, in a context that may not have been taught, and asks for processing and judgement: a gradient, an intercept, an uncertainty, a conclusion that the numbers actually support. Students who have only analysed data from their own practical work find the unfamiliarity itself to be the obstacle. The remedy is volume under time: enough unfamiliar data sets that the format stops being novel and the only thing left to think about is the physics. Uncertainty arithmetic is the single most common specific loss, and it is a twenty-minute teaching job repeated until it is automatic.

faqs.question: How much maths does Higher Level physics assume before Christmas of Year 12?
faqs.answer: More than the maths course has usually delivered by then. Trigonometric resolution appears in the motion theme almost immediately, inverse-square relationships arrive with fields, logarithmic behaviour comes with the nuclear theme, and all of it needs confident rearrangement of equations under time pressure. Students who look as though they cannot do physics very often cannot rearrange an expression with three variables quickly. If your child takes Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics, expect this gap to be wider, because that course leans on graphing technology and leaves symbolic manipulation thinner than the physics papers assume.

faqs.question: Which physics theme should a struggling DIFC student fix first?
faqs.answer: Space, time and motion, whatever the school happens to be teaching this term. It carries the vector work, the graph reading and the energy accounting that every later theme reuses, so a gap there reappears disguised as a fields problem and then as a waves problem. Fields come second, because electric and gravitational field thinking is the same mathematics applied twice and learning it once is cheap. Wave behaviour third, where losses are usually vocabulary and diagram convention. The particulate and quantum themes are the most self-contained and the safest to leave for a short block closer to the exam.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose the research question for the scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to should be declined. The research question is part of what criterion A assesses, and the student has to own it. What a tutor can legitimately do is interrogate a question the student has proposed: ask whether the data it generates could distinguish between outcomes, whether the variables can be controlled in a school laboratory, and whether the scope is answerable in the time available. That conversation is where most of the investigation marks are decided, and it has to happen before any apparatus is booked. After the data exists, a badly framed question cannot be rescued.

faqs.question: What are the four criteria the scientific investigation is marked against?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each for a total of 24, contributing 20% of the physics grade. Research design covers the question, the method and the controlled variables. Data analysis covers processing, uncertainties and graph choice. Conclusion asks whether the result is supported by the data and placed in scientific context. Evaluation asks for real limitations and realistic improvements, not generic remarks about human error or insufficient time. Most students have never been shown the criteria in this form, which is why the marks cluster around the middle even when the practical work was competent.

faqs.question: Why does IB Gram teach DIFC students online instead of sending somebody to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Because the two things a family wants, a physics specialist and a short journey, are rarely available together in this district. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Insisting on proximity means choosing from the few tutors who can reach DIFC on a weekday afternoon rather than from everybody who has taught the current course. Over live video the shortlist is built on teaching history and on the specific paper the student is losing marks on, the evening loses no time to traffic, and the whiteboard, the past paper and the student's own working are all on screen together.

faqs.question: What do DIFC families pay per hour for Higher Level physics support in this market?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put qualified subject tutors working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, specialist IB and IGCSE tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500 once travel is included. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and providers including Unitors, TutorChase and BartyED publish figures across those bands, with BartyED at the top at AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other companies' prices quoted with their names attached. IB Gram quotes its own rate before anything is booked, and the first lesson carries no charge.

faqs.question: How does the physics schedule change during Ramadan in Dubai?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, which frees the afternoon, and energy levels through the middle of the day drop, which changes what a session should contain. In practice most families move to an earlier slot or to a post-Iftar one, and the content shifts towards past-paper work and consolidation rather than new theory. Because Ramadan can land close to mock season or close to the May session depending on the year, this is worth planning in January rather than negotiating in week one. Online delivery makes the change trivial: the slot moves, nobody re-plans a drive, and the tutor stays the same.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start physics support in the second term of Year 13?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to be different. With a term left there is no time to rebuild foundations and chase the syllabus simultaneously, so the work becomes triage: identify the two themes where the most marks are recoverable, drill Paper 2 technique hard because it carries 44% of the grade, and leave the rest alone. Students routinely move a grade this way, and just as routinely lose the chance by spending the term rereading notes. What cannot be rescued late is the scientific investigation, since its deadline sits inside Year 13 and schools do not extend it.

faqs.question: Where should I check the exact date of my child's physics exam?
faqs.answer: With the school's IB coordinator and on the IB organisation's own website, not from a tutoring page. UAE schools sit the May session, and the school publishes its own examination timetable with room allocations and start times. No specific IB session or results date is published on this page, because the IB organisation's site blocks automated checking and a date a parent acts on must come from the authority that sets it. For Cambridge or Pearson qualifications taken alongside, use the official board timetable for the correct administrative zone, since using the wrong zone's version is a known cause of missed exams.

faqs.question: What happens if no physics specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we say what the alternatives are. Specialist availability in one subject at one hour in Gulf Standard Time is finite, and the honest options are a different time with the right tutor, the right time with a tutor whose specialism is adjacent, or a short wait. We will not quietly put a generalist into a Higher Level physics slot, because a tutor learning the course alongside the student produces the worst outcome of the three and the family only discovers it in February. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit; this one is written down so you can hold us to it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.closingHeading: Start with the evening you actually have
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-difc.closingBody: Send three things: the school, whether physics is Higher or Standard Level, and the two evening windows that are genuinely free after the drive back into DIFC. We will shortlist physics teachers who have taught the current two-paper course and who can take one of those windows, and the first 55-minute lesson is at no charge with no card details taken. The tutor will work through recent class material and one unfamiliar past-paper question, then write a short note saying whether this is a foundational gap, a Paper 2 technique problem or content the school has not reached. If the answer is that your child does not need tutoring, the note will say that too.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-discovery-gard.tutorsIntro: These are the physics tutors a Discovery Gardens family is matched with. The useful test is to ask how they would mark an extended response, and whether they teach uncertainty propagation as a set of rules or as a topic.

intro.heading: Physics marks are lost in the shape of the answer
paragraphs: The physics student who understands the subject and scores below their understanding is the most common case in Diploma tutoring, and the diagnosis is almost always the same three things. Extended responses that describe what happens without naming the principle that causes it. Uncertainty left untreated because nobody taught it as a set of rules. And gradients read from two plotted points rather than from a line of best fit, which is a single habit costing marks in every data question.

None of those is a content gap, and none is fixed by covering more syllabus. That matters because the default response to a disappointing physics grade is to revise the themes again, which produces a student who knows more physics and scores the same. A tutor working from a marked paper rather than from the student's sense of which topics feel hard will see this in the first session.

This page is written at the level of the answer rather than the level of the syllabus. It sets out the anatomy of a Paper 2 extended response, the uncertainty rules as rules with examples, how to linearise a relationship so a gradient means something, why the multiple-choice section is a separate skill, and what the investigation's analysis and evaluation criteria actually reward.

Discovery Gardens affects the logistics. It is a high-density apartment community of 291 buildings in themed districts beside Ibn Battuta, with its own Route 2020 metro station. Diploma students travel out for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30 and physics sessions run at 18:00 or later. Study space is typically a desk in a shared room rather than a study, which is a constraint worth planning for rather than apologising about.

That setup works for physics provided the session is built around shared written working and shared annotation, which is how we run them. IB Gram delivers one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and no tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. What the arrangement needs at your end is a desk, headphones, paper for sketching and the marked work to hand.

On dates: UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session, and we publish no specific IB exam or results dates anywhere, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date a parent might act on is worse than none. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the internal calendar, including the investigation deadline, which is the document worth asking for in September. The investigation deadline in particular arrives earlier than most families expect, and twenty per cent of the grade depends on data collected well before it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-discovery-gard.subjectsIntro: Physics shares demands with several other subjects and families here often need more than one covered. These are the components and neighbours we are asked about most.

subjects.name: Physics HL
subjects.description: The five themes at greater depth, with the added demand being sustained quantitative reasoning and longer explanations rather than extra topics. Paper 2 extended responses reward an answer built from a named principle, and students who describe what happens score consistently below their understanding.

subjects.name: Physics SL
subjects.description: The same themes with reduced depth, the same Scientific Investigation at twenty per cent, and identical data and uncertainty demands. Families under-buy here on the assumption that Standard Level is light, and most Standard Level marks are lost in the data section and the investigation.

subjects.name: Paper 2 extended response
subjects.description: Carries the larger share of the written marks and is where command terms decide outcomes. Explain, describe, outline, discuss and compare each require a different structure, and a well-informed answer to the wrong command earns little regardless of its accuracy.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data-based questions
subjects.description: A written practical examination: instrument reading, data processing, plotting, gradient and intercept interpretation, and uncertainty handling. Students revise themes and leave this to chance, which makes it the most recoverable set of marks available in the subject.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: multiple choice
subjects.description: Rewards recognition and speed and punishes a student who works every question algebraically. The skill is elimination and estimation under timing, which is practised by doing timed sets rather than by learning more content.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error analysis
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation rules through addition, multiplication and powers, significant figures justified by the uncertainty, and uncertainty bars used to judge whether a relationship is supported. Rule-based and quickly taught.

subjects.name: Graph and gradient work
subjects.description: Linearising a relationship so a gradient has meaning, choosing axes accordingly, reading a gradient from a line of best fit, and interpreting an intercept physically. Taught properly in two sessions and worth marks in every component including the investigation.

subjects.name: The Scientific Investigation
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade on four criteria. Analysis and evaluation carry the marks most often left on the table: processed data with propagated uncertainty, and a critical assessment of the method rather than a list of apologies about equipment.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, indices, standard form, logarithms, small-angle approximations and trigonometry. Where a student explains the physics well and stalls on the algebra, the right purchase is mathematics support rather than more physics teaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry alongside Physics
subjects.description: Shares the investigation structure and the same uncertainty and graphing demands, so families often arrange both. Where one tutor genuinely covers both to the level needed that is efficient, and where they do not, two specialists outperform one generalist.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research. Physics essays fail on feasibility rather than ambition: a question needing equipment the student cannot access becomes a literature review. One early session on the question prevents that.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the natural sciences
subjects.description: Students taking Higher Level Physics are frequently asked to write about scientific knowledge, and generic claims about the scientific method score poorly. A physics tutor's useful contribution is supplying real examples from the course that can carry an argument.

sections.heading: The anatomy of a Paper 2 extended response
paragraphs: Ask a physics student why they lost marks on an extended response and they will usually say they did not know enough. Read the answer and the physics is frequently all present, arranged in a way the mark scheme cannot credit. Extended responses are marked for a sequence: the principle that applies, the mechanism by which it produces the effect, and the consequence in the terms the question asked about. Students write the consequence and assume the rest.

That is why command terms matter so much here. Describe asks for an account without reasons, and a student who adds reasons spends time for no additional credit. Explain asks for the reasons, and an answer describing the effect has not explained anything. Discuss asks for a balanced treatment. Compare asks for similarities and differences together rather than two separate descriptions. The physics can be identical in each and the mark very different.

The teachable version is a structure rather than a style. Name the principle or law. State the relationship, in symbols if useful. Say what changes and in which direction. Then answer the question that was asked, in its own terms. A student who writes in that order produces answers that mark schemes credit, and the order becomes automatic after perhaps six marked attempts.

This is slow work for a tutor, which is worth knowing as a buyer. Writing answers, marking them strictly and rewriting one is less comfortable for everyone than talking through a topic, and it is the thing that moves a physics grade. If a prospective tutor describes their sessions entirely in terms of covering content, they are describing something other than this.

table.caption: WHAT AN EXTENDED RESPONSE HAS TO CONTAIN
rows: Names the law or relationship that applies
No credit for an unnamed principle
States how the quantities depend on each other
Says how one change produces another
The reasoning step is the marked step
Direction without a reason earns nothing
Responds in the question's own terms
The question was not actually answered
The same shape for every term

sections.heading: Uncertainty as a set of rules, not a topic
paragraphs: Uncertainty is treated in most classrooms as a short unit near the start of the course and then assumed. In the examinations and in the investigation it is permanent. It appears in the data-based section of Paper 1, in Paper 2 questions about experimental results, and it carries a substantial share of the investigation's analysis and evaluation marks. No individual theme has that reach.

The reason students struggle is that it is usually taught as a concept when it behaves as a set of rules. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty are definitions. Propagation has rules: add absolute uncertainties when quantities are added or subtracted, add fractional or percentage uncertainties when they are multiplied or divided, and multiply the fractional uncertainty by the power when a quantity is raised to a power. Those are learnable in one session with examples.

Significant figures follow from the uncertainty rather than from habit. A result cannot honestly carry more precision than its uncertainty allows, and students who round to three figures because three looks right are guessing. Stating the uncertainty and then matching the precision to it is a two-step habit that examiners reward and that costs nothing once established.

The final piece is uncertainty bars on graphs, used to judge whether a proposed relationship is actually supported by the data. A line that passes within the bars supports the relationship; one that does not, does not, however appealing the hypothesis. That reasoning is exactly what the investigation's conclusion and evaluation criteria ask for, which is why four sessions on uncertainty reach both the papers and twenty per cent of the grade.

sections.heading: Graph work: making a gradient mean something
paragraphs: A physics graph exists to turn a relationship into a straight line whose gradient is a physical quantity. Students who learn graph plotting as a presentation exercise miss that entirely, and then cannot explain what their gradient represents. The first question to ask of any plot is what the gradient will be, in physical terms, and whether the axes chosen make it that thing.

Linearising is the technique and it is routinely under-taught. Where a relationship is not linear in the measured quantities, plotting a function of one against the other produces a straight line whose gradient carries the constant of interest. Choosing what to plot is therefore a physics decision rather than a drawing decision, and a student who can make it has an approach to every unfamiliar data question.

Then there is the single most common graph error across every science: reading a gradient from two plotted data points rather than from the line of best fit. The line exists precisely because individual points carry uncertainty, and using two of them discards the averaging the line provides. One session establishes the habit of taking widely spaced points on the line, and it earns marks in physics, chemistry and biology alike.

Intercepts deserve the same treatment. An intercept is a physical quantity, not a leftover number, and questions frequently ask what it represents. Students who have only ever been asked to plot neatly have no answer. Asking what both the gradient and the intercept mean, every time a graph is drawn, is a free habit that converts plotting practice into physics understanding.

sections.heading: The themes as recurring ideas rather than units
paragraphs: The current syllabus is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level deepens the same themes rather than adding separate content. A tutor should be able to name all five without checking, and one working from an older guide will instead describe additional higher-level topics, which is the wrong shape for this course.

The more useful observation is that the examination does not respect theme boundaries. Energy appears in all five. Field concepts recur. Proportionality and graphical relationships run throughout. A question will use wave behaviour inside a fields context or thermal reasoning inside a nuclear one, and a student who revised each theme as a sealed unit recognises every piece of content and cannot assemble the answer.

So the revision that works is organised around the recurring ideas, with whole composite questions used as the practice. Energy transfer and conservation, proportional reasoning, graphical interpretation, and uncertainty treatment are the four threads worth drilling across themes. Each one appears in every paper and none belongs to a single unit, which is why a theme-by-theme plan systematically underprepares.

There is an exception and it should be said. Where a marked paper shows a genuine content gap in a specific theme, teach that theme. The argument here is against theme-by-theme revision as the default response to a disappointing grade, not against content teaching where the evidence calls for it. The distinction matters because the default costs a term and is almost never questioned.

sections.heading: The multiple-choice section is its own skill
paragraphs: Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, and the multiple-choice part is where strong students most often lose marks they cannot explain. The reason is strategic rather than academic: a student who works every question through algebraically runs out of time, and a student who rushes misreads. Neither problem is addressed by knowing more physics.

The skills that help are elimination, estimation and recognition. Many questions can be narrowed to two options by dimensional reasoning or by a limiting case, without any full calculation. Others are faster to check by substituting a convenient value than by rearranging. A student who practises timed sets with explicit attention to these techniques improves measurably in a handful of sessions.

Careless losses are the other half. On multiple choice a misread sign, a missed prefix or an answer transferred to the wrong line costs as much as not knowing the physics. Those errors reduce when a student has a fixed procedure: read the question twice, note what is asked, eliminate, then answer. Dull as it sounds, it is the difference between two scores on identical knowledge.

The practical consequence for a Discovery Gardens family is that multiple-choice preparation should be timed and separate. Mixing it into general revision does not develop the pacing, because pacing only exists under time pressure. Two or three sessions of timed sets, discussed afterwards in terms of why each question was slow rather than why it was wrong, usually does the job.

sections.heading: Analysis and evaluation in the Scientific Investigation
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is twenty per cent of the Physics grade, reported in up to three thousand words, assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Design is where feasibility is decided, and the two criteria where students most often leave marks unclaimed are analysis and evaluation, both of which depend entirely on the uncertainty and graph work described earlier on this page.

Analysis asks for raw data processed properly, uncertainty propagated through the processing, and a graph that answers the research question with a gradient or relationship extracted from it. What students submit is frequently a neat table of raw readings, a plot without uncertainty bars, and a stated result with no indication of its precision. The physics may be sound and the criterion is about treatment.

Evaluation is the one students misread most completely. It is read as a confession, so it becomes a list of complaints about imprecise equipment. What it asks for is a critical assessment: which limitations materially affected the result, in which direction, and what specific improvement would address each. A limitation named without its effect is not an evaluation, and that reframing is worth several marks for one session's work.

Conclusion sits between them and has its own trap: restating the results rather than answering the research question and comparing the finding with accepted physics. A conclusion should say what the answer is, how confident the data allows one to be, and how it compares with the published value or expected relationship. All three are explicit expectations and all three are frequently absent.

sections.heading: What a physics session needs in a Discovery Gardens flat
paragraphs: Physics is slightly more demanding than mathematics to run well online, because a session involves diagrams, graphs and written explanations rather than working alone. It is still entirely workable, and the requirements are modest: a desk, over-ear headphones with a microphone, paper for sketching, and the marked work to hand. Being able to photograph or share a hand-drawn diagram quickly matters more than any specialised software.

In a community of mostly one and two bedroom apartments, the harder constraint is interruption rather than equipment. A physics explanation takes a sustained few minutes, and a session broken every ten minutes does not recover its thread any better than a Paper 3 question does. The answer is a household agreement reached once, treating the hour as a timetabled lesson rather than homework.

This is also where hosting a visiting tutor becomes impractical for reasons unrelated to cost. Inviting an adult into a shared living space for an hour in the evening, with family present and nowhere else to be, is a real imposition in a flat. Families here raise that more often than price when explaining why they stopped looking for someone to come to the home.

IB Gram visits no UAE addresses, so the question does not arise: every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30, and home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The practical benefit in a physics context is that a session missed to a late bus or a fixture can move to the next evening rather than the next week, which matters in a subject where topics build on each other.

sections.heading: Availability, honesty and what we will not do
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics is one of the scarcer specialisms in this corridor, and that is worth stating rather than implying a bottomless roster. Physics at both levels is reasonably well covered across the UAE set and usually matched within a few days, with availability tightening in January and February when every Diploma 2 family in Dubai is after the same evening slots. Where we cannot cover a request, we say so rather than offering a Standard Level tutor for Higher Level work.

That substitution is the specific thing to guard against in this subject, because the gap shows up in exactly the places this page has described: marking extended responses against command terms, and teaching uncertainty propagation as rules. A tutor comfortable to Standard Level will teach the content adequately and the assessment poorly, and a family usually notices in week six rather than week one.

On the investigation the boundary is fixed and stated at the first session. A tutor may read the four criteria with the student, question the research question and the measurement plan, teach the uncertainty and graphical techniques the data requires, show how published work structures an analysis, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write the report, process the data, supply the analysis or outline it for completion.

On materials and claims: we do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, and we cite and link official sources instead. We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. We do not guarantee grades, and we do not describe tutors as IB examiners without evidence of current status, since examiner status confers no access to marking or paper content.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose physics marks on answers that contain the right physics?
faqs.answer: Because extended responses are marked for a sequence and students write only the end of it. The marked structure is the principle that applies, the relationship between the quantities, the mechanism by which one change produces another, the direction of that change with its reason, and then the answer in the question's own terms. Most students assert the outcome and assume the rest is understood. Six marked and rewritten answers usually fixes it, and the gain applies to every paper afterwards.

faqs.question: How should uncertainty propagation be taught?
faqs.answer: As rules with worked examples, not as a concept. Add absolute uncertainties when quantities are added or subtracted. Add fractional or percentage uncertainties when they are multiplied or divided. Multiply the fractional uncertainty by the power when a quantity is raised to a power. Then match the significant figures of a result to what the uncertainty allows rather than rounding to three by habit. That is one session of teaching, and it reaches Paper 1B, Paper 2 and the investigation.

faqs.question: What is the single most common graph mistake in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Reading a gradient from two plotted data points instead of from the line of best fit. The line exists precisely because individual points carry uncertainty, so using two of them discards the averaging it provides. One session establishes the habit of taking widely spaced points on the line, and it earns marks in physics, chemistry and biology alike. The related habit worth building is asking what both the gradient and the intercept represent physically, every time a graph is drawn.

faqs.question: What does linearising a relationship actually mean?
faqs.answer: Plotting a function of one measured quantity against another so that the result is a straight line whose gradient carries the physical constant you want. Where a relationship is not linear in the raw quantities, choosing what to plot is a physics decision rather than a drawing decision. A student who can make that decision has an approach to every unfamiliar data question, which is why it is worth a session even though it appears in no single theme.

faqs.question: Why do strong students lose marks on the multiple-choice section?
faqs.answer: For strategic reasons rather than academic ones. A student who works every question through algebraically runs out of time, and one who rushes misreads signs and prefixes. The techniques that help are elimination, estimation, limiting cases and dimensional reasoning, which narrow many questions to two options without a full calculation. These only develop under timing, so preparation has to be timed sets discussed afterwards in terms of why a question was slow rather than only why it was wrong.

faqs.question: What does the investigation's Evaluation criterion want?
faqs.answer: A critical assessment, not a confession. It asks which limitations materially affected the result, in which direction, and what specific improvement would address each one. What students write instead is a list of complaints about imprecise equipment, which identifies problems without analysing their effect or proposing a real fix. A limitation named without its consequence is not an evaluation. Reframing it from apology to critique is worth several marks and takes about one session to explain.

faqs.question: What should the Conclusion section of a physics investigation contain?
faqs.answer: Three things: what the answer to the research question is, how confident the data allows one to be, and how the finding compares with accepted physics or a published value. Students commonly restate their results instead, which is a different task and scores poorly. The confidence element depends directly on the uncertainty work, which is why uncertainty is not a separate topic but the backbone of both the analysis and conclusion criteria.

faqs.question: How is IB Physics organised, and why does that matter when hiring?
faqs.answer: Into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level deepening the same themes rather than adding separate ones. It matters because a tutor working from an older guide will describe additional higher-level topics, which is the wrong shape for this course and makes their revision planning unreliable. Ask them to name the five themes and say what Higher Level adds.

faqs.question: Why does theme-by-theme revision underprepare a student?
faqs.answer: Because examination questions deliberately cross theme boundaries. A question will use wave behaviour inside a fields context or thermal reasoning inside a nuclear one, and a student who revised each theme as a sealed unit recognises all the content and cannot assemble the answer. Better to drill the four recurring threads, energy transfer and conservation, proportional reasoning, graphical interpretation and uncertainty treatment, then practise whole composite questions and mark them.

faqs.question: Is my child's difficulty physics or mathematics?
faqs.answer: One session with a marked paper will tell you. If they explain what is happening physically and then stall on rearranging the relationship, the problem is mathematical: indices, standard form, logarithms, small-angle work and algebra under time pressure are routine demands in this course. If the algebra is fluent and the explanations are vague, the problem is structural, in the shape of the answer. Treating a mathematical difficulty with more physics teaching is common and expensive.

faqs.question: Can physics really be taught well over video from an apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a modest setup: a desk, over-ear headphones with a microphone, paper for sketching, and the marked work to hand. Being able to share a hand-drawn diagram quickly matters more than any specialised software. The harder constraint in a flat is interruption, because a physics explanation needs a sustained few minutes, and the answer to that is a household agreement that the hour is a timetabled lesson rather than homework.

faqs.question: What time do physics sessions run for Diploma students here?
faqs.answer: Usually 18:00, and 19:00 on a day with a fixture or a Creativity, Activity, Service commitment. Students in this community travel out for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, and are home from about 16:30. Middle Years students are often home by 16:00, so 16:30 works for them. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, and a missed one moves to the next evening rather than the next week, which matters in a subject that builds.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level physics worth paying to support?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and families routinely under-buy on the assumption that it is light. The Scientific Investigation is the same twenty per cent at Standard Level with the same four criteria and the same three thousand word limit, and the data-based section of Paper 1 makes identical demands. Most Standard Level marks are lost in exactly those two places rather than in advanced content, so the support that helps is the same support described throughout this page.

faqs.question: Would a Standard Level tutor cope with Higher Level physics?
faqs.answer: They will teach the content adequately and the assessment poorly, and the gap shows up within about two sessions. Specifically it appears in marking extended responses against command terms and in teaching uncertainty propagation as rules, both of which require having done them to this assessment before. Higher Level Physics is one of the scarcer specialisms in this corridor, so this substitution is common. Ask directly whether a tutor has taught and marked at Higher Level.

faqs.question: Can a tutor process my child's investigation data if the method was sound?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the processing and uncertainty techniques the data requires, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the processing answers the research question, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not process the data, supply the analysis, write or rewrite the report, or outline it for completion. That is stated at the first session of any investigation block, and feedback is given in writing so the school can see its nature.

faqs.question: On a small budget, which physics skill has the widest reach across the papers?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty rules and graph work, in that order. Those skills are examined in the data-based section, reappear in Paper 2 questions about experimental results, and carry a substantial share of the investigation's analysis and evaluation marks, so their reach is wider than any single theme. They are also rule-based rather than conceptual, which means four sessions is genuinely enough to establish them, and the gain applies for the remainder of the course.

intro.heading: Why a Downtown Dubai physics problem is usually a timetable problem
paragraphs: Downtown Dubai has the Burj Khalifa, the Opera District and the Boulevard. What it does not have is a private school inside its own boundary. Every child who lives in a tower on Mohammed bin Rashid Boulevard or in the Old Town low-rises is bussed out of the district each morning: north to Al Satwa and Al Safa, east to Oud Metha and Al Jaddaf, south to Sobha Hartland, Nad Al Sheba and Meydan. That single fact shapes everything about physics tuition here, and almost no tutoring page mentions it.

The practical effect is a long day. A Year 12 student at a school in Nad Al Sheba or Sobha Hartland leaves a Downtown lobby somewhere between 6.40am and 7.10am, finishes lessons at about 3.15pm, and reaches home between 4.15pm and 5.00pm depending on whether the bus takes Al Khail Road or Financial Centre Road. Add a co-curricular commitment on two afternoons and the realistic window for a focused physics lesson is 5.30pm to 8.30pm on weekdays, plus Saturday mornings. A tutor who needs 40 minutes to drive in and 40 minutes to drive out has already eaten a third of that window.

Physics is also the subject where lost time shows up fastest. The 2023 IB Physics guide puts 36% of the final grade on Paper 1, 44% on Paper 2 and 20% on a single Scientific Investigation. Paper 1 splits into 1A, a multiple-choice section, and 1B, a data-analysis section that students meet properly for the first time in the exam hall if nobody has drilled it. A student can understand Newton's laws perfectly and still lose eight marks on a gradient, an uncertainty and a log plot. Those are teachable in two sessions. They are not teachable in a car.

Online delivery solves the geometry rather than compromising on it. Your child opens a laptop at 5.45pm in a Downtown apartment and works with a tutor who teaches Physics HL for a living, shares a whiteboard, annotates a past-paper scan live, and can pull up the exact mark scheme wording for a six-mark explain question. The pool is no longer whoever happens to live within a 20-minute drive of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Boulevard; it is whoever is genuinely good at Fields and Nuclear and quantum physics. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE, and we say so plainly rather than letting a parent find out at booking.

This page is written around the school run because that is the question Downtown parents actually ask first. Below you will find which schools this district feeds, what time each day ends, when a session realistically fits, how IB Physics is examined now, where Downtown students lose marks, what the Dubai market charges per hour, and what a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment. Read the tables; they carry more than the prose.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics in the DP is a two-year course assessed by two written papers and one Scientific Investigation. The 2023 guide organises content into five themes: Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; and Nuclear and quantum physics. HL students take the same themes to greater depth and sit longer papers. Paper 1 is 36% of the grade, Paper 2 is 44%, and the investigation is 20%.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is graded against four criteria rather than a percentage: Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, and Reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is marked out of 8. A student who has never written a hypothesis with a justified independent variable will meet that demand again in DP Physics, where Research design is one of the four IA criteria worth six marks.

The transition still bites: MYP marking rewards process and reflection, while DP Paper 2 rewards precise physics in command-term form.

programmes.name: IGCSE to DP Physics bridge
programmes.description: Most Downtown children attend British-curriculum schools and sit Cambridge 0625 Physics or 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences before choosing a post-16 route. IGCSE Physics is strong on recall and structured calculation. DP Physics asks for proportional reasoning, graphical analysis and extended explanation. The bridge work is uncertainty arithmetic, vectors handled properly, and writing four lines of physics instead of one.

Both are accepted by UAE universities; the honest answer depends on how many subjects your child wants to carry, not on which is harder.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A handful of Dubai schools offer the IB Career-related Programme, in which students take two or more DP courses alongside a career-related study. Where Physics is one of those DP courses, the subject content and assessment are identical to the full Diploma, so the tutoring is the same. What changes is the surrounding workload and the reflective project timeline.
programmes.countryNote: CP students in Dubai are far rarer than DP students, and that scarcity is exactly where a local tutor search fails. An online match ignores the problem: a tutor who knows DP Physics assessment can teach a CP Physics student without ever having met the CP framework before.

subjects.description: Chosen alongside Physics by students targeting medicine or biomedical engineering. The marking rewards precise terminology in a way Physics does not, and a strong physicist often writes biology answers that are correct but unrewarded.

subjects.description: A common third science for Physics students in the central corridor. The HL course adds abstract data structures and resource management. The solution to the internal assessment is a developed product, which demands project discipline across a full year.

subjects.description: Overlaps with Physics on materials, forces and energy. The design cycle and the HL major project reward documented iteration, which is a different skill from the structured problem solving Paper 2 wants.

sections.heading: What a Downtown Dubai parent is actually asking
paragraphs: The search phrase is "IB physics tutor in Downtown Dubai", but the question underneath it is narrower: can someone who genuinely understands Physics HL teach my child between the time the bus drops them off and the time they need to sleep. That is a scheduling question wearing a subject-expertise costume, and the two parts pull against each other. Physics specialists are scarce in any city. Physics specialists who happen to live a short drive from the Boulevard and have a free 6pm slot are scarcer still.

Dubai's private-school market is large — 227 private schools serving 387,441 students across 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for 7% of enrolment, according to Dubai Media Office figures published in January 2025. A 7% share across a city that size is a real cohort, but it is spread thinly across campuses from Al Barsha to Academic City. The practical consequence for a Downtown family is that the nearest IB Physics HL teacher is statistically unlikely to be in the next tower.

So the honest answer to the search is that proximity is the wrong filter. The right filter is whether the tutor can read a Theme D field question and tell your child, inside thirty seconds, which of the three standard traps they just fell into. IB Gram matches on that, delivers the lesson over live video, and sets the time by your child's bus rather than by a tutor's commute. Home visits are an India-only service and are not available anywhere in the UAE.
Everything that follows is built to answer the practical version of your question. The next section maps the school run properly, with a table you can check against your own child's timetable.

sections.heading: The Downtown school run, hour by hour, and where a physics lesson fits
paragraphs: Three bus corridors leave Downtown each morning. The northern run to Al Safa, Al Satwa and Jumeirah is the shortest and returns first. The eastern run to Oud Metha and Al Garhoud crosses the creek and sits in Financial Centre Road traffic both ways. The southern run to Sobha Hartland, Meydan, Nad Al Sheba and Al Quoz uses Al Khail Road, which is fast in the morning and slow at 3.30pm. Which corridor your child is on decides, almost entirely, whether a 5.30pm lesson is realistic or whether 6.30pm is the earliest sensible start.

The table below sets out the pattern families report. Treat the times as the shape of the day rather than a published timetable — your school's bus operator will give you exact figures, and Ramadan timings shift the whole day earlier. The column that matters is the last one: the earliest hour at which a child can sit down and think about physics rather than recover from a bus.

Two further constraints are worth naming. Co-curricular activities at most Dubai schools run immediately after lessons, which means two afternoons a week commonly return home an hour later than the table shows. And DP2 students in the second half of the year are often carrying mock results, Internal Assessment deadlines in two or three subjects, and Extended Essay drafting at the same time. A fixed weekly slot survives that; an ad-hoc arrangement does not.

Online delivery is what makes the narrow window usable. A lesson that starts at 6.15pm and ends at 7.45pm does not need a tutor to have left their own home at 5.30pm, and it does not collapse because Sheikh Zayed Road closed a lane. If your child is unusually tired on a Tuesday, the slot can move to Thursday without anyone writing off a journey.

sections.heading: How IB Physics is examined under the 2023 guide
paragraphs: The structure changed with the 2023 subject guide and a surprising number of parents are still working from the old one. Physics is now assessed by two written papers and one Scientific Investigation, with no separate options paper. Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and is split into Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, a data-analysis section built on a short experimental context. Paper 2 carries 44% and runs from short structured questions into extended response. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20%.

Content is organised into five themes rather than a topic list: Space, time and motion; The particulate nature of matter; Wave behaviour; Fields; and Nuclear and quantum physics. HL and SL share the themes. HL goes deeper inside each and sits longer papers, which in practice means more multi-step problems and more questions where the physics has to be selected before it can be applied.

The split matters for how you buy tuition. A student who is weak on content needs theme-by-theme teaching, which is slow and takes most of a year. A student who knows the physics but underperforms needs Paper 1B and command-term work, which is fast and takes a handful of sessions. Parents in Downtown frequently buy the first when they needed the second, and the diagnostic question is simple: compare your child's Paper 1 and Paper 2 percentages from the last mock. If Paper 1 is well below Paper 2, the problem is probably technique.

sections.heading: Where Downtown physics students lose marks, specifically
paragraphs: The pattern is consistent enough to name. The first loss is vector resolution in Theme A. A student who can state that forces are vectors will still add two perpendicular forces arithmetically under time pressure, or resolve along the wrong axis on an inclined plane. It costs two or three marks per paper and it is fixable in one session followed by twenty minutes of practice a week for a month.

The second loss is graphical work in Paper 1B. The section gives a short experimental context and asks for a gradient, an intercept interpreted physically, an uncertainty, and sometimes a linearisation. Students who have only ever drawn graphs in a lab write-up, where neatness was the implicit criterion, do not realise the exam wants a value with a unit and a justification. The marks are mechanical once the method is drilled, which is why a technique intensive moves this number faster than any amount of extra content teaching.

The third loss is in Theme D. Field questions ask students to explain, and explain in IB command-term terms means giving reasons or causes, not restating the situation. A student writes "the field is stronger closer to the mass" and stops, when the mark scheme wanted the inverse-square relationship named and applied. The fix is a response template per command term, practised against real mark schemes until the shape is automatic.

The fourth, and the one that costs the most, is the Internal Assessment. Twenty per cent of the grade rides on a single investigation, and the commonest failure is a research question chosen because the apparatus was available rather than because the relationship is analysable. That is covered in its own section below, because the fix has to happen before data collection starts, not after.
bullets: Vector resolution under time pressure, especially on inclined planes

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation: four criteria, 24 marks, and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is the single largest block of marks a Physics student controls directly. It is assessed against four criteria — Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation — each worth six marks, for a total of 24 scaled to 20% of the final grade. The report has a 3,000-word limit. Students who have read the criteria usually write better reports than students who have only read an exemplar, because the criteria tell you exactly what the examiner is looking for.

The most common structural mistake is treating the investigation as a school practical with a longer write-up. Research design rewards a clearly stated and focused research question with justified methodology, including a sensible range of values for the independent variable. If the independent variable only takes three values, Data analysis has nothing to work with and Conclusion has nothing to compare against theory. That single decision, made in week one, caps the mark before any data exists.

What a tutor may legitimately do is narrow and sharpen. They can ask whether the relationship your child is testing is one the data will actually reveal. They can point out that a measurement will be swamped by an uncertainty they have not thought about. They can read a draft and say which criterion it is currently failing. They can teach uncertainty propagation properly. What a tutor may never do is write, redraft to completion, produce the analysis, or supply the data. IB academic honesty rules make authorship the student's responsibility and a breach is a malpractice matter for the student, not an inconvenience for the tutor.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs in the Dubai market, and what proximity adds to the bill
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number that decides whether tuition continues past February. A single 60-minute session a week for a school month is four hours. At the qualified-subject-tutor rates published by Unitors — IGCSE from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200 an hour — that is roughly AED 600 to AED 800 a month. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Physics HL candidate in DP2 sits in that top band, and a parent budgeting from an advertised hourly rate is usually surprised by the total.

The in-home premium is where the Downtown geography becomes a money question. Bestimate records in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, against online specialist rates that overlap at the bottom and stop lower at the top. Monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The arithmetic is not subtle: the in-home package costs roughly twice as much per contact hour, and the difference is paying for a car on Al Khail Road, not for better physics.

At the cheaper end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Those figures buy a university student or a generalist, which is a reasonable purchase for Year 9 homework support and a poor one for Theme D at Higher Level. At the premium end, TutorChase quotes AED 270 an hour and BartyED AED 650, the latter for named or examiner-linked tutors. These are the market's published numbers, each attributable to the provider that published it, and none of them is an IB Gram price. IB Gram quotes after the free trial lesson, once the subject, level and frequency are known.

What a parent can verify independently: ask any provider for the rate per 60 minutes rather than per session, ask whether travel is inside or outside that figure, and ask what happens to the fee if a session is cancelled by the tutor. The answers vary more than the headline rates do.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for a Downtown tower, compared honestly
paragraphs: There is a genuine case for in-home tuition and it is worth stating before the comparison. A tutor in the room can see a student's page, notice when they stop writing, and manage a younger child who will not stay seated. For a Year 4 pupil, that matters a great deal. For a 17-year-old working through Paper 2 past papers on a shared screen, it matters much less, and it costs considerably more.

The Downtown-specific arguments cut the other way. Tower access is slow: visitor parking in a Downtown basement is limited and often paid, security sign-in takes time, and a tutor arriving at 5.50pm for a 6pm start frequently arrives at 6.10pm. Over a 30-week year that is five hours of lesson time lost to a lift lobby. Traffic is the larger factor — a tutor coming from Al Barsha or Mirdif to Downtown at 5.30pm is budgeting 45 to 60 minutes, and that cost is inside their rate whether you see it itemised or not.

The pool argument is the decisive one. Filtering for physics specialists who also live within a 20-minute drive of the Boulevard removes almost everyone good. Filtering for physics specialists who can be online at 6.15pm Gulf Standard Time removes almost nobody. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so this is not a sales preference dressed as analysis; it is why the service is built the way it is. Home tutoring remains an India-only service for us.

sections.heading: The exam calendar for a Downtown physics student, counted backwards
paragraphs: Dubai schools running the IB Diploma sit the May session, and the practical planning problem is that the deadlines a student controls fall long before the exams they worry about. The Internal Assessment is marked internally and moderated externally, so the school's own submission date is the one that binds — typically in the first half of DP2 and set by the IB coordinator, not by the IB itself. A student who starts the investigation in the term it is due has already lost the chance to repeat a measurement.

We do not publish IB session or results dates on this page. The reason is specific rather than coy: ibo.org blocks automated verification, so every IB date we could print would be second-hand, and a date a parent plans around has to be right. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the current session timetable and the internal deadlines for Physics, and plan from that. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the position is different, because both publish timetables openly, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series.

What can be planned confidently is the work, counted backwards from the exam window. Twelve months out, the investigation research question should be settled and the data collection method tested. Nine months out, data collected and the first analysis drafted. Six months out, the report submitted to the school and full past papers started under timed conditions. Three months out, Paper 1B drilled as a discrete skill and command-term templates automatic. Six weeks out, past papers by theme rather than by paper, so weak themes get the last of the time.
