sections.heading: KHDA, the permit question, and what a Downtown parent can check
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which the UAE government describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects schools annually and publishes a rating on a six-band scale. Those reports tell you about your child's school. They tell you nothing about a private tutor, because KHDA does not inspect individual tutors, and any tutoring provider implying otherwise is describing something that does not exist.

Private tutoring itself is regulated, but through a different body. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone.

A separate and much larger requirement applies to anyone running a tutoring centre with premises and staff in Dubai: a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no such permit and operates no centre or office in the UAE, which is why you will not find an address on this page. Our tutors work online, and the ones based in the UAE are responsible for holding the MoHRE permit that applies to them.

The practical check for a parent is short. Ask whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit. Ask what their actual physics qualification is and which level they have taught to. Ask for the first lesson free so you can judge the teaching rather than the pitch. And treat any claim of regulatory approval as a reason to ask one more question.

sections.heading: What happens if no Physics HL specialist is free at your slot
paragraphs: This is the question no competitor in the Dubai tutoring market answers, and it deserves a straight response. Physics HL is a narrow specialism. On any given week there are more requests for a 6.30pm Sunday-to-Thursday slot than there are Physics HL tutors with that hour free, because every Downtown, Business Bay and DIFC family is asking for the same window for the same reason. Sometimes the honest answer to a request is not yet.

When that happens, we say so rather than substituting a generalist and hoping. The options we offer are a different hour in the same week, a different day, a tutor who covers Physics SL confidently and the HL extension less so with that limitation stated openly, or a wait with a named date. A Physics HL student put with a maths graduate who last read Theme E at university loses a term before anyone notices, and that is a worse outcome than waiting nine days.

The second honesty point concerns where tutors are. Some of our physics specialists are UAE residents; others teach from India, where our in-home service operates, and work with UAE students over video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not hide non-UAE delivery behind a local number, and we do not claim a Dubai office. What we commit to is the subject match and the timezone, both of which are what actually affect the lesson.

The free trial exists to make this checkable rather than promised. One lesson, no fee, and you decide whether this person can teach your child physics. If they cannot, you have lost an hour of an evening, not a term.

faqs.question: Which schools do Downtown Dubai families send their children to for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: No private school sits inside Downtown Dubai itself, so every family commutes out. The IB Diploma campuses Downtown parents most often name are in Sobha Hartland, Meydan, Nad Al Sheba, Al Jaddaf, Al Safa and Al Garhoud, with Hartland International School, North London Collegiate School Dubai, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy, Jumeirah Baccalaureate School and Deira International School recurring most. Which one your child attends matters for tuition because it sets the bus corridor and therefore the earliest hour a lesson can realistically start. Schools are named here as local context only; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them.

faqs.question: What time can an IB Physics lesson realistically start if my child is bussed from Downtown?
faqs.answer: It depends on the corridor. Children bussed north to Al Safa, Al Satwa or Jumeirah are usually home between 3.45pm and 4.15pm, which makes a 5.30pm start workable. Those bussed south to Nad Al Sheba or Al Quoz often reach home closer to 5pm, so 6.15pm is more honest. Add an hour on co-curricular days. Because lessons run online, the slot does not need padding for a tutor's drive, which is what makes the narrow window usable at all. Pick a time your child can think at, not the earliest one that technically fits.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Physics grade comes from the Scientific Investigation?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Higher and Standard Level under the 2023 subject guide. It is marked against four criteria — Research design, Data analysis, Conclusion and Evaluation — each worth six marks, giving 24 marks in total, and the report has a 3,000-word limit. The remaining 80% is split between Paper 1 at 36% and Paper 2 at 44%. That makes the investigation the largest single block of marks a student controls directly, and the reason the research question deserves more attention in week one than it usually gets.

faqs.question: Is Paper 1B really worth separate practice for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the fastest available gain for most students. Paper 1B gives a short experimental context and asks for gradients, intercepts interpreted physically, uncertainties and sometimes a linearisation. Students who have only drawn graphs for lab write-ups treat it as a presentation exercise rather than a calculation, and lose marks that are mechanical once the method is drilled. Four to six focused sessions on past-paper 1B questions typically moves the score more than the same hours spent on new content. Compare your child's Paper 1 and Paper 2 percentages to see whether this applies.

faqs.question: Can a physics tutor help with my child's Internal Assessment without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may help narrow the research question until it is measurable, point out that an uncertainty will swamp the effect being measured, teach uncertainty propagation, suggest which graph the data needs, and read a draft and say which criterion it is currently failing. A tutor may not write any part of the report, redraft it to completion, produce the analysis or supply data. Under IB academic honesty rules the work must be the student's own, and a breach is a malpractice matter for the student. We state that limit before the first session rather than after.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics tutor cost per month in Dubai rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: One 60-minute session a week is about four hours a month. Using the rates providers publish, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200 an hour, which puts a weekly session near AED 800 a month. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table estimates AED 240 to AED 600 monthly at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. A Physics HL candidate in the second year sits in that top band. These are market figures from the sources named, not IB Gram prices; we quote after the free trial.

faqs.question: Why is in-home physics tuition more expensive in Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for the journey. Bestimate records in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, while monthly packages advertised locally run around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. That is roughly double per contact hour. In Downtown there is a second cost: basement visitor parking is limited and tower security sign-in takes time, so a 6pm start often becomes 6.10pm. IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: Does my child need a lab to do well in IB Physics if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Your child's school provides the lab, and that is where the Scientific Investigation data must be collected. Online tuition does not replace practical work; it prepares your child to use the lab time well and to analyse what comes out of it. That means designing a method that will produce a usable graph, knowing which uncertainties matter before the first measurement, and handling the processing properly afterwards. The marks in Data analysis and Evaluation are won at a desk, not at a bench, which is why remote support fits this component better than parents expect.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but underperforms in exams. What actually fixes that?
faqs.answer: Usually command-term discipline and timed practice, not more content. IB mark schemes reward specific response shapes: an explain question wants reasons or causes, a describe question wants the observable account, and a student who answers the first as though it were the second loses marks while writing true physics. The fix is a template per command term, practised against published mark schemes until it is automatic, combined with full papers under exam timing. Six weeks of that moves a predictable loss into a predictable gain, and it is cheaper than a year of re-teaching.

faqs.question: Is IB Physics HL harder than A Level Physics for a Dubai student?
faqs.answer: They are hard in different directions and the honest comparison depends on your child. IB Physics HL carries five themes, a Scientific Investigation and the surrounding Diploma load of six subjects plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. A Level Physics goes deeper in a narrower space with fewer subjects alongside it. UAE universities accept both. The practical question is whether your child performs better carrying breadth or depth, and a Year 11 student who is already stretched by nine IGCSEs usually answers that question themselves.

faqs.question: Do private physics tutors in Dubai need a permit, and can I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold the permit.

faqs.question: Does KHDA approve or inspect private physics tutors in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA is described by the UAE government as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and it inspects schools annually on a six-band scale. It does not inspect individual private tutors, so no tutor can hold a KHDA rating. A separate KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff in Dubai. Any tutoring provider suggesting regulatory endorsement of its individual tutors is describing something that does not exist, and that is worth one follow-up question before you book.

faqs.question: My child is in DP2 with mocks in a few weeks. Is it too late for physics tuition?
faqs.answer: No, but what the sessions should do changes. With a short runway there is no time to re-teach five themes, so the work becomes triage: identify the two weakest themes from the mock paper, drill Paper 1B as a discrete skill, and fix command-term responses so the physics your child already knows earns full marks. That sequence is deliberately narrow because narrow is what works in six weeks. Bring the marked mock to the free trial lesson and the tutor can tell you within the hour which two themes to spend the time on.

faqs.question: What happens if no Physics HL tutor is available at the time we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with options and a date, rather than matched to a generalist. Demand in Dubai concentrates on the same weekday evening window because every family in Downtown, Business Bay and DIFC is working around the same bus timings. When the hour is full, the choices are a different hour, a different day, a Physics SL-confident tutor with the HL limitation stated openly, or a short wait. Some of our physics tutors are UAE residents and others teach from India over video in Gulf Standard Time; we do not conceal that behind a local number.

faqs.question: Should we use the same tutor for Physics HL and Maths AA, or two separate specialists?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. The overlap is real: calculus and trigonometric identities in AA carry directly into kinematics and wave behaviour, so a tutor strong in both can use one subject to repair the other. The limit is Higher Level in both at once, where the depth required in each usually means two specialists serve the student better than one generalist. We will say which situation you are in rather than selling a convenient bundle, and the trial lesson is the cheapest way to test it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-academic.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Physics at Higher and Standard Level and the MYP sciences that lead into it, including scientific investigation coaching on the student's own data and the mathematics physics assumes but does not teach.

intro.heading: Why physics marks and physics understanding come apart
paragraphs: The characteristic physics problem is not ignorance. It is a student who can recount what happens in a circuit, or why a satellite stays in orbit, and whose written answer scores two marks out of five. Physics mark schemes reward a specific kind of sentence: one that names the quantity that changed, states the relationship, and reaches the consequence. An answer that describes the phenomenon in everyday language has not answered the question, however correct it is.

The second recurring loss is uncertainty. Every physics course requires students to handle measurement uncertainty, propagate it through a calculation, and reflect on it in the scientific investigation, and almost no student has been taught this systematically. It appears in data-analysis questions and it is where investigation marks quietly disappear. It is also entirely teachable, in a handful of sessions, because the rules are mechanical.

The third is graphs. Physics asks students to linearise a relationship, choose what to plot against what, and extract a physical quantity from a gradient or intercept. Students who can plot accurately often cannot say what the gradient represents, which is the actual question. This is not a drawing skill and it is not covered adequately in most schemes of work.

The current IB physics syllabus is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Those themes replaced the older topic-and-options structure, so a tutor working from a guide that mentions options is working from the wrong document. Ask your child's school for the subject guide and the component weightings that apply to their cohort, because weightings are revised and the school holds the authoritative version.

One more thing a marked paper tends to reveal. Physics mark loss sorts into three buckets rather than one, and they need three different plans. Marks lost on extended-response questions mean the command terms are not being read. Marks lost on data-analysis questions mean uncertainty and graph work were never taught. Marks lost across one theme mean a content gap. Diagnosing which bucket dominates takes twenty minutes and saves weeks of the wrong work.

Geographically this cluster has a particular problem with physics specifically. Dubai International Academic City is a university free zone whose own secondary, Dubai English Speaking College, runs the British route. The nearest IB Diploma physics teaching is at GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis, with Uptown International School in Mirdif, Universal American School in Al Warqa and the Nad Al Sheba schools beyond that. Physics at Higher Level is the single hardest combination to staff locally in eastern Dubai.

IB Gram delivers this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service for us. For Higher Level physics that is not a compromise but the whole point, because the number of people within driving distance of Academic City who teach it is close to zero, and the number who can coach an investigation through uncertainty propagation is smaller still.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-academic.programmesIntro: Physics tutoring from this cluster arrives at three points, and the useful work differs sharply between them.

programmes.name: MYP sciences into Diploma physics
programmes.description: MYP sciences are graded 1-8 against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Marks go missing on criteria B and C rather than A, because students who know the content still design weak investigations and process data without evaluating it. Those are exactly the skills Diploma physics then assumes.

A student who has been assessed mainly on criterion A arrives in the first Diploma year without having designed an investigation independently, and the scientific investigation is where that shows. Working on criteria B and C in MYP 5 is cheaper than repairing it in DP1.

programmes.name: Physics, Standard Level
programmes.description: The full set of themes at standard depth, with written papers and the scientific investigation. Standard Level physics is frequently taken by students whose main interests are elsewhere, and the characteristic problem is mathematical rather than conceptual: rearranging equations, handling powers of ten, and reading a graph quantitatively under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level physics tutoring requests from Academic City and Silicon Oasis are often really requests for mathematics support inside a physics context. That is a legitimate and efficient thing to buy, but it should be named, because it changes who the right tutor is and how long the work takes. One diagnostic session usually settles which of the two problems you have.

programmes.name: Physics, Higher Level
programmes.description: Additional content on top of Standard Level, greater mathematical demand, and longer papers. Higher Level physics is the usual requirement for engineering and physics degrees and is often taken alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, which is a heavy quantitative load across two years.

We say so at the enquiry stage with a realistic wait rather than assigning a Standard Level tutor and letting a pleasant first lesson carry the arrangement.

programmes.name: The scientific investigation
programmes.description: A single independent investigation worth 24 marks across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. It is the only part of the physics grade a student fully controls, and the only part where a weekend of careful work reliably outperforms a term of revision. It is also the most neglected.
programmes.countryNote: The practical constraint in this cluster is laboratory access. Students at schools with limited apparatus sometimes design investigations they cannot execute, and the fix is choosing a question that works with what the school actually has. A tutor is useful here as a reality check on feasibility before the research design is committed to, not as a source of data.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-academic.subjectsIntro: Physics tutoring is theme and skill work in roughly equal measure. These are the areas families in this cluster raise, and what each one actually demands.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, energy and circular motion, with rigid-body and relativity content at Higher Level. Marks are lost on free-body diagrams that omit a force, and on momentum questions where the direction convention is never stated before the arithmetic begins.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws, and the kinetic model. The recurring error is explaining temperature change in terms of heat as a substance rather than as energy transfer, which mark schemes treat as a misconception rather than loose phrasing.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave properties, superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference, with more demanding treatment at Higher Level. Path-difference questions reward drawing the geometry; students who attempt them algebraically from memory lose most of the available marks.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, circuits and electromagnetic induction. This is the largest source of confusion in the course and the most common presenting problem. Induction questions in particular require the direction argument to be made explicitly rather than asserted.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and quantum phenomena. Mark loss is mostly numerical: powers of ten, unit prefixes, and electronvolt-to-joule conversion applied inconsistently inside one calculation.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products, quotients and powers, and uncertainty in a gradient. Examined directly in data-analysis questions and central to the investigation's evaluation criterion. Mechanical rules, rarely taught, quickly learned.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing what to plot against what so a relationship becomes a straight line, then extracting a physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. The question is almost never 'plot this' but 'what does the gradient represent', and that distinction is where marks sit.

subjects.name: The mathematics physics assumes
subjects.description: Rearranging multi-variable equations, logarithms, small-angle approximations, trigonometry in resolving vectors, and standard form arithmetic at speed. Physics does not teach these and penalises their absence throughout, which is why some physics tutoring is properly mathematics tutoring.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: State, outline, describe, explain, deduce, determine, sketch and compare each specify a different kind and length of answer with different mark allocations. Students who answer every one as 'describe' lose marks on every extended-response question in the paper.

subjects.name: Experimental design and variable control
subjects.description: Independent, dependent and controlled variables, range and interval choice, repeat readings, and the systematic and random error distinction. Assessed in the investigation's research design criterion and in written data-analysis questions, and almost always the weakest part of a first draft.

subjects.name: Scientific investigation coaching
subjects.description: Research-question framing, feasibility against the school's apparatus, data handling, uncertainty treatment and the evaluation the criteria reward. All worked on the student's own data. The student designs, measures and writes; the tutor questions and gives feedback on drafts.

subjects.name: Physics for Extended Essay supervision support
subjects.description: Where a student writes the Extended Essay in physics, the recurring failure is a research question that cannot be answered experimentally within the available apparatus and word count. A tutor interrogates the question and the method and reads the student's drafts, and writes nothing.

sections.heading: The five themes and what each one actually demands
paragraphs: The current IB physics syllabus is organised into five themes rather than the older numbered topics with optional units. That restructuring matters for tutoring because a tutor working from an older guide will talk about options that no longer exist and may miss content that moved between levels. Ask the school for the subject guide that applies to your child's cohort, and ask specifically about component weightings, which are the detail most often out of date in third-party summaries.

What does not change is the character of each theme. Space, time and motion is where free-body diagrams and direction conventions decide marks. The particulate nature of matter punishes language that treats heat as a substance. Wave behaviour rewards drawing the geometry before reaching for an equation. Fields is the largest single source of confusion in the course. Nuclear and quantum physics is mostly a numerical-discipline problem rather than a conceptual one.

The table below sets out each theme with the characteristic failure and the diagnostic question a tutor can use to find it in one session. Those diagnostic questions are the useful part: they are quick, they are specific, and they separate a student who has a content gap from one who has a writing or numerical habit problem.

One scheduling note for this cluster specifically. Fields usually arrives in the second half of the first Diploma year, which is also when the scientific investigation starts competing for time. Families who book physics support before fields rather than during it have an easier year, because the theme is hard enough on its own without a coursework deadline running alongside.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, six marks each
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is worth 24 marks, assessed against four criteria carrying six marks apiece: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. No page competing for this search names a single criterion, which is a strange omission, because the equal weighting is the most actionable fact about the whole task. A brilliant conclusion cannot compensate for a weak research design, and most students spend their effort in the wrong place.

Research design is where the investigation is won or lost, and it happens before a single measurement is taken. It needs a research question that is answerable with the apparatus available, with the independent and dependent variables identified, the controlled variables named and actually controlled, and a method with a sensible range and interval and enough repeats to say something about reliability. Students in this cluster regularly design investigations their school's laboratory cannot execute.

Data analysis is processing, uncertainty treatment and presentation. This is where uncertainty propagation earns its marks and where most students lose them, because nobody taught the rules. Conclusion requires a statement justified by the data and placed in scientific context. Evaluation requires specific, prioritised limitations with realistic improvements - not 'more repeats would help', which earns nothing.

On process: the student chooses the research question, designs the method, takes the measurements, processes the data and writes the report. A tutor tests the feasibility of the question, explains what each criterion rewards, questions the design, and reads and comments on the student's drafts. One operator competing for these searches sells completed investigations at a published price; a malpractice finding from that falls on the candidate, not on the seller.

sections.heading: Uncertainty: the mechanical rules nobody taught
paragraphs: Uncertainty is the clearest example of a topic where a few hours of teaching produces marks that no amount of content revision would. The rules are mechanical. Absolute uncertainty from an instrument's resolution or from the spread of repeats. Fractional and percentage uncertainty from dividing by the measured value. Addition of absolute uncertainties when quantities are added or subtracted. Addition of percentage uncertainties when quantities are multiplied or divided. Multiplication of the percentage uncertainty by the power when a quantity is raised to one.

Those five rules cover almost every uncertainty question a Diploma physics student will meet, in written papers and in the investigation. Students who know them answer data-analysis questions confidently and write evaluation sections that score, and students who do not lose marks in both places without understanding why. It is the highest-return hour in physics tutoring and it almost never appears in a scheme of work as a lesson of its own.

The second part is uncertainty in a gradient, which appears in graph questions and in investigations with a linear relationship. Drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines through error bars and taking half the difference is a procedure, and like all procedures it becomes reliable with practice rather than with explanation. Four or five worked examples usually settle it.

The third part is knowing what to say about it. An evaluation that identifies the largest single source of uncertainty, explains why it dominates, and proposes a specific change that would reduce it scores where a list of generic limitations does not. That is a writing skill built on the numerical one, and it is the difference between a mid-band and a top-band evaluation criterion.

sections.heading: Graph linearisation and what a gradient represents
paragraphs: Physics graph questions are rarely about plotting. They ask a student to turn a non-linear relationship into a straight line by choosing the right quantities for the axes, and then to identify what the gradient and intercept physically represent. A student who plots accurately and cannot answer the second part has done the easy half of the question.

The method is a habit rather than a topic. Start from the equation relating the quantities. Rearrange it into the form of a straight line. Read off what must be plotted on each axis, what the gradient equals in terms of the physical constants, and what the intercept means. Then, and only then, plot. Students taught this way stop guessing at axis choices and start deriving them, which takes a fortnight of practice rather than a term of explanation.

The error-bar and best-fit decisions follow from the same discipline. A line of best fit, not a join-the-dots curve. Error bars where the uncertainty is significant on the scale of the graph. A gradient calculated from widely separated points on the line rather than from two data points. Each of these is a specific mark in a data-analysis question and each is commonly dropped.

This also matters for the investigation, where a linear relationship presented well and analysed with gradient uncertainty is the clearest route to a strong data-analysis criterion. A student who has practised linearisation on past-paper questions has already done most of the thinking their own investigation will require, which is an argument for doing the skill work early rather than saving it for the data.

sections.heading: Command terms, and why good physics scores badly
paragraphs: The most frustrating thing a parent can see is a physics answer that is true, well expressed and worth two marks out of five. Almost always the cause is the command term. Each one specifies a different kind of answer: state wants a short factual response with no reasoning, outline wants a brief account, describe wants the features without causes, explain wants the causes, deduce wants a conclusion reached from given information, and determine wants a numerical answer with working.

Students answer nearly all of them as 'describe', which is the most comfortable mode and the one that earns fewest marks on extended-response questions. The fix is mechanical and fast: underline the command term before writing, and know what each one requires. A fortnight of deliberate practice on this alone moves marks across every paper, which is why technique work beats content revision in the final weeks.

The mark allocation printed beside the question is the second half of the instruction. A four-mark explanation needs four distinct creditable points, and a student who writes one point in beautiful detail has lost three marks to a number printed in bold on the page. Teaching students to plan an answer against its mark allocation takes one session and lasts the whole course.

The table below sets out the command terms most often misread in physics, with what the mark scheme is looking for. The diagnostic is easy: take one marked paper and check how many extended-response answers described rather than explained. In our experience it is usually most of them.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level in physics
paragraphs: The difference between the two levels in physics is content volume and mathematical demand rather than a change of subject. Higher Level adds material on top of every theme and expects the mathematics to be handled fluently rather than carefully. A student who can rearrange an equation with effort will find Higher Level physics exhausting, because the rearrangement is a step inside a longer problem rather than the problem itself.

The combination question matters more than the level question. Higher Level physics taken alongside Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is a heavy quantitative load, and taken alongside a third demanding written subject it produces a January in the second Diploma year that effort alone will not solve. If your child is still choosing, map the assessment load across both years rather than looking at interest alone.

For university entry, Higher Level physics is the usual requirement for physics and engineering degrees, and Standard Level is frequently insufficient for those routes. Check the published requirements for the specific institutions, including the UAE ones, during the first Diploma year. Dropping from Higher to Standard Level is usually possible and dropping back up is usually not, which makes the early check worth doing properly.

For tutoring the practical difference is availability. Standard Level physics we can generally staff within days. Higher Level physics in the weeks before mock examinations is the single hardest thing on our list, because demand across Dubai peaks in the same fortnight. Booking in the first term costs the same and secures somebody who teaches the level rather than somebody who is free.

sections.heading: Practical work, laboratories and what online tutoring can and cannot do
paragraphs: A fair question deserves a direct answer. Apparatus work happens in the school laboratory, and no tutor on a video call can substitute for standing at a bench with a metre rule and a light gate. If your child's physics teaching depends on practical sessions they are not attending properly, tutoring is not the remedy; a conversation with the school is.

What a tutor can do is everything that surrounds the apparatus, and that is where the assessed marks sit. Choosing variables and a sensible range. Deciding how many repeats are worth taking and why. Recording to a consistent number of significant figures. Estimating and propagating uncertainty. Linearising and plotting. Calculating gradient uncertainty. Writing an evaluation that identifies the dominant error source. Every one of those is taught better on a shared screen with real data than standing beside a clamp stand.

The feasibility conversation is the other thing worth paying for. Students regularly propose investigations that need equipment their school does not own or precision it cannot reach, and discover this after a week of frustration. Half an hour spent testing a research question against the apparatus list is the single most useful intervention available before data collection starts.

What we do not do is contribute to the investigation itself, supply data, or provide IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads. We cite and link the official sources, which is also the only way to be sure the version is current. Schools hold past papers and the subject teacher is usually the quickest route to the right ones.

sections.heading: The physics year counted backwards, and the honest limits
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session. For physics the internal calendar matters as much as the external one, because the scientific investigation has a school deadline that typically lands in the second half of the first Diploma year or early in the second, where it competes with mock examinations and the Extended Essay in a crowded few weeks in January and February.

Counting backwards changes the plan. Uncertainty and graph skills built in the first term of the first year rather than discovered during data analysis. Research question tested for feasibility before the apparatus is booked. Investigation data collected and processed before mock revision begins. Timed data-analysis questions started in the first term of the second year rather than after the mocks.

We publish no specific IB session or results dates on this site. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date, so confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dates are sourced: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, the February and March series being offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November.

The honest limits: we make no promises about grades, publish no predicted scores and offer no guarantee, because nobody can honour one. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we have no office or centre anywhere in the UAE. On regulation, the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted at you.

process.title: Name the level and the theme
process.description: Higher or Standard, which school, which theme the class is on, and what the last marked paper came back as. Physics divides into content problems, numerical problems and writing problems, and naming the theme lets a tutor guess which of the three before the first session.

process.title: One marked paper, read for pattern
process.description: Marks lost on extended-response questions point to command terms. Marks lost on data-analysis questions point to uncertainty and graph skills. Marks lost across a theme point to content. Those three diagnoses lead to three completely different plans, and the paper settles it in twenty minutes.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written note
process.description: A real lesson on real physics, with the student working and the tutor diagnosing. Afterwards a plain written summary: whether the problem is content, numbers or writing, and what the available weeks would target. Say no and nothing further is owed.

process.title: Skills in parallel with themes
process.description: Uncertainty, graph linearisation and command terms built alongside the theme the class is covering rather than saved for the investigation or the final term. The student keeps an error log and it is checked for recurrence each session.

process.title: Feasibility check before the investigation
process.description: Half an hour testing the research question against the apparatus the school actually has, before any data is collected. It is the cheapest session in the whole arrangement and it prevents the commonest investigation failure in this cluster.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty taught as five mechanical rules
whyPoints.description: Absolute from resolution, add absolutes when adding, add percentages when multiplying, multiply by the power, gradient from maximum and minimum lines. Those five cover almost every uncertainty question in the course and almost no scheme of work teaches them as a lesson.

whyPoints.title: The investigation criteria named with their marks
whyPoints.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each, twenty-four in total. Equal weighting is the most actionable fact about the task and no competitor page in this market mentions a single criterion.

whyPoints.title: Command terms as a fortnight of work
whyPoints.description: Explain means causes; describe means features; deduce means a conclusion from given information. Students answer everything as describe. Fixing that moves marks across every paper faster than any amount of content revision.

whyPoints.title: Linearisation derived, not guessed
whyPoints.description: Start from the equation, rearrange into straight-line form, read the axes and the gradient's meaning off the rearrangement, then plot. Taught this way, students stop guessing at axis choices, which is where the second half of every graph question lives.

whyPoints.title: Feasibility before data collection
whyPoints.description: Students in this cluster regularly design investigations their school's laboratory cannot execute, and find out a week in. Half an hour spent testing the research question against the apparatus list prevents the most common investigation failure here.

whyPoints.title: We say when Higher Level is unavailable
whyPoints.description: Physics at Higher Level in the weeks before mocks is the single hardest combination we staff, because demand across Dubai peaks in one fortnight. You hear that at the enquiry stage with a realistic wait rather than meeting a Standard Level tutor at specialist rates.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB physics tutor in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your address, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. Physics is the clearest case for it in this district: Academic City is a university free zone whose own secondary runs the British route, and the number of people within driving distance who teach Diploma physics at Higher Level is close to zero. Matching online replaces proximity with whether the tutor teaches the level, which is what decides the grade.

faqs.question: Which syllabus themes will my child's physics class actually cover?
faqs.answer: Space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. These replaced the older numbered topics with optional units, which matters when choosing a tutor: anybody discussing option units is working from a superseded guide. Ask your child's school for the subject guide that applies to their cohort, and ask specifically about component weightings, since those are the detail most often out of date in third-party summaries of the course.

faqs.question: How are the 24 investigation marks split between the four criteria?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four marks, split equally across four criteria of six each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. That equal weighting is the most useful fact about the task, because it means a strong conclusion cannot rescue a weak research design, and research design is decided before any measurement is taken. Most students spend their effort on writing the report and lose marks on a method whose controlled variables were named but never actually controlled.

faqs.question: My daughter understands physics but her answers score badly. Why?
faqs.answer: Nearly always the command term. Explain requires causes and physical reasoning; describe requires features without causes; deduce requires a conclusion reached from information given; determine requires a numerical answer with working. Students answer almost everything as describe, which is the most comfortable mode and the lowest scoring on extended-response questions. The second cause is ignoring the mark allocation: a four-mark question needs four distinct creditable points, not one point explained beautifully.

faqs.question: Does my son need to be taught uncertainty separately?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly, and it is the highest-return hour in physics tutoring. Five rules cover nearly everything: absolute uncertainty from instrument resolution or repeat spread, add absolute uncertainties when adding or subtracting, add percentage uncertainties when multiplying or dividing, multiply percentage uncertainty by the power when raising to a power, and find gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines through the error bars. They are mechanical, rarely taught as a lesson, and examined directly in data-analysis questions.

faqs.question: What does a physics graph question actually test?
faqs.answer: Not plotting. It tests whether a student can turn a non-linear relationship into a straight line by choosing the right quantities for the axes, and then say what the gradient and intercept physically represent. The method is to start from the equation, rearrange it into straight-line form, read the axes and the gradient's meaning off the rearrangement, and only then plot. A student who plots accurately and cannot interpret the gradient has completed the easier half of the question.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's physics investigation legitimately?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor can test whether the research question is feasible with the school's apparatus, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, question the design, teach uncertainty treatment on the student's own measurements, and read and comment on drafts. A tutor cannot choose the question, design the method, supply or process data, or provide text for the report. The test is whether your child could explain, without notes, why every number and sentence is there.

faqs.question: Should my child drop physics from Higher to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Materially, and the difference is content volume plus mathematical fluency rather than a change of subject. Higher Level adds material across every theme and expects equation rearrangement to be automatic, because it is a step inside a longer problem rather than the problem itself. The combination matters as much as the level: Higher Level physics with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a heavy quantitative load, and adding a third demanding written subject produces a very difficult second Diploma year.

faqs.question: How can online lessons help if the practical work is in the school lab?
faqs.answer: Apparatus handling has to happen in the laboratory and no video call substitutes for it. But the assessed marks sit in what surrounds the apparatus: choosing variables and a sensible range, deciding how many repeats and why, recording to consistent significant figures, estimating and propagating uncertainty, linearising and plotting, calculating gradient uncertainty, and writing an evaluation that names the dominant error source. All of that is taught better on a shared screen with real data than beside a clamp stand.

faqs.question: Which theme causes the most trouble for Diploma physics students?
faqs.answer: Fields, consistently. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential and electromagnetic induction together produce more confusion than the rest of the course combined, partly because potential and field strength are routinely conflated and partly because induction questions require a direction argument to be derived rather than asserted. It also tends to arrive in the second half of the first Diploma year, just as the scientific investigation starts competing for the same hours.

faqs.question: My child came from a CBSE school. What is different about IB physics?
faqs.answer: Usually the numerical fluency is strong and the writing and uncertainty work are not, which is a very specific and quickly addressed gap. Students arriving from Indian-curriculum schools in Al Warqa or International City tend to compute confidently and then lose extended-response marks by describing rather than explaining, and lose data-analysis marks because uncertainty was never part of their previous course. Two or three sessions on command terms and five on uncertainty usually closes most of the distance.

faqs.question: When should the investigation be finished to avoid the February crush?
faqs.answer: Research question tested for feasibility and data collected before mock preparation begins, with the report drafted while there is still slack in the timetable. In most schools in this cluster the investigation deadline, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the mock examinations collide within a few weeks in January and February. The investigation is the piece that gets sacrificed because it feels furthest from the examination, and it is worth twenty-four marks.

faqs.question: How much does Diploma physics tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers publishing them: qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650; in-home one-to-one with travel runs AED 180 to 500. For Higher Level physics the budget band under AED 100 rarely contains anybody who teaches the level.

faqs.question: Is a physics tutor in Dubai required to hold a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level physics tutor is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You hear that at the enquiry stage rather than in session three. Higher Level physics in the fortnight either side of mock examinations is the hardest combination on our list, because demand across the emirate concentrates in the same weeks. In that case we give a realistic wait, offer interim support in the adjacent mathematics if that genuinely helps and say where the boundary is, or decline. What we will not do is put a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-academic.closingHeading: Send one marked physics paper and we will tell you what it shows
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-academic.closingBody: If your child is taking IB physics and you live in Dubai International Academic City, Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, Al Warqa or International City, one recent marked paper answers most of the useful questions. Marks lost on extended responses point to command terms; marks lost on data questions point to uncertainty and graph work; marks lost across one theme point to content. Those are three different plans. Tell us the level, the school and the theme the class is on, and we will say honestly whether a specialist is free. The trial lesson is free and lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Programme Physics at Higher and Standard Level. Each works from the syllabus your child's school is actually teaching, including the data-booklet conventions, the Paper 3 practical questions and the internal assessment criteria, rather than from general school physics.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near Dubai Creek Harbour who actually knows the IB Physics syllabus?
paragraphs: That is the real question behind the search, so here is the direct answer. Dubai Creek Harbour is a new waterfront district built along the Ras Al Khor side of the creek, and it does not yet contain a large cluster of IB World Schools inside its own master plan. Families living in Creek Beach, Harbour Views, Creek Gate, Address Harbour Point and the surrounding towers drive out of the district for school, mostly towards Al Jaddaf, Nad Al Sheba, Al Garhoud and Sobha Hartland. The number of qualified Diploma Programme Physics teachers who both live within twenty minutes of your tower and have free evening hours is, realistically, very small. Anyone who tells you otherwise is describing a marketing area, not a staffing reality.

There is a second problem that parents discover only after paying for a few sessions. Physics tutoring is widely advertised, but Diploma Programme Physics is a specific qualification with its own command terms, its own data booklet, a 1.5-hour Paper 1 split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and an internal assessment marked against five named criteria. A tutor who knows A Level Physics or CBSE Class 12 Physics well can still mark an IB investigation incorrectly, because the IB does not reward the same things. The commonest symptom is a student who leaves tutoring with better algebra and the same grade.

IB Gram does not solve this by pretending to have a Physics teacher in every district. We solve it by removing distance from the matching decision altogether. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, so the constraint becomes whether a tutor has taught your child's exact course rather than whether they can reach Creek Harbour before the Al Khail Road evening build-up. A Creek Harbour family gets a Physics HL specialist who has marked dozens of investigations against criteria Personal Engagement through Communication, instead of the nearest available generalist.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India, and we state that on every UAE page rather than letting a parent find out after booking. If your firm preference is a tutor physically at your dining table in Creek Beach, this is not the right service and we would rather say so in the first paragraph than the eighth. What we do offer, and what the rest of this page sets out in detail, is screen-shared Physics teaching where the whiteboard, the graph and the marked-up past paper are all saved and sent to you afterwards.

The rest of the page is written to let you check us rather than trust us. There is a table of what the Dubai market charges for Physics tutoring at each tier, with the source of every figure. There is a table of the ten questions to ask any prospective Physics tutor, with the answer a genuine DP specialist gives and the answer that tells you to walk away. There is the assessment structure with real weightings, a section on exactly where Creek Harbour students lose Physics marks, the academic-honesty boundary around the IA, and the regulator and equivalency facts that affect your child's paperwork long after the exam.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.programmesIntro: Physics does not begin in the Diploma Programme. Most Creek Harbour students who struggle in DP1 Physics arrive from a Middle Years Programme science course or an IGCSE Physics course, and the gap between those and DP Physics is predictable enough to be taught around. These are the programme stages we cover and what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Physics in the Diploma Programme is sat at Higher or Standard Level. Both share a common core organised around measurement, mechanics, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, circular motion and gravitation, atomic and nuclear physics, and energy production. Higher Level adds further material inside each of those themes and a substantially larger mathematical load, particularly in fields, induction and quantum phenomena. Assessment is three external papers plus one internal investigation of 3,000 words or fewer.
programmes.countryNote: Creek Harbour students mostly sit DP Physics at schools in Al Jaddaf, Nad Al Sheba, Sobha Hartland and Al Garhoud, all regulated by KHDA. Because those schools set their own internal investigation deadlines, usually in the second term of DP1 or the first term of DP2, two Creek Harbour neighbours in the same tower can be on completely different Physics timelines. We work from your child's school deadline sheet, not a generic one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria rather than papers: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students are graded 1-8 on each. The programme builds investigation design and data handling early, which is precisely the skill the DP Physics internal assessment later rewards, but it does not build the algebraic fluency that DP Physics Paper 2 assumes.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP Physics step is the single most common reason a Creek Harbour parent contacts us in October of DP1. A student who scored 7s against MYP criteria can still find the first DP Physics test hard, because MYP rarely demands rearranging a formula under timed conditions. We treat that as a mathematics gap inside a physics course and close it with targeted work on substitution, units and significant figures before touching new topics.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics (pre-DP route)
programmes.description: Many Creek Harbour families follow a British-curriculum school to Year 11 and then move into the IB Diploma. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is syllabus 0625 and Pearson's International GCSE Physics is 4PH1. Both separate into a core and an extended or higher tier at Cambridge, and both demand practical skills assessed on paper rather than in a lab. The grades matter for DP route choice: a student entering DP Physics HL from IGCSE core content usually needs catch-up on electricity and on graph interpretation.
programmes.countryNote: For British schools licensed by KHDA in and around Al Jaddaf and Al Garhoud, the IGCSE route feeds both A Level and the IB Diploma. Cambridge runs its IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series for UAE centres, and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November. The March series is offered to India only and does not apply to your child, whatever an aggregator site tells you.

programmes.name: Physics internal assessment and extended essay support
programmes.description: The Physics internal investigation is worth 20% of the final Physics grade at both levels and is marked by the school against criteria the IB names by letter and title. A Physics extended essay is a separate 4,000-word research piece supervised by the school. Both are the student's own work. Our role is to teach the methodology, question the research design, explain what each criterion rewards and give written feedback on drafts the student has written.
programmes.countryNote: Creek Harbour sits beside the Ras Al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary and a working creek, which generates genuinely good local physics investigations: tidal data, salinity and density, sound attenuation across open water, solar irradiance on the tower facades. We will happily help a student interrogate whether such a question is measurable to the precision the IB expects. We will not supply a topic list and we will not write a word of the report.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.subjectsIntro: Physics is the page you came for, but most Creek Harbour families eventually ask about a second subject. These are the IB courses we cover for this district, described by what the assessment actually tests rather than by topic lists a school website already gives you.

subjects.name: Physics HL
subjects.description: Three papers and one investigation. Paper 1 splits into multiple choice and a data-analysis section; Paper 2 is extended response; Paper 3 covers experimental technique and the option material. HL marks are lost most often on fields and induction, where sign conventions and direction arguments carry as much credit as the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Physics SL
subjects.description: The same core themes with the additional-higher-level content removed and a lighter mathematical demand. SL students lose marks disproportionately on definitions and on explaining rather than calculating. A command term like 'outline' asks for a different answer length from 'explain', and SL papers punish the difference.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most DP Physics students take, because the calculus and trigonometry overlap directly with mechanics and waves. Proof, sequences and the HL calculus option are where marks disappear. A Physics student who is weak in AA almost always presents as weak in Physics Paper 2 first.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led, with a graphical and modelling emphasis and a heavier technology requirement. Workable alongside Physics SL. Students should check the prerequisite pages of any engineering degree they are considering before choosing AI over AA, because some faculties specify the AA route.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Commonly paired with Physics by Creek Harbour students aiming at engineering or medicine. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms account for most lost marks. Chemistry shares the Physics problem of a 20% internal investigation marked at school against stated criteria.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy on terminology precision and on command-term discipline. The difference between 'state', 'outline' and 'explain' decides several marks per paper. Students who enjoy the Physics investigation often find the Biology investigation harder because variables are less clean.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pairs naturally with Physics for students heading towards engineering. Assessment includes a substantial solution-development project. Marks are lost on documenting the design process rather than on writing code, which surprises confident programmers.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered by a minority of Dubai IB schools and genuinely useful for a Physics student. The design cycle and the extended coursework reward the same evidence discipline the Physics investigation does, so support transfers across both.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A frequent third subject for Physics students who want a non-science option that still uses graphs and data. The internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles, each with a strict word limit and a required diagram.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Includes an individual oral assessed on the student's own chosen extracts. Physics students often treat this as the subject that will look after itself and then lose points on the paper 1 guided analysis, where structure matters more than vocabulary.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects. Physics students have an advantage here because the natural-sciences area of knowledge gives them concrete examples, provided they move past 'science is objective' as a claim.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.regionsTitle: Dubai Creek Harbour and the districts around it
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-creek-ha.regionsIntro: Creek Harbour does not stand alone. It sits in the central corridor of Dubai, between Al Jaddaf and Ras Al Khor, and your child's school, friends and tutoring timetable are all shaped by the districts next door. These are the neighbourhoods whose families we most often teach alongside Creek Harbour.

regions.name: Dubai Creek Harbour
regions.note: A master-planned waterfront district including Creek Beach, Harbour Views, Creek Gate and the Address Harbour Point towers. Few schools within the boundary, so almost every secondary student commutes out, usually north towards Al Jaddaf or south towards Nad Al Sheba.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Directly across the creek and the nearest significant school cluster, home to an IB continuum school and several healthcare and hospitality towers. A ten-minute drive outside peak, considerably longer at school-run times on Al Khail Road.

sections.heading: What a Creek Harbour parent is really asking, and the honest answer
paragraphs: The literal answer first. There is no large pool of Diploma Programme Physics specialists resident in Dubai Creek Harbour, because the district is new, its school provision is still filling in, and DP Physics teachers are a small professional group across the whole emirate. Dubai has 227 private schools and the International Baccalaureate accounts for about 7% of private-school enrolment, which means DP Physics is taught in a few dozen schools rather than hundreds. Spread those teachers across Dubai's geography and the number with free evening hours inside your district is close to zero.

What families do next usually falls into one of three patterns. Some hire whoever is nearest and advertises physics, which produces a tutor who is competent in school physics and unfamiliar with IB command terms and the internal investigation criteria. Some hire a university student at the bottom of the market, which can work for arithmetic confidence and rarely works for Paper 3. Some decide tutoring is not available locally and wait, which is the costliest option because DP Physics compounds: an unsecured treatment of uncertainty in DP1 becomes a lost Paper 1B section in DP2.

The fourth option is to stop treating geography as a selection criterion. Once the lesson runs over live video, the question becomes which tutor has taught this exact course, marked this exact investigation and sat with students through this exact paper. That is a far better filter than driving distance, and it is the whole argument for the format. The table below sets out what we can and cannot cover for a Creek Harbour family, including what happens when a specialist is not immediately free, because availability transparency is something no competitor page in this market publishes.

sections.heading: How IB Physics is actually assessed, paper by paper
paragraphs: Before any tutoring decision, it helps to know where the marks sit. IB Diploma Physics is assessed through three external examination papers and one internally marked investigation. The investigation is worth 20% of the final grade at both Higher and Standard Level, which means a fifth of your child's Physics result is decided months before the examination session and is marked by their own teacher against published criteria. Families routinely discover this late, after the window for improving it has closed.

The external papers divide the work differently from most national systems. Paper 1 is split: one section is multiple choice across the whole course, the other is a data-analysis section built on an unseen experiment. Paper 2 is extended response, where structure and command-term discipline earn marks that pure calculation does not. Paper 3 covers experimental technique and the course's optional material, and it is where students with strong content knowledge and weak laboratory experience are exposed, because the questions assume familiarity with real apparatus behaviour.

A Higher Level student carries the same structure with more content inside every theme and significantly heavier mathematics. The practical consequence for tutoring is that HL and SL need different session shapes. An HL student usually needs 90-minute sessions to work a full Paper 2 question set with review; an SL student often makes faster progress in 60-minute sessions focused on definitions, command terms and data handling. The table gives the structure in the form worth pinning to a fridge.

sections.heading: Ten questions that reveal whether a Physics tutor knows the IB
paragraphs: This is the section to use whether or not you book with us. A parent cannot assess physics competence directly, but a parent can absolutely assess whether someone knows the IB's machinery, and that distinction is where most of the money in this market is wasted. The questions below take about four minutes to ask on a trial call, and each one has an answer a genuine Diploma Programme Physics teacher gives without hesitation.

Notice what the questions do not ask. They do not ask about qualifications in the abstract, because a physics degree says nothing about IB familiarity. They do not ask about results, because any figure quoted without a sample size, a date and a method is unverifiable and we do not publish such figures ourselves. They ask about the specific, checkable mechanics of the course: the number of assessment criteria, the data booklet, the word limit, the split inside Paper 1, what the tutor would do with a research question that is not measurable.

If a prospective tutor gives three red-flag answers, the problem is not that they are a poor teacher. The problem is that they will teach your child physics while the IB marks them on something adjacent to physics. That gap is invisible on a progress report and obvious in a final grade. Ask the questions before the first payment, not after the first mock.

One more thing worth asking, because it costs nothing and tells you a great deal: ask what the tutor would want to see before the first lesson. A specialist asks for the school's scheme of work and a recently marked script, because those two documents locate the problem precisely. A generalist asks for the syllabus, which is publicly available and tells them nothing about your child. The difference between those two answers is the difference between a tutor who will teach your child and a tutor who will teach the course at your child.

sections.heading: Where Creek Harbour Physics students actually lose marks
paragraphs: Across the students we support in Dubai's central corridor, lost Physics marks cluster in a small number of places, and almost none of them are the topics parents expect. Quantum physics and nuclear physics look frightening on a syllabus and are usually taught carefully because teachers know they frighten people. The marks disappear in the unglamorous material that gets covered quickly in DP1 and never revisited: uncertainties, significant figures, unit prefixes, and the mechanics of reading a gradient off a graph with a scale nobody chose sensibly.

The second cluster is command terms. A student who writes a correct and complete physical explanation in answer to 'state' has wasted time they needed elsewhere; a student who writes one line in answer to 'explain' has thrown away marks that required no new knowledge. This is pure technique, it is learnable in a handful of sessions, and it is the highest-yield intervention available to a DP2 student in the final term. It also transfers: the same discipline recovers marks in Chemistry and Biology.

The third cluster is the investigation, and it is the most expensive because it cannot be fixed late. A research question that is too broad produces data that will not support a conclusion, and no amount of careful writing recovers that. A student whose investigation question was settled in a rushed week before a school deadline is usually capped by that decision, whatever they do afterwards. For Creek Harbour students the local environment offers unusually tractable options, from the creek's tidal range to solar incidence on tower facades, but tractable is not the same as measurable to the precision the criteria want.

sections.heading: What Physics tutoring costs around Dubai Creek Harbour
paragraphs: Start from the cheapest end, because that is where most families begin and where the decision is usually made. A university student tutoring online advertises from roughly AED 45 to 65 per hour on EdFlik and from about AED 33 to 52 on Tutopiya, figures those providers publish themselves. For arithmetic confidence in MYP science, that is reasonable value. For DP Physics Paper 3, it is not, and the reason is specific rather than snobbish: the course's marks sit in criteria and command terms a tutor learns by teaching the qualification, not by having passed it.

Move one tier up and the published numbers change shape. Unitors lists IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 per hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above, with in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching AED 500. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a named or examiner-led tutor. Monthly packages appear in the market at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

What is worth noticing is the travel premium hiding inside those bands. The gap between the online specialist band and the in-home band is not a quality gap; it is largely the tutor's unpaid driving time priced into your hour. For a Creek Harbour address that premium is real, because almost any tutor reaching you crosses either the Ras Al Khor approaches or Al Khail Road in the evening. IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages, because our matching depends on level, subject and frequency. We publish the market so you can judge any quote, including ours, and the trial lesson is the point at which you see the teaching before any payment.

sections.heading: Online Physics teaching versus a tutor driving to Creek Harbour
paragraphs: This comparison deserves a straight treatment rather than a sales pitch, because in-home tutoring has genuine advantages and a Creek Harbour parent should know what they are. A tutor in the room can read a child's face, confiscate a phone, and hold the attention of a twelve-year-old who will not sit still for a screen. For younger students and for students with particular attention needs, that matters, and we would not argue otherwise.

For Diploma Programme Physics specifically, the balance moves the other way, and the reasons are concrete. The pool of tutors available to a Creek Harbour address is bounded by the evening traffic radius; the pool available over video is bounded by nothing except timezone. The screen is a better teaching surface for this subject than a dining table, because graphs, simulations, past-paper scans and annotated mark schemes can all be shared, saved and sent afterwards. And the travel premium in the market rate buys driving, not teaching.

To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Our tutors do not come to Creek Beach, Harbour Views, Creek Gate or any other UAE address. Home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. We target the phrase because it is what parents type, and we answer the question honestly rather than taking a booking under a misunderstanding. The table compares the three realistic formats on the measures that decide the choice.

There is also a point about continuity that parents raise after a term. Creek Harbour families travel, and many spend part of the summer and part of the winter break outside the UAE. A tutor who drives to your address cannot follow you to Europe or South Asia for three weeks, so the arrangement pauses and the student loses momentum at exactly the point in the calendar when coursework deadlines sit. A video lesson follows the family, which matters most in the DP1 summer when the investigation is usually being written.

sections.heading: The Physics investigation and the academic-honesty line
paragraphs: This section exists because the same search results that brought you here also contain services selling completed Internal Assessments. One of the pages in this market offers finished IB coursework at a published price. A parent under deadline pressure in the final weeks of DP1 can rationalise that purchase in about thirty seconds, and it is the single most damaging thing that can happen to a Diploma candidate. IB academic-honesty rules treat submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the vendor.

So here is where the line sits, stated as plainly as we can. A tutor may teach experimental method. A tutor may ask questions that force a student to narrow a vague research question themselves. A tutor may explain what each assessment criterion rewards, using the IB's own published criterion titles. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and give written feedback identifying which criterion is losing marks and why. A tutor may teach uncertainty propagation, graph selection and the data booklet conventions that the report will need.

A tutor may not choose the research question. A tutor may not supply data. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit-to-completion any part of the report, including the abstract or the conclusion. A tutor may not provide a template to be filled in, which is ghost-writing with extra steps. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them, cite the official source and link to it, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. If a service in this market offers you anything on the second list, that is the signal to close the tab.
bullets: Allowed: teaching method, questioning the research design, explaining criteria, written feedback on the student's own draft
