sections.heading: The exam run counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Almost no competitor page in this market mentions an exam session at all, which is strange, because the session is the only fixed point in the year. UAE IB schools sit the May session. We deliberately do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date we restated would be unverified, and an unverified date that a parent plans around is worse than no date. Confirm your child's exact dates with their school's IB coordinator, who receives them directly.

What can be published is the shape of the year, because the shape does not change. Work backwards from the session and the sequence is: option and level choices settled in the term before DP1 begins; investigation question agreed and data collected in DP1 or early DP2, on a deadline the school sets; extended essay drafts through DP1 into DP2; mock examinations typically in the second term of DP2; final internal deadlines for all coursework ahead of the school's upload window; then the session itself, results to schools, and the enquiry-upon-results window for any remark.

For Cambridge and Pearson, real sourced dates do exist and are worth knowing if your child sits IGCSE on the way to the Diploma. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with every centre allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always open the live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date, including ours.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory UAE subjects and what they do to a Physics timetable
paragraphs: Your child's school is licensed and inspected by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the published report for any Dubai private school is worth reading before you blame a tutor-shaped problem on your child. Across the UAE the regulator map is complete and worth knowing: ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education supervising Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The point that affects Physics directly is the mandatory-subject requirement. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited.

Read that as a timetable fact rather than a policy note. Those mandatory hours sit inside the same school week as Physics, and they are not optional for your child even in a DP cohort. That is part of why a Creek Harbour DP2 student can genuinely have less Physics contact time than a parent assumes, and why evening tutoring frequently has to do consolidation work the school week could not fit. To be explicit about our own standing: IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or accreditation, and we are not a licensed training institute. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to institutes with premises, which we do not have and do not claim.

sections.heading: Permits, and how to check whether a tutor may legally teach your child
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, and a parent can verify compliance in a single question. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', with a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow. First, anyone describing the permit as expensive, slow or optional is wrong on all three counts, and that misdescription is usually a sign they do not hold one. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no credible page will quote you an amount, and any page that does has invented it. Second, the permit carries a code of conduct. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own conduct rules bar serving students affiliated with the teacher's school. This is press-reported, so verify the current ADEK wording before relying on it.

The practical reading for a Creek Harbour family is simple. Never arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately for payment, however convenient it looks, because the exposure sits with the teacher and the awkwardness lands on your child. Ask any independent tutor directly whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit; it is free and quick to obtain, so there is no sympathetic reason not to have one. And treat a tutor's willingness to answer that question at all as information in itself.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the paperwork a Physics student needs later
paragraphs: A Physics grade is not the only thing that decides what happens after school in the UAE. Certificate equivalency through the Ministry of Education is what allows a secondary qualification to be recognised for university admission and employment here, and it catches families by surprise because almost nobody in this market mentions it. It is worth understanding in DP1, not in the summer after results, because some of its requirements are tests your child must sit and pass separately.

For the British track the requirements are documented. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That five-subject rule is worth holding on to, because at least one ranking competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically, we publish no points threshold, because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae and an invented figure on a page like this would be repeated by parents as fact. Verify the IB position with the Ministry of Education directly or with your school's university counsellor. Equivalency is a process the authority performs, not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or accelerates, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Getting started from Creek Harbour, including what can go wrong
paragraphs: The useful version of this section includes the failure modes, because every tutoring arrangement has them and a page that pretends otherwise is not telling you anything. What we ask for first is specific: your child's school, the exact course and level, the school's scheme of work if you can get it, and one recently marked Physics script. The marked script is the single most valuable thing a parent can send. A tutor can read a student's actual problem off a marked paper in ten minutes, and cannot read it at all off the sentence 'she is struggling with physics'.

Then there is a free trial lesson of about 45 minutes, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel if you do not continue. The trial is diagnostic rather than promotional: the tutor works a real question with your child and then tells you what they found, including when the answer is that tutoring is not the right intervention. Occasionally the honest finding is that the student needs a conversation with their school about level, or needs mathematics support rather than physics support. We would rather say that than sell twelve sessions against the wrong problem.

Where it goes wrong, it usually goes wrong in one of three ways. The specialist a student needs is not free at the hour the family wants, and we offer a date instead of quietly substituting someone else. The personality match is wrong, which is nobody's fault and is fixed by changing tutor at no additional cost rather than by persevering. Or expectations are mismatched: a parent books four sessions in May expecting a grade movement that a year of missed foundations will not give up in four hours. We will say so at the start. No tutor can promise a grade, and we never will.

faqs.question: Is there an IB Physics tutor near me in Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and that is the honest answer. Creek Harbour is a new district with few schools inside its boundary, and Diploma Programme Physics teachers are a small group across the whole of Dubai, where the IB accounts for about 7% of private-school enrolment. The chance that a DP Physics specialist lives within twenty minutes of your tower and has free evening hours is low. IB Gram's answer is to drop distance as a criterion: lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so your child is matched to a tutor who has taught their exact course and level instead of to whoever is nearest.

faqs.question: Do your tutors come to homes in Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, including Creek Beach, Harbour Views, Creek Gate and the Address Harbour Point towers. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. For UAE families every lesson is delivered live, one-to-one, over video. We target the phrase 'home tutor' because it is what parents search for, and then answer the question rather than take a booking under a misunderstanding. If having a tutor physically present is a firm requirement for your family, we are not the right service and we would rather say so now.

faqs.question: How much does an IB Physics tutor cost around Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: The market, not our price list. Budget online tutoring advertises from about AED 45-65 per hour on EdFlik and AED 33-52 on Tutopiya. Qualified online subject tutors sit around AED 150-300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutoring runs AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table reaching 450-plus. In-home visits cost AED 180-500 because travel time is inside the rate. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, per BartyED. All figures were read in October 2026 from the providers' own pages.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Physics HL and SL for tutoring purposes?
faqs.answer: Both levels share the same core themes and the same 20% internal investigation, but Higher Level adds further content inside every theme and a much heavier mathematical load, particularly in fields, induction and quantum phenomena. In practice this changes the session shape rather than the subject. HL students usually need 90 minutes to work a full Paper 2 question set with proper review afterwards. SL students often progress faster in 60-minute sessions concentrating on definitions, command-term discipline and data handling, because that is where SL marks are most commonly lost.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Physics internal investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we state plainly. A tutor may teach experimental method, question the research design until the student narrows it themselves, explain what each of the five assessment criteria rewards, teach uncertainty propagation and graph choice, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not choose the research question, supply data, or write, rewrite or edit any part of the report. Services in these same search results sell completed Internal Assessments; submitting that work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on your child's diploma.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP Physics student usually need?
faqs.answer: Most Creek Harbour families start with one hour a week and adjust after about a month. One session weekly is enough to keep pace with the school's scheme of work and to close small gaps as they appear. Two becomes sensible when a student is a term behind, is carrying Physics HL alongside Maths AA HL, or is inside the final eight weeks before a session. Short intensive blocks make sense around an investigation deadline. We will give a view after the trial lesson rather than before, because the marked script usually changes the recommendation.

faqs.question: My child's Physics exam is six weeks away. Is it worth starting now?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, provided the goal is realistic. Six weeks is enough to drill command terms, practise data-booklet navigation, sit timed Paper 1 sections with mark-scheme review, and fix uncertainty handling. Those are the highest-yield items available late and they often move marks noticeably. Six weeks is not enough to rebuild two years of missed foundations, and no honest tutor will suggest otherwise. What we will not do is promise a grade. After the trial you will get a specific answer about what six weeks can and cannot reach for your child.

faqs.question: Which schools do Dubai Creek Harbour students actually attend?
faqs.answer: Because the district has limited school provision inside its own boundary, almost every secondary student commutes out. The nearest cluster sits across the creek in Al Jaddaf and Al Garhoud, which includes an IB continuum school and several long-established international schools. The other major direction is south towards Nad Al Sheba, Sobha Hartland and Meydan, which hold some of Dubai's largest IB cohorts and several selective British schools. A third group of families chooses Downtown, Business Bay or Al Quoz for proximity to work. All sit under KHDA regulation.

faqs.question: What time can a Physics session realistically start on a weekday?
faqs.answer: From about 4.30pm Gulf Standard Time for most Creek Harbour families. School days in the nearby clusters typically end between 2.45pm and 3.15pm, but buses from Nad Al Sheba, Al Quoz and Al Garhoud do not reach Creek Harbour towers until around 4pm, and the Ras Al Khor and Al Khail approaches are slow at that hour. A 3.30pm slot looks fine on paper and is missed in practice. Later slots from 6pm work well, and because the tutor has no commute, an evening start costs nothing extra in travel.

faqs.question: Is the tutor I hire for Creek Harbour legally allowed to teach privately?
faqs.answer: They need a permit, and you can verify it with one question. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are all listed as eligible. MoHRE quotes a two-working-day completion time through its app, website and e-services. Since it is free and fast, there is no sympathetic reason for a working tutor not to hold one. Operating without it attracts penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Should we ask a teacher from my child's own school to tutor them?
faqs.answer: Our advice is not to. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported detail and verify the current wording, but the direction of travel is unambiguous across the UAE. There is also a practical reason beyond compliance. The teacher who tutors your child is often the teacher who marks their internal investigation, and that is an uncomfortable position to put a sixteen-year-old in.

faqs.question: Is online Physics teaching genuinely as good as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For Diploma Programme Physics, we think it is better, and for specific reasons rather than general ones. The screen is a superior teaching surface for this subject: graphs, simulations, scanned past papers and annotated mark schemes can all be shared, saved and sent afterwards, which a dining table cannot do. More importantly, the tutor pool stops being bounded by evening traffic. For a much younger student, or one with particular attention needs, a tutor physically present can hold focus better, and we would not argue the point. For DP Physics the balance is clear.

faqs.question: What is in the IB Physics data booklet and does it help?
faqs.answer: The data booklet supplies specific equations and physical constants for use in the examinations, which means the examination is not testing memorisation of formulae. It does test whether a student can find the right relationship quickly under time pressure, and that is a practised skill rather than knowledge. Students who have never worked systematically with the booklet lose minutes per paper hunting for an equation they know exists. We treat navigation as a drillable item in its own right, usually in the final weeks. The official booklet comes from the IB; we reference it rather than reproducing it.

faqs.question: Does the February exam series apply to my child in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and this one catches families out because aggregator websites repeat it carelessly. Cambridge International's February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. IB candidates in the UAE sit the May session. We publish no specific IB examination or results date on these pages, because the IB's own site cannot be verified automatically and a wrong date is something a parent plans a revision schedule around. Ask your child's IB coordinator, who receives the dates directly.

faqs.question: Do I need to think about MoE equivalency while my child is still in DP1?
faqs.answer: It is worth understanding early, because parts of it are separate tests. For the British track, a student needs five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. For the American track, SAT Math 450-plus and English via IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT reading-writing 450. For the IB we publish no points figure because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae. Verify with the Ministry; equivalency is their process, not ours.

faqs.question: The first tutor did not click with my son. What then?
faqs.answer: We move him to a different one, at no extra cost, and we do not ask you to persevere first. A mismatch between a teenager and a tutor is nobody's failing and is not solved by effort or by more hours. We prefer to judge the match against the next real piece of marked work rather than against a feeling: if a school test or an investigation draft has not shifted and the tutor cannot say precisely why, we treat that as our problem to fix. What we will not do is suggest a longer package in the hope that volume covers a matching error.

intro.heading: The physics week a Dubai Festival City Diploma student actually has
paragraphs: Start with the timetable, because physics is the Diploma subject most likely to break a tidy tuition plan. Secondary dismissal at the schools Dubai Festival City families use lands between about 2.15pm and 3.30pm. On top of that, a Diploma physics student frequently has a double period that leaves them genuinely tired, a practical session that overruns, and in many schools an after-school science or robotics commitment one afternoon a week. None of this appears on a report, and all of it decides which evenings are usable.

Then the journey. A bus from a Garhoud or Festival City campus reaches Al Badia in minutes and Al Khawaneej or Al Warqa in thirty-five to fifty. Add the half hour for food that every experienced tutor builds in, and the realistic earliest start for a Diploma student is around four o'clock in the inner communities and five or later in the outer ones. For physics specifically, a late evening slot is a poor purchase: the subject asks for sustained algebraic reasoning, and that is the first thing a tired student loses.

Now the investigation. The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the physics grade and its internal deadlines are set by the school, not by the board. Those deadlines cluster, because every Diploma science subject sets one and the Extended Essay sits nearby. A family that discovers in February that three deadlines land in the same fortnight has a scheduling emergency that money cannot fully solve. Asking the school for the dates in September is free and is the single most useful planning act available.

Against all of that, an in-home tutor has to arrive inside a narrow window having crossed Garhoud Bridge or the Dubai-Al Ain interchange at the worst hour. The lesson starts when the traffic allows and the missing fifteen minutes come out of the teaching rather than the fee. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons here are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the session starts at the time you booked it.

For physics the online format has a specific advantage beyond punctuality. Physics teaching is mostly working through problems line by line, and a shared screen puts the same working in front of both people at the same size, with the tutor able to annotate the exact line where a unit was dropped or a rearrangement went wrong. A past-paper mark scheme can be opened alongside the student's own attempt. Across a table, the tutor is reading upside down.

The rest of this page sets out the five themes of the current syllabus, what each paper component asks, how the investigation criteria work, where marks go missing in this subject specifically, and how to place sessions in a week that already contains a double period and a lab afternoon.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-festival.programmesIntro: Physics arrives in the Diploma from one of two directions and the step feels different depending on which. These are the stages and what each one leaves a student ready or unready for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Integrated or discrete sciences assessed against four criteria, A to D, each on a 1 to 8 scale. The investigating criterion is where MYP most closely resembles what the Diploma will ask for, and it is also the criterion students most often treat as a write-up rather than as a designed piece of work.
programmes.countryNote: A Dubai Festival City student arriving at Diploma physics from MYP usually has sound investigation instincts and uneven mathematics. The gap is almost never conceptual physics; it is rearranging formulae, handling indices and standard form, and manipulating units, all of which are maths skills doing physics work.

programmes.name: IGCSE physics or combined science
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 for separate physics, or a combined science entry covering all three subjects more narrowly. Students arriving from a combined entry meet substantially more content in the Diploma than those who sat separate physics, which is worth knowing before DP1 starts rather than in November.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools near Dubai Festival City run IGCSE before splitting at 16, so this is the commoner route locally. The honest warning is that a grade 8 in IGCSE physics does not predict comfort in Diploma physics, because the Diploma's demand for extended written reasoning is new rather than harder.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme physics
programmes.description: Five themes covering space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Assessed by Paper 1, which contains a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and Paper 2 of structured and extended-response questions, plus a scientific investigation worth 20 per cent.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level adds content across the themes and raises the extended-response demand. Deira International School runs the IB continuum to Diploma and GEMS Modern Academy at Nad Al Sheba is a long-established Diploma centre, so most physics requests in this corridor come from students at one of a handful of schools with broadly similar timetable shapes.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-festival.subjectsIntro: This grid is the current physics syllabus split into what sessions are actually bought for, with the part of each theme that costs marks. Take any three to a prospective tutor and ask them to talk about where students go wrong.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, work and energy, momentum, and circular motion and gravitation. The theme where marks are most often lost to a free-body diagram drawn carelessly, because a missing force makes every line after it wrong however good the algebra is.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, current and circuits. Circuit questions reward a student who redraws the circuit before calculating, and punish one who starts substituting into formulae from the diagram as printed on the paper.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave models, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Interference and diffraction questions are where the algebra is manageable and the physical reasoning is not, so explanation marks go missing more than calculation marks.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, and electromagnetic induction at Higher Level. Field questions reward sign conventions and consistency; students who treat the minus sign as decoration lose marks they have otherwise earned.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Structure of the atom, radioactive decay, nuclear fission and fusion, and quantum phenomena. Usually taught late in DP2, which makes it the theme most likely to be met under time pressure and therefore the commonest late-booking request.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.description: Graph drawing, gradient and intercept interpretation, absolute and percentage uncertainty, and propagation. This appears in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and inside the investigation, and it is the single most under-prepared skill in Diploma physics.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: Multi-mark written answers requiring a chain of physical reasoning rather than a calculation. Students lose marks by describing an effect without naming the mechanism, and by writing three sentences that each repeat the first in different words.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An independent investigation on a question of the student's own choosing, marked against published criteria. Thin evaluation and a research question that is too broad to answer with the available equipment are the two commonest and most expensive failures.

subjects.name: Mathematics for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, indices and standard form, trigonometry, logarithms and gradients. A student who is not fluent here will appear weak across all five themes, because the same gap resurfaces in each of them wearing different clothes.

subjects.name: Practical skills and apparatus reasoning
subjects.description: Choosing apparatus, identifying systematic and random error, suggesting improvements. Assessed in written form on the papers as well as in the investigation, which means it can be taught and practised without a laboratory bench.

sections.heading: Finding the afternoon a physics session can actually live on
paragraphs: Ask for the timetable, not the student's opinion. A Diploma physics student will tell you every afternoon is busy, and the timetable will show that one of them carries a single period and no practical. That afternoon is where the weekly session belongs, and locating it is a ten-minute job that most families never do because the question is never framed this way.

The specific conflicts to look for are three. A physics double period, after which a student has done two hours of the subject and is a poor candidate for a third. A timetabled practical session, which frequently overruns and which leaves the student with a write-up to begin that evening. And an after-school commitment, whether that is a science club, a sports fixture or a Creativity, Activity, Service obligation, which eats the whole window rather than part of it.

Against those, map the journey. sections.heading: The five themes, and what each one demands
paragraphs: The current IB physics syllabus is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level covers additional content within those themes rather than a separate list. Your child's teacher holds the subject guide, which is the authority on exactly what sits where, and we do not reproduce board documents, so ask for the school's copy and work from it.

What the themes demand differs more than their names suggest. Space, time and motion is largely algebraic and rewards clean free-body diagrams. The particulate nature of matter contains the circuit work, which rewards redrawing a circuit before calculating anything. Wave behaviour is where physical reasoning carries more marks than algebra, so a student who is strong at calculation and weak at explanation will look suddenly worse here.

Fields is the theme where sign conventions matter most and where students most often lose marks they have genuinely earned, by treating a minus sign as a typographical detail. Nuclear and quantum physics is usually taught last, which means it is met in DP2 under time pressure and is the commonest subject of a late tuition request. A family that knows this in September can plan for it instead of reacting in March.

For a tutoring plan the useful consequence is that a diagnosis should be theme-specific rather than general. A student is rarely weak at physics; they are weak at explanation-heavy questions, or at circuits, or at anything involving uncertainty. Two marked papers sorted by theme and by question type will usually show one dominant pattern, and a plan aimed at that pattern costs less than one aimed at the subject as a whole.

sections.heading: What each paper component actually asks
paragraphs: Diploma physics is assessed by two written papers and the scientific investigation. Paper 1 contains a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 contains structured and extended-response questions. The investigation is internally assessed against published criteria and carries 20 per cent of the final grade. For the exact weightings and durations at your child's level, use the school's copy of the subject guide rather than any website, including this one.

The component most students under-prepare is the data-analysis section of Paper 1. It asks for graph drawing and interpretation, gradient and intercept reasoning, and handling of absolute and percentage uncertainty. These are learnable procedures, they appear every series, and almost nobody practises them deliberately because they do not feel like physics. A short block on this one component is the best-value physics purchase available.

Paper 2's extended-response questions are the Higher Level discriminator. A multi-mark answer wants a chain of physical reasoning in which each step follows from the last and names a mechanism. What students write instead is three sentences restating the first in different words, which earns one mark and looks like three. Teaching the difference takes marked practice with a mark scheme open beside the attempt, which is exactly what a shared screen makes easy.

Multiple choice deserves a note of its own. It is the section students assume needs no preparation and it is where careless reading costs the most marks per minute. The useful drill is not more content but a timed set followed by a discussion of every wrong answer, asking what the distractor was designed to catch. Most students find the same two or three traps catching them repeatedly, which is a fixable pattern rather than a knowledge gap.

sections.heading: The investigation, scheduled backwards from the school's deadline
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the physics grade and the deadline that governs it is set by the school. This is the single most important scheduling fact in Diploma physics, because every other science subject sets one too and the Extended Essay sits in the same stretch of the calendar. Three internal deadlines in one fortnight is a routine occurrence and a predictable one, and the fix is to ask for all of them in September.

Working backwards is straightforward once the date is known. A complete draft should exist two to three weeks before the deadline, so that feedback can be acted on rather than merely received. Data collection has to finish before that, which means the method and the apparatus reasoning must be settled earlier still, and the research question earlier than that. A question chosen two weeks before the deadline produces a report that cannot score well whatever the student does with it.

The two expensive failures are both avoidable at the planning stage. The first is a research question too broad to answer with available equipment, which produces data that cannot support a conclusion. The second is uncertainty treatment planned after the data is collected, which usually means it cannot be done properly at all. Both are conversations rather than lessons, and both belong at the start where they are cheap.

The boundary here is absolute. A tutor may discuss the research question, explain each criterion, model a comparable investigation on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of it. The report is declared as the student's own work and moderated by the IB, so the consequence of anything else lands on your child, not on whoever was paid.

sections.heading: Where physics marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of it, and only one is about not knowing physics. The first is units and standard form. A student computes correctly, writes the number, and omits or mismatches the unit, or leaves an answer in the wrong power of ten. This is an arithmetic and habit problem, it appears in every theme, and it is fixed by marked practice in which the unit is checked explicitly every single time.

The second is compressed working. A multi-step calculation written as two lines cannot be awarded method marks, because the method is not visible. Students do this to save time and lose more than they save. Teaching a standard layout, formula written out, substitution shown, answer with unit, takes one session and pays back across both papers for two years.

The third is explanation that names no mechanism. An extended-response question asking why something happens wants a causal chain. What arrives is a description of what happens, three times. This is the Higher Level discriminator and the hardest of the four to fix, because it requires the student to be shown the mark scheme repeatedly until they can see which of their sentences earned nothing.

The fourth is uncertainty, which sits in both the data-analysis section and the investigation and is the most neglected skill in the subject. Absolute uncertainty, percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and what an uncertainty implies about a conclusion. None of it is conceptually hard and almost none of it is practised deliberately. For most students a four-session block here moves more marks than four sessions on any theme.

sections.heading: Practical skills without a laboratory bench
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how practical work can be supported when the tutor is not in the room. The answer is that most of the practical marks in Diploma physics are awarded for reasoning that is expressed in writing, not for manipulating apparatus. Choosing an appropriate instrument, identifying systematic versus random error, explaining why a measurement was repeated, suggesting a specific improvement rather than a generic one: all of that is taught and practised on paper.

The laboratory itself belongs to the school, and it should. Your child has access to equipment, to a teacher who knows it, and to technicians who maintain it. A tutor who offered to replicate that would be offering something worse than what the student already has. What a tutor adds is the thinking either side of the bench: designing the investigation properly before it runs, and interpreting the data honestly afterwards.

Data analysis is where online delivery is genuinely superior. A student's graph can be shown on screen and annotated, the line of best fit discussed, the gradient computed and its units reasoned about, and the uncertainty bars drawn in while both people watch. Done across a table, the tutor is reading a graph upside down and pointing at it from the wrong side, which is a surprisingly large practical difference.

One honest limitation. A student who has not actually used the apparatus will write about it less convincingly than one who has, and no amount of tutoring substitutes for having done the practical. If your child is skipping laboratory sessions, that is the problem to solve first, and it is a conversation with the school rather than a purchase from us.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level, and what follows from it
paragraphs: Higher Level physics covers additional content within the same five themes and demands more extended written reasoning. It is the extended-response demand rather than the extra content that catches students, because the content can be learned and the reasoning habit has to be built. A student who is comfortable with Standard Level calculation and uncomfortable writing a four-sentence causal explanation will find Higher Level harder than the syllabus difference suggests.

The consequence of the choice sits in university admissions, and requirements are set by individual institutions and courses rather than by any general rule. Engineering, physics and some computer science programmes commonly specify Higher Level physics or a Higher Level science. Medicine and life sciences usually specify chemistry and biology instead. The reliable method is to read the admissions page for the specific course in the specific year and to involve the school's university counsellor early.

For UAE routes, Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate matter from a university's own entry requirements. For the British track, the sourced requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the IB Diploma we publish no points figure, because none has been read on an official Ministry source.

The tutoring consequence is about timing rather than about level. If Higher Level physics is required by a target course, the money belongs in DP1 building the reasoning habit while there is time for it to become automatic. If it is not required, Higher Level physics chosen for its appearance on a transcript will consume tutoring hours for two years and deliver nothing that needed to be delivered. Ask before the choice is locked.

intro.heading: Five themes, two papers, and a subject that assumes the mathematics
paragraphs: The current IB physics course is organised into five themes covering motion and spacetime, the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields, and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds depth inside each theme rather than a separate body of content, which has a useful consequence: a Higher Level gap sits inside familiar territory rather than outside it. The IB revised this guide in recent years, so the first thing to establish with the school is which guide your child's cohort follows, because older resources describe a different structure with an extra paper and option topics.

A physics grade is a pattern across those themes rather than a single level of ability. A student at a 4 is almost never weak in all five. They are usually secure in two, workable in two, and carrying one theme that collapses under examination conditions, with technique losses layered on top. Fields is the theme that most often collapses, and within it the circuit material rather than the field concepts. Identifying which theme and which kind of loss takes one session with a marked script, and it determines everything after it.

The subject also assumes a quantity of mathematics that is rarely stated. Rearranging a multi-variable expression under time pressure, handling indices and standard form, reading and constructing logarithmic plots, propagating uncertainty through a product, and resolving vectors are all prerequisites rather than content. A student who is secure in the physics and insecure in those will produce a script that looks like a physics problem and is not one, and will be given physics teaching that does not touch it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-harbour.subjectsIntro: These are the themes and adjacent subjects we match physics tutors for. Each entry names what the theme contains, what Higher Level adds, and the failure that characterises it.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and spacetime
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum, work, energy and circular motion, with relativity content at Higher Level. The characteristic loss is a free-body diagram drawn with unlabelled or missing forces, after which correct algebra is applied to a configuration the examiner cannot verify.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws and the kinetic model, extended at Higher Level. Marks go on failing to state the assumption in use and on mixing temperature scales mid-calculation, both of which are mechanical and both of which survive untouched into DP2.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave properties, superposition, standing waves and interference, with further diffraction and resolution work at Higher Level. Path-difference arguments asserted rather than shown, and phase relationships described in words where a diagram would have earned the mark, dominate the losses.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits and electromagnetic induction, with substantial Higher Level extension into field strength, potential and energy. Circuits redrawn incorrectly before any analysis is the single most expensive habit in the whole subject.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactivity, nuclear reactions and energy, the photoelectric effect and quantum ideas, extended at Higher Level. Students handle the concepts and lose marks on orders of magnitude and unit prefixes, because the scales are unfamiliar enough that an error of a thousand looks plausible.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and data analysis
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation, gradient uncertainty read from error bars, and what a line of best fit does and does not justify. Examinable in the data-based questions and scored again in the investigation, which makes it the most efficient block in the subject.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation carrying roughly a fifth of the grade, marked on criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Its internal deadline is set by the school and is the earliest hard date in the subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion at Higher Level. Multi-variable rearrangement under time pressure, indices and standard form, and logarithmic plotting are shared ground, so a physics calculation problem is frequently a mathematics problem in a physics question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken alongside physics by students heading towards engineering or medicine. The shared skills are uncertainty treatment, graph interpretation and the structure of an evaluation, so investigation coaching in one subject usually improves the other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Physics supplies unusually strong TOK material, because questions about models, measurement, and what counts as evidence for an unobservable entity are genuinely open. A physics tutor can help find examples that withstand scrutiny rather than examples that sound impressive.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level adds to each
paragraphs: Treating physics as one subject is the commonest planning error, because the five themes fail independently and for different reasons. Motion and spacetime fails on representation: a free-body diagram with unlabelled forces cannot be credited however sound the reasoning behind it. The particulate nature of matter fails on unstated assumptions and mixed temperature scales. Wave behaviour fails on arguments asserted rather than shown. Fields fails on circuits redrawn incorrectly. Nuclear and quantum fails on orders of magnitude rather than on concepts.

Higher Level adds depth inside each of those rather than new territory, which is strategically useful. A Higher Level student struggling with fields is struggling with an extension of material they already meet, so the repair starts from something familiar rather than from scratch. It also means the Higher Level extension content is where a genuine level problem shows itself: a student who handles the shared material confidently and fails specifically on extension questions is giving you real information about the level choice.

The practical request to make of any physics tutor is for a theme-level diagnosis with the error type attached. A student losing marks evenly across all five themes has a technique problem rather than five content problems, and the fortnight on diagrams, prefixes and command terms will move more marks than any theme revision. A student whose losses concentrate in one theme has a content gap, and the sessions should go there. Those two plans look identical from a grade and opposite from a script.

sections.heading: Two papers, two different examinations
paragraphs: The written assessment splits into a paper combining multiple choice with data analysis and a paper of extended response. Those are not two samples of the same skill. Multiple choice rewards speed, elimination and recognising a distractor; a student who works each option from first principles runs out of time rather than out of knowledge. Data analysis rewards uncertainty technique, graph reading and the discipline of saying what a gradient physically represents. Extended response rewards structure, command-term discipline and the stamina to sustain an argument across several marks.

Preparing for them together is why generic revision so often moves neither. A student weak on multiple choice needs timed sets with elimination practised explicitly, not more content. A student weak on data questions needs the uncertainty block, which is finite and mechanical. A student weak on extended response needs to write answers and mark them against the scheme repeatedly, which is uncomfortable and effective. Three different blocks, three different measures.

Higher Level sits longer versions of both papers, which adds a stamina dimension that is genuinely trainable. Students who have never sat a full-length paper in one sitting before the mock discover that their accuracy falls in the final third, and that is a practice problem rather than a knowledge one. Two or three full papers under genuine timing fix it. Confirm the current paper structure and weightings with your child's teacher, because the IB revises subject guides and an older resource will describe a different arrangement.

sections.heading: The mathematics physics assumes and does not teach
paragraphs: This is the most under-diagnosed problem in Diploma physics. The course assumes a set of mathematical skills as prerequisites: rearranging a multi-variable expression quickly and correctly, handling indices and standard form without hesitation, resolving vectors along chosen axes, reading and constructing a logarithmic plot, and propagating uncertainty through products and powers. None of those is taught as physics content and all of them are required constantly.

A student who is secure in the physics and insecure in those will produce scripts that look like physics failures. The explanation is right and the final number is wrong because the rearrangement went astray. The reasoning is sound and the answer is out by a factor of a thousand because a prefix was mishandled. The method is correct and the vector was resolved along the wrong axis. Give that student more physics teaching and nothing changes, because the physics was never the problem.

The diagnosis is straightforward: hand the student five pure rearrangement tasks with no physics context and time them. If they are slow or inaccurate, the mathematics block comes before any theme work, and it is four to six sessions rather than a term. This is also why we ask which mathematics course a physics student takes, because a student in Applications at Standard Level carrying Physics at Higher Level is very likely to need this block and is rarely offered it.

One further sign worth watching for. A student who checks their answer against the expected order of magnitude catches most prefix errors themselves, and a student who never does will keep making them however many times they are corrected. Installing the habit of a written magnitude estimate before any calculation is cheap, dull and removes a whole category of loss.

sections.heading: Command terms, and why a correct explanation scores four
paragraphs: Physics extended responses are capped by their command term in exactly the way every other Diploma subject is, and physics students are the least likely to have been told so. State wants the fact. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants a mechanism, with the causal step made visible. Determine and calculate want working. Discuss and evaluate want a judgement with both sides. A student who writes a thorough description where explain was printed has written a correct answer to a different question.

In physics there is an additional trap. Many questions want the explanation to proceed through a named physical principle, and an answer that reaches the right conclusion by a different route may not collect the marks, because the mark scheme is awarding the steps rather than the destination. That is why writing the principle being used as the first line of an answer is such a reliable habit: it earns a mark and it forces the student to choose a route deliberately rather than arriving at an answer by familiarity.

The repair is two or three sessions and it is permanent. Take a dozen past extended-response questions, identify the command term and the principle each one expects, write what each demands before writing any physics, then compare the answer against the structure of the mark scheme rather than its exact wording. Students who do this stop producing long answers to short questions, which also recovers time for the questions at the end of the paper that were previously left blank.
bullets: Explain wants a mechanism; describing it thoroughly does not substitute

sections.heading: Fields, and the habit that costs most in the whole subject
paragraphs: If one theme deserves separate treatment it is fields, and within it the circuit material. The conceptual content is manageable: potential difference, current, resistance, series and parallel combinations, internal resistance and induction. The losses come from a redrawing error. A student reads a circuit, redraws it to work with, gets the topology wrong, and then performs an impeccable analysis of a circuit that was not on the paper. The marks disappear and nothing in the working reveals why.

The repair is a drawing discipline rather than a teaching one. Redraw the circuit, label every component, mark the direction of conventional current, and identify which components are genuinely in series and which in parallel before writing any equation. Students resist this because it feels slow, and it is strictly faster than the alternative, which is a correct calculation of the wrong thing. Two sessions of enforcement usually install it, and the gain shows up immediately because circuit questions appear on every paper.

Induction adds a second, separate loss: sign conventions and the direction of an induced effect, which students handle by memorising a rule and then misapplying it when the geometry changes. Teaching it from the underlying reasoning rather than from a mnemonic takes longer and survives an unfamiliar configuration, which is what the paper supplies. At Higher Level the field strength, potential and energy material adds algebraic demand on top, which is where the mathematics block often becomes necessary.

At Standard Level the same circuit discipline applies with less algebra on top, which makes it an even faster repair. It is worth doing before anything else in the theme, because every later topic in fields assumes the student can read a circuit correctly.

sections.heading: The investigation as a scheduled component
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries roughly a fifth of the physics grade and behaves like a deadline rather than like content, which means it has to be scheduled rather than revised. It is marked on criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and because the marks are spread across those areas it is lost in pieces: a workable question with too little data, good data with a two-line evaluation, or a conclusion the data does not support.

Two interventions carry most of the available benefit and both happen early. The first is a feasibility check before the research question is fixed: does the school have the apparatus, and will the planned measurements produce enough points to establish a relationship? The second is drafting the evaluation while the method is still fresh rather than weeks later, because a real evaluation names specific limitations of the student's own procedure and distinguishes random from systematic effects, and that detail is not reconstructable from memory.

The boundary is firm throughout. A tutor may test the feasibility of a question, explain what each criterion requires, question the data handling, ask whether the conclusion follows, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the experiment, supply or process data, or write any part of the report. Invented data is a malpractice matter in itself, and one page researched for this market sells completed internal assessments outright, which puts the student's whole Diploma at risk.
bullets: Schedule it against the school's internal deadline, not around revision
Check apparatus and data volume before the question is fixed
Draft the evaluation while the method is fresh, not weeks later
A tutor questions and gives feedback; the student does all the work

sections.heading: What the first month of physics support should show
paragraphs: Session one should produce a written diagnosis: lost marks sorted by theme and by error type, with a judgement about whether the dominant problem is content, representation, mathematics or command terms. That document is the plan and the family should be able to read it. A tutor who finishes the first session having explained a topic well but produced no such breakdown will go on improving content knowledge while the grade holds, which is the commonest outcome in this subject.

By the end of week two the diagram discipline should be visible without prompting: forces labelled, circuits redrawn and annotated, axes chosen explicitly. By week four, the same question types that were failing should be answered correctly on unfamiliar examples. By week six the student should sit a timed component, mark it strictly against the official scheme, and predict their own total within a few marks, with the tutor auditing the marking rather than simply providing it.

If those markers do not appear, the diagnosis was wrong, the format is not suiting the student, or the work between sessions is not happening, and all three are better raised in week three than at the end of a term. We would rather change a tutor or a plan early than defend either. Physics in particular rewards problem sets done between sessions: an hour a week can direct those hours and cannot replace them.

The documents matter as much as the sessions. Keep the written breakdown and the marked papers in one place, because a new tutor handed that folder starts where the last one finished rather than spending an hour rediscovering it.

sections.heading: Booking a physics specialist from Dubai Harbour
paragraphs: Send the level, which subject guide the school is following, which mathematics course the student takes, the most recent marked paper, the investigation deadline, and the hours that genuinely exist after a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30. The mathematics course is the item families never think to include and it frequently changes the first block, because a Higher Level physics student in a lighter mathematics course often needs the rearrangement work before any theme work.

We match a tutor who teaches physics at that level and propose a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, with investigation work placed at weekends where ninety uninterrupted minutes exist. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing a written breakdown by theme and error type with estimates against each. If the match is wrong after the trial or in week two, we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist.

The limits, plainly. Higher Level physics specialists at popular evening hours are among the scarcest matches we make, and when nobody suitable is free we will say so and offer a weekend slot or a defined short block rather than substituting a tutor whose depth is in another science. We cannot promise a grade and nobody who has marked a physics paper would. And the problem sets between sessions are the student's work, which no arrangement can do for them.

If the enquiry is urgent because a deadline is close, say so in the first line. A deadline in three weeks changes which block we propose and sometimes changes whether we take the work at all, and we would rather say that at the outset.

faqs.question: Which physics theme should we work on first?
faqs.answer: Whichever the marked script says, and the answer is usually fields rather than the theme the student finds most intimidating. Fields contains the circuit material, where the dominant loss is a redrawing error rather than a conceptual gap: a student reads a circuit, redraws it wrongly, and performs an impeccable analysis of a circuit that was not on the paper. That repairs in about two sessions of drawing discipline and pays on every subsequent paper, which makes it unusually good value.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics and still score 4?
faqs.answer: Because understanding is not what the papers award. They award a labelled diagram, a laid-out calculation, a named principle, and an answer matched to the command term. A student who can explain a situation fluently and draws three unlabelled forces gives the examiner nothing to credit. The pattern is visible in a marked script in minutes: correct reasoning, correct conclusion, missing representation. It repairs in a fortnight and no amount of further explanation touches it.

faqs.question: What if the physics is understood and the numbers keep coming out wrong?
faqs.answer: Very often, and it is the most under-diagnosed issue in the subject. The course assumes multi-variable rearrangement under time pressure, indices and standard form, vector resolution, logarithmic plotting and uncertainty propagation as prerequisites and teaches none of them. Hand the student five pure rearrangement tasks with no physics context and time them. If they are slow or inaccurate, a four to six session mathematics block comes before any theme work, because more physics teaching will not change those scripts.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level actually add to each theme?
faqs.answer: Depth inside the same five themes rather than separate territory: relativity content in motion and spacetime, further thermodynamic treatment in the particulate theme, additional diffraction and resolution work in waves, field strength, potential and energy in fields, and further nuclear and quantum depth. That structure is strategically useful, because a Higher Level gap sits inside familiar material. It also means failure concentrated specifically in extension questions is genuine evidence about the level choice.

faqs.question: How should multiple-choice questions be practised?
faqs.answer: In timed sets, with elimination practised explicitly rather than by working each option from first principles. A student who derives every option runs out of time rather than out of knowledge, and the paper is designed with distractors that reward recognising a plausible-looking error. Track two measures: questions per minute, and which themes the errors cluster in. The second tells you where content work is needed and the first tells you whether the problem was ever content.

faqs.question: Is the uncertainty work really worth separate sessions?
faqs.answer: It is the most efficient block available in physics, because the skills are finite and they score twice. Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through sums, products and powers, gradient uncertainty read from error bars, and what a line of best fit justifies are examinable in the data questions and scored again in the investigation's analysis criterion. Many schools teach uncertainty as a formatting rule applied at the end, which is exactly why those marks are so often recoverable.

faqs.question: Why do extended-response marks stay low when the content is known?
faqs.answer: Command terms, and in physics a second trap alongside them. Explain wants a mechanism with the causal step visible, and a thorough description does not substitute. Many schemes also award the steps rather than the destination, so an answer that reaches the right conclusion by an unexpected route may collect little. Writing the physical principle being used as the first line earns a mark and forces a deliberate route, and two or three sessions on this hold for the rest of the course.

faqs.question: When should the scientific investigation be coached?
faqs.answer: Before the research question is fixed, which is eight to ten weeks before the school's internal deadline in most cases. The two interventions that carry most of the benefit are a feasibility check on apparatus and expected data volume, and drafting the evaluation while the method is still fresh. Coaching that starts at the draft stage can improve communication and cannot rescue a design that could never have produced enough data to support a conclusion.

faqs.question: Does a tired student's physics script look different?
faqs.answer: Noticeably, and it misleads tutors who were not watching the working. Physics problems are multi-step, so an error in step two is invisible until step five, and a fatigued student generates arithmetic and transcription slips that read as conceptual confusion. From this district, where children leave before 07:00 and return after 15:30, a session before 17:00 produces exactly that script. Choosing the hour honestly is worth more than choosing the tutor carefully and hoping.

faqs.question: How many full papers should a Higher Level student sit before the mock?
faqs.answer: Two or three, in one sitting each, under genuine timing. Higher Level papers are long enough that accuracy falls in the final third for students who have never experienced the duration, and that is a practice problem rather than a knowledge one. Sitting a full paper also reveals pacing: count the marks left unattempted on the last page, because that number is invisible in a percentage and is frequently the largest single loss on the script.

faqs.question: Is one appointment enough for Physics HL and Analysis HL together?
faqs.answer: Only where that person genuinely teaches both at the required level, which is less common than it sounds. The overlap is real, so a tutor who teaches Analysis at Higher Level and Physics at Higher Level to a Diploma standard is a legitimate single appointment and can be efficient. What does not work is a physics specialist taking the mathematics because the family asked. Ask which components of each subject they have taught at that level and expect two names if the answer is vague.

faqs.question: What if the losses are spread evenly across all five themes?
faqs.answer: Then it is almost certainly technique rather than five content gaps, and the plan should be a fortnight on representation, prefixes and command terms rather than a tour of the syllabus. Evenly spread losses are the clearest signal available that the content is broadly present and the marks are being lost in how answers are constructed. A tutor who responds to that script with a theme-by-theme revision programme has not read it carefully.

faqs.question: How do we prepare for practical work if lessons are over video?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work happens at school and the examinable skills around it are written. Apparatus choice, sources of error, uncertainty treatment, graph construction and the structure of an evaluation are all taught on paper, and a shared page lets a tutor watch a graph being drawn and intervene when an error bar is wrong. What video cannot do is handle apparatus for a student, which matters for younger children and very little for a Diploma candidate.

faqs.question: Which subject guide is our school using?
faqs.answer: Ask the physics teacher directly; they will answer in a sentence. The IB revised the physics guide in recent years, and older revision books describe a different structure with an additional paper and option topics. A student working from one of those will spend hours on material that is no longer examined and will arrive at the paper expecting a component that does not exist. This is the single cheapest check available and it is rarely made.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-hills-es.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below is listed against a level rather than a subject group. A Physics HL student who cannot rearrange an equation and a Physics SL student whose investigation has no usable data range need different people, and matching to general science is how this goes wrong in a thin specialist market.

intro.heading: Physics does not get harder at Diploma; the maths inside it does
paragraphs: The most common physics story in this corridor runs like this. A student takes an 8 or a 9 in IGCSE Physics, chooses it at Higher Level because they enjoyed it, and by the second term of the first Diploma year is sitting somewhere between a 3 and a 5 with no obvious explanation. The school says they need to work harder. The student says they understand the lessons. Both are usually telling the truth, and the diagnosis is almost always the same: the physics is fine and the mathematics inside it has outrun them.

Diploma physics asks for algebraic rearrangement as a reflex, for logarithms where IGCSE asked for substitution, for uncertainty propagated through a calculation rather than mentioned at the end, and for a graph treated as a source of a gradient with units rather than as a picture of a trend. None of that is physics content and all of it is assessed inside physics questions. A tutor who responds to a 4 by re-teaching Theme A will produce a student who knows kinematics better and still scores a 4, because the loss was never in the kinematics.

This page compares Dubai Hills Estate with the communities around it, because that is what the brief for this page is, and because the comparison produces an unexpectedly clear result. Dubai Hills Estate is as close as any Dubai villa community gets to the campuses that teach Diploma physics. The resident population is large and well qualified. If a local Physics HL tutor market existed anywhere in the emirate it would exist here. It does not, in any reliable sense, and the reason is arithmetic: there are not many people who have taught Physics HL, and the ones who have are not distributed by neighbourhood.

What the comparison does usefully is separate the two things parents are buying. One is logistics, and on logistics Dubai Hills Estate wins: bus runs from the Al Khail campuses often land before 15:40, which makes a 16:00 start genuine rather than optimistic, and that is earlier than Arabian Ranches, Sobha Hartland or Nad Al Sheba can manage. The other is specialism, and on specialism the four communities are indistinguishable, because the constraint is national rather than local.

So the rest of this page is physics rather than geography. The five themes of the current guide and what Higher Level adds to each. The three assessed components with their weightings and what each one rewards. The places physics marks actually go missing, which are more repeatable than most parents expect. The Higher Level against Standard Level decision and its last sensible moment. The mathematics pairing that decides university routes. The investigation, criterion by criterion. What the market charges, with every figure attributed. And a plain statement of how lessons are delivered.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-hills-es.programmesIntro: Physics support is useful at four distinct points, and the right intervention at each is different enough that treating them as one service produces the wrong plan. These are the four stages families in this corridor ask about.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, the physics strand
programmes.description: Physics appears inside an integrated sciences course marked against four criteria out of 8, so there is no physics grade to compare against a later Diploma one. The habits that decide a Diploma physics grade are built here: writing a method that could be repeated, quoting a measurement with its uncertainty, and explaining a relationship rather than describing a shape. A student arriving in the first Diploma year able to describe a graph but not extract a gradient is carrying an MYP criterion gap.

Both arrive at the same Diploma classroom, and the two cohorts have different gaps, which is why the first session with a new student is diagnostic rather than instructional.

programmes.name: IB Physics SL
programmes.description: The same five themes as Higher Level at reduced depth, with shorter papers under the current guide. Standard Level physics is frequently taken because a target course asks for a science rather than because the student chose physics, which changes the tutoring: less extension, more securing of the reliably available marks. Definitions quoted precisely, equations selected from the data booklet quickly, units carried through, and graphs read for a gradient rather than a trend.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of Standard Level physics students in this corridor are aiming at engineering foundation, architecture or computer science routes at UAE and overseas universities. Those published entry requirements differ by institution and by intake, so read the current page for the specific programme rather than relying on what a sibling needed two years ago.

programmes.name: IB Physics HL
programmes.description: Higher Level extends every theme rather than adding a sixth, with additional depth in fields, in nuclear and quantum physics and in the quantitative treatment throughout. The papers are materially longer, so stamina becomes a real variable rather than an afterthought. The commonest Higher Level profile in this corridor is a capable student whose algebraic fluency has not kept pace, and the fix is mathematical before it is physical.
programmes.countryNote: Physics HL is the science we are asked for most often from the Al Khail corridor and the one with the thinnest specialist supply anywhere in Dubai, which is why hiring by distance from Dubai Hills Estate fails so reliably. Online delivery makes the tutor's calendar the constraint instead of their commute, and we say plainly when an early weekday slot cannot be covered.

programmes.name: The physics investigation and a physics Extended Essay
programmes.description: The scientific investigation is a fifth of the grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each, and it depends on laboratory access, which makes its school-set deadline the least movable thing in the course. A physics Extended Essay is a separate 4,000-word piece with its own supervision. Both are legitimate areas for teaching, feasibility testing and criterion-referenced marking, and neither is an area where a tutor may write anything.

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor in Dubai Hills Estate has to fix first
paragraphs: The answer, in one line: whatever the marked paper says, and it is usually mathematics rather than physics. Across the diagnostic Paper 2 scripts we mark for students in this corridor, the largest single category of lost marks is not a physics misconception. It is algebraic rearrangement attempted and abandoned, logarithms avoided, units dropped between lines, uncertainty quoted once and never carried, and gradients read off a graph without units or with the axes misidentified. A student can hold a correct mental model of a field and lose every mark in the question.

That is why the first session is diagnostic and why the plan is written after it rather than before. A school report saying physics is a 4 does not say which 4 it is. A student scoring 42% on Paper 2 might have full marks on every short-answer recall item and nothing on anything multi-step, or the reverse, and those two profiles need opposite interventions. The mark total averages them into one number that hides the information you are paying to act on. Marking a full paper question by question against the published scheme is the only reliable way to see it.

The second thing to establish early is level suitability, honestly. Higher Level physics is a two-year commitment made at 16 on the strength of an IGCSE grade that tested different skills. Some students in this corridor should move to Standard Level, and the moment to decide that is the end of the first Diploma year, on two or three pieces of marked evidence, rather than in the spring of the second year under pressure. A tutor who will not raise that conversation is selling hours rather than advice, and the conversation costs them money to have.

The third is the investigation, because it is the only part of the grade that is on a fixed external clock and the only part that cannot be recovered late. It depends on laboratory access, a research question approved by the school, and data collected in a window the school controls. A student in the spring of the second year with no approved research question is in a materially worse position than a student with weak paper marks and an approved question, even though both describe themselves as behind in physics.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what Higher Level adds to each
paragraphs: The current DP Physics guide organises the course into five themes: A, space, time and motion; B, the particulate nature of matter; C, wave behaviour; D, fields; and E, nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level extends each of those rather than adding a sixth, which is the single most useful structural fact a parent can hold, because it explains a phenomenon families find baffling. A Higher Level student with a Standard Level weakness does not lose Higher Level marks. They lose the same mark twice, once in the shared question and again in the extension built on top of it.

The practical consequence is that Higher Level remediation almost always has to go backwards before it goes forwards. A tutor who begins at the Higher Level material because that is what the student asked for will produce two months of apparent progress followed by a mock result that has not moved, because the foundation underneath the extension was never repaired. Parents reasonably find this frustrating to hear and it is cheaper to hear it in October than to discover it in February.

Theme D, fields, is the theme that costs this corridor the most marks, and the reason is specific rather than general. Fields require a student to hold an abstract model and to manipulate inverse-square relationships algebraically at the same time, and students who can do either separately frequently cannot do both at once under time pressure. Theme E compounds it, because nuclear and quantum physics asks for the same algebraic confidence applied to quantities whose magnitudes offer no intuition to check an answer against.

One rule about materials, because this is where families most often get caught out. IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are the IB's copyright. We reference them, cite them and work from the student's own legitimately obtained copies through the school. We do not reproduce or distribute them, and a tutoring service offering a downloadable pack of IB physics papers is distributing material it does not own. Ask where a tutor's practice material comes from; the answer tells you something.
