sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: what each component rewards
paragraphs: Under the current guide, DP Physics is assessed by Paper 1 at 36%, Paper 2 at 44% and the scientific investigation at 20%, at both levels. Paper 1 is in two parts: Paper 1A is multiple choice and Paper 1B is data analysis set on the experimental programme, which means it tests the practical work the student has actually done rather than content recall. Paper 2 is short and extended response. Confirm the current durations and the exact split with your child's Diploma coordinator, because assessment detail is revised between guide cycles.

Paper 1B is the component with the widest gap between what it is worth and how much it is practised, and physics is the subject where that gap is widest of all. Students arrive having worked through large numbers of multiple-choice items and almost no data-analysis questions, because data questions are slow to self-mark and schools under time pressure set what can be marked quickly. The result is a student who can recall every equation and cannot extract a gradient from a graph whose axes are scaled awkwardly.

Paper 2 is where command terms and working discipline decide the grade. State, outline, describe, explain, determine, deduce and discuss each carry a mark allocation shaped to them, and in physics there is a second layer: marks for method survive a wrong final answer only if the method is written down. A student who does the algebra on a calculator and writes one number has thrown away the recoverable marks. Teaching that habit is a handful of sessions and it is the highest-return item on most physics plans.

Stamina is a genuine variable at Higher Level because the papers are materially longer, and a student who has only ever practised in thirty-minute blocks loses marks in the final third to fatigue rather than to physics. Three full-length timed papers before the session is the minimum that fixes it, and it is the part of a plan families most often drop, because a two-and-a-half-hour paper on a school night is hard to schedule in a household that already commutes twice a day.

sections.heading: Where the physics specialists actually sit, community by community
paragraphs: This is the comparison this page exists to make, so here is the honest version of it. Across the four communities in the table, session start times vary by roughly an hour, driven entirely by how long the bus loop is. Physics HL specialist availability does not vary at all. Al Barsha South, which has campuses inside the district, is no better supplied than Arabian Ranches, which is twenty-five minutes out. Dubai Hills Estate, which should be the strongest case for hiring locally anywhere in Dubai, is not better supplied either.

The reason is arithmetic rather than geography. Physics HL is taught by a small number of people in any city, and in Dubai that number is small in absolute terms. Narrowing it to those willing to drive to a specific villa community on a specific weekday evening does not produce a shortlist; it usually produces nobody, or it produces a capable general science tutor presented as a physics specialist. That second outcome is the one families should worry about, because it is invisible for about six weeks.

Where Dubai Hills Estate genuinely wins is timing, and for physics specifically that is worth more than it sounds. Higher Level physics needs full-length timed papers, and a full-length Paper 2 does not fit into a 17:30 start on a school night. A community whose buses land before 15:40 can run a ninety-minute session at 16:00 and still have an evening left, which means the hard practice happens on weekdays rather than being pushed entirely into weekends. That is a real operational advantage and it is the only one in the table.

The practical conclusion is to invert the usual search. Instead of filtering by distance and then asking about physics, filter by physics and then ask about timing. The question that discriminates is narrow: which level have you taught, for how many cohorts, and will you mark one of my child's Paper 2 scripts against the published scheme and return it with the loss pattern named. That last request costs a tutor an hour and tells you more than any amount of reading profiles.

sections.heading: Where physics marks actually go missing
paragraphs: The losses repeat with unusual consistency in physics, more than in chemistry or biology, and almost none of them are conceptual. The largest is method not written down: a student performs a three-step calculation on a calculator, writes one number, gets it wrong and scores zero where the mark scheme would have given two or three for the method. That is not a physics problem and it is fixable in two sessions, and it recovers marks on every paper the student sits afterwards.

The second is units and prefixes. Millimetres entered as metres, kilojoules treated as joules, kelvin and celsius interchanged in a gas law, a density in grams per cubic centimetre used in an equation expecting kilograms per cubic metre. Each individual instance looks like carelessness. Collectively, across a paper, they are a substantial share of the loss at Standard Level, and treating them as a skill with its own checklist and its own practice is what closes them.

The third is uncertainty, which students treat as a formality attached to the end of a practical and which the assessment treats as part of the reasoning. An uncertainty quoted in a raw data table and then dropped from the processed values is an inconsistency a marker can see immediately and a student cannot, because they have read their own work five times. In Paper 1B the same skill appears as error bars and as the question of whether a gradient is actually supported by the spread of points.

The fourth is the gradient itself, which deserves naming separately because it is the most physics-specific of the set. A graph in a Diploma physics question is a source of a quantity with units, not a picture of a trend, and that quantity is frequently the answer. Students who were rewarded at IGCSE for describing a shape are penalised at Diploma for not extracting a value, and the transition between those two expectations is unmarked and untaught. It is the clearest single thing a physics tutor can fix in the first month.

sections.heading: Physics HL or Physics SL, and the last sensible moment to change
paragraphs: The level decision is taken at 16 on the strength of an IGCSE grade that tested different skills, and it is revisited more often than families expect. The table compares the two routes across the things that actually differ, because the usual framing, that Higher Level is harder, is true and useless. What matters is which differences bite for a particular student: the longer papers, the extended quantitative treatment, the deeper fields and quantum work, and the fact that a Standard Level weakness costs a Higher Level student the mark twice.

The honest case for moving down is specific rather than general. A student whose marked evidence shows the extension content is consistently out of reach, and whose target university courses do not require Higher Level physics, is usually better served at Standard Level, where the same five themes are assessed at a depth they can secure. Their total points often rise, and the two hours a week they get back go into a subject that is closer to a threshold. That is an arithmetic argument rather than a concession.

The honest case against moving down is equally specific. Some published entry requirements for engineering, physics and some medical routes name Higher Level physics, and dropping it closes those doors in a way that is hard to reopen. The research method is to read the current page for the specific programme at the specific institution rather than to reason from what a sibling needed. That research takes an evening and it is the input the decision actually requires.

The timing is set by the school rather than by the IB, and it is the part families miss. There is a last date on which a level change can be processed, it differs between campuses in this corridor, and it is usually earlier than parents assume. Ask for it in writing at the end of the first Diploma year, before the question is urgent. A decision taken calmly in June on three pieces of marked evidence is a different decision from the same one taken in February with a mock result in hand.

sections.heading: The mathematics pairing that decides where physics can take a student
paragraphs: Physics at Diploma level is partly a mathematics course, and the choice of mathematics route is therefore a physics decision as much as a maths one. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-led and rewards manipulation; Applications and Interpretation is statistics-led and calculator-heavy. Both are legitimate courses. The practical difference for a physics student is that the algebraic fluency Higher Level physics assumes is developed systematically in Analysis and Approaches and only partially in Applications and Interpretation.

That produces the single most common structural mismatch we see in this corridor: a student taking Physics HL with Applications and Interpretation SL, struggling with the physics, and being tutored in physics. They need the algebra. A tutor who treats the symptom teaches more fields questions to a student who cannot rearrange an inverse-square relationship, and the grade does not move. A tutor who treats the cause spends three weeks on rearrangement, logarithms and identities inside physics questions, and the grade does.

The university dimension matters and should be researched rather than assumed. Some published engineering and physics entry requirements name Analysis and Approaches specifically rather than accepting either mathematics route, and some name Higher Level rather than Standard. Requirements differ by institution and by intake and they change, so the only reliable method is to read the current page for the specific programme. Tutoring is not required for university admission, and any suggestion that an admissions process depends on buying hours is false urgency.

The decision window is the same as the level decision: the end of the first Diploma year, taken on marked evidence, with the school's last date for a change established in writing beforehand. The table pairs the common combinations with what each one makes easy and hard. It is deliberately blunt, because the vague version of this advice is what produces students discovering in the second year that their two subject choices do not support each other.

sections.heading: The physics investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: A fifth of the physics grade is one independent investigation, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. No competitor page in this market names a single criterion or its mark allocation, which is odd given that this is the part of the grade a student has months of control over. In physics specifically the investigation has a failure mode that is more mechanical than in the other sciences, and it is almost always visible at the proposal stage if anyone looks.

The failure is range. A physics investigation lives or dies on whether the independent variable can be varied enough, across enough levels, with enough repeats, to produce a graph with a measurable gradient. A student measuring a period against three closely spaced lengths will produce three points that could be joined by any number of lines, and no amount of careful writing afterwards rescues an analysis with nothing to analyse. The useful intervention is a ten-minute feasibility conversation before any apparatus is touched: what is your range, how many levels, how many repeats, and what will the gradient be if your hypothesis holds.

Data analysis and conclusion reward consistency above sophistication. Raw data with units in the column headings, uncertainty quoted and then carried into every processed value, one worked example of the processing shown in full, a graph with correctly scaled axes and error bars, and a gradient extracted with its units and its own uncertainty. The conclusion then has to stay inside what that gradient supports. Students lose marks for claiming a relationship their spread of points does not establish, which is a reasoning error rather than a physics one.

Evaluation is six marks and is routinely treated as a closing paragraph. Listing human error is worth nothing. Naming a specific methodological limitation, stating the direction in which it would have skewed the result, and proposing a realistic improvement is worth the band. The boundary on all of it is firm: a tutor tests feasibility, teaches technique, explains what a descriptor asks for and marks against the published criteria. No tutor should write the investigation, draft the conclusion or complete the coursework, and we decline those requests when they are made.

sections.heading: What Physics HL tuition costs in this corridor, and what the specialism premium is
paragraphs: Physics at Higher Level sits at the expensive end of this market for a reason that has nothing to do with branding: the number of people who have taught it is small, and scarcity prices itself. So the useful way to read a physics quote is to ask where it sits relative to the specialist band rather than relative to the cheapest band, because a rate at the bottom of the market for Higher Level physics is telling you something about who is teaching it.

The published bands, with their sources. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above an hour, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED's premium named tier reaches AED 650. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which are real services generally delivered online by university-student tutors.

Read against those numbers, a Higher Level physics quote at the budget tier is not a bargain, it is a different product. A quote in the AED 200 to 450 band is consistent with a specialist. A quote above it is consistent with scarcity, named reputation or examiner claims, and on the last of those a note of caution: a tutor should not be described as an IB or Cambridge examiner where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, and examiner status never implies access to marking, boundaries or paper content. Ask for evidence and treat vagueness as an answer.

For context on the household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for Dubai private schools for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. IB Gram publishes no rate card: a free trial lesson with the matched tutor comes first, no card details are taken beforehand, and a figure for the specific level and session length follows. Tutoring is not required for the Diploma, for equivalency, for admission or for progression.

sections.heading: How lessons reach Dubai Hills Estate, and where the honesty line sits
paragraphs: Stated plainly: IB Gram delivers tutoring to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. The phrase families type deserves an answer rather than a dodge, so here it is: if you want somebody physically present in Dubai Hills Estate, that market exists, its published rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is priced in, and we are not in it.

For Higher Level physics the online argument is as strong as it gets anywhere in this set, and it is about supply rather than price. The specialist pool is small nationally and it is not distributed by neighbourhood, so a proximity filter does not narrow it, it empties it. Removing the drive constraint makes the tutor's calendar the limit instead, which is a far weaker limit, and it means a Dubai Hills Estate student gets somebody who has taught Physics HL rather than the nearest person who has taught science.

What video delivery requires in physics is more specific than in most subjects, because physics marks live in the working. A stable connection, a device with a camera, and a way to show a handwritten page: a document camera, or a phone on a stand pointing at the desk. Without that, a student reads answers aloud and the tutor loses the ability to see where the rearrangement broke, which is the single thing they are being paid to see. It takes twenty minutes to set up and is worth doing in week one.

On academic honesty, the line is the same on physics as everywhere and the pressure arrives on a predictable date. A tutor may teach content, test whether a research question can produce a gradient, explain what a criterion descriptor asks for, mark a draft against the published descriptors, and ask the questions that expose a conclusion going beyond the data. No tutor should write the investigation, draft the Extended Essay or complete the coursework, and those requests are declined rather than negotiated, because the malpractice finding falls on the student and not on whoever helped.

process.title: Send the level, the campus and the marked paper
process.description: Higher or Standard Level, which campus, and the most recent marked physics paper you have, ideally a Paper 2. Those three decide whether a specialist is available in your window, what the realistic session start is, and whether the first month should be algebra, command terms or the investigation.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: Sixty minutes with the tutor who would teach, not a consultant and not a different person. No card details taken beforehand. The student brings one question that has been bothering them, and the session ends with a specific observation about where the marks are going rather than a general impression.

process.title: A full Paper 2 marked against the scheme
process.description: Within the first fortnight, under timing, marked question by question. This is what separates a physics gap from an algebra gap, a command-term problem and a stamina problem, which need four different plans. You get the marked script back with the loss pattern named in writing.

process.title: A written plan, with the level question addressed
process.description: Ordered by marks lost rather than by theme sequence, with Paper 1B given its own sessions and new content stopping two weeks before the target date. Where the evidence suggests a level change, the plan says so and names the school's last date for it. It arrives before the second paid session.

process.title: Fortnightly review against marked work
process.description: Checked every two weeks against evidence rather than against how sessions felt. If the diagnosis was wrong it changes. If the student has reached the point where hours are better spent on mathematics or on a different subject, we say which and why, and the hours move.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the level, not the subject group
whyPoints.description: Physics HL and general science are different jobs, and matching on the group is how a family ends up with a capable biologist teaching fields. In a specialist market this thin, level matching is the difference between hours that move a grade and hours that produce a pleasant term.

whyPoints.title: The algebra named as the problem when it is
whyPoints.description: Most Diploma physics grade drops in this corridor are algebraic rather than conceptual, and the plan says so explicitly rather than quietly teaching more content. Parents sometimes query a physics plan that starts with rearrangement, and it is the fastest route to a grade change.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1B given its own sessions
whyPoints.description: Data analysis questions are slow to self-mark, so schools set fewer of them and students arrive with almost no practice in a component carrying part of 36% of the grade. Timetabling it explicitly rather than assuming it is covered is a small decision with a disproportionate return.

whyPoints.title: The level conversation raised, not avoided
whyPoints.description: Where marked evidence suggests Standard Level is the better route and the target courses allow it, we say so, with the school's last date for a change. That conversation costs us hours to have, which is exactly why most of this market does not have it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits stated before payment
whyPoints.description: Physics HL in an early weekday slot is among the hardest requests to fill in Dubai, and when we cannot field a genuine specialist we say so first. The alternatives are a different slot, a weekend morning, a short wait, or a bounded clinic rather than a generalist in a specialist seat.

faqs.question: My son took a 9 in IGCSE Physics and is now getting a 4 at Higher Level. What happened?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the mathematics inside the physics rather than the physics. Diploma physics expects algebraic rearrangement as a reflex, logarithms where IGCSE expected substitution, uncertainty propagated through a calculation rather than mentioned at the end, and a graph treated as a source of a gradient with units. A student can hold a correct model of a field and lose every mark in the question. The diagnosis is visible the moment a full Paper 2 is marked question by question against the published scheme, and the repair is usually three weeks of algebra inside physics questions.

faqs.question: Is there any realistic chance of finding a Physics HL tutor who lives in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: Low, and that is not a fact about Dubai Hills Estate. Physics at Higher Level is taught by a small number of people in any city, and in Dubai the absolute number is small. Narrowing it to those willing to drive to one villa community on a specific weekday evening usually produces nobody, or produces a general science tutor presented as a physics specialist, which is invisible for about six weeks. Dubai Hills Estate is the best case for local hiring in the emirate and it still fails at this level, which tells you the constraint is national.

faqs.question: What does Dubai Hills Estate actually gain over Arabian Ranches for physics tutoring?
faqs.answer: Time, and for physics that is worth more than it sounds. Bus runs from the Al Khail campuses often land before 15:40, making a 16:00 start genuine, while an Arabian Ranches Dubailand loop pushes it to 16:30 or later. Higher Level physics needs full-length timed papers, and a two-and-a-half-hour Paper 2 does not fit a 17:30 start on a school night. A 16:00 start lets the hard practice happen on a weekday instead of being pushed entirely into weekends. Specialist supply is identical in both communities.

faqs.question: Which theme in DP Physics costs students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Theme D, fields, by a clear margin in the papers we mark from this corridor, with Theme E compounding it. Fields require a student to hold an abstract model and manipulate inverse-square relationships algebraically at the same time, and students who can do either separately frequently cannot do both under time pressure. Nuclear and quantum physics adds a second difficulty: the magnitudes involved offer no intuition to sanity-check an answer against, so an algebraic slip passes unnoticed. Both respond to practice on the algebra rather than to re-teaching the concepts.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B in physics and why do so few students prepare for it?
faqs.answer: Paper 1B is the data analysis part of Paper 1, set on the experimental programme rather than on content recall. Students barely practise it because data questions are slow to self-mark, so schools under time pressure set multiple choice instead, and the gap stays invisible until a mock. The skills are specific: reading axes, extracting a gradient with its units, judging whether a spread of points supports a claimed relationship, and handling error bars. It responds quickly to targeted practice, which makes it one of the better uses of early sessions.

faqs.question: Should my daughter drop Physics HL to Standard Level, and when is the last moment?
faqs.answer: It depends on two things: whether marked evidence shows the extension content is consistently out of reach, and whether her target university programmes name Higher Level physics. Where the evidence is clear and the programmes allow it, moving down often raises her total points and returns two hours a week to a subject closer to a threshold. The timing is set by the school rather than the IB, differs between campuses in this corridor, and is usually earlier than parents assume. Ask the school in writing at the end of the first Diploma year, before it becomes urgent.

faqs.question: Can my child take Physics HL with Mathematics Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Schools allow it and it is the most common structural mismatch we see here. Applications and Interpretation is statistics-led and does not develop rearrangement, logarithms and trigonometric identities to the depth Higher Level physics assumes, so the student struggles in physics and gets tutored in physics while the cause sits in the maths. If the combination is already fixed, treat the algebra as the primary problem for the first month. Before it is fixed, check whether target engineering or physics programmes name Analysis and Approaches specifically, because some do.

faqs.question: How are marks split inside the DP Physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four marks across four criteria worth six each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, together making a fifth of the grade. Research design is decided before any apparatus is touched, which is why a narrow independent variable range cannot be rescued by careful writing afterwards. Evaluation is the criterion students treat as a closing paragraph and it is a quarter of the total, so listing human error there is expensive. Ask the subject teacher for the current published descriptors; self-marking against them is more useful than any amount of redrafting.

faqs.question: What makes a physics investigation fail at the proposal stage?
faqs.answer: Range, nearly always. A physics investigation needs the independent variable varied across enough levels, with enough repeats, to produce a graph whose gradient can actually be measured. Three closely spaced values give three points that any number of lines would fit, and there is then nothing to analyse. A ten-minute feasibility conversation before data collection fixes it: what is your range, how many levels, how many repeats, and what gradient do you expect if the hypothesis holds. That conversation is the single highest-value tutoring intervention on the investigation.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their final physics answer is almost right?
faqs.answer: Because the method is not written down. Physics mark schemes award marks for the steps, and those marks survive a wrong final answer only if the steps are visible. A student who performs a three-stage calculation on a calculator and writes one number scores nothing where two or three marks were available. It is not a physics problem, it is a habit, it takes about two sessions to install, and it recovers marks on every paper afterwards. Units and prefix conversions are the second category in the same family.

faqs.question: Does a physics tutor need to see my child's handwritten working on screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the difference between a useful session and an expensive conversation. Physics marks live in the working, so a tutor who cannot see the page is listening to answers rather than diagnosing where a rearrangement broke. A document camera or a phone on a stand pointing at the desk solves it. It takes twenty minutes to set up and is worth doing in the first week, because a term of sessions where the student reads out answers wastes most of what you are paying for.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a house in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Lessons for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market here is real, with published rates of roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour from Bestimate's 2026 table and independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is included. For Higher Level physics specifically, the online argument is about supply rather than price: the specialist pool is small nationally and is not distributed by neighbourhood.

faqs.question: What should a Higher Level physics tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Read it against the specialist band rather than the cheapest one. Bestimate's 2026 table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. A Higher Level physics quote at the AED 33 to 65 budget tier is not a bargain, it is a different product, and the right response is to ask what level and how many cohorts they have taught. Above the specialist band you are paying for scarcity or reputation, which may be reasonable but should be evidenced.

faqs.question: How should I treat a tutor who says they are an IB physics examiner?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence of current status, and understand what the claim can and cannot mean. A tutor should not be described as an IB or Cambridge examiner where current examiner status cannot be evidenced, and examiner status never implies access to marking, boundaries or unpublished paper content. Treat any suggestion of inside knowledge as a reason to walk away rather than as a selling point. What is genuinely valuable is someone who can mark your child's paper against the published scheme and name the loss pattern, which you can simply ask them to demonstrate.

faqs.question: What happens if no Physics HL specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so before you pay anything. Higher Level physics in an early weekday window is among the hardest requests to fill in Dubai, and the alternatives we will offer are a different time, a weekend morning where full-length paper work fits better anyway, a short wait for a specialist's calendar to open, or a bounded investigation clinic rather than weekly teaching. What we will not do is put a general science tutor into a Higher Level physics seat and let you discover it in week six. No competitor page audited in this market discloses a coverage limit.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-hills-es.closingHeading: Send a marked paper, not a description
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-hills-es.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB physics tutor in Dubai Hills Estate, the most useful thing you can send is your child's most recent marked Paper 2 together with their level and campus. A description of the problem tends to say the physics is hard; a marked paper says whether the loss is algebra, command terms, unwritten method or stamina, and those four need four different plans. The trial lesson is with the tutor who would teach, no card details are taken, and lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. If the honest answer is that the hours belong in mathematics instead, we will say that.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-internet.tutorsIntro: These physics tutors work with Diploma students across the TECOM strip, Al Sufouh, Barsha Heights and the Marina. Each teaches physics at a stated level, knows the data booklet, and takes the later weekday slots this strip needs.

intro.heading: The comparison families on this strip keep running
paragraphs: Dubai Internet City is a free zone in Al Sufouh with the Red Line Metro station serving this strip, offices and innovation space, residential towers and no school. Next door seaward sits Dubai Media City with the tram stop; next along is Dubai Knowledge Park with its university campuses; inland across the Metro line is Barsha Heights. Four districts in a row, none with a school in it except by accident of boundary, and all four generating the same physics requests.

The question we get asked is whether any of this matters. It does, but less than families expect and in a narrower way. Barsha Heights children are closer to the Al Barsha cluster and get home earlier, which makes a 5pm session genuinely workable. Knowledge Park skews to older students, so more DP2 and fewer DP1 requests. Internet City and Media City are effectively interchangeable. What does not vary anywhere on the strip is the physics: the same syllabus, the same papers, the same data booklet, the same investigation marked out of 24.

Nor does the tutor pool vary. Physics is a narrower request than mathematics, and Higher Level physics is narrower still. The IB holds roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment according to KHDA's 2024-25 figures, which record 387,441 students across 227 private schools licensed for 17 curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent, Indian schools 26 per cent and American schools 14 per cent. Divide the IB share across three programmes, six subject groups and two levels and the number of Higher Level physics specialists within any drive of Al Sufouh is not a pool, it is a handful.

So the comparison, done honestly, points at the same conclusion from all four addresses: choose on level and on diagnosis, not on distance. The level matters because Higher Level physics raises the reasoning demand across every component rather than simply adding chapters. The diagnosis matters because physics requests arrive described as the subject being hard and resolve into one of three specific failures, each with a different remedy.

This page therefore does two things. It runs the district comparison properly, because nobody else publishes it and families here deserve a straight answer. Then it goes into the physics: what the Higher Level extension is, the three failure modes in order of cost, how the data booklet and calculator rules shape revision, and the particular problem of an investigation designed from an apartment rather than a villa.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm. Physics travels well over a screen, because the work is a shared graph, a numerical solution built line by line and a past-paper answer annotated live.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-internet.programmesIntro: Physics appears in a different form in each programme this strip's schools run. The programme, not the district, decides what support should look like.

programmes.name: Diploma Physics
programmes.description: Offered at Higher and Standard Level, assessed by written components plus a single internally assessed investigation marked out of 24 and moderated externally. A data booklet is provided in the examination, which means the examined skill is selecting and applying a supplied relationship rather than recalling it.
programmes.countryNote: UAE IB schools sit the May session, with November as the second sitting used mainly for retakes. Specific IB session and results dates are not published here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself; your school's coordinator is the authority. Diploma physics runs at GEMS Wellington International School in Al Sufouh and Dubai American Academy in Al Barsha among others.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Four criteria marked out of eight, with criterion B asking for a method a stranger could repeat and criterion C for the processing and evaluation of the student's own data. Criterion C is the direct ancestor of the Diploma investigation, and a student who never mastered it meets the same demand again with higher stakes.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai IB schools carry the MYP through all five years and others enter students for IGCSE at 16, so students arriving in DP1 physics come from two quite different backgrounds. MYP leavers usually have better evaluation habits and weaker quantitative speed than IGCSE leavers, and the two need opposite opening sessions.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the other feeder
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, both externally examined. Students arrive in DP1 with strong content recall and no experience of formal uncertainty treatment, which IGCSE physics does not examine. The gap is narrow and specific, and the summer before DP1 closes it cheaply.
programmes.countryNote: Many students on this strip sit IGCSE physics and move into the Diploma at a different school, which is the transition that produces a confused DP1 autumn. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; Pearson runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

programmes.name: A Level Physics as the alternative
programmes.description: The route most British-school students on this strip take instead: narrower, deeper, with a practical endorsement rather than a single assessed investigation and no requirement to carry six subjects. Assessment is almost entirely terminal, which suits some students considerably better.
programmes.countryNote: For engineering and physics degrees both routes are widely accepted and the usual requirement is physics at the higher level of whichever system, often alongside mathematics. Requirements vary by university, country and intake year, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas institutions, so read the individual programme page rather than relying on a general rule.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-internet.subjectsIntro: Physics requests from this strip concentrate in a short list of topics and components. These are the places marks actually go, with what each is assessed on.

subjects.name: Mechanics and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy. Numerical questions go reasonably; explanation questions do not, because students describe a motion graph without naming the quantity the gradient represents or assert conservation of momentum without stating the condition. The repair is written reasoning rather than more problems.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, gas laws and the kinetic model. Marks go in algebraic rearrangement under time pressure and in molecular explanations given out of order. Students who use heat and temperature interchangeably lose the same mark repeatedly across the paper.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.levels: HL and SL, with HL extending the treatment
subjects.description: Wave properties, superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference. The reliable loss is a correct diagram with no written path-difference argument connecting it to the numerical answer. Diagram plus sentence, every time, is the habit worth building.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. The most requested topic on this strip at both levels. Students who calculate confidently still lose potential-divider reasoning marks, because the sequence of consequences is held in the head rather than written.

subjects.name: Fields and electromagnetic induction
subjects.description: Field strength and potential, orbital motion, induction. At Higher Level this is where students either consolidate or quietly fall behind, partly because the mathematics is denser and partly because it arrives late in the course when coursework deadlines are live.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and particle physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, with the standard model at HL
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy, mass defect and nuclear models. Students like the topic and still leak marks, which is diagnostic: the losses are arithmetic with unit prefixes and powers, plus failing to state what a calculated figure means physically.

subjects.name: Energy production
subjects.description: Sources, efficiency, Sankey diagrams and the physics of generation. Questions are often part-qualitative, and students write general environmental commentary where the scheme wants a named physical mechanism and a number. Among the easiest places to recover marks quickly.

subjects.name: Quantum physics at Higher Level
subjects.description: Photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality and related models. It arrives late in DP2 when revision has begun and is frequently half-learned as a consequence. Treating it deliberately in the autumn rather than the spring is a scheduling choice that changes the outcome.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and data handling
subjects.levels: HL and SL; examined in the papers and the investigation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation, error bars, maximum and minimum gradients, and honest significant figures. Procedural, examined repeatedly, rarely taught deliberately, and reliable within four to six focused sessions. No level specialist is required.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing axes so a relationship becomes linear, extracting a gradient with units, taking a constant from the intercept. Students plot correctly and then quote a gradient without units or without showing the triangle, which the scheme does not forgive. A checklist handles most of it.

subjects.name: The investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, marked out of 24
subjects.description: One scientific investigation designed, conducted, processed and evaluated by the student, moderated externally. The usual failure is a question too broad for the apparatus available. A tutor may coach the method and comment on the student's own drafts, and may write none of it.

subjects.name: The mathematics underneath
subjects.description: Rearranging multi-term expressions, logarithms, trigonometry and, at Higher Level, calculus-adjacent reasoning. A student whose algebra is slow looks bad at physics because every question becomes an algebra race with a clock on it. This is the most frequently missed diagnosis.

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor search returns from this address
paragraphs: An IB physics tutor in Dubai Internet City means a physics specialist at a stated level, teaching one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, for a student who attends school somewhere else entirely. There is no school in the free zone and no staff room to draw on, so a proximity search surfaces the tuition centres inland in Al Barsha and whichever agencies have bought the local advertising.

Run the same search from Media City and the results are near-identical, which is the first useful finding. The two free zones share a Metro station, a stretch of Al Sufouh and the same school destinations, so a list ranked by distance is ranking almost nothing. Knowledge Park returns the same set again. Only Barsha Heights produces a materially different experience, and the difference is the hour rather than the people.

Physics narrows the pool further than most subjects. A general science tutor can be genuinely useful for the procedural part of the course, but Higher Level field and quantum reasoning needs someone who has marked those answers against the real scheme. The arithmetic is unforgiving: the IB's 7 per cent share of Dubai enrolment, split across three programmes, six subject groups and two levels, does not leave a market inside a twenty-minute drive.

That is why the practical recommendation is identical from all four addresses. Diagnose first, match on level second, ignore distance third. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run over live video, which for physics costs almost nothing: the work is a shared graph, a worked numerical solution and an annotated past-paper answer.

paragraphs: Here is the comparison set out properly. The columns that matter for a Diploma physics student are the school destination, the realistic earliest session time, how deep the local specialist market is, and whether anything about the physics recommendation shifts.

The pattern is clear once it is tabulated. Internet City, Media City and Knowledge Park differ in resident profile rather than in options. Barsha Heights shortens the school run enough to change the slot. The Marina and Palm Jumeirah lengthen it and raise any in-home premium sharply. In no case does the physics change, because the syllabus, the papers, the data booklet and the 24-mark investigation are set nationally rather than locally.

The third column deserves attention. These free zones are working districts with mobile residential populations, so the informal networks that recommend tutors in the villa belt barely exist. A parent in Emirates Hills hears three names at the school gate; a parent in an Internet City tower starts from a search engine. For a narrow request like Higher Level physics, that disadvantage is larger than it looks, because word of mouth is the only mechanism that reliably surfaces rare specialists locally.

The final column repeating itself is the point of the exercise rather than a flaw in it. Families on this strip spend real energy on a geographic question that has no geographic answer, and publishing the comparison is more useful than implying each district needs its own strategy.

sections.heading: What the Higher Level extension actually adds
paragraphs: Parents are told that Higher Level is harder, which is true and not useful. What is useful is knowing what the extension consists of, because it determines whether a student can carry the subject alongside five others and where a term of support should go.

Three things change. First, content: additional topics including the heavier field material and quantum physics, much of which arrives late in the course. Second, a third written component devoted to extended problem-solving in an unfamiliar context, which rewards sustaining a long chain of reasoning rather than recalling more. Third, and least discussed, the depth of written explanation expected across every component rises, so an answer that would have earned full marks at Standard Level can score partially at Higher Level.

The best predictor of coping is algebraic fluency rather than enthusiasm. A student who rearranges a three-term expression quickly and handles logarithms without hesitation can usually carry Higher Level physics. A student whose algebra is slow finds that every physics question becomes an algebra question with a clock on it, and the cost appears in the other five subjects as well as in physics.

The table sets out the comparison. Exact component names, weightings and durations are set by the current subject guide and can change between versions, so confirm specifics with your child's school. Use this to decide where the hours go and whether the level is sustainable, not to argue with a teacher about a weighting.

sections.heading: The three failure modes, in order of cost
paragraphs: Physics requests arrive described as the subject being hard, and they resolve into three specific failures. Knowing which one applies decides what to buy, how long for and at what rate, and one marked paper usually settles it in twenty minutes.

The most expensive is unstated reasoning. A student writes a true statement where the scheme wants a sequence: resistance increases, so current falls, so the potential difference across the component falls, so the reading falls. Each link is a mark. Students who have never had an explanation answer marked in front of them do not know the links are credited separately, and they lose marks on every explanation question in both papers. The fix is writing answers out and having them marked, which takes two or three sessions and holds.

The second is procedural: uncertainty treatment, graph conventions and significant figures. This is examined in the data-analysis work and throughout the investigation, it is almost never taught deliberately, and it rewards drilled practice rather than insight. Four to six focused sessions makes a student reliable at it permanently, and it does not require a level specialist, which matters when you are deciding what rate to pay.

The third is the quiet one: algebraic slowness. A student who can do the physics but takes three times as long to manipulate an expression will appear weak at physics, run out of time in papers, and conclude they are bad at the subject. This is the diagnosis most often missed, and it is also the cheapest to fix, because the repair is mathematics rather than physics and can be bought at the qualified rather than the specialist rate.
bullets: Unstated reasoning: the most expensive, fixed in two or three sessions of marked writing

sections.heading: The data booklet, the calculator and what revision should stop being
paragraphs: A data booklet is provided in the physics examination. That single fact should reshape revision and usually does not. If the relationships are supplied, rehearsing them is practising the one thing the examination has removed, and an hour spent writing out equations is an hour not spent on the skill actually being tested.

What the booklet cannot supply is selection and interpretation: which of the provided relationships applies to the situation described, what each symbol denotes in that context, and which quantity the question has actually given you. Those improve only through past-paper questions where the first step is choosing from the booklet and justifying the choice. It is a short drill and almost nobody runs it.

The calculator rules differ by component, and a student who has only ever worked with one available loses marks when it is not, while a student who uses it slowly loses marks to the clock. Both are mechanical problems. More subtly, an answer produced on a screen has no visible method unless the student writes down what they asked the calculator to do, and method is credited separately from the result.

Put together, this means a physics revision hour should look unlike most physics revision hours. Less reading of notes, more attempting questions under time, more marking against the official scheme, more writing of explanation chains, and a deliberate rotation through data-analysis questions, which students avoid precisely because they are the ones that feel unfamiliar. The avoidance is the reason the marks are available.

sections.heading: Designing an investigation from a tower rather than a villa
paragraphs: This is a practical problem specific to apartment living that nobody writes about. The physics investigation is designed by the student, and plenty of good investigations involve equipment, space and repeated measurements over time. A student in a villa community can set something up in a garage or a garden and leave it there. A student in an Internet City tower cannot.

The consequence is that question choice has to respect the apparatus genuinely available, which usually means the school laboratory and the time the laboratory is open. A question that requires fifty repeats across a week is not a good question for a student whose only access is two timetabled sessions. Discovering that in week six is how a 24-mark component becomes a salvage operation.

The constraint is not a disadvantage if it is used early. Investigations that work well within school apparatus and limited laboratory time tend to be narrow, with a clean independent variable and a measurable dependent variable, and narrow is exactly what the criteria reward. Students aiming for something ambitious and physically awkward are usually optimising for how the title sounds rather than for what the mark scheme credits.

The honesty line applies as it does everywhere. A tutor may help narrow the question to the apparatus available, teach uncertainty planning before data collection, teach data processing and graphing conventions, explain what each criterion rewards, and read the student's own draft and say exactly where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure any part of it, and may not supply a model to adapt. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; the risk sits with the student, and the school supervisor remains the authority on process.
bullets: Tower living means the school laboratory is usually the only apparatus available

sections.heading: Physics, engineering and medicine routes from this strip
paragraphs: Physics is taken at Higher Level mostly for a reason outside the Diploma: engineering, physics, computer science and some architecture programmes expect it, often alongside Higher Level mathematics. That turns a physics grade into an application gate, and it changes how a family should think about spending on it.

The requirement varies considerably. Some engineering programmes specify Higher Level physics; many accept Standard Level physics with Higher Level mathematics; a few treat mathematics as the binding constraint and physics as desirable. Requirements differ by university, by country and by intake year, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas institutions, so read the individual programme page in the application year. A tutoring website is the wrong place to learn an admissions requirement, including this one.

There is a related planning point about mathematics. A student aiming at engineering with Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches may find the mathematics route, not the physics grade, is what limits their options. Those two decisions are usually made separately, in different conversations, a year apart, and they interact. Asking the coordinator to look at them together in DP1 is worth more than a term of tutoring.

For Ministry of Education equivalency, which is a separate matter from admissions, the published British-track rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold appears in the source we could read, so no figure should be quoted to you without a moe.gov.ae reference. Equivalency is completed with the authority, is not something a tutoring platform performs or accelerates, and tutoring is not required for it.
bullets: Some engineering programmes specify Higher Level physics; many accept Standard with HL mathematics

sections.heading: What physics support costs along this strip
paragraphs: Published rates in Dubai sort into tiers, and matching the tier to the failure mode is how the budget stays sensible. Budget online tutoring runs from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors online are published from AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors at IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

Applied to the three failure modes, the sorting is clean. Procedural repairs in uncertainty and graph work belong in the qualified band, because no level judgement is involved. Algebraic slowness also belongs there, and can be bought from a mathematics tutor rather than a physics one. Unstated reasoning at Higher Level, and any investigation close to moderation, belong in the specialist band and will waste money below it.

In-home visits are published between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour with travel included, and Bestimate's in-home band is AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For a subject whose repairs are procedural and need frequent repetition, eight shorter contacts beat four longer ones, and the in-home package costs roughly double. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Those are other providers' published figures rather than IB Gram prices. Before paying anything, establish the rate, whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether travel is inside the number, the cancellation terms and the remedy if the match is wrong. Three of the six strongest-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no rate at all, which is why a sourced table belongs here.

faqs.question: Would a physics tutor be easier to find if we lived in Media City instead?
faqs.answer: No. Internet City and Media City adjoin each other in Al Sufouh, share a Metro station and the same school destinations, and neither contains a school. A search from either address returns essentially the same listings. Knowledge Park produces the same set again. Only Barsha Heights behaves differently, and the difference is that children get home earlier so a 5pm slot works. The physics itself, and the pool of people who can teach it, are unchanged by any of these moves.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level physics so much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Three things change rather than one. It adds content, including the heavier field material and quantum physics, much of which arrives late in the course. It adds a third written component devoted to extended problem-solving in an unfamiliar context. And it raises the depth of written explanation expected across every component, so an answer that would score fully at Standard Level can score partially at Higher Level. Algebraic fluency, not enthusiasm for physics, is the best predictor of coping with all three.

faqs.question: What are the three usual reasons an IB physics student loses marks?
faqs.answer: Unstated reasoning, where a true statement is written instead of the sequence of consequences the scheme credits link by link. Procedural losses in uncertainty treatment, graph conventions and significant figures, which are examined repeatedly and rarely taught deliberately. And algebraic slowness, where the physics is understood but every question becomes an algebra race against the clock. One marked paper distinguishes them in about twenty minutes, and each has a different remedy and a different sensible price.

faqs.question: How do I test whether Higher Level physics is sustainable for my child?
faqs.answer: With a timed algebra exercise rather than a conversation. Give them several multi-term rearrangements and a couple of logarithm questions under time. If that is fluent, Higher Level physics is viable. If it is slow and error-prone, the subject will consume two evenings a week and the cost will appear in the other five subjects as well as in physics. That test takes fifteen minutes and is considerably more informative than asking whether they enjoy the subject.

faqs.question: Should revision include writing out the equations if a data booklet is provided?
faqs.answer: No, and this is one of the commonest wasted hours in physics revision. If the relationships are supplied, rehearsing them is practising the one thing the examination has removed. What is examined is selection and interpretation: which supplied relationship applies here, what each symbol denotes in this context, and which quantity the question has given you. Past-paper questions where the first step is choosing from the booklet and justifying that choice are the right use of the time.

faqs.question: Why does my child avoid data-analysis questions in revision?
faqs.answer: Because they feel unfamiliar, which is precisely why the marks are sitting there. Uncertainty propagation, error bars, maximum and minimum gradients and honest significant figures are procedural and feel unlike the physics the student enjoys, so revision drifts towards comfortable topics. Four to six focused sessions makes a student reliable at the whole set permanently, and the marks are awarded for procedure rather than insight, so they are earned every time the question appears.

faqs.question: Our flat has no space for an investigation. Does that limit the options?
faqs.answer: It shapes the question, which is manageable if it is done early. For most students in these towers the school laboratory is the only apparatus genuinely available, and laboratory access time is limited, so an investigation requiring fifty repeats over a week is not a realistic choice. Narrow questions with a clean independent variable work well within those constraints and are what the criteria reward anyway. Discovering the constraint in week six is what turns a 24-mark component into a salvage job.

faqs.question: When should the uncertainty plan for the investigation be made?
faqs.answer: Before any data is collected. A student who knows in advance how they will propagate uncertainties measures the right quantities, takes enough repeats, and records instrument resolutions as they go. One who decides afterwards finds the required information was never written down and cannot recover it without repeating the practical, which needs laboratory time the school may not have spare. It is a ten-minute conversation that routinely saves a fortnight and several marks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a physics investigation that is nearly due?
faqs.answer: Yes, within the rules, and with a lower ceiling than earlier help would have had. A tutor may teach data processing and graphing conventions, explain what each criterion rewards, and read the student's own draft and name precisely where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure any part of it or supply a model to adapt. Marks tied to method and data are already fixed by then, which is why the autumn conversation is worth so much more.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level physics for engineering?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. Some engineering programmes specify Higher Level physics; many accept Standard Level physics alongside Higher Level mathematics; a few treat mathematics as the binding requirement. It varies by university, by country and by intake year, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas institutions, so read the individual programme page in the application year rather than relying on a general rule or a tutoring website. Ask the coordinator to review the physics level and the mathematics route together, because they interact.

faqs.question: Can a general science tutor handle IB physics, or do we need a physics specialist?
faqs.answer: It depends on the failure mode rather than the level. Procedural work in uncertainty, graphs and significant figures is well served by a competent science tutor in the published AED 150 to AED 300 band, because the material is mechanical. Algebraic repair can come from a mathematics tutor at the same rate. Higher Level field and quantum reasoning, and an investigation close to moderation, need the specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 and above.

faqs.question: What time do physics sessions run from an Internet City tower?
faqs.answer: Usually between six and eight in the evening. Diploma students here travel to Al Barsha, Al Sufouh or the villa belt, the roads around the larger gates stall for about an hour after the final bell, and a bus serving several communities adds stops, so a student is typically home between four and five. Add food and a start on school work and six is the realistic opening. From Barsha Heights a 5pm slot is workable; from the Marina, usually 6.30pm.

faqs.question: Is one physics session a week enough in DP2?
faqs.answer: Through the autumn, usually yes, alongside a problem set attempted alone and one timed data-analysis section between sessions. In the final term many families move to two or three sessions a week for six to eight weeks, which is worth disrupting the rhythm for, and that block should end when the examination session starts rather than drifting. Buying four hours a week earlier mostly consumes the independent practice time where the remaining marks actually sit.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the tutor is not based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: For physics, what matters is Gulf Standard Time scheduling and familiarity with the current subject guide, not the tutor's address. The lesson is a shared graph, a numerical solution built line by line and a past-paper answer annotated live. Where a match is a tutor based outside the UAE, we say so before you book rather than behind a local-sounding number, because two providers ranking for Dubai searches route parents to numbers in another country without disclosing it.

faqs.question: What should be different after four physics sessions?
faqs.answer: Something visible in marked work. Explanation answers written as a chain rather than a statement. Graphs with units, a gradient triangle shown and a sensible number of significant figures. Data-analysis sections attempted rather than skipped. If none of that has changed, the honest reading is that the match or the diagnosis was wrong rather than that more hours are needed, and re-matching is the right response rather than extending the block.

intro.heading: In physics, the expensive purchase is usually the wrong one
paragraphs: Start with the journey, because in this district it sets what a physics week can actually hold. Dubai Investments Park runs along the southern corridor in two halves, DIP 1 and DIP 2, industrial and commercial plots threaded through residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, with Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and the district's own Metro station towards Expo City carrying the traffic out. Two IB schools and a British-curriculum school sit inside the boundary, but most secondary students travel out of it - to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan or Dubai South - and it is the return leg that makes an unbroken hour for a full data question harder to find here than forty minutes for command-term drilling.

Physics is the subject where families here most often report spending money and seeing nothing change. The reason is a diagnostic error rather than a tutoring one. A disappointing physics grade looks like a knowledge problem, so a parent buys content teaching, and in most cases the marked script shows that the student knew the physics and failed to be paid for it. Those are different problems with wildly different costs.

The three failures that produce this pattern are all finite. Describe offered where the question said explain, which can score nothing on a paragraph of correct physics. A gradient reported without units or physical meaning, where three separate marks were available. And uncertainty ignored in a data question, forfeiting the whole uncertainty allocation. Each is three to four sessions of work with no new content involved, and each is visible in a marked script within minutes.

The fourth, specific to Higher Level, is the two-step collapse: an answer correct for two steps of a five-mark question that then stops. That one is a longer block, six to eight sessions, because sustained reasoning is built by practice rather than explained. And the fifth, the internal investigation at 20 per cent of the grade, is cheap to help with before data collection and essentially impossible to help with afterwards.

There is a scheduling dimension too, because physics work divides unevenly. Command term drills, script marking and uncertainty arithmetic are self-contained and survive a short session after a long school run. A full data question needs an unbroken hour, since the graph, the error bars and the gradient interpretation form one continuous piece of work. Higher Level extended response practice needs the longest slot of all, because the chain has to be written out whole before it is compressed.

That turns out to be convenient rather than limiting. The three cheapest and highest-value physics fixes all fit a weekday evening, and only the one long block genuinely needs a weekend morning. A household in this corridor that can offer forty minutes midweek plus one protected weekend slot can work through everything on this page in the right order.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one physics tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. For physics the shared screen is a practical gain, because a data question with a graph and three columns of uncertainties is far easier to work through when both people can annotate the same thing at once.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-investme.subjectsIntro: Physics is organised here by what is assessed and what each area costs to fix, because that is the information a family actually needs before spending anything.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and momentum
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum and impulse. The recurring loss is an answer stating what happens to an object rather than naming the law that makes it happen, which forfeits the explanation marks even where the physics is understood.

subjects.name: Work, energy and power
subjects.description: Energy transfer, efficiency and power. Marks go missing when an energy statement does not specify which store the energy left and which it entered, and when efficiency is given as a ratio without saying what was wasted.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the gas laws. Characteristic errors are Celsius used where kelvin is required, which invalidates a whole calculation, and heat and temperature used interchangeably in written answers.

subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation, error bars, lines of best and worst fit, and gradient interpretation. The most recoverable block of marks in the subject because the technique list is short and finite, and roughly three sessions of work.

sections.heading: What each kind of physics support costs and buys
paragraphs: This is the table a family should see before anyone quotes an hourly rate, because in physics the length of the block varies more than the rate does. Three of the five common problems are three to four session fixes; one is six to eight; one is a design conversation that takes two.

Rates next, attributed and dated October 2026 so any quote can be judged against them - but multiply each by the block length above, because that product is what you actually pay. Take the commonest fix on this page, a four-session command-term block. At Tutopiya's AED 33 to 52 an hour it is AED 132 to 208. At EdFlik's AED 45 to 65 it is AED 180 to 260. At the AED 150 to 300 per hour a qualified subject tutor charges online it is AED 600 to 1,200. Across the AED 200 to 450 and above that IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists charge it is AED 800 to 1,800 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270 giving AED 1,080 and BartyED at AED 650, the premium end, giving AED 2,600. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table, which in this corridor is largely paying for Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road rather than for physics. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

The important column is the last one. A block with a completion test ends; a block with only an end date becomes a standing arrangement, and a standing arrangement gets reviewed when the invoice becomes uncomfortable rather than when the work is done. In physics the tests are unusually clean: the student predicts their own mark, the gradient gets its units without prompting, the five-mark answer reaches the end.

One piece of household context changes how those block prices should be read. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. With the largest line in an education budget held flat, tutoring becomes the main variable line in most families this year - which is an argument for buying the three-to-four-session block the marked script actually points at, rather than letting an open-ended weekly arrangement expand into the space a fee rise would otherwise have taken.

sections.heading: Where physics spending earns nothing
paragraphs: Four purchases reliably fail in physics, and naming them is more useful than any amount of description of what we do instead. None involves an incompetent tutor; in each case somebody is working hard and the marks are not moving.

First, content re-teaching of material the marked script shows the student already knows. This is the default purchase because it is what tutoring looks like, and in physics it is usually aimed at the wrong thing entirely. One script read before booking prevents it, and the reading takes ten minutes.

Second, help with the internal investigation after the data has been collected. At that point the design has already set the ceiling on the analysis and evaluation criteria, and no amount of writing support changes it. Paying a specialist rate for investigation support in the final fortnight is paying for reassurance rather than for marks.

Third, more multiple-choice practice because it is easy to set. A student weak on extended response gets faster at something they were already adequate at while the component actually costing marks goes untouched. Fourth, a premium or examiner-led rate for routine practice supervision, where the task requires company rather than expertise. Match the rate to the task and most households spend less overall.

A fifth failure is specific to households already short of hours: supporting three sciences at once because all three feel urgent. Three simultaneous plans with no sequencing produce three shallow efforts and no completed fix, at three times the cost. One component, verified on a timed paper, then the next, is cheaper and faster.

And a sixth, which costs availability rather than money: waiting until mock results arrive before seeking Higher Level cover. That is asking for the scarcest thing in the market at the exact moment demand peaks, and the families who get the slot they want are the ones who agreed a pattern beforehand.

sections.heading: The uncertainty list, and why it is the best value in the subject
paragraphs: Of everything on this page, this is the clearest value for money, because the technique is finite. There is a list, the list is short, and a student who can execute it reliably stops losing those marks entirely rather than reducing the loss by some uncertain amount.

The list runs roughly as follows. Distinguish absolute from percentage uncertainty and convert between them without hesitating. Propagate correctly through addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and powers. Decide how many significant figures the data actually supports and be able to justify it. Plot with error bars that reflect the measurement rather than decorating the graph. Draw lines of best and worst fit and use the difference to estimate the uncertainty in the gradient. Report the gradient with its unit and say what it represents physically.

That is about three sessions for most students, at mid-market rates, and it pays twice over: once in every data question on every paper, and again in the internal investigation, where the same skills are assessed against the criteria and carry a share of 20 per cent of the grade. Very little else in Diploma physics has that double return.

It goes untaught for structural reasons rather than anyone's fault. It sits alongside the content in a crowded two-year course, it feels like arithmetic rather than physics, and students who are confident in physics find it tedious. That combination is precisely why it remains reliably available as recovered marks for any family willing to spend three sessions on it.

sections.heading: The investigation, costed before and after
paragraphs: The internal scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the physics grade, is marked by the school against lettered criteria and is moderated by the IB. Its cost profile is unlike anything else in the subject, because help is cheap and decisive at one stage and worthless at another.

Before data collection, two to four sessions can change the ceiling of the whole piece. A tutor tests whether the research question can be measured precisely enough with the equipment a school actually has, teaches what each criterion rewards, and makes sure the uncertainty treatment is planned into the method rather than attempted afterwards. A single run per condition makes an uncertainty analysis impossible to produce later, and that is a design decision rather than a writing one.

After data collection, the position is different and should be said plainly. The design has set the ceiling on the analysis and evaluation criteria, and the remaining scope is presentation and clarity. Help at that point is worth something but it is not worth a specialist rate, and any provider implying that late investigation support can transform the mark is selling comfort.

The honesty boundary applies throughout and is not negotiable. A tutor may teach criteria, interrogate a research question, demonstrate uncertainty technique on unrelated practice data, read the student's own draft and say which criterion it fails and why. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it. One operator researched for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost the entire Diploma, and the consequence falls on the student. The test after any session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words.
