sections.heading: Why Higher Level physics is scarce, and what that costs
paragraphs: This is a cost that does not appear on an invoice. Higher Level physics is the hardest Diploma specialism to cover at a specific early-evening hour anywhere in Dubai, and in the southern corridor the in-home version is close to unobtainable at peak times. The scarcity has four compounding causes and every one of them bites hardest on exactly the request DIP families most often make.

The specialism is narrow: a physics teacher who can also teach uncertainty technique and extended reasoning is a smaller group than physics teachers in general. The demand is concentrated: every DP2 household in Dubai wants the same early-evening window. The supply is rationed by travel for in-home work, and DIP sits off two motorways in the south. And moderate school cohorts in this corridor mean a single staffing change creates sudden simultaneous demand from one cohort.

What this costs a family is optionality. Waiting until mock results arrive before seeking Higher Level physics support means asking for the scarcest thing at the moment demand peaks. The families who get the slot they want are those who agreed the pattern before mocks, which costs nothing and secures the time. That is a genuinely free action, and it is the single most useful piece of planning advice on this page.

When we cannot cover a request, you are told, offered the nearest workable alternative and given a realistic date for when the slot opens. Nobody general is substituted for a specialist you asked for. And where no UAE-based specialist is available, the match may be a teacher working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time, which is stated rather than concealed behind a non-UAE phone number.

sections.heading: Reading the script yourself, before anyone quotes you
paragraphs: A family that can name the failure cannot be sold the wrong block, and naming it needs no physics expertise. Sit with the marked script, ignore the grade, and look for four patterns. This takes about fifteen minutes and is the highest-return unpaid work available.

Pattern one: a long, correct-looking answer with one or two marks. That is a command term mismatch, almost always a description where an explanation was required, and it is a three to four session fix. Pattern two: a graph question where the gradient is calculated and the mark is low. That is units and physical meaning missing, two to three sessions.

Pattern three: a data question where processing is correct and marks are still lost. That is uncertainty treatment absent, three sessions, and it is the best value in the subject because the same work pays again in the investigation. Pattern four: a five-mark question with two correct lines and then nothing. That is the Higher Level two-step collapse, and it is the one long block at six to eight sessions.

If none of those patterns appears and the losses are scattered with no structure, you are probably looking at a genuine content gap, which is a term of weekly work rather than a block. That is worth knowing honestly before you spend, and it is the one answer a provider has a commercial incentive not to give you quickly.

One practical note on doing this reading. Compare two scripts rather than one, ideally from different papers, because a single bad paper can be an off day while a pattern across two is a pattern. And look at the annotations rather than the ticks: the marker's shorthand usually names the failure directly, in almost the same words every time, which is exactly the information a tutor would otherwise charge you a session to find.

sections.heading: Fitting physics into a southern corridor week
paragraphs: Physics has an unusual scheduling property: some of its work divides neatly and some does not. That matters in a corridor where arrival home ranges from under four o'clock to past six depending on whether a child attends a school inside DIP or travels to Jebel Ali, Dubai South or further north.

Command term drills, script marking and uncertainty arithmetic are self-contained and survive a short, tired session perfectly well. A full data question needs an unbroken hour, because the graph, the error bars and the gradient interpretation form one continuous piece of work. Extended response practice at Higher Level needs the longest slot of all, because the method is to write the chain out in full and then compress it, and that cannot be done in fragments.

The convenient consequence is that the three cheapest and highest-value physics fixes all fit a weekday evening, while the one long block belongs at the weekend. A household that can offer forty minutes midweek plus one weekend morning can address everything on this page in the right order, which is a better position than it sounds.

The holidays matter disproportionately here. The summer between Year 11 and DP1 carries no school run at all and is the natural home for the transition block. The winter break sits after investigation drafts should exist and before the mock window, which makes it the one period in DP2 when a student can work on a component with no competing deadline. Sessions continue if the family travels, because nothing depends on a Dubai address, and Ramadan sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing for the month.

sections.heading: What to verify before paying anyone
paragraphs: Five checkable items, and a provider who answers all five plainly is telling you something real. Ask them of us as well as of anyone else.

One: a published rate, or a clear statement of how the price is set, in dirhams rather than a currency you do not transact in. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. Two: a stated position on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is granted free of charge for two years, and whose absence exposes the tutor to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion.

Three: a free trial with any condition stated on the same screen. Four: a tutor who can estimate a block length and a completion test from two marked scripts, which in physics is a reliable test of whether they know the scheme. Five: no claimed approval from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because an independent tutoring platform holds none and IB Gram holds none either.

A sixth item is yours rather than theirs: a review point agreed before the first session and tied to a real school event such as a mock or an investigation checkpoint. Without it, the likely outcome is not a bad tutor but an unreviewed arrangement, which is how a sensible hourly rate becomes an unreasonable annual total.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Send four things: the level, the school, the last two marked physics scripts or the current investigation draft, and the session length your household can sustain on a weekday. The free trial lesson comes before any payment and produces the two numbers that make this a financial decision rather than a hopeful one: which failure you have, and how many sessions it should take.

If the honest answer is three sessions, you will be told three sessions. If it is a term of content work, you will be told that too, which is the answer a provider has least incentive to give quickly and the one a family most needs. And if Higher Level cover is not available in your preferred slot, you will get a date rather than a substitute.

What will not be claimed. No grade promise, because nobody can honestly make one, and no claim that a particular number of sessions produces a particular grade. No suggestion that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, university admission or school progression, which would be a false claim about a regulatory process. No regulator or board approval, no UAE office or centre, and no satisfaction statistics, because a figure without its sample, date and method is decoration.

Finally, we do not publish, reproduce or supply IB past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables or subject guides as downloads, because that material is the organisation's copyright and unreleased content carries a malpractice exposure. We cite the official source, link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides. A provider advertising those files as a feature is distributing someone else's property.

faqs.answer: Most often because it was aimed at content when the marked script showed the content was known. The three common physics failures are a description offered where the question said explain, a gradient reported without units or physical meaning, and uncertainty ignored in data questions. Each is a three to four session fix involving no new content, and each is invisible in a grade and obvious in a script. Content re-teaching is the default purchase and usually the wrong one.

faqs.question: Can we book in-home physics lessons at our DIP address?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Physics is taught one-to-one into DIP homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. In this corridor the in-home option is also the most expensive and least available, since Higher Level physics is the scarcest specialism and a visiting tutor must cross two motorways at peak hour.

faqs.question: How many sessions should a physics problem take?
faqs.answer: Three of the four common problems are short. Command term errors: three to four sessions. Gradients reported without units: two to three. Uncertainty treatment absent: three. The exception is the Higher Level two-step collapse, where a five-mark answer stops after two correct lines, which takes six to eight sessions because sustained reasoning is built by repetition rather than explained. Ask any provider for the estimate and for what will show the block is done.

faqs.question: What is the best value physics work we can buy?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty and graph technique, at about three sessions. The technique list is short and finite: absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation, significant figures, error bars, best and worst fit lines, and a gradient reported with value, unit and meaning. It pays twice over, once in every data question on every paper and again in the internal investigation, where the same skills are assessed and carry a share of 20 per cent of the grade.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for investigation help in the final fortnight?
faqs.answer: Not at a specialist rate, and we would rather say so. By then the design has set the ceiling on the analysis and evaluation criteria, and the remaining scope is presentation and clarity. Before the research question is fixed, one or two sessions can change the ceiling of the whole piece, and before the laboratory session the uncertainty plan can still be built into the method. Any provider implying that late support transforms the mark is selling comfort.

faqs.question: Someone offered to write the investigation for us. Is that ever acceptable?
faqs.answer: No, under any circumstances. One operator researched for this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and buying one is an academic honesty breach that can cost the entire Diploma, with the consequence falling on your child rather than the seller. A tutor may teach the criteria, interrogate the research question, demonstrate technique on unrelated data and comment on your child's own draft. The test afterwards is whether your child could defend every change themselves.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level physics so hard to arrange out here?
faqs.answer: Four reasons compound. The specialism is narrow, since a physics teacher who also teaches uncertainty technique and extended reasoning is a smaller group than physics teachers generally. Demand is concentrated into the same early-evening window across all of Dubai. In-home supply is rationed by drive time, and DIP sits off two motorways in the south. And moderate school cohorts here mean one staffing change produces sudden simultaneous demand. Agreeing a pattern before mocks is the free remedy.

faqs.question: Our child does lots of multiple choice practice. Is that helping?
faqs.answer: Probably not, if the marks are being lost on extended response. More multiple choice is easy to set and feels productive, and it improves a component the student was usually already adequate at while the expensive component goes untouched. If the script shows five-mark questions abandoned after two lines, the work needed is timed extended response written out in full and then compressed, which is slower, less satisfying and the thing that actually moves the grade.

faqs.question: What hourly rates should we expect to be quoted for physics?
faqs.answer: The market, attributed and dated October 2026: a qualified subject tutor online roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, IB and A Level specialists AED 200 to 450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650, in-home visits AED 180 to 500 including travel, and budget online provision from AED 33 to 65. Ours is set after the free trial, because the honest figure depends on which block the marked scripts show you actually need.

faqs.question: Can physics work be done in a forty-minute weekday session?
faqs.answer: Some of it, and conveniently it is the cheapest and highest-value part. Command term drills, marking a script against the scheme and uncertainty arithmetic are all self-contained and survive a short session after a long school run. A full data question needs an unbroken hour because the graph, error bars and gradient interpretation form one continuous piece. Higher Level extended response practice needs a weekend morning, since the chain must be written out whole before it is compressed.

faqs.question: Is Standard Level physics worth supporting as a sixth subject?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and briefly, which makes it decent value. The common pattern is a Standard Level physics student carrying two heavier Higher Levels who gives physics the least preparation time and then loses marks on technique rather than content. Four sessions on command terms and data handling typically moves it further than a term of content revision, because content was not the problem. The question is whether those points matter to the offer being chased.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to intervene in physics?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, and the two best windows carry no school run. The summer between Year 11 and DP1 is the natural home for transition work on command terms and uncertainty, which prevents the first-term fall most families then spend a year repairing. The winter break in DP2 sits after investigation drafts should exist and before mocks, making it the only period when a student can fix one component with no competing deadline.

faqs.question: Do you supply IB physics past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider advertising them as a feature is distributing someone else's property. IB past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and subject guides are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. We reference them, cite the official source, link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides. The subject teacher also remains the authority on exactly what this cohort sits, since the IB revises its guides.

faqs.question: What if the script shows no clear pattern at all?
faqs.answer: Then you are probably looking at a genuine content gap, which is a term of weekly work rather than a short block, and that is worth knowing before you spend. It is also the answer a provider has least commercial incentive to give you quickly, which is a reason to ask for it explicitly. A family told honestly can decide whether to commit to a term; a family not told discovers the same thing after four sessions and usually blames the tutor.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-investme.closingHeading: Diagnose first, then buy the block
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-investme.closingBody: Physics rewards diagnosis more than almost any Diploma subject, because three of its four common failures cost three or four sessions and involve no new content, while the purchase families instinctively make is a term of content teaching. Spend fifteen unpaid minutes with the marked script, find the pattern, then ask any provider for the session count and the completion test. If Higher Level cover is what you need, agree the pattern before mocks rather than after. Send us the level, the school and two marked scripts, and take the free trial lesson. Lessons run live online into your DIP home on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Knowing physics and knowing the Diploma physics course are different jobs
paragraphs: There are a lot of capable physicists in Dubai. Engineers, former teachers, graduate students, people who sat A Level physics and did well. Far fewer of them know the current IB Diploma physics course well enough to tell a Marina parent where their child's marks are going. That is the gap this page is about, and it is a fair question to ask before paying anybody.

The reason the distinction bites is that Diploma physics was restructured. Content is now organised into five themes, lettered A to E, rather than the numbered core-and-options arrangement families with older children remember. The practical scheme has been consolidated into a single scientific investigation. The tools strands covering experimental technique, technology and mathematics run across the whole course rather than sitting in one place. A tutor working from the previous guide will still teach momentum correctly, but their sense of what is examined, how it is examined and where the emphasis falls will be out of date, and that shows up in the questions they choose to practise.

A second, quieter gap matters just as much. A large share of lost marks in Diploma physics is not physics at all. It is uncertainties, significant figures, units inside a multi-step calculation, and the discipline of answering the command term that was actually used. Explain means something specific. So does deduce, suggest, outline and discuss. Students who can do the physics routinely lose marks because they wrote a description where an explanation was asked for, and this is coachable in a way that content gaps are not.

Then there is the scientific investigation, which is where families most often want help and where the boundaries are strictest. A tutor may teach the underlying skills, explain what the criteria reward, discuss whether a research question is viable, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the investigation, write it, or edit it to completion. The supervisor of record is the school teacher. We state that in writing before anyone starts, because in this market at least one provider sells completed internal assessments outright, and a student who buys one is risking their diploma.

On delivery, the position is simple and we state it rather than imply it. IB Gram does not send a physics tutor to a Marina address and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Diploma physics tuition for UAE families is one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a subject with this few genuine Higher Level specialists in any one neighbourhood, that is what makes the right tutor reachable at 6pm on a weekday rather than whoever happens to live within a short drive of your tower.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-marina.programmesIntro: Physics at a Marina-serving IB school arrives in three stages, and the right support looks different at each. The fourth entry below is the parallel British route, included because several households in this cluster are choosing between them for the same child.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Two years, taken at Standard or Higher Level, assessed on two written papers plus an internally assessed scientific investigation. Content is organised into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level extends most themes rather than adding separate ones, which is why a student can appear to be coping until the extension content arrives.
programmes.countryNote: In the Marina cluster physics Higher Level is the subject most often dropped to Standard Level at the end of the first Diploma year. The decision usually happens in April or May of Year 12, and it is far better taken on the evidence of a marked paper than on how the term felt. A short diagnostic block before that decision is one of the highest-value uses of tutoring in the whole two years.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The stage before the Diploma in continuum schools. Sciences are assessed against four criteria rather than by paper, and the mathematical demand is markedly lower than Diploma physics requires. MYP 5 students heading for physics Higher Level benefit most from algebraic fluency and from graph interpretation, neither of which the MYP criteria push hard.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single most common source of a surprise in the first Diploma term around the Marina. A student with strong MYP science grades meets Diploma physics and finds the mathematics, not the physics, is the obstacle. Addressing it in the summer between MYP 5 and Year 12 costs a fraction of addressing it in November.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the entry route
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are the usual codes in the British-curriculum schools near the Marina. Extended or Higher tier is effectively a prerequisite for Diploma physics Higher Level, because the algebraic rearrangement and graph work assumed on day one of the Diploma is the Extended tier content rather than the Core.
programmes.countryNote: A student arriving into a Diploma school from an IGCSE school elsewhere in Dubai may have sat Core tier physics, which leaves a real gap into Higher Level. It is identifiable in an hour and closeable over a summer, and it is much better found in July than in a November test.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the Diploma
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They sit on the timetable in addition to the six Diploma subjects, the core and the investigation.
programmes.countryNote: For a Diploma physics student this matters mainly as timetable pressure. A Higher Level physics student in a Dubai school carries a genuinely full week, and the realistic conclusion is often that one weekly tutoring hour has to replace something rather than be added to everything.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: Diploma physics is examined as a set of topic areas with a mathematical skill set running underneath them. Below is each area, what Higher Level adds, and the specific loss that recurs in marked papers rather than a general comment about difficulty.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: Motion graphs, projectile motion, Newton's laws and the free-body diagram. The reliable loss is a free-body diagram drawn with forces that do not act on the chosen body, after which every subsequent line of working is wrong but internally consistent. Graph gradient and area interpretation is examined constantly and taught quickly.

subjects.name: Work, energy and momentum
subjects.description: Conservation arguments, elastic and inelastic collisions, power and efficiency. Students lose marks by invoking conservation of energy where momentum is the conserved quantity, and by failing to state the system within which the conservation applies. At Higher Level the questions combine both in a single multi-step item.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and gases
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the kinetic model and the ideal gas relationships. The commonest error is unit mismatch between kelvin and degrees Celsius inside a single calculation. Explanations of the kinetic model are marked for the molecular mechanism, not for a restatement of the gas law.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Travelling and standing waves, superposition, the Doppler effect, interference and diffraction. The standing-wave questions reward a precise account of nodes, antinodes and boundary conditions. At Higher Level the interference content goes further and is a common source of partial marks because the path difference argument is written loosely.

subjects.name: Gravitational and electric fields
subjects.description: Field strength, potential, and the relationship between them. This is where the Higher Level extension bites hardest: potential and potential energy are distinct quantities with distinct signs, and a student who has treated them loosely at Standard Level will lose whole questions at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Electric circuits
subjects.description: Resistance, internal resistance, potential dividers and power. Circuit questions reward practice more than reading, and the potential divider is the single most commonly misread circuit in the course. Internal resistance questions are usually lost at the point where the terminal potential difference is confused with the electromotive force.

subjects.name: Magnetic effects and induction
subjects.description: Magnetic force on a current and on a moving charge, and electromagnetic induction. Direction conventions are where marks go: a student who has learned a hand rule without knowing which quantity each finger represents will be right about half the time, which is indistinguishable from guessing.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and atomic spectra. Binding energy per nucleon is reliably misread off the curve. At Higher Level the quantum content extends and the explanations are marked for the photon argument rather than for a wave description.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and data analysis
subjects.levels: Both levels, examined on both papers
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, error bars and the uncertainty in a gradient. This is examined directly in the data-based section and indirectly everywhere else, and it is the single most under-taught part of the course relative to the marks it carries.

subjects.name: Mathematical tools for physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, logarithms, small-angle approximations, unit algebra and significant figures. Most physics marks lost by otherwise strong students are lost here rather than in the physics, which is why a diagnostic session should look at working rather than at content knowledge.

sections.heading: What the current Diploma physics course actually contains
paragraphs: If you are judging a tutor, start by asking them to describe the structure of the course your child is sitting. The current guide organises content into five themes rather than a numbered core with options, and a tutor who reaches for the older arrangement is telling you when they last taught it. The themes are: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Running underneath them are tools strands covering experimental technique, use of technology and the mathematics the course assumes.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with more homework. In most themes Higher Level extends the same material further rather than introducing separate topics, which has a specific consequence: a student can look as though they are coping for two terms and then meet the extension content and fall away quickly. Fields is the clearest example. Treating potential and potential energy loosely is survivable at Standard Level and is not survivable at Higher Level, where the sign conventions and the relationship between field strength and potential gradient are examined directly.

The table below maps the themes and names where the Higher Level extension usually causes trouble. Treat it as orientation rather than as a specification: the authoritative document is the subject guide your child's school issues, and the IB publishes its own course information at ibo.org. Ask your child's teacher for the school's scheme of work, because the order in which themes are taught varies between schools and a tutor should follow that order rather than impose their own.

sections.heading: How the marks are divided, and what each component rewards
paragraphs: Diploma physics is assessed on two written papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. Paper 1 carries a multiple-choice section and a data-based section; Paper 2 carries short and extended response questions; the investigation is marked in school against published criteria and moderated by the IB. Higher Level papers are longer than Standard Level papers and carry a higher content ceiling. For the exact durations and percentage weightings applying to your child's session, read the assessment outline in the subject guide the school issues, because those details have changed between guide versions and a figure copied from an out-of-date page is worse than no figure.

What matters more than the exact percentages is what each component rewards, because that is what support should be aimed at. The multiple-choice section rewards breadth and speed and punishes a student who has learned three themes thoroughly and skimmed two. The data-based section rewards uncertainty handling, graph work and the ability to read an unfamiliar experiment, which is a skill set rather than a body of knowledge. The extended response questions reward command-term discipline. And the investigation rewards design quality and honest evaluation far more than it rewards an impressive-sounding topic.

That breakdown has a practical implication for how a family buys support. A student weak across the board needs content work, and that is slow. A student whose content is sound but whose data-based section is poor needs something much narrower and much faster: perhaps four sessions on uncertainty propagation, error bars, gradient uncertainty and the language of evaluation. Diagnosing which situation you are in takes one marked paper, which is why the first session should always start from your child's own script.

The table below sets out what each component asks for and where marks are commonly surrendered. It deliberately carries no durations or percentages, so that nothing on this page can go stale against a guide revision.

sections.heading: Command terms: the marks a competent physicist still loses
paragraphs: A striking share of lost marks in Diploma physics has nothing to do with physics. It is the gap between what the question asked for and what the student provided. The command terms are defined, the markschemes are written against those definitions, and a student who has never had the difference made explicit will write a good description where an explanation was required and score about half.

Describe asks what happens. Explain asks why, and a credited explanation names a mechanism rather than restating the observation. Deduce asks for a conclusion with the reasoning that forces it. Suggest invites a plausible answer where more than one exists, and is marked generously if the reasoning is sound. Outline asks for the main points without development. Discuss asks for more than one side. State requires no working at all, which means spending two minutes on working for a state question costs time and earns nothing.

This is learnable in a handful of sessions and it is almost never taught deliberately, because a school teacher with a full class and a syllabus to finish has limited time to mark forty short answers per student against the published wording. One to one is the format where it can be done. The method is unglamorous: the student writes the answer, the tutor marks it against the markscheme language, and the student rewrites it. After thirty or forty of those the habit is set and it transfers across both papers.

It is worth saying what this is not. It is not learning to game a markscheme, and a page promising that would be selling something hollow. It is learning to answer the question that was asked, which is a legitimate academic skill and the one most likely to be missing in a student who understands the subject and underperforms on it.
bullets: Explain requires a mechanism; a restated observation scores as a description
Deduce requires the reasoning that forces the conclusion, not just the conclusion
State requires no working, so working on a state question is time spent for nothing
Discuss requires more than one position to be put

sections.heading: Uncertainties, significant figures and the graph nobody taught properly
paragraphs: Ask a Diploma physics student to state the percentage uncertainty in a quantity they measured, propagate it through a calculation involving a square, and then quote the answer to an appropriate number of significant figures, and you will learn more in four minutes than a diagnostic test would tell you in an hour. This skill set is examined directly in the data-based section of Paper 1 and indirectly throughout Paper 2, and it underpins the investigation. It is also the part of the course most often left to be picked up rather than taught.

The specific gaps recur. Students add absolute uncertainties where they should add fractional ones. They propagate through a square without doubling the fractional uncertainty. They draw a line of best fit without considering the steepest and shallowest lines that still pass through the error bars, which is how the uncertainty in a gradient is found. They quote a calculated result to eight significant figures because that is what the calculator showed. And they write an evaluation that lists sources of error without saying which one dominates, which is the judgement the criteria actually reward.

Each of those is a short, concrete fix. A block of four to six sessions aimed only at this will frequently move a physics grade more than a term of general content revision, because the loss is concentrated and systematic rather than spread thin. It is also durable: a student who has learned to handle uncertainty properly keeps the marks for the rest of the course and carries the skill into a university laboratory.

For a Marina family this is a useful thing to ask about when choosing a tutor, precisely because it separates a physicist from a physics teacher. Somebody who works with data professionally will handle uncertainty correctly. Somebody who teaches this course will also know which of these errors the markscheme penalises and how heavily, which is the part a parent is paying for.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: supervisor, tutor, and the line between them
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation is the component families most want help with and the one where the rules are tightest. The supervisor of record is the teacher at your child's school. They confirm the work is the student's own. A tutor sits outside that relationship entirely, which defines what a tutor may usefully do and what would put your child's diploma at risk.

What a tutor may do: teach the physics the investigation rests on; explain what each criterion rewards and in what language; discuss whether a proposed research question can realistically generate data that can be analysed; teach uncertainty treatment and graphing; read a draft the student has written and give feedback the student then acts on themselves. That is a substantial and legitimate contribution, and it is usually the difference between a competent investigation and a strong one.

What a tutor must not do: choose the research question, design the method, process the data, draft any part of the report, or edit it to completion. We put that in writing before the first session. At least one provider in this market sells completed internal assessments as a product. That is academic malpractice under IB rules, the exposure falls on the student rather than on the seller, and the sanction can reach the whole diploma rather than the single subject. If a provider's pitch includes delivering the work, that is the end of the conversation.

One practical note on viability, because it is where most marks are quietly lost. Students pick research questions that sound impressive and cannot produce analysable data: too few data points, a dependent variable that barely changes across the range, or equipment the school does not have. A tutor reading the proposal before three weeks have gone into it is the cheapest intervention available on this component, and it is entirely within the rules.

sections.heading: Five questions that reveal whether a tutor knows Higher Level
paragraphs: A profile will say Diploma physics. These questions tell you whether that means the current course at Higher Level. They take under ten minutes on a trial call and none of them is a trick; a teacher who marks the paper answers each one immediately, and the fluency is what you are buying.

First: describe how the course is structured, and which themes carry the heaviest Higher Level extension. A current answer names the themes and identifies fields as the usual stumbling block. Second: what is the difference between gravitational potential and gravitational potential energy, and why do the signs matter? Third: how do you find the uncertainty in a gradient from a graph with error bars? Fourth: what does a credited explain answer contain that a describe answer does not? Fifth: what is the first thing you would check in a student's proposed research question for the investigation?

Then one about process rather than physics: what would the first three sessions cover, and why those? The answer you want references a marked paper and names specific losses. The answer that should concern you is an offer to go through the themes from the beginning, because that ignores the evidence already sitting in your child's script and is the slowest route available.

A final check belongs here and it concerns legality rather than competence. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so ignore any specific figure quoted at you. Asking a tutor whether they hold it is a reasonable question and a permitted tutor will answer it without friction.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs here, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Look first at the gap between in-home and online rates, because it is the most misread number in this market. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with home tutors reaching AED 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. For a Marina or Palm address the upper end of the in-home range is where you will usually land, because the journey is long and the parking is slow. What that premium buys, almost entirely, is the journey. It does not buy a better physicist.

The rest of the published picture, for context. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is the group and university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED quotes AED 650 at the named end. Monthly estimates in the same Bestimate table run AED 240 to 600 for budget weekly sessions, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Each figure is that provider's own, recorded in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price.

For Diploma physics Higher Level specifically, the travel premium has a second cost that nobody prices: it narrows the pool to people who can reach your building. Higher Level physics cohorts in Dubai schools are small, the number of people who teach the current guide at that level is correspondingly small, and the subset of those who are both free at 6pm and within twenty minutes of a Marina tower may be empty. Paying a premium to restrict your choice is the wrong trade on this subject more than on almost any other.

To be explicit about what we sell: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and the in-home figures above are other providers' market rates rather than an offer. Tuition is one to one over live video, there is no rate card published on these pages, and the sensible first step is a free trial lesson followed by an honest estimate of how many sessions the diagnosed problem needs. Ask any provider whether a quote includes VAT, because the published market figures are inconsistent on that point.

sections.heading: Physics Higher Level, and what Gulf and overseas universities read into it
paragraphs: Physics Higher Level is often taken because of what it keeps open rather than because the student loves it, and that is a legitimate reason. Engineering courses commonly expect it alongside Higher Level mathematics, and the combination is read as evidence of quantitative capability well beyond either subject alone. Where a student is aiming at engineering, the honest advice is usually to hold the Higher Level and get support, rather than drop to Standard Level and discover in Year 13 that a target course assumed otherwise.

Medicine is the more commonly confused case. Chemistry Higher Level is the subject most medical routes expect, with biology frequently paired, and physics is seldom the deciding subject. A Marina student taking physics Higher Level primarily because it sounds rigorous, while carrying chemistry at Standard Level, may have the combination the wrong way round for their stated ambition. That is a conversation for the school's university counsellor in the first Diploma year, not for a tutoring website, but it is worth raising before the level decision is taken.

On the regulatory side, UAE recognition of a Diploma for local university entry runs through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, not through any tutoring provider. The Ministry's published requirements for the British track are specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No equivalent IB points threshold has been verified from the Ministry's own publications, so do not rely on a figure you see on a tutoring site, including an estimate. Check the current requirement with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority directly.

The level decision itself usually arrives in April or May of the first Diploma year, and it should be taken on a marked paper rather than on how the year felt. A short diagnostic block before that point is one of the highest-value uses of tutoring across the whole two years, because it converts an anxious guess into an evidenced decision. Whichever way the decision goes, it is better made with the mark breakdown in front of everybody.

process.title: Tell us the level and the themes taught so far
process.description: Standard or Higher Level, which themes the school has covered, and whether the scientific investigation has started. If you have a recent marked paper, send it; a photograph is enough. The marked script converts a general worry into a list of specific losses, which is what a first session should work from.

process.title: Name a slot that survives a full Diploma week
process.description: Higher Level physics students in Dubai schools carry genuinely full weeks, including the mandatory UAE subjects on top of six Diploma courses. Give the quietest evening and a backup, and tell us which days carry co-curricular commitments so the slot is not placed on one of them.

process.title: Take the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: One session at no cost, spent on a question your child lost marks on. The tutor establishes whether the loss was content, mathematics, uncertainty handling or command-term reading. Those four causes need four different responses, and guessing between them wastes a term.

process.title: Agree a plan with an end point
process.description: After the trial you get a short list: the themes or skills to target, roughly how many sessions, and when the plan will be reviewed. For a data-skills problem the honest answer is often four to six sessions rather than a standing weekly hour, and we will say so.

process.title: Review at the level decision and after each mock
process.description: The April or May level decision in Year 12 and every subsequent mock are the natural review points. The topic list is rewritten from the mark breakdown each time, and where physics has stabilised the sessions stop or move rather than continue out of habit.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the current guide
whyPoints.description: Tutors are matched against the five-theme structure of the course your child is actually sitting, at the correct level. A tutor working from an older arrangement teaches correctly and emphasises wrongly, and the mismatch shows up in which questions they choose to practise rather than in anything you would spot on a profile.

whyPoints.title: Data skills treated as a subject in their own right
whyPoints.description: Uncertainty propagation, error bars, gradient uncertainty and significant figures carry marks directly in the data-based section and indirectly everywhere else. They are the most under-taught part of the course relative to the marks at stake, and they respond to a short, focused block rather than to general revision.

whyPoints.title: Command terms marked, not mentioned
whyPoints.description: The method is writing an answer, having it marked against the published wording, and rewriting it. Thirty or forty of those sets a habit that transfers across both papers. A full class rarely allows for that volume of individual marking; one to one does.

whyPoints.title: The investigation boundary stated in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the physics, explains the criteria, tests whether a research question is viable, and gives feedback on a draft your child wrote. A tutor does not design, draft or edit the work. The school teacher is the supervisor of record and nothing we do interferes with that.

whyPoints.title: No journey in the price, and a wider pool
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for comparable qualifications; most of that gap is travel. For Higher Level physics the second effect matters more: dropping the radius is what makes a genuine specialist reachable on a weekday evening.

whyPoints.title: Thin coverage disclosed before booking
whyPoints.description: Higher Level physics cohorts are small and specialist availability varies by time slot. Where the best honest match is a weekend morning or a short wait, we say so rather than filling a Tuesday with somebody who has not taught the current guide.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a physics tutor knows the current Diploma course?
faqs.answer: Ask them to describe how the course is structured and which themes carry the heaviest Higher Level extension. A current answer names the five themes and identifies fields as the usual stumbling block, because potential and potential gradient are examined directly there. Then ask how they would find the uncertainty in a gradient from a graph with error bars, and what a credited explain answer contains that a describe answer does not. A teacher who marks the paper answers all three instantly. Somebody working from the older numbered core and options arrangement will describe a course your child is not sitting.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics just Standard Level with more content?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference is structural rather than a matter of volume. Higher Level extends most of the same themes further instead of adding separate ones, which produces a specific pattern: a student appears to cope for two terms and then meets the extension material and falls away quickly. Fields is where this shows up most. Treating gravitational potential and gravitational potential energy loosely is survivable at Standard Level and is not at Higher Level, where the sign conventions and the field-potential relationship are examined head on. Higher Level papers are also longer, which changes how timing has to be practised.

faqs.question: My son is strong at physics but keeps losing marks. What is going on?
faqs.answer: In most cases one of three things, and a marked paper will tell you which in minutes. Command terms: a good description written where an explanation was required scores about half, because a credited explanation names a mechanism. Uncertainties: adding absolute uncertainties where fractional ones were needed, or propagating through a square without doubling the fractional uncertainty. Or units and rounding: a kelvin and Celsius mismatch mid-calculation, or rounding at an intermediate step so the final accuracy cannot be defended. None of those is a physics gap, and all three respond quickly to one-to-one correction.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the scientific investigation without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the physics the investigation rests on, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a research question can realistically produce analysable data, teach uncertainty treatment and graphing, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the question, design the method, process the data or write any part of the report. The school teacher remains the supervisor of record. We state this in writing before the first session, because at least one provider in this market sells completed internal assessments and the sanction for that falls on the student.

faqs.question: What is the most common mistake in choosing an investigation topic?
faqs.answer: Picking something that sounds impressive and cannot produce data worth analysing. The usual failures are too few data points across the range, a dependent variable that barely moves, equipment the school does not actually have, or a design where the uncertainty swamps the effect being measured. Three weeks can disappear before that becomes obvious. Having someone read the proposal before the practical work starts is the cheapest useful intervention on this component and is entirely within the rules, because testing viability is advice rather than design.

faqs.question: We are deciding whether to drop physics from Higher to Standard Level. When?
faqs.answer: The decision usually arrives in April or May of the first Diploma year, and it should rest on a marked paper rather than on how the year has felt. Before that point a short diagnostic block is one of the highest-value uses of tutoring in the whole two years, because it converts an anxious guess into an evidenced choice. Where a student is aiming at engineering, holding Higher Level and getting support is often better than dropping and discovering in Year 13 that a target course assumed otherwise. Where the ambition is medicine, chemistry at Higher Level usually matters more than physics does.

faqs.question: How much does an online Diploma physics tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors advertising IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase listing AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with BartyED quoting AED 650 at the named end, and the budget online tier starting around AED 33 to 65 at EdFlik and Tutopiya. Those are each provider's own published rates recorded in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. We publish no rate card on these pages.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home physics tutor quoted so much higher in this area?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for the journey. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with home tutors reaching AED 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for comparable qualifications. For a Marina, Palm or Bluewaters address the upper end is where a visiting tutor usually lands, since the drive is long and the parking is slow. The premium buys travel, not a better physicist, and it has a hidden second cost: it restricts you to specialists who can reach your building, which on Higher Level physics may mean nobody.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to our apartment in Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Diploma physics tuition for UAE families is delivered one to one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For this subject that is an advantage rather than a compromise. Higher Level physics cohorts in Dubai schools are small, so the number of people teaching the current guide at that level is small, and the subset who are both free at 6pm and close to your tower may be empty. Removing the journey is what makes the right tutor reachable.

faqs.question: My daughter came from MYP sciences and is struggling in Year 12 physics. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually the mathematics rather than the physics. MYP sciences are assessed against criteria and the mathematical demand is markedly lower than Diploma physics assumes from the first week: algebraic rearrangement at speed, logarithms, unit algebra, and confident reading of gradients. A student with strong MYP grades can meet Diploma physics and find the obstacle is manipulation, not concepts. It is identifiable in one session and closeable in a short block, and it is much cheaper to address in the summer before Year 12 than in a November test week.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week should a Diploma student have?
faqs.answer: For most students, one, or one every two weeks through the first year. Physics is cumulative, so a fortnightly slot that keeps pace with the school's teaching order and catches misconceptions early is better value than a weekly hour started in a panic in Year 13. In the final term the pattern changes to timed questions and whole papers. Two sessions a week is justified where a specific component is failing and the household can protect both slots, but beyond that the independent practice attached to each session stops happening and the tutoring replaces it rather than prompting it.

faqs.question: Is it worth buying sessions only on uncertainties and data analysis?
faqs.answer: For a student whose content is sound and whose data-based work is weak, it is one of the best-value blocks available. Four to six sessions covering absolute against fractional uncertainty, propagation through powers, error bars, the uncertainty in a gradient from steepest and shallowest lines, significant figures and the language of evaluation will often move a grade more than a term of general revision. The loss is concentrated and systematic rather than spread thin. It is also durable, because the skill keeps earning marks for the rest of the course and transfers to university laboratory work.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both physics and maths for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and for this pairing it works better than most. Diploma physics assumes algebraic fluency, logarithms and confident graph work, and a tutor covering both can fix a manipulation problem in the maths slot and see the benefit appear in the physics the following week. A ninety-minute combined session usually beats two separate hours because the handover disappears. Where the student needs Higher Level physics specialism and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialism simultaneously, two tutors is the honest answer even though it is less convenient.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give us past papers and markschemes for physics?
faqs.answer: They should not hand over a library of them, and nor should any provider. Subject guides, past papers and markschemes are IB copyright and are distributed through the school and the IB's own channels. The correct behaviour is to work from the material your child's school provides and to reference the IB's published course information at ibo.org rather than redistributing documents. If a provider's main selling point is a private vault of papers, that is a question to ask rather than a benefit to accept, and it tells you something about how else they operate.

faqs.question: Does the physics tutoring have to pause during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: No, but the slot usually moves. The school day shortens during Ramadan and the household rhythm changes, so an early-evening session that worked in January often will not. The practical adjustment is to shift later, frequently after Iftar, and to use the period for content and derivation work rather than for timed papers, which need an alert start. Tell us before the period begins so the diary is rearranged once rather than cancelled repeatedly. Families who plan it in advance lose no continuity, and the long summer break is similarly workable because the lesson follows the laptop.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingHeading: Ask the five questions, then book the trial
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IB physics tutor for a Dubai Marina household, the fastest route to a decision is not a longer profile. It is five specific questions about the current course, the fields extension, gradient uncertainty, command terms and research-question viability, followed by one free trial lesson built around a question your child actually lost marks on. You will know within the hour whether you are dealing with somebody who teaches this course or somebody who knows physics. Send the level, the themes covered so far and a photograph of a recent marked paper, and the trial can be placed in an evening slot that fits a full Diploma week.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-media-ci.tutorsIntro: These are the physics tutors working with Diploma students across Al Sufouh, the Marina and the villa belt. Each teaches physics at a stated level rather than science in general, knows the data booklet, and takes the later weekday slots this corridor needs.

intro.heading: Why physics requests from this corridor arrive late and look the same
paragraphs: Dubai Media City is a free zone of offices and studios in Al Sufouh, between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, with Dubai Internet City inland and Dubai Knowledge Park along the tram line. It holds residential towers and no school. Secondary students here travel out to GEMS Wellington International School next door, into the Al Barsha cluster, or to the IB schools in Emirates Hills and the villa belt. They get home in the late afternoon, and physics homework is usually the last thing attempted.

Physics requests reach us later in the year than mathematics requests, and they arrive in a recognisable shape. A student who was comfortable in MYP or IGCSE science finds DP1 physics manageable until the first data-analysis question, then until the first uncertainty calculation, then until the Internal Assessment. By the DP1 spring the pattern is set: the content is understood, the marks are not arriving, and nobody can say precisely why.

The reason is that IB physics is assessed on three things at once, and only one of them is physics. The second is quantitative handling: uncertainties, gradients, units, significant figures, linearising a relationship. The third is written reasoning: explanation questions where the physics is correct and the chain of because-therefore is missing from the page. Students revise the first and lose marks on the second and third, which is why more content revision does not help.

The Internal Assessment adds a fourth demand. A single scientific investigation, marked out of 24 and moderated externally, in which the student designs the work, collects data, processes it with proper uncertainty treatment and evaluates the method. It is a research skill rather than a physics skill, and the commonest failure has nothing to do with physics: the research question is too broad to produce a usable dataset, which is discovered in week six.

That is the diagnosis this page is built around. Pin down which of the four demands is failing and the remedy is short and specific. Guess, and you buy a term of general physics teaching that the student already had at school. A tutor who cannot tell you which of the four is the problem after one marked paper is not going to find it in ten weeks.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm. Physics travels well over a screen because the work is a shared graph, a worked numerical solution and an annotated past-paper answer, and because the quantitative habits that need fixing are visible the moment the student writes anything.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-media-ci.programmesIntro: Physics appears in a different form in each programme this corridor's schools run, and the step between them is where most requests originate.

programmes.name: Diploma Physics
programmes.description: Offered at Higher and Standard Level, assessed by written papers plus a single internally assessed investigation marked out of 24 and moderated externally. A data booklet is provided in the examination, which changes what revision should consist of: not memorising equations, but knowing which of the provided ones applies and what each symbol means in the situation described.
programmes.countryNote: UAE IB schools sit the May session, with November as the second sitting used mainly for retakes. Specific IB session and results dates are not published here, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself; the school's IB coordinator is the authority on them. Around Media City, Diploma physics runs at GEMS Wellington International School and Dubai American Academy among others.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria out of eight, with criterion B asking for a method a stranger could repeat and criterion C for the processing and evaluation of the student's own data. Criterion C is the bridge to Diploma physics, and students who never mastered it in MYP 5 meet the same demand again in DP1 with higher stakes attached.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai complicates the picture because some IB schools run the MYP for all five years and others switch to IGCSE at 14. A student arriving in DP1 from MYP 5 sciences usually has better evaluation habits and weaker quantitative speed than one arriving from IGCSE Physics, and the two need opposite first sessions.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the other feeder
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1, both externally examined. Students arrive in DP1 with solid content recall and no experience of formal uncertainty treatment, because that is not what IGCSE physics examines. The gap is narrow and specific, and a short block in the summer before DP1 closes it almost entirely.
programmes.countryNote: Plenty of students in the Media City towers sit IGCSE physics and then move into the Diploma at a different school, which is exactly the transition that produces a confused DP1 autumn. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; Pearson runs May/June and November, with its November 2026 timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

programmes.name: A Level Physics as the alternative
programmes.description: The route most British-school students in this corridor take instead: narrower, deeper, with practical endorsement rather than a single assessed investigation, and no requirement to carry five other subjects. Families comparing them usually ask which is harder, when the better question is which assessment style suits the student.
programmes.countryNote: A student who writes well and works steadily across many commitments tends to do better in Diploma physics; a student who wants depth in three subjects and dislikes extended writing tends to do better at A Level. Both routes exist within a short bus ride of Media City, so the decision is a real one rather than a theoretical comparison.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-media-ci.subjectsIntro: Physics requests from this corridor concentrate in a small number of places. These are the topic areas and components, with what each is examined on and where marks disappear.

subjects.name: Mechanics and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy. Students handle numerical questions well and lose marks on explanation: describing a motion graph without naming the quantity the gradient represents, or asserting that momentum is conserved without stating the condition. The repair is written reasoning rather than more problems.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, gas laws and the kinetic model. Marks go missing in the algebraic rearrangement under time pressure and in the explanation questions where the molecular account has to be given in order. Students who describe temperature as heat lose marks repeatedly on the same misuse.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.levels: HL and SL; HL extends to more demanding treatment
subjects.description: Wave properties, superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference. The standing-wave questions and path-difference arguments are reliable mark-losers because students draw the diagram and omit the reasoning that connects it to the numerical answer. Diagram plus sentence is the habit worth drilling.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. This is the most requested topic from this corridor at both levels. Students who can calculate confidently still lose marks on potential-divider reasoning and on explaining what happens to a reading when a component changes, which is a sequencing problem.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational, electric and magnetic
subjects.description: Field strength and potential, orbital motion, electromagnetic induction. At Higher Level this is where students either consolidate or quietly fall behind, because the mathematics is denser and the conceptual distinction between field and potential is easy to blur. Weekly work through DP1 pays for itself here.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and particle physics
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy, mass defect and the standard model at Higher Level. Mark losses are mostly arithmetic with unit prefixes and powers, plus failing to state what a figure means physically. The content is well liked and the marks still leak, which tells you the problem is quantitative handling.

subjects.name: Energy production
subjects.description: Energy sources, efficiency, Sankey diagrams and the physics of generation. Questions here are frequently part-qualitative, and students write general environmental commentary where the mark scheme wants a specific physical mechanism and a number. It is one of the easiest places to recover marks with a short, targeted session.

subjects.name: Quantum and nuclear physics at Higher Level
subjects.description: Photoelectric effect, wave-particle duality, tunnelling and nuclear models. These topics arrive late in DP2 when revision has started, and are often half-learned as a consequence. Treating them deliberately in the autumn rather than the spring is a scheduling decision that changes the outcome.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and data analysis
subjects.levels: HL and SL; examined in Paper 1 and the investigation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation, error bars, gradient uncertainty from a graph, and the significant figures a result can honestly carry. This is the largest single source of avoidable loss in IB physics and the least deliberately taught. It is mechanical and it responds very quickly.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing axes so a relationship becomes linear, calculating a gradient with units, extracting a constant from the intercept. Students plot correctly and then quote a gradient without units or without showing the triangle, which the mark scheme does not forgive. A checklist fixes most of it.

subjects.name: The Internal Assessment investigation
subjects.levels: HL and SL, marked out of 24
subjects.description: One scientific investigation designed, conducted, processed and evaluated by the student, moderated externally. The usual failure is a research question too broad to produce a usable dataset, chosen early and discovered late. A tutor may coach the method and comment on the student's own drafts, and may not write any part of it.

subjects.name: The mathematics underneath

sections.heading: What an IB physics tutor search from Media City usually means
paragraphs: An IB physics tutor in Dubai Media City means, in practice, a physics specialist at a stated level, teaching one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, for a student who is almost always in DP1 or DP2 at a school elsewhere in the city. Media City has no school inside it; the nearest gates are in Al Sufouh and the Al Barsha cluster, and the nearest tuition centres are inland.

The request usually arrives with a vague description and a specific cause. The description is that physics is hard. The cause, nine times out of ten, is one of four things: uncertainty and graph handling, written reasoning in explanation questions, a stalled Internal Assessment, or algebraic slowness masquerading as conceptual weakness. Those four need different first sessions, and buying generic physics teaching gives the student more of what school already provides.

Pinning down which one it is takes a single marked paper and about twenty minutes. In uncertainty questions the loss is visible immediately. In explanation questions it looks like a correct statement with no because. A stalled Internal Assessment announces itself. Algebraic slowness shows as abandoned multi-step questions and arithmetic errors with unit prefixes, and it is the one most often misdiagnosed as a physics problem.

Once the diagnosis exists, where the tutor lives is irrelevant. Level matters, because Higher Level physics is not Standard Level with extra topics: the field and quantum content and the depth of written reasoning make it a different specification. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons are a shared screen with a graph, a worked numerical solution and an annotated answer, which is what physics teaching looks like anyway.

sections.heading: The assessment shape, and why the data booklet changes revision
paragraphs: IB physics is assessed by written papers plus a single internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 contains two distinct demands, multiple choice and data analysis, which students prepare for as if they were one thing. Paper 2 is extended response, where the marks sit in reasoning as much as in numbers. A data booklet is provided in the examination.

That last point reshapes what revision should be. If the equations are supplied, memorising them is close to worthless, and the skill being examined is selection: knowing which of the provided relationships applies to the situation described, what each symbol denotes in that context, and which quantity the question has actually given you. Students who revise by writing out equations are practising the one thing the examination has removed.

The data-analysis part of Paper 1 is where the most marks are available to a well-prepared student and the most are lost by an unprepared one. It asks for uncertainty handling, gradient extraction, significant figures and interpretation, all of which are mechanical and all of which reward practice over understanding. Most students have attempted far fewer data-analysis questions than multiple-choice ones, simply because they are less comfortable, which compounds the problem.

Exact weightings and durations are set by the current subject guide and can change between versions, so confirm the detail with your child's school and the official documentation. The shape in the table below is what matters for planning a term: where the marks are, what each component actually tests, and how the hours should therefore be divided.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: the quiet, expensive topic
paragraphs: If one section of this page is worth acting on, it is this one. Uncertainty treatment is the largest single source of avoidable marks in IB physics, it is assessed in Paper 1 and again in the investigation, and it is almost never taught deliberately because it sits in nobody's topic list. Schools cover it when a practical requires it and then move on.

The specific skills are finite: reading an instrument's resolution and converting it to an absolute uncertainty, converting between absolute, fractional and percentage forms, propagating through addition, multiplication and powers, drawing error bars, extracting a maximum and minimum gradient, and knowing how many significant figures a result can honestly carry. That is a short list. A student can become reliable at all of it in four to six focused sessions.

The reason it pays so well is that uncertainty marks are awarded for procedure rather than insight. There is no cleverness involved. A student who knows the procedure gets the marks every time the question appears, and it appears in every data-analysis section and throughout the investigation. Compare that with learning an extra topic, which may or may not be examined in the form the student practised.

The same logic applies to graph work. A gradient quoted without units scores less than one with them; a gradient quoted without the triangle shown invites a method mark to be withheld; axes without units lose marks before any physics happens. These are checklist items. A student who runs the checklist every time stops losing those marks permanently, which is a much better return than another hour on fields.

sections.heading: Topic by topic: where physics marks actually go
paragraphs: Students name topics when asked what is hard, and the names are usually right about discomfort and wrong about where the marks went. Marked papers show a consistent split: numerical questions are answered reasonably and explanation questions are answered incompletely, with the physics correct and the reasoning chain absent.

The commonest version is a student who writes a true statement instead of an argument. Asked to explain why a reading falls, they state that resistance increases. The mark scheme wants the sequence: resistance increases, so current falls, so the potential difference across the component falls, so the reading falls. Each link is a mark. Students who have never had an explanation answer marked in front of them do not know the links are separately credited.

The table sets out the topics this corridor asks for most, with the specific loss in each. Notice how few of the entries are about not knowing the physics. That is the point: by DP2 most students know more physics than their marks suggest, and the gap is in how the knowledge reaches the page. This is also why a term of tutoring can move a grade without covering new content.

Higher Level students have one extra exposure. The field and quantum material arrives late, often in the DP2 autumn when the Extended Essay and other Internal Assessments are also live, and it is frequently half-learned as a result. Scheduling that content deliberately earlier in the year is a planning decision that changes the outcome more than any amount of spring revision.

sections.heading: The investigation: 24 marks, one dataset, and a line nobody should cross
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment in IB physics is a single scientific investigation, designed and carried out by the student, marked out of 24 and moderated externally. It is the most controllable component of the course and the one students handle least well, and the reason is almost never physics.

Weak investigations fail at the research question. A student picks something broad and interesting, spends weeks on apparatus, and discovers in the processing stage that the data cannot answer the question asked. A narrow question with a clean independent variable, a measurable dependent variable and a sensible range produces a better mark than an ambitious question answered partially, every single time. The first session of investigation coaching is therefore usually spent replacing the question, and that is where the grade is won.

The second avoidable failure is planning the uncertainty treatment after the data is collected. If a student decides how they will propagate uncertainties before measuring anything, they measure the right things, repeat enough trials, and record instrument resolutions as they go. If they decide afterwards, half the information needed is missing and cannot be recovered without redoing the practical. This is a ten-minute conversation that saves a fortnight.

The boundary is firm and worth stating. A tutor may teach research design, uncertainty planning, data processing, graphing conventions and what each criterion rewards, and may read the student's own draft and say precisely where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure any part of the investigation, and may not supply a model to adapt. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; for the student, that is an academic honesty finding rather than a shortcut, and the school supervisor remains the authority on the process throughout.
