sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and when to change
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is not Standard Level with extra chapters. It carries additional content, including the heavier field and quantum material, and it raises the written reasoning demand across the whole paper. A student comfortable at Standard Level can be genuinely stuck at Higher Level for reasons that have nothing to do with effort.

The diagnostic question is about mathematics rather than physics. A student whose algebra is fluent, who can rearrange a three-term expression quickly and handle logarithms without hesitation, can usually carry Higher Level physics. A student whose algebra is slow will find that every physics question becomes an algebra question with a clock attached, and that the time cost appears in five other subjects as well.

Moving from Higher to Standard Level is usually administratively straightforward early in DP1 and progressively harder after that. It is also frequently the right decision, and it is under-made because it feels like a retreat. A student carrying three Higher Levels, an Extended Essay and a Diploma core is running a genuinely heavy week, and a physics Higher Level that consumes two evenings is being paid for by the other five subjects.

Check the university requirement before changing anything. Some engineering and physics programmes specify Higher Level physics; many others accept Standard Level alongside Higher Level mathematics. Requirements vary by institution, by country and by intake year, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas universities, so read the individual programme page rather than relying on a general rule or on a tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: Fitting physics into the week after the Al Barsha bus
paragraphs: Physics is the subject most often squeezed out of a Diploma week, because its homework is finite and skippable in a way that essay drafting is not. A student who runs short of time does the English draft and leaves the physics problem set, and by the time that pattern is visible in a report it has been running for a term.

The afternoon in this corridor sets the constraint. Most schools finish in the middle of the afternoon, the roads around the Al Barsha and villa belt gates stall for roughly an hour afterwards, and a bus serving several communities adds collection stops. A student from a Media City tower is usually home between four and five, sometimes later with an activity. The sensible physics slot in this corridor is between six and eight, after food and a short burst of school homework.

The weekly shape that works is one tutored hour, one problem set attempted alone, and one past-paper data-analysis section done to time. The independent work matters more in physics than in most subjects, because the skills being built are procedural and need repetition the student performs rather than watches. A session where the tutor solves and the student nods produces very little.

Two scheduling notes specific to physics. Sessions shift later during Ramadan rather than pausing, since a four-week gap in a procedural subject undoes more than it does in a content subject. And the week after a mock is the single most valuable session of the year: marking the paper properly against the scheme, question by question, is where the next eight weeks of work comes from, and most students never do it.

sections.heading: What a physics specialist costs, and where a generalist is enough
paragraphs: Published rates in Dubai give a clear structure. Budget online tutoring runs from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are published from AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors at IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

For physics the tier that matters depends on the diagnosis rather than on the level. A student whose problem is uncertainty procedure and graph checklists can be served well by a competent science tutor at the qualified band, because the material is mechanical and does not require a Higher Level physics specialist. A student whose problem is written reasoning in Higher Level field questions, or a stalled investigation heading for moderation, needs the specialist band and will waste money below it.

In-home visits are published between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour with travel included, and Bestimate's band for in-home work is AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For a procedural subject, eight shorter contacts beat four long ones: the skills need frequent repetition, not extended exposure. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

These are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram prices. The verifiable questions before you pay anything are the rate, whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether travel is inside the number, the cancellation terms and the remedy if the match is wrong. Three of the six strongest-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no rate at all, which is why a sourced comparison belongs here rather than in a brochure.

faqs.question: The physics seems understood and the marks still do not arrive. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of four things. Uncertainty and graph handling, which is procedural and rarely taught deliberately. Explanation answers that stop at a true statement instead of giving the chain of consequences the mark scheme credits link by link. A stalled Internal Assessment eating the time that revision needs. Or algebraic slowness, which makes every physics question a race. One marked paper distinguishes them in about twenty minutes, and each needs a different first session.

faqs.question: Why is uncertainty work worth more attention than another topic?
faqs.answer: Because the marks are awarded for procedure, so a student who knows the procedure earns them every time the question appears, and it appears in every data-analysis section and throughout the investigation. Four to six focused sessions makes a student reliable at all of it. Another topic may or may not be examined in the form practised.

faqs.question: If the data booklet is provided, what should revision actually consist of?

With the relationships supplied, the examined skill is knowing which one applies to the situation described, what each symbol means in that context, and which quantity the question has given you. Students who revise by writing out equations are practising the one thing the examination has removed. Better use of the same hour: past-paper questions where the first step is choosing the right relationship from the booklet and justifying the choice.

faqs.question: What does an explanation question in physics want that my child is not giving?
faqs.answer: A sequence, with each link separately credited. Asked why a reading falls, a student commonly writes that resistance increases and stops. The scheme wants resistance increases, so current falls, so the potential difference across the component falls, so the reading falls. Students who have never had an explanation answer marked in front of them do not know those links earn separate marks. Writing explanations out and having them marked, rather than discussed aloud, fixes this in two or three sessions.

faqs.answer: Narrow, with a clean independent variable, a measurable dependent variable and a sensible range. Almost every weak investigation failed at this step: a broad, interesting question was chosen early, weeks went into apparatus, and the processing stage revealed that the data cannot answer it. A narrow question answered properly outscores an ambitious one answered partially every time. If investigation coaching does one thing, it should replace the question in the first session.

faqs.question: When should the uncertainty plan for an investigation be decided?
faqs.answer: Before any data is collected, which almost nobody does. A student who knows in advance how they will propagate uncertainties measures the right quantities, takes enough repeats and records instrument resolutions as they go. A student who decides afterwards finds half the required information was never recorded and cannot be recovered without repeating the practical. It is a ten-minute conversation that routinely saves a fortnight and several marks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics Internal Assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor may teach research design, uncertainty planning, data processing, graphing conventions and what each criterion rewards, and may read the student's own draft and name exactly where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure any part of it, and may not supply a model to adapt. The school supervisor remains the authority on the process, and the most valuable legitimate help arrives before any data is collected.

faqs.answer: It is worth considering seriously and early, because the move is administratively simple in the first part of DP1 and much harder later. A Higher Level physics course that consumes two evenings a week is being paid for by the other five subjects and the Extended Essay. Check the specific university programme requirement first: some engineering and physics courses specify Higher Level physics, while many accept Standard Level alongside Higher Level mathematics. Read the programme page, not a general rule.

faqs.question: Which physics topics do students around Al Sufouh ask about most?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits by a clear margin, then waves and superposition, then thermal physics. At Higher Level, fields arrive late in the course and are frequently half-learned because they land in the DP2 autumn alongside the Extended Essay and other Internal Assessments. Scheduling that content deliberately earlier in the year changes the outcome more than spring revision does, and it is a planning decision rather than a teaching one.

This matters more in physics than in most subjects because the skills being built are procedural: uncertainty propagation, graph checklists, explanation chains. Live annotation of a data question is at least as effective as leaning over a table. The real limit is a student who will not engage without an adult physically present, which is a genuine constraint rather than a marketing objection.

intro.heading: Physics is a two-year subject, and the calendar decides what works when
paragraphs: Most families arrive at physics tutoring in a particular week, after a particular test, wanting the topic from that test fixed. That is almost always the wrong first move. IB Physics is assessed by two written papers plus a scientific investigation worth roughly twenty per cent, and the investigation is completed during the course. Which means that at any given point in the two years, there is a highest-value thing to be working on, and it is frequently not the topic that produced the bad mark.

In DP1, the highest-value work is the investigation and the uncertainty skills it requires. A research question agreed in the second half of DP1 that cannot produce enough measurable variation caps a fifth of the grade before revision begins, and no paper practice in the spring of DP2 recovers it. Uncertainty treatment, meanwhile, is examined on the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and assessed inside the investigation, so it pays twice.

In the autumn of DP2, the highest-value work is explain-question structure and the first serious timed papers. By the spring of DP2 the internal component is banked and the only remaining variable is the written papers, so the work narrows to timed questions on identified weak themes. Doing that narrowing in October rather than in March is what separates a plan from a reaction.

Dubai Production City has no IB World School inside it. Students travel to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, to the Al Barsha ring, or to Fairgreen International School to the south. The bus day is long, which compresses the evening and makes short frequent physics sessions a better investment than long weekend blocks, particularly for the kind of work that needs concentration rather than stamina.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. For physics the online format carries a real advantage: graph work, error bars and gradient calculations are done on a shared whiteboard and saved, so a student working on the data-analysis section in April is reading their own corrected working from November.

We do not publish IB session or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be correct. UAE IB schools sit the May session; confirm exact windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. What this page sets out instead is the sequence and the lead times, which do not move, and the component structures published in the subject guide your child's school already holds. Reviewed October 2026, and every figure on it is attributed to the source it came from.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-producti.programmesIntro: Three stages matter for physics in this cluster. The MYP-to-DP step and the IGCSE-to-DP step produce different gaps, and treating them the same way is the most common planning error we see.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The current syllabus organises content into themes with Higher Level extensions, covering space time and motion, the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields, and nuclear and quantum physics. Assessment is Paper 1, with multiple-choice and data-analysis sections, Paper 2 extended response, and the scientific investigation at roughly twenty per cent.
programmes.countryNote: Production City students commute to campuses that set their own internal deadlines for the investigation, typically clustering it in the autumn and winter of DP2 after data collection late in DP1. Ask for the school's internal deadline calendar at the first parents' evening of DP1, because that document, not the IB's, is what governs the student's year.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria scored one to eight: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criteria B and C are direct preparation for the Diploma investigation, and students who take them seriously arrive in DP1 already able to frame a research question.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP entrant typically arrives in DP1 well prepared for the investigation and poorly prepared for timed papers, because the MYP has no external examination. The final MYP term is the right place to introduce timed questions, command-term reading and the habit of naming a physical principle rather than describing an outcome.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics entry route
programmes.description: Students entering DP1 from Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 arrive with solid procedural physics and timed-paper experience, and with almost no experience of open-ended investigation. They can rearrange equations and recall definitions; they have rarely designed an experiment, chosen a measurement range or propagated an uncertainty.
programmes.countryNote: Al Furjan and Jebel Ali send more IGCSE entrants into the Diploma than Dubai Investments Park does. For those students the first term of DP1 should prioritise experimental design and uncertainty, not content, because the content advantage they already hold will carry them for a term while the investigation will not wait.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-producti.subjectsIntro: The physics themes that generate the most requests in this cluster, with the specific place marks go missing. These notes come from marking scripts rather than from a syllabus summary.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and circular motion. Marks go missing in sign conventions and in free-body diagrams drawn without labelled forces. A student who assigns down as positive in one part of a question and negative in the next loses marks their physics had already earned.

subjects.name: Energy and work
subjects.description: Work, power, efficiency and energy transfers. The recurring failure is an energy argument stated without identifying the system boundary, so the examiner cannot see which transfers are being counted. Naming the system first turns a vague answer into a scoring one.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. The reliable trap is a potential divider treated as a series circuit without accounting for the load. Students also lose marks explaining a change in brightness without naming the quantity that changed.

subjects.name: Fields: gravitational and electric
subjects.description: Field strength, potential, and potential energy, plus orbital motion. The distinction between field strength and potential is the single most commonly muddled pair in the course, and the mark scheme is unforgiving about it because the units give the answer away.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Superposition, interference, diffraction, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Standing wave questions are lost on diagrams: nodes and antinodes unlabelled, or a harmonic drawn with the wrong number of half-wavelengths for the stated boundary conditions.

subjects.name: Thermal and particulate physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the gas laws and kinetic theory. Students manage the calculations and lose marks on kinetic-theory explanations, where the mark scheme wants molecular behaviour named rather than a macroscopic restatement of the observation.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, mass defect and the photoelectric effect. Binding energy per nucleon questions are lost on arithmetic with unit conversion between atomic mass units and joules, which is mechanical and worth drilling until it is automatic.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and data analysis
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation, error bars and gradient uncertainty from a best and worst line of fit. Examined on the Paper 1 data-analysis section and assessed inside the investigation, which makes it the highest-value single skill in the course.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: A single internally assessed piece worth roughly twenty per cent, assessed across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design constrains every criterion that follows, which is why the question matters more than the write-up.

sections.heading: Two years of physics, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May session, and almost every deadline that actually governs a physics student's two years is set by the school rather than by the IB. The investigation has an internal submission date. Data collection has a window before that. Mocks are internal. The student's year is shaped by a calendar their coordinator publishes, and most families never ask for it.

Counting backwards makes the priorities obvious. The written papers come last and need timed practice in the final two terms. The internal component comes earlier and needs design work in DP1 and writing in the autumn of DP2. Uncertainty skills sit underneath both and therefore belong at the very start, because they are the only thing in the course that is assessed twice.

What goes wrong is almost always sequencing. A family starts tutoring in the spring of DP2 because a mock went badly, and discovers that the twenty per cent held by the investigation is already fixed, that the uncertainty work needed for the data-analysis section was never built, and that the remaining weeks can only address the written papers. The hours still help. They help less than the same hours spent eighteen months earlier.

Ask the IB coordinator for the internal deadline calendar at the first parents' evening of DP1 and keep it visible. We build the plan around it, and we re-check every four to six weeks because those dates move more often than families expect.

sections.heading: Uncertainty, the one skill that pays twice
paragraphs: If a Production City family can only buy a handful of physics hours across two years, they should spend them on uncertainty. It is the only part of the course examined in the written papers and assessed inside the internal component, and it is the part schools have least time to teach properly because it sits across topics rather than inside one.

The content is finite and learnable. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, and how each is written. Propagation through sums, differences, products, quotients and powers. Error bars plotted from absolute uncertainties. Gradient uncertainty taken from best and worst lines of fit through those error bars. Deciding how many significant figures a result can honestly carry given the precision of the measurements.

Marks go missing in predictable places. A student quotes a result to four significant figures from measurements good to two. A student propagates uncertainty through a sum by multiplying fractional uncertainties. A student draws error bars and then takes the gradient of the best fit line only, with no worst line and therefore no gradient uncertainty at all. Each of those is a handful of marks on the data-analysis section and a criterion-level problem in the investigation.

Taught as one system rather than as scattered rules, it takes three or four focused sessions. Taught topic by topic as it comes up, it never quite settles, which is why so many students arrive in DP2 able to do the physics and unable to say how well they know it.
bullets: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty taught as one system, not three rules
Propagation: add absolutes for sums and differences, fractionals for products and quotients
Error bars plotted from absolute uncertainties, in both directions where relevant
Gradient uncertainty needs a worst-fit line, not just a best-fit one
Significant figures in a result are limited by the precision of the measurements

sections.heading: Explain questions, and the gap between knowing and scoring
paragraphs: The most common pattern in a physics script from this cluster is a student who clearly understands what happens and scores two marks out of four for saying so. The reason is almost always that they described the outcome instead of naming the principle, and the mark scheme awards the principle.

A question asking why the brightness of a lamp changes when a second lamp is added in parallel wants the total resistance, the consequence for current drawn from the supply, the effect of internal resistance on terminal potential difference, and then the brightness. A student who writes that the lamp gets dimmer because more current goes elsewhere has described the result and named nothing, and the mark scheme has no line to award.

The structure that fixes it is mechanical. Name the physical quantity that changes. Name the relationship that connects it to the next quantity. State the direction of the change. Then state the observable consequence. Four steps, in that order, and the answer usually earns every available mark without being longer than what the student was writing before.

The same discipline applies to command terms generally. State wants a fact. Describe wants an account. Explain wants a mechanism. Discuss wants balance. Outline wants brevity. A student writing a paragraph for a two-mark state question is not being thorough; they are spending four minutes on two marks and will run out of time on Paper 2. Allocating roughly a minute per mark, and glancing at the mark value before starting, is a habit worth more than any extra content revision in the final term.
bullets: Name the quantity that changes, then the relationship, then the direction, then the effect
Describing an outcome scores nothing on an explain question, however correct it is
A two-mark state question wants one line, not a paragraph
Time should be allocated by mark value, not by how interesting the question is
Command-term definitions are published in the subject guide the school holds

sections.heading: The investigation, criterion by criterion and deadline by deadline
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is a single piece of internally assessed work worth roughly twenty per cent, assessed across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Almost no competitor page in this market names a single criterion, which is strange, because the criteria are the entire instruction and they sit in the subject guide every school holds.

Research design decides the rest. A question that cannot produce enough measurable variation across a sensible range leaves the student with a flat dataset, which makes the data-analysis criterion hard and the conclusion criterion nearly impossible. Students choose questions they find interesting rather than questions their apparatus can answer, and the marks follow the apparatus.

The deadline structure matters as much as the criteria. Design has to be settled before the data collection window opens, because the window is finite and shared with a class. Data collection has to finish before the write-up period, with enough repeats to justify an uncertainty. Writing has to finish before the school's internal submission date, which is typically in the autumn or winter of DP2 and is not negotiable.

Our role is bounded and stated plainly. We teach what each criterion asks for, interrogate the research question before time is spent on it, discuss whether the method will produce usable data, and give feedback on drafts the student wrote. We do not write, rewrite or complete any part of an investigation. One operator in our research sells completed internal assessments; buying one is a malpractice risk carried by the student.
bullets: Research design constrains data analysis, conclusion and evaluation
Test the question against the apparatus before the data window opens
Enough repeats to justify an uncertainty, not just enough to plot a line
Evaluation needs stated limitations and realistic improvements, not apologies
We teach criteria and review the student's drafts; we never write the work

sections.heading: Reading a physics mock at component level
paragraphs: A mock grade in physics is almost uninformative, because the grade blends three completely different failure modes. The script separates them, and the school will provide component marks on request. Ask for them before deciding what to buy.

Pattern one is theme-specific content gaps, visible as clusters of blank or abandoned questions in particular areas. Fields and quantum physics are the usual candidates, because they arrive late and abstractly. This needs teaching, in dependency order, and it takes weeks rather than days.

Pattern two is explain-question structure, visible as attempted questions marked at half the available credit across the whole paper. This is the fastest thing to fix and the largest single pool of recoverable marks in most scripts. Three or four sessions of deliberate structure work changes it measurably.

Pattern three is the data-analysis section, which is diagnostic on its own. A student who scores well on multiple choice and poorly on data analysis has an uncertainty problem rather than a physics problem, and treating it as a physics problem wastes a term. The three patterns need different work, different numbers of hours and different tutors' attention, and the only way to tell them apart is the script.

Two smaller patterns are worth naming because they are cheap to fix and often dismissed as carelessness. A script with repeated arithmetic slips involving unit conversion, particularly between atomic mass units and joules or between millimetres and metres, needs an hour or two of drilling rather than any physics teaching at all. And a script that is strong at the start and thin at the end is a pacing problem, solved by allocating time against mark value under timed conditions. Neither is a knowledge failure, and treating either as one wastes weeks that the student does not have in the spring of DP2.

sections.heading: What two years of physics support costs in Dubai
paragraphs: Think across the two years rather than per hour, because that is how the decision actually plays out. A weekly session through DP1 and DP2 is roughly sixty to seventy hours. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month, with mid-tier at AED 600-1,200.

By the hour, the Dubai bands read as follows, all taken from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table in October 2026. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650.

For physics specifically, the uncertainty and investigation work genuinely requires the specialist band, because a tutor who has not supervised an investigation against the published criteria cannot give criterion-level feedback. Content catch-up on kinematics or circuits does not, and paying specialist rates for it is the standard overspend in this subject.

A useful piece of context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. These are market figures and not IB Gram prices. We publish no price list here and start with a free trial lesson instead.

sections.heading: Practicals, honesty and the regulators
paragraphs: A question Production City families reasonably ask is whether online physics tutoring can support practical work. For the parts that are assessed, yes. Experimental design, choice of measurement range, repeats, uncertainty propagation, graph construction, gradient analysis and evaluation are all paper skills and all teachable over video. What online tutoring cannot replace is the hours a student spends handling apparatus, which is the school's responsibility and which schools do.

The honesty boundary is firm. A tutor teaches the physics, explains each criterion, questions the design, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any part of an investigation, generate data, or supply text. The line is authorship, and the consequence of crossing it is an academic malpractice finding against the student rather than against the tutor.

We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. We reference the official source and work from papers the student or school legitimately holds. Any provider offering a downloadable library of IB material is distributing material it does not own.

On regulation: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, with ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the Ministry of Education covering Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Individual tutors need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram is not IB authorised, KHDA approved or ADEK approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit and has no UAE office.

sections.heading: Starting physics support at whatever point you are at
paragraphs: Send three things: the level, the school, and either a recent marked script or the investigation draft. A marked script distinguishes a content gap from a structure problem from an uncertainty problem, and those need entirely different work. The investigation draft is more urgent if one exists, because it has a deadline and the papers do not yet.

Then take the free trial lesson, which is a real teaching hour on the current sticking point rather than a consultation, with a short written note afterwards on what the tutor found in theme and criterion terms. No card is held, nothing renews, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge.

On availability, Higher Level physics with investigation supervision in a specific evening slot is one of the thinner parts of our coverage, and a wait of two to four days is normal, longer near mocks. We give the date rather than substituting somebody who teaches a different science. If the specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

Production City sessions usually land at 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time or later on weekdays, with weekend mornings better for graph and uncertainty work that needs concentration. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots are a normal request and the slot is held. What we will not do, in IMPZ or anywhere in the UAE, is send a tutor to your address; that service runs in India only.

faqs.answer: Because he is describing outcomes where the mark scheme wants principles named. An explain question asking why a lamp dims when another is added in parallel awards marks for total resistance, current drawn, the effect of internal resistance on terminal potential difference, and then the brightness. Writing that current goes elsewhere describes the result and names nothing the examiner can credit. The fix is a four-step structure: name the quantity that changes, name the relationship, state the direction, state the consequence. Three to five hours usually changes it measurably.

faqs.question: How is uncertainty actually examined in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: In two places, which is why it is the highest-value single skill in the course. On the Paper 1 data-analysis section, where students plot error bars, take a gradient with its uncertainty from best and worst fit lines, and justify significant figures. And inside the scientific investigation, where the data analysis and evaluation criteria both depend on it. Taught as one system covering absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty plus propagation rules, it takes three to five focused sessions. Taught piecemeal as topics arise, it never quite settles and students arrive in DP2 without it.

faqs.question: Which internal deadlines should we ask the school about in DP1?
faqs.answer: Four: when the investigation design has to be agreed, when the data collection window opens and closes, when the write-up is due, and when the school's internal submission date falls, which is typically in the autumn or winter of DP2. Ask for the whole internal deadline calendar at the first DP1 parents' evening, because those dates govern the student's year far more than any IB date does, and they move more often than families expect. We build the plan around that calendar and re-check it every four to six weeks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics investigation without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can teach the physics the investigation rests on, explain each criterion and what the descriptors require, interrogate the research question until the apparatus can actually answer it, discuss whether the method will produce usable data with enough repeats, and read a draft the student wrote and say where it falls short. A tutor cannot write any part, supply text, generate data, rewrite a section to final form or choose the topic. The test is authorship: every word and number must be the student's own.

faqs.question: Our daughter's mock was a 4. What does that actually tell us?
faqs.answer: Very little on its own, because the grade blends three unrelated problems. Ask the school for component marks. Clusters of blank questions in one theme mean a content gap, usually fields or quantum physics, needing eight to fifteen hours of teaching in dependency order. Attempted questions at half credit throughout mean explain-question structure, three to five hours. Strong multiple choice with weak data analysis means an uncertainty problem, not a physics problem, and treating it as physics wastes a term. Only the script distinguishes them.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics significantly harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is more content and genuinely different content, rather than the same material examined harder. The Higher Level extensions across fields, thermal physics and quantum physics add abstraction that Standard Level students never meet, and the paper demands rise accordingly. The practical implication for tutoring is that a tutor should be matched to the level the student is actually taking, because somebody comfortable teaching Standard Level is not automatically comfortable with the extensions. Check whether the target degree requires Higher Level before committing, since some engineering and physics programmes specify it.

faqs.question: Can online lessons prepare a student for the data-analysis section?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arguably better than in-person work, because graph construction, error bars and gradient analysis are done on a shared whiteboard that saves every step. A student practising in April reads their own corrected working from November instead of reconstructing the method from a notebook. What online tutoring cannot replace is the hours spent physically handling apparatus, which is the school's responsibility. The assessed skills, though, are design, measurement choice, repeats, propagation, plotting and evaluation, and all of those are paper work.

faqs.question: What do fields questions catch students out on most?
faqs.answer: The distinction between field strength and potential. They are different quantities with different units, one a vector and one a scalar, and students treat them as interchangeable descriptions of the same thing. The mark scheme is unforgiving here because the units give the answer away: a student writing about potential in units of newtons per kilogram has told the examiner exactly what they have confused. Teaching them as a pair, side by side, with the units written every time, is the intervention, and it takes a session or two rather than a term.

faqs.question: How many hours of physics support does a two-year plan need?
faqs.answer: A weekly session across DP1 and DP2 is roughly sixty to seventy hours, but the useful figure is smaller and better targeted. Uncertainty as a system takes three to five hours. Investigation design and criteria work takes six to ten. Explain-question structure takes three to five. A spring timed-paper block takes ten to sixteen. That is under forty hours spent where the marks are, spread across two years, which is a different purchase from an open-ended weekly arrangement and usually a better one.

faqs.question: What does specialist physics tuition cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The IB specialist band runs roughly AED 200-450 an hour, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, and budget or university-student tutors advertise from AED 45. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai monthly estimates put specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more. All figures were read in October 2026 and describe the market rather than our price list. We start with a free trial lesson instead.

faqs.question: Does it matter that our son came into DP1 from IGCSE physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it predicts exactly which half of the course he will find hard. An IGCSE entrant arrives with solid procedural physics and real timed-paper experience, and with almost no experience of open-ended investigation: he can rearrange equations and recall definitions but has rarely designed an experiment, chosen a measurement range or propagated an uncertainty. So the first term of DP1 should prioritise experimental design and uncertainty rather than content, because the content advantage will carry him for a term and the investigation deadline will not wait.

faqs.question: Which session do UAE physics candidates sit, and when should we begin?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be right, so confirm windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. On timing, physics rewards starting in DP1 more than almost any other subject, because the investigation and the uncertainty skills both have to be built before the papers arrive, and both are nearly impossible to retrofit in the final term.

faqs.question: Do you send a physics tutor to our home in Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For physics specifically the online format keeps a shared whiteboard archive of graphs, error bars and gradient work that a student can revise from months later. Independent home tutors do work in this area, at roughly AED 180-350 an hour on published Dubai market rates, and for a younger child who needs physical supervision they can genuinely be the better choice.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level physics specialist is free in our slot?
faqs.answer: We give you a date rather than a substitute. Higher Level physics with investigation supervision in a specific evening slot is one of the thinner parts of our coverage, and two to four days is normal, longer in the weeks around mocks. Putting a tutor who teaches a different science in front of a physics student wastes the hours, because explain-question conventions and uncertainty treatment differ between subjects. If the available specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-producti.closingHeading: Sequence beats intensity in a two-year subject
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-producti.closingBody: Physics punishes late starts more than most Diploma subjects, because two of the three things that decide the grade have to be built before the papers arrive. Uncertainty as a system, early, since it is assessed twice. A research question the apparatus can actually answer, in DP1, since a weak one caps a fifth of the grade. Then explain-question structure in the autumn of DP2 and timed questions on identified themes in the spring. Ask the school for its internal deadline calendar, send a recent marked script, and take a free trial lesson before committing to anything.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB physics at Higher and Standard Level and are matched to the level rather than the subject. For sequence-led work the useful tutor is one who asks which themes have been taught and when the school's investigation deadline falls, before proposing any topic.

intro.heading: Where in the physics sequence your child actually is
paragraphs: Diploma physics is taught in an order, and the order has consequences that almost no tutoring page mentions. The current syllabus covers five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Most schemes of work begin with motion and forces, because they anchor everything else, and finish with nuclear and quantum physics. That means the last theme arrives in DP2, under maximum time pressure, alongside mocks and the investigation deadline.

The two moments families in Silicon Oasis most often call are therefore predictable. The first is early in DP1, when a capable student meets extended written reasoning for the first time and the marks drop. The second is the second term of DP2, when nuclear and quantum physics, the scientific investigation, mocks and in some cases university applications all occupy the same six weeks. Those two calls need completely different work.

Underneath both sits uncertainty. Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and what an uncertainty implies about a conclusion are needed twice: in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and inside the scientific investigation, which carries 20 per cent of the grade. It is the most under-prepared skill in Diploma physics and one of the few structural-looking gaps that is genuinely closable late, because the procedures are finite.

The investigation deadline is the date everything else bends around, and it is set by the school rather than by the board. Since every Diploma science sets one and the Extended Essay milestones sit nearby, those dates cluster. A parent who asks the coordinator for all of them in September of DP1 can plan around the cluster; one who meets them individually cannot. That request costs nothing and changes more than a term of lessons would.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City, The Villa and Nad Al Sheba, physics lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format is an advantage: teaching physics is mostly working through problems line by line, and a shared screen puts the same working in front of both people with the tutor able to annotate the exact line where a unit was dropped.

What follows is the sequence in detail. Which themes land when, what each one demands, how the investigation timeline runs backwards from the school's date, what the final ten weeks can and cannot reach, and why uncertainty belongs at the front of almost every physics plan regardless of which term you are in.

One framing worth carrying into the detail. Physics is a subject where the diagnosis matters more than the quantity of help, because the two common presentations look identical on a report and need opposite plans. The student who was fine until the hardest themes arrived needs content and a calmer calendar. The student who has been losing the same marks since the first term of DP1 needs the slow work. Spending the same money on the wrong one of those is the commonest way a physics budget achieves nothing.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-.programmesIntro: Physics arrives in the Diploma from two directions and the gap differs by route. These are the stages and what each leaves a student ready or unready for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Integrated or discrete sciences assessed against four criteria, A to D, each marked 1 to 8. The inquiring and designing criterion is the closest analogue to what Diploma physics will demand of an investigation, and students who treated it as a write-up rather than as a designed piece of work carry that habit forward.
programmes.countryNote: A Silicon Oasis student arriving from MYP typically has sound investigation instincts and uneven mathematics. The gap is rarely conceptual physics; it is rearranging formulae, indices and standard form, and unit manipulation, all of which are mathematics doing physics work and all of which are cheapest to fix before DP1 starts.

programmes.name: IGCSE physics or combined science
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 for separate physics, or a combined entry covering all three sciences more narrowly. Students arriving from a combined entry meet substantially more Diploma content, particularly in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics, which compounds the late-sequence problem.
programmes.countryNote: This is the commoner route from schools along this corridor. The honest warning is that a strong IGCSE physics grade predicts comfort with Diploma calculation and says very little about extended written reasoning, which is the Higher Level discriminator and which is new rather than harder.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme physics
programmes.description: Five themes assessed by Paper 1, which contains a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and Paper 2 of structured and extended-response questions, plus a scientific investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade. Higher Level extends content within the same themes and raises the extended-response demand.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School, GEMS Modern Academy at Nad Al Sheba and the other Diploma centres reachable from this corridor each set their own scheme-of-work order and their own investigation deadline. Ask your school for both, because a generic sequence is a useful starting point and the school's actual order is what the plan must follow.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-.subjectsIntro: This grid is the physics syllabus sorted by when it typically arrives and what it demands at that point. Use it to work out whether your child's current difficulty is a sequence problem or a capability one.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Usually taught first. Kinematics, forces, work and energy, momentum, circular motion and gravitation. The theme where marks are most often lost to a carelessly drawn free-body diagram, because a missing force makes every subsequent line wrong however good the algebra is.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws, current and circuits, typically taught in DP1. Circuit questions reward a student who redraws the circuit before calculating and punish one who substitutes straight from the printed diagram, which is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave models, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, usually spanning the DP1 to DP2 boundary. This is where physical reasoning in words carries more marks than algebra, so a calculation-strong student can look suddenly worse here.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, and electromagnetic induction at Higher Level, generally taught in DP2. Sign conventions matter most in this theme, and students lose marks they have otherwise earned by treating a minus sign as a typographical detail.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Atomic structure, radioactive decay, fission, fusion and quantum phenomena, almost always taught last. Arrives alongside mocks and the investigation deadline, which makes it the single commonest subject of a late physics tutoring request along this corridor.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and data analysis
subjects.description: Graph drawing, gradient and intercept interpretation, absolute and percentage uncertainty and propagation. Assessed in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and inside the investigation, so a single block of work serves two components at once.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: Multi-mark written answers requiring a chain of physical reasoning in which each step names a mechanism. Students write three restatements of the first sentence instead, which earns one mark. A habit built over a term, so it belongs in DP1.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An independent investigation on a question the student chooses, marked against published criteria. Thin evaluation and a research question too broad for the available apparatus are the two expensive failures, and both are settled at the planning stage.

subjects.name: Mathematics for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, indices and standard form, trigonometry, logarithms and gradients. A student without fluency here appears weak across all five themes, because the same deficiency resurfaces in each one. Often the cheapest intervention in the subject.

subjects.name: Practical reasoning in writing
subjects.description: Apparatus choice, systematic versus random error, precision of recording, and specific rather than generic improvements. Assessed in written form on the papers as well as inside the investigation, which means it is teachable without a laboratory bench.

sections.heading: The two-year physics sequence, and why the hardest part comes last
paragraphs: Most schemes of work begin Diploma physics with space, time and motion, because kinematics, forces and energy anchor everything that follows and because students arrive with some of it from IGCSE or MYP. The particulate nature of matter, with thermal physics and circuits, usually follows in DP1. Wave behaviour commonly spans the DP1 to DP2 boundary. Fields and then nuclear and quantum physics sit in DP2, in that order.

That ordering is pedagogically sensible and calendrically brutal. It places the two themes with the least prior scaffolding into the term that also contains the scientific investigation deadline, the mock window and, for students applying overseas, university deadlines. A student who has coped adequately through DP1 can appear to collapse in the second term of DP2 without anything having changed about their ability.

Recognising that is the single most useful diagnostic a parent can apply. If a student was fine until fields arrived, the problem is probably sequence and workload rather than capability, and the right response is a focused content block on the late themes. If a student has been losing the same kinds of marks since the first term of DP1, the problem is capability, and a content block in DP2 will not touch it.

The table below gives the typical order with what each theme demands. Treat it as a template to check against your own school's scheme of work rather than as the authority, because schools along this corridor order the themes differently and some teach two in parallel. Ask the physics teacher for the order and the dates; it is one message and it makes every subsequent decision easier.

sections.heading: Uncertainty: the block that serves two components
paragraphs: Absolute uncertainty, percentage uncertainty, propagation through a calculation, and what an uncertainty implies about whether a conclusion is supported. None of it is conceptually hard. Almost none of it is practised deliberately, because it does not feel like physics and because it sits across two components rather than inside a named theme, so neither the scheme of work nor a revision timetable naturally allocates time to it.

The consequence is twofold. In the data-analysis section of Paper 1 students lose marks on questions that are procedural once learned. And in the scientific investigation, which carries 20 per cent of the grade, uncertainty treatment is one of the thinnest sections in most reports, because it was not planned before the data was collected and therefore could not be done properly afterwards.

That combination makes a four to six session uncertainty block the highest-return physics purchase at almost any point in the two years. It is finite, so it closes. It is procedural, so it closes late if necessary. And it serves two assessed components at once, which no other block in the subject does. For most Diploma physics students it moves more marks than four sessions on any single theme would.

The timing preference is clear though: before the investigation data is collected rather than after. A student who understands propagation while designing the method will record the right things with the right precision and will have something real to write in the evaluation. A student who meets it after the data exists can learn the Paper 1 procedures but cannot retrofit the investigation, and that is 20 per cent of the grade sitting on a planning decision.

sections.heading: The investigation timeline, counted back from the school's date
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the physics grade, and its deadline belongs to the school rather than to the board. Every Diploma science sets one and the Extended Essay milestones sit nearby, so the dates cluster and three deadlines in a fortnight is routine. Asking the coordinator for all of them in September of DP1 turns a predictable congestion into a plan, and it costs nothing.

Working backwards gives the schedule. A complete draft two to three weeks before submission, so that feedback can be acted on rather than merely received. Data collection finished before that, with enough margin to repeat a run that fails. Method, apparatus and the uncertainty plan settled before any data is collected. And the research question narrowed earliest of all, because a question too broad for school apparatus produces data that cannot support a conclusion.

For physics specifically, two planning errors recur along this corridor. Choosing a relationship whose variation cannot be measured reliably with available equipment, and leaving uncertainty until the numbers are recorded. Both are conversations rather than lessons, both belong at the front of the process, and both are far cheaper to prevent than to patch. Two or three well-timed hours here outperform a term of content teaching.

The boundary is absolute. A tutor may discuss the research question, explain each criterion, model a comparable investigation on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of it. The report is declared as the student's own work and moderated by the IB, so the consequence of anything else falls on your child.

sections.heading: What the final ten weeks can reach in physics
paragraphs: Ten weeks before the May examinations is when most Diploma physics tutoring in Dubai is bought, and the ceiling is real but not as low as in some subjects. Physics is unusual in that one of its characteristic weaknesses, uncertainty treatment, is procedural and therefore closable late. So is sign-convention discipline in fields. So is the content of nuclear and quantum physics, if the mathematics underneath is sound, because that theme is largely definitional.

What ten weeks cannot deliver is extended-response reasoning from scratch. A multi-mark question asking why something happens wants a causal chain in which each step follows from the last and names a mechanism, and students who have spent two years writing descriptions instead cannot acquire that chain in ten weeks. They can acquire a partial version: a structure to follow, a checklist of what a mechanism sentence contains, which captures some of the marks.

Nor can ten weeks install the mathematics. A student who cannot rearrange a formula confidently in March will hesitate in May, and the hesitation costs time across both papers. The honest response is to target the questions that minimise that exposure and to drill the specific rearrangements the common question types require, rather than attempting general mathematical fluency.

So a final-block physics plan should be explicit. Uncertainty and data analysis first, because it is finite and worth marks in two places. Then the late themes, content-led. Then extended-response structure as a checklist rather than as a habit. And a stated exclusion: general mathematical fluency is not in scope, and the student should be told so, because a plan carrying an unachievable goal produces the sense of failure rather than progress.

sections.heading: Practical work, the school's laboratory and what a tutor adds
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how practical physics can be supported when the tutor is not in the room, and the answer is that most assessed practical reasoning is expressed in writing rather than performed. Choosing an appropriate instrument, distinguishing systematic from random error, explaining why a measurement was repeated, reading a scale to the correct precision, and suggesting a specific rather than generic improvement are all taught on paper and marked on paper.

The laboratory belongs to the school and should. Your child has access to apparatus, a teacher who knows it, and technicians who maintain it. A tutor offering to replicate that would be offering something worse than what the student already has. What a tutor adds is the thinking on either side of the bench: anticipating error sources before the experiment runs, and interpreting the numbers honestly once it has.

Data analysis is where the online format is genuinely superior rather than merely adequate. A student's graph can be displayed and annotated, the line of best fit discussed, the gradient computed and its units reasoned about, and uncertainty bars drawn in while both people watch the same screen at the same magnification. Across a table, the tutor is reading a graph upside down and pointing at it from the wrong side.

One honest limitation deserves stating. A student who has not actually used the apparatus writes about it less convincingly than one who has, and no amount of tutoring substitutes for having done the practical sessions. If your child is missing laboratory work, that is the problem to solve first and it is a conversation with the school rather than a purchase from anybody.

sections.heading: Paper components, and what to practise for each
paragraphs: Diploma physics is assessed by two written papers plus the scientific investigation. Paper 1 contains a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 contains structured and extended-response questions. For exact weightings and durations at your child's level, use the school's copy of the subject guide, which is the authority; we do not reproduce board documents on this site.

Multiple choice loses marks to careless reading rather than to ignorance, and the useful drill is a timed set followed by analysis of every wrong answer, asking what the distractor was designed to catch. Most students find the same two or three traps recurring, which is a fixable pattern rather than a knowledge gap and which responds within two or three sessions.

The data-analysis section is the under-prepared one, and it is the same work as the uncertainty block described above, which is why that block does double duty. Paper 2's structured questions reward a standard layout: formula written out, substitution shown, answer with units. A calculation compressed into two lines cannot be awarded method marks because the method is not visible.

Paper 2's extended-response questions are the Higher Level discriminator and the slowest to move. The requirement is a causal chain in which each step names a mechanism. Teaching it requires marked practice with the mark scheme visible, repeatedly, until the student can see which of their own sentences earned nothing. That is a DP1 job done properly and a partial job done in DP2.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level, and when the decision bites
paragraphs: Higher Level physics covers additional content within the same five themes and demands considerably more extended written reasoning. It is the second of those that catches students, because content can be learned in weeks and a reasoning habit takes months. A student comfortable with Standard Level calculation and uncomfortable writing a four-sentence causal explanation will find Higher Level harder than the syllabus difference alone suggests.

The decision bites at two points in the calendar. The first is at the start of DP1, when the level is chosen, and that is when the reasoning habit should start being built if Higher Level is the plan. The second is in the second term of DP2, when fields and nuclear physics arrive at Higher Level depth in the most crowded term of the course, and the gap between the two levels becomes most visible.

On university requirements, engineering, physics and some computer science programmes commonly specify Higher Level physics or a Higher Level science, while medicine and life sciences usually specify chemistry and biology instead. Requirements are set course by course and change between admissions cycles, so the reliable method is to read the admissions page for the specific course in the specific year and to involve the school's university counsellor early.

The tutoring consequence is about timing rather than level. If a target course requires Higher Level physics, the money belongs in DP1 building the reasoning habit while there is time for it to become automatic. If no target course requires it, Higher Level physics chosen for its appearance on a transcript will consume tutoring hours across two years and deliver nothing that was needed. Ask before the choice is locked.

The theme list is the item nobody sends and the one that most improves the plan, because it distinguishes a sequence problem from a capability one. We then match a tutor to the level and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost.

Afterwards you receive a written note setting out where marks are being lost, sorted by component rather than by theme, with a recommended shape. For most physics students the first block is uncertainty and data analysis, because it is finite and serves two components. For a Higher Level student in DP1, a weekly arrangement on reasoning and mathematics is frequently right, and we will say which situation you are in.

The limits, stated plainly. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none. We hold no IB, regulator or board approval. We publish no IB examination or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date a family plans around is worse than silence; your child's coordinator holds the real calendar.

And the investigation boundary, once more. A tutor may discuss the question, explain the criteria, model a comparable investigation on a different topic, read your child's own draft and say where it falls short, and teach citation. process.title: Send the list of themes taught so far
process.description: It takes a line and it distinguishes the two possible diagnoses. A student who was fine until fields arrived has a sequence and workload problem; one losing the same marks since the first term of DP1 has a capability problem. Those need completely different plans and the same amount of money.

process.title: Ask the coordinator for every science deadline
process.description: The physics investigation deadline, the other sciences, and the Extended Essay milestones. They cluster, and knowing the cluster in September of DP1 turns a February emergency into a plan. One request, one reply, and it costs nothing at all.

process.title: Buy the uncertainty block first
process.description: Four to six sessions on absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation and graph reasoning. It is finite, so it closes, and it serves both the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and the scientific investigation, which no other block in the subject does.

process.title: Place the session in the earlier window
process.description: Physics depends on sustained algebraic reasoning, which is the first thing a tired student loses. Find the afternoon that carries no physics double period and no practical, and book there. A weekend morning block is usually better value than a second weekday evening.

process.title: Review by component after the mock
process.description: Sort the lost marks into multiple choice, data analysis, structured questions and extended response. Most students show one dominant weakness, and the next block should aim at it rather than at general revision across all five themes.

whyPoints.title: The sequence is mapped, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Nuclear and quantum physics is usually taught last, arriving in the term that also holds the investigation deadline and mocks. A student who collapses then has a sequence problem rather than a capability one, and recognising the difference changes what should be bought.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty treated as a component
whyPoints.description: It is assessed in Paper 1 data analysis and inside the 20 per cent investigation, it is finite and procedural, and almost nobody practises it deliberately. One block serving two components is the best value available in Diploma physics at any point in the two years.

whyPoints.title: An honest ceiling on ten weeks
whyPoints.description: Uncertainty, sign conventions and late-theme content are reachable. Extended-response reasoning is only partly reachable and mathematical fluency is not. Stating the exclusion is what makes the block succeed rather than producing a sense of failure.

whyPoints.title: Investigation support with a written boundary
whyPoints.description: Question narrowing, criteria explanation, a comparable model on a different topic, and feedback on your child's own draft. No drafting, no completing, no supplied material. The report is moderated by the IB and declared as the student's own work.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what online cannot do
whyPoints.description: The school's laboratory is where the apparatus belongs and a tutor should not pretend otherwise. What a tutor adds is the thinking either side of the bench, and graph and uncertainty work is genuinely easier on a shared screen than across a table.

faqs.question: Why did my child's physics grade fall in the second term of DP2?
faqs.answer: Often because of where the scheme of work placed the content rather than because anything changed about their ability. Fields and then nuclear and quantum physics are usually taught last, so they arrive in the term that also holds the scientific investigation deadline, the mock window and, for overseas applicants, university deadlines. A student who coped through DP1 and struggles then usually has a sequence and workload problem, which responds to a focused content block.

faqs.question: Which physics topic gives the best return on tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty and data analysis, at almost any point in the two years. Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation, graph drawing and gradient reasoning are finite procedures, so four to six sessions closes them, and they are assessed twice: in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and inside the scientific investigation, which carries 20 per cent of the grade. No other block in Diploma physics serves two components from one purchase.

faqs.question: When should a Silicon Oasis family buy physics tuition?
faqs.answer: DP1 if the problem is extended written reasoning or the mathematics underneath the subject, because both are habits that need months. DP2 if the problem is the late themes, since fields and nuclear physics are content-led and genuinely respond to a focused block. The uncertainty block is worth buying at either point, and ideally before the investigation data is collected rather than afterwards, because it cannot be retrofitted.

faqs.question: How much of the physics grade is the scientific investigation, and when is it due?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, and the deadline is set by the school rather than by the board. Every Diploma science sets one and the Extended Essay milestones sit nearby, so the dates cluster and three in a fortnight is routine. Ask the coordinator for all of them in September of DP1. Counting backwards, a complete draft should exist two to three weeks before submission so feedback can actually be acted on.

faqs.question: Can a tutor support the physics investigation without being in the laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the parts that carry most of the marks. Narrowing the research question until school apparatus can answer it, planning for systematic and random error, settling the uncertainty treatment before data is collected, and reading a draft and saying where it falls short against the criteria are all off-bench work. The laboratory belongs to the school, where the apparatus and technicians are, and a tutor should not try to replace it.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to Cedre Villas or Academic City for physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For physics the online format is an advantage rather than a compromise, because teaching the subject is mostly working through problems line by line. A shared screen puts the same working in front of both people, lets the tutor annotate the exact line where a unit was dropped, and allows a graph to be marked up while both watch.

faqs.question: What can ten weeks of physics tutoring realistically achieve?
faqs.answer: More than in some subjects. Uncertainty and propagation are finite and close readily. Sign-convention discipline in fields responds to drilling. The nuclear and quantum content is largely definitional and can be learned, given sound mathematics. What ten weeks cannot do is build extended-response reasoning from scratch or install mathematical fluency, though a structure and a mechanism checklist will capture some of the extended-response marks.

faqs.question: Why does my child calculate physics correctly and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Usually units and compressed working. An answer written without its unit, or left in the wrong power of ten, loses the mark however sound the arithmetic. And a multi-step calculation written in two lines cannot be awarded method marks because the method is not visible to the examiner. Teaching a standard layout of formula, substitution, then answer with units takes about one session and pays back across both papers for the rest of the course.

faqs.question: Which physics themes do students along this corridor ask for most?
faqs.answer: Fields first, because sign conventions matter most there and students lose marks they have otherwise earned by treating a minus sign as decoration. Then nuclear and quantum physics, because it is taught last and therefore met under maximum pressure. Wave behaviour is a close third, since it rewards physical reasoning in words rather than calculation, which catches students who are strong at the algebra and weak at the explanation.

faqs.question: Does weak mathematics explain a weak physics grade?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is the commonest misdiagnosis in the subject. Rearranging formulae, handling indices and standard form, trigonometry and gradient work are mathematics doing physics work, so a student without fluency appears weak across all five themes because the same deficiency resurfaces in each. Fixing the mathematics first can lift physics without anybody being paid to teach physics, which is why a diagnosis should examine both.

faqs.question: What exactly makes HL physics harder than SL for a DP2 student?
faqs.answer: The additional content is manageable; the extended-response demand is what catches students. A multi-mark written answer wants a causal chain in which each step follows from the last and names a mechanism, and students write three restatements of the first sentence instead, which earns one mark. Content can be learned in weeks and the reasoning habit takes months, which is why Higher Level support belongs in DP1 rather than in the final term.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week suit a Dubai Silicon Oasis Diploma student?
faqs.answer: One, placed on the afternoon that carries no physics double period and no practical session. A second weekday evening is usually worse value than a weekend morning block, because physics depends on sustained reasoning and a 7.30pm session delivers noticeably less than a 10am one for the same student. Where a Higher Level student is genuinely behind, a longer weekend block plus the weekday hour works better than three tired evenings.

faqs.question: Do universities require Higher Level physics for engineering from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Many do and some accept alternatives, and requirements are set course by course and change between admissions cycles, so no tutoring page should give you a rule. Engineering, physics and some computer science programmes commonly specify Higher Level physics or a Higher Level science. Open the admissions page for the specific course and year and involve the school's university counsellor early. Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate matter from a university's own requirements.

faqs.question: Should we practise multiple choice, or is that a waste of a session?
faqs.answer: It is worth two or three sessions, not more. Multiple choice loses marks to careless reading under time pressure rather than to ignorance, and the useful drill is a timed set followed by analysis of every wrong answer, asking what the distractor was designed to catch. Most students find the same two or three traps recurring, which is a fixable pattern. Beyond that the time is better spent on data analysis or extended response.

faqs.question: What should a Silicon Oasis family see after four physics sessions?
faqs.answer: Three things and no grade. Your child should know which component is costing marks, stated as multiple choice, data analysis, structured questions or extended response. You should hold a written note sorted that way. And one habit should visibly change, most often writing the unit on every answer or laying out working so that method marks can be awarded. Grade movement takes longer and nobody can honestly promise it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-.closingHeading: Find your place in the sequence first
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-.closingBody: Physics rewards a family that knows where the course has got to. A student struggling since the first term of DP1 needs the reasoning and mathematics work that only a long block delivers. A student who was fine until fields arrived needs a focused content run and a calmer calendar. The two look identical on a report and need different money. So send the level, the themes taught so far and the school's investigation deadline. The free trial lesson costs nothing, and the written note that follows will say which of the two you are dealing with.
