dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-south.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma Physics at Higher and Standard Level to students across Dubai South, Emaar South, Al Furjan and Dubai Investments Park. Physics Higher Level is one of the thinnest parts of any local tutor market, which is the practical reason this page exists.

intro.heading: Physics marks are lost in units, uncertainties and graphs, not in concepts
paragraphs: Parents arranging physics support in Dubai South usually describe a student who understands the ideas and cannot convert that into marks. That description is accurate far more often than it sounds, and it points at something specific. IB Physics awards a large share of its marks for things that are not conceptual at all: stating a unit correctly, carrying a prefix, reading a gradient off a line of best fit, quoting an uncertainty to a defensible number of significant figures, and labelling a graph axis with both quantity and unit. None of those is hard. All of them are rarely practised.

The second structural fact is that the three papers reward three different skills, and a plan built on topics touches only one of them. Paper 1 is multiple choice and awards nothing for method, so a correct chain of reasoning ending in the wrong power of ten scores zero. Paper 2 is extended response and does award method, which means partial credit is available for a well-structured answer that finishes at the wrong number. Paper 3 at Higher Level examines data analysis and the option topic, and is reliably met last.

The investigation is 20% of the grade. It is the component a student controls with time rather than with performance on a single morning, and the one most likely to be weak for a reason nobody told them: the exploration and analysis criteria reward a defensible uncertainty treatment, and a student who collected clean data and never propagated an error will sit mid-band with a tidy report. The deadline for it is set by the school's IB coordinator rather than by the IB, and it falls earlier than most families expect.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script, the official markband and the data booklet open on a shared screen. For physics that arrangement matters more than it does for an essay subject, because a graph can be drawn, annotated and corrected on a shared surface and the correction stays legible the following week.

One point on availability, because this is where honesty costs us something and should. Physics at Higher Level is among the thinnest specialisms in any tutoring market, Dubai included. A Dubai South family filtering by proximity is choosing from a very short list indeed, and that list is selected by willingness to drive the southern corridor rather than by what anyone has taught. Online delivery removes the travel cut. It does not create physicists, and where no Higher Level specialist is free we say so and give a date rather than seating a general science tutor in the chair.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: Physics reaches Dubai South students through the Diploma, and they arrive at it from the Middle Years Programme or from IGCSE. Both routes leave characteristic gaps that show up in different components.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme physics
programmes.description: Taken at Higher or Standard Level, with Papers 1 and 2 at both levels, Paper 3 added at Higher Level, and the scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade. Higher Level adds fields, electromagnetic induction and quantum phenomena to the core, and raises the analytical demand of the markbands at the top end. Grades run 1 to 7 with boundaries set after each session.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South Diploma candidates sit the May session. The dates that govern the physics year are internal rather than external: the school's deadline for the investigation draft, the final submission date, and the mock window. Those come from the IB coordinator and differ by several weeks between the Dubai Investments Park and Dubailand schools, so ask rather than assume.

programmes.name: Middle Years Sciences
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria from A to D, each 0 to 8, converted to a 1-7 grade. Criterion B is inquiring and designing and criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science, so a student can hold a strong grade on investigation design and reflection while quantitative physics lags. That gap surfaces immediately in Diploma Paper 1, where arithmetic and prefixes decide the mark.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving from Middle Years Sciences into Diploma Physics in this cluster usually need a short block on quantitative technique rather than on content: prefixes, standard form, rearranging formulae and significant figures. Four to six sessions across the summer before Year 12 closes most of it, and left undone it costs a term of Year 12 while new content is also arriving.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into the Diploma
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 is the usual entry route. The gap to Diploma Physics is mathematical rather than conceptual: Diploma questions expect algebraic rearrangement, graph interpretation and uncertainty language that IGCSE touches lightly. Students who took Additional Mathematics alongside their physics arrive noticeably better prepared for the quantitative work.
programmes.countryNote: Several British-curriculum schools in the Al Furjan and Jebel Ali arc feed Diploma cohorts elsewhere in Dubai, so a student may change school and system at sixteen. That transition needs the gap written down over the summer, because Diploma Physics assumes mathematical fluency the IGCSE course did not require.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where physics is taken as one of the Diploma courses within the Career-related Programme, it is examined identically, investigation included. Students on this route sometimes have fewer timetabled contact hours for the same assessment, which makes independent practice between sessions more important rather than less and makes the investigation harder to supervise in school.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is uncommon in this part of Dubai, so a family whose child takes physics within it has no local comparison for whether an investigation draft is on track. A specialist who has supervised the component elsewhere is the straightforward remedy, and online delivery is the only route to one from Dubai South.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The components and topics a Dubai South physics student actually needs work on, broken out by where marks go rather than listed as one subject.

subjects.name: Paper 1: multiple choice
subjects.description: No method marks at all, so a single prefix slip or an arithmetic error destroys a question that was fully understood. The skills that raise a Paper 1 score are estimation, unit checking and dimensional sanity rather than deeper conceptual work. It responds well to high-volume timed practice, which is also the least popular form of revision available.

subjects.name: Paper 2: extended response
subjects.description: Method marks are available, which means a structured answer finishing at the wrong number still scores. The recurring losses are failing to state an assumption, omitting a unit from a final answer, and describing a trend without quoting a value from the graph or data given. Structure can be taught explicitly in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: Data analysis questions plus the chosen option topic. Because it examines a different skill set from Papers 1 and 2, revising the core content does not prepare a student for it. Students meet it late and lose marks that were straightforwardly available, which makes it the clearest planning error in Higher Level physics.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Worth 20% of the grade and marked on criteria that reward a methodology addressing all relevant variables and a processing section that is correct and includes uncertainties. A tidy report with clean data and no error propagation sits mid-band. The deadline comes from the school's IB coordinator, not from the IB.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products and powers, and quoting a result to a defensible number of significant figures. Examined in both papers and in the investigation, and almost never drilled. The single highest-yield topic in the subject for most candidates.

subjects.name: Graph work and gradients
subjects.description: Drawing a line of best fit, reading a gradient with a sensible triangle, linearising a relationship so it can be plotted straight, and labelling axes with quantity and unit. Marks are awarded for each of these independently of the physics, which makes graph technique an efficient place to spend sessions.

subjects.name: Mechanics and energy
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum, work and power. The conceptual content is accessible and the marks go on sign conventions, on resolving forces consistently, and on choosing between an energy and a momentum approach. Drawing the free-body diagram before calculating recovers marks across the whole topic.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Travelling and standing waves, superposition, Doppler effect and simple harmonic motion. Phase relationships and the standing-wave boundary conditions produce the most errors. Higher Level deepens the mathematical treatment of simple harmonic motion, where the energy relationships are a reliable source of marks.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance combinations, internal resistance and the potential divider. The failure is almost always circuit reading rather than calculation: students who redraw a confusing circuit before analysing it outperform those who attempt to reason from the printed diagram as given.

subjects.name: Fields and induction at Higher Level
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, potential, and electromagnetic induction. The topic rewards treating field and potential as separate quantities with separate units, which students conflate. Induction questions fail on the direction of the induced effect more often than on its magnitude, and that is a rule to drill rather than derive.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the ideal gas relationships and kinetic theory. Marks go on unit consistency, particularly on temperatures that must be in kelvin, and on recognising a phase change within a multi-stage heating problem. Short topic, dependable marks, frequently rushed in revision.

subjects.name: Quantum and nuclear physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, deeper at HL
subjects.description: Photoelectric effect, atomic spectra, radioactive decay and binding energy. The commonest loss is unit confusion between electronvolts and joules, and mass defect calculations that round early. Higher Level adds depth that rewards careful algebra rather than conceptual leaps, which makes it responsive to targeted practice.

sections.heading: Three papers, three different skills
paragraphs: The most useful thing a physics plan can do is stop treating the subject as one thing. Paper 1 and Paper 2 reward almost opposite habits, and Paper 3 at Higher Level rewards a third set. A student revising topics is implicitly preparing for Paper 2 and hoping the rest follows. It does not follow, and the mark distribution punishes the assumption.

Paper 1 is multiple choice with no method credit. The consequence is stark: a candidate who understands a question perfectly, sets it up correctly and mishandles a prefix in the final step scores nothing on it. The skills that raise a Paper 1 mark are therefore estimation, unit checking, dimensional sanity and speed, and the way to build them is a high volume of timed questions with the wrong answers analysed. Most students have never done that deliberately.

Paper 2 is extended response and does award method, which changes the strategy completely. Here a structured answer that states its assumptions and shows its working earns partial credit even when the arithmetic fails. The losses on Paper 2 are therefore structural: no assumption stated, no unit on the final answer, a trend described without a value quoted from the data. Those are writing habits and they can be fixed in a handful of sessions.

Paper 3 at Higher Level examines data analysis and the chosen option. It is the component most reliably met last and most reliably under-practised, and the marks on it are among the most accessible in the subject because the question types repeat. The table sets the three out side by side so a plan can name which paper each block of sessions is for, which is the discipline that stops a revision timetable from being a topic list.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: the highest-yield topic almost nobody drills
paragraphs: If a Dubai South physics student is scoring below their understanding, uncertainty handling is the first place to look. It is examined in Paper 2, it is examined in Paper 3, and it is explicitly rewarded in the investigation's analysis criterion, which asks for processing that is correct and includes uncertainties. Despite appearing in three places, it is treated in most classrooms as a formality attached to practical work rather than as examinable content.

The skills are finite and learnable. Absolute uncertainty from an instrument's resolution. Fractional and percentage uncertainty. Propagation through a product or quotient by adding fractional uncertainties, and through a power by multiplying. Quoting a final result so that the uncertainty determines the significant figures rather than the calculator display. Deciding whether two results agree within their uncertainties. That list is short enough to cover in two sessions and deep enough to take four to make fluent.

The payoff appears in places a student does not expect. A Paper 2 question asking whether a measured value is consistent with a theoretical one is an uncertainty question wearing a concepts costume. An investigation whose data is clean and whose analysis has no error bars loses marks in the criterion that carries six of them. A Paper 3 data-analysis question asking for the uncertainty in a gradient is routine once practised and impossible when met for the first time under time.

The honest reason this is under-taught is that it is dull to teach and easy to defer. A tutor working from a marked script rather than a syllabus cannot defer it, because the losses show up on the page. That is the practical difference between a session aimed at a component and a session aimed at a topic, and it is why the first physics session here reads a script rather than teaching from one.

sections.heading: Graph technique as a source of marks in its own right
paragraphs: Graph questions award marks for things that are independent of the physics, and that is good news for a student whose concepts are sound. An axis labelled with quantity and unit earns credit. A sensible scale earns credit. A line of best fit drawn through the spread rather than between the first and last points earns credit. A gradient read with a large triangle and the values stated earns credit. None of these requires understanding the experiment.

The skill that does require teaching is linearisation. A relationship that is not straight has to be rearranged so that a straight-line plot becomes possible, which means deciding what to put on each axis before any plotting happens. Students who have not practised this will plot the raw quantities, get a curve, and have nothing to extract a gradient from. Recognising the standard forms, so that a square root or a reciprocal suggests itself immediately, is pattern matching built by volume.

Uncertainty reappears here, because a graph with error bars supports a question about the uncertainty in the gradient, usually by drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines. That is a procedure rather than an insight and it is worth drilling until it is automatic. Candidates who meet it for the first time in a Paper 3 data-analysis question lose several marks that were available to anybody who had seen it once.

Online delivery helps specifically here. A graph drawn on a shared digital surface can be corrected live, annotated with the error the student made, and saved. When the same habit reappears four weeks later the earlier graph is still there to compare against, which turns a repeated mistake into evidence rather than an impression. On loose paper passed across a table, that record does not survive the term.

sections.heading: The investigation, and what the criteria actually reward
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is 20% of the physics grade and the only part a student can secure months in advance. What makes it go wrong is rarely effort. It is a research question whose independent variable cannot be measured well enough to produce a usable trend, or a method that ignores a variable an examiner will notice, or an analysis that processes data correctly without ever propagating an uncertainty.

The criteria are published and they are specific. The exploration criterion rewards a methodology that addresses all relevant variables, which means the write-up has to show that the student thought about what else could have changed and controlled or accounted for it. The analysis criterion rewards processing that is correct and includes uncertainties, which is why clean data with no error treatment caps the mark. Reading those two descriptors before designing the experiment changes the design.

Sequencing matters as much as content. Question selection comes first and sets the ceiling. Then a pilot run, which students skip and which reliably reveals that the chosen range is too narrow or the instrument too coarse. Then the real data collection, then processing with uncertainties, then a complete draft in time for the one permitted round of substantive feedback, then submission on the school's date. That date comes from the IB coordinator and differs between schools in this cluster by several weeks.

The boundary on help is firm and worth stating plainly, because a page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments. A tutor may teach the physics, discuss and reject an unworkable question, explain each criterion and its mark allocation, and give feedback on a complete draft the student has written. A tutor may not write a section, supply data, rewrite the analysis or edit to completion. A malpractice finding falls on the student's Diploma.

sections.heading: Mark-scheme traps, topic by topic
paragraphs: These are the specific, repeatable losses that appear on Dubai South physics scripts, and naming them is most of the fix. In mechanics the trap is sign convention: a student who does not fix a positive direction before starting will produce a correct magnitude with the wrong sign, and in momentum questions that is the whole answer. Drawing the free-body diagram first is the habit that prevents it.

In electricity the trap is circuit reading rather than circuit calculation. Examiners draw circuits that are deliberately awkward to read, and candidates who analyse the printed diagram as given will combine the wrong resistors. Redrawing the circuit in a standard layout before any calculation takes ninety seconds and converts a hard question into a routine one. In thermal physics the trap is units, specifically temperatures that must be in kelvin, and multi-stage heating problems where a phase change hides between two gradients.

In fields at Higher Level the trap is conflating field strength and potential, which have different units and different relationships to distance. In induction the direction of the induced effect causes more losses than its magnitude, and the direction is a rule to drill rather than a result to derive under time. In quantum and nuclear physics the trap is electronvolts against joules, and mass defect calculations rounded early enough to lose the final answer.

In waves the trap is phase. Standing-wave questions depend on boundary conditions that students know and apply inconsistently, and Doppler questions depend on whether source or observer is moving, which changes the expression. Each of these is diagnosable from a marked script in minutes, which is why the first session reads the script rather than starting a topic. The table collects them so a student can audit their own paper against the list.

sections.heading: What Higher Level adds, and whether to stay on it
paragraphs: Higher Level physics adds content, adds Paper 3, and raises the analytical demand of the markbands at the top. Those are three separate changes and the distinction matters when a family is deciding whether to continue. The extra content is listed in the subject guide and can be covered. The extra paper requires its own practice and is where unprepared Higher Level candidates lose most. The markband shift is subtler and shows up as a mid-band ceiling on otherwise competent answers.

The mathematical demand is the practical filter. Higher Level physics expects comfortable algebraic rearrangement, work with logarithms and exponentials in decay and attenuation contexts, and the confidence to manipulate an expression before substituting numbers. A student taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics is not disqualified, but will find the algebra heavier going than a classmate on Analysis and Approaches. That interaction is worth raising in Year 11 when subjects are chosen together.

The decision to drop to Standard Level should be checked against university requirements first, because some engineering and physical-science programmes specify Higher Level physics by name and will not substitute. The honest diagnostic is whether the student is a band below target in one component or across all of them. One weak component is a technique problem worth fixing. Weakness across every component, in physics and in two other Higher Level subjects at once, is a workload problem, and facing it in Year 12 leaves far more options than facing it in Year 13.

For a Dubai South family there is a supply dimension too. Physics Higher Level specialists are thin everywhere and thinner in a newer district, which means a student who stays on the Higher Level course needs support arranged earlier rather than later. Where no specialist is free we say so and give a date, because a general science tutor opposite a Higher Level physics candidate teaches nothing the textbook would not have supplied.

sections.heading: What a physics specialist costs in Dubai, and why generalists are cheaper
paragraphs: The price ladder in this market tracks specialism and delivery model rather than any measurable quality claim, and physics shows that more clearly than most subjects. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33-52 an hour on Tutopiya and AED 45-65 on EdFlik, usually delivered by university students or non-specialists. At that band a tutor can supervise homework competently and cannot diagnose why a Paper 2 answer lost its uncertainty marks.

Qualified subject tutors online sit higher. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200-450 or more, and premium named tutors reach AED 650 on BartyED. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on the same table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is in the hour.

Where the spend goes wrong in physics specifically is buying cheap hours for a specialist problem. A student losing marks to uncertainty propagation and graph technique needs somebody who knows those are marked separately from the physics. A generalist will teach the concepts again, which the student already has, and the script will come back the same. That is the most expensive hour available in this market, because it costs money and a term.

Bestimate's monthly estimates give the planning figures: AED 240-600 for budget provision at one hour a week, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every figure belongs to the provider named; these are market bands rather than IB Gram prices, and our own conversation begins with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis.

sections.heading: Specialist availability from Dubai South, stated honestly
paragraphs: No tutoring page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is strange, because availability is the thing a parent most needs to plan around. Physics at Standard Level is reasonably well covered and a match usually takes a few days. Physics at Higher Level is thinner, and a request in a busy week can take longer. The option topic for Paper 3 narrows it further, because not every physics teacher has taught every option.

Proximity makes this considerably worse. Start with everyone who can teach Higher Level physics competently. Remove everyone unwilling to drive to Dubai South for a single evening session. Remove everyone whose free slot does not match your child's. For a Standard Level subject the surviving pool is workable. For Higher Level physics with a specific option, the proximity filter removes very nearly everybody, and a near-me search in this district returns a list selected almost entirely by willingness to travel.

Online delivery removes one cut, which is the expensive one. It does not manufacture specialists, and this page will not pretend otherwise. Where no Higher Level physics specialist is free in the week you ask, we say so and give a date. The alternative, seating a general science tutor opposite a Higher Level candidate, costs the family money and the student confidence while teaching nothing the textbook would not have supplied, and it is the quiet default across much of this market.

Where a wait is genuinely unworkable, there is a middle route worth naming. A shorter block with a different specialist on the single most urgent component — uncertainty technique, or graph work, or the investigation's analysis section — is useful in its own right and does not require the option-topic match. That is a smaller promise than a full term of Higher Level teaching and it is an honest one, which is the distinction this section exists to draw.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand physics but score badly in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Most often because the marks they are losing are not conceptual. IB Physics awards marks for stating a unit, carrying a prefix, labelling a graph axis with quantity and unit, reading a gradient with a sensible triangle and quoting an uncertainty to a defensible number of significant figures. None of that requires deeper understanding and none of it is usually drilled. A marked Paper 2 script shows the pattern within minutes, and four to six sessions on those mechanical skills typically moves a score more than another term of concept teaching would.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Physics Paper 1 and Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is multiple choice and awards no method marks, so a perfectly set-up question with a mishandled prefix in the final step scores nothing. Paper 2 is extended response and does award method, which means a structured answer stating its assumptions earns partial credit even when the arithmetic fails. The practical consequence is that they need different preparation: Paper 1 responds to high-volume timed practice with unit checking, while Paper 2 responds to answer structure. Treating them as the same revision task is common and costly.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Physics grade is the investigation?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Higher and Standard Level. It is marked on criteria that reward a methodology addressing all relevant variables and processing that is correct and includes uncertainties, which is why a tidy report with clean data and no error treatment sits mid-band. The deadline comes from the school's IB coordinator rather than from the IB, and in this part of Dubai it differs by several weeks between schools. Establishing that date in Year 12 is the single most useful administrative action a parent can take.

faqs.question: What does uncertainty propagation actually involve?
faqs.answer: A short, finite set of procedures. Absolute uncertainty from an instrument's resolution. Fractional and percentage uncertainty from that. Propagation through a product or quotient by adding fractional uncertainties, and through a power by multiplying by the index. Quoting a final result so that the uncertainty, rather than the calculator display, determines the significant figures. And deciding whether two values agree within their uncertainties, which is a question type rather than a judgement. Two sessions covers it; four makes it fluent, and it pays marks in Paper 2, Paper 3 and the investigation.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 3 a problem for Higher Level physics students?
faqs.answer: Because it examines data analysis and a chosen option topic rather than the core content of Papers 1 and 2, so revising the core does not prepare a student for it. A plan built around topics never touches it, and students routinely meet whole Paper 3 questions for the first time in the final fortnight. The marks on it are among the most accessible in the subject because the data-analysis question types repeat across sessions, which makes arriving unpractised a genuine waste rather than bad luck.

faqs.question: What is linearisation and why do students lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: Linearisation is rearranging a relationship so that a straight-line graph becomes possible, which means deciding what to plot on each axis before any plotting starts. A student who has not practised it will plot the raw quantities, obtain a curve, and have no gradient to extract. Recognising the standard forms so that a square root or a reciprocal suggests itself is pattern matching built by volume rather than by explanation. It appears in Paper 2, in Paper 3 data analysis and in most investigations, so it earns its practice time.

faqs.question: Does the maths route affect Higher Level physics?
faqs.answer: It affects how heavy the algebra feels rather than whether the course is possible. Higher Level physics expects comfortable rearrangement, work with logarithms and exponentials in decay and attenuation contexts, and the habit of manipulating an expression before substituting numbers. A student on Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches meets those skills in their maths lessons; a student on Applications and Interpretation generally does not and has to build them inside physics instead. That interaction is worth raising in Year 11 when the two subjects are chosen together.

faqs.question: Where is the line on investigation help for a Dubai South physics student?
faqs.answer: The line sits at production. Within the IB's limits, most of the useful work is still available. A tutor may teach the physics, discuss a proposed question and reject one whose independent variable cannot be measured well enough, insist on a pilot run, explain each criterion with its mark allocation, and give feedback on a complete draft the student has written. A tutor may not write a section, supply data, rewrite the analysis or edit to completion. A malpractice finding falls on the student's Diploma, so any provider offering a finished investigation should be refused outright.

faqs.question: Should my child drop Higher Level physics to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Check the university requirement first, because some engineering and physical-science programmes specify Higher Level physics by name and will not substitute. Beyond that, the useful diagnostic is whether the student is a band below target in one component or across all of them. One weak component is a technique problem worth fixing. Weakness across every component, in physics and two other Higher Level subjects simultaneously, is a workload problem. Facing that in Year 12 leaves far more options than facing it in the spring of Year 13.

faqs.question: Are there IB Physics Higher Level tutors available near Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Very few, honestly. Higher Level physics is among the thinnest specialisms in any tutoring market, and Dubai South is a newer district with a smaller resident supply of experienced subject teachers than the older Jumeirah or Al Barsha belt. A proximity-filtered search then removes anyone unwilling to drive the southern corridor at 17:00. Online delivery removes that travel cut, which is the expensive one, but it does not create specialists. Where no Higher Level physicist is free we give a date rather than seating a general science tutor.

faqs.question: What are the commonest mark-scheme traps in IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Sign conventions in mechanics, where a correct magnitude with the wrong sign loses a momentum question. Circuit reading, where analysing an awkward printed diagram as given produces the wrong resistor combination. Celsius where kelvin is required in thermal problems. Conflating field strength with potential at Higher Level. The direction of an induced effect, which causes more losses than its magnitude. Electronvolts against joules in quantum and nuclear work. And phase or boundary conditions in standing-wave and Doppler questions. All seven are visible on a marked script.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a Dubai South address?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script, the markband and the data booklet open on a shared screen and graphs drawn on a shared surface that is saved week to week. For physics that record is a genuine advantage, because a recurring graph or unit habit becomes visible rather than remembered differently by two people.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week does a Dubai South Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: One a week through Year 12, rising to two in the spring of Year 13 and in the weeks before the May papers, with a separate block for Paper 3 at Higher Level. The limiting factor is how much independent practice a student completes between sessions rather than how much teaching they can absorb. A more effective shape than a flat weekly commitment is a lighter Year 12 with a concentrated block around the investigation, then a heavier spring when timed papers and Paper 3 both need attention.

faqs.question: Is the data booklet useful if a student has never read it?
faqs.answer: It is permitted in the examination and it is a liability for anyone meeting it cold. Candidates lose time searching for a relationship that is printed on a page they have never opened, and occasionally derive something that was supplied. Twenty minutes spent reading the booklet and noting which relationships are provided and which must be recalled is among the cheapest revision actions available in physics, and it is as under-used as the formula lists at IGCSE. Do it weeks before the paper, not in it.

faqs.question: What should a Middle Years science student do before Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: A short quantitative block rather than content revision. Middle Years Sciences is marked against four criteria, with criterion B rewarding inquiring and designing and criterion D rewarding reflection on the impacts of science, so a student can hold a strong grade while arithmetic and prefix handling lag. Diploma Paper 1 exposes that immediately. Four to six sessions across the summer before Year 12 on prefixes, standard form, rearranging formulae and significant figures closes most of the gap before new content starts arriving.

faqs.answer: Published figures split by band. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33-52 on Tutopiya and AED 45-65 on EdFlik, which buys homework supervision rather than component diagnosis. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or more, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and BartyED reaches AED 650. In physics the cheap hour is often the expensive one, because a generalist reteaches concepts the student already has. These are market bands, not IB Gram prices.

intro.heading: The three comparisons that decide a physics grade
paragraphs: Physics produces a particular kind of enquiry. The student is not confused, the teaching is not poor, and the homework has been done. The paper comes back anyway at a 4 or a 5 and nobody can say why. Parents in Dubai Sports City then compare options — a tutor from Motor City or one from Al Barsha, an agency or a platform, in person or online — when the comparison that would actually help is a different one.

The first comparison that matters is Higher against Standard Level, because they are not the same course with different reading loads. Higher Level adds syllabus depth in every topic and a further written paper, which changes both the content to cover and the shape of the examination. A student struggling at Higher Level in the first Diploma year has a genuine decision in front of them, and it is better made with evidence than with optimism.

The second is physics against the other sciences. Students pick physics for engineering, for medicine, or because a sibling did it, and the subject rewards something quite specific: comfort with algebraic rearrangement and with explaining a mechanism in words. A student strong at recall and weak at manipulation will find chemistry or biology less punishing, and that is worth knowing before Year 12 rather than during it.

The third is the one the search is actually about: a nearby tutor against a specialist. And here the comparison resolves the same way from every community in this belt. A Diploma cohort in Sports City, Victory Heights, Arabian Ranches or DAMAC Hills might contain a handful of Higher Level physics students in a given year. The pool of tutors who have taught the Higher Level extensions, rather than general secondary science, is small in every one of those communities equally.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. What that buys in physics is a tutor matched to the level and to the components the student is failing, rather than to a twenty-minute driving radius that happens to contain a biology graduate.

The rest of the page works through those comparisons with data rather than adjectives: what Higher Level adds, where the marks are actually withheld on a physics paper, how much of the difficulty is mathematics wearing a physics hat, how practical work is examined when lessons are on a screen, and what the market charges for a specialist.

Confirm every date with the school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the internal deadlines that bind first in any case.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubai-sports-c.subjectsIntro: Physics divides into a small number of demands, and a student is rarely weak in all of them. Each entry below names what the topic asks for and where the paper withholds marks.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: Motion graphs, equations of motion, forces, momentum and energy. Marks are lost to direction being dropped from a vector quantity and to sign conventions abandoned halfway through a problem. Momentum questions reward stating conservation explicitly before any arithmetic.

subjects.name: Circular motion and gravitation
subjects.description: Centripetal acceleration, orbital motion and gravitational fields, with Higher Level extending into potential and escape conditions. Students confuse the force providing centripetal acceleration with an additional force, which produces an extra term and a wrong answer that looks careless.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the gas laws and kinetic theory. The reliable loss is unit conversion: temperatures left in degrees Celsius where kelvin is required, or volumes in litres where cubic metres are needed. Both are mechanical and both repeat every series.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves, the Doppler effect and, at Higher Level, further oscillation work. Phase and path difference questions separate the grades. Diagrams drawn and then never referenced in the written answer lose the analysis marks.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. The common failure is answering 'explain why the reading falls' with a formula instead of a chain of consequence. The paper wants resistance rises, current falls, potential difference across the component falls.

subjects.name: Magnetism and induction
subjects.description: Magnetic fields, forces on conductors and, at Higher Level, electromagnetic induction and alternating current. Direction conventions are the whole difficulty: students who have not drilled the hand rules produce correct magnitudes with reversed directions.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and particle physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear energy, binding energy and fundamental particles. Energy-mass calculations lose marks to unit choice between joules and electronvolts, and to rounding before the final step in a multi-stage answer.

subjects.name: Energy production
subjects.description: Energy sources, efficiency, Sankey diagrams and the physics of generation. Marks are accessible here and students under-prepare it because it feels descriptive. Efficiency questions still require the calculation to be set out, not asserted.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation marked against published criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Roughly half the available marks concern process and communication rather than the result, which is why a good experiment with two sentences of evaluation under-scores.

subjects.name: Mathematical skills inside physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, indices, standard form, logarithms where required, gradients and uncertainties. Most difficulty labelled as physics is this. A student who cannot make a quantity the subject of an equation will stall in mechanics, circuits and thermal physics identically.

sections.heading: What this search is really asking, and what is on offer
paragraphs: An IB physics tutor in Dubai Sports City means one-to-one Diploma physics teaching arranged outside school for a student in or around the Sports City master plan. IB Gram provides that live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, which is stated here rather than discovered later.

The specific thing most families want is someone who can read a marked physics paper and say what went wrong. That is a narrower skill than knowing physics. It means recognising that a correct calculation lost its final mark to a rounded intermediate value, that an explanation scored two of four because it named the effect without the mechanism, and that a vector answer was marked down for having no direction. Those judgements come from having taught the course and marked its papers.

The second thing families want, usually unstated, is permission to believe the problem is fixable. It generally is, and the evidence sits in the paper itself. When lost marks are sorted by cause, the proportion that are mechanical — units, rounding, direction, working not shown, command term misread — is typically larger than the proportion that represent genuinely absent physics. Mechanical losses are teachable in weeks.

What is not on offer is a promised grade, a tutor described as an examiner without evidence, or any help with producing assessed work. A tutor teaches the investigation criteria, questions the method, discusses whether the data supports the conclusion and gives feedback on the student's own writing. Writing, completing or producing any part of it is a malpractice finding against the student, and no deadline justifies it.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level in physics
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is not Standard Level with extra reading. It extends the syllabus within each topic, adds an additional written paper, and asks for longer chains of reasoning on the same underlying content. A student can hold a reasonable Standard Level profile and find the Higher Level extensions genuinely difficult, because what the extensions demand most is mathematical confidence rather than more facts.

That makes the level decision a real one, and it is usually made in the pre-Diploma year on the basis of IGCSE or MYP science grades. Those grades predict Higher Level physics performance imperfectly, because IGCSE physics is far less mathematically demanding than the Higher Level extensions. A better predictor is how fluently a student rearranges equations and handles indices and standard form without hesitation.

Where a student is already in the first Diploma year and struggling, the question is whether to move down. The honest framing is about what the course is for: if the intended degree requires Higher Level physics, the work is to rebuild the mathematics and stay. If it does not, a strong Standard Level grade is worth more than a weak Higher Level one on almost any application, and the move should be made early enough for the student to consolidate.

sections.heading: Where physics marks are actually withheld
paragraphs: Physics mark schemes are precise, and the reasons they withhold marks fall into a short list. Learning that list is the fastest work available to a student in the second Diploma year, because each item recurs on every paper and each is mechanical rather than conceptual. Most students have never been shown a mark scheme and are therefore guessing at what earns credit.

The largest category is explanation structure. A question that says 'explain' wants a chain: a cause, the mechanism by which it acts, and the resulting effect. Students write the effect alone, or quote the relevant equation, and score a fraction. Writing three linked clauses rather than one is a habit, not an insight, and it transfers across every topic in the subject immediately.

The second is unit and direction discipline. Temperatures left in Celsius where kelvin is required. Volumes in litres where cubic metres are needed. A vector magnitude given with no direction. Energies in joules where electronvolts were asked for. Each costs a mark, each repeats, and all of them are fixed by procedure rather than by understanding.

The third is arithmetic presentation: rounding an intermediate value and carrying it forward, or holding the working in a calculator so no method marks are available. The table below sets these out with the specific fix for each, and it is designed to be held against a marked script. Counting which rows a student's lost marks fall into gives the order of work for the next eight weeks.

sections.heading: Why Sports City and Arabian Ranches reach the same answer
paragraphs: Families comparing communities expect one to be better served. For physics the comparison resolves identically everywhere in this belt, and the reason is arithmetic rather than geography. Higher Level physics is a minority subject inside a Diploma cohort that is itself a minority of a school's year group. A given school in Sports City, Victory Heights, Arabian Ranches or DAMAC Hills may have a handful of Higher Level physics candidates in a year.

A local tutor market sized to that demand cannot be deep. There is no community in Dubailand with a surplus of teachers who have covered the Higher Level extensions, taught induction properly, and marked the extended-response paper. The scarcity is not a Sports City problem being solved by moving to Motor City; it is a structural feature of a subject taken by few students across every community at once.

What differs between the communities is only the clock. Sports City students are home earliest because their schools sit inside the master plan. Motor City loses weekday evenings to sport. Victory Heights adds a commute. DAMAC Hills and Remraam add more. Those differences decide when a session is booked and nothing else, and they disappear entirely once the lesson arrives over video.

So the comparison a parent should run is not between neighbourhoods but between a tutor matched by distance and a tutor matched by level and component. The first is chosen from a pool of a few people free in one corridor on one evening. The second is chosen from everyone who has taught the course. For a subject with small cohorts, that is the only comparison with a different answer at the end of it.

sections.heading: Practical work when the lessons are on a screen
paragraphs: The question comes up in every physics enquiry: how does practical work happen if tuition is online? The answer separates two things that are often conflated. The laboratory is the school's job. Handling apparatus, taking readings under supervision, and watching an experiment behave unexpectedly are school experiences and cannot be replaced by any tutor, online or in a room.

What is assessed, though, is overwhelmingly the written craft around practical work. For the internally assessed investigation, the published criteria concern research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. For the written papers, data questions ask which variable should be controlled, how to handle uncertainty, whether a conclusion is supported, and what is wrong with a described method. All of that is teachable on a shared screen with real data in front of both people.

In practice the screen is a better surface for it. Graphs can be plotted, re-scaled and annotated live. Uncertainty bars can be added and their effect on a gradient shown immediately. A student's own data table can be marked against the criteria while they watch. Doing the same work on paper across a table means the tutor reads the table upside down and redraws the graph by hand.

The division of labour to state to a student directly is this: the school supplies the bench, and the marks for practical work are awarded for the thinking and the writing. Students who assume practical marks reward dexterity with apparatus are consistently surprised by how much of the assessment is about control of variables, uncertainty and evaluation of method.

sections.heading: Physics, chemistry or biology as the third science
paragraphs: A good proportion of physics enquiries from Sports City are really subject-choice enquiries in disguise. A student is struggling, and the underlying question is whether they should be taking this subject at this level at all. That is a fair question and it deserves a straight comparison rather than encouragement.

Physics rewards two things: fluency in rearranging equations, and the ability to explain a mechanism in words. It is relatively light on memorisation. Chemistry rewards calculation discipline in a narrower set of forms — moles, energetics, equilibrium — plus a substantial body of organic reactions that has to be known. Biology rewards precise terminology and careful data interpretation, with the largest volume of content to retain.

A student who recalls well and manipulates poorly will find biology least punishing and physics most. One who manipulates comfortably but dislikes memorising will find the reverse. That is not a statement about ability; it is about the shape of the assessment. A student aiming at a degree with a named prerequisite has less freedom, and in that case the work is to rebuild the mathematics rather than to change course.

Where the subject genuinely is wrong, the earlier the move the better, and the first Diploma year is where it can still be made cleanly. Where it is right but hard, the honest plan usually starts with a mathematical rebuild rather than with physics teaching, because the obstacle is upstream of the physics and no amount of topic revision will reach it.

sections.heading: What a physics specialist costs, and why
paragraphs: Specialist scarcity shows up in price, and it is worth understanding where the premium comes from before deciding whether to pay it. The published bands in this market run as follows. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors.

In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted, and monthly packages advertised locally include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an exam year. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026 and none is IB Gram's price list.

For physics specifically the budget band is a poor fit, and it is worth saying plainly. A university student who passed physics can supervise homework. Reading a marked Higher Level script and identifying that an explanation scored two of four for naming the effect without the mechanism is a different skill, and it is the skill the enquiry is actually for. Paying the budget rate for that work usually means paying twice.

The in-home premium is a separate question and resolves against physics particularly clearly. The premium buys a journey. What the same money buys online is a tutor who has taught the Higher Level extensions. In a subject where a community might contain four Higher Level candidates, that is not a marginal improvement in choice — it is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available science graduate.

sections.heading: Permits, claims and what this page will not say
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications are made through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

In Abu Dhabi there is an additional consideration, reported in the press rather than quoted from policy: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are reported to prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same. Any family relying on that should verify it against the current ADEK document. It is mentioned because 'your child's own teacher, privately' is a proposition sometimes offered and not one to accept lightly.

IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Tutors are not described as examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status is never presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content.

Two further omissions are deliberate. This page publishes no IB session or results dates, because none could be verified from the IB itself, and a wrong date a parent plans around does real damage. And it publishes no success statistics, because any figure without a sample size, a date and a method is unverifiable by the reader, which makes it worthless as evidence however good it looks.

faqs.question: Is IB Physics Higher Level significantly harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference is not only extra reading. Higher Level extends the syllabus within each topic, adds a further written paper, and asks for longer chains of reasoning on the same content. What the extensions demand most is mathematical confidence rather than more facts, which is why fluent equation handling predicts Higher Level performance better than a previous science grade does. A student with weak manipulation will find the extensions hard regardless of how well they understood IGCSE physics.

faqs.question: Can a physics tutor visit a villa in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Published in-home market rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching. In physics the online pool matters more than in most subjects, because a community of this size may contain only a handful of Higher Level candidates and correspondingly few specialists.

faqs.question: My child understands physics in class but scores badly on papers. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the written answers are not in the form the scheme pays for. 'Explain' questions want a chain — cause, mechanism, effect — and students write the effect alone or quote an equation instead. Add unconverted units, a vector given without direction, and an intermediate value rounded early, and a competent student loses a grade's worth of marks mechanically. Sort the lost marks on the last paper by cause; the mechanical count is usually the larger one.

faqs.question: How are physics practicals assessed if my child is tutored online?
faqs.answer: The marks for practical work are awarded for research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and for the written data questions on the papers: which variable to control, how to handle uncertainty, whether a conclusion is supported, what is wrong with a described method. All of that is teachable on a shared screen with real data. Handling apparatus in a laboratory remains the school's part of the work and no tutor replaces it, online or otherwise.

faqs.question: Is my child in the wrong science, or just behind in physics?
faqs.answer: Test the mathematics first. Physics rewards fluent rearrangement and the ability to explain a mechanism in words, and it is comparatively light on memorisation. A student who recalls well and manipulates poorly will find biology less punishing and physics most. If the intended degree names physics as a prerequisite, the answer is to rebuild the manipulation rather than to change subject. If it does not, a strong Standard Level grade usually beats a weak Higher Level one.

faqs.question: When should the scientific investigation be started?
faqs.answer: Early enough that data collection can fail once and be repeated, which in practice means agreeing the research question a term before the school deadline. Laboratory access is the binding constraint, so the data cannot simply be rescheduled the way an essay can. Roughly half the available marks concern process and communication rather than the result, so a competent experiment written up with two sentences of evaluation under-scores badly against the published criteria.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write up my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the criteria, explain the mark ceiling on each, question the variable control, discuss whether the data supports the conclusion and give feedback on what the student has written. A tutor cannot write, complete or produce any part of it. That is an IB academic-honesty rule rather than a house preference, and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student, whatever pressure the deadline is applying.

faqs.question: Which physics topics cause the most trouble for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits, where explanation questions are answered with formulae instead of causal chains; magnetism and induction, where direction conventions decide the marks; and thermal physics, where unit conversion between Celsius and kelvin or litres and cubic metres is the recurring loss. Circular motion produces a specific confusion: students treat the force providing centripetal acceleration as an extra force, which adds a term and produces an answer that looks like carelessness.

faqs.question: How much of physics difficulty is really mathematics?
faqs.answer: A large share of it. Rearrangement, indices, standard form, gradients and uncertainty handling run through mechanics, circuits and thermal physics alike, so a student who stalls at the same algebraic step in three different topics has one problem rather than three. The diagnostic is simple: ask them to make a quantity the subject of an equation and watch the hesitation. Where the obstacle is upstream, physics revision never reaches it.

faqs.question: Does it matter that our Diploma cohort has only four Higher Level physics students?
faqs.answer: It matters for finding a tutor, which is the structural reason this search is difficult. A local market sized to four candidates cannot be deep, and that holds in every Dubailand community rather than only in one. It is also why availability tightens across the whole emirate at the same point in the year, after mock results. Booking before the mock window rather than after it is the practical response, and it costs nothing to ask early.

faqs.question: What should a student do with the extra Higher Level paper?
faqs.answer: Sit it to time, early, and expect the first attempt to be poor. Higher Level students commonly meet their additional paper for the first time in a mock, which measures unfamiliarity as much as physics. Attempting it in the first term of the second Diploma year, then again a few weeks later, converts a shock into information. The technique is partly about tolerance: writing something for every part, since partial credit exists and a blank earns nothing.

faqs.question: How long does a physics block need to be?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions for explanation structure and unit discipline, which transfer across every topic and show up quickly on a marked paper. Eight sessions for two or three genuinely weak topics drilled against past questions. One to two terms if the real obstacle is mathematical fluency, because that is built with short frequent practice rather than taught in a lesson. Any quote given before someone has read a marked script is guesswork.

faqs.question: What does a Higher Level physics specialist cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published specialist rates run from AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate placing specialists in the same range. Qualified online subject teaching is published from AED 200 for IB by Unitors. The budget band of AED 33 to 65 an hour, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, buys homework supervision rather than script diagnosis. All figures are provider-published and were read in October 2026; none is IB Gram's own price list.

faqs.question: Will moving from Higher to Standard Level physics harm a university application?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the course. Some degrees in engineering and the physical sciences name Higher Level physics as a requirement, and for those the answer is to rebuild the mathematics and stay. Where no such requirement exists, a strong Standard Level grade generally reads better than a weak Higher Level one on an application. The decision should be made against the admissions pages of the specific universities and courses under consideration, early in the first Diploma year.

intro.heading: Physics is the subject a late school run damages most
paragraphs: Most subjects tolerate a tired student for an hour. Physics does not. A mechanics problem requires the student to hold three or four quantities in mind, choose a route, carry units through and check whether the answer is physically sensible. A student who walked in from a forty-minute bus journey twelve minutes ago cannot do that, and the hour produces a comfortable conversation rather than learning. In the Dubailand belt, where Diploma students travel out to schools on Al Khail Road and in the Al Barsha and Jumeirah corridor, this is the practical problem that decides whether tutoring works.

The timing detail is specific. School days across Dubai's private sector finish broadly between half past two and half past three, but a bus serving several Dubailand communities takes much longer than the distance suggests, and the student dropped last is often home an hour after the bell. Add the thirty or forty minutes a teenager needs to eat and stop being a passenger, and the earliest honest start for a Diploma physics session in Arabian Ranches or DAMAC Hills is around half past five. In Town Square it is later.

Then there is what already occupies the week. Dubai Sports City and Motor City households run on academy timetables that take the five-to-seven window on several weekdays. On top of that, Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and KHDA advising no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. The taught week is fuller than a six-subject Diploma list implies, and the homework that follows it is proportionate.

The physics-specific consequence is that the subject needs the best hour available rather than the leftover one, and often that hour is on a weekend morning. Problem sets, data-analysis practice and internal assessment work all reward sustained concentration. Short weekday slots are good for consolidating a topic taught that fortnight and poor for anything that requires thinking at length. Recognising that split is worth more to a Dubailand family than any revision technique.

IB Gram's answer is to take travel out of the arrangement entirely. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so a session can start minutes after the student is home, move to a Saturday morning without rearranging a car, and be matched on level rather than on who lives nearby. Home visits are a service we run only in India; nobody is sent to a Dubailand address, and that is stated up front rather than buried in a term sheet. dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: Physics is best diagnosed by topic, because the losses are topic-specific and each has a different size of fix. These are the areas Dubailand students most often need rebuilt.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws, momentum and impulse. Taught early and relied on everywhere afterwards, so a gap here resurfaces for two years. Marks are lost by starting from an equation rather than from a free-body diagram that was never drawn.

subjects.name: Work, energy and power
subjects.description: Energy transfer, efficiency and conservation arguments. The recurring failure is an answer that computes correctly and never states which energy went where, which is what the markscheme pays for in the longer questions.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. Jointly with mechanics this is where the largest share of marks sits. Students lose them on potential dividers and on circuits redrawn incorrectly rather than on the underlying physics.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Superposition, standing waves, diffraction and simple harmonic motion. Higher Level goes substantially further. Phase relationships are the specific thing students describe loosely and lose marks for, because the language has to be precise.

subjects.name: Fields, gravitation and magnetism
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Field lines, potential, orbital motion and electromagnetic induction. Sign conventions and direction rules are the common loss, and they are drillable rather than conceptual, which makes this an efficient block of work.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and gases
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the gas laws. Questions often combine a calculation with an explanation of particle behaviour, and candidates answer one half and omit the other. A compact block, usually three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy, mass-energy equivalence and quantum phenomena. Content-heavy with fewer calculations, so it rewards organised notes and precise vocabulary, and it is a sensible topic for a shorter weekday session.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.levels: SL and HL, and the internal assessment
subjects.description: Error propagation, gradients with uncertainty, and the use of significant figures. This is where strong candidates leak marks on both the written papers and the internal assessment, and it is among the most reliably recoverable areas in the whole course.

subjects.name: The internal assessment
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation assessed against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The band is largely decided by whether the research question yields usable data, which is settled before any practical work begins.

sections.heading: Placing a physics session in a Dubailand week
paragraphs: The scheduling question comes before the teaching question, because a badly placed physics hour is close to worthless. Three facts drive it in this belt. Diploma students travel out of Dubailand to school. The journey home is longer than the distance suggests, because buses serve several communities on one route. And the early evening in Motor City and Sports City is already committed to training.

Work it through for a specific household. A Year 12 student at a school on Al Khail Road finishes at three, boards a bus that calls at two other communities, and reaches Arabian Ranches at twenty past four. They need to eat. A session starting at five is being paid for while the student is still catching up with themselves; a session at half past five works and holds. In Town Square the same chain pushes the start to a quarter past six, and that is the slot to book rather than the one that looks tidier.

Now split the week by task. Consolidating a topic the school covered this fortnight fits a short weekday slot comfortably: a worked example, a few questions, a check on understanding. Multi-step mechanics problems, uncertainty propagation and full timed papers do not, because they need the student to sustain a chain of reasoning for twenty minutes without interruption. Those belong on a weekend morning, and a family that plans both from the outset gets more from two sessions than from four badly placed ones.
The table below sets out the pattern by task rather than by community, since the task is the part a parent controls. The point of it is simple: decide what the hour is for before deciding when it is.

sections.heading: How IB Physics is assessed, and what that means for the plan
paragraphs: The structure matters because it tells a family where the available marks are. In all IB science courses the internal assessment carries 20 per cent of the final grade, leaving 80 per cent to the written papers. The IB revised the science syllabuses recently, so the exact number of papers and the split of weight between them should be confirmed with the school's own coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one. Our position on dates and weightings is the same throughout: if we have not verified it from an official source, we do not publish it.

What can be stated confidently is the character of the assessment. The written papers combine multiple-choice and structured questions with data-based items that ask candidates to read a graph, process numbers, and comment on uncertainty or validity. Extended response questions reward precise physical language and a visible chain of reasoning. Command terms do real work: state, describe, explain, deduce and discuss ask for different quantities of writing, and answering a describe as an explain wastes time while answering an explain as a describe loses marks.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with more questions. The syllabus is larger, the mathematical demand higher, and the questions more likely to combine two topics in a single item. A student who can handle a kinematics question and an energy question separately may still fail a Higher Level question that requires both at once. That combinatorial difficulty is the specific thing Higher Level practice builds, and it is why a tutor who has taught Higher Level recently is worth more than one who has taught Standard Level extensively.

The planning conclusion is straightforward. Secure the 20 per cent first, because it is the part with a fixed deadline and the part a student can control most directly. Then build paper technique across the final months. Families who reverse that order arrive at the internal assessment deadline with revision notes and no investigation.

sections.heading: Where physics marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Teachers who have marked these papers see the same losses repeatedly, and almost none of them are failures of understanding. That is the useful news for a parent, because habits change faster than knowledge gaps close. A diagnostic session with marked work in front of both people usually identifies the pattern immediately.

The largest single category is presentation of method. Physics markschemes award credit for a stated principle, a substituted equation and a correct manipulation, so a student who writes a final number alone collects a fraction of what the question offers. The second is units and significant figures, which costs marks on content the candidate knows perfectly and is purely a discipline problem. The third is diagrams never drawn: free-body diagrams in mechanics, redrawn circuits in electricity, ray diagrams in optics. Students attempt these questions from the equation sheet and go wrong at step one.

The fourth is imprecise language in explanation questions. Physics has a vocabulary, and loose phrasing reads as a misconception even where none exists. Saying that a force acts on an object because of its momentum, when the student means something defensible, earns nothing. The fifth is uncertainty treatment, where candidates can compute a gradient and cannot state its uncertainty or justify the number of figures quoted. The sixth is time management on longer multi-topic Higher Level items, which is drilled rather than taught.

None of these is addressed by covering the syllabus again, which is what a generalist tutor offers because it is the only plan available without seeing marked work. This is the argument for insisting on a diagnosis in the first session rather than a schedule.
