sections.heading: The internal assessment, and where it fits a crowded week
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade sits in an individual investigation, and the single biggest determinant of the band is whether the research question yields data that can actually be analysed. That decision is made before any apparatus is touched. A question that produces three data points, or a relationship with no measurable variation, caps the mark regardless of how carefully the write-up is done.

The work therefore divides into two unequal halves. The first, shorter half is choosing and testing the question, and it is where tutoring has the most leverage. A specialist can look at a proposal and say within a session whether the variable range is wide enough, whether the uncertainty will swamp the effect, and whether the analysis will support a graph with a meaningful gradient. The second half is the investigation and the writing, and that belongs to the student.

The scheduling problem is that the internal deadline is set by the school months before the board's window, and it falls in a term already full of subject deadlines. A Dubailand student travelling an hour a day does not have spare weekday evenings in that period. The practical answer is to place the internal assessment block on weekend mornings or inside a school holiday, which are the only periods in a Diploma year with genuinely uninterrupted time. Families who try to fit it into a Tuesday half hour produce a rushed investigation and a disappointed student.

The boundary is absolute and worth stating plainly. A tutor may test a research question, explain what each criterion rewards, teach uncertainty treatment and graphing, read a draft the student has written and identify where it loses marks, and demonstrate an analysis on different data. A tutor must never carry out the investigation, write the report, or redraft it to the point where the work is no longer the student's. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, which is an IB malpractice trigger, and the penalty falls on the student rather than the seller.

sections.heading: Practical work: what the school does and what a tutor does
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how a physics student is supported online when physics involves laboratories. The honest division of labour answers it, and it is not a compromise.

The school runs the practical programme. It has the equipment, the technician and the safety framework, and the internal assessment investigation is conducted there or under the school's arrangements. Nothing about online tutoring changes or substitutes for that. What a tutor works on is the part of practical physics that is assessed on paper, and that is a substantial part: identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, criticising a method, reading an instrument scale, propagating uncertainty, plotting with error bars, finding a gradient and its uncertainty, and writing an evaluation that distinguishes random from systematic error.

Those skills are taught better on a shared screen than at a bench, because both people can annotate the same data table and graph in real time. A tutor can put up a flawed method and ask what is wrong with it, which is exactly the question format the written papers use. A student can bring their own messy data from a school practical and have it processed properly, which is the single most useful thing that can happen to an internal assessment in progress.

On materials, the position is firm. We do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables; those are the board's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style. A provider advertising a download library of papers has a problem that a parent using it would be sharing.

sections.heading: What a physics specialist costs around the Dubailand belt
paragraphs: Physics has fewer specialists than mathematics, and at Higher Level fewer again, which shows up in both rate and availability. The sourced bands first, since three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

For Higher Level physics specifically, the budget band is rarely the right purchase. The work involves combined multi-topic questions, uncertainty treatment and precise explanation language, none of which a generalist can diagnose without having worked the syllabus. The sensible pattern is the qualified or specialist band for Diploma physics and the budget band reserved for MYP science fluency, where frequency matters more than expertise.

The in-home premium is the part a Dubailand family should examine closely. In this belt a visiting tutor is attaching up to eighty minutes of driving to a sixty-minute lesson, and the teaching inside that hour is not better for having arrived by car. Monthly, the comparison is roughly AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions: half the contacts for about twice the money, with the difference being the journey along Al Qudra Road. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

None of these figures is an IB Gram price list. Each is attributed to the provider or source that published it so a parent can check a quote rather than trust it. Our own answer to the price question is a free trial lesson and a conversation, because what matters is whether this specialist can name the loss pattern and fix it, which no rate card reveals.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and what a tutoring platform may claim
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the facts are simple enough that every tutoring page should carry them. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is speculating. There is a second rule worth knowing: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. That reporting is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy text, so verify against the current ADEK document.

Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall to ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

What that does not permit is a claim of endorsement. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal at least thirty days before expiry; that permit belongs to an institution with a location, which is not what this service is.

whyPoints.title: The 20 per cent secured first
whyPoints.description: The internal assessment has a fixed school deadline and the band is largely decided by whether the research question yields usable data. That is tested before practical work rather than rescued at the drafting stage, which is where most support arrives too late.

whyPoints.title: Weightings and dates only where verified
whyPoints.description: The IB science syllabuses were revised recently and ibo.org could not be verified by automated checking for this project, so we publish no IB examination date and no paper weighting we have not confirmed. Dates and splits come from the school's coordinator.

whyPoints.title: No approval claimed and no outcome promised
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no UAE office, no grade promise, and no statistic without the number of students, the date and the method behind it. The MoHRE private tutor permit, meanwhile, is free of charge.

faqs.question: What time should a physics session start for a Dubailand Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents expect. School finishes between half past two and half past three, but a bus serving several Dubailand communities often gets the last student home an hour after the bell, and a teenager needs thirty or forty minutes before they can think. In Arabian Ranches that puts the first workable slot around half past five; in Town Square it is nearer a quarter past six. Physics specifically punishes a depleted hour, because the problems require holding several quantities in mind at once, so the slot matters more here than in most subjects.

faqs.question: Is IB Physics HL substantially harder than SL?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference is not only volume. The Higher Level syllabus is larger, the mathematical demand higher, and the questions much more likely to combine two topics in a single item. A student who can answer a kinematics question and an energy question separately can still fail a Higher Level item requiring both at once, and that combinatorial difficulty is a distinct skill. It is also why the pairing with Mathematics Analysis and Approaches matters, and why a tutor who has taught Higher Level recently is worth more than one with broad Standard Level experience.

faqs.question: Which physics marks do Dubailand candidates drop most often?
faqs.answer: Six places, almost none of them understanding. Method not presented, where a final number alone collects a fraction of the available credit. Units and significant figures, which docks marks on content the student knows. Diagrams never drawn, so mechanics and circuit questions go wrong at step one. Imprecise explanation language, which reads as a misconception. Uncertainty treatment, where a gradient is found but its uncertainty is absent. And time management on long multi-topic Higher Level items. All six are habits, and habits change faster than knowledge gaps close.

faqs.question: How is the physics internal assessment supported without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: By working on the parts that are legitimately a teacher's job. A tutor may test whether a research question will yield analysable data, explain what each criterion rewards, teach uncertainty propagation and graphing, read a draft the student has written and show where marks are being lost, and demonstrate an analysis on different data. A tutor must never conduct the investigation, write the report or redraft it until the work is no longer the student's. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger and the student carries the consequence.

faqs.question: Can my child prepare for physics practical questions through online lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the practical skills examined on paper are screen-friendly. Identifying variables, criticising a method, reading scales, propagating uncertainty, plotting with error bars, finding a gradient and its uncertainty, and distinguishing random from systematic error are all taught better on a shared annotated document than at a bench. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school, which has the equipment and the technician. A particularly useful session is one where the student brings their own messy data from a school practical and has it processed properly.

faqs.question: Does a weekend physics session work better than a weekday one?
faqs.answer: For some tasks, considerably. Multi-step mechanics and fields problems, uncertainty and data analysis, full timed papers and internal assessment work all need sustained concentration that a 45-minute weekday slot after a long journey cannot provide. Weekday slots suit consolidating the topic the school taught that fortnight. The pattern that works through a full year in this belt is usually one short weekday session plus one longer weekend morning block, and deciding that split at the start beats adding sessions later.

faqs.question: What are the hardest physics topics for students in this belt?
faqs.answer: Electricity and fields produce the most consistent difficulty, for two different reasons. Circuits go wrong because students work from the equation sheet instead of redrawing the circuit, so potential dividers and internal resistance questions collapse. Fields and electromagnetic induction go wrong on sign conventions and direction rules, which are drillable rather than conceptual. Waves and oscillations cause trouble through imprecise language about phase. Mechanics underlies everything and is taught first, so a weakness there resurfaces for two years and should be addressed early.

faqs.question: My child came from Cambridge 0625 and is struggling in DP physics. Is that usual?
faqs.answer: Very. The step is about mathematical fluency and the expectation of explanation rather than new content. International GCSE rewards reliable recall and procedure; the Diploma asks for a visible chain of reasoning in precise physical language, and a student who scraped a good grade on recall finds the first Diploma term harder than their result predicted. The transition term is where most ground is lost and where targeted work is cheapest, because the second Diploma year leaves no room to rebuild a foundation.

faqs.question: What does an online IB physics specialist cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. Budget provision at AED 45 to 150 is rarely the right purchase for Higher Level physics, because diagnosing combined multi-topic losses requires somebody who has worked the syllabus. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included.

faqs.question: What weekly physics pattern survives a Dubailand term?
faqs.answer: One well-placed session plus occasional longer blocks is the pattern that holds, rather than two squeezed weekday slots. Frequency helps with consolidation; length helps with problem solving and data work. In the final months before the session the frequency usually rises for technique drilling, where repetition matters more than session length. What does not work in this belt is three weekday evenings, because the journey home and the training calendar make at least one of them collapse within a month.

faqs.question: Which exam session will a Dubailand IB physics candidate sit?
faqs.answer: IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. No specific IB examination or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unsourced date on a tutoring page is a liability; confirm dates with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications siblings may be sitting alongside, the UAE series are June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and its November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Why are Higher Level physics specialists hard to find locally?
faqs.answer: Because scarcity at that level is city-wide rather than local. Higher Level physics cohorts at individual Dubai schools are often small, so the number of teachers who have taught the course to completion recently is smaller than the number who teach science. Independent tutors also cluster where journeys are short, which in Dubai means the coastal corridor and Al Barsha rather than a villa belt forty minutes inland. A distance filter therefore narrows an already thin pool on the wrong axis, which is why removing travel widens the choice.

faqs.question: Do you provide IB physics past papers and data booklets?
faqs.answer: No. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets and grade boundary tables are the board's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from material the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. Be cautious of any provider advertising a paper library: it is a copyright problem they have not resolved, and a family using it would be sharing in that.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect a physics tutoring schedule here?
faqs.answer: School days shorten across the Emirates and energy moves to the evening, which matters more for physics than for most subjects because the work needs concentration. Sessions typically move later, often after Iftar, and shorten while holding their frequency. Heavy new content is better front-loaded before the month begins, with the Ramadan weeks used for consolidation, command-term work and discussion that tolerates a shorter attention span. Non-fasting students are affected too, since the school day has shortened for everyone in the household's week.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Fix the hour, then fix the physics
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: An IB physics tutor in Dubailand is only as good as the slot they teach in. Work out the real arrival time, decide which tasks belong to a short weekday session and which need a weekend morning, and protect the internal assessment window before anything else. Then match on level rather than on distance, because Higher Level physics specialists are scarce city-wide and a radius filter narrows the pool on the wrong axis. Book a free trial lesson at the hour you intend to use, judge it on whether the tutor names the loss pattern, and plan from there.

intro.heading: Three comparisons that decide an IB physics grade
paragraphs: Physics is the Diploma subject where families most often make a decision on the wrong information. The first comparison is Higher against Standard Level, and it is usually framed as a question of ability when it is really a question of content volume and of what the extra depth is for. The second is between IB Physics and the IGCSE physics a student has just completed, where the step is real but narrower than reputation suggests and lands in a specific place. The third is between Physics HL and A Level Physics, which matters because many schools in this cluster offer both pathways and the choice is made at 16.

Underneath all three sits a simpler question that a good tutor answers in one session: where are the marks actually going? IB physics assessment splits across multiple-choice and data-analysis work, extended written response, and a scientific investigation carrying roughly a fifth of the grade. A student at a 4 is rarely weak across all three. They are typically competent on recall, losing marks in uncertainty and graph work, and sitting in the lower bands of the investigation's evaluation criterion. Those are three repairs with three timescales.

The current course is organised into five themes covering motion and spacetime, the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields, and nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level adding depth inside each. The IB revised the subject guide in recent years, so the first thing to establish with your child's teacher is which guide their cohort follows, because older revision resources describe a different structure with an extra paper. Working from the wrong guide produces revision on content that is no longer examined.

Emaar Beachfront's practical constraints set when any of this can be done. The peninsula has one road link, no school and no tuition centre inside it, and visitor access to tower basements needs a resident escort. Children travel out before 07:00 to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah and come back after 15:30. Physics requires sustained attention on multi-step problems, so the realistic weekday floor is 17:00. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India.

The sections that follow compare Higher and Standard Level on content and assessment, name the topics where physics marks disappear and why, set out the step from IGCSE 0625 or 4PH1 into the Diploma course, explain the uncertainty and graph work that decides the data-based questions, map the investigation criteria to their allocations, and compare Physics HL with A Level Physics for a family choosing at 16. Confirm every weighting and requirement with your school; a tutoring page is a guide to the questions, not a substitute for the subject guide.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-emaar-beachfro.programmesIntro: Physics is taught under three different assessment models across the IB stages, and the skills that transfer between them are narrower than families assume. This is what each stage actually rewards.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Four criteria marked 0-8, covering knowledge and understanding, inquiry and design, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Students who can recall content but cannot design a fair test or evaluate a method plateau in the middle bands, and that plateau predicts difficulty with the Diploma investigation almost exactly.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school runs MYP to Year 9 and switches to IGCSE, students meet a written tiered examination instead of criterion marking. The investigative habits built in MYP remain useful for the Diploma investigation later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme physics
programmes.description: Five themes, two written papers and a scientific investigation. Higher Level adds depth within every theme and longer papers rather than a separate body of content. Multiple-choice and data-analysis work sits in one paper and extended written response in the other, which means two quite different exam skills are being tested.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. The investigation's internal deadline falls well ahead of it, usually in DP1 or early DP2, and it is the component students most often leave too late to coach properly.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with DP physics
programmes.description: Where physics is taken as one of the DP courses inside a Career-related Programme, it is marked to full Diploma standards and the tutoring is identical to a Diploma student's. The career-related study alongside it may add applied numerical work, which draws on the same proportional reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision across Dubai is narrow, so a family in this cluster pursuing it is likely to be choosing between a small number of schools rather than between neighbourhoods.

programmes.name: A Level Physics, the alternative at 16
programmes.description: The main alternative offered across this cluster's British-curriculum schools. Narrower than the Diploma in breadth, deeper in individual topics, with a different practical assessment model. Not inherently easier or harder; it suits a student who wants to specialise rather than one who wants six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving the Beachfront and Harbour towers offer both routes, which makes this a genuine decision at 16 rather than a consequence of where a family lives.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-emaar-beachfro.subjectsIntro: These are the physics themes and adjacent subjects we are asked for most in this cluster, with the characteristic failure in each. The failures are specific because that is the level at which a session plan is written.

subjects.name: Motion, forces and spacetime
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum, work and energy, with relativity content at Higher Level. Almost every lost mark traces to a free-body diagram drawn with unlabelled or missing forces, after which the algebra is impeccable and the physics is wrong.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws and the kinetic model. Marks go on failing to state the assumption being used and on mixing temperature scales mid-calculation. Students who memorise the gas law relationships rather than deriving them cannot handle a two-stage change.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave properties, interference, standing waves and, at Higher Level, further diffraction work. The commonest loss is a path-difference argument asserted rather than shown, and phase relationships described in words where a diagram would have earned the mark.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits and electromagnetic induction, with substantial Higher Level extension. Circuit questions are redrawn incorrectly before any analysis begins, which is the single most expensive habit in the subject.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactivity, nuclear energy, the photoelectric effect and quantum ideas, extended at Higher Level. Students lose marks on orders of magnitude and unit prefixes rather than on concepts, because the numbers involved are unfamiliar in scale.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and data analysis
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation, gradient uncertainty from a graph, and error bars. Examinable in the data-based paper and in the investigation, taught thinly in many schools, and responsible for a large share of recoverable marks.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation carrying roughly a fifth of the grade, marked on lettered criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Evaluation is the weakest criterion for most students, and it is the easiest to improve before a final draft exists.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion to Physics HL. Algebraic rearrangement under time pressure, logarithmic graphing and proportional reasoning are shared ground, so a physics calculation problem is frequently a mathematics problem wearing a physics question.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken alongside physics by students heading towards engineering or medicine. The shared skills are uncertainty treatment, graph interpretation and the structure of an evaluation, so investigation coaching in one subject usually improves the other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Physics supplies unusually good TOK material because questions about models, measurement and what counts as evidence are genuinely open. A physics tutor can help a student find examples that stand up rather than examples that sound impressive.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level: what the extra actually is
paragraphs: Families treat the Higher and Standard decision as a judgement about ability, and schools often present it that way. It is more usefully understood as a question about volume and destination. Higher Level covers the same five themes with additional content inside each, and sits longer papers. It is not a separate course with separate topics: a Standard Level student who later discovers they need Higher Level content has a gap inside familiar territory rather than an unfamiliar syllabus.

The destination question is the one that should decide it. University programmes in engineering, physics, and several medical and applied science routes commonly specify Physics at Higher Level or treat it as strongly preferred, and those requirements are set by the receiving institution and revised annually. Many other programmes accept Standard Level or do not require physics at all. The only reliable method is to read the current requirement on each target university's own admissions page for the named programme, in Year 11, before subject choices are locked.

The tutoring implication is practical. A Higher Level student needs more time on the extension content and considerably more practice on extended written response, because the longer paper rewards structure and stamina. A Standard Level student aiming at a 6 or 7 usually needs the same technique work in a smaller volume, and gains disproportionately from the uncertainty and investigation work that applies at both levels. A student struggling at Higher Level should be asked honestly whether the problem is the extension content or the technique, because moving down a level fixes only one of those.

sections.heading: Where physics marks actually disappear
paragraphs: The losses in IB physics are remarkably consistent and remarkably mechanical. First and largest: the free-body diagram. A student draws three forces, labels none, and then performs flawless algebra on a configuration the examiner cannot verify. The physics may be correct and it cannot be credited, because the diagram is the working. Second: circuits redrawn incorrectly before analysis, which produces a perfect calculation of a different circuit.

Third: uncertainty treatment, which is examinable and is taught thinly in many schools. A student who calculates correctly and omits the uncertainty, or propagates it wrongly, loses marks they had earned. Fourth: orders of magnitude and unit prefixes, concentrated in the nuclear and quantum material where the numbers are unfamiliar in scale and a factor of a thousand looks plausible. Fifth: extended responses that answer a cheaper command term than the one printed, which is the same loss that occurs in every Diploma subject.

None of these is addressed by re-teaching a theme, which is what usually gets sold. A student losing most of their marks to diagrams, uncertainty and command terms should spend a month on those three and leave the content alone. The marked script tells you which situation applies, and sorting the losses by type takes a competent tutor one session. This is why we ask for the script before matching anyone rather than after the second week.

There is a sixth loss worth naming because it is invisible on a script: questions left unattempted at the end of a paper. Students who work carefully through the early questions and run out of time have a pacing problem, not a physics problem, and the repair is a timing rule rather than a topic. Count the blanks on the last page before concluding anything about content, because a paper with four unattempted marks at the end was not a test of what the student knows.

sections.heading: From IGCSE physics into the Diploma course
paragraphs: The step from IGCSE 0625 or Edexcel 4PH1 into IB physics is real, and it is not primarily a content step. Most of the IGCSE content reappears, extended. What changes is the mathematical demand, the expectation that a student will justify rather than state, and the arrival of uncertainty treatment as an examinable skill in its own right. A student who finished IGCSE physics with a grade 8 and starts DP1 expecting the same relationship between effort and grade is in for a surprise in the first term.

The three gaps are predictable. Algebraic rearrangement now happens under time pressure and with multi-variable expressions, which is where a mathematics weakness surfaces as a physics problem. Extended response now requires a structured argument rather than a correct statement, so a student who wrote accurate short answers at IGCSE finds their marks capped. And uncertainty, barely touched at IGCSE beyond repeat readings, becomes a scoring component in both the data-based paper and the investigation.

All three are cheap to close in the first term of DP1 and expensive to close after the first mock, because by then a year of habit has formed and the student has concluded they are not a physics person. The useful intervention is six to eight sessions in the autumn of DP1 covering algebraic fluency applied to physics expressions, the structure of an extended response, and uncertainty from first principles. That is not remedial work; it is the work the transition requires and almost nobody schedules.

sections.heading: Uncertainties, graphs and the data-based questions
paragraphs: The data-based questions are the most recoverable marks in the subject, because the skills are finite and almost nobody teaches them thoroughly. A student needs to be able to state an absolute uncertainty, convert between absolute and percentage, propagate uncertainty through a sum, a product and a power, read a gradient with its uncertainty from a graph with error bars, and say what a line of best fit does and does not justify. That is a short list and it is examinable.

The usual teaching failure is to introduce uncertainty as a rule to apply at the end of a calculation. Students then treat it as a formatting requirement rather than as part of the physics, and they omit it under pressure or propagate it by the wrong rule. Taught from first principles, with the question "how well do we actually know this number?" in front of each step, it becomes something a student can reconstruct rather than recall. That distinction is the difference between remembering it in April and not.

Graph work deserves the same treatment. Students who only ever plot digitally cannot draw a sensible line through error bars by hand, cannot estimate a maximum and minimum gradient, and cannot explain why an intercept is not zero. Drawing by hand for a few sessions before returning to software fixes all three. The skills also pay twice, because the investigation's data analysis criterion rewards exactly the same competence, which makes this the single most efficient block of work available in IB physics.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation and the evaluation gap
paragraphs: The investigation carries roughly a fifth of the physics grade and is marked on lettered criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The marks are distributed across those criteria rather than concentrated in one, which means a student who collects excellent data and writes two lines of evaluation has forfeited a substantial share of the component. This is the most predictable loss in Diploma physics and it is entirely avoidable if the criteria are read before the work starts.

Research design is the second common failure and it happens earliest. A question requiring apparatus the school does not have, or producing too few data points to establish a relationship, cannot be rescued by good writing. Checking the apparatus and the expected data volume before the question is fixed takes one session and prevents most investigation disasters. Students who arrive with a draft and an unworkable design are salvaging rather than writing.

Evaluation is where coaching pays most and must happen before the final draft. A real evaluation examines the limitations of the method that produced the data, distinguishes random from systematic effects, and proposes specific improvements rather than generic ones. "More repeats would improve accuracy" is not an evaluation. Throughout this, the boundary is firm: a tutor may question the design, review the data handling and give feedback on the student's own draft, and may not design the experiment, process the results or write any part of the report. Invented data is a malpractice matter in itself.

sections.heading: Physics HL or A Level Physics: choosing at 16 in this cluster
paragraphs: Several schools serving Emaar Beachfront and Dubai Harbour offer both the Diploma and A Level, which makes this a real decision rather than a consequence of enrolment. The comparison is often reduced to breadth against depth, which is accurate and incomplete. The Diploma requires six subjects plus the core, so a physics student also carries mathematics, another science, a language and the Extended Essay. A Levels typically mean three or four subjects, allowing more hours inside each.

The assessment models differ in ways that suit different students. Diploma physics distributes the grade across a multiple-choice and data paper, an extended-response paper and an individual investigation, so a student with one weak exam skill has other components to compensate. A Level physics is assessed through a different structure with its own practical arrangements, and depth within topics is greater. Neither is harder in the abstract; they are harder for different people.

The honest decision framework is to look at the student rather than the qualification. A student who wants to specialise, dislikes carrying six subjects and has a clear direction tends to do better at A Level. A student who is strong across subjects, benefits from the core's writing discipline, or has not settled on a direction tends to do better in the Diploma. Then check the destination: university requirements are published per programme and change annually, so read the current requirement from the institution itself rather than relying on the general reputation of either qualification.

sections.heading: What a physics session should look like
paragraphs: The student works and the tutor watches the diagram appear. That is the whole format. A physics problem goes wrong at the point where the situation is represented, not at the point where the arithmetic is done, so a tutor who sees only the final answer is diagnosing from the wrong evidence. On a shared page the tutor can stop the student at the moment a force goes unlabelled or a circuit is redrawn incorrectly, which is the moment the correction is worth something.

A session should end with a small, specific task. Six problems targeting the diagnosed habit beat twenty that revisit secure content, and the next session opens by checking them. Where the block includes uncertainty work, the task should include one hand-drawn graph, because that skill decays without practice and students avoid it when given the choice. Across a term the pattern is narrow work, then whole papers under timing, then narrow work on whatever the paper exposed.

Every fortnight the student should sit a timed component, mark it strictly against the official mark scheme, and have the tutor audit the marking. The measure that matters is the gap between the predicted and actual mark, because a student who can predict their own score has internalised the scheme. Official papers and mark schemes come from the school or the board: we reference and explain them and do not redistribute board material, which is not ours to hand out.

Say at the outset if the investigation is the live issue, because the timing and the work are different. Investigation coaching should start before the research question is fixed and be scheduled against the school's internal deadline. Say too if the data-based paper is the problem, because that is a four to six session block with its own measure. Naming the real problem in the first message is what gets the right block in week one instead of week four.

The limits, plainly. We cannot promise a grade and no tutor who has marked a paper would. faqs.question: Should my child take Physics at Higher or Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Decide on destination first and aptitude second. Higher Level covers the same five themes with additional depth and longer papers, and many engineering, physics and applied science programmes specify or strongly prefer it. Those requirements are set by the receiving university and revised annually, so read the current rule on each target programme's own admissions page in Year 11. If no target requires Higher Level, a strong Standard Level grade is worth more than a modest Higher Level one on the same transcript.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose physics marks when the calculation is right?
faqs.answer: Almost always the diagram. A free-body diagram with three forces and no labels gives the examiner nothing to credit, so impeccable algebra on an unverifiable configuration scores a fraction of the available marks. Circuits redrawn incorrectly cause the same problem in reverse: a perfect analysis of a different circuit. Both are habits rather than knowledge gaps, both are visible in a marked script within minutes, and both repair in two or three sessions of enforced labelling and redrawing.

faqs.question: How much of the IB physics grade comes from the investigation?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth, marked on lettered criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Because the marks are spread across those areas rather than concentrated in one, a student who collects excellent data and writes a two-line evaluation forfeits a substantial share of the component. Confirm the current weighting and criteria with your child's teacher, since the IB revises subject guides on a cycle and no tutoring page should be the source of truth for a percentage.

faqs.question: Is uncertainty work really worth spending sessions on?
faqs.answer: It is the most efficient block available in the subject. The skills are finite: absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through sums, products and powers, gradient uncertainty read from error bars, and what a line of best fit justifies. They are examinable in the data-based paper and they score again in the investigation's analysis criterion, so the same four to six sessions pay twice. Many schools teach uncertainty as a formatting rule applied at the end, which is why it is so often recoverable.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE physics to the Diploma course?
faqs.answer: Smaller in content than its reputation suggests and larger in three specific skills. Algebraic rearrangement now happens with multi-variable expressions under time pressure. Extended response now requires a structured justification rather than an accurate statement. Uncertainty becomes an examinable scoring component rather than a note about repeat readings. Six to eight sessions in the autumn of DP1 covering those three is the intervention that works, and it is almost never scheduled because the early reports still look fine.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor touch on my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may test whether the research question is answerable with the apparatus available, check that the planned data volume will support a conclusion, explain what each lettered criterion requires, question the data handling, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the experiment, process the results, or write any part of the report. Invented or supplied data is a malpractice matter in itself, and our tutors decline that request directly.

faqs.question: My child is at a 4 in Physics HL. Should they drop to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Not before someone has read a marked script. A 4 produced by weak technique across diagrams, uncertainty and command terms will often become a 5 or 6 at Higher Level after a month of targeted work, because none of those losses is about the extension content. A 4 produced by genuine difficulty with the Higher Level material is a different matter and a level change may be right. Diagnose first; a level change made on a reported grade is a decision taken on the wrong evidence.

faqs.question: Which physics theme causes the most trouble for Diploma students?
faqs.answer: Fields, and specifically the circuit and electromagnetic induction material. The conceptual content is manageable; the losses come from redrawing a circuit incorrectly before any analysis and from sign conventions in induction problems. Nuclear and quantum material produces a different problem: students handle the concepts and lose marks to orders of magnitude and unit prefixes, because the scales are unfamiliar enough that an answer wrong by a factor of a thousand looks reasonable on the page.

faqs.question: Do physics lessons work over video if there is no laboratory?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work happens at school, and the examinable skills around it are written. Apparatus choice, sources of error, uncertainty treatment, graph construction and the structure of an evaluation are all taught on paper, and a shared page lets the tutor watch a graph being drawn and intervene when an error bar is wrong. What a video session cannot do is handle apparatus for a student, which matters for younger children and much less for a Diploma candidate.

faqs.question: Should we choose Diploma physics or A Level physics at 16?
faqs.answer: Look at the student before the qualification. A student who wants to specialise, finds six subjects a burden and has a clear direction often does better at A Level, where there are more hours inside each subject. A student strong across subjects, or not yet settled on a direction, often does better in the Diploma, where the grade is spread across a data paper, an extended-response paper and an investigation. Then read the current requirement for each target programme from the university itself.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a physics problem take to fix?
faqs.answer: It depends on the loss, which is why we ask for a script first. Diagram labelling is two or three sessions because it is a habit. Unit prefix and order-of-magnitude errors are one or two plus a checking routine. An uncertainty gap is a four to six session block. Extended-response structure is two or three and then permanent. A genuine gap in Higher Level extension content is longer, and anyone quoting a session count before reading a script is quoting a package.

faqs.question: Does Physics HL require Maths Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It is not formally required and in practice the overlap is heavy. Algebraic rearrangement under time pressure, logarithmic graphing and proportional reasoning are shared ground, so a student struggling with physics calculations frequently has a mathematics problem presenting as a physics one. If both subjects are weak, diagnose the mathematics first: closing that gap usually moves both grades, while closing a physics content gap moves one. Check your school's own recommendation on the subject combination as well.

faqs.question: What hour suits a physics session from a Beachfront tower?
faqs.answer: 17:00 at the earliest, 17:30 if the bus from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh is unreliable. Physics problems are multi-step and an error in step two is invisible until step five, so a tired student generates errors that look conceptual and get diagnosed as such. Weekend mornings are where we schedule investigation work, which needs ninety uninterrupted minutes. Choosing the hour honestly matters more than choosing the tutor carefully and hoping the hour holds.

faqs.question: Can you work alongside our school's investigation deadline?
faqs.answer: That is the only sensible way to schedule it. The school sets the internal deadline for the investigation and the reporting cycle around it, and those are the dates the coaching is built against. Send the deadline at the start so the design session happens before the question is fixed rather than after a draft exists. Coaching that begins at the draft stage can improve evaluation and communication, and cannot rescue a research design that was unworkable from the first week.

intro.heading: The honest answer to is there anyone near me who knows this
paragraphs: Yes, there are people who know IB Physics properly. No, there are very few of them within driving distance of Emaar South, and a parent deserves that stated plainly rather than discovered after a term. This page is written to answer the question directly, including the parts that are not flattering to us, because the alternative in this market is a confident claim that nobody can test.

Start with why the pool is small. Physics is a minority subject at Diploma level to begin with: most IB schools run one or two physics classes against several for biology. Of the teachers who deliver it, a smaller number teach Higher Level, which adds fields, electromagnetic induction and quantum phenomena and raises the analytical demand at the top of the markbands. Of those, a smaller number again have taught the particular Paper 3 option a given school has chosen. Each step narrows the field substantially, and none of the steps is about Emaar South at all.

Then add geography. Emaar South has no school inside it, so no resident teaching population has formed here. A tutor coming to this community is making a twenty-five to forty-five minute journey each way out to the southern edge of the emirate, in afternoon traffic, for one lesson. The number of Higher Level physics teachers who both exist and are willing to do that is small enough that a proximity-filtered search returns a list selected almost entirely by willingness to travel.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, so we are not competing on that journey at all. Emaar South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script, the markband and the data booklet on a shared screen and graphs drawn on a shared surface that is saved. That removes the travel filter from the match. It does not create physicists, and this page will not suggest otherwise.

What the rest of this page gives you is something more useful than a claim: a way to test one. There are six specific questions a parent can ask any physics tutor, in any market, whose answers distinguish somebody who has taught the course from somebody who is good at physics. They cost nothing to ask, they work on us as well as on anybody else, and they are a better protection than any amount of marketing copy, including this.

One factual note. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the reports. It does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. It is a legal licence, not evidence that anybody has taught physics.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The physics components and topics where a specialist and a generalist diverge most sharply. Each note says what somebody who has taught the course knows that somebody who merely knows physics does not.

subjects.name: Paper 1: multiple choice
subjects.description: A specialist knows no method marks exist here, so a correct chain ending in a wrong power of ten scores nothing, and that Paper 1 improvement therefore comes from unit discipline, estimation and speed rather than deeper understanding. A generalist teaches the physics again and the score does not move.

subjects.name: Paper 2: extended response
subjects.description: Method marks are available, so a structured answer stating its assumptions earns partial credit even when the arithmetic fails. A specialist teaches that structure explicitly. A generalist assumes a correct answer is the goal, which leaves available marks uncollected on every long question.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: Data analysis plus the school's chosen option topic, examined separately from the core. A specialist asks which option before agreeing to teach. A generalist does not know the question exists, and a student taught only the core arrives at Paper 3 having never attempted one whole.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error propagation
subjects.description: Examined in Paper 2, in Paper 3 and explicitly in the investigation's analysis criterion. A specialist treats it as examinable content with finite rules. A generalist treats it as laboratory housekeeping, which is how a student with clean data and no error bars ends up mid-band.

subjects.name: Graph technique
subjects.description: Axis labels with quantity and unit, sensible scales, a line of best fit through the spread, gradients read with a large triangle, and maximum and minimum gradient lines for uncertainty. Each earns marks independently of the physics, which a specialist knows and treats as a block of its own.

subjects.name: Linearisation
subjects.description: Rearranging a relationship so a straight-line plot is possible, deciding what goes on each axis before plotting. A specialist drills the standard forms until a square root or reciprocal suggests itself. A generalist can do it and has never taught a student to recognise when to.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Worth 20%, marked on criteria rewarding a methodology addressing all relevant variables and processing that includes uncertainties. A specialist insists on a measurable independent variable and a pilot run. A generalist helps with the physics and lets the design fail quietly.

subjects.name: Fields and induction at Higher Level
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, potential, and electromagnetic induction. The examined losses are conflating field strength with potential and getting the direction of an induced effect wrong. A specialist drills the direction rule rather than deriving it under time pressure.

subjects.name: Quantum and nuclear physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, deeper at HL
subjects.description: Photoelectric effect, atomic spectra, decay and binding energy. The recurring loss is electronvolts against joules, and mass defect calculations rounded early. Both are conversion habits a specialist names on sight from a marked script.

subjects.name: Mechanics and momentum
subjects.description: The trap is sign convention: without a fixed positive direction a student produces a correct magnitude with the wrong sign, which in a momentum question is the whole answer. A specialist makes the free-body diagram a non-negotiable first step.

subjects.name: Electric circuits
subjects.description: Examiners draw circuits that are awkward to read on purpose. A specialist teaches redrawing in a standard layout before any calculation, which takes ninety seconds and converts a hard question into a routine one. Very few students have ever been told to do it.

subjects.name: The data booklet
subjects.description: Permitted in the examination and a liability for anyone meeting it cold. A specialist sets an hour of annotating it weeks in advance, so a candidate neither searches for a relationship under time pressure nor derives something that was printed.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of a very small pool
paragraphs: Here is the funnel, stated plainly, because a parent asking whether anyone nearby knows this syllabus is entitled to see the working rather than a reassurance. Begin with teachers who can teach physics competently at secondary level. Narrow to those who have taught the IB Diploma specifically, which is a minority of them, since most physics teaching worldwide is A Level, AP or a national curriculum. Narrow again to those who have taught Higher Level, with its fields, induction and quantum content and its higher markband demand.

Narrow a third time to those who have taught the particular Paper 3 option a given school has chosen, because the option is examined and not every physics teacher has delivered every one. Narrow a fourth time to those with a free slot that matches a student's actual availability, which in Emaar South is late because of the journey. Each of those four cuts is substantial, and the result is a pool measured in individuals rather than in dozens.

Now add the fifth cut, which is the one a near-me search applies and the only one that has nothing to do with teaching: willingness to drive twenty-five to forty-five minutes each way to the southern edge of the emirate, through afternoon traffic, for a single lesson. In a subject whose pool has already been cut four times, that fifth cut removes very nearly everybody who remains.

Online delivery removes the fifth cut and leaves the first four intact. That is the honest description of what it does: it does not expand the number of people who have taught Higher Level physics with your school's option, it stops geography deciding which of them you can reach. The table sets the funnel out so a family can see where their own request sits, which also predicts how long a match will take.

sections.heading: Six questions that test any physics tutor's claim
paragraphs: These work on us as well as on anyone else, and they cost nothing to ask. Each has a short definite answer that somebody who has taught the course gives immediately and somebody who is simply good at physics does not. Use them on the free trial lesson, or in a first message, before any money changes hands.

First: which Paper 3 option have you taught? A specialist names one or more options. Anybody who asks what you mean has not taught Higher Level recently. Second: how many method marks are available on Paper 1? The answer is none, and a tutor who does not know that will prepare for Paper 1 as though it were Paper 2, which is the commonest structural error in physics tutoring.

Third: what does the analysis criterion in the investigation require beyond correct processing? The answer is uncertainties, and a tutor who does not say so will help a student produce a tidy report that caps mid-band. Fourth: how do you find the uncertainty in a gradient? The answer involves maximum and minimum gradient lines, and it is a procedure rather than an insight, so fluency with it is a reasonable proxy for having taught the course.

Fifth: what is in the data booklet that students most often fail to use? A specialist will name something specific rather than talking generally. Sixth, and the most revealing: what would you set in the first session? A specialist names a component and a technique, such as a timed Paper 2 section on graph and uncertainty work. A generalist describes an approach or names a topic. The table collects these with what a good and a weak answer sound like.

sections.heading: The Paper 3 option, and why it narrows the pool again
paragraphs: Paper 3 at Higher Level has two parts: data-analysis questions, which every candidate sits, and an option topic chosen by the school. The option is real examined content, taught in class, and it is not interchangeable. A tutor who has taught one option can prepare a student for its data-analysis section competently and cannot teach an option they have never delivered, any more than a chemistry teacher can teach an unfamiliar option from the textbook in a week.

That is why the first question we ask an Emaar South family enquiring about Higher Level physics is which option the school teaches, before anything else. It sounds administrative and it is the difference between a genuine match and a nominal one. A family who does not know the answer should ask the department, and the answer should be in writing, because it determines who can actually help.

There is a related honesty point about what a non-option specialist can still do. The data-analysis half of Paper 3 is option-independent: it tests graph work, linearisation, uncertainty in a gradient and the interpretation of processed data, all of which transfer across any option. So a tutor without the option match can genuinely improve half of that paper, plus Paper 2 technique, plus the investigation. That is a real and limited offer, and describing it accurately is more useful than overstating it.

What nobody should do is accept an option match on vague terms. If a provider says their tutors cover all options, ask which option this tutor has taught, and to how many cohorts. The answer is short and checkable. In a subject this thin, the temptation to blur that question is considerable, and a family who asks it directly filters out most of the risk in one message.

sections.heading: What a non-specialist gets wrong in physics specifically
paragraphs: The risk in hiring a competent physicist who has not taught the course is not that they will teach wrong physics. It is that they will teach the right physics towards the wrong target, and the script will come back looking the same. That is worth describing concretely, because it is the failure an Emaar South family is most likely to buy when the local pool is thin and somebody plausible is available.

The first error is treating Paper 1 and Paper 2 as one revision task. Paper 1 awards no method marks, so a candidate who understands a question perfectly and mishandles a prefix in the final step scores nothing on it, which means Paper 1 improvement comes from unit discipline, estimation and speed. Paper 2 awards method, so structure and stated assumptions collect partial credit. A tutor who does not know this prepares for one and hopes the other follows.

The second is treating uncertainty as laboratory housekeeping rather than examinable content. It appears in Paper 2, in Paper 3 and explicitly in the investigation's analysis criterion, which asks for processing that is correct and includes uncertainties. A non-specialist helps a student produce clean data and a tidy write-up with no error propagation, which caps the mark in a criterion carrying six marks and leaves everyone puzzled.

The third is missing graph marks entirely. Axis labels with quantity and unit, sensible scales, a line of best fit through the spread, a gradient read with a large triangle, and maximum and minimum gradient lines for uncertainty are each marked independently of whether the student understands the experiment. A tutor who has not taught the course treats graphs as a presentational matter. A specialist treats them as a block of marks worth its own sessions.

sections.heading: What happens when nobody is free, said in advance
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit. This one does, because an Emaar South family planning a Year 13 autumn needs to know which requests are filled quickly and which are not, and a pleasant surprise is worth less than an accurate expectation.

Physics at Standard Level is reasonably covered and a match usually takes a few days. Higher Level core is moderate and can take up to a week. Higher Level with a specific Paper 3 option is thin and can take a week or considerably more, depending on which option. Investigation supervision alone, and uncertainty and graph technique alone, are both better covered because neither needs an option match.

When a specialist is not free, what we do is say so and give a date. What we do not do is seat a general science tutor opposite a Higher Level physics candidate, because that costs a family money and a student confidence while teaching nothing the textbook would not have supplied, and it is the quiet default across much of this market. Declining work is unusual enough in this industry to be worth stating as policy rather than as a sentiment.

Where a wait is genuinely unworkable, there is a middle route and it is an honest one. A shorter block on the single most urgent option-independent component, usually uncertainty and graph technique or the investigation's analysis section, is useful in its own right and available immediately. It is a smaller promise than a term of Higher Level teaching. It is also one we can keep, which is the relevant difference.

sections.heading: How to verify what a tutor tells you
paragraphs: Claims in this market are cheap and verification is mostly free, so it is worth knowing which things can actually be checked. Three can: the legal permit, the specifics of teaching experience, and the output of a trial session. One cannot, and it is the one most heavily advertised.

The permit is straightforward. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's app, website or e-services with a two working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A tutor can show it, and since it is free there is no reason not to hold one.

Teaching specifics are checkable by asking narrow questions rather than broad ones. Which Paper 3 option, to how many cohorts. How many method marks on Paper 1. What the analysis criterion requires. These have short right answers. Broad questions, such as whether somebody is experienced with the IB, have no checkable answer and should not be asked, because the answer is always yes.

The thing that cannot be verified is examiner status, and it is the claim most often made. Unless a provider can evidence an individual's current examiner appointment, describing a tutor as an IB examiner is not something a parent can check, and using examiner status to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content would be a false suggestion in any case. IB Gram does not describe its tutors as examiners, holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE or IB approval or partnership, and operates no UAE centre.

sections.heading: Why physics is thin everywhere, not just here
paragraphs: It helps to know this is a supply problem rather than something about Emaar South, because it changes what a family does about it. Physics graduates have a wide range of employment open to them, and school physics teaching competes for them against engineering, software, finance and research. The result, across many education systems, is that physics is the hardest secondary subject to staff, and specialist shortage is a documented feature of the profession rather than a local quirk.

Within the IB specifically, the pool narrows further for structural reasons. Most IB schools run fewer physics classes than biology classes, so fewer teachers accumulate Diploma physics experience even within IB schools. Higher Level cohorts are smaller again. And because the Paper 3 option is a school-level choice, experience fragments across options rather than accumulating in one place.

What that means practically is that a family's expectation should be calibrated to the subject rather than to the general tutoring market. Finding a good IGCSE maths tutor in Dubai is easy and a reasonable benchmark for nothing else. Finding a Higher Level physics tutor with a matching Paper 3 option is a different exercise, and a family that budgets a week of searching rather than an afternoon is simply being realistic.

It also means early booking is worth more in this subject than in any other. A request made in September is filled on different terms from the same request made in February, because the small number of people who can do the work are allocated by then. For an Emaar South household with a Year 13 physics student, booking in the summer before Year 13 is the single most effective thing available, and it costs nothing to ask early.

sections.heading: What the scarce specialist costs, in published AED
paragraphs: Scarcity shows up in price, and the published bands reflect it. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200-450 or more an hour. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors online. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online and typically delivered by university students.

For in-home provision Bestimate puts one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. From Emaar South that figure sits at the top of its band because the journey is long, and in this subject specifically the in-home option is largely theoretical: the number of Higher Level physics specialists willing to drive here for one lesson is small enough that the band describes a service that is rarely actually available.

The specifically physics-shaped cost error is buying at the budget end for a diagnostic problem. A student losing marks to uncertainty propagation, graph conventions and Paper 1 unit discipline needs somebody who recognises those as three separate marked faults. A university student at AED 45 an hour will re-explain the physics, which the student broadly has, and the next script will look the same. That is the most expensive hour in this market, because it costs money and a term.

Every figure here belongs to the provider named and is published by them. None is an IB Gram price: our conversation begins with a free trial lesson and a written diagnosis. Bestimate's monthly estimates give the planning frame: AED 240-600 for budget provision at one hour a week, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

Each works from the current guide rather than from memory of an older syllabus.

intro.heading: Two neighbourhoods, one physics problem
paragraphs: Emirates Hills and The Meadows share a boundary, a set of roads and, in several cases, a school bus. A parent in one searches for an IB Physics tutor nearby; a parent in the other does the same thing twenty minutes later. The two searches return slightly different local results and lead to exactly the same conclusion, which is worth stating up front rather than burying: the useful variable in IB Physics tutoring is subject depth, and subject depth has nothing to do with which gate the tutor drives through.

It is easy to see why proximity feels like it should matter. These are villa communities with long internal roads and controlled access. A tutor who already lives inside the community saves half an hour at either end of a lesson. But look at what that saving costs. The pool of people who can reach an Emirates Hills plot by five o'clock on a school night is small. The pool who can do that and also discuss, without notes, how the 2023 guide restructured fields into Theme D and what Paper 1B now expects of a data-analysis response, is smaller still. Optimising for the drive quietly deselects the specialist.

The second reason the answer is the same in both communities is that the students are sitting the same assessment. IB Physics is examined in two papers and one internal assessment at both levels. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent of the grade and splits into Paper 1A, a multiple-choice section, and Paper 1B, a set of data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is extended response. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent and is marked against four criteria worth six marks each. None of that changes between The Springs and The Lakes.

What does differ between neighbourhoods is logistics, and this page takes that seriously rather than waving it away. The realistic start time for a weekday session is different in Springs 3, where children walk home, from the time that works in Emirates Hills, where the bus run is long. Which school a community feeds changes which physics teacher your child has and therefore which topics were rushed. A comparison table further down sets this out community by community, because it is the one genuinely local thing on the page.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run a UAE office and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India. The rest of this page is the physics: what the current guide assesses, where marks are lost theme by theme, how the Scientific Investigation is actually marked, what the market charges, and the boundary a tutor must not cross on a student's own report.
