dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-emirates-hills.programmesIntro: Physics requests from this cluster arrive at four different points in a child's school career, and the tutoring looks different at each. These are the four, with what the neighbourhood schools actually run.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Standard Level and Higher Level share Themes A to E and differ in depth, in additional HL content and in paper length. The experimental programme is 40 hours at SL and 60 at HL, including the collaborative sciences project and the Scientific Investigation. Students who struggle are usually not weak on physics; they are weak on converting a physical situation into a diagram, then into an equation, then into a number with a unit.
programmes.countryNote: Several IB World Schools within a short drive of Emirates Hills run DP Physics, including the IB continuum schools in Emirates Hills and The Meadows and the larger campuses along Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. Class sizes in HL Physics are often small, which is a strength for discussion and a weakness when a student misses a fortnight and there is no second set to join.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Physics sits inside integrated Sciences, assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is marked out of eight. Students who reach DP1 without having had criterion B and C work marked rigorously arrive unable to design a fair test or to handle uncertainty, which is precisely what Paper 1B and the investigation demand.
programmes.countryNote: The IB continuum schools serving this cluster run MYP straight into DP, so the MYP Year 5 science grade is a reasonable early signal of whether HL Physics is sensible. Families moving in from a British-curriculum school mid-MYP usually need a term of criterion-specific work rather than content teaching.

programmes.name: IGCSE to DP Physics transition
programmes.description: The most common single request on this page. A student finishing Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 moves into DP Physics and meets three new demands at once: calculus-adjacent reasoning, uncertainty propagation, and extended written explanation of a model. The content overlap is large; the assessment style overlap is small. Six to eight weeks of focused work over the summer closes most of the gap.
programmes.countryNote: Because the British-curriculum schools in Springs 3 and the IB schools in Emirates Hills and The Meadows sit inside the same residential cluster, a family switching sector at 16 often stays in the same community. That transition is predictable and should be planned in the spring of Year 11, not in October of DP1.

programmes.name: DP Physics retake and November session preparation
programmes.description: A student retaking Physics carries forward a marked investigation and needs almost entirely paper technique. The work is narrow and measurable: the question types that cost marks, the themes where recall failed, and the timing pattern that left Paper 2 unfinished. It is one of the few situations where a short, intensive block is genuinely the right purchase.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools predominantly enter candidates for the May session, so a retake conversation usually begins in July and runs to the following spring. Confirm which sessions your school offers before assuming a November entry is available locally, and check dates with the IB coordinator or on ibo.org.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-emirates-hills.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely tutored alone. The combinations below are the ones that actually appear on timetables in this part of Dubai, and each note says what the pairing does to the workload.

subjects.name: IB Physics HL
subjects.description: Themes A to E with additional HL content, a 2-hour Paper 1 and a 2 hour 30 minute Paper 2. The additional material in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics is where HL candidates separate from SL, and where a weak algebraic base shows up as a physics problem when it is not one.

subjects.name: IB Physics SL
subjects.description: The same five themes at lower depth, with a 1 hour 30 minute paper at each sitting. SL students most often lose marks on Paper 1B, because data-handling is taught through the practical programme rather than through the textbook and is easy to under-practise.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The usual pairing for HL Physics and for engineering applications. Calculus taught in AA arrives in physics before the maths course has covered it, which is why the first term of DP1 feels harder than it later turns out to be.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Workable alongside HL Physics but the algebraic fluency has to be deliberate. Students on this combination benefit most from physics sessions that spend their first ten minutes on the mathematics the question is about to need.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by students heading away from engineering. It is a legitimate pairing with SL Physics, but anyone considering a competitive engineering or physical sciences course should check the named university's stated prerequisite before settling it in DP1.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the assessment architecture with Physics: two papers, the same 36, 44 and 20 per cent split, and a single Scientific Investigation. Students taking both can learn investigation technique once and apply it twice, which is a real efficiency if the tutoring is sequenced.

subjects.name: IB Computer Science
subjects.description: A frequent third science in this cluster. The overlap with Physics is in logical decomposition rather than content, and students who are strong here often respond well to physics taught as a sequence of models rather than as a set of formulae.

subjects.name: IB Design Technology
subjects.description: Shares the experimental mindset and the obsession with evidence. Students who have done design work well tend to find criterion A of the physics investigation straightforward and criterion D, evaluation, much harder than they expect.

subjects.name: IB Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Taken alongside Physics by a number of students here. Its data-handling demands are similar, so tutoring on uncertainty, graph choice and error bars pays off across both subjects at once.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: The years that decide whether HL Physics is realistic. Criterion B, inquiring and designing, is the single best predictor of how a student will handle the DP investigation, and it is the criterion most often marked generously inside school.

sections.heading: Emirates Hills or the next community over: the comparison, done properly
paragraphs: Parents in this cluster compare neighbourhoods constantly, usually over school choice and sometimes over tutoring. It is a reasonable instinct and it deserves a real answer rather than reassurance. So here is the comparison stated plainly: between Emirates Hills, The Meadows, The Springs, The Lakes, The Greens and The Views, the things that actually differ are the school your child attends, the length of the journey home, and therefore the earliest hour a session can start. Everything to do with the physics is identical.

The school difference is the one with teeth. A community that feeds an IB continuum school produces DP Physics students who have come through MYP Sciences and have met criterion-based assessment since they were eleven. A community that feeds a British-curriculum secondary produces students arriving into DP1 from Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1, fluent in content and unpractised in uncertainty. Those two students need different first lessons, and the thing that tells a tutor which is which is the school, not the villa.

The commute difference decides timing and nothing else. In Springs 3 a child can be at a desk by four. From an Emirates Hills plot after a long bus run, five is optimistic and half past five is honest. On the Al Khail Road and Umm Suqeim Road corridors in the evening, that half hour is not padding. Booking a slot the student cannot reliably reach is the most common reason a tutoring arrangement quietly fails in month two.

What is identical is the examination. The same two papers, the same weightings, the same single investigation, the same data booklet. A student in The Views and a student in Emirates Hills are marked by the same examiner against the same criteria. That is why the recommendation does not change by community: find the person who knows that assessment best, take the session over live video, and spend the saved travel time on marked practice instead.

sections.heading: What IB Physics assesses now, theme by theme
paragraphs: The current subject guide restructured physics into five themes rather than a long list of topics, and a tutor working from an older syllabus will teach the right content in the wrong order. Theme A covers space, time and motion. Theme B is the particulate nature of matter. Theme C is wave behaviour. Theme D is fields. Theme E is nuclear and quantum physics. Running through all five are the tools of the subject, including experimental technique, technology and mathematics, and the nature of science.

The assessment is where families most often hold out-of-date information. There are two written papers. Paper 1 carries 36 per cent of the grade and has two parts: Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, a set of data-based and experimental questions drawn from the practical programme. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is extended response. The Scientific Investigation carries 20 per cent. Standard Level sits 1 hour 30 minutes for each paper; Higher Level sits 2 hours for Paper 1 and 2 hours 30 minutes for Paper 2.

Two practical consequences follow. First, Paper 1B is worth planning for separately, because it tests the practical programme rather than the textbook and is the component students most often meet cold. Second, a data booklet is supplied in the examination, so hours spent memorising formulae are hours misallocated. The skill being examined is selecting and applying the right relationship under time pressure, which is a different thing entirely and is trainable.

Treat the table below as a working summary and confirm the detail against the current guide through your school's IB coordinator. Guides are revised, schools receive the authoritative version, and no tutoring page should be the last word on a weighting your child's grade depends on.

sections.heading: Where students in this cluster actually lose physics marks
paragraphs: Loss is patterned, not random, and after enough marked scripts the pattern is predictable. In Theme A the damage is done by sign conventions and by treating a velocity-time graph as a picture of the motion rather than as a source of gradients and areas. Students who can describe projectile motion fluently still lose marks because they resolve components inconsistently between the two halves of a question.

Theme B costs marks through the gas laws and internal energy, where candidates write about heat and temperature interchangeably. Theme C punishes imprecision in wave language: path difference and phase difference are used as synonyms, and superposition questions are answered qualitatively when the mark scheme wanted a number. Theme D, fields, is where HL candidates separate out, and the separation is mathematical as often as it is conceptual, because potential and field strength demand that a student keep track of what is a vector and what is not.

Theme E, nuclear and quantum physics, loses marks for a different reason: it frequently arrives late in DP2 when the class is already revising, so it is learnt once and never revisited. A tutor who starts in January of DP2 should ask immediately whether Theme E has been taught, because the answer changes the whole plan.

Across all five themes, the largest single recoverable loss is not conceptual. It is the unfinished Paper 2. Students write excellent physics for the first two questions and leave the last one blank. That is a timing problem, it costs more marks than any topic gap, and three sessions of timed practice with an honest stopwatch fixes most of it.

sections.heading: The Scientific Investigation: four criteria, 24 marks, one chance
paragraphs: One fifth of the physics grade rests on a single piece of work that most students start badly. The investigation is capped at 3,000 words and marked against four criteria, each worth six marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Nobody in the competitive set for these queries names a single criterion letter, which is remarkable given that the criteria are what the marks are actually awarded against.

The failure mode is almost always criterion A, and it happens in week one. A research question is chosen that cannot be controlled, or that has only one independent variable in name. Everything downstream inherits the problem: the data cannot show a relationship, so the analysis has nothing to analyse, the conclusion overstates what the data permits, and the evaluation becomes a list of excuses. This is why useful tutoring on an investigation happens before the data is collected, not after the draft exists.

Criterion B rewards treatment of uncertainty that most school practical work never demanded: propagating error, choosing the right graph, drawing error bars that mean something, and extracting a gradient with its own uncertainty. Criterion C asks whether the conclusion is justified by the data and compared with accepted physics. Criterion D asks for a specific, prioritised evaluation of method rather than a confession that more time would have helped.

The boundary matters as much as the technique. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards, challenges the research design, points at a graph that does not support the claim being made, and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor never writes, completes or produces any part of the investigation. Work submitted to the IB must be the student's own, and a provider offering to produce it is offering your child a malpractice finding.

sections.heading: What a physics specialist costs here, and what driving between gates adds
paragraphs: Three of the six pages competing for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. A Dubai family budgets in AED, so here is the market in AED with the sources named. Bestimate's Dubai rate tables put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270. At the top of the market BartyED publishes AED 650. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, is advertised from around AED 45 to 150.

Now look at what the in-home figure contains. Published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to 500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799, against an advertised online package of AED 799 a month for eight sessions. The gap is not a quality premium. It is a vehicle, a security gate and an hour of evening traffic, priced into the lesson. In a community laid out like Emirates Hills, that is a large share of what the premium buys.

There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice. A tutor who spends two hours travelling for one hour of teaching can only work a handful of evenings, which means they cannot afford to specialise narrowly. HL Physics with confident command of Theme D and of uncertainty propagation is a narrow specialism. The economics of villa visits push the market towards generalists, and a generalist is not what a DP2 student six weeks from Paper 2 needs. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so this is an explanation of the model rather than an upsell.

Two cautions on all of the above. The figures are market rates published by named providers and read in October 2026, not IB Gram's price list; ask for a current quote. And none of it is a statistic about outcomes: no page on this site publishes a grade claim, because a grade claim without a sample size and a method is worth nothing to you.

sections.heading: HL Physics, the maths pairing, and what universities actually ask for
paragraphs: The decision that shapes a physics grade most is taken before DP1 starts: Higher or Standard Level, and which mathematics course alongside it. Families in this cluster often make it on the basis of ambition rather than evidence, and then spend DP1 absorbing the consequences.

The practical reality is that HL Physics leans on mathematics the maths course has not yet covered. Calculus-adjacent reasoning appears in physics in the first year, and a student in Applications and Interpretation meets it there first. That is manageable with support and it is not an argument against the combination; it is an argument for knowing it is coming. Students in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level have the smoothest run, which is why that pairing dominates HL Physics cohorts.

Where it becomes consequential is admissions. Competitive engineering and physical sciences courses state their own prerequisites, and some name the mathematics route explicitly. The only safe method is to read the requirement on the university's own admissions page for the year of entry, for every course on the list, before the subject choice is finalised. A tutoring provider is not the right authority for that, and any page that tells you which course a university prefers without naming the source is guessing.

A tutor's useful contribution here is narrower and more valuable: an honest read on whether the student is coping with HL, early enough that a change of level is still administratively possible. That conversation belongs in the first term of DP1. By DP2 the options have narrowed considerably, and the work shifts to getting the best available grade out of the course the student is already in.

sections.heading: The Dubai layer: regulator, permit and mandatory subjects
paragraphs: Physics does not exist in a vacuum here, and three pieces of local context change how a tutoring plan should be built. The first is the regulator. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and it inspects schools annually. If you want to know how a school's science provision is judged, the regulator's own published report is the source, and it is free to read. No tutoring provider should be describing itself as approved by KHDA, because a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises.

The second is the permit position for individual tutors. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure is quoted here.

The third is the mandatory subject load, which is the reason a Dubai DP timetable is fuller than its equivalent elsewhere. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with combined classes strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Those hours are real and they come out of the week a physics revision plan was counting on.

If your family is in Abu Dhabi rather than Dubai, the regulator is ADEK, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document. It is worth knowing before asking your child's own physics teacher for private sessions.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens when the right specialist is not free
paragraphs: The first message should name four things: Higher or Standard Level, which themes the school has already covered, whether the Scientific Investigation has been started, and the date of the next assessment that matters. Those four answers decide the match. HL with Theme D outstanding and an investigation draft due in three weeks is an entirely different brief from SL with a year to run.

The first lesson is free and is spent on evidence rather than introductions. The tutor asks for the most recent marked paper and reads it properly, grouping lost marks by cause: content not known, physics understood but not converted into a number, uncertainty mishandled, or questions left unanswered. The output is a written plan with dates, naming the themes being targeted and the components being drilled. You decide after that lesson whether to continue, and nothing is owed if you do not.

Coverage deserves an honest paragraph, because no competitor in this market offers one. HL Physics at Gulf Standard Time evening slots is a reasonably well-covered specialism. A narrow combination at an awkward hour, or a request that lands in the fortnight before a May session, is not always coverable. When the specialist is not available you are told before booking, offered the nearest available alternative and the slot that genuinely exists, and told plainly if the honest answer is no.

Nobody here will promise a grade, a points total or an improvement. Physics grades depend on the student's work, the school's teaching and the paper on the day, and a provider claiming otherwise is selling a feeling. What is on offer is a specialist who knows the current guide, marked practice between sessions, feedback on the student's own investigation, and a plan that counts the weeks you actually have.

process.title: Name the level and the themes already taught
process.description: The useful opening message says HL or SL, which of Themes A to E the school has covered, whether the Scientific Investigation has been started, and the date of the next assessment. Those four facts decide the match more than anything else you could tell us.

process.title: A free first lesson spent on a marked paper
process.description: The matched tutor reads the most recent marked script rather than making introductions, and groups the lost marks by cause. If the remaining weeks will not reach the grade you are hoping for, that is said in this lesson. You decide afterwards whether to continue.

process.title: A written plan counted back from the paper
process.description: You receive a week-by-week sequence naming the themes being targeted, the components being drilled and where the investigation sits. It is a document you can show the school, which is more useful than a verbal assurance about effort.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked work in between
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on a held Gulf Standard Time slot, with written notes afterwards and physics questions set for the week. The tutor marks that work, because unmarked practice simply rehearses the same mistake more fluently.

process.title: Investigation feedback at the design stage
process.description: If the Scientific Investigation is live, the research question and method are challenged before data collection, when there is still time to change them. Feedback is given on the student's own draft and the report stays entirely their own work.

process.title: A midpoint review against a fresh timed paper
process.description: Halfway through, the plan is tested against a new paper under exam timing rather than against how the lessons felt. Closed topics are dropped, the next costliest replace them, and a tutor who is not the right fit is changed without discussion.

whyPoints.title: The current guide, not a remembered one
whyPoints.description: Physics was restructured into five themes with a two-part Paper 1 and a single investigation. Tutors work from that structure, which matters because a student taught in the old topic order revises in an order no paper follows.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1B treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: The data-based and experimental half of Paper 1 comes from the practical programme and is where SL students most often meet questions cold. It gets deliberate practice every fortnight rather than a mention in the last week.

whyPoints.title: Criterion letters, not vague encouragement
whyPoints.description: Investigation feedback is given against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks. Naming the criterion is the difference between advice a student can act on and praise they cannot use.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on whose work it is
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, challenge a research question and respond to the student's own draft. They do not write any part of the investigation. This market contains providers who sell completed assessments outright, and the student carries that risk.

whyPoints.title: Market rates with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated. No invented statistics, no self-reported ratings, no claim about what a percentage of students achieved.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and coverage stated up front
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; there is no UAE office and no tutor is sent to a UAE address. Where a specialism is thin, you are told before you book rather than after.

faqs.question: Is an IB Physics tutor in Emirates Hills any different from one in The Meadows?
faqs.answer: Not in anything that affects the grade. The two communities share roads and gates, their students sit the same two papers and the same investigation, and they are marked against the same criteria. What differs is the journey home, which moves the earliest workable session from about four o'clock in The Meadows to half past five from an Emirates Hills plot, and the school sector, which changes whether a DP1 student arrives from MYP Sciences or from Cambridge 0625. A tutor adjusts the start time and the first lesson accordingly. The physics teaching itself is identical in both.

faqs.question: How is IB Physics weighted between Paper 1, Paper 2 and the investigation?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36 per cent of the grade and divides into Paper 1A, which is multiple choice, and Paper 1B, which is data-based and experimental. Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is extended response. The Scientific Investigation carries the remaining 20 per cent. Standard Level sits 1 hour 30 minutes for each written paper; Higher Level sits 2 hours for Paper 1 and 2 hours 30 minutes for Paper 2. Confirm the current detail through your school's IB coordinator, because subject guides are revised and the school holds the authoritative version.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B and why do students find it harder than Paper 1A?
faqs.answer: Paper 1B is the data-based and experimental section of Paper 1, drawn from the practical programme rather than from the textbook. It asks students to handle raw data, treat uncertainty, choose and read graphs, and extract a quantity with its units from a gradient. Students find it harder because school practical work is often taught as method-following, so the underlying skills were never assessed rigorously. It responds very well to practice: a fortnightly data question through the course means the skill is warm by the exam rather than met cold in a hall.

faqs.question: Which five themes does the current IB Physics guide cover?
faqs.answer: Theme A is space, time and motion. Theme B is the particulate nature of matter. Theme C is wave behaviour. Theme D is fields. Theme E is nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level covers the same five themes with additional content and greater depth, particularly in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics. The tools of the subject, including experimental technique, technology and mathematics, run through all five rather than sitting as a separate unit. A tutor working from an older topic list will teach correct physics in an order that does not match any current paper.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB Physics Scientific Investigation worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four, across four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It carries 20 per cent of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level and is capped at 3,000 words. The criterion that most often costs students marks is research design, because a question chosen too broadly in week one cannot be rescued later. Useful support therefore happens before data collection, when the method can still change. The report must be the student's own work throughout; a tutor gives feedback on it rather than contributing to it.

faqs.question: Where exactly does a tutor stop on an IB Physics investigation draft?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, challenge the research question while it can still be changed, point out that a graph does not support the claim being made, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor must never write, complete or produce any part of the report, and must not edit it to the point where the words stop being the student's. Providers in this market do sell completed assessments; the person who carries the malpractice finding is the student, so the line matters more than the convenience.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to an Emirates Hills villa?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. There is no UAE office or centre. The reasoning is in the arithmetic: a tutor reaching an Emirates Hills plot for five o'clock spends roughly two hours on the journey for one hour of teaching, which caps how many evenings they can work and therefore how narrowly they can specialise. Removing travel widens the pool to the strongest available specialist at that hour.

faqs.question: How much does an online IB Physics specialist cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours: Bestimate's Dubai tables put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. TutorChase publishes AED 270 and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. Budget online tutoring is advertised from around AED 45 to 150. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to 500, with monthly in-home packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against an online package advertised at AED 799. Ask for a current quote and take the free first lesson.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE 0625 into DP Physics. What is the real gap?
faqs.answer: Content overlap is large; assessment overlap is small. The three new demands are calculus-adjacent reasoning, proper treatment of uncertainty, and extended written explanation of a physical model rather than a short structured answer. Students who scored well on 0625 Paper 4 often find DP Paper 2 unfamiliar for that last reason alone. Six to eight weeks of focused work, ideally over the summer before DP1, closes most of it. The work is not revision of IGCSE material; it is learning to write physics at length and to carry uncertainty through a calculation.

faqs.question: Should my child take HL Physics with Applications and Interpretation maths?
faqs.answer: It is a workable combination and it needs eyes open. HL Physics draws on mathematics that the maths course has not always reached, so an Applications and Interpretation student meets calculus-style reasoning in physics first. That is manageable with support. The real question is admissions: competitive engineering and physical sciences courses state their own prerequisites and some name the mathematics route. Read the requirement on each university's own admissions page for the year of entry before the choice is finalised. No tutoring provider is the right authority on a named university's entry requirement.

faqs.question: When is it too late to start IB Physics tutoring before the May session?
faqs.answer: The goal changes rather than disappearing. With two terms left, themes can be taught, practised and retested properly. With eight weeks, the realistic plan is the two themes costing the most marks plus timing work on Paper 2. With three weeks, the honest target is protecting marks already earned: question order, command terms, data booklet navigation and finishing the paper. Dubai schools predominantly sit the May session, so count the usable weeks after mocks, Eid and family travel are subtracted before deciding. Confirm the session dates with your school's IB coordinator.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep running out of time on Physics Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 2 rewards structure and most students write linearly. The common pattern is a thorough, well-reasoned answer to the first long question, a slower second one, and a blank third. That costs more marks than any topic gap on the paper. The fix is mechanical rather than conceptual: practise allocating minutes against marks, start each part by stating the physics in one line before any algebra, and leave a deliberate gap to return to rather than stalling. Three sessions of timed whole-paper practice with an honest stopwatch recovers most of it.

faqs.question: Does a physics tutor working with Dubai students need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any quoted figure with suspicion. The official route is MoHRE's private tutor licensing service through its app, website and e-services.

faqs.question: How does the KHDA mandatory subject requirement affect a physics revision plan?
faqs.answer: It removes hours the plan was counting on. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. A Dubai DP timetable is therefore fuller than the equivalent elsewhere. When counting usable revision weeks, subtract these commitments honestly rather than assuming evenings and weekends can absorb them indefinitely.

faqs.question: What if no HL Physics specialist is free at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than after. Evening Gulf Standard Time slots for HL Physics are reasonably well covered, but a narrow request at an awkward hour, or one arriving in the fortnight before a May session, is not always coverable. When that happens you are offered the nearest available specialist and the slot that genuinely exists, and told plainly if the honest answer is no. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why it is stated here instead of discovered in week three.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-emirates-hills.closingBody: Compare the neighbourhoods on what actually differs: the school your child attends, the length of the journey home and therefore the hour a session can start. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time for students in Emirates Hills, The Meadows, The Springs, The Lakes, The Greens and The Views.

intro.heading: Most wrong physics answers are a belief, not a gap
paragraphs: A Diploma physics student gets a question wrong and the natural response is to reteach the topic. Often that changes nothing, and the reason is that the student did not have a gap. They had a belief: a model of how the world works that is intuitive, stable, and incompatible with the physics. Reteaching does not displace a belief. Finding it and confronting it does.

The classic examples are familiar to every physics teacher and almost never addressed in tutoring. That a force is needed to keep something moving at constant speed. That current is used up as it goes round a circuit. That voltage is a property a component possesses rather than a difference between two points. That the force in circular motion points outwards. That heat and temperature are the same quantity with different names. Each of those survives a competent lesson and keeps producing wrong answers afterwards.

This page is therefore organised around the syllabus and around what students actually believe about it. It sets out the five themes of the current physics guide, explains what the Higher Level extensions add inside each, lists the misconceptions that recur in marked scripts from this catchment with the question type that exposes each one, and then covers the paper anatomy and the scientific investigation.

There is a practical reason this distinction matters to a family paying by the hour. A gap is cheap to close: the content is taught, the student absorbs it, the marks follow. A belief is expensive, because it has to be found first, and it hides behind correct recall. A student can define Newton's first law accurately in one question and draw a net forward force on a body at constant velocity in the next, and nothing on the report card distinguishes that from not having learned the law at all. Buying content teaching for a belief problem is the commonest way physics tutoring money is spent without effect.

Green Community gives this a practical edge. The community sits inside Dubai Investments Park, low-rise and walkable, and most things a family needs are close. Diploma physics specialists are not among them: Dubai's IB provision is 7% of private enrolment across 227 schools and 17 curricula, and the schools serving this catchment keep Higher Level physics cohorts small. A radius search here reliably returns general science tutors and rarely returns somebody who can tell a belief from a gap.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Practical work stays in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision, as the IB requires. What a tutor contributes is the physics before it and the analysis and writing after it.

One note on dates. Cambridge and Pearson publish their timetables and we cite them where relevant. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one UAE schools sit and publishes no specific IB examination or results date.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-green-communit.subjectsIntro: The five themes with what each one actually demands, plus the cross-cutting skills that belong to no theme and are therefore the ones nobody revises.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, energy and circular motion, with Higher Level extensions into rotational dynamics and relativity. The dominant loss is a free-body diagram never drawn, so forces are summed from a mental picture and a direction is lost.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the kinetic model, gas laws and current electricity. Unit and scale errors dominate: temperatures in Celsius where kelvin is required, volumes in litres entering an equation expecting cubic metres.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, travelling waves, superposition, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with Higher Level extensions. Diagram questions reward precision about phase and path difference; a vague account of interference earns almost nothing.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction. The hardest theme in this catchment, because it asks a student to hold an abstract model and a sign convention simultaneously under time pressure.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear energy and quantum behaviour, with Higher Level extensions. Content-dense and usually taught late, which makes it the theme most likely to be unfinished when the mock window arrives.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, marked against criteria. Fails on measurement precision more often than on topic: data too noisy to support a claim leaves the evaluation criterion carrying the whole piece.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations and uncertainty bars on a graph. Belongs to no theme, appears on every data question, and is consequently the least revised content in the course.

subjects.name: Graph handling and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing what to plot so a relationship becomes linear, then extracting a gradient with units and saying what it physically represents. A gradient without units is a discarded mark on almost every data-based question.

subjects.name: Algebraic transposition under time
subjects.description: Rearranging a relationship before substituting. The skill that decides whether the back half of a multi-part question is reachable at all, and a loss that has nothing to do with the student's physics.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: "State", "describe", "explain", "discuss" and "evaluate" set four or five different depths. A correct formula where "explain" was asked earns part marks at best, because the question wanted a causal chain in words.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what each one actually asks a student to do
paragraphs: The current physics guide organises content into themes rather than a long list of topics, and the organisation is useful because each theme makes a different demand. Space, time and motion is largely about representing a situation correctly before computing anything: the free-body diagram is the working, not an illustration, and students who sum forces from a mental picture lose direction and sign marks the diagram would have protected.

The particulate nature of matter is about scale and units. Thermal physics and the gas laws punish a temperature left in Celsius, a volume left in litres, a pressure in the wrong unit. These are not conceptual failures and they are the single most common arithmetic loss in the theme, which makes writing the unit at every line the cheapest available fix.

Wave behaviour is about precision of language. Superposition, phase difference, path difference and standing waves all have questions whose marks hang on exact statements: a phase difference quoted as a fraction of a cycle, a path difference related to a wavelength. An approximately right account of interference scores very little, and students find that disproportionate until they see the mark scheme.

Fields is the hard one, and it is hard for a structural reason. It requires an abstract model - a field as a property of space - plus a sign convention, held together while a calculation proceeds. Nuclear and quantum physics is dense rather than difficult, and its real problem is scheduling: it is usually taught late, so it is the theme most likely to be unfinished when mocks arrive.

sections.heading: What the Higher Level extensions actually add
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is often described to families as "more content", which is true and unhelpful. The extensions sit inside the themes rather than after them, and what they mainly add is a requirement to reason across several linked steps on unfamiliar ground. That is a different demand from knowing more facts, and it needs different preparation.

Inside space, time and motion, the Higher Level work extends into rotational dynamics and relativistic treatment, both of which require a student to apply a familiar principle in a setting where their intuition is no help at all. Inside fields, the extensions push further into potential and induction, where the abstraction deepens and sign conventions multiply. Inside wave behaviour and nuclear physics, the extensions add quantitative treatment to what was descriptive at Standard Level.

The practical consequence is that the Higher Level paper punishes abandonment. A long question whose second part does not resolve cleanly causes students to stop, when the third and fourth parts are frequently reachable from a partial result. Practising persistence specifically - carrying an incomplete value forward deliberately and seeing which later parts it opens up - is a separate exercise from practising content, and it is rarely done.

For a family deciding between the levels, the honest test is tolerance for sustained unfamiliarity rather than comfort with the current content. A student who is comfortable with the Standard Level material but stops at the first unclear step may achieve a better grade at Standard Level, and that is a legitimate choice rather than a retreat. Read the entry requirements of two or three target degree programmes before confirming either way.

sections.heading: The misconceptions that survive good teaching
paragraphs: Physics education research has catalogued these for decades and tutoring almost never uses the catalogue. A misconception is not ignorance. It is a working model of the world, built from experience, that produces correct predictions in everyday life and wrong answers in physics. Because it works most of the time, a lesson that contradicts it does not displace it; the student learns the formal answer for the test and keeps the belief.

The commonest one is that a force is required to maintain motion at constant velocity. Everyday experience supports this, because everyday motion involves friction. The student learns Newton's first law, answers a recall question correctly, and then on a question about a body moving at constant speed draws a net forward force. The question that exposes it asks what happens to an object in deep space when the engine stops.

In electricity there are two. That current is used up as it flows round a circuit, which produces answers where the current after a lamp is smaller than before it. And that voltage is a property a component has, rather than a difference in potential between two points, which makes series and parallel reasoning collapse. In circular motion, the belief in an outward force is almost universal and survives a correct definition of centripetal force. In thermal physics, heat and temperature are treated as one quantity, which breaks every question about latent heat.

The method for all of them is the same and it is not reteaching. Ask the student to predict, out loud, before any calculation. Then present the case their model cannot explain and work through the contradiction with them rather than announcing it. That takes longer than an explanation and it is the only thing that moves a belief, which is why it is worth a session rather than a sentence.

sections.heading: Paper anatomy, and the habit each section punishes
paragraphs: Diploma physics is examined across paper components that combine multiple-choice questions, a data-analysis section and short and extended written response. Each punishes a different behaviour, which means whole-paper practice late in the course tells a student their total and hides the cause.

Multiple choice punishes recognition in place of reasoning. The distractors are built from exactly the misconceptions listed above, plus the common algebraic slips, so an option that feels obviously right is frequently the designed trap for a student holding one of those beliefs. The remedy is to work the physics rather than to recognise the shape, which costs seconds and saves marks.

The data-analysis section punishes weak uncertainty and graph handling, and rewards a skill that is barely taught: judging what the data can and cannot support. A student who asserts a proportional relationship from points whose uncertainty bars overlap has made a physics error. Linearisation, gradient units and the physical meaning of a gradient are all marked here, and all are learnable in three or four sessions.

Extended response punishes depth mismatch. "Explain" wants a causal chain in words; "discuss" wants both sides reaching a destination; "evaluate" wants a judgement with evidence. A student whose default register is a correct statement of physics scores well on recall and consistently loses the high-tariff marks, paper after paper, without ever identifying the pattern - because each individual loss looks like bad luck.

The practical consequence is that late preparation should separate the sections rather than sitting whole papers. Twenty multiple-choice questions, then one data-analysis section, then four extended-response questions, each marked separately, tells a student which of the three is leaking marks. A whole paper tells them a total and leaves the cause buried.

sections.heading: The investigation is physics, and it is marked as physics
paragraphs: Students treat the scientific investigation as a writing task with a practical attached. The criteria treat it as physics: whether the research design can answer the question, whether the data is treated honestly, whether the conclusion follows from the evidence, and whether the evaluation understands the limitations of what was done.

Physics investigations in this catchment fail on measurement more often than on topic choice. A dependent variable that cannot be measured to a useful precision with the school's apparatus produces data so noisy that no conclusion is defensible, and the student then writes a conclusion anyway. The fix is upstream: before committing, estimate the expected size of the effect and compare it against the resolution of the instrument available. If the effect is smaller than the uncertainty, the question needs changing.

The second recurring failure is uncertainty treated as decoration. An uncertainty quoted as a plausible round number rather than derived from the instrument's resolution; a percentage uncertainty calculated once and never propagated through the subsequent multiplication; uncertainty bars drawn as a constant width because it looked tidy. Each of those costs marks in the analysis criterion and then again in the evaluation criterion, because there is nothing real for the evaluation to engage with.

The boundary is firm. A tutor may help narrow the question, check that the effect is measurable with the available apparatus, teach the physics, explain each criterion and its mark ceiling, check propagation, question whether the conclusion follows, and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the question, or produce or adjust data. Services in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and submitting bought work risks the whole Diploma.

sections.heading: The mathematics inside physics, which is where many physics marks actually go
paragraphs: A good proportion of what looks like weak physics is weak mathematics wearing a physics costume, and separating the two is one of the more valuable things a first session does. Three skills account for most of it.

Transposition first. A student who recognises a relationship but cannot rearrange it quickly loses every part of a multi-part question after the first, because each later part needs the subject changed. This is not a physics problem and it will not improve with more physics. It improves with ten minutes of manipulation practice per session, by hand, marked.

Second, powers of ten and prefixes. Physics is full of quantities spanning many orders of magnitude, and a nano mishandled or a kilo applied twice invalidates an otherwise flawless calculation. Students who are confident with the physics and careless with the prefix produce answers wrong by a factor of a thousand and do not notice, because nothing about the method looked wrong.

Third, proportional reasoning. Many questions ask what happens to one quantity when another doubles, and the efficient route is proportional rather than computational. Students who substitute numbers into the full relationship each time arrive at the same answer more slowly, and in a timed paper slower is fewer marks. Teaching the proportional route is a single session that pays across every theme.

The diagnostic for all three is quick. Give the student a relationship and ask them to make a named quantity the subject, out loud, with a timer running. Then give them a calculation containing a prefix and watch whether they convert before substituting. Then ask what happens to one quantity when another doubles, and see whether they reach for numbers or for a ratio. Five minutes, and it usually settles whether the next month is about physics at all.

paragraphs: Four bands, read October 2026 and attributed to whoever published the figure. Online entry: Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45-65. Online subject tuition: Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. In the home: Dubai rate guidance puts one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors advertising to AED 500. And the specialist exam-year tier, published at AED 200-450 and above, where TutorChase quotes around AED 270 and BartyED publishes AED 650. Hold the two extremes together before reading on, because the comparison is the whole argument of this section: the top of that list is close to twenty times the bottom for one hour of somebody's attention, and in Diploma physics it is nowhere near twenty times as useful.

For Diploma physics the entry band does very little that is relevant. Someone at the lower end can keep a student working through questions and cannot find the belief behind a wrong answer, which is the specific skill this subject needs. The real decision is between the AED 150-300 online band and the AED 180-500 in-home band, and the difference between those is substantially the journey.

Monthly figures help with planning. Dubai rate guidance estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. None of these are IB Gram prices, and this page has no rate card because the fee depends on level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The bands exist so that a quote can be judged against something published. sections.heading: Online physics from Green Community, with the limits named
paragraphs: The format fits the assessed work. Diploma physics tutoring is mostly document and diagram work: a marked script, a data question, a draft investigation, a graph that needs interrogating, a free-body diagram that was never drawn. A shared screen where both people annotate the same plot or diagram is better than one paper copy across a table, and the session is reviewable afterwards.

Misconception work in particular suits it, because the method requires the student to commit to a prediction in writing before any calculation. On a shared screen that prediction is visible, timestamped and impossible to quietly revise, which is exactly the pressure the method needs. Across a table it is easier for a student to slide from their actual belief to the answer they think is wanted.

One limit here is structural rather than pedagogical, and it was stated near the top of this page rather than left down here to be discovered: IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE, because in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. A Green Community family weighing that against a local in-home quote should know why we put it in the opening paragraphs instead. Two providers ranking for UAE searches route the enquiry to an Indian telephone number without disclosing anywhere on the page that delivery is remote, and a parent who has budgeted the AED 180-350 in-home band for somebody to arrive at the house deserves to learn that before the first invoice rather than after it.

The honest limits: a student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better in person; a weak connection shortens the hour whatever the clock says; a shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines the lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room; and no online tutor substitutes for laboratory time, which under IB rules belongs to the school. If one of those applies, hire locally and ask about the MoHRE private tuition work permit first.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and how to start
paragraphs: The section above ended with an instruction to ask about the permit, so here is what you would be asking about. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, it is issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states that it is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible list runs to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 - which is to say almost everybody who teaches physics privately in this part of Dubai. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of those penalties is published, so distrust any figure quoted at you as though it were. One arrangement to refuse whatever the permit says: never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher.

What we do not claim: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation or partnership. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not evidenceable for individuals and is routinely used in this market to imply access to marking or grade boundaries that nobody has. We promise no grade, points total or improvement figure, and publish no statistic without its source and date.

We also do not host or distribute IB papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, which are copyright material. We reference and link the official sources and work from the copies your child's school is licensed to provide, and a service offering a complete library of papers or unreleased material is worth declining on that basis.

To start, send the level - Higher or Standard - the school, and a photograph of the most recent marked script, or the current investigation draft if that is the live deadline. The first session reads the script for two things: which beliefs are producing wrong answers, and whether the losses are physics or the mathematics inside it. The written note at the end says which, and it is yours whether or not you continue.

faqs.question: Why does reteaching a physics topic not improve my child's marks?
faqs.answer: Because the problem is often a belief rather than a gap. A student may hold a working model of the world - that a force is needed to keep something moving, that current is used up round a circuit - which produces correct predictions in everyday life and wrong answers in physics. A lesson that contradicts it teaches the formal answer for the test and leaves the belief intact. What displaces it is being asked to predict first, then being shown the case the belief cannot explain, and working through the contradiction.

faqs.question: How is the current IB physics syllabus organised into themes?
faqs.answer: The guide organises content into themes covering space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level extensions sitting inside each theme rather than appended after it. Each theme makes a different demand: representation before computation in the first, unit and scale discipline in the second, precision of language in the third, abstraction plus sign conventions in the fourth, and volume recalled accurately in the fifth. Confirm the current structure against your school's subject guide.

faqs.question: Which IB physics theme causes most trouble in this catchment?
faqs.answer: Fields, consistently, and for a structural reason rather than a difficulty of content. It asks a student to hold an abstract model - a field as a property of space - together with a sign convention, while a calculation proceeds. Errors appear mid-working and are invisible afterwards. Nuclear and quantum physics causes a different problem: it is dense rather than hard and usually taught late, so it is the theme most likely to be unfinished when the mock papers arrive and the content window has closed.

faqs.question: My child thinks current gets used up in a circuit. Is that common?
faqs.answer: Very, and it is one of the most durable misconceptions in the subject. It produces answers in which the current after a lamp is smaller than before it, and it makes every series and parallel question unreliable. The exposure is simple: ask what two ammeters placed either side of a lamp would read, and have the student commit to a prediction before measuring or calculating. Working through why charge is conserved while energy is transferred is what replaces the belief, and it takes a session rather than a sentence.

faqs.question: Are my child's physics marks lost to physics or to maths?
faqs.answer: Frequently to the mathematics inside the physics, and separating the two is one of the more useful things a first session does. Three skills account for most of it: transposing a relationship quickly, which decides whether the later parts of a multi-part question are reachable; handling powers of ten and prefixes, where a misplaced nano produces an answer wrong by a factor of a thousand; and proportional reasoning, where substituting full numbers costs time a ratio would have saved. None of those improve with more physics teaching.

faqs.question: How do multiple-choice physics questions catch students out?
faqs.answer: The distractors are built from the standard misconceptions and the common algebraic slips, so an option that feels obviously right is often the designed trap for a student holding one of those beliefs. An outward force in circular motion, a smaller current after a lamp, a latent heat question answered with a temperature change: each has a waiting option. The remedy is to work the physics rather than recognise the question shape, which costs a few seconds per question and is the cheapest marks available on that section.

faqs.question: What does "explain" mean in an IB physics question?
faqs.answer: A causal chain written in words: this changes, which causes that, which produces the stated outcome. A correct formula is not a chain, and neither is a restatement of the question in physics vocabulary. Both are extremely common among students arriving from IGCSE, where a correct substitution usually carried the mark, and both earn part marks at best. The drill is to take explanation questions only, strip the numbers out, and require linked clauses with no equations permitted, then add the equation back as supporting detail.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics investigation without breaching IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary. A tutor can help narrow the research question, check that the expected effect is measurable with the school's apparatus, teach the physics involved, explain each criterion and its mark ceiling, check whether uncertainties were derived or invented, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the question, or produce or adjust data. Every sentence must be typed by your child.

faqs.question: Why do physics investigations produce unusable data?
faqs.answer: Usually because the expected effect is smaller than the measurement uncertainty, and nobody checked before the practical. The student collects data too noisy to support any conclusion, writes a conclusion anyway, and loses marks in both the analysis and the evaluation criteria. The check is upstream and takes twenty minutes: estimate the size of the effect the question expects, then compare it against the resolution of the instrument actually available in the school laboratory. If the effect is smaller, the question needs changing while there is still time.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics the right choice for a Green Community student?
faqs.answer: The honest test is tolerance for sustained unfamiliarity rather than comfort with the current content. The Higher Level extensions sit inside each theme and mainly demand reasoning across several linked steps on unfamiliar ground, which punishes a student who stops at the first part that does not resolve cleanly. A student comfortable with Standard Level material who abandons unclear questions may achieve a better grade at Standard Level, and that is a legitimate choice. Read two or three target degree entry requirements before deciding either way.

faqs.question: How does an online physics tutor handle diagrams?
faqs.answer: Better than a paper copy on a table, in practice. The commonest loss in space, time and motion is a free-body diagram never drawn, so a format where the shared screen makes drawing the default is useful rather than a compromise: the tutor draws the diagram the student skipped, and the student redraws it immediately on the same page. The whole session is also reviewable afterwards, which matters for diagram conventions that need to become automatic rather than being understood once.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match a physics specialist near Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Standard Level physics usually matches within a day. Higher Level in the second Diploma year takes two or three days, because the specialist pool is genuinely narrow and a general science tutor in front of Higher Level work is worse than a short wait. We state the expected wait at the enquiry rather than afterwards. A radius search from here for the same specialism reliably returns general science tutors, because Higher Level physics cohorts in this catchment are small and the local market grew up around other curricula.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB physics examination dates?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one almost all UAE schools enter candidates for and goes no further. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we cite those where relevant. For your child's actual dates, the school's Diploma coordinator holds both the external session dates and the internal investigation deadline, and the internal one usually drives the term plan more than the external one does.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to gain physics marks before the papers?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order. Uncertainty and graph handling, because they appear on every data question, belong to no theme and are therefore the least revised content in the course. Command-term depth, because a student answering every question at one depth loses the high-tariff marks consistently. And transposition speed, because it decides whether the later parts of multi-part questions are reachable. All three are behaviours rather than content, which is why they move in weeks while a missing theme does not.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach physics as a method rather than as a body of facts. Each has taken Diploma students through to examination and marks against the published scheme, and each will start by asking the student to attempt a question rather than by explaining a topic.

intro.heading: Most physics marks are lost in the first thirty seconds of a question
paragraphs: The students we are asked to help in Diploma physics are rarely the ones who do not know the content. They are the ones who read an unfamiliar question, cannot see where to start, write something plausible, and lose marks that had nothing to do with their understanding. That is a method problem. It is diagnosable from a marked script in twenty minutes and it is trainable, and almost nobody teaches it because it does not look like teaching physics.

The method itself is less mysterious than it feels. Diploma physics questions come in a small number of recognisable shapes: a mechanics situation that wants a free-body diagram first, an energy problem that wants an accounting statement, a circuit that wants redrawing before any calculation, a graph that wants linearising, a data set that wants an uncertainty treatment. A student who can classify a question in the first thirty seconds has a first move. A student who cannot is improvising, which is expensive under time pressure.

The second thing we work on is what students write rather than what they know. Method marks exist on multi-step questions even when the final value is wrong, and a student who writes only answers forfeits marks they had already earned. Formula, substitution and result on separate lines, units carried through, significant figures set by the least precise input: these are habits rather than insights, and because they are mechanical they survive examination pressure far better than understanding alone does.

Hor Al Anz is a dense apartment district in Deira, next to Abu Hail and Al Muteena, inland from Al Mamzar, with the Green Line of the Metro running through it. Diploma provision used by families here mostly sits across the Creek or towards Al Mamzar and Festival City, so a physics student from this district usually commutes, often for an hour a day in total. A plan that assumes an empty weekday evening does not survive that, which is why session length and weekend slots are part of the plan rather than scheduling detail.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. For physics the screen genuinely helps: a graph can be annotated and rebuilt three times in two minutes, a diagram drawn while the student predicts the next force, and the session recorded so a derivation can be re-watched at the moment it is needed rather than when it was taught.
What follows is the method in detail. If you read one section, read the one on question archetypes, because the first move is where the marks are won and lost.

sections.heading: Question archetypes, and the first move for each
paragraphs: Physics questions look endlessly varied and are not. Across a Diploma paper, most questions belong to one of a handful of recognisable types, each with a reliable first move. Teaching a student to classify before calculating is the single most transferable thing a physics tutor can do, because it converts an unfamiliar question from a blank page into a known procedure with a known starting point.

The classification is not subtle once it is named. A situation with several forces acting wants a free-body diagram before anything else. A problem that mentions a height, a spring, a speed and a final state wants an energy accounting statement rather than a sequence of equations. A circuit wants redrawing into a clean series-parallel form before any numbers are touched. A graph with a curve wants linearising. A data table wants an uncertainty treatment and a gradient. A question quoting a very large or very small number wants standard form handled before the physics starts.

What students do instead is pattern-match on the topic name and reach for the formula they associate with it. That works on familiar questions and fails on exactly the unfamiliar ones that distinguish grades. It also wastes time, because an unproductive first move usually has to be abandoned and restarted, and in a timed paper the minutes spent on a false start are the minutes the last question needed.

The table sets out the archetypes with the first move and the usual mistake. We use it as a working document in method clinics: the student reads a question, names the archetype out loud, states the first move, and only then begins. Within a few sessions the naming becomes silent and automatic, which is the point.

sections.heading: Free-body diagrams and energy accounting: the two habits that carry mechanics
paragraphs: Almost every mechanics mark a Diploma student loses can be traced to one of two omissions. The first is a free-body diagram that was never drawn, or was drawn without labels. A diagram with the forces named, their directions marked and the object isolated turns a confusing situation into a short list of components to resolve. Without it, students resolve from memory and drop a force, usually the one that acts in an unexpected direction.

The habit has to be unconditional to be useful. A student who draws the diagram only when a question looks difficult will not draw it when a question looks easy and turns out not to be, which is where the marks actually go. We insist on it for every mechanics question for a few weeks until it stops being a decision, and the improvement shows up in questions the student would previously have attempted carelessly.

The second habit is energy accounting. When a problem involves a height, a spring, a speed, friction or a temperature change, the productive first line is a statement of what energy was where at the start and where it ended up, including whatever was dissipated. That single line resolves most of these questions and makes the algebra almost incidental. Students instead chain equations and lose track of which quantities are initial and which final, which is why sign errors proliferate in exactly these problems.

Both habits also protect method marks, because both produce written evidence of reasoning before any arithmetic happens. A student whose script shows a labelled diagram and an energy statement has already earned marks even if the final value is wrong, and a student whose script shows only a number has not. That is worth saying to a teenager plainly: the diagram is not preparation for the answer, it is part of the answer.

sections.heading: Graph linearisation: turning a curve into a straight line
paragraphs: Linearisation is one of the most reliable sources of marks in Diploma physics and one of the least practised. The principle is simple: a gradient can be read accurately from a straight line and cannot be read accurately from a curve, so when a relationship is not linear the examiner expects the student to choose what to plot against what in order to straighten it. The question usually signals this by asking what should be plotted to produce a straight line, and students who have not practised it answer vaguely.

The procedure is mechanical. Write the relationship. Decide which combination of the variables will produce a linear form. Identify what the gradient and the intercept will represent. Then plot, draw the line, read the gradient from the line rather than from two data points, and quote it with units. Each of those steps carries marks somewhere, and the last one is the one students forget most often: a gradient without units is incomplete.

The cases that recur are limited enough to learn. A relationship with a power wants logarithms on both axes, with the gradient giving the power. A period depending on the square root of a length wants the square of the period against the length. A velocity-squared relationship wants velocity squared against displacement. A lens or resistance reciprocal relationship wants reciprocals plotted. An exponential decay wants a natural logarithm against time. That is most of what appears.

The table lists these with what gets plotted and what the gradient means. In sessions we practise it the other way round as well: given a straight-line graph and its axes, state what relationship it implies. That reverse exercise is what builds genuine confidence, because the examination sometimes asks the question in that direction and students who have only drilled one direction freeze.

sections.heading: Circuits and fields: the reasoning students skip
paragraphs: Circuit questions are where carelessness is punished most reliably, because the arithmetic is easy and the structure is not. The productive first step is always to redraw the circuit into clean series and parallel groups, labelling what is in common with what. Students who calculate directly from the diagram as drawn apply a series rule inside a parallel branch, which gives a plausible wrong answer that is hard to spot afterwards.

The second circuit habit is tracking what is shared. Components in series share a current; components in parallel share a potential difference. Almost every circuit question is answered by applying that sentence repeatedly to progressively simpler groups. Students who learn circuit rules as a list of formulae rather than as that single principle struggle whenever the arrangement is unfamiliar, which is the arrangement the examination chooses.

Fields is the theme students most often name as the hardest and the reason is partly structural. The material is abstract, it rewards reasoning about an inverse relationship rather than calculating with a formula, and at higher level the extension is substantial and usually taught at the end of the theme when the class is moving on. The result is the most frequently under-rehearsed HL content in the subject, which is an organisational failure rather than an intellectual one.

The way to work on fields is to make the reasoning explicit and repeated. What is the source, what does the field do to a test object, how does the strength vary with distance, what happens to the potential, and what does the graph of each look like. A student who can produce that sequence for gravitational and electric cases has most of the theme, and the derivations become memorable because they sit on a structure rather than floating free.
