sections.heading: The data booklet, and what is not worth memorising
paragraphs: Candidates are given a data booklet in the physics examination. It contains constants, formulae and reference data in a fixed structure, and a surprising number of students have never practised using it under time pressure. The practical consequence is twofold: they waste revision time memorising what is supplied, and they lose minutes in the examination hunting for what they did not know was there.

The useful discipline is to keep the booklet open in every session from the start of the course, so that navigation becomes automatic. A student who knows which page carries which group of relationships moves faster than one who is searching, and the saved minutes land on the last question of the paper, which is often where the recoverable marks are. This is a small intervention with a direct mark return and it costs nothing.

What does need memorising is different and smaller: which quantities the symbols refer to, the standard unit for each, and the relationships that are not in the booklet because they are expected to be derived or constructed. A student who can read a booklet formula and immediately say what each symbol means and what units it carries is in a strong position. One who recognises the formula and cannot populate it is not, and the distinction is invisible until a question requires it.

The related habit is significant figures. A result is entitled to the precision its least precise input allows, and a student copying ten digits from a display is announcing that they do not know this rule. It takes about two weeks to establish and then holds for the rest of the course, which makes it one of the few genuinely free improvements available. We check it on every numerical answer rather than mentioning it once.

sections.heading: How a marked script is read, and how long each fix takes
paragraphs: Our first request is always a marked paper, because it answers a question no conversation can. Physics marks drain away in a limited number of distinct ways, and each has a different repair time. A plan that does not distinguish between them will spend six weeks on something that needed two and two weeks on something that needed six, which is how tutoring money gets wasted without anybody behaving badly.

The categories are specific. Entry-point failure looks like a blank space or an abandoned start on an unfamiliar question. Command-term failure looks like a correct paragraph where a single statement was wanted, or a statement where a reasoning chain was required. Working-not-shown looks like a bare wrong answer on a multi-step question with no method marks awarded. Uncertainty failure looks like a gradient without units, or an uncertainty ignored until the final line. Content failure looks like consistent loss across every question on one theme. Timing failure looks like a strong first half and an empty last page.

Each of those has a different fix and a different timescale, and being honest about the timescale is part of the job. Command terms and working discipline change inside a fortnight. Entry-point method takes four to six sessions of deliberately unfamiliar questions. Uncertainty arithmetic takes four to six sessions. A genuine content gap in a theme takes as long as the theme takes. Timing improves with whole papers under time and nothing else.

The table sets this out as a diagnostic tool. A parent can use it with a marked script in front of them and reach a reasonable view before speaking to anybody, which we think is a better basis for a conversation than a general sense that physics is going badly.

sections.heading: The investigation, and the line that does not move
paragraphs: The scientific investigation carries twenty per cent of the grade under the current guide and is the largest block of marks a physics student controls directly. It is assessed against published criteria and marked internally, with the school setting the deadlines that actually govern a student's term. Those deadlines are the first thing to obtain in writing, because they almost always arrive earlier than families expect and frequently sit close to a mock series.

The most common fatal flaw is a research question that cannot be measured reliably with school apparatus in the time available. An effect too small to detect produces data that supports nothing, and no amount of good writing recovers it. The second is a data set too thin for the analysis then attempted. The third is an evaluation that lists apologies rather than identifying which limitation actually mattered and what would be done about it. All three are planning failures, visible in the first fortnight, and cheap to prevent.

What a tutor may do is narrow and genuinely useful. Teach how a question is made measurable, how variables are identified and controlled, how uncertainty is estimated and propagated, how an analysis is structured, and how an evaluation argues rather than apologises. Read a draft the student wrote and reply with the questions an examiner would ask next. That is teaching and it is what we offer.

What a tutor must never do is write, draft, complete or rewrite any part of the investigation, supply data, or hand over another student's work as a model to adapt. One provider examined for this project advertises completed internal assessments at a published price; buying that is an academic-malpractice trigger under the International Baccalaureate's own rules and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. The school supervisor is the authority on what support is permitted in your child's case.

sections.heading: A commuting student's week, and the honest limits of what we claim
paragraphs: A Diploma physics student travelling from Hor Al Anz across the Creek or to Al Mamzar loses a real part of the day to the journey. Most are home between 16:00 and 17:00, and after food the usable window starts around 17:30. For a student carrying three higher level subjects, the core and an investigation, that window is contested before any tutoring is added. Sixty focused minutes on a travel day beats ninety that drift, and weekend mornings are the best slot for whole papers because nothing competes and the student is not already tired.

Practically, the student needs a hard surface, squared paper and a ruler for graph work, their own calculator rather than a phone, the data booklet open, and headphones so a busy household is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page, because watching the working appear is the entire diagnostic method in this subject. Where siblings share a room, staggered evenings work and a shared session does not. Ramadan sessions move to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, agreed before the month begins.

On what we are: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform holding no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE, we run no home visits anywhere in the Emirates, we do not enter candidates for examinations and we do not perform Ministry equivalency. Private tutoring here is regulated by the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years; tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, treat any quoted amount as unverified.

We also publish no IB examination or results dates, because the International Baccalaureate's own site is the authoritative source and should be checked directly or through your school's IB coordinator. We will say that UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. We reference and link official documents rather than reproducing them, and we publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind any of them.

faqs.question: Our child knows the physics but freezes on unfamiliar questions. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most common thing we are asked to fix. It is an entry-point problem rather than a knowledge one: the student reads an unfamiliar question, cannot classify it, and either stalls or writes something plausible. Diploma physics questions come in a small number of recognisable shapes, each with a reliable first move, and learning to classify in the first thirty seconds converts a blank page into a known procedure. It takes four to six sessions of deliberately unfamiliar questions, with the student attempting the first move before anything is explained.

faqs.question: Can a physics tutor visit our home in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Physics sessions here are one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the screen is a genuine advantage: a graph can be annotated and rebuilt three times in two minutes, a diagram drawn while the student predicts the next force, and the session recorded so a derivation can be re-watched at the moment it is needed. For a commuting student it also removes a second journey from an evening that already started late.

faqs.question: Why does our child lose marks when the final answer is correct?
faqs.answer: Usually units, significant figures or working that was never written down. A result is entitled to the precision its least precise input allows, so copying ten digits from a display loses marks. A gradient without units is incomplete. And method marks exist on multi-step questions even when the final value is wrong, so a student who writes only answers forfeits marks they had earned and also leaves the examiner nothing to credit when the arithmetic slips. Laying out formula, substitution and result as separate lines fixes most of this within a fortnight.

faqs.question: What is linearisation and why does it come up so often?
faqs.answer: It is choosing what to plot against what so that a non-linear relationship produces a straight line, because a gradient can be read accurately from a line and not from a curve. A power relationship wants logarithms on both axes with the gradient giving the power. A period depending on the square root of a length wants the period squared against the length. An exponential decay wants a natural logarithm against time. Examiners ask it frequently because it tests understanding of the relationship rather than recall, and students who have not practised it answer vaguely.

faqs.question: Why is fields the theme students find hardest?
faqs.answer: Partly because it is genuinely abstract and partly for a scheduling reason. The material rewards reasoning about how a quantity varies with distance rather than substituting into a formula, and at higher level the extension is substantial and is usually taught at the end of the theme as the class moves on. That makes it the most under-rehearsed higher level content in the subject. The remedy is organisational as much as intellectual: list the HL field material separately in the revision plan, and make the reasoning sequence explicit and repeated rather than memorising derivations.

faqs.question: Should our child memorise the physics data booklet?
faqs.answer: No. It is supplied in the examination, so memorising its contents wastes revision time twice over. What does need learning is different: what each symbol refers to, the standard unit for each quantity, and which relationships are expected to be derived rather than looked up. The practical habit is to keep the booklet open in every session from the start of the course so navigation becomes automatic, because minutes saved hunting for a formula land on the last question of the paper, which is often where recoverable marks sit.

faqs.question: How do you decide what to work on first?
faqs.answer: From a marked script, by category. A blank or abandoned start on an unfamiliar question is entry-point failure, which takes four to six sessions. A paragraph where a single statement was wanted is command-term failure, which shifts in two or three. A bare wrong answer with no method credited is a working habit, which takes a fortnight of insistence. A gradient without units is experimental-skills failure. Consistent loss across one theme is a real content gap with no shortcut. An empty last page is timing. Each has a different fix and a different timescale.

faqs.question: Our child came from IGCSE physics and the first Diploma term went badly. Why?
faqs.answer: Three new demands usually arrive together. Uncertainty arithmetic, which IGCSE barely touches and the Diploma expects to be carried through a calculation. Command terms applied literally, where IGCSE was more forgiving about answer length. And the expectation that a conclusion is argued from data rather than stated. None is conceptually difficult and all three are unfamiliar, which is why a strong Extended-tier grade is a poor predictor of a comfortable start. Six to eight focused sessions on those three items closes most of the gap.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: With the design and the reasoning, yes. A tutor can teach your child how to narrow a research question until it is measurable with school apparatus, how to identify and control variables, how to estimate and propagate uncertainty, how to structure the analysis, and how an evaluation identifies which limitation actually mattered. A tutor can read a draft your child wrote and reply with the questions an examiner would ask next. A tutor must not write, draft, rewrite or supply any part of it, or provide data. The school supervisor sets the rules for permitted support.

faqs.question: How much harder is higher level physics for a student in this district?
faqs.answer: The course covers the same five themes with additional material inside each, so the difference is depth and rehearsal rather than a different syllabus. The local complication is that higher level physics sets in Dubai schools are often small, so a student stuck on a specific derivation may have nobody in the class working on the same problem, and for a commuting student that is harder to resolve informally. That isolation, rather than the difficulty of the material, is the most common reason families in Hor Al Anz look for support outside the school.

faqs.question: Is our child's physics problem actually a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is worth establishing early. Rearranging a formula when the unknown sits in the denominator, handling standard form on very large or very small values, logarithmic manipulation for linearisation, and reading a gradient accurately are mathematical skills examined inside a physics paper. When a marked script shows the physics reasoning intact and the algebra collapsing, the honest recommendation is a short block of maths work rather than more physics teaching. We say so when we see it, because selling physics sessions to fix an algebra gap wastes a term.

faqs.question: When should a commuting Diploma student book physics sessions?
faqs.answer: Weekdays from 17:30, in sixty-minute blocks, and weekend mornings for anything long. Students travelling from this district to Diploma schools across the Creek or towards Festival City are usually home between 16:00 and 17:00, and after food the usable window starts later than parents expect. Sixty focused minutes on a travel day is more productive than ninety drifting ones. Weekend mornings are the best slot for whole papers under time and long investigation work, and they are consistently the least requested slot we offer.

faqs.question: Do you teach A Level physics as well as the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it matters in this district because many families have one child on each route. The content overlaps substantially: the same algebraic fluency, the same graph and uncertainty discipline, the same problem-solving method of classifying a question and drawing the diagram before calculating. What differs is the assessment structure, the practical arrangements and the mark-scheme conventions. Tell us the board and specification code when you enquire, because past papers do not transfer between boards and revising on the wrong set wastes real time.

faqs.question: What does IB physics tutoring cost for a family in Deira?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the journey sits inside the fee. Monthly estimates from the Bestimate Dubai table run about AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-band weekly support and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an examination year. Those are market figures with sources rather than our price list; we quote after the free trial lesson.

intro.heading: When the laboratory is a bus ride away
paragraphs: Every Diploma science carries a scientific investigation worth roughly a fifth of the subject grade, assessed against four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. For most students the hard part is the analysis. For a student travelling out of International City to Silicon Oasis, Al Warqa or Mirdif, the hard part is getting back into the laboratory.

This is not a small operational detail. A student who lives near their school can return at four for twenty more minutes of readings, or repeat a run that went wrong, or check an instrument they were unsure about. A student in the Persia Cluster whose school is in Silicon Oasis cannot, because the bus has gone and the journey is not one a working household makes twice in an evening. So the investigation has to be designed to be finishable in the laboratory time the school timetables, and that design decision happens weeks before any data exists.

The consequence is that feasibility becomes the first coaching conversation rather than a later one. What apparatus does the school actually have? How many timetabled sessions are available before the deadline? What is the smallest division on the instruments, and what uncertainty does that imply for the final result? Can the temperature be held constant, and with what? Half an hour on those questions is worth more than any amount of help with the write-up.

The reassuring half of the picture is that most of the marks sit in work that can be done at home. Framing a research question, identifying and controlling variables, choosing a range and interval, propagating uncertainty, linearising a relationship, extracting a quantity from a gradient, calculating gradient uncertainty, and writing an evaluation that names the dominant error source. Not one of those requires a bench, and together they account for far more of the twenty-four available marks than the measuring itself ever does.

The same is true of the written papers. Physics marks are mostly lost to three things that have nothing to do with apparatus: explanations written in everyday language rather than with defined quantities, uncertainty work nobody taught, and graph questions where the student plots accurately and cannot say what the gradient represents. All three are teachable on a shared screen with real data.

IB Gram delivers physics tuition online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service. For this subject in this district that is not a compromise: a travelling tutor cannot get your child into a laboratory either, and the pool of Higher Level physics specialists reachable from Al Warsan by car is effectively empty.

programmes.name: The scientific investigation
programmes.description: One independent investigation worth twenty-four marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is the only part of the grade a student fully controls, and in this district it is also the part most constrained by logistics rather than by ability.
programmes.countryNote: The binding constraint is laboratory access, which is why the feasibility conversation comes before anything else. A design needing an extra afternoon of readings is a design that will not be completed from these clusters, and discovering that after a week of data collection costs more than the entire coaching block.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-international-.subjectsIntro: What physics actually requires, separated into the parts that need a laboratory and the parts that do not.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products, quotients and powers, and uncertainty in a gradient. Examined directly in data-analysis questions, central to the investigation's evaluation, mechanical in its rules, and almost never taught as a lesson of its own.

subjects.name: Graph work and linearisation
subjects.description: Rearranging an equation into straight-line form, choosing what to plot against what, and extracting a physical quantity from the gradient or intercept. The question is rarely 'plot this' but 'what does the gradient represent', and that is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Experimental design and variable control
subjects.description: Independent, dependent and controlled variables, range and interval choice, repeat readings, and the systematic and random error distinction. Assessed in the research design criterion and in written method questions, and the weakest part of almost every first draft.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, energy and circular motion, with rigid-body and relativity content at Higher Level. Marks go on free-body diagrams with a force missing and on momentum questions where no direction convention is stated before the arithmetic.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws and the kinetic model. The recurring error is explaining temperature change in terms of heat as a substance that flows rather than as energy transferred, which mark schemes treat as a misconception rather than loose phrasing.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave properties, superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference. Path-difference questions reward drawing the geometry first; students who attempt them algebraically from memory forfeit most of the available marks.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, circuits and electromagnetic induction. The largest single source of confusion in the course, chiefly because potential and field strength get conflated and induction directions are asserted rather than derived.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, fission and fusion, the photoelectric effect and quantum phenomena. Mark loss is mostly numerical discipline: powers of ten, unit prefixes and electronvolt conversions applied inconsistently inside one calculation.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: State, outline, describe, explain, deduce, determine, sketch and compare each specify a different answer with a different mark allocation. Students answer nearly all of them as 'describe', which is the most comfortable mode and the lowest scoring on extended responses.

subjects.name: The mathematics physics assumes
subjects.description: Rearranging multi-variable equations, logarithms, small-angle approximations, resolving vectors with trigonometry and standard-form arithmetic at speed. Physics does not teach these and penalises their absence throughout, which is why some physics tutoring is properly mathematics tutoring.

subjects.name: Investigation coaching from home
subjects.description: Research-question framing, feasibility against the school's apparatus and timetable, variable control, uncertainty treatment, graph work and the evaluation the criteria reward. All of it on the student's own data. The student designs, measures and writes.

subjects.name: Apparatus handling
subjects.description: The one part that must happen at school. Reading instruments, following a method under time pressure and recording as you go. For a commuting student the implication is to use every timetabled laboratory session fully, because there is no second chance later in the day.

sections.heading: Designing an investigation you can actually finish
paragraphs: The question to answer before anything else is how many timetabled laboratory sessions exist between now and the school's deadline. Ask the teacher, get a number, and design within it. From these clusters there is no realistic extra afternoon, so an investigation needing one is an investigation that will be submitted incomplete - and incomplete data damages three of the four criteria at once, not just one.

Within that constraint, the designs that work are the ones with a short, repeatable measurement cycle and a tolerant apparatus requirement. A pendulum or spring oscillation study, a resistance-against-length investigation, a terminal velocity measurement, a lens or refraction study, or a cooling curve. Each produces usable data in a single session with repeats, and each has a relationship that linearises cleanly, which the data-analysis criterion rewards.

The designs that fail from this district are the ones needing precision the school's instruments cannot deliver, or temperature control the laboratory cannot sustain, or a number of runs that will not fit the available sessions. Those are not bad physics - they are good physics in the wrong circumstances, and a student who discovers that in week three has lost the time they most needed.

The table below sets out common designs with what each needs and where each tends to fail. Treat the apparatus column as a checklist to take to the teacher rather than an assumption, because laboratory provision varies considerably between schools a few kilometres apart in this part of Dubai.

sections.heading: The marks that do not need a laboratory
paragraphs: This is the reassuring arithmetic. Of the twenty-four investigation marks, the measuring itself earns none directly. Research design is six marks for the question, the variables, the method and the justification - all decided before the apparatus is touched. Data analysis is six for processing, uncertainty treatment and presentation. Conclusion is six for a justified answer in scientific context. Evaluation is six for specific limitations and realistic improvements.

So at least eighteen of the twenty-four marks are earned away from the bench, and the remaining six depend on a method designed away from it too. For a student who cannot return to the laboratory, that is the whole argument for spending coaching time on design, uncertainty and evaluation rather than on technique with a clamp stand.

The same holds in the written papers, where the recoverable marks cluster in three places. Uncertainty: five mechanical rules that cover nearly every question and which almost no scheme of work teaches as a lesson. Graph linearisation: rearranging the equation into straight-line form, reading the axes and the gradient's meaning off that rearrangement, and only then plotting. Command terms: explain means causes, describe means features, deduce means a conclusion from given information, determine means a numerical answer with working.

None of those three needs equipment, and together they are worth more across a set of physics papers than any single theme. A student who can propagate uncertainty, linearise a relationship and read a command term correctly will outscore a student who knows more physics and does none of those things, which is an uncomfortable fact and a useful one.

sections.heading: A physics week with an hour of travel in it
paragraphs: Physics divides into content that needs sustained attention and skills that respond to short practice, and a commuting student has very little of the first and some of the second. The arrangement that works puts the sustained work at the weekend and the skills practice on weekday evenings, rather than trying to do everything in one weekday hour.

Specifically: the weekday session carries theme content and the mark-scheme walkthrough of recent work, because that can be done in sixty minutes with a tired student if the material is already familiar. The weekend morning carries data-analysis question sets and full papers, because those need two to three hours and a clear head. Short weekday practice carries uncertainty calculations and command-term rewriting, which take fifteen minutes and improve through repetition.

The reason to separate them deliberately is that physics data questions punish fatigue more than most subjects. A student who misreads an axis at seven in the evening after a long bus journey has not learned anything about graphs; they have learned that graphs are confusing. The same student at ten on a Saturday morning gets it right and builds the habit the paper rewards.

The table below sets out the week. As with every plan on this site, it is deliberately modest, because an ambitious schedule abandoned in October is worth less than a sustainable one that runs to May. The test is whether it still happens on a bad week rather than a good one.

sections.heading: Why physics answers that are true still score badly
paragraphs: The most frustrating thing a parent sees in physics is an answer that is correct, well expressed and worth two marks out of five. The cause is almost always the command term. Explain requires the causes and the physical reasoning. Describe requires the features without the causes. Deduce requires a conclusion reached from information given. Determine requires a numerical answer with working shown.

Students answer nearly all of them as describe, because describing is the most comfortable mode and the one school work rewards most often. The fix is mechanical and quick: underline the command term before writing anything, and know what each one requires. A fortnight of deliberate practice on this alone moves marks across every paper, which is why technique work outperforms content revision in the final weeks.

The second half of the same problem is the mark allocation printed beside the question. A four-mark explanation wants four distinct creditable points, and a student who writes one point in beautiful detail has lost three marks to a number printed in bold on the page. Teaching students to plan an answer against its allocation takes one session and lasts the whole course.

The third is the habit of writing physics in everyday language. 'The current gets used up', 'heat flows into the object', 'the force pushes it round the corner' - each describes something real and none of them names the quantity the mark scheme wants. Replacing that vocabulary is slow but permanent, and it is the single clearest difference between a mid-band and a top-band extended response.

sections.heading: Higher Level, the commute, and the subject combination
paragraphs: Higher Level physics adds content across every theme and expects the mathematics to be handled fluently rather than carefully. For a student losing ten hours a week to travel, that matters in a practical way: the course assumes homework time that this student has less of, so the subject combination needs thinking about rather than assuming.

Higher Level physics with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a common engineering-track pairing and a genuinely heavy quantitative load. Adding a third demanding written subject produces a second-year January that effort alone will not solve, and from these clusters an hour a day of that effort is already spent on a bus. If choices are still open, map the deadlines across both years rather than looking only at interest.

The laboratory question also bears on subject choice, which nobody mentions at options evenings. Some subjects' internal assessments require apparatus access and some require only reading and writing. For a student who cannot easily return to school, a combination with three laboratory-based assessments landing in the same term is harder than the same combination would be for a student living next door to the school.

On university entry: Higher Level physics is the usual requirement for physics and engineering degrees and Standard Level is frequently insufficient for those routes. Read the published requirements for the specific institutions and courses during the first Diploma year, because dropping from Higher to Standard Level is generally possible and moving up usually is not.

sections.heading: Counting the physics year backwards
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session. For physics the internal calendar is the binding one, because the investigation deadline typically lands in the second half of the first Diploma year or early in the second, where it collides with mock examinations, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay inside a few weeks in January and February.

Counting backwards produces a clear order for a commuting student. Uncertainty and graph skills built in the first term of the first year, before they start costing marks in data questions. Investigation feasibility checked against the apparatus list and the timetabled session count well before data collection. Data collected and processed before mock preparation begins. Timed data-analysis questions started in the first term of the second year rather than after the mocks.

We publish no specific IB session or results dates on this site. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date at all, so confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dates are sourced: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November.

Ramadan falls inside the revision period in most years, and for physics the implication is specific. The school day shortens, which frees the afternoon, but data-analysis work in the late afternoon during the month is usually poor value. Weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work. Fix the pattern before the month begins, and remember that laboratory sessions may also be rearranged, which affects any investigation still in progress.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line on an investigation
paragraphs: This needs stating plainly because the search results this page sits in include an operator selling completed internal assessments at a published price. Under IB academic-honesty rules, submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate: a subject grade withheld, or the Diploma itself. The seller is not exposed. The seventeen-year-old is.

So the boundary in operational terms. A tutor may test whether a research question is feasible with the school's apparatus and timetable. May explain what each of the four criteria rewards and what a strong response looks like in general terms. May teach uncertainty propagation, linearisation and gradient uncertainty on the student's own measurements. May read a draft and give written feedback the student then acts on.

A tutor may not choose the research question, design the method, take or supply data, process the data, produce the graphs, or provide text that ends up in the report. The working test is whether the student could explain, unprompted and without notes, why every number and every sentence is there. Applied honestly this makes coaching slower, because a draft comes back with questions rather than corrections.

We also supply no IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We cite and link the official sources, which is both the correct position on copyright and the only way to be certain the version is current. Schools hold past papers and the subject teacher is usually the quickest route to the right ones.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Every figure here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram rate. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, with published online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. For Higher Level physics the band below AED 100 an hour rarely contains anybody who teaches the level, which is the most useful thing to know about it.

On availability, we publish the limit rather than hiding it. Higher Level physics in the fortnight either side of mock examinations is the hardest thing on our list, because demand across the emirate concentrates on the same people in the same weeks. In that case you get a realistic wait, or adjacent mathematics support with the boundary stated plainly, or a refusal - not a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate.

And what we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson; no promises about grades and no published predicted scores. On regulation: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no fine schedule published.

process.title: Find out how many laboratory sessions are left
process.description: Ask the physics teacher for the number of timetabled sessions between now and the investigation deadline, and for the apparatus list. From these clusters there is no extra afternoon, so the design has to fit the number you are given.

process.title: Send one marked physics paper
process.description: Marks lost on extended responses point to command terms. Marks lost on data questions point to uncertainty and graph work. Marks lost across one theme point to content. Those are three different plans, and the paper settles it in twenty minutes.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written note
process.description: A real lesson on real physics with the student working. Afterwards a plain summary: whether the problem is content, numbers or writing, what the available weeks will target, and whether the investigation design is feasible as it stands.

process.title: Split the week deliberately
process.description: Theme content and walkthrough in the weekday session, fifteen minutes of uncertainty and command-term practice on two other evenings, and data-analysis or full papers on a weekend morning. Data work punishes fatigue more than any other part of physics.

process.title: Use every laboratory session fully
process.description: The one thing a tutor cannot do for a student in this district is get them into a laboratory. Every timetabled session should be treated as the only chance it is - instruments checked, repeats taken, readings recorded as they happen rather than reconstructed later.

whyPoints.title: Feasibility before physics on the investigation
whyPoints.description: From these clusters there is no extra afternoon in the laboratory, so a design needing one will be submitted incomplete - which damages three criteria at once. Half an hour on apparatus, instrument resolution and session count prevents the commonest failure here.

whyPoints.title: Eighteen of twenty-four marks are earned away from the bench
whyPoints.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation are all decided or produced outside the laboratory. For a student who cannot return to school, that is where coaching time belongs rather than on apparatus technique.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty taught as five mechanical rules
whyPoints.description: Absolute from resolution, add absolutes when adding, add percentages when multiplying, multiply by the power, gradient from maximum and minimum lines. They cover nearly every uncertainty question in the course and almost no scheme of work teaches them as a lesson.

whyPoints.title: Data work moved to the weekend on purpose
whyPoints.description: Graph and data-analysis questions punish fatigue more than any other part of physics. A student who misreads an axis at seven in the evening after a bus journey learns that graphs are confusing rather than how to read one.

whyPoints.title: Command terms as a fortnight of work
whyPoints.description: Explain means causes, describe means features, deduce means a conclusion from given information. Students answer everything as describe, and fixing that moves marks across every paper faster than any content revision.

whyPoints.title: We say when Higher Level is unavailable
whyPoints.description: Higher Level physics around the mock window is the hardest combination we staff, because demand across the emirate lands in the same fortnight. You hear that at the enquiry stage with a realistic wait rather than meeting a Standard Level tutor.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB physics tutor in International City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your flat, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. For physics the decisive point is that a travelling tutor could not get your child into a laboratory either - apparatus work happens at school under any arrangement. What a tutor can do is everything around it, which is where at least eighteen of the twenty-four investigation marks and most written-paper marks actually sit.

faqs.question: How does my child do a physics investigation when school is a bus ride away?
faqs.answer: By designing it to be completable in the timetabled laboratory sessions available, which means asking the teacher for that number and for the apparatus list before choosing a research question. From these clusters there is no realistic extra afternoon, and a design needing one gets submitted with incomplete data - which damages research design, data analysis and conclusion simultaneously rather than just one criterion.

faqs.question: Which investigation designs work best for a commuting student?
faqs.answer: The ones with a short repeatable measurement cycle and tolerant apparatus needs: pendulum period against length, resistance against wire length, spring extension and oscillation, terminal velocity in a fluid, or a refraction and lens study. Each produces usable data in one session with repeats and each has a relationship that linearises cleanly, which the data-analysis criterion rewards. Designs needing a sustained water bath at fixed temperature are usually not completable without a return visit.

faqs.question: How are the 24 investigation marks distributed?
faqs.answer: Four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The measuring itself earns none directly. Research design is decided before the apparatus is touched; data analysis rewards processing, uncertainty treatment and presentation; conclusion rewards an answer justified by the data and placed in context; evaluation rewards naming the dominant uncertainty source and proposing one specific improvement rather than saying more repeats would help.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on physics answers that are correct?
faqs.answer: Nearly always the command term. Explain requires causes and physical reasoning; describe requires features without causes; deduce requires a conclusion from information given; determine requires a numerical answer with working. Students answer almost everything as describe, because that is the most comfortable mode and the one school work rewards. The second cause is ignoring the mark allocation: a four-mark question wants four distinct creditable points, not one explained beautifully.

faqs.question: Does uncertainty really need to be taught separately?
faqs.answer: Almost always, and it is the highest-return hour in physics tutoring. Five rules cover nearly everything: absolute uncertainty from instrument resolution or repeat spread, add absolute uncertainties when adding or subtracting, add percentage uncertainties when multiplying or dividing, multiply percentage uncertainty by the power when raising to a power, and find gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines through the error bars. They are mechanical, examined directly, and rarely taught as a lesson.

faqs.question: What does a physics graph question actually want?
faqs.answer: Not plotting. It wants the student to rearrange the governing equation into straight-line form, decide from that rearrangement what goes on each axis, state what the gradient and intercept physically represent, and only then plot. A student who plots accurately and cannot interpret the gradient has done the easier half. Taught as a procedure rather than a skill, it takes about a fortnight of practice to become automatic.

faqs.question: Why should data-analysis work happen at the weekend?
faqs.answer: Because graph and data questions punish fatigue more than any other part of physics. A student who misreads an axis at seven in the evening after an hour on a bus has not learned anything about graphs - they have learned that graphs are confusing. The same student at ten on a Saturday morning reads it correctly and builds the habit the paper rewards. The weekend slot also competes with no school homework.

faqs.question: Which physics theme causes the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Fields, consistently. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, potential, circuits and electromagnetic induction together produce more confusion than the rest of the course combined, partly because potential and field strength are routinely conflated and partly because induction questions require a direction argument to be derived rather than asserted. It also tends to arrive while the investigation is live, which is why support booked in the first term is worth more than the same hours in February.

faqs.question: Should the commute affect whether he takes physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It should be part of the conversation, which it rarely is. Higher Level physics assumes homework time, and a student losing ten hours a week to travel has less of it. Higher Level physics with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a heavy quantitative pairing, and a third demanding written subject on top produces a very difficult second-year January. Check university requirements too, because dropping to Standard Level later is usually possible and moving up usually is not.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my daughter's investigation?
faqs.answer: Test whether the research question is feasible with the school's apparatus and timetable, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, teach uncertainty propagation and graph work on her own measurements, question the design, and read and comment on her drafts. A tutor may not choose the question, design the method, take or supply data, process it, produce graphs, or provide text. A malpractice finding falls on her, not on the tutor, and one operator in these results sells completed assessments.

faqs.question: When should physics support start for a student here?
faqs.answer: The first term of the first Diploma year, for uncertainty and graph skills, before they start costing marks in data questions. Then feasibility checking before investigation data collection, and timed data-analysis work from the first term of the second year rather than after the mocks. In most schools in this cluster the investigation deadline, the Extended Essay and the mocks all land within a few weeks in January and February.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan affect physics work and laboratory sessions?
faqs.answer: Both. The school day shortens so the bus returns earlier, which makes an afternoon session possible - but data-analysis work in the late afternoon during the month is usually poor value, so weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work better. Laboratory sessions may also be rearranged, which matters if an investigation is still in progress. Ask the physics teacher early what happens to practical sessions during the month, and fix the tutoring pattern before it starts.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level physics tutoring cost from this district?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 and attributed to the providers publishing them: qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650; in-home one-to-one with travel at AED 180 to 500. The band below AED 100 rarely contains anybody who teaches Higher Level physics.

faqs.question: Is a Higher Level physics specialist usually available at short notice?
faqs.answer: You hear it at the enquiry stage rather than in session three. Higher Level physics in the fortnight either side of mock examinations is the hardest combination on our list, because demand across the emirate concentrates on the same specialists in the same weeks. dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jbr.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Physics at Standard and Higher Level for students living in JBR, Dubai Marina and the towers along The Walk. Each one teaches the current guide, works from your child's own school timeline, and reads a recent marked paper before deciding what the first month should fix.

intro.heading: A subject that punishes vagueness, taught to a child who gets home at half past four
paragraphs: JBR has no secondary school inside it. The towers along The Walk send their children inland and along the coast, to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Jumeirah Park, The Greens and Emirates Hills, and the school bus brings them back somewhere between half past three and half past five depending on the day and on whether an activity ran. That single fact shapes every Physics tutoring decision a JBR family makes, because the window in which a tired sixteen-year-old can think clearly about rotational equilibrium is narrow and it moves from one weekday to the next.

Physics is also the group 4 subject least forgiving of a thin fortnight. Two missed weeks in Theme A can be rebuilt from a textbook over a weekend. Two missed weeks in Theme D, where electric, magnetic and gravitational fields are deliberately taught as one idea rather than three separate chapters, leaves a student guessing at every later question that mentions potential. Students almost never notice that gap at the time. It surfaces in a mock, in the shape of full, confident working that arrives at a number no mark scheme recognises.

The current guide also changed what tutoring has to cover. First examinations in 2025 brought five themes, one syllabus shared between Standard and Higher Level with additional higher level content held inside each theme, and the end of the old option papers. Paper 3 is gone. What remains is Paper 1, split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, Paper 2 of extended response, and a single scientific investigation marked out of 24. Any tutor still planning a year around options and Paper 3 is teaching a course your child is not sitting.

Delivery here is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a JBR address, and it does not offer home visits in Dubai; household visits are a service offered only in India. For a Physics family that is the better arrangement rather than a compromise. The real constraint on a JBR tutor is not distance, it is specialism, and a household that insists on someone able to drive to Dubai Marina by five o'clock is choosing from whoever happens to live nearby instead of from whoever actually teaches Theme D well.

What follows is the physics rather than the sales pitch: the five themes and what each one demands, the whole written assessment with its real weightings, the four investigation criteria and the marks attached to each, the topics where marks reliably disappear, an honest timetable for the JBR afternoon, and the published market rates for Dubai with the source of every figure named. There is also the question JBR parents ask most often once the rates are clear, which is how much of the Physics investigation a tutor may legitimately touch, and that is answered against the published IB expectations rather than left vague.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes matter to a JBR household asking about Physics: the Diploma course itself, the Middle Years sciences that decide whether a student arrives ready for it, and the Career-related Programme that a smaller number of schools in this corridor run alongside the Diploma.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Physics in the Diploma runs over two years at Standard or Higher Level. Both levels share five themes, with additional higher level material inside each one rather than bolted on at the end. Assessment is Paper 1, split into multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 of extended response, and one scientific investigation written up in no more than 3,000 words. The investigation is internally marked and externally moderated, and it is worth a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: JBR students sit this course at schools in Al Sufouh, Al Barsha, Emirates Hills and The Meadows, almost all of them inspected annually by KHDA on its six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. Dubai schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which means mocks fall across January and February and the investigation deadline is set internally, usually in the autumn term of DP2.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP sciences are assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student who scores well on criterion A and badly on criterion B is not weak at science, they are weak at designing a method, and that is the single best predictor of how the Diploma investigation will go two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools JBR families use run the Middle Years Programme before the Diploma, so a child can meet criterion B language in MYP 4 and then meet it again as Criterion A of the Diploma investigation. Families who move in from a British-curriculum school at Year 10 often arrive without ever having designed an experiment, and that gap is worth closing before DP1 starts rather than during it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs a career-related study with two or more Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. Where Physics is one of the Diploma courses taken inside the Career-related Programme, the subject content and the assessment are identical to the full Diploma version. The difference is workload around it, which changes how often a weekly session is genuinely useful.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is run by a minority of Dubai schools, so a JBR family on this route is often the only one in the building navigating it. Universities in the UAE and abroad assess it case by case, and the Ministry of Education equivalency route for it should be confirmed on moe.gov.ae rather than taken from a tutoring page, including this one.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Physics rarely arrives on its own. The subjects below are the ones JBR households most often add to a Physics request, either because the maths underneath is the real problem or because a second science shares the same investigation skills.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level covers all five themes with the additional higher level content inside each: rotational dynamics and relativity in Theme A, thermodynamic cycles in Theme B, standing waves and interference in detail in Theme C, induction and capacitance in Theme D, and quantum and nuclear structure in Theme E. Paper 2 runs two and a half hours, which is a stamina problem as much as a physics one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Standard Level sits inside the same five themes without the higher level extensions. Students lose marks in the same places as their Higher Level classmates, chiefly in Paper 1B data analysis and in the evaluation criterion of the investigation, and the shorter papers reward precision over speed. A Standard Level student with secure algebra can reach the top bands on fewer hours than Higher Level demands.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Physics assumes this course without saying so. Calculus for rates of change, logarithms for the exponential decay in Theme E, trigonometry for resolved components, and small-angle approximations all appear in physics questions before they are secure in maths lessons. Where a student is losing physics marks on algebraic rearrangement, the cheaper fix is often three maths sessions rather than ten physics ones.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Applications and Interpretation is a legitimate pairing with Physics, and it is also the pairing that most often needs support. The course spends less time on algebraic manipulation and more on modelling, so a student takes Physics Paper 2 with fewer rearrangement reps than their Analysis and Approaches classmates. That gap is closeable with targeted practice rather than a change of course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Chemistry shares the group 4 assessment model exactly: Paper 1A, Paper 1B, Paper 2 and one scientific investigation marked against the same four criteria. A student taking both can be taught investigation skills once and apply them twice, which is the most efficient hour a double-science household buys.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology rarely overlaps Physics content, but it shares the data-analysis demand. Gradient interpretation, uncertainty, controlled variables and the language of the evaluation criterion are identical across the group, so a Physics tutor's work on Paper 1B transfers directly to a Biology candidate in the same household.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Computer Science attracts the same JBR students as Physics and its internal assessment is a different animal: a developed solution with documentation rather than an experiment. Where a student takes both, the two internal deadlines often land within a fortnight of each other, which is a planning problem worth mapping in September rather than December.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Design Technology pulls on mechanics, materials and energy, and its design project runs alongside the Physics investigation. Students who enjoy both frequently underestimate the written demand in Design Technology, where command terms behave exactly as they do in Physics Paper 2 and are marked just as strictly.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Middle Years sciences are where investigation habits are formed or missed. Criterion B asks a student to design a method with controlled variables; criterion C asks them to process data and evaluate it. A student who has never been pushed on those two criteria arrives in DP1 with a content base and no method, which is the pattern behind most late investigation panics.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jbr.regionsIntro: JBR sits at one end of a corridor whose schools, bus routes and traffic patterns decide when a session can start. The areas below are the ones that matter to a Physics timetable for a child living in the towers.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: The immediate neighbour, sharing the same bus pick-ups and the same late-afternoon congestion on the Marina loop. Families here ask for identical session timing, and a tutor who can hold a 17:00 slot four weeks running is worth more than one who is nominally nearby.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: Connected to JBR by footbridge, with no school of its own, so children cross into the same bus network. The single access road means a late pick-up can cost twenty minutes that would otherwise have been physics.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: The nearest secondary cluster and the reason JBR afternoons look the way they do. Schools here finish mid-afternoon, and a bus that leaves on time puts a student back in the tower before four o'clock, which makes a 16:45 physics start realistic on a day without activities.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: A larger and more mixed cluster, further inland, with longer bus runs and the Hessa Street and Al Khail traffic to cross. Students from here are commonly home closer to half past four, so the sensible physics slot is 17:30 rather than 17:00.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: A short hop inland, popular with JBR families who move for space. The schools used are largely the same, and so are the session timings, which makes this the group most likely to share a tutor with neighbours in the towers.

regions.name: Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Village
regions.note: A longer run on First Al Khail Road, with buses that often arrive back after five once an activity is added. Physics sessions here work better on the two quietest weekdays than spread evenly across five.

regions.name: Emirates Hills and The Meadows
regions.note: Home to several Diploma schools that JBR students bus to, and the furthest realistic run on a daily basis. The commute explains why so many Marina and JBR families eventually choose an online tutor over one who has to make the same drive.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Immediately inland across Sheikh Zayed Road, with a similar tower-household profile and the same shortage of secondary schools inside the community. Physics requests from JLT and JBR tend to arrive in the same weeks of the DP2 autumn term.

schoolClusters.city: Schools on the Al Sufouh and Al Barsha run
schoolClusters.note: The closest secondary schools to the towers, and the reason a mid-afternoon finish is the default assumption in JBR. Most run the British curriculum to IGCSE before splitting towards A Level or the Diploma, so a Year 11 physicist in this cluster may not know yet which course they will be sitting in September.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma schools JBR students bus to
schoolClusters.note: The schools in this group run the Diploma through to Year 13, which makes them the usual destination for a JBR student who wants Physics Higher Level. The buses are longer, the finish is later, and the investigation deadlines are set school by school rather than by the IB, so two children in the same tower can be six weeks apart.

schoolClusters.city: The Jumeirah Park and Jumeirah Village corridor
schoolClusters.note: Further inland and growing quickly, with several schools that JBR families use when places closer to the coast are full. Journeys on this corridor are the longest in the set, and the arrival time back in the tower is the single number that should set the session slot.

sections.heading: What a JBR parent means by an IB Physics tutor in JBR
paragraphs: An IB Physics tutor in JBR, in practice, means an online one-to-one teacher who knows the 2023 guide and can work inside the ninety minutes between the school bus and dinner. Three requests arrive more often than any others from the towers: rescue work in Theme D, where fields are examined as a single concept; investigation supervision through DP2; and grade conversion for a student whose class marks are fine and whose exam marks are not.

That last one is the most common and the least understood. A student who can derive an expression correctly and still score four out of nine is not short of physics. They are short of the habits the mark scheme rewards: a stated assumption, a diagram with labelled forces, a substitution shown before the number appears, a unit carried through the working, a final answer given to a defensible number of significant figures. None of that is taught in a hurry, and none of it shows up in a report that says the student is working hard.

The second request is seasonal. From October in DP2 the investigation report competes with mocks, the Extended Essay and university applications, and it is the one piece of work where a tutor's role is tightly bounded by IB rules. A tutor can ask whether the research question is answerable with the apparatus available, whether the uncertainty treatment is defensible, and whether the conclusion follows from the data. The report itself is the student's own work from first line to last, and that boundary is stated here because the alternative is an academic-honesty investigation at the school.

sections.heading: The Physics course the way the IB now runs it
paragraphs: The guide in force for first examinations in 2025 organises the whole subject into five themes, each built around a central idea rather than a list of chapters. Theme A covers space, time and motion; Theme B the particulate nature of matter; Theme C wave behaviour; Theme D fields; and Theme E nuclear and quantum physics. Standard and Higher Level share every theme, with additional higher level content placed inside the theme it belongs to.

That structure has a practical consequence for tutoring. Because the additional higher level material is embedded rather than appended, a Higher Level student who is shaky on the shared content of Theme D cannot simply skip the harder half and keep the easier marks. Induction sits on top of magnetic flux, and capacitance sits on top of electric potential. Sequencing matters more than it used to, and a tutor who starts with whatever the class is covering this week, without checking what was secure three themes ago, will spend a term treating symptoms.

Running underneath the themes are the tools and the inquiry process: experimental technique, use of technology, and the mathematics the course assumes. These are not examined separately. They are the reason two students with identical content knowledge can be four marks apart on a data question, and they are the part of the course that most reliably improves with one-to-one attention rather than more class time. For a JBR family choosing between more school support and one-to-one time, that distinction is the one worth holding on to: the class teaches the content, and the marks that remain sit in technique.

Theme B: thermal physics, the gas laws, current electricity, and at Higher Level thermodynamic cycles
Theme C: travelling waves, superposition, standing waves, the Doppler effect and interference
Theme D: gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated as one idea, with induction and capacitance at Higher Level
Theme E: radioactivity, nuclear structure, the quantum nature of radiation and particle physics

sections.heading: Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2: all of the written assessment
paragraphs: There are two written papers, not three. Paper 1 is sat in two sections, a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and together they carry just over a third of the grade. Paper 2 is extended response and carries the largest single share. The scientific investigation supplies the rest. Competitor pages in this market still describe a Paper 3 and a set of options, which is the clearest sign that a page has not been revised since the guide changed.

The shape of the paper matters for how an hour is spent. Paper 1A gives no credit for method, so a student who makes one algebraic slip loses the whole mark, and the distractors are written from the slips examiners expect. Paper 1B is the opposite: a long unfamiliar experiment where almost every mark is awarded for the handling of data rather than for recall. Paper 2 is where command terms decide the outcome, because a question asking a student to explain and answered as though it asked them to describe will collect roughly half of what was available.

The table below sets out each component, what it genuinely tests, the duration at each level, its share of the final grade and the specific place marks leak away. Durations are the ones published in the current subject guide; the weightings have been stable since first examinations in 2025. Confirm your child's own session and timetable with the school's Diploma coordinator, since entry details are set by the centre rather than by any tutor.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The investigation is a single piece of work: one student-designed experiment, written up in no more than 3,000 words, marked out of 24 against four criteria of six marks each, worth a fifth of the final grade. It is marked by the school and moderated by the IB. Four criteria, six marks each, is the whole of it, and knowing that changes how a student allocates their time, because evaluation is worth exactly as much as data analysis and is usually given a fraction of the attention.

Two of the four criteria are where almost all of the loss happens. Research design fails when the question is too broad to answer with the apparatus actually available in a school laboratory in Dubai, which is the commonest version of the problem: an ambitious question, a borrowed data set, and no controlled variable. Evaluation fails when limitations are described generically, as human error, more trials and better equipment, rather than as the specific thing that limited this measurement on this apparatus.

A tutor's job on this piece is bounded and should be stated plainly. Questioning a research question, pointing at an uncertainty that has not been propagated, and asking why a conclusion goes beyond the data are all teaching. Supplying text, restructuring a report into its final form, or handing over a method is not, and under IB academic-honesty rules it puts the student's whole diploma at risk. The student does the work; the tutor asks what a moderator will ask.

sections.heading: Where Physics marks actually go missing, theme by theme
paragraphs: Diagnosis beats coverage. A student who has sat one mock has already told you where the marks are going, and a tutor who reads that script before the first lesson can usually name the three recurring errors inside twenty minutes. In this corridor the same handful of failures turn up again and again, and they are rarely about the hardest content in the course.

Theme A loses marks on momentum and on circular motion, almost always because the free-body diagram was skipped and the resolved components were guessed. Theme B loses them on the distinction between heat and temperature in words, and on the gas laws when a volume is left in cubic centimetres. Theme C loses them on standing waves, where students describe what a node is without saying what it means for the wavelength. Theme D loses them wholesale, because potential and field strength are treated as interchangeable and the signs are lost.

Theme E loses marks on decay calculations, where logarithms are the real obstacle, and on the photoelectric effect, where a student who can recite the equation cannot say which quantity the gradient of the graph gives. None of this needs a longer course. It needs a tutor who marks the student's own work against the published expectations and then refuses to move on until the same question is answered cleanly a second time, a week later. The pattern repeats often enough across themes that it is worth stating as a rule: the second clean answer a week later is the evidence, and the first one is only a hope.

sections.heading: The JBR afternoon: when a Physics session can realistically start
paragraphs: The most common reason a tutoring arrangement in the towers fails is not the tutor. It is a session booked at a time that only existed on paper. A slot agreed in September for 16:30 collapses in October when an activity starts, and after three rescheduled lessons the family concludes that tutoring does not work for their child. Picking the slot from the afternoon pattern, rather than from the parent's calendar, fixes that before it happens.

The patterns are predictable. On a plain weekday with no activity, a student bussing back from Al Sufouh is inside the tower before four and can start at a quarter to five with their head still working. Add one after-school activity and arrival slides past five, which makes an 18:00 start the honest option and makes new teaching a poor use of it. A double-period science day is the one to avoid entirely: three hours of physics before lunch means a fourth hour in the evening buys almost nothing.

Two patterns are worth planning for in advance. Mock fortnight frees up mornings, which is the only time in the year when timed papers can be sat and marked in the same session. And a shortened Friday, where the school runs one, gives the single unhurried block that suits the investigation, the one task that cannot be done well in forty-five minutes between a bus and a meal.
