sections.heading: What a Physics tutor may and may not touch, and who is permitted to teach
paragraphs: Two boundaries are worth knowing before you hire anyone. The first is academic honesty. Under IB rules the scientific investigation must be the student's own work, and a tutor who supplies a method, rewrites a conclusion or hands over text has exposed the student to a malpractice finding that can cost the whole diploma. Feedback, questioning and teaching are permitted and valuable. Production of assessed material is not, and any provider offering a finished investigation should be treated as a warning sign rather than a convenience.

The second is permits. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here.

The permit also carries a code of conduct that bars a teacher from tutoring students affiliated with their own school, which is why the offer of your child's own class teacher for private lessons is a question to ask rather than a perk to accept. Separately, a tutoring operation running premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a different thing from an individual's permit. IB Gram is an online matching platform and holds no regulator or examination-board endorsement of any kind.
bullets: Teaching, questioning and written feedback on the student's own draft are all permitted
Supplied text, a supplied method or a restructured report are not, under IB rules
The private tuition work permit is free for two years and applied for through MoHRE
Ask any tutor which permit category they fall into, and whether your child attends their school

process.title: Send the marked paper, not the report card
process.description: A report says a grade. A marked Paper 2 says where the marks went, which is what a physics tutor needs. Send a photograph of the last marked script, the current theme, the level and the school's investigation deadline, and the first session can start with a diagnosis instead of an introduction.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson before paying anything
process.description: The first lesson is a free trial, booked before any payment is made, and it is a teaching session rather than a sales call. Listen to how the tutor handles one question your child got wrong. If the explanation is clearer than the one that failed at school, that is the signal to look for.

process.title: Fix the session to one weekday and the bus timetable
process.description: Pick the slot from the afternoon pattern in the table above, not from the family calendar. A slot that survives an added activity in October is worth more than a slightly earlier one that collapses, because three reschedules in a term is how a sound arrangement gets abandoned.

process.title: Agree one measurable target for the first month
process.description: Not better physics. Something checkable: uncertainty propagation handled correctly in Paper 1B, or command-term discipline on three consecutive Paper 2 questions. A target you can verify on a marked script is what tells you in four weeks whether the hours are working.

process.title: Review at four sessions and change the tutor if the fit is wrong
process.description: Physics teaching is personal, and a tutor who is excellent for one student can be wrong for another. Reviewing at four sessions makes a change a normal step rather than a complaint, and a replacement who inherits the diagnosis rather than starting again loses nothing.

whyPoints.title: Taught on the guide your child is actually sitting
whyPoints.description: Five themes, two written papers, one scientific investigation, higher level content inside the themes rather than in options. Any tutor still planning around Paper 3 is teaching a course that was retired, and in a subject this cumulative that error costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around the bus, not around a drive
whyPoints.description: An online slot does not move because Al Sufouh Road is slow, which means the session a JBR family books in September is the session they still have in February. The time saved is not a convenience; it is the difference between four sessions a month and two.

whyPoints.title: Specialism instead of proximity
whyPoints.description: The pool of physics teachers who can reach Dubai Marina by five on a weekday is small. The pool who can teach Theme D fields and defend an uncertainty calculation is larger and lives elsewhere. Choosing online means choosing from the second pool.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, with the month it was read. That is deliberate: in this market three of the six strongest ranking pages publish no price at all, and a parent cannot judge a quote without a benchmark.

whyPoints.title: Stated limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor here questions a research question, challenges an evaluation and marks a script. They do not supply text for an investigation or an Extended Essay. That boundary protects the student's diploma, and saying so out loud is a differentiator in a market that includes providers selling finished coursework.

faqs.question: Does IB Physics still have a Paper 3?
faqs.answer: No. The guide in force for first examinations in 2025 removed Paper 3 and the old options. Assessment is now Paper 1, sat as a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section and carrying 36% of the grade, Paper 2 of extended response carrying 44%, and one scientific investigation carrying the remaining 20%. If a tutor, a revision site or an agency page still advertises Paper 3 preparation or option-topic teaching, it has not been updated since the change, which tells you something useful about how current the rest of its advice is.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Physics grade is the scientific investigation worth?
faqs.answer: A fifth. The investigation is one student-designed experiment, reported in up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 by the school and moderated by the IB. The marks split evenly across four criteria worth six each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. That even split is the part students miss. Evaluation carries exactly as many marks as data analysis, and it is routinely written in the last hour before the deadline, which is why it is the single cheapest place to recover marks.

faqs.question: My son is at school in Al Barsha and gets back to the tower at half past four. When can a Physics session start?
faqs.answer: Half past five or six o'clock, on a day without an after-school activity. A student who walks in at 16:30 needs a break before abstract work, and a session that starts the moment the bus arrives usually produces forty minutes of useful thinking out of sixty. If an activity runs, move the session to 18:00 and use it for problem sets rather than new teaching. On a double-period science day, skip physics entirely and use a different evening.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Physics more content than Standard Level, or just harder questions?
faqs.answer: Both, and the extra content is positioned differently from how parents expect. Higher Level does not add separate chapters at the end; it adds material inside each of the five themes, so rotational dynamics and relativity sit within Theme A and induction and capacitance within Theme D. That means the shared content has to be secure first, because the higher level material is built directly on top of it. Paper 2 also runs two and a half hours at Higher Level against one and a half at Standard, which is a stamina demand in its own right.

faqs.question: Which Physics themes cause the most trouble in DP1?
faqs.answer: Theme D by a wide margin. Fields are taught as one unified idea covering gravitational, electric and magnetic cases, which is elegant and brutal: a student who does not separate field strength from potential will get the algebra right and the signs wrong, repeatedly. Theme B is second, usually through units left unconverted in gas-law work. Theme A looks harmless and quietly costs marks whenever a free-body diagram is skipped and the resolved components are guessed rather than drawn.

faqs.question: Will a Physics tutor drive out to a JBR tower for the lesson?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Lessons for families in the UAE are one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; household visits are a service it runs only in India. For physics specifically that is a better fit than it sounds. The limiting factor on a tutor who travels is the drive, which means a small pool, whereas an online slot gives access to teachers who specialise in the exact theme or component that is costing marks.

faqs.question: My daughter takes Mathematics Applications and Interpretation with Physics Higher Level. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a known friction point rather than a mistake. Applications and Interpretation spends less time on algebraic manipulation than Analysis and Approaches, so a student arrives at a Physics Paper 2 rearrangement with fewer repetitions behind them. The fix is usually narrow: logarithms for decay work in Theme E, rearrangement of multi-variable expressions, and resolved components in trigonometry. Three or four targeted sessions on those specific skills tend to do more for a physics grade than a general change of course.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics tutor cost around JBR and Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: Published market figures for this part of Dubai run from roughly AED 45-65 an hour at the budget online end, advertised by EdFlik, through AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visiting rates sit higher because travel is inside the fee: Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives AED 180-350 and independent home tutors quote up to AED 500. Named and examiner-tier specialists go further again, with BartyED publishing AED 650. All figures as read in October 2026.

faqs.question: How far can a JBR tutor help with the Physics IA without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can ask whether the research question can be answered with the apparatus the school actually has, point out an uncertainty that has not been propagated, challenge a conclusion that goes beyond the data, and push an evaluation past human error towards specific limitations. What a tutor must not do is supply a method, provide text or restructure the report into its final form. The student authors every line. Any provider offering a finished investigation is offering a malpractice risk, not a service.

faqs.question: We have five weeks until the mock. Is it too late for Physics tutoring to help?
faqs.answer: Five weeks is enough for mark conversion, not for rebuilding a theme. Used well, that window is spent on timed Paper 1B and Paper 2 sections, marked live against the published expectations, with the three recurring errors identified in week one and retested in weeks three and five. Students commonly gain more from this than from new teaching, because the typical loss in a mock is not missing content but missing method: no diagram, no stated assumption, a command term misread, a unit abandoned halfway through.

faqs.question: How do online Physics lessons handle diagrams, derivations and graph work?
faqs.answer: On a shared whiteboard, with the student holding the pen more often than the tutor. The practical test of an online physics session is whether your child is drawing the free-body diagram or watching one being drawn. A good tutor screen-shares the student's own marked script, asks them to redo the question live, and types nothing themselves beyond a prompt. Graph work is done on the student's own plotted data, which also means the investigation and Paper 1B practice can share the same hour.

faqs.question: Does my child need to repeat laboratory work at home for the investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and they should not try to. The investigation is designed around apparatus available at school, and the research question should be chosen to match what the laboratory can actually supply. Where an online tutor adds value is before the data exists: testing whether the question is answerable, whether the controlled variables are genuinely controlled, and whether the measurement range will produce a gradient worth analysing. Afterwards, the work is in the processing, the uncertainty treatment and the evaluation, none of which needs a bench.

faqs.question: Is one Physics session a week enough in the final year?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, provided the cadence changes at the right moments. One weekly hour through the term handles the current theme and keeps exam habits alive. Around the investigation deadline a fortnightly clinic on that specific piece is better value than general teaching. In the four to six weeks before mocks and before the May session, a short block of timed-paper work earns more than the same hours spread thin. Two sessions a week every week for two years is usually spending without a plan.

faqs.question: Can a Physics session move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families it should. School days are compressed during Ramadan and finish earlier, which brings students back into the towers in the early afternoon when they are least able to concentrate. A slot around 20:30, after Iftar, usually produces better work than an afternoon one. Use that period for revision of material already taught rather than for new content, and plan the heavier sequencing for the weeks either side of it.

faqs.question: Does a Physics tutor need a UAE permit, and how would we check?
faqs.answer: Anyone giving private lessons in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Ask the tutor directly which category applies to them. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, which lists a two-working-day completion time.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jbr.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper and one honest look at the afternoon
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jbr.closingBody: Two pieces of information decide whether Physics tutoring works for a family in JBR: what the last marked script says about where the marks are going, and what time your child genuinely walks back into the tower on each weekday. Send the script, name the theme and the level, and pick the slot from the afternoon pattern rather than from the family calendar. The first lesson is a free trial, taken before anything is paid for, and it is a teaching session rather than a pitch. Judge it on one thing: whether the explanation your child heard was clearer than the one that did not land at school.

intro.heading: Diploma physics is a two-year calendar, not a list of topics
paragraphs: Physics tutoring usually begins in a panic about a topic. Fields went badly, or the student cannot do anything with uncertainties, and a tutor is booked to teach that thing. That is a reasonable response and it is also why a great deal of physics tutoring produces no change in the grade: the work is organised around the symptom instead of around the term the student is actually in.

The Diploma physics course has a shape with three hard edges. The scientific investigation has to be designed, run and written to a school-set deadline. The mock window sits roughly a term before the papers and exists to produce diagnostic data. The final eight weeks are for timed papers and nothing else, because new content introduced there displaces the practice that converts knowledge into marks. A session spent teaching fields in week four of that final run is a session spent wrongly.

This page is built on that calendar. It counts backwards from the May session, which is the one almost every UAE school enters its candidates for, and names what should exist at each point. Around that it sets out the content themes of the current physics guide, the data-and-uncertainty skills that quietly decide a grade, and the AED market bands with their sources.

Jebel Ali's geography is why the delivery model gets a section of its own. The district sits at the industrial western edge of Dubai, around the port and the free zone, with its residential communities spread through Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community, Dubai South and Emaar South. A physics specialist who agrees to drive to any of those arrives at the end of the useful part of the evening, and the number who will agree at all shrinks the further south the address sits.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For physics the format fits the work: most of what a tutor does is read a marked script or a draft investigation on a shared screen, interrogate a graph, and check whether an uncertainty was propagated or guessed. The hands-on laboratory work stays with the school, as the IB requires.

One note on dates before the tables. Cambridge and Pearson publish their timetables and this page cites them where relevant. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session and publishes no specific IB examination or results date. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds both the external dates and the internal deadlines, and the internal ones usually drive the term plan.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jebel-ali.programmesIntro: Physics requests from this catchment come from three stages, and the calendar pressure on each is completely different. Only one of them ends in an external paper.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Available at Higher and Standard Level. The current guide organises content into themes running from space, time and motion through the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour and fields to nuclear and quantum physics, with Higher Level extensions inside each. Assessment combines externally marked papers with an internally assessed scientific investigation moderated by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: Most Jebel Ali physics candidates arrive from an IGCSE background, where physics rewarded recall and clean substitution. The Diploma rewards causal explanation, uncertainty handling and sustained reasoning across linked question parts, so a strong IGCSE grade predicts the content will be manageable and nothing about the first Diploma report.

programmes.name: The scientific investigation and the Diploma core
programmes.description: The investigation is the internally assessed component, marked against criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It carries a substantial share of the subject grade; confirm the exact weighting in your school's current subject guide. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service compete for the same weeks.
programmes.countryNote: The investigation deadline in this catchment is set by the school and lands in the same term as the Extended Essay deadline and the mocks. Students who chose a research question before the long summer break have time to evaluate; students who did not lose marks on the evaluation criterion because there is nothing left to think with.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each worth up to eight marks, covering knowledge and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. There is no external paper for most students, so the record is a set of criterion judgements.
programmes.countryNote: MYP 5 students in Al Furjan and Green Community heading for Diploma physics are usually well prepared for the inquiry side and under-prepared for the algebra. Formula rearrangement under time pressure is the skill the Diploma assumes from the first week, and the MYP never required it at speed.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of Diploma physics that generate requests from this catchment, each with the specific place marks go missing. Physics is diagnosable: a marked script usually shows the failure within two questions.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy, with Higher Level extensions into rotational and relativistic work. Marks go on free-body diagrams never drawn, so the forces are summed from memory of the situation rather than from the diagram.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws and the kinetic model. The recurring loss is unit mismatch: temperatures in Celsius where kelvin was needed, or a volume in litres entering an equation expecting cubic metres.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Oscillations, wave phenomena, superposition and standing waves, with Higher Level extensions. Diagram-based questions reward precision about phase and path difference, and vague descriptions of interference earn almost nothing.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields and the circuits that follow. The commonest single weakness in this catchment, because it requires holding an abstract model and a sign convention at the same time under time pressure.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactivity, nuclear energy and quantum behaviour, with Higher Level extensions. Content-heavy and often taught late, which makes it the topic most likely to be unfinished when the mock window arrives.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Internally assessed and marked against criteria covering design, analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Most drafts fail on a research question the collected data cannot actually answer, and on conclusions that restate the trend without the physics.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty bars on a graph. Guessed rather than propagated uncertainties cost marks on both the papers and the investigation, and almost nobody drills this.

subjects.name: Graph analysis and linearisation
subjects.description: Choosing what to plot so a relationship becomes linear, then extracting a gradient with units and interpreting it physically. A gradient quoted without units is a thrown-away mark, and it recurs on every data-based paper.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: "State", "describe", "explain", "discuss" and "evaluate" set four different depths. A correct formula where "explain" was asked earns part marks at best, because the question wanted a causal chain in words.

subjects.name: Algebraic rearrangement under time
subjects.description: The skill that decides whether the back half of a multi-part question is reachable. Students who recognise an equation but cannot transpose it quickly lose marks that have nothing to do with their physics.

sections.heading: The physics year counted backwards from the session
paragraphs: Begin at the papers and walk back. The final eight weeks are for timed practice: papers sat under real conditions, marked by someone who is not the student, with each session attacking what the marking found. Before that sits the mock window, a term out, whose purpose is to produce data rather than a verdict. Before that, the scientific investigation has to be finished to a school deadline. Before that, it has to be designed, which means the first Diploma year should end with a workable research question.

Set out that way, the usual pattern of enquiries looks mistimed. Most physics requests from this catchment arrive after the mocks, when the content window has closed. A student who has not met nuclear and quantum physics by then cannot both cover it properly and do the timed practice that converts it into marks, and one of the two has to give. The honest conversation is about which, and it should happen in the first session rather than in April.

The second thing the backwards count exposes is the collision. School deadlines for the physics investigation, the Extended Essay and the mock papers frequently land within the same six weeks. Three substantial pieces of independent work and one calendar. Students who designed the investigation early survive it; students who did not lose marks on evaluation, because evaluation is the part that needs unhurried thought.

A note on precision: we name the May session as the one UAE schools sit and publish no specific IB examination or results date here, because IB dates are not confirmable from the IB by automated means. The dates that matter more to your term plan are internal anyway, and your school's Diploma coordinator holds them.

sections.heading: Uncertainty and graph work: the marks nobody revises for
paragraphs: Ask a Diploma physics student what they are weak at and they will name a theme. Ask their marked script and it will usually name uncertainty treatment and graph handling instead. These are cross-cutting skills that appear on every data-based question and inside the investigation, and they are rarely taught as a separate discipline because they do not belong to any one topic.

The specific failures recur. An uncertainty quoted as a round number because it looked reasonable, rather than derived from the instrument's resolution. A percentage uncertainty calculated once and then not propagated through the subsequent multiplication. Uncertainty bars drawn as a decorative constant width across a plot. A gradient quoted to four significant figures from a hand-drawn line of best fit whose own uncertainty is larger than the final digit.

Graph choice is the other half. The useful skill is deciding what to plot so that a non-linear relationship becomes a straight line, then recognising what the gradient and the intercept physically represent. Students who plot the raw variables and then describe a curve have thrown away the analytical mark that linearisation would have earned. This is learnable in three or four sessions and it pays on the papers and the investigation simultaneously.

There is a third, quieter skill: knowing when the data does not support the claim. A conclusion that asserts proportionality from five points with overlapping uncertainty bars is a physics error, not a writing error, and the evaluation criterion in the investigation is built precisely to catch it. Teaching a student to look for that is more valuable than another pass through fields.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The investigation is internally assessed and externally moderated, and it is the component where a tutor can do the most legitimate good. It is also where the academic-honesty boundary gets tested, because the work is a document and documents can be written by other people.

The legitimate space is wide. A tutor can help narrow a research question until the available apparatus can actually answer it, teach the physics the investigation needs, explain what each criterion rewards and what it caps, check whether uncertainties were propagated or guessed, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, and mark a draft against the descriptors. That covers nearly everything a student genuinely needs.

What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite or complete any part of it, supply the research question wholesale, produce or adjust the data, or edit the document to a finished state. The test after every session is whether every sentence in the draft was typed by your child. There are services in this market selling completed Internal Assessments, one advertising them at AED 3,750; submitting bought work is a malpractice matter that can cost the whole Diploma, and no price makes that reasonable.

On the practical side, the division of labour is set by the IB rather than by us. The hands-on laboratory work happens at school, under the teacher's supervision and with the school's apparatus and risk assessment. A tutor works on the design before it, the analysis after it, and the writing throughout. We also do not distribute IB papers, mark schemes, boundary tables or subject guides, which are copyright material; we reference and link the official sources.

sections.heading: Why physics explanations lose marks when the physics is right
paragraphs: A large share of the marks a Jebel Ali physics student loses go on questions they could answer verbally. The reason is that "explain" in an IB physics paper means a chain: this changes, which causes that, which results in the stated outcome. A correct formula is not a chain. A restatement of the question in physics vocabulary is not a chain. Both are extremely common and both earn part marks at best.

The pattern comes from IGCSE, where a correct substitution and a correct answer usually carried the mark. The Diploma asks for reasoning in prose and marks it against the reasoning. A student whose default register is "state the formula and compute" scores well on calculation questions and consistently loses the explanation marks, paper after paper, without identifying the pattern - because each individual loss looks like bad luck.

The drill is specific and unglamorous. Take explanation questions only, strip the numbers out, and require the answer as a sequence of linked clauses with no equations permitted. Then add the equation back as supporting detail. After a handful of sessions students start hearing the command term before they start writing, which is the behaviour change that moves the mark.

The same discipline fixes the diagram problem. Free-body diagrams, field diagrams and ray diagrams are not illustrations; they are the working. A student who sums forces from their mental picture of the situation makes sign errors that the diagram would have prevented, and loses marks the examiner was waiting to award for the diagram itself.

sections.heading: What IB physics tutoring costs in Dubai, and what the premium buys
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read in October 2026 and attributed to whoever published them. At the entry level, Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. A qualified subject tutor online is published at AED 150-300, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 per Dubai rate guidance, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. Specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

For physics specifically, the entry band is close to irrelevant. A capable undergraduate at AED 50 an hour can supervise homework; they cannot tell a student that their uncertainty bars make the asserted proportionality indefensible. The useful comparison in physics is between the AED 150-300 online band and the AED 180-500 in-home band, and the difference there is largely travel.

What the travel premium buys from a Jebel Ali or Emaar South address is a person in the room, which matters for a student who will not start work unsupervised. What it costs is the later start and the narrower list, because only tutors willing to make that drive appear in it at all. For Higher Level physics in this catchment, that list is short enough that the specialist question usually outweighs the presence question.

None of these are IB Gram prices and this page has no rate card; our fee depends on level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The bands are published so a quote can be judged against something real, which three of the pages currently ranking for this search do not permit, and two of the rest quote US dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

sections.heading: Online physics lessons from Jebel Ali, limitations stated plainly
paragraphs: The format fits the assessed work. Diploma physics tutoring is mostly document work: a marked script, a data question, a draft investigation, a graph that needs interrogating. A shared screen on which both people annotate the same plot is better than one paper copy across a table, and screen sharing lets a tutor rebuild a linearisation step by step while the student writes it.

The scheduling gain matters more in physics than in most subjects because of the algebra. A 4.30pm session catches a student who can still rearrange an equation accurately. A 6.15pm session, after a tutor has crossed Dubai in term traffic, catches one who makes transposition errors. Parents commonly read those errors as weak physics; they are frequently fatigue.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we put that near the top of the page because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote. A family is owed that disclosure before booking rather than after.

The honest limitations: a student who needs an adult present to begin work is better served in person; a weak home connection shortens the hour regardless of the clock; a shared study space in a Discovery Gardens apartment undermines any lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room; and no online tutor substitutes for laboratory time, which under IB rules belongs to the school anyway. If one of those describes your household, hire locally and ask the tutor about the MoHRE private tuition work permit first.

sections.heading: The honesty rules worth holding a physics tutor to
paragraphs: Physics attracts overclaiming because its results look objective. Three claims are worth discounting immediately when hiring anyone for Diploma physics in Dubai.

Promised outcomes come first. No tutor can commit to a 7, a points total or a grade improvement, and grade boundaries are set after each session is marked, so even a well-informed prediction is a prediction. We publish no outcome promise, no success percentage and no self-asserted rating, because a statistic without n, date and method is a liability rather than evidence. Any page offering a figure of that kind should be asked to produce the underlying data.

Examiner claims come second. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for individuals, and in this market examiner status is routinely used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content that nobody has. We also do not host or distribute board papers, mark schemes, boundary tables or subject guides; we reference the official sources and work from the school's licensed copies.

Regulatory endorsement comes third. IB Gram is not KHDA approved - a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, and we hold none and operate no UAE office. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation or partnership. Separately, private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

sections.heading: Starting mid-calendar, and what we say when we cannot help
paragraphs: Most families start somewhere in the middle of the calendar, which is workable as long as the plan reflects where that is. Send the level - Higher or Standard - the school, and a photograph of the most recent marked assessment, or the current draft of the investigation if that is the live deadline.

The first session is diagnostic, not introductory. The tutor reads the script against the mark scheme and tells you which of three positions you are in: habit marks recoverable in weeks, unfinished content needing a term, or both with a deadline too close to serve either properly. The third answer is the one families least want to hear and most need, because it determines what gets sacrificed and by whom.

Matching takes about a day for Standard Level physics. Higher Level in the second Diploma year can take two or three days, because the pool is genuinely narrow and a general science tutor in front of a Higher Level investigation is worse than a delay. We tell you the expected wait at the enquiry rather than letting you discover it.

When no suitable physics specialist has a slot at the hour you need, we say so and offer real alternatives: a different weekday with the right tutor, a short block until a regular slot frees up, or an honest recommendation to look locally with the permit question in hand. No competitor in this market publishes what happens when it cannot help, which is why that sentence is on this page rather than in a delayed reply.

process.title: Say the level and the live deadline
process.description: Higher or Standard, and whether the next pressure point is the investigation, the mocks or the papers. The same weakness needs different work in each phase, and misreading the phase is the usual cause of a wasted term.

process.title: Send a marked script or the investigation draft
process.description: A photograph of the most recent marked assessment, or the current draft if that is what is due. Physics is diagnosable from a script: explanation depth, diagram habits and uncertainty treatment all show within two questions.

process.title: Physics specialist matched at that level
process.description: Never a general science tutor. Standard Level usually matches within a day; Higher Level in the second Diploma year can take two or three, and we tell you which case applies before you start waiting.

process.title: Free diagnostic trial lesson online
process.description: A real one-to-one lesson with the matched specialist, built on the script or draft you sent, ending in a written note of what it showed and what the next month should target. No card details and nothing to commit to.

process.title: Weekly slot, re-cut at each pressure point
process.description: The same tutor at the same Gulf Standard Time hour, with the plan rewritten after the mocks and again eight weeks out. Slots shift for Ramadan and examination weeks as a calendar change, since nobody is travelling.

whyPoints.title: The plan follows the calendar, not the complaint
whyPoints.description: Content in the first year, investigation around the school deadline, habit repair after the mocks, timed papers in the final eight weeks. Teaching new fields content in week four of the final run is the commonest wasted session in Diploma physics.

whyPoints.title: Data and uncertainty taught as a discipline
whyPoints.description: Propagation, uncertainty bars, linearisation and gradient interpretation appear on every data question and inside the investigation, and they belong to no single theme, which is exactly why they go unrevised.

whyPoints.title: Explanation marks targeted directly
whyPoints.description: An IB physics "explain" question wants a causal chain in words. Students arriving from IGCSE default to formula-and-answer and lose those marks consistently, and the fix is a drill rather than more content.

whyPoints.title: The investigation line held
whyPoints.description: Tutors narrow the question, teach the physics, check propagation and mark drafts. They never write, rewrite or supply data. Services selling finished coursework in this market put a student's whole Diploma at risk.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names its publisher and the month it was read. Three of the pages ranking for this search publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families transacting in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Earliest usable hour of the day
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from about 4pm Gulf Standard Time because no tutor is driving to Jebel Ali or Emaar South. For physics that matters: transposition errors at 6.15pm look exactly like weak physics and are usually fatigue.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should a Jebel Ali physics student start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, because the constraint is calendar rather than content. The first Diploma year is when explanation habits and diagram discipline are cheap to build, and when the investigation can still be designed unhurriedly. Once the mocks are marked, the content window has effectively closed: a student who has not met nuclear and quantum physics by then cannot both learn it and do the timed practice that converts it into marks. Past that point the honest plan is habit repair and papers rather than new teaching.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on physics questions they can explain out loud?
faqs.answer: Because "explain" in an IB physics paper means a written chain of causes, and a correct formula is not a chain. Students arriving from IGCSE default to stating an equation and computing, which scored well there and consistently loses the explanation marks here. Each loss looks like bad luck in isolation, so the pattern is rarely identified. The drill is to take explanation questions only, strip out the numbers, and require linked clauses with no equations permitted, then add the equation back as supporting detail.

faqs.question: How do online lessons handle the physics practical work?
faqs.answer: They handle the assessed thinking, not the apparatus. The internally assessed investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and all of that is document work: checking whether an uncertainty was propagated or guessed, whether the chosen plot linearises the relationship, whether the conclusion follows from points with overlapping uncertainty bars. The hands-on procedure happens in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision with the school's apparatus and risk assessment, as the IB requires, and no tutor substitutes for that.

faqs.question: What is the hardest part of IB physics for students in this catchment?
faqs.answer: Fields, consistently, because it requires holding an abstract model and a sign convention simultaneously under time pressure. Nuclear and quantum physics causes a different problem: it is often taught late, so it is the theme most likely to be unfinished when the mocks arrive. Beneath both sits the real difficulty, which is cross-cutting rather than topical - uncertainty treatment and graph analysis, which appear on every data question and inside the investigation and belong to no single theme, so nobody revises them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help design my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help narrow the research question until the available apparatus can actually answer it, which is the single most valuable thing anyone does for an investigation. They can teach the physics it needs, explain what each criterion rewards, check whether uncertainties were propagated properly, question whether the conclusion follows from the data, and mark the draft against the descriptors. What they cannot do is supply the question, write any part of the document, or produce or adjust the data. Every sentence must be typed by the student.

faqs.question: Should a Jebel Ali student take physics at Higher or Standard Level?
faqs.answer: It is broader and it demands more sustained reasoning rather than simply more content. Higher Level adds extensions inside each theme and more questions requiring several linked steps to be carried through, which punishes students who abandon a question when one part does not resolve cleanly. The practical consequence for tutoring is the match: Standard Level physics specialists are reasonably available, while Higher Level in the second Diploma year has a narrow pool, and a general science tutor in front of Higher Level work is a false economy.

faqs.question: What should the last eight weeks before the physics papers look like?
faqs.answer: Timed papers and marking, with no new content. The student sits full papers under real conditions, including the data-based sections, and someone who is not the student marks them against the official scheme. The result is a ranked list of repeated habits, and the next session attacks those rather than moving to a fresh paper. New teaching in this window displaces the practice that converts existing knowledge into marks, which is why a late content push so reliably produces no change in the result.

faqs.question: Does my child need physics tutoring and maths tutoring separately?
faqs.answer: Sometimes one specialist covers both, and it works when the shared problem is algebraic - formula rearrangement failing in both subjects under time pressure. It works less well when the physics difficulty is really about causal explanation or about the investigation, which are different competencies from mathematical method. Our default is one subject per tutor, because the match is for component-level knowledge of a specific mark scheme. Tell us both subjects and we will say honestly whether one tutor fits your child's particular case.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match an HL physics tutor for Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Two to three days rather than one, and we say so at the enquiry rather than afterwards. Higher Level physics in the second Diploma year has one of the narrower specialist pools of any subject we cover, and substituting a general science tutor for a specialist wastes the family's money and the student's remaining weeks. A radius search from Dubai South or Emaar South for the same specialism commonly returns general science tutors only, which is why the delivery model changes the outcome here rather than only the price.

faqs.question: Why do uncertainties cost so many marks in Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Because they are examined everywhere and taught nowhere in particular. Absolute uncertainty should come from the instrument's resolution rather than from a plausible-looking round number. Percentage uncertainty has to be propagated through each subsequent operation, not calculated once and forgotten. Uncertainty bars have to be real rather than a decorative constant width. And a gradient quoted to four significant figures from a hand-drawn line whose own uncertainty is larger than the last digit is simply wrong. Three or four focused sessions usually fix all of it.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5 and wants Diploma physics. What should we do now?
faqs.answer: Build the algebra rather than the content. The MYP assesses against four lettered criteria out of eight and rewards inquiry and communication, which is good preparation for the investigation. What it does not require is fast, accurate formula rearrangement, and Diploma physics assumes that from the first week. A summer of deliberate transposition practice, plus the habit of drawing a free-body or field diagram before any calculation, is worth more than reading ahead into themes the school will teach properly anyway.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB physics exam dates?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is worth stating. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one almost all UAE schools enter candidates for and goes no further. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we cite those where they are relevant. For your child's actual dates, the school's Diploma coordinator holds both the external session dates and the internal deadlines for the investigation and the Extended Essay, and the internal ones usually drive the term plan.

faqs.question: Can physics sessions move around Ramadan without losing ground?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the frequency is protected rather than the length. School hours shorten, households reorganise their evening around iftar, and a weekday 5pm slot usually becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. For physics the thing that decays fastest when sessions stop is algebraic fluency, so two shorter sessions a week hold more than one long one when a student is fasting. Because nobody is travelling to your address, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute.

faqs.question: What does the free trial physics lesson actually produce?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis, and it is yours whether or not you continue. The matched specialist - not a salesperson - teaches a real one-to-one lesson online on the script or investigation draft you sent, and finishes by writing down what the document showed: whether the losses are explanation depth, diagram habits, uncertainty treatment or genuinely unfinished content, and what the first month should target. No card details are needed to book it and there is no package to commit to beforehand.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jlt.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Physics to JLT families over live video. Each works at a stated level and theme set rather than across all of science, so ask which themes they have taught to examination and how many scientific investigations they have supervised to submission.

intro.heading: JLT has no Diploma school, so physics help here starts with the journey home
paragraphs: Jumeirah Lakes Towers is a residential cluster of towers around three artificial lakes, and it contains no IB Diploma school. A Year 12 student living in Cluster J or Cluster X is enrolled somewhere else: Emirates Hills, The Meadows, Al Barsha, Al Sufouh, Dubai Media City or further along Al Khail Road. That single fact shapes every tutoring decision a JLT parent makes, and almost nothing written about tutoring in this part of Dubai acknowledges it.

The practical consequence is that your child's academic day does not end when the final bell rings. It ends when the bus has worked its way through a drop-off sequence, crossed Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road in the late-afternoon direction, and reached a tower entrance where the lift is busy. Families who try to book a physics session for the time the school day ends discover within a fortnight that the slot cannot hold. Families who measure their own journey once, then build the session around the real arrival time, keep the slot for two years.

Physics is unusually sensitive to this. It is not a subject that rewards a tired half hour of reading. The work that moves an IB Physics grade is derivation, unit analysis, graph interpretation and multi-step problem solving under time pressure, and all four of those collapse when the student is running on the last of the day. A chemistry student can memorise reagents when flat. A physics student cannot derive the period of a mass-spring system from scratch when flat, and pretending otherwise wastes the hour you paid for.

The second consequence of having no school in the towers is tutor supply. A family in a villa community can sometimes find a physics teacher who lives twenty minutes away and will drive over. From a JLT tower, that pool is small, expensive once travel is priced in, and almost never contains a Higher Level physics specialist who is free at six on a weekday. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so this is not a trade-off we are asking you to make in our favour: it is the reason the online format exists. Delivering the lesson over live video means the person on the screen is chosen for teaching Physics Higher Level, not for proximity to Cluster R.

What follows is organised the way a JLT week actually runs. First the schools the towers feed and what each does to the evening. Then the physics course itself, theme by theme and paper by paper, with a note on which component suits which part of the evening. Then the scientific investigation, the market rates in dirhams, the permit rules a parent can check, and four worked week shapes you can copy. Every figure here is attributed to the source that published it, and every regulatory statement comes from a UAE government page you can open yourself.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: JLT children reach IB Physics by different routes depending on which school the bus goes to. Some have been in an IB continuum since primary and met the sciences through MYP criteria; others arrive from an IGCSE double or triple award at sixteen. The route changes what a physics tutor should be doing in the first term.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Sciences in the Middle Years Programme are assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Physics is usually taught inside an integrated sciences course rather than as a separate subject until the final year or two, so a student can reach MYP 5 having done less formal mechanics than an IGCSE peer.
programmes.countryNote: For a JLT family the MYP question is whether the child has met enough quantitative physics to choose Higher Level with confidence. Criterion C work builds genuine graph and uncertainty skills, which transfers straight into Paper 1B. What it does not build is algebraic speed under timed conditions. An MYP 5 student in this area usually needs problem-set volume rather than more investigation practice.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics sits in Group 4 and may be taken at Standard or Higher Level. The current guide organises content into five themes and three skills tools, assessed through a multiple-choice paper, a data and experimental paper, an extended-response paper and an internally assessed scientific investigation. Higher Level covers the same themes to greater depth with additional higher-level-only content in each one.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma physics students living in JLT are spread across at least six IB World Schools, which means your child's class is at a different point in the themes from the child two floors down. A tutor working with a JLT student should ask for the school's own scheme of work in the first session rather than assuming a standard order, because the sequence varies considerably between Dubai schools.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A route combining two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a core of personal and professional skills. Where physics is taken within it, the course and its assessment are identical to the Diploma version, including the scientific investigation and the same three examination papers.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Dubai schools run this route, so most JLT families will not meet it. If your child is on it, the physics workload is the same as a Diploma candidate's but the surrounding timetable has a different rhythm, and the investigation deadline is the item most often missed because the rest of the programme does not cue it.

programmes.name: The route in from IGCSE
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools around JLT run Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1, or a co-ordinated or double-award science. Each ends with a terminal written examination and, in the Cambridge case, an alternative-to-practical paper. The content overlaps the first theme or two of the Diploma course and stops well short of the rest.
programmes.countryNote: The IGCSE-to-Diploma physics step catches JLT students reliably, because the schools they attend teach the two courses in different buildings and sometimes in different years. IGCSE Physics rarely asks for calculus, almost never asks for a formal uncertainty propagation, and treats fields descriptively. Higher Level physics assumes all three within a term. That gap is the commonest reason a JLT parent searches for a tutor in October of Year 12.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: The list below breaks IB Physics into the parts a tutor is actually hired for, with the places marks leave the page. Use it to name a theme rather than booking general physics help, because naming the theme is what lets a specialist prepare the right hour.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, work, energy, momentum, and at Higher Level rigid body mechanics and the Galilean and special relativity material. Marks go on sign conventions in momentum questions, on treating energy as conserved when a resistive force is present, and on students who can quote a formula but cannot say which of two bodies the symbol refers to.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, the kinetic model, and at Higher Level the thermodynamic treatment including entropy and real-world heat engines. The common loss is unit and scale: temperatures used in degrees Celsius where kelvin is required, and specific heat capacity questions where mass is read off the stem incorrectly.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave characteristics, superposition, standing waves, the Doppler effect, and at Higher Level the full treatment of diffraction and interference. Students lose marks by describing phase in words rather than in radians, and by drawing standing-wave diagrams with the wrong number of nodes for the stated harmonic.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, electric cells and circuits, magnetic effects of currents, and at Higher Level induction, capacitance and orbital motion. This is the theme JLT students most often ask for help with. The losses are conceptual rather than arithmetic: potential confused with field strength, and induction answers that omit the direction of the induced effect.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Structure of the atom, radioactive decay, fission and fusion, and at Higher Level the quantum material including the photoelectric effect and the standard model of particles. Marks go missing on decay-equation bookkeeping, on binding energy per nucleon read off a graph in the wrong units, and on photoelectric answers that describe intensity where frequency is the variable.

subjects.name: Paper 1A: multiple choice
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper covering the whole syllabus with no mark for working. It rewards fast estimation, confident unit reasoning and a willingness to eliminate rather than solve. Students trained only on long-form questions routinely run out of time here, and the fix is timed practice at a per-question pace rather than more content revision.

subjects.name: Paper 1B: data and experimental
subjects.description: Questions built on unfamiliar data sets and experimental scenarios, drawing on the skills tools rather than on recall. It asks students to linearise a relationship, handle uncertainty, judge a method and comment on a graph. It is the component where strong classroom students most often underperform, because it cannot be revised from a textbook.

subjects.name: Paper 2: extended response
subjects.description: Short and extended written questions mixing calculation with explanation. Command terms carry the marks: explain, outline, discuss and justify each require a different shape of answer, and a correct number written under the wrong command term still scores poorly. Higher Level questions chain three or four steps where Standard Level questions chain two.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: An individual investigation written up as a report and marked against four criteria out of twenty-four marks in total, carrying a fifth of the subject grade. The criteria reward a research question with a clear independent variable, raw data properly processed, a conclusion tied back to published values, and an evaluation that names specific methodological weaknesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics required by physics
subjects.description: Logarithmic plots, small-angle approximations, vector resolution, gradient and area interpretation, and at Higher Level a working comfort with rates of change. A physics tutor often spends the first fortnight on this rather than on physics, especially with students who took Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Practical skills and the tools
subjects.description: The three skills tools cover experimental technique, technology including spreadsheets and simulation, and the mathematics listed above. They are examined inside Paper 1B and assessed inside the investigation, so they are never a separate revision topic and are therefore the thing students skip. Deliberate practice on them pays disproportionately.

regions.note: A short hop across Sheikh Zayed Road from JLT and home to one of the nearer British-curriculum primaries. Families here often have a younger child at a school JLT families also use, so sibling drop-off timing is the constraint rather than the journey length.

regions.note: Two of the IB World Schools JLT Diploma students attend sit on this edge of Emirates Living. The journey is short in distance and unpredictable in time because it runs against the afternoon flow on Al Khail Road and through gated community traffic.

sections.heading: What a JLT address actually commits your evening to
paragraphs: Start with the geography, because it is the thing that decides whether a tutoring arrangement survives. JLT is built as lettered clusters of towers around three lakes, bounded by Sheikh Zayed Road on one side and Al Khail Road on the other, with Metro stations at either end. It is residential and commercial. It has nurseries and early-years provision, and it does not have an IB Diploma school. Secondary students leave the community every morning and return to it every afternoon.

That return is where the planning goes wrong. Parents tend to anchor a tutoring slot to the school's published finish time, which is the one number the school advertises. The number that matters is different: it is the time your own child, on your own route, with your own stop position, walks through the door. Between those two numbers sit the bus loading sequence, the drop-off order, one of two major arterial roads in the afternoon direction, and a tower lift at the busiest point of its day.

The gap between the two is not a constant. It is longer when the route serves JBR or Discovery Gardens after JLT, longer again when Al Khail Road has a diversion, and shorter when a parent drives the Al Sufouh leg themselves. It also changes between terms, because transport offices re-cut routes when enrolment shifts. A family that measures once in September and once in January has better information than any generic timing advice, including this page's.

The table below is a checklist for that measurement, not a set of timings we have invented. Fill the last column in yourself for your own route, then set the session after that time with a buffer, and the slot will hold for the year. Set it before that time and you will be rescheduling by the third week, which is the single commonest reason a tutoring arrangement in this part of Dubai quietly stops.

sections.heading: Which part of physics the hour can carry, and which it cannot
paragraphs: Once you know when your child is actually at a desk, the useful question becomes what physics can be done then. This is not a wellbeing point. Different components of this course make different demands on working memory, and the components that make the heaviest demands are the ones that move grades. Spending a late, tired hour on the wrong component is how families conclude that tutoring does not work for their child.

Derivation is the heaviest. Producing the expression for the period of a simple pendulum, or deriving the relationship between orbital radius and period from first principles, requires holding three or four algebraic steps in mind while checking the dimensions of each. That is hard at four in the afternoon and close to impossible at nine at night. The same is true of Paper 2 extended questions, where the student must carry information from part (a) into part (d) without rereading the stem.

The lighter work is real work too, and it is what a late hour should contain. Checking a multiple-choice set against the answers and writing one line on why each wrong option was tempting. Reading a marked script and tagging each lost mark with a reason code. Drawing and labelling field patterns. Rehearsing command terms by writing three-mark answers to prompts without doing the calculation. None of this is filler and all of it survives tiredness.

The table sets this out component by component so a parent can match the slot to the work rather than hoping. If your measured arrival time puts the session late, do not shorten the course: move the heavy components to a weekend morning and use the weekday hour for the lighter ones. Most JLT families who get two years out of a tutoring arrangement are running exactly that split.

sections.heading: Theme D is where JLT students ask for help, and why
paragraphs: Across the physics enquiries that come from this part of Dubai, fields is the theme named most often, and it is named at a particular moment: a few weeks after the class has moved on from it. That pattern is informative. Fields is not difficult to follow in a lesson. It is difficult to retain, because the theme contains four distinct field types, two potential concepts, and a sign convention that flips depending on which quantity you are discussing.

The specific confusions are consistent enough to name. Field strength and potential are treated as versions of the same idea, so students divide when they should multiply and lose the whole chain. Gravitational potential is described as negative without any account of why the zero is at infinity. Electric circuit questions are answered with memorised formulae rather than by tracing which component the current actually passes through. At Higher Level, induction answers give a magnitude and omit the direction, and the direction is where the mark sits.

None of that is fixed by rereading the chapter. It is fixed by building the student's own one-page map of the theme, in their handwriting, with the two potentials on it and the sign of each stated, then testing it against past questions until the map stops needing corrections. A tutor can do that in three or four sessions with a student who has the content in their notes already, which is the usual position by the time a parent gets in touch.

The reason this matters for a JLT family specifically is scheduling. Fields sits in the middle of the two-year course for most Dubai schools, which means the request arrives in a term that is already crowded with the scientific investigation and the first serious mock. If you can see that fields is the weak theme in November rather than in April, three sessions in a quiet fortnight will do what six sessions in a loud one cannot.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, and the month it needs rather than the term
paragraphs: A fifth of the physics grade is internally assessed through an individual investigation, written up against four criteria worth twenty-four marks in total. The criteria reward a research question with a genuinely manipulable independent variable, raw data presented before any processing, a conclusion compared against a published value or accepted relationship, and an evaluation that names specific weaknesses in the student's own method rather than listing generic sources of error.

What goes wrong is nearly always the research question, and it goes wrong early. A student picks a topic that interests them and discovers four weeks in that the independent variable cannot be varied enough to produce a trend, or that the dependent variable cannot be measured with the equipment available. By then the deadline is close and the write-up is built on data that will not support a conclusion. A single hour spent testing the viability of a question before any apparatus is touched saves the whole exercise.

The boundary on what help is permitted matters more here than anywhere else on this page. A tutor may teach the criteria, discuss whether a question is viable, explain uncertainty propagation, show how to linearise a relationship, and give written feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor must never write the investigation, supply the data, or rewrite a paragraph into its final form. We state that in writing at the start of any investigation support so that the school can see the help was legitimate if it is ever asked.

Practically, the investigation needs one concentrated month rather than a thin term. For a JLT student the month to protect is the one where the weekday evenings are shortest, because the work is spreadsheet-heavy and graph-heavy and suits a weekend morning block better than a tired hour. Families who schedule two long weekend sessions for the processing and analysis, and keep the weekday slot for the examined course, finish the report without losing ground in the taught content.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs around the JLT towers, in dirhams
paragraphs: Price is the one thing this cluster of search results refuses to discuss. Of the competitor pages reviewed in October 2026, three published no hourly figure at all and two quoted in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family pays a tutor in. So here are the published dirham figures, each attached to the provider that published it, as read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price list.

Begin at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where the decision usually starts. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, both of which buy a general tutor rather than a Higher Level physics specialist. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work at AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED's premium named tutors at AED 650.

The in-home comparison is the figure worth reading carefully. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and home tutors generally at AED 200 to 500, with travel built into the rate. For a JLT tower, that premium buys a journey through two arterial roads and a visitors' car park, not more teaching. It also narrows your choice to whoever can make that journey before seven, which in Higher Level physics is a very short list. IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

Monthly packages are quoted too, and they are the clearest way to compare. The market shows around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Set that against the KHDA confirmation of 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, and a tutoring line in the household budget is at least a stable number this year.

sections.heading: Four JLT week shapes, and when each one is the right answer
paragraphs: Generic advice about session frequency is useless in this community because the journeys differ so much. A student at a school in Al Sufouh and a student at a school in Al Barsha both live in JLT and have completely different evenings. So here are four shapes, each built from a real constraint, and the signal that tells you which one is yours.

The short-route shape is the simplest. If your child is home within forty minutes of the final bell and that is stable across the week, a six o'clock weekday slot works and will hold. Run one hour weekly against the school's scheme of work, use it for Paper 2 practice and new derivations, and keep a second shorter slot in reserve for the term the investigation is due.

The long-route shape inverts it. If the measured arrival is late and variable, stop trying to force a weekday hour and move the main session to a weekend morning of ninety minutes to two hours. Use the extra length properly: a timed Paper 1B section, then its review, then a derivation block. Leave the weekday evenings for the light work described earlier, which the student can do without a tutor present.

The two shapes left are the crowded-activity shape and the examination-term shape. Where swimming, football or music occupies three weekday evenings, the realistic answer is one weekend session plus one short midweek review rather than two full evening hours that will be cancelled. And in the final examination term, when study leave begins and the school day shortens, the whole pattern should move to mornings, which is the only period of a JLT student's two years when the best hours of the day are actually available.
