sections.heading: Is the tutor two towers away legally permitted to teach your child?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is worth knowing before you hire someone informally through a building group chat. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students.

The route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with no fee stated and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are, in the government's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published, so any page quoting you a figure is quoting something unverified.

There is a second rule that matters more than families expect. A teacher at your child's own school tutoring your own child privately is the arrangement parents ask for most often and the one that carries the most risk. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document, but do not build a plan around it.

A separate thing entirely is a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai, which requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not hold that permit, does not operate premises in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board. We are an independent tutor-matching platform, and saying so plainly is more useful to you than a badge nobody can verify.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside a physics timetable
paragraphs: Something no competitor page in this cluster mentions: your child's physics revision is competing with mandatory subjects that sit outside the IB programme entirely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details help a parent plan. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it advises that any mandatory-subject lesson lasts at least twenty-five minutes. Schools are required to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which is why tutoring in these subjects follows the school's material rather than an outside scheme.

What this means for a JLT physics plan is simply arithmetic. Those lessons occupy timetable space and carry their own assessments, so a Diploma student's week has less slack than the subject list suggests. If your child is also sitting an Arabic assessment in the fortnight you planned for physics past papers, move the physics. We can stream Arabic support separately where a family wants it, following the school's own material, and the two plans should be made in the same conversation rather than in two.

sections.heading: Getting started from a JLT tower, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The first message is short and it decides the quality of everything after it. Send the level, Standard or Higher, the school and year group, the themes already taught, the component where marks are going, and two evening windows that work after your measured arrival time. If you can add photographs of the last two marked assessments with the teacher's annotations visible, the trial lesson becomes diagnostic rather than introductory.

We then match a physics specialist at that level and offer a free trial lesson, online, with no payment and no card details taken. Watch two things during it. Does the tutor work from your child's own lost marks or from a generic worksheet? And does your child talk during the hour? A student who is silent through a trial is a signal worth acting on immediately rather than after a month.

Sometimes the honest answer is that nobody suitable is free in your window. Higher Level physics in a six o'clock Gulf Standard Time slot is the most contested combination we handle, and when it is full we say so and offer either a different time or a date when the slot opens. We do not substitute a general science tutor into a Higher Level physics brief. A mismatched specialist costs a term, and a Diploma student does not get the term back.

After the match, the arrangement is reviewed against the error log rather than against how the sessions felt. Every four to six weeks, look at whether the losses in a named theme have stopped appearing. If they have, the work there is done and the focus should move. If nothing has shifted in six weeks, change the approach or change the tutor rather than extending the booking out of politeness. That review habit is what separates two useful years from two expensive ones.

process.title: Measure one journey home
process.description: Before you ask anyone for a slot, time your own child's route once from final bell to desk. Note the stop position on the bus order if you can get it from the transport office. That one number is worth more than any advice about session timing, including everything on this page, because it is the only version that is true for your route.

process.title: Name the level and the component
process.description: Tell us Standard or Higher Level, the themes covered so far, and whether the marks are going in Paper 1A, Paper 1B, Paper 2 or the investigation. Add the school and the examination session your child is working towards. This is what lets us match a physics specialist rather than a general science tutor.

process.title: Send the marked work
process.description: The last two marked assessments and the most recent mock, with annotations visible. Photographs from a phone are fine. A tutor who has read marked work before the trial arrives with a hypothesis about where the marks are going, which turns the first hour into a diagnosis instead of an introduction.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full lesson online, with no payment and no card details. The trial is the point at which you judge whether the tutor teaches from your child's errors and whether your child engages. Both are visible within twenty minutes, and neither can be judged from a profile page.

process.title: Fix the slot after the arrival time
process.description: Agree a weekly time that sits safely after the journey, with a buffer, and agree what happens between sessions: a short problem set, an error log entry, or a timed paper section. The cycle matters more than the length of the lesson, and a slot that holds for two years beats a longer one that collapses in October.

process.title: Review against the log every six weeks
process.description: Look at whether named losses have stopped appearing rather than at whether the hour felt productive. Move the focus when a theme is fixed. Change the approach or the tutor if six weeks have produced no change in the pattern, instead of letting the arrangement continue by default.

whyPoints.title: Matched on level and theme, not on distance
whyPoints.description: Because the lesson runs over live video, the person teaching your child is selected for having taught Physics Higher Level to examination rather than for living near Cluster R. From a JLT tower that difference is the whole value, since the pool of specialists who can physically reach the towers by six is very small.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built on your measured journey
whyPoints.description: We set the slot after the time your child actually walks in, not after the school's published finish time. It is a small change and it is the reason tutoring arrangements in this community survive past the third week instead of quietly stopping.

whyPoints.title: Component-level diagnosis
whyPoints.description: Physics grades are lost in identifiable components, not in the subject as a whole. We ask for marked scripts first so the work starts from your child's own lost marks, and so a Paper 1B weakness is treated as a skills problem rather than as a reason to reread the textbook.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on investigation help
whyPoints.description: Support on the scientific investigation means teaching the criteria, discussing viability and giving written feedback on your child's own draft. It never means writing it, supplying data or rewriting a paragraph into final form. We put that boundary in writing so the school can see the help was legitimate.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check yourself
whyPoints.description: Every dirham range on this page is attributed to the provider that published it with the month it was read, and every regulatory statement comes from a UAE government page. Nothing here is a statistic we generated about ourselves, because an unverifiable number is worth nothing to a parent making a decision.

whyPoints.title: A straight answer when the slot is full
whyPoints.description: Higher Level physics in an early-evening Gulf Standard Time slot is our most contested combination. When it is full we tell you and offer an alternative time or a date, rather than filling the brief with a generalist. Disclosing the limit is more useful than concealing it.

faqs.question: Where do JLT students sit IB Physics, given there is no Diploma school in the towers?
faqs.answer: Jumeirah Lakes Towers has nurseries and early-years provision but no IB Diploma school, so every Diploma physics student living here travels out. The schools JLT families most often use sit in Emirates Hills, The Meadows, Al Barsha, Al Sufouh and Dubai Media City, with a few further along Sheikh Zayed Road. The practical consequence is that your child's class is at a different point in the five themes from the child two floors down, so a tutor should ask for your school's own scheme of work in the first session rather than assuming a standard order of teaching.

faqs.question: What time can a physics session start if my child buses back to JLT from Al Barsha?
faqs.answer: Measure it rather than estimate it. The Al Barsha school cluster is the largest in the city and the drop-off sequences are long, so the gap between the final bell and your child reaching a desk is wider on this route than on most. Time one real journey, note whether JLT is early or late in your bus order, then set the session after that time with a buffer. Families on this corridor often end up with a weekend morning as the main session and a shorter weekday slot for lighter review work, which holds better than forcing an early evening hour.

faqs.question: How many evenings a week does IB Physics Higher Level realistically need?
faqs.answer: Most Higher Level students we support start with one session a week and add a second only for a specific reason: an investigation month, a Paper 1B block, or the final examination term. Two full sessions a week from the start usually means the work is being spread thin rather than targeted. What matters more than frequency is the cycle around the session, which is a short problem set between lessons and a marked script read at the start of the next one. A single well-used hour with that cycle beats two hours without it.

faqs.question: Which of the five IB Physics themes causes the most trouble for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Fields is the theme named most often in enquiries from this part of Dubai, and usually a few weeks after the class has moved past it. The content follows easily in a lesson and is hard to retain, because it holds four field types, two potential concepts and a sign convention that changes with the quantity being discussed. The specific confusions are field strength treated as the same idea as potential, gravitational potential described as negative without explaining where the zero sits, and Higher Level induction answers that give a magnitude and leave out the direction.

faqs.question: Can Paper 1B data and uncertainty work be taught properly over video?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arguably better than in person, because the work is screen-based anyway. Paper 1B uses unfamiliar data sets and experimental scenarios, so the session involves a spreadsheet, a graph and a published mark scheme on a shared screen with both people annotating. A tutor can linearise a relationship live, show the uncertainty carried through each step, and have the student redo it immediately. What video cannot replace is handling apparatus, which is what the school laboratory is for. Confirm the current paper structure against your school's IB subject guide, since the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: Are physics derivations workable on a shared whiteboard, or does my child need paper?
faqs.answer: Both, and the good version uses both. The student works on paper and holds it to the camera, or writes directly on the shared whiteboard with a stylus while the tutor annotates in a second colour. What matters is that the tutor can see the working and not just the answer, because a derivation loses marks at the step that was skipped rather than at the final line. Sessions end with the annotated whiteboard saved and sent, which gives the student a record of their own derivation rather than a textbook version of it.

faqs.question: When should the IB Physics scientific investigation actually start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most students start it, and the critical hour is before any apparatus is touched. The commonest failure is a research question whose independent variable cannot be varied enough to produce a trend, discovered four weeks in when the deadline is close. Spend one session testing viability: can the variable be changed across a useful range, can the dependent variable be measured with the equipment available, and is there a published value or relationship to compare the conclusion against? Get those three right and the write-up needs one concentrated month rather than a thin term.

faqs.question: My child is strong in lessons and loses marks in Paper 2. What causes that?
faqs.answer: Almost always command terms rather than physics. Paper 2 asks students to explain, outline, discuss, justify, determine and describe, and each demands a different shape of answer. A correct calculation written under a command term that asked for an explanation scores poorly, and the student leaves the examination believing they did well. The second cause is information carried across linked parts: a four-part question expects part (a) data to be used in part (d) without rereading the stem. Both are trainable in a few sessions using past questions and the published mark schemes.

faqs.question: Does a physics tutor need a UAE permit to teach a child living in JLT?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated through the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

faqs.question: Should a physics session sit before or after dinner in a JLT household?
faqs.answer: Before, if your measured arrival time allows it, because the components that move a physics grade are the ones that need working memory. Derivations, Paper 2 extended questions and Paper 1B analysis all degrade sharply when a student is running on the last of the day. If the journey makes an early slot impossible, do not shorten the course: move the heavy work to a weekend morning and use the late weekday hour for marked-script review, error tagging, field-pattern diagrams and timed multiple choice, all of which survive tiredness.

faqs.question: How do we fit physics around three committed evenings of sport and music?
faqs.answer: With one weekend session and one short midweek review, rather than two weekday hours that will be cancelled. A ninety-minute to two-hour weekend block carries a timed Paper 1B section, its full review and a derivation block, which is more than two tired evening hours achieve. The midweek slot then becomes twenty-five to thirty minutes of error tagging and recall, which the student can partly do alone. Cutting an activity to make room is rarely the right first move, because the activity is usually what makes the rest of the week tolerable.

faqs.question: What do physics tutors charge per hour around Jumeirah Lakes Towers?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai figures read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online end, where EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 table puts specialist IB and IGCSE work at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium named tutors at AED 650. In-home visiting rates sit at AED 180 to 500 because travel is priced in. Those are other providers' numbers, not ours.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IB Physics and Mathematics Analysis for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The overlap is real: logarithmic plots, vector resolution, gradient and area interpretation, and rates of change all appear in both courses. A tutor who teaches Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Physics Higher Level can use one to reinforce the other and saves you a slot in a crowded week. What you should not accept is a general science or general maths tutor covering both, because the component-level work in each subject needs someone who has taught it to examination.

faqs.question: What happens to physics sessions during Ramadan and study leave?
faqs.answer: Both are scheduling changes rather than pauses. During Ramadan the school day shortens and sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot or to a late morning, and the content should move with the slot: lighter recall work when energy is low, heavier derivation work in the morning. Study leave is the opposite and the best news in a JLT student's two years, because mornings finally become available. That is the period to run full past papers under timed conditions and review them mark scheme by mark scheme, which no term-time evening slot can accommodate.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level physics specialist is free in the slot we want?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and offer either a different time or a date when the slot opens. Higher Level physics in an early-evening Gulf Standard Time window is the most contested combination we handle, and the honest version of that is more useful to you than a quiet substitution. We will not put a general science tutor into a Higher Level physics brief, because a mismatched specialist costs a term of a two-year programme and that term cannot be recovered. If the wait is long, we say how long rather than leaving the enquiry open.

faqs.question: How do we book a free trial physics lesson from a JLT address?
faqs.answer: Send five things: the level, Standard or Higher; the school and year group; the themes taught so far; the component where marks are going; and two evening windows that work after your measured arrival time. Add photographs of the last two marked assessments if you have them. We match a physics specialist at that level and the trial lesson runs online, in full, with no payment and no card details taken. During it, watch whether the tutor works from your child's own errors and whether your child talks.

intro.heading: Physics marks are awarded by a mark scheme, so that is where the teaching starts
paragraphs: A Diploma Physics grade is produced by three things: a multiple-choice and data paper, a written paper, and a 24-mark scientific investigation. Each is marked against a published scheme with specific, repeatable behaviours. A student who understands the physics and does not know those behaviours loses marks every single paper, and the loss is invisible in class because class discussion rewards understanding rather than the written form an examiner can credit.

That is why this page is organised around the assessment rather than around the syllabus. The five themes of the 2023 guide - space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics - are the content, and the Higher Level extensions sit inside the same five. What separates a 5 from a 7 is rarely a missing theme. It is a student writing two points where the command term wanted three, quoting a gradient without its unit, or propagating an uncertainty by addition when the quantities multiplied.

Paper 1 is split in two. Paper 1A is multiple choice, and Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions common to both levels. Paper 1B is reliably the least-practised component in a school course, because it does not map onto a topic and so it does not fit neatly into a scheme of work. Together they carry 36 per cent of the grade. Paper 2, with its short-answer and extended-response questions, carries 44 per cent, and the scientific investigation carries the remaining 20.

Jumeirah 1 students mostly travel out to school. Jumeirah Baccalaureate School sits inside the district and runs the Diploma, but the physics cohort on this page is also at Raffles World Academy in Umm Suqeim, Emirates International School in Umm Al Sheif, Dubai International Academy in Al Barsha and Dubai American Academy, and the bus home down Al Wasl or the beach road lands most of them between 15:45 and 16:45. A 17:00 or 18:30 session holds through a term; an earlier one does not.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Jumeirah 1 address, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. For physics that format is a genuine advantage rather than a concession: a derivation can be written line by line on a shared whiteboard while the original question stays visible beside it, a graph can be annotated without redrawing it, and the recording can be rewatched the week of the paper. What it removes is the drive, and the limit that a tutor has to live nearby.

The sections that follow are practical. A table of command terms and what a full-mark answer to each contains. The recurring traps theme by theme. The uncertainty rules. The derivations the course expects. A phased past-paper programme. Then the Dubai market rates, with their sources, and the academic-honesty boundary around the investigation, which matters more in physics than families expect.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: Physics arrives in a Dubai student's timetable through one of a few routes, and the route decides what the first sessions have to repair. The five stages below are the ones that matter for a Jumeirah 1 family, with a note on each about what Dubai schools actually do rather than what the programme describes.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences, integrated
programmes.description: Physics inside integrated sciences, assessed against four MYP criteria rather than against a content syllabus. Students are marked on knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The upside is that experimental design and data processing are taught early. The gap is content coverage: a strong MYP science student may arrive at the Diploma having never met a free-body diagram or a logarithmic scale.
programmes.countryNote: At Dubai IB continuum schools, including Jumeirah Baccalaureate School and Raffles World Academy, the move from MYP Year 5 into Diploma Physics is the commonest reason a Jumeirah 1 family looks for help in October of DP1. The criterion marking a student has learned to satisfy does not match what a Paper 2 scheme rewards, and that mismatch reads to a parent as a sudden drop in ability.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics 0625 or 4PH1 before the Diploma
programmes.description: The British-school route, with a content syllabus, a practical component and a grade on either the A*-G or the 9-1 scale. It teaches more physics content than MYP but with fewer marks for experimental design and almost none for uncertainty. Students arriving in the Diploma from here are usually strong on recall and weak on the two things Paper 1B tests: processing real data and judging how good it is.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah College, Dubai College and the other British schools serving the Jumeirah corridor feed A Level rather than the Diploma, so a student moving from IGCSE into Diploma Physics has usually also changed school. That means a new scheme of work, a new teacher and a new assessment model in the same September, and the physics is rarely the hardest part of it.

programmes.name: Diploma Physics Standard Level
programmes.description: The five themes at Standard Level, with Paper 1 of ninety minutes and Paper 2 of ninety minutes, plus the scientific investigation. The content is substantial but the questions are shorter, and the marks concentrate on clear single-step reasoning, correct units and a defensible number. Standard Level punishes vagueness more than it punishes ignorance: an answer that gestures at the physics without naming a mechanism scores nothing.
programmes.countryNote: Standard Level Physics is the common choice in Dubai for a student taking Chemistry or Biology at Higher Level and needing a third science that does not consume the week. The decision point is usually February of DP1, which is also when the investigation work begins, and the two conversations should happen together rather than separately.

programmes.name: Diploma Physics Higher Level
programmes.description: The same five themes with additional depth and extension content, a two-hour Paper 1 and a two-and-a-half-hour Paper 2. The additional material is concentrated in fields, rotational and relativistic mechanics, and quantum physics, and the extended-response questions in Paper 2 expect sustained reasoning across several marks. Mathematical fluency becomes the quiet gate: logarithms, small-angle approximations, vectors and calculus-adjacent reasoning all appear.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students aiming at engineering or physical sciences, in the UAE or abroad, usually need Physics at Higher Level, and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches alongside it is the combination most admissions pages assume. Taking Higher Level Physics with Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is possible and is done, but the field and oscillation work costs noticeably more tutoring hours in that pairing.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: TOK, Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are assessed alongside the six subjects and together contribute up to three points. A physics Extended Essay is a research question answered with the student's own data or analysis, and it is the piece most likely to collide with an academic-honesty boundary because the physics is genuinely hard and the temptation to outsource is real.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools set internal Extended Essay deadlines well ahead of the submission window, usually with a first full draft due in DP2 autumn term. For a physics essay that means the experimental work has to be finished during DP1 summer, which is exactly when a Jumeirah 1 family is travelling. Planning the data collection before the holiday is the single most useful piece of advice on this page.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: Physics is the subject this page is about, but a physics problem is often a maths problem wearing a different coat, and a Diploma timetable is bought as a package. The grid below is the set a Jumeirah 1 household most often needs alongside it, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E on the 2023 guide, Paper 1A and 1B at 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44, the scientific investigation at 20. Teaching concentrates on command terms, uncertainty arithmetic and the written form a mark scheme can credit.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route that carries Higher Level Physics most comfortably. Calculus, trigonometric identities, logarithms and proof. Students lose marks in the unstructured questions, where no part (a) tells them which tool the examiner had in mind.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-led solutions. Workable alongside Physics, but the field, oscillation and logarithmic work in Higher Level Physics has to be taught rather than assumed, which usually costs extra sessions in DP1.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity on the current guide, with the same assessment shape as Physics: Paper 1A and 1B, Paper 2, and a 24-mark investigation. Students who have learned uncertainty rules in Physics carry them straight into Chemistry data questions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, continuity and change. The lightest calculation load of the three sciences and the heaviest on command-term precision, where describe, explain and suggest earn different answers.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Systems fundamentals, computational thinking and the internal assessment project. Physics students often take it as a sixth subject and then discover the project and the scientific investigation share the same DP1 summer.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Design cycle, materials and the design project. Overlaps usefully with Physics on mechanics, stress and material properties, and its own internal assessment is larger than most students expect at the point they choose it.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Anatomy, physiology and biomechanics, with a scientific investigation of the same shape as Physics. Popular in Dubai as a third science and often chosen without anyone checking its own data-handling demands.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary subject that can satisfy either group 3 or group 4. Useful for a student who needs a science without the mathematical load, though its systems diagrams and data questions are more demanding than the reputation suggests.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy, plus three internal assessment commentaries. The quantitative marks reward a student who can handle a percentage change and a simple elasticity calculation without a calculator.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the individual oral and the HL essay. The component most physics students underestimate, because Paper 1 is a timed skill rather than a body of content.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three points on the diploma total. Support is process coaching: framing a knowledge question, choosing a research question narrow enough to answer, planning data collection, and reading drafts to say what is not yet justified.

sections.heading: What the mark scheme actually pays for
paragraphs: Every question in Diploma Physics opens with a command term, and the command term is an instruction about the form of the answer, not a synonym for the word think. State wants one line. Outline wants two creditable points. Explain wants a cause, a mechanism and a consequence. Deduce wants the evidence, the physics that links it and then the conclusion, in that order. A student who writes a beautiful explanation where the paper asked them to state has spent four minutes earning one mark.

This is the cheapest improvement available in the subject, and it is almost never taught explicitly. Classroom physics rewards understanding demonstrated out loud; the paper rewards a written structure. The gap between the two is where most of the marks sit for a student already scoring a 5. Working through a marked script question by question, naming the command term and counting whether the answer contains that many distinct creditable points, usually recovers marks within two sessions.

The table below is the version of this we work from. It is not a glossary - the IB publishes one of those and it should be read - but a map from the term to the shape of a full-mark answer. The right-hand column is the useful one: it says what has to be physically present on the page. A student can self-mark against it, which matters because self-marking is the habit that makes independent past-paper work worth anything.

Two command terms deserve particular attention in physics. Show that means the answer is given and the marks are for the route, so every algebraic step has to be written even when it feels obvious; students who jump three lines lose two of the three marks. And sketch means axes labelled with quantity and unit, intercepts marked, asymptotes indicated - a shape with no labels earns nothing at all, however correct the curve.

sections.heading: Reading a physics question backwards
paragraphs: Strong physics students lose marks by starting at the first word and working forwards. The more reliable attack starts at the end. Read what the question wants, in what unit, to what precision. Then read the data given, and notice which quantities are supplied, because an examiner rarely supplies a number that is not used. Only then decide which relationship connects the two. The physics is usually the shortest part of the process.

This matters most in Paper 2, where multi-part questions are built so that part (c) depends on part (a). A student who misreads part (a) carries the error forward, and although mark schemes allow error carried forward, the method marks for part (c) are only available if the method is visible. Writing a method line before substituting any number is therefore worth marks independently of whether the arithmetic is right, and it is a habit that can be installed in one session and drilled in two.

The second half of the technique is units and figures. A physics answer is a number, a unit and a justified precision. Marks are lost for a gradient quoted without its unit, for an answer given to five significant figures from data supplied to two, and for a final value that has not been checked against the physical sense of the situation - an acceleration of 400 metres per second squared for a falling ball should stop a student rather than be written down.

Students in Jumeirah 1 schools arrive at this from two directions. Those from MYP Sciences are good at designing an investigation and weak at the compressed written answer a Diploma paper wants. Those from IGCSE are good at recall and weak at reading data they have not been told how to use. The attack above fixes both, because it moves the student's attention from what they know to what the question is paying for.

sections.heading: The traps that recur in the question bank, theme by theme
paragraphs: The 2023 guide organises physics into five themes, and each has a small number of recurring places where marks disappear. These are not the hardest ideas in the theme. They are the places where a plausible-looking answer is wrong in a way the mark scheme catches every time, which is why they repeat across sessions and across schools.

In theme A, graph reading does most of the damage: a velocity-time graph read as though it were a displacement-time graph, or the area under a curve confused with its gradient. The fix is mechanical. Before any calculation, the student annotates the axes with what the gradient represents and what the area represents. It takes ten seconds and removes a whole class of error. Theme B's version is energy accounting, where specific heat capacity and specific latent heat are used interchangeably inside one mixed calculation.

Theme C turns on phase, where a difference quoted in radians is offered to a question that asked for a fraction of a cycle, or the other way round. Theme D is the theme Dubai students name most often, and the trap there is conceptual rather than careless: potential and potential energy are different quantities, the negative sign in the gravitational case is physics rather than decoration, and an answer that drops it is marked wrong. Theme E's recurring loss is reading total binding energy from a graph whose axis is binding energy per nucleon.

Across all five, Paper 1B adds experimental technique, and the single biggest loss there is uncertainty propagated by the wrong rule. That has its own section below because it is worth the space: it is examined directly, it is rarely drilled in school, and it is the part of the subject where a few hours of deliberate practice produce the most reliable mark gain.

sections.heading: Derivations the course expects, and the ones it does not
paragraphs: Physics students waste time memorising derivations the paper will never ask for, and are then caught by the handful it does. The distinction is worth drawing explicitly, because it changes what revision looks like in the last month. A show that question is a derivation with the answer printed, and the marks are for the steps. Those steps are therefore the ones worth rehearsing until they can be written without thought.

The reliably examined ones sit in a short list. The suvat relationships from a velocity-time graph, because the graph argument is the physics. Centripetal acceleration expressed through angular velocity. The ideal gas relation assembled from the separate gas laws. The relationship between field strength and potential gradient. Simple harmonic motion defined from the restoring-force condition and then solved. The mass-energy relation applied to a binding-energy calculation. Each is short, each appears in multiple past series, and each is worth a guaranteed two or three marks when it does.

What is not examined as a derivation is anything the data booklet supplies in finished form and the course treats as a tool. A student who spends an evening reproducing a result the booklet gives them has revised nothing. The better use of that evening is the opposite exercise: taking a relationship from the booklet and practising substituting into it under time pressure, with units, from awkward data.

The practical method in a session is to work from past series. A question is read, the command term identified, and if it is show that, the student writes every line including the ones that feel too obvious to write. The commonest loss in this category is a student who moves from the second line to the fifth because the algebra was clear in their head. The mark scheme cannot see a student's head, and that is the entire lesson.

sections.heading: Uncertainty arithmetic: the rules Paper 1B assesses directly
paragraphs: Paper 1B is a set of data-based and experimental questions common to Standard and Higher Level, and a large share of its marks are for handling uncertainty correctly. This is the most reliably under-taught part of the Diploma Physics course, for an understandable reason: it does not belong to a theme, so it does not appear as a unit in a scheme of work. It appears in the exam regardless.

The rules are few and they are mechanical. An instrument reading carries half its smallest division, or the resolution the question states. Repeated readings carry half the range. Quantities that are added or subtracted have their absolute uncertainties added - including when they are subtracted, which is the step students get wrong. Quantities multiplied or divided have their fractional or percentage uncertainties added. A quantity raised to a power has its fractional uncertainty multiplied by that power, which is why a volume or an inverse-square relationship carries a much larger uncertainty than students expect.

Graph work has its own rule. The uncertainty in a gradient comes from drawing maximum and minimum lines through the error bars and taking half the difference of their gradients. A student who draws one line of best fit and estimates has not answered the question asked. Error bars themselves must be plotted from the uncertainties, not sketched, and a line drawn outside them is evidence the student has not understood what the bars mean.

The final rule is presentation, and it is worth a mark on its own: round the uncertainty to one significant figure, then quote the value to the matching decimal place. An answer of 9.81457 plus or minus 0.3 is self-contradictory and is marked as such. Four or five hours of deliberate practice across these rules is, in our experience of marked scripts, the highest-yield block of work available to a Diploma Physics student who already understands the physics.

sections.heading: A past-paper programme that is more than doing papers
paragraphs: Most students who say they have done past papers mean they have attempted questions and looked at answers. That produces familiarity and very little else. A past-paper programme that changes a grade has phases, and each phase has a different purpose, a different level of support and a different way of being marked. The sequence below is what we run, and it takes about ten weeks at one session a week with independent work between.

The early phases are deliberately easy. Topic-only questions, untimed, with notes open, exist to answer one question: is this a content gap or a command-term gap? Those are different problems and a student cannot tell them apart alone. The same questions closed-book and timed at roughly a mark a minute then convert understanding into recall. Only after that do mixed papers make sense, because a mixed paper attempted too early tells a student they are bad at physics rather than telling them anything useful.

Paper 1B gets its own phase. It is the component least practised at school, it carries uncertainty and graph marks that nothing else in the course assesses, and it responds unusually well to concentrated work. A student who has never systematically worked through Paper 1B questions from several series is leaving a predictable block of marks on the table, and that block is the same size regardless of how strong the rest of their physics is.

The last phase is the one that gets skipped, and it is the one that proves the programme worked. Questions the student previously failed come back cold, weeks later, unannounced. If a fix held, it shows here. If it did not, that is worth knowing in March rather than in the examination hall. Official past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB and are referenced through the school's own legitimate access rather than redistributed.

sections.heading: Where Jumeirah 1 students sit Physics, and what their school changes
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with UK curriculum schools at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. That last figure is the one that shapes this page: Diploma Physics is a minority route in Dubai, taught in a limited number of schools, and the ones a Jumeirah 1 family can reach are concentrated in Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha.

Which school a student attends changes the first month of tutoring more than their ability does. A student from an IB continuum school has come through MYP Sciences, assessed against four criteria, and is comfortable designing an investigation while being unused to the compressed written answers a Diploma paper wants. A student who moved in from a British school has IGCSE Physics behind them, which means strong recall and almost no experience of uncertainty arithmetic. Both are normal. They need different first sessions.

Dubai's sector is also still growing, which matters for families choosing schools alongside tutoring. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened in 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. KHDA also confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

KHDA inspection reports are public and worth reading, with one caveat. The six-band overall rating, from Outstanding to Very Weak, is a whole-school judgement. It does not tell a parent whether the physics department is strong, whether Higher Level is taught by a specialist, or whether the Diploma cohort is twelve students or ninety. Those answers come from the subject pages of the report and from asking the school directly, and they are the answers that predict whether a student needs support.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: the supervisor's job, and where a tutor's stops
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent of the Diploma Physics grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks. It is an individual piece of work on a research question the student chooses, written up within a word limit, and it is supervised by the school's own teacher. That supervision is formal: the supervisor confirms the work is the student's own.

The division of labour is therefore clear, and it is worth stating to a family before any sessions are booked. The school supervisor owns the authentication, the internal deadlines and the subject-specific guidance on what the criteria mean at that school. A tutor can help with the process around it: narrowing a research question until it is actually answerable with available equipment, identifying which variable is genuinely controllable, planning enough repeats to justify an uncertainty, and explaining what each criterion rewards.

What a tutor must not do is produce any part of the work. Not the research question handed in as the student's own, not the analysis, not a rewritten paragraph, not a corrected draft returned until it is right. A tutor reads a draft and asks questions: which claim does your data not support, where is the uncertainty you have not propagated, why is this graph a scatter rather than a line. The student makes every change. That boundary protects the candidate, because IB academic-honesty rules make the alternative a malpractice matter.

The research behind these pages found a site in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is a route to a candidate losing their diploma. A page that states the boundary plainly is giving a parent information they can use when comparing providers, and the question to ask any tutor is a simple one: what exactly will you put on the page, and the right answer is nothing.

sections.heading: What Physics tuition costs in Dubai, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start their research. Budget online tutoring in Dubai, usually delivered by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, and on a weekly hour that is about AED 240 to 600 a month. At that price a tutor can supervise homework and re-explain a topic that was taught badly. What that band generally cannot do is teach Higher Level fields properly, mark a Paper 2 extended response against a scheme, or judge whether an investigation design will satisfy criterion A.

The next band up is a qualified subject teacher working online, quoted at about AED 150 to 300 an hour, around AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one weekly session. Above that sits the IB and IGCSE specialist band at AED 200 to 450 and above, where a two-session week lands near AED 1,000 to 2,000 a month on published estimates. Premium named or examiner-led tutors are advertised at AED 500 to 650 and above. All of these are market figures from published rate tables and providers' own pages read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with monthly in-home packages advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. The spread above the online band is travel, not teaching quality. A tutor crossing the city to a Jumeirah 1 address at 17:00 loses an hour each way and the rate carries it. For a thin subject such as Higher Level Physics, insisting on that model also shrinks the available pool to whoever will make the drive.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; they are a service we offer only in India. Physics for a Jumeirah 1 family is taught online, one-to-one, with a free trial lesson first and nothing payable before it. Two further costs belong in a realistic budget: a private candidate entry, where a school will not enter a student for an additional subject, is paid to the exam centre; and the VAT treatment of tuition fees should be checked with the Federal Tax Authority rather than taken from any tutoring page.

faqs.question: Which command terms in IB Physics cost my child the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain and deduce, by a wide margin, followed by show that. Explain wants a cause, a mechanism and a consequence, and a student who gives one of the three earns one mark out of three. Deduce wants the evidence, the physics that links it and then the conclusion, in that order, and answers that give the conclusion first are frequently marked down. Show that is a derivation with the answer printed, so marks go to the written steps rather than the result. The fix is to read a marked script, name the command term above each answer, and count whether the response contains as many distinct creditable points as the mark allocation implies.

faqs.question: How many marks a minute should a Diploma physics paper be attempted at?
faqs.answer: Roughly a mark a minute is the working figure for Paper 2, which is why timing practice uses that rate rather than a stopwatch on individual questions. It means a six-mark extended response gets about six minutes, and a student who spends fifteen on it has taken nine minutes from somewhere else. Paper 1A runs faster because multiple choice does not reward deliberation beyond a certain point. The practical consequence is a two-pass approach: answer everything accessible at speed, then return to what is left with the time that remains. Students usually recover several marks from this alone, with no additional physics.

faqs.question: Which half of Paper 2 does my child lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: The extended-response questions, almost always, and not because the physics in them is harder. They are marked against several distinct points, and a student writing a flowing paragraph often makes two of the four and repeats one of them in different words. The structural fix is to answer in numbered or clearly separated points matching the mark allocation, so each creditable statement is visible to the examiner. The second loss is time: extended responses sit late in the paper, and a student who has worked strictly front to back arrives at the highest-value marks with the least time left.

faqs.question: Which derivations does the Physics course expect my child to reproduce?
faqs.answer: A short list, and knowing it saves a great deal of wasted revision. The suvat relationships from a velocity-time graph, because the graph argument is the physics being tested. Centripetal acceleration expressed through angular velocity. The ideal gas relation assembled from the separate gas laws. Field strength as the gradient of potential, with the sign. Simple harmonic motion from the restoring-force condition. The mass-energy relation applied to binding energy. Anything the data booklet supplies in finished form is a tool rather than a derivation, and reproducing it is not revision. Show that questions come from the first list, so those are the steps worth rehearsing until automatic.

faqs.question: How do I check my child's uncertainty working is right before the exam?
faqs.answer: Four rules cover almost everything. Added or subtracted quantities have their absolute uncertainties added, including when subtracting. Multiplied or divided quantities have their fractional or percentage uncertainties added. A quantity raised to a power has its fractional uncertainty multiplied by that power. A gradient's uncertainty comes from maximum and minimum lines drawn through the error bars, taking half the difference. Then presentation: the uncertainty rounds to one significant figure and the value matches its decimal place. A parent can check the last rule without knowing any physics, and it is worth a mark on its own.

faqs.question: Why does my child get the number right and still lose the mark?
faqs.answer: Three causes account for most of it. The unit is missing, which is not a technicality in physics - a gradient without its unit is not an answer. The precision is wrong, with five significant figures quoted from data supplied to two, or an uncertainty of 0.3 attached to a value given to five figures. Or the method is invisible: the student did the working mentally and wrote only the result, so the method marks were unavailable even though the answer was correct. All three are habits rather than knowledge, and all three respond to two or three sessions of deliberate correction.

faqs.question: What does 'show that' expect that 'calculate' does not?
faqs.answer: Show that gives the student the answer and pays for the route. Every algebraic step has to appear on the page, including the ones that feel too obvious to write, because the marks are allocated to the steps rather than to the result. The commonest loss in this category is a student jumping from the second line to the fifth because the intervening algebra was clear in their head. Calculate, by contrast, pays for a method line, substituted values and a correctly presented answer with units. Both require written working; only show that is marked against a route the examiner already knows.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Physics student actually sit?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families imagine, worked harder. Six full papers properly marked, classified by error cause and followed up produce more than twenty attempted and skimmed. The sequence matters more than the count: topic-only questions open-book first, then the same closed and timed, then Paper 1B on its own, then full papers under the clock, then previously failed questions returning cold weeks later. A student who has attempted twenty papers and never re-sat a question they got wrong has no evidence that anything was repaired, which is the only thing a past-paper programme exists to produce.

faqs.question: Should past papers be marked by the student or by the tutor?
faqs.answer: Both, at different phases, and the order matters. Early work is marked together in the session, because a student cannot yet tell a content gap from a command-term gap and will mis-diagnose themselves. Once the command terms are understood, the student marks their own work against the published scheme and brings the disagreements, which is the single most useful habit in the subject - self-marking is what makes independent practice worth anything. Full timed papers are marked by the tutor and reported back by cause rather than as a total, since a score tells a student how they did and a cause breakdown tells them what to do next.

faqs.question: Which Diploma schools do Jumeirah 1 students travel to for Physics?
faqs.answer: Jumeirah Baccalaureate School runs the Diploma inside the district itself. Beyond that, the realistic options from a Jumeirah 1 address are Raffles World Academy and Emirates International School in the Umm Suqeim and Umm Al Sheif cluster, and Dubai International Academy, Dubai American Academy and the Al Barsha campuses further inland along Sheikh Zayed Road. The International Baccalaureate accounts for about 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment, so Diploma Physics is a minority route here and the choice of campus is genuinely limited. Which school a student attends changes the first month of tutoring more than their ability does.

faqs.question: What time does a Physics session fit into a Jumeirah 1 evening?
faqs.answer: Most Diploma students living in Jumeirah 1 bus out to Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh or Al Barsha and are home between 15:45 and 16:45, later when the beach road or Sheikh Zayed Road is slow. That makes a 16:00 start unrealistic and a 17:00 start workable on most days. The slot that survives a full term, including late buses and a sibling's pick-up, is 18:30. Because lessons are online there is no travel either side, so the hour that is booked is the hour that is taught, and a fixed weekly slot stays fixed rather than drifting.

faqs.question: Does the scientific investigation need a school laboratory?
faqs.answer: Usually yes for the data collection, and that part belongs to the school. The investigation is supervised by the student's own teacher, who authenticates the work and gives subject-specific guidance, and the apparatus comes from the school's physics department. What a tutor contributes sits either side of the laboratory session: narrowing the research question until it is answerable with the equipment available, deciding which variable is genuinely controllable, planning enough repeats to justify an uncertainty, and afterwards working through the processing and the graph. Some investigations use published datasets or simulations instead, which the course permits, and those can be planned entirely online.

faqs.question: Who supervises the investigation, and what can a tutor add?
faqs.answer: The school's physics teacher supervises it and confirms the work is the student's own. A tutor works on the process around that: helping frame a research question with a controllable independent variable, planning the repeats and the range before any data is taken, explaining what each of the four criteria rewards, and reading a draft to ask which claim the data does not support. The student makes every change themselves. A tutor who offers to supply the analysis or rewrite sections is offering something that puts the candidate's diploma at risk, and the right answer to the question of what a tutor will put on the page is nothing.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics tutor in Jumeirah 1 cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market bands read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500 to 650 and above at the premium named end. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 because the rate carries travel. On a weekly hour that works out at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist on two sessions. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our Jumeirah 1 villa for a Physics lesson?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not sell in-home tuition anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are a service we offer only in India. Diploma Physics for a Jumeirah 1 family is taught online, one-to-one, over live video, with the question, the mark scheme and a shared whiteboard all on screen. For physics that is a strong format: derivations build line by line while the original question stays visible, graphs get annotated rather than redrawn, and the session can be rewatched the week of the paper. The Dubai in-home market exists and is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, which is a useful comparison when weighing the two.

faqs.question: Does a Physics tutor teaching a Jumeirah 1 student need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they are providing private tutoring in the UAE. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. It is applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation app, website or e-services, under Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day turnaround. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts has been published.

intro.heading: What two years of IB Physics support actually costs a Jumeirah 2 family
paragraphs: Most pages about physics tuition answer the hourly question and stop. That is the least useful number available. A Diploma Programme physics student is in the subject for two years, and what a Jumeirah 2 family will actually spend depends on how many of those twenty-four months carry a weekly session, whether the investigation gets its own block of hours, and whether the spring of DP2 turns into panic buying at a higher rate. The hourly figure moves by a factor of three across this market. The total moves by a factor of ten, and almost entirely because of decisions made about scheduling rather than about price.

Here is the shape of the published market as of October 2026, attributed. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level rates at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, both at the university-student tier. BartyED sits at the top at around AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. On monthly estimates, Bestimate gives AED 240 to 600 for a budget weekly hour, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Put those against a real two-year plan and the arithmetic becomes visible. A single weekly hour at the qualified-tutor band across the thirty-four teaching weeks of DP1 and the twenty-eight of DP2, with a double slot from January of DP2 and a block of six hours on the investigation, is roughly eighty-four hours. At the mid band that is a four-figure annual commitment and at the specialist band a considerably larger one. The question worth asking before any of it is which of those eighty-four hours actually change a grade.

In our experience of this subject the answer is uneven. The hours spent on the scientific investigation are the highest-value hours in the whole course, because the investigation is 20% of the final grade, it is assessed against four published criteria worth six marks each, and most students lose marks in the same two places every year. The hours spent on Paper 1B data analysis are the second-highest, because that component is a technique rather than a body of knowledge and responds to drilling faster than anything else in physics. The hours spent re-explaining a topic the school taught badly are worth having. The hours spent on generic revision in April of DP2 are mostly wasted, and they are the hours families buy most of.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a physics family in Jumeirah 2 that matters financially as well as practically: the published in-home premium is AED 30 to 150 an hour over the equivalent online rate, and across eighty-four hours that premium alone is larger than the entire investigation support block.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: Physics appears in three different forms across the schools serving Jumeirah 2, and the cost of support differs sharply between them because the assessment differs.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Taken at Standard or Higher Level over two years on the syllabus introduced in 2023 and first examined in 2025. Content sits in five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Assessment is Paper 1 at 36% of the grade, Paper 2 at 44%, and the internally assessed scientific investigation at 20%. Higher Level sits the same components over longer durations with additional content in every theme.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students are 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places in total. For a Jumeirah 2 family the practical consequence is a growing DP Physics cohort and school sets of twenty or more, which is the single clearest argument for one-to-one hours on the investigation rather than on content.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The five years before the Diploma, where physics is taught inside integrated sciences and assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. There are no papers and no percentage weightings, which is why MYP support costs less per month and why the jump into DP Physics surprises families who had no earlier warning signs to read.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim ring run MYP before the Diploma. The cheapest intervention a family in this district can make in physics is six hours in the MYP 5 summer on algebraic rearrangement, unit handling and graph work, rather than thirty hours in DP2 on the consequences of not having them.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE Physics
programmes.description: The British-curriculum route at 16, usually Cambridge 0625 at Core or Extended tier or Pearson 4PH1. Both are examined entirely by written paper, with practical skills assessed through an alternative-to-practical component rather than by coursework. Rates sit a band below IB in every published table: Unitors quotes IGCSE from AED 150 against IB from AED 200.
programmes.countryNote: Most Jumeirah 2 students who end up in DP Physics arrive from 0625 Extended or 4PH1. The gap between a comfortable grade 8 at IGCSE and a comfortable 6 at DP Higher Level is mathematical rather than conceptual: calculus-adjacent reasoning, vector resolution and logarithmic scales. That is what the DP1 autumn term should be spent on, and it is cheaper to buy then than in DP2.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International A Level Physics
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route taken at several British schools in this catchment, with a practical endorsement or a written practical paper depending on the board. Families comparing costs should know that A Level physics support is usually quoted at the same specialist band as IB, because the content depth is comparable even though the assessment structure is not.
programmes.countryNote: Where it matters for a Jumeirah 2 budget is the absence of an internally assessed 20% component. An A Level physics plan can be built almost entirely around past papers, which is cheaper per grade point than a DP plan that has to fund investigation supervision alongside paper practice.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely bought alone in this district. These are the subjects most often added to a DP Physics booking, with what each one actually assesses and why the combination affects the total cost.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1A multiple choice, Paper 1B data analysis, Paper 2 extended response, plus a scientific investigation worth 20%. Marks concentrate in explanation quality rather than calculation: a correct number with no reasoning scores a fraction of the available credit on a Paper 2 six-marker.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual companion to Physics HL and the subject that decides whether physics feels hard. Differentiation of trigonometric functions, logarithmic linearisation and vector algebra all appear in physics before the maths course has finished teaching them, which is a timing problem worth planning around.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Booked alongside physics by almost every medicine and engineering applicant here. The shared skill is quantitative reasoning under a mark scheme: significant figures, units, uncertainty and the discipline of writing the working out in the order the examiner reads it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Taken with Physics SL more often than families expect. It is sufficient for SL physics but leaves Higher Level students short on the algebraic manipulation that fields and quantum topics assume, so a student on this combination usually needs more physics hours, not fewer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third science in most medicine applications. Its investigation is assessed against the same four criteria as the physics one, which means investigation coaching bought once transfers across both subjects and is one of the few genuine economies available in a DP budget.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Increasingly chosen alongside Physics HL by engineering applicants. The overlap is logical structure and the discipline of tracing a process step by step, which is the same habit that rescues a physics student on a multi-stage energy problem.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Shares the physics of materials, structures and energy, and shares the pain of a long internally assessed project. Families running both should expect to fund two separate coursework blocks rather than one, which is a budget line most parents discover late.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Often taken instead of a second science. Its quantitative demands are lighter, so a student carrying Physics HL and ESS SL has a more affordable support profile than one carrying two Higher Level sciences.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Compulsory, assessed by an essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition. It carries no separate physics content but it competes for the same DP2 hours as physics revision, which is why the physics plan has to be written against the school's whole assessment calendar.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece, frequently written in physics by students in this catchment. Supervision is the school's job; what a tutor can legitimately add is subject feedback on the student's own drafts and help with experimental design, never writing.

sections.heading: The published AED rates, and what each tier actually gets you
paragraphs: Every figure in the table below was published by the provider named and is dated October 2026. None of them is our price. The reason to set them out at all is that three of the six strongest-ranking pages in this market publish no price whatsoever, and two of the remaining three quote in US dollars, a currency no family in Jumeirah 2 pays anybody in. A parent who cannot see a number cannot judge whether a quote is reasonable.

Reading the tiers from the bottom up is more useful than reading them from the top. At AED 45 to 65 an hour you are buying a university student or a recent graduate who knows the subject at the level they studied it and has not taught it. For MYP sciences and for IGCSE confidence-building that is often entirely adequate and it is the band most families should start in. It is not adequate for DP Higher Level, because the thing an HL physics student needs is somebody who has read the published assessment criteria for the investigation and marked against them.

The AED 150 to 300 band is where qualified subject teachers sit, and it is the band most of a two-year DP plan should be bought in. Above AED 450 you are paying for scarcity or reputation rather than for a different quality of teaching, and the marginal return is hard to see in a grade. BartyED's published AED 650 is a real rate for a real service, but a Jumeirah 2 family deciding between sixty hours at AED 250 and twenty-three hours at AED 650 for the same money should choose the sixty almost every time, because physics marks accumulate with contact time and not with the prestige of the contact.

One figure deserves separate attention. The in-home premium, AED 30 to 150 an hour over an equivalent online rate, is a travel charge. Across an eighty-four-hour plan it is between AED 2,500 and AED 12,600 spent on somebody driving along Al Wasl Road. That is not an argument against in-home tutoring, which has real advantages for younger children. It is an argument for knowing what the line item is.

sections.heading: Where Jumeirah 2 families waste money on physics
paragraphs: The first waste is buying content hours for a problem that is not a content problem. A student who understands momentum conservation perfectly and scores four out of nine on a Paper 2 question about it does not need momentum explained again. They need to be taught that the mark scheme awards credit for naming the principle, stating the condition under which it applies, substituting with units, and commenting on the direction of the result — and that writing the right number in a box collects a fraction of those marks. Sessions that re-teach understood content are the most expensive comfortable hours in this subject.

The second waste is buying hours in the wrong months. Physics support bought in April of DP2 arrives after the investigation has been submitted, which means 20% of the grade is already fixed and no amount of money can move it. The same hours bought in the second term of DP1, when the investigation is being designed, act on that 20% directly. Families in this district reliably buy late, because the trigger for buying is a disappointing mock result and mocks fall after the point of maximum leverage has passed.

The third waste is paying a specialist rate for work a cheaper tier does equally well. Drilling Paper 1A multiple choice, going through unit conversions, and checking that a student can read a logarithmic axis are all tasks a competent graduate at AED 60 an hour performs as well as a specialist at AED 400. Reserve the specialist band for the investigation, for Paper 2 extended response technique, and for the Higher Level content that genuinely needs a subject expert. A mixed plan is cheaper and better than a uniform one.

The fourth waste is unmeasured hours. If nobody is marking complete papers against the official mark scheme and writing down the score, there is no evidence any of it is working, and a family can spend a year on sessions that feel productive and change nothing. We write a note after each session and a marked paper score at least monthly, because the alternative is buying on faith.

sections.heading: IB Physics assessment structure, and what each component is worth
paragraphs: The current syllabus, introduced in 2023 and first examined in 2025, assesses physics through two external papers and one internal component. Paper 1 is worth 36% of the final grade and splits into Paper 1A, multiple choice, and Paper 1B, a set of data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2 is worth 44% and consists of short and extended response questions. The scientific investigation, internally assessed and externally moderated, is worth 20%. Higher Level candidates sit the same components over longer durations and across additional content in every theme.

Those weightings decide where money should go. Paper 2 is the largest single component and the one where technique is worth the most marks per hour of coaching, because extended response answers are scored against explicit reasoning steps. Paper 1B is the component that improves fastest: it is a skill set — reading uncertainties, linearising a relationship, identifying the systematic error in a described method — and six focused hours visibly change a score. Paper 1A rewards breadth and speed and responds to volume rather than to teaching.

The investigation is the component families underestimate most. It is a single piece of independent experimental work, reported in no more than 3,000 words, assessed against four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Twenty-four marks, 20% of the grade, and the two criteria where students most often lose marks are evaluation and research design rather than the data handling everybody worries about. Students describe a method instead of justifying the choices inside it, and they list weaknesses instead of explaining how each one would propagate into the result.

The content sits in five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level adds depth in every one rather than a separate option. A tutor should be able to say which theme your child's last paper lost marks in without being told, from the script alone.
