sections.heading: The scientific investigation: the cheapest 20% you will ever buy
paragraphs: If a Jumeirah 2 family has a limited budget for physics, the investigation is where it should go, and the hours should be bought at the design stage rather than at the writing stage. Four criteria, six marks each, twenty-four marks in total, 20% of the final grade. Six well-spent hours before a single data point is collected routinely moves a student from the middle band to the upper band on research design and evaluation, which is worth more than twenty hours of revision in DP2.

What those six hours contain is specific. First, interrogating the research question until it is narrow enough to be answered and broad enough to be interesting: most weak investigations fail here, with a question that cannot produce a relationship. Second, the independent and dependent variables and the controlled ones, with a stated reason for each control rather than a list. Third, the range and number of measurements, because five data points across a narrow range cannot support a conclusion no matter how carefully they are processed. Fourth, a plan for uncertainty before the experiment runs, since uncertainties invented afterwards are visible to a moderator.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else on this page. A tutor may question a research question, teach uncertainty propagation, explain what the evaluation criterion rewards and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the investigation, and we will not do it. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. For the student that is a malpractice finding and a potentially lost Diploma, which is a far larger loss than the marks involved.

A practical note on timing for this district. Internal deadlines for the investigation differ by months between schools in the Jumeirah and Al Sufouh ring, and some fall in the final term of DP1 rather than in DP2. Ask your child's physics teacher for the internal deadline in writing at the start of DP1. That date, not the exam date, is what the physics budget should be planned around.

sections.heading: What the in-home travel premium actually buys in Jumeirah 2
paragraphs: In-home physics tutoring is a legitimate service and plenty of families in this district use it. The honest version of the comparison is that it costs AED 30 to 150 an hour more than an equivalent online arrangement, that the difference is a travel charge, and that the travel in question is Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road between 4pm and 5:30pm, which is when a DP student is actually available. A tutor who commits to that journey four times a week is pricing roughly six hours of unpaid driving into their rate, and they are right to.

What the premium buys is a physical presence, which is worth something real for a thirteen-year-old and much less for a seventeen-year-old doing vector resolution on a shared screen. What it costs is selection. The requirement "can reach Jumeirah 2 by 4:45pm" eliminates most of the people who have marked a scientific investigation against the published criteria. The requirement "knows the 2023 physics syllabus and is free at 4:45pm Gulf Standard Time" eliminates almost nobody.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and we state that on every UAE page rather than discovering it for a parent on a sales call. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the student's own paper, script or spreadsheet open on a shared screen. For physics specifically the shared screen is an advantage rather than a compromise: graphing software, a simulation and the student's own marked script can all be on the same display, which is not true at a dining table.

sections.heading: Budgeting physics across DP1 and DP2 month by month
paragraphs: The useful planning unit in this subject is the term, not the month, and the terms are not equal. The DP1 autumn term is where the mathematical gap from IGCSE shows up: vector resolution, logarithmic scales, rearranging an equation with three variables under a square root. Six to eight hours here prevents a year of compounding difficulty, and it is the single highest-return block in the two years after the investigation. Families almost never buy it, because nothing has gone wrong yet.

The DP1 spring and summer terms are investigation months at most schools in this catchment. Six hours at the design stage, as set out above. Beyond that, DP1 rarely needs weekly support for a student who is coping, and a family that buys it anyway is funding reassurance rather than marks. We would rather say so and lose the booking than take sixty hours where thirty would do the same work.

The DP2 autumn term is where content finishes and the first complete papers become possible. This is the point to shift from explanation to timed practice, and the point where a weekly hour genuinely earns its rate. The DP2 spring term should be almost entirely papers: complete Paper 1 and Paper 2 sittings, marked against the official mark scheme, with the score written down. Eight full papers is a reasonable target for a Higher Level candidate. Most manage three.

The exam session itself is the May series for schools in this catchment. We will not publish specific IB exam or results dates on this page. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been verified from the IB itself, and a wrong date in a physics plan is worse than no date. Confirm the session dates and your school's internal deadlines with your child's DP coordinator, and build the budget backwards from those.

sections.heading: Checking a physics tutor is permitted to teach in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page for it is titled "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published. A figure circulating online as a maximum penalty could not be verified against any official source, so no amount should be quoted to you by any provider, including us. If a page states a specific fine, treat that as a signal about the page.

There is a second rule worth knowing in this catchment. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported rather than read from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK before relying on the exact wording. The practical point applies in Dubai too: never arrange for your child's own class teacher to tutor them privately for a fee.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold that permit and does not describe itself as having regulator approval of any kind. We do not operate a UAE office or centre, and we say so.

sections.heading: Physics, MoE equivalency and what a UAE university will want
paragraphs: Families in Jumeirah 2 planning on a UAE university place after the Diploma need to separate two things that get conflated: what the university asks for, and what the Ministry of Education equivalency process asks for. They are different processes with different paperwork, and tutoring is not required for either.

On the British track the sourced equivalency rule is specific. Students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five, and publishing the correct rule is a reasonable thing to expect from a page asking for your money.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no published points threshold in the source we have read, so we will not state one. Any page that publishes an IB equivalency points figure without a moe.gov.ae citation is guessing on your behalf.

What physics specifically affects is the university side rather than the equivalency side. Engineering programmes in the UAE and abroad generally expect Physics at Higher Level alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and some expect Higher Level in both. A student taking Physics SL with Applications and Interpretation should check the prerequisite pages of their target programmes in DP1 rather than DP2, because the subject change window closes early. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry runs; we describe them and point you to the official channel rather than performing them.

process.title: Tell us the level and the term

process.title: Send the last marked script
process.description: A marked Paper 2, a unit test or a mock script tells a physics tutor more in five minutes than a conversation does in thirty. We want to see where credit was withheld, not only what was wrong, because those are different problems with different prices.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: A 45 to 60 minute one-to-one session over live video at no cost, with no card details requested beforehand. The tutor spends it diagnosing against the mark scheme and you receive a written note saying which component is actually costing marks.

process.title: Agree a plan in hours, not months
process.description: We quote a block of hours against named objectives rather than an open-ended monthly arrangement, so the cost is visible at the start. Our rate is confirmed in AED in writing before anything is booked.

process.title: Measure with marked papers
process.description: At least one complete paper a month, marked against the official mark scheme, with the score recorded. Unmeasured sessions are how a family spends a year and learns nothing about whether the spending worked.

process.title: Stop when the plan is done
process.description: Blocks end. If the objectives are met, we say so rather than rolling the arrangement forward automatically. A provider whose plan never finishes is selling months rather than marks.

whyPoints.title: Rates shown with the source and the date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it and dated October 2026, and none of them is presented as our price. Three of the strongest pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in dollars, so a parent here is usually comparing nothing against nothing.

whyPoints.title: Hours placed where they change a grade
whyPoints.description: The investigation and Paper 1B respond fastest; April revision in DP2 responds least. We will tell you when the hours you want to buy cannot act on the component that is costing marks, including when that means a smaller booking than you offered.

whyPoints.title: A mixed plan where a mixed plan is cheaper
whyPoints.description: Multiple-choice drilling does not need a specialist rate and investigation supervision does. Splitting the plan across tiers by task routinely costs a third less than a uniform arrangement and produces the same marks.

whyPoints.title: No travel priced into the hour
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so no part of the rate pays for Al Wasl Road at 4:30pm. The published in-home premium of AED 30 to 150 an hour is, across an eighty-four-hour plan, larger than the entire investigation block.

whyPoints.title: A stated academic-honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: The tutor questions the research question, teaches uncertainty handling and gives feedback on the student's own draft. No part of an investigation, Extended Essay or coursework is written or completed for a student, and we say so to the student in session one.

whyPoints.title: No dates we have not verified
whyPoints.description: We publish Cambridge and Pearson dates with their source. We do not publish IB session or results dates, because the IB's own site cannot be checked automatically and an unverified date in an exam plan is worse than no date at all.

faqs.question: What does an IB physics tutor charge per hour for a Jumeirah 2 family?
faqs.answer: The published market splits into clear bands. EdFlik advertises online tuition from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, both at the university-student tier. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level work and Bestimate puts specialist rates at AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED sits at around AED 650. Those are market figures as published in October 2026, not our prices. We confirm our own rate in AED in writing before anything is booked.

faqs.question: How many hours of physics support does a two-year IB Diploma actually need?
faqs.answer: A realistic plan is seventy to ninety one-to-one hours across the two years, and a well-placed thirty-five can achieve most of it. The pattern we recommend is six to eight hours in the DP1 autumn on the mathematical gap from IGCSE, six hours on the scientific investigation at the design stage, ten to fourteen in the DP2 autumn on first complete papers, and fifteen to twenty in the DP2 spring on timed sittings. Buying sixty hours spread evenly costs more and achieves little extra, because the months are not equally valuable.

faqs.question: Why is the scientific investigation the best place to spend a limited physics budget?
faqs.answer: Because it is 20% of the final grade, it is assessed against four published criteria worth six marks each, and it can only be influenced before submission. Six hours spent at the design stage, interrogating the research question and planning the controlled variables, uncertainty and measurement range, routinely moves a student up a band on research design and evaluation. The same money spent in April of DP2 arrives after the mark is fixed. Students lose marks on evaluation and research design rather than on the arithmetic everybody worries about.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use an online physics tutor or a home tutor in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: Online is cheaper, and the gap is a travel charge rather than a quality difference. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for an equivalent qualified online tutor. The premium of roughly AED 30 to 150 an hour pays for a drive along Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road at the worst hour of the afternoon. Across an eighty-four-hour two-year plan that premium alone comes to between AED 2,500 and AED 12,600.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a home in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video with a shared screen. For physics in particular the shared screen is an advantage: graphing software, a simulation and the student's own marked script sit on one display at the same time, which is not possible at a dining table. We say this on the first screen of every UAE page rather than letting a parent discover it on a call.

faqs.question: What are the current IB Physics paper weightings at SL and HL?
faqs.answer: On the syllabus introduced in 2023 and first examined in 2025, Paper 1 is worth 36% of the final grade and splits into Paper 1A multiple choice and Paper 1B data-based and experimental questions. Paper 2, short and extended response, is worth 44%. The internally assessed scientific investigation is worth 20%. Higher Level candidates sit the same components over longer durations and across additional content in all five themes. Those weightings are why Paper 2 technique and the investigation are the two highest-value things to coach.

faqs.question: Which IB Physics topics cost Jumeirah 2 students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Fields and the quantum material, almost always for mathematical rather than conceptual reasons: a student who cannot comfortably manipulate an inverse-square relationship or an exponential will struggle with both however well they understand the physics. After that, anything requiring a reasoned explanation rather than a number. A Paper 2 six-marker about momentum conservation awards credit for naming the principle, stating the condition, substituting with units and commenting on direction, and students who write only the final number collect a fraction of it.

faqs.question: Can a cheaper tutor handle some of the physics work and a specialist the rest?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families it is the better value. Drilling Paper 1A multiple choice, practising unit conversions and checking that a student can read a logarithmic axis are all done as well by a competent graduate at AED 60 an hour as by a specialist at AED 400. Reserve the specialist band for the scientific investigation, Paper 2 extended response technique and Higher Level content that genuinely needs subject depth. A mixed plan across tiers typically costs about a third less than a uniform one for the same outcome.

faqs.question: My child's physics mock was poor and the exams are in four months. What should we buy?
faqs.answer: Paper technique, not content, and we would tell you if the investigation has already been submitted because that fixes 20% of the grade regardless of what you spend. The plan would be a complete Paper 1 and Paper 2 in week one, marked against the official mark scheme, then a written list of the two components costing the most marks, then weekly timed sittings with Paper 1B drilled separately because it improves fastest. Four months is enough to move a grade. It is not enough to make a Standard Level student into a Higher Level one.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor write or correct my child's scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may question the research question, teach uncertainty propagation and graph linearisation, explain what each assessment criterion rewards and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of it, and we will not. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750, which is an academic-integrity breach and for the student a malpractice finding that can cost the Diploma. The marks at stake are far smaller than that risk.

faqs.question: Do physics tutors in the UAE need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no provider should quote you an amount.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by KHDA or the IB to teach physics in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider claiming regulator or board approval should be asked to show the permit number. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific document issued to institutes with physical premises. We do not hold one, we do not operate a UAE office or centre, and we do not describe ourselves as accredited by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. We are an independent tutor-matching platform.

faqs.question: When does a Jumeirah 2 physics student sit the IB exams?
faqs.answer: Schools in this catchment sit the May session. We will not publish specific IB exam or results dates on this page, because the IB's own site returns an error to automated checking and no IB date in this project has been verified from the IB directly. A date a family plans around has to be right, and an approximate one is worse than none. Ask your child's DP coordinator for the session dates and, more importantly, for the school's internal deadline for the scientific investigation, which is the date the physics budget should be built around.

faqs.question: Does Physics Higher Level matter for engineering applications from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Generally yes. Engineering programmes in the UAE and abroad usually expect Physics at Higher Level alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and some expect Higher Level in both. A student carrying Physics SL with Applications and Interpretation should read the prerequisite pages of their target programmes during DP1, because the window for changing subjects closes early in the first year. This is an admissions question rather than an equivalency one: Ministry of Education equivalency and university prerequisites are separate processes with separate paperwork, and tutoring is required for neither.

faqs.question: Can physics sessions be scheduled around a late school finish in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they usually have to be. A Diploma student at Dubai College or Kings' School Dubai with a co-curricular commitment is often not home before 5pm, and the Al Wasl run between 4pm and 5pm is the slowest hour of the day in this district. Because lessons run over live video there is no travel to coordinate, so an evening slot at 6pm or 7pm costs nothing extra and holds reliably. During Ramadan most families here move to a post-iftar slot, confirmed in writing before the month begins.

faqs.question: How will we know the physics tuition is working rather than just happening?
faqs.answer: By a marked score, written down, at least once a month. A complete Paper 1 or Paper 2 sat under timed conditions and marked against the official mark scheme produces a number that either moves or does not. Session notes describing what was covered are useful but they are not evidence. Families who run a year of physics support without a single marked full paper have no way to judge the spending, and that is the most common reason an expensive arrangement turns out to have achieved nothing.

intro.heading: Physics in Jumeirah 3, counted from the exam date backwards
paragraphs: Most searches for an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah 3 happen in one of three weeks of the year: the fortnight after the first set of DP1 unit tests, the week mock results come home in January, and the panicked days after a scientific investigation draft gets a comment the student did not expect. The subject does not get harder in those weeks. The calendar does. Physics is the one DP subject where a term lost to vague revision cannot be recovered by working harder in May, because the paper rewards practised technique rather than remembered content.

So this page is organised around time rather than around topics. It sets out what the assessment model actually asks for, what the next eight weeks have to achieve depending on where your child sits in the two-year programme, and what a weekly session should produce by way of evidence that it worked. If your child is in DP1 and the first internal assessment deadline is six weeks away, the work is different from a DP2 student eleven weeks out from the May session, and a tutor who treats both the same is being paid to teach a syllabus instead of a student.

Jumeirah 3 is a villa district between Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road, and the families here sit across a wide spread of schools: IB continuum schools in Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha, British schools in Al Safa and Al Sufouh running IGCSE then A Level, and a handful of students doing DP at schools a full thirty minutes inland. That spread matters for one practical reason. The school a child attends sets the internal deadline calendar, and no two of those calendars agree. A tutor working to the IB's published assessment structure but ignoring the school's own submission dates will have your child revising Theme D while a draft is overdue.

Online delivery is the part of this that reads like a compromise and is not. IB Gram runs every UAE lesson as one-to-one online tuition over live video; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The gain is specificity. A Jumeirah 3 family gets a Physics HL specialist who has marked uncertainty propagation badly enough times to spot the exact error your child keeps making, rather than whichever science graduate can reach Jumeirah 3 by 4.30pm. The second gain is the clock. A session that does not need a car can start at 4pm, pause for a 20-minute break, and finish before homework starts.

What follows is specific: the weightings of each paper, a week-by-week plan for a block of eight weeks, the four criteria the scientific investigation is marked against, what Dubai providers published as their 2026 rates, and the line a tutor must not cross on assessed work. Read the exam-session table even if your child is in DP1. Entry deadlines, internal submission dates and mock windows all sit months before the paper, and almost every family that arrives late arrives late because nobody counted backwards.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 3 students reach DP Physics along two routes: through an IB continuum school that ran the Middle Years Programme, or from an IGCSE science course at a British school in Al Safa or Al Sufouh. The gap to close in the first eight weeks of DP1 is different for each, so the programme notes below are written for this neighbourhood's actual intake.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, three at Higher Level. Physics sits in Group 4 and is assessed by two written papers plus a scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade. The subject guide in force for current candidates organises content into themes A to E, with HL extension material inside each theme rather than bolted on at the end, and a set of experimental and mathematical tools examined through the papers.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the DP cohort is a minority of the private-school population, which has a practical consequence for Jumeirah 3 families: a school may run only one Physics HL class, and if that class loses a teacher mid-year there is no second set to move into. Several families here use weekly online tuition specifically as continuity insurance against that, rather than as remediation.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. In Sciences those criteria reward knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. A student who scored well on criterion A and poorly on criterion C arrives in DP1 able to recall definitions but unable to handle a gradient, an intercept or an uncertainty.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students from Umm Suqeim and Al Barsha continuum schools usually transfer into DP Physics with strong investigation design and weak algebraic fluency, because MYP Sciences rarely demands the rearrangement speed Paper 2 assumes. The first four weeks of tuition for this group is normally pure mathematics applied to physics contexts, not new physics content.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics into DP Physics
programmes.description: The commonest Jumeirah 3 route. Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 ends with recall-heavy theory papers and a practical or alternative-to-practical component. DP Physics then asks for the same content expressed as relationships: proportionality, log plots, error bars and the reasoning behind a straight-line graph. Students who earned an A* by memorising definitions often meet their first real difficulty here.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 students in Al Safa and Al Sufouh who already know they want Physics HL benefit most from a short bridging block in June and July, before DP1 starts. Six to eight sessions on vectors, logarithms, graph linearisation and uncertainty notation removes most of the autumn-term panic that drives the January search for help.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely tutored alone. The combinations below are the ones Jumeirah 3 families actually request alongside it, and the notes say what each one assesses and where the marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Themes A to E, with Paper 1 split between multiple choice and data analysis, Paper 2 extended response, and a scientific investigation. Marks are lost disproportionately on uncertainty treatment, graph interpretation and the difference between the command terms explain, describe and state.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual pairing with Physics HL. The overlap that matters is calculus applied to motion and fields, plus logarithms for exponential decay. A student weak in AA algebra will read every Physics question twice and still mishandle the rearrangement.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Chosen by Physics SL students more often than schools expect. Its statistics and regression content actually helps the data-analysis half of Paper 1, but it gives less practice in symbolic manipulation, so algebra needs separate attention in sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Taken with Physics by most engineering and medicine applicants here. The shared skill is quantitative reasoning under time pressure; the shared failure is the scientific investigation, where both subjects demand the same methodological rigour and students write two weak reports instead of one good method twice.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A Group 4 alternative that some Jumeirah 3 students pair with Physics. Useful overlap in modelling and logic; no overlap at all in laboratory technique, which means the investigation has to be learned once rather than practised across two subjects.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Offered by a few Dubai IB schools and often misread as the easier Group 4 option. It rewards iterative design documentation rather than numerical problem solving, so it is a poor substitute for Physics on an engineering application and a reasonable companion to it.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Chosen by students who want applied science without heavy mathematics. Its mechanics content leans on the same force and moment concepts as Physics Theme A, so a tutor can treat the two together when a student takes both.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece supervised by a school teacher. Tutoring here is process coaching: narrowing a research question, judging whether the measurement is feasible with school apparatus, and reading a draft critically. The argument, the words and the data must be the student's own.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay and exhibition both reward precise examples, and Physics gives good ones: measurement uncertainty as a knowledge limit, models that are known to be wrong but useful. Sessions tend to focus on turning a physics example into a knowledge claim rather than a summary.

subjects.name: IB Physics IA support
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. IB Physics IA support in a session means pressure-testing the research question, checking that the independent variable is genuinely controllable, and teaching uncertainty propagation before data collection rather than after.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 3 family is really asking when they search for a Physics tutor
paragraphs: The literal answer first: an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah 3, through IB Gram, is a DP Physics specialist who teaches your child one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, usually weekly, starting with a free diagnostic lesson. Nobody drives to your villa. The subject specialist is chosen for the level and the theme your child is struggling with, not for proximity to the beach road.

Underneath the search sits a different question, which is usually some version of how much time is left. A parent searching in October has a DP1 student whose first unit test on Theme A came back lower than their IGCSE results suggested it would. A parent searching in January has mock grades and eleven or twelve weeks. A parent searching in March has a draft investigation and a school deadline. Those are three different jobs, and the honest thing a tutor can do in a first lesson is say which one applies and what it realistically achieves.

The mistake that costs Jumeirah 3 families the most money is booking general science help in week six and discovering in week twelve that the sessions have been revisiting content the student already knew. Physics marks are lost in technique: reading a graph axis, propagating an uncertainty, choosing the right form of an equation, answering a six-mark question with six scoring points instead of three good sentences. A tutor who does not diagnose that in the first hour will fill a term pleasantly and change nothing.

So the first session has one job. The student works through a short mixed set under time, talking aloud, and the tutor records where the error happens rather than whether the answer is right. Three or four error families usually emerge, and the term plan is written against them. That diagnostic is free, it produces a written summary, and families are welcome to take the summary and work from it themselves.

January request: post-mock triage, eight to twelve weeks of paper work
March request: investigation and final-topic consolidation only

sections.heading: The DP Physics assessment model, paper by paper
paragraphs: DP Physics is assessed by two written papers and one piece of internally assessed coursework. Paper 1 carries 36% of the final grade and comes in two parts: a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section built on an unseen experiment. Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response, mixing short answers with longer structured questions. The scientific investigation accounts for the remaining 20%, and it is marked by the school against IB criteria and then externally moderated.

That split is the single most useful fact on this page, because it tells you where tuition hours should go. Four marks in five come from written papers, and the data-analysis half of Paper 1 is the part students practise least. It is also the part that transfers: the skill of reading an unfamiliar experiment, identifying the controlled variables and interpreting a gradient is the same skill the investigation is marked on. Time spent there is counted twice.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with harder questions. It is more content inside the same five themes, longer papers, and a markedly higher expectation of algebraic fluency. A student can hold an acceptable SL grade while rearranging equations slowly, and the same habit at HL will cost them Paper 2 marks on time alone. The table below sets out the structure; the weightings are those published in the subject guide for current candidates, and your child's DP coordinator can confirm the version their cohort sits.

One caution about dates, since it comes up in the first lesson most weeks. IB examination and results dates are published by the IB and by your school, and this page does not restate them, because a date restated second-hand and then revised is worse than no date. Ask the DP coordinator for the cohort's own timetable and the internal submission calendar, and bring both to the first session.

table.caption: DP PHYSICS ASSESSMENT STRUCTURE AND WHERE MARKS GO MISSING
rows: Rapid recognition across all five themes, no calculator-heavy work
Misreading the question stem; changing a correct first instinct under time pressure
An unseen experiment: variables, graphs, gradients, uncertainties
Uncertainty treatment, error bars, and stating a conclusion the data does not support
Structured multi-part questions, derivations and explanation
Answering a six-mark question with three ideas; confusing explain with describe
An independent experiment reported against four criteria
A research question too broad to answer; evaluation that lists problems without weighing them
Examined inside both papers rather than separately
Graph linearisation, logarithms, unit conversion and significant figures

sections.heading: The next eight weeks, counted backwards
paragraphs: An eight-week block is the unit most Jumeirah 3 families can realistically commit to, and it is long enough to change a grade if it is spent on the right things. The structure below assumes two sessions a week for a DP2 student working toward the May session, with the first session diagnostic and the last two spent entirely on recurring errors. A DP1 student runs the same shape over sixteen weeks at one session a week.

The reason this is written as a countdown rather than a syllabus plan is that revision has a natural order and most students get it backwards. They begin with the topic they like, leave the weakest theme until last, and run out of time before it is covered. Counting backwards forces the opposite: the weakest theme is rebuilt first, when there is still time to practise it, and the strong topics are maintained with short timed sets rather than re-taught.

Evidence matters as much as the plan. Each week should produce something checkable, because a session that feels productive and leaves no trace is indistinguishable from a conversation. A marked timed section, a graph drawn correctly to scale, an uncertainty calculated to the right number of figures, an error log with three entries closed out: these are the artefacts that tell a parent paying by the hour whether anything moved.

Ramadan falls inside the Dubai revision calendar in most years, and it changes the shape of a week rather than cancelling it. Families usually move sessions later, after Iftar, and shorten them to 45 or 60 minutes. Shorter and more frequent works better than long weekend blocks during fasting, and the last fortnight before a paper is a poor time to change tutor or format.

sections.heading: Where Physics marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Five error families account for most of the difference between a 4 and a 6 in DP Physics, and none of them is a knowledge gap. The first is uncertainty: students quote a reading uncertainty and forget that it propagates through a calculation, or add percentages where they should add absolutes. The second is graph work: plotting raw data when the relationship needs linearising, drawing a line of best fit through the origin because the equation suggests it should pass through, or reading a gradient off two data points instead of the line.

The third is command terms, and it is the cheapest to fix. State, describe, explain, outline, deduce and justify ask for structurally different answers, and the mark scheme pays for the structure. A student who writes a paragraph of correct physics in answer to a two-mark state question loses time they needed elsewhere, and a student who gives one sentence to a six-mark explain question loses four marks they already knew. One session on command terms, with past-paper mark schemes read side by side, usually moves Paper 2 more than a month of content revision.

The fourth is algebra under time. Physics Paper 2 assumes rearrangement is automatic, and for a student who learned to solve equations by substitution rather than manipulation it never is. This is the one gap that genuinely needs mathematics teaching rather than physics teaching, and it is why a Physics HL student weak in Mathematics AA often needs both subjects addressed in the same session for a few weeks.

The fifth is the written investigation, where marks are lost before any data is collected. A research question that cannot be answered with the apparatus available, an independent variable that cannot be controlled cleanly, too few levels of that variable to show a relationship: these are design faults, and no amount of careful writing afterwards recovers the marks. That is why the investigation clinic starts with the question and the method rather than the report.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, twenty-four marks, and the line a tutor holds
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation in DP Physics is worth 20% of the final grade and is marked against four criteria, each carrying six marks, for twenty-four in total: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Those letters and totals are the single most useful piece of information a parent can have, because they convert a vague instruction to write a good report into four separate things that can be practised. Competitor pages in this market almost never name a criterion, let alone a mark allocation.

Research design is where the grade is usually decided. The criterion rewards a research question with a clearly identified independent and dependent variable, a method that controls the rest, and a justification for the range and number of measurements. Data analysis rewards correct processing, including uncertainties carried through to the final result and graphs that show the relationship rather than decorate the page. Conclusion asks for an answer to the research question supported by the data and compared with accepted physics. Evaluation asks for weaknesses weighed by their impact, not simply listed.

The boundary on a tutor's role is firm and worth stating plainly, because this SERP contains businesses that sell finished coursework. A tutor teaches technique, asks questions about a draft, points at a criterion and explains what the examiner expects to see. A tutor does not supply text, does not edit a report into shape, and does not provide a method for the student to adopt as their own. The report, the data and the reasoning must come from the student; anything else is academic malpractice under IB rules and the risk sits with your child, not with the tutor.

In practice that means feedback is delivered as questions. Which variable did you decide not to control, and why? What does the gradient of your graph physically represent? If your uncertainty is this large, can you still claim the relationship you have claimed? A student who answers those questions and then revises their own report has both learned the criterion and kept their work their own.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and how a Jumeirah 3 parent checks a tutor is allowed to teach
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The MoHRE private tutor permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through its app, website and e-services system. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Schools are regulated separately and by emirate. Dubai private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. KHDA inspection bands are published per school on the authority's own site, and that is where to read them: a band is a judgement about a whole school across many measures, not a prediction about one Physics class. A school rated Very Good can still have a weak year in one Group 4 subject, which is precisely the situation that brings families to this page.

Two further rules are worth knowing before you hire anyone locally. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a similar restriction. Treat any offer of your child's own class teacher, privately, as a problem rather than a shortcut. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes; an individual online tutor is a different legal category entirely.

IB Gram holds no regulator or examination-board accreditation and claims none. We are an independent matching platform: we introduce a subject specialist, the lessons run online, and you can ask any tutor for their permit status before the first paid session. We also do not publish inspection ratings on these pages, because a rating read second-hand and then revised is a liability. Check the school's current report on the KHDA site and the permit position on mohre.gov.ae.

sections.heading: Getting started from Jumeirah 3, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You send the level, the themes causing trouble, the school and the next deadline. We come back with one or two Physics specialists and a proposed slot in Gulf Standard Time. The trial lesson runs as a diagnostic, after which you receive a written summary naming the error families and a suggested plan length. If you continue, the slot is held weekly for the term; if you do not, the summary is yours to use.

DP Physics tutoring in Jumeirah is one of the narrower requests we handle, and honesty about availability matters more than a confident promise. A Physics HL specialist with current experience of the subject guide is a smaller pool than a general maths tutor, and in the eight weeks before a session that pool is largely committed. If no UAE-based specialist is free at the time your family needs, we say so and offer the two alternatives: a specialist in another time zone whose evening is your afternoon, or a wait for a slot that opens. We do not substitute a general science tutor and describe them as a Physics specialist.

A word on what good looks like after a month. The student can name their own error families without prompting. Timed Paper 1 sections are being completed inside the time rather than abandoned at question 25. The investigation has a research question that survived being challenged. And homework from school is being used as practice rather than treated as a separate burden. If none of that has happened in four sessions, the match is wrong and should be changed rather than persevered with.

Families in Jumeirah 3, Umm Suqeim, Jumeirah 2 and Al Safa share the same teaching slots, so the popular 4pm and 5pm weekday windows fill first each term. Booking the slot before the term starts is worth more than booking extra hours later, and a single weekly session held reliably for twelve weeks beats six sessions crammed into April on every measure we can see.

faqs.question: How many weeks of Physics tutoring does a Jumeirah 3 student need before the May session?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong rather than on how far away the papers are. A technique gap in uncertainties, graphs and command terms is usually addressable in an eight-week block of two sessions a week, and most of the improvement shows up in timed Paper 1 work by week five. A content gap spanning two or three themes needs a term. Arriving with four weeks left means choosing: either the weakest theme or paper technique, not both. The diagnostic in the free trial lesson is designed to tell you which case applies before you commit to a length.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah 3 come to the villa?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers every UAE lesson as one-to-one online tuition over live video; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Physics that trade is strongly in your favour, because the pool of tutors who have taught the current subject guide at Higher Level is small and spread across time zones, while the pool who can reach Jumeirah 3 by 4.30pm on a Tuesday is tiny. Online also means a 4pm start is realistic, shared whiteboard files carry over between sessions, and nothing is cancelled because Sheikh Zayed Road has stopped moving.

faqs.question: What exactly is in Paper 1 for DP Physics, and why does everyone say it is the one to practise?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and has two parts: a multiple-choice section across all five themes, and a data-analysis section built on an experiment the student has never seen. The second part is the one students practise least and the one that transfers most, because identifying variables, linearising a graph and judging whether a conclusion is supported by the data is exactly what the internally assessed investigation is marked on. Time spent on Paper 1B therefore counts twice. Most eight-week plans we write put a timed data-analysis section in every single week.

faqs.question: My child got an A* in IGCSE Physics and is now getting 4s in DP1. What changed?
faqs.answer: The question style did. IGCSE Physics rewards accurate recall of definitions and standard calculations; DP Physics asks the same content to be used as relationships, with uncertainties carried through and graphs chosen to reveal proportionality. A student who learned to recognise question types rather than manipulate equations meets that wall in the first term of DP1. It is a technique problem, not an ability problem, and twelve to sixteen weeks of weekly work on algebraic fluency, graph linearisation and command terms usually closes it. Starting in October is far cheaper than starting in February.

faqs.question: Where is the line between coaching the scientific investigation and writing it for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may challenge the research question for feasibility, teach uncertainty propagation using the student's own measurements, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, and read a draft and respond with questions. A tutor may not supply the research question, hand over a method, process the data, or rewrite the report. The investigation is worth 20% of the grade and is externally moderated, and work that is not the student's own puts their IB registration at risk. Feedback delivered as questions keeps the learning and keeps the authorship where it belongs.

faqs.question: How are the four Physics investigation criteria weighted?
faqs.answer: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation each carry six marks, giving twenty-four in total, which the school converts and the IB externally moderates. Research design is where most marks are won or lost, because a question that cannot be answered with the available apparatus caps everything that follows. Data analysis rewards uncertainties carried through to the final result. Conclusion must answer the question and compare with accepted physics. Evaluation must weigh weaknesses by their impact rather than list them. Knowing the letters and the mark split turns a vague task into four practisable ones.

faqs.answer: Timing shifts rather than stopping. School examination weeks are usually paused entirely, because a student sitting internal exams needs sleep more than an extra hour of fields revision. What we avoid is changing tutor or format in the final fortnight before a paper, when continuity is worth more than any marginal improvement in teaching style.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL necessary for engineering at a UAE university?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements are set by each university and change, so the only safe answer is to read the course page for the exact programme and intake year. In general, engineering and physical-science degrees in the UAE and abroad look for Physics and Mathematics at Higher Level, and some will accept Physics SL with strong Mathematics. Tutoring cannot change an admissions rule and nobody should suggest it can. What a tutor can do is make Higher Level survivable for a student whose algebra is the limiting factor rather than their physics.

faqs.answer: The student works through a short mixed set under light time pressure while talking aloud, and the tutor records where each error occurs rather than whether the answer was right. That usually surfaces three or four error families: uncertainty handling, graph interpretation, command-term structure, algebraic speed. The tutor then shows one fix live, sets two questions for the week, and writes a summary naming the families and a realistic plan length. You receive that summary whether or not you continue, and it is specific enough to work from alone.

The overlap is real: calculus applied to motion and fields, logarithms for decay, and the rearrangement speed Paper 2 assumes. Once the algebra is no longer the limiting factor, most families split the subjects again, because deep Mathematics AA work and deep Physics work compete for the same hour. We say which case applies after the diagnostic rather than selling two slots by default.

intro.heading: Physics at 5pm after a Dubai school day is a waste of a session
paragraphs: Physics is the least forgiving Diploma subject to teach to a tired student. It requires holding a model in mind, applying mathematics to it, and tracking units and directions at the same time. A fourteen or seventeen-year-old who left Jumeirah Golf Estates at seven in the morning, sat through a full timetable, queued at the Jumeirah Park gate, drove back through the Al Khail junction and then went to training in Dubai Sports City cannot do that at five o'clock. They can do it at seven.

That is why this page starts with the clock rather than the syllabus. The arithmetic for this community is consistent: campus finish between 2.45pm and 3.30pm, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue, twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving depending on whether the school sits in Al Barsha South or out towards Arabian Ranches, then twenty minutes before a teenager is capable of anything. Add a club and the usable window starts after six. A physics session placed earlier than that is bought at full price and delivered at half capacity.

The second thing the school day does to physics is practical access. The scientific investigation is worth 20 per cent of the grade and is built on data the student collects, usually in the school laboratory on a timetable the school controls. That constrains when outside support is useful: the valuable work happens at the design stage, before the data exists, and then again at the analysis stage once it does. In between, there is nothing a tutor can usefully add.

The third is mathematics. Physics at Higher Level assumes manipulation that many students are learning simultaneously in Mathematics, and the ones who struggle with physics are frequently struggling with rearranging an equation rather than with the physics. Diagnosing which it is takes one marked paper and it changes the whole plan, because the fix for one is nothing like the fix for the other.

There is a fourth thing worth naming, which is scarcity. Physics teachers who have taught the Diploma to examination standard are thin on the ground in any school system, and the catchment of one gated community of a few thousand households is very unlikely to contain one who is also free at the single hour your child can work. That is arithmetic rather than a complaint about the neighbourhood, and it is the reason we match by level and theme rather than by distance.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Golf Estates students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is an India-only service. The scheduling advantage is the point: with no travel on the tutor's side, the session can sit in the only part of the evening where physics actually works.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws, momentum and impulse. The characteristic error is direction: a student treats velocity as a number, loses the sign convention, and produces an answer of the right magnitude pointing the wrong way. Marks go for the vector nature, not the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Work, energy and power
subjects.description: Energy transfers, efficiency and conservation arguments. Students lose marks by writing numbers without naming the energy stores involved, which is what the extended-response mark scheme actually asks for. Three sessions usually corrects the habit permanently.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and the particulate model
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the gas laws and the kinetic model. A reliable source of lost marks because explanations are given in terms of temperature where the mark scheme wants particle behaviour and mean kinetic energy.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Superposition, standing waves, interference, diffraction and the Doppler effect. Standing waves on strings and in pipes are the single most commonly muddled topic in the theme, and they are efficient to tutor because the rules are finite and diagrammatic.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, with substantial HL extension
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits, electromagnetic induction and, at Higher Level, orbital motion and field potential. The heaviest Higher Level theme and where most of the session count goes. Circuits in particular collapse when the diagram is unfamiliar rather than when the theory is missing.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, the photoelectric effect and, at Higher Level, quantum phenomena. Content-dense and self-contained, which makes it one of the more efficient topics to tutor: four or five focused sessions and it is usually secure.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.levels: SL and HL, assessed in Paper 1B
subjects.description: Gradients from graphs, error bars, propagation of uncertainty and linearising a relationship. Assessed as its own skill and taught unevenly in schools, which makes it one of the highest-return things a tutor can work on. Two or three sessions is often worth a grade boundary.

subjects.name: Experimental technique and the investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: Research design, control of variables, data collection and evaluation, marked out of 24 across four criteria. The valuable support is at the design stage before any data exists, and then on analysis once it does, always as feedback on the student's own work.

subjects.name: Mathematical fluency for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging equations, standard form, significant figures, unit conversion and trigonometry in resolution of vectors. Not a syllabus topic and frequently the real problem. A marked paper shows it immediately: the physics reasoning is sound and the algebra fails.

subjects.name: Extended response technique
subjects.description: Structuring a multi-mark explanation so each mark-scheme point is clearly made in order. Students who know the physics still lose marks by writing a paragraph in which three correct ideas are tangled together and only one is creditable.

sections.heading: The usable hour, worked out properly
paragraphs: Start from the campus, not from the calendar. Secondary finish times across the schools Jumeirah Golf Estates families use for Diploma physics run from about 2.45pm to 3.30pm. The gate queue costs ten to twenty minutes before a car moves. The drive is twelve to twenty minutes from the JVT and Al Barsha South ring, twenty to thirty from Arabian Ranches, and thirty to thirty-five from Al Sufouh.

That puts most students home between 4.10pm and 4.45pm. Add the twenty minutes a teenager needs to stop being a passenger and start being a student, and the earliest honest start is 5.15pm. For the substantial proportion of children in this community who train in Dubai Sports City, that start moves to 7pm or later. None of this is unusual; it is simply rarely written down before a weekly slot gets agreed.

Physics makes the timing matter more than other subjects. Mathematics tolerates a tired student better, because a familiar procedure can be executed on autopilot. Physics cannot: a student has to hold a physical model, apply mathematics to it and track units and vector directions simultaneously. Done at 5pm after a long day in Dubai heat, the same forty minutes produces visibly less.

The sensible plan for a Jumeirah Golf Estates physics student is a weekday slot between 6.30pm and 8.15pm, after a first attempt at the school's problem set, plus a weekend morning when a full timed paper is needed. The table gives the arithmetic by cluster so you can pick from your own row rather than from an optimistic guess.

sections.heading: What the physics papers carry
paragraphs: Revision is usually spread evenly, and the assessment structure says it should not be. Physics is assessed through two written papers plus the internally assessed scientific investigation, which contributes 20 per cent of the grade. Paper 1 divides into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, and Paper 2 carries the extended structured questions. Confirm the exact weightings for your child's cohort with the school's subject guide, because science assessment models are periodically revised.

Two things follow immediately. The data-analysis section is a distinct skill with its own marks, and it is taught unevenly across schools because it falls between the physics and the mathematics departments. A student who has never been shown how to propagate an uncertainty or how to linearise a relationship is guessing at those marks, and two or three sessions fixes it. That is the cheapest available grade movement in the subject.

The second is that the extended-response marks on Paper 2 are structural as much as conceptual. A mark scheme lists discrete points, and a student who writes a flowing paragraph containing three correct ideas tangled together frequently earns one mark rather than three. Teaching a student to make one point per sentence, in the order the question implies, is technique work that transfers across every theme.

A practical note on the multiple-choice section: it rewards elimination and unit reasoning rather than full calculation, and students burn time doing complete algebra on questions that could be answered by checking which option has plausible units. Timed practice is the only way to build that, which is another argument for the weekend morning slot.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: 24 marks across four criteria
paragraphs: The internally assessed investigation is worth 20 per cent of the physics grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Confirm the current criteria and allocations with your school, since the science guides were restructured relatively recently and schools work from the version their cohort sits.

The structure tells you where the help is worth buying. The research design criterion is decided before a single measurement is taken, which means the most valuable conversation happens weeks before the laboratory session. A question that cannot generate enough data points, or where a variable cannot genuinely be controlled, produces a capped mark no amount of later writing recovers. Three sessions at that stage is a small block with a large effect.

The evaluation criterion is where otherwise strong students lose marks, because it asks for honest limitation of the method rather than a list of generic improvements. Writing that more repeats would have helped earns little; identifying that the timing method introduced a systematic error of a particular size, and saying what that does to the conclusion, earns a great deal. That is a taught skill.

The boundary matters here as much as anywhere in the Diploma. A tutor may question the research design, point out that a method will not produce analysable data, explain what each criterion rewards, mark a draft against the criteria and teach referencing and uncertainty convention. A tutor may not write any part of the report, rewrite the student's prose, supply a research question as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit a draft to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross it, and one operator in this market was found selling completed Internal Assessments outright, which is malpractice with consequences that fall on the student.

sections.heading: Is it physics, or is it algebra?
paragraphs: This is the most useful diagnostic question in the subject and it is answered in twenty minutes by a marked paper. A substantial proportion of students described as weak at physics have intact physical reasoning and failing mathematics. They know that the component of weight along the slope is what accelerates the block, and then they cannot rearrange the resulting expression under time pressure.

The signature is visible in the script. Physics-reasoning weakness looks like a blank or a wrong starting equation. Mathematical weakness looks like the correct starting equation followed by an algebraic slip, a unit left unconverted, or a rearrangement done in the wrong order. The second pattern is cheaper to fix and the fix transfers immediately to Mathematics as well.

At Higher Level the overlap is larger still. Fields, orbital motion and quantum phenomena all assume comfortable manipulation of indices, logarithms and trigonometric resolution, and a student taking Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches may not meet some of that elsewhere. Where that is the case, a short mathematical-fluency block before the fields theme is better value than more physics teaching during it.

The practical instruction for a Jumeirah Golf Estates parent is therefore simple: send the marked paper before asking for a quote, and ask the prospective tutor which of the two patterns they see. A specialist will tell you, with examples from the script. Somebody who starts at the beginning of the syllabus has not looked.
bullets: A blank or wrong starting equation points to physics reasoning
A right equation and a failed rearrangement points to algebra

sections.heading: Where physics marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Units first. A numerically correct answer with a missing or wrong unit loses the mark, and in a paper of thirty such answers that is a grade boundary's worth of marks for a reason that has nothing to do with physics. Significant figures behave the same way: an answer quoted to six figures from data given to two is marked down, and students do it constantly because the calculator offers it.

Direction next. Velocity, force, momentum and field strength are vectors, and a question that asks for a value expects the direction stated or the sign convention honoured. Students treat them as numbers and lose the vector mark while getting the magnitude right.

Then the controlled variable. In data-analysis and investigation contexts, a student describing an experiment without naming what was held constant loses marks that are explicitly available for it. It is a sentence, and it is missing from most first drafts.

And finally language precision in explanations. Thermal physics answers that explain in terms of temperature rather than particle behaviour and mean kinetic energy, energy answers that do not name the stores involved, and wave answers that describe interference without reference to path difference. Each of these is a specific, fixable sentence habit, and each is visible on a marked Paper 2. Between them they account for more lost marks in this subject than any genuine conceptual gap.

The encouraging consequence is that the repair work is short. None of these four requires new content to be learned, and a student who has them all is usually two or three sessions from not having them, provided somebody reads the script rather than restarting the syllabus.

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs around Jumeirah Golf Estates
paragraphs: Published rates in Dubai for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one UK-based agency publishing AED 270. Budget online tuition, typically delivered by a university student, is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150, one platform listing from AED 33 to AED 52. Premium named or examiner-led provision is quoted as high as AED 650 an hour.

For physics in particular, the budget band is a poor fit. Supervision and encouragement do not resolve a fields problem or an uncertainty propagation, and the shortfall will not be visible until a mock. The specialist band is where the subject sits, and the useful thing to compare is not the rate but the block: two or three sessions for data analysis, four or five for nuclear and quantum, ten to fourteen for Higher Level fields taught properly.

In-home visits in Dubai are advertised at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with one provider publishing AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. For physics the in-home premium is particularly hard to justify, because the thing that helps most is a shared screen with a graph being built and annotated, which video does better than a notebook.

All of those figures were read from the providers' own pages in October 2026 and describe the market rather than IB Gram. Our own fee is quoted after the free trial lesson, once a marked paper has established whether this is a three-session data-analysis job or a two-term fields programme.

sections.heading: Laboratory access and what a tutor cannot replace
paragraphs: Physics is a practical subject and online tuition does not change that. The school laboratory is where the investigation data is collected, and it is where a student develops a feel for what a measurement actually looks like: the parallax on a metre rule, the way a stopwatch reaction time dwarfs a short interval, the drift on a thermometer. Nothing delivered over video substitutes for that, and we would not claim otherwise.

What video does well is the part either side. Before the laboratory session, a tutor can interrogate a research design, estimate whether the expected range of readings is measurable with the equipment available, and spot that a variable cannot in practice be controlled. That conversation saves laboratory time, which in a Dubai school is a rationed resource.

After the session, a tutor can work through the raw data on a shared screen: plotting it, considering whether a straight-line form exists, propagating the uncertainties, and testing whether the conclusion the student wants to draw is actually supported. That work is better done on a shared screen than on paper, because both people see the same graph being built and annotated in real time.

The one thing to be clear about is materials. We do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads; tutors reference them and link to the official source. A provider offering a complete folder of everything is describing something they should not be doing, and it is a reasonable signal about the rest of their practice.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to teach physics privately in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no figure can honestly be quoted and we do not quote one.

One boundary applies directly to physics, where the pool of qualified teachers in any emirate is small and parents sometimes approach the school. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being relied on as exact wording. The practical rule stands regardless: do not engage your child's own physics teacher privately.

Finally, what nobody is approved for. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Nor do we describe any tutor as a current examiner, because that status cannot be evidenced from a website and should never be implied to confer access to marking or boundaries.
