faqs.question: What time should a physics session run for a Jumeirah Golf Estates student?
faqs.answer: Between 6.30pm and 8.15pm on weekdays, and later if there is training. Work your own row: campus finish between 2.45pm and 3.30pm, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue, twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving depending on whether the school is in JVT or out at Al Sufouh, then twenty minutes before a teenager can think. Physics tolerates tiredness worse than any other Diploma subject, because it requires holding a model, applying mathematics and tracking units at the same time. Weekend mornings suit full timed papers.

faqs.question: Is my child's physics problem actually a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Often, and one marked paper settles it. Physics-reasoning weakness looks like a blank page or a wrong starting equation. Mathematical weakness looks like the correct starting equation followed by an algebraic slip, an unconverted unit, or a rearrangement done in the wrong order. The second pattern is cheaper to fix and the fix transfers straight into Mathematics. At Higher Level the overlap is larger, since fields and quantum content assume comfortable work with indices, logarithms and trigonometric resolution of vectors.

faqs.question: How is the IB physics investigation marked?
faqs.answer: It is worth 20 per cent of the grade and marked out of 24 across four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Confirm the current criteria with your school, since the science guides were restructured relatively recently. The structure matters because the design criterion is settled before a single measurement is taken: a question that cannot generate enough usable data produces a capped mark that no amount of later writing recovers. Evaluation is where strong students lose marks, by listing generic improvements instead of specific systematic errors.

faqs.question: When is the best moment to get help with the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Twice, in two short blocks, and not in between. Three sessions before the laboratory work, to interrogate the research question, check that the expected readings are measurable with the available equipment, and confirm a variable can genuinely be controlled. Then two sessions after collection, working through the raw data on a shared screen: plotting, testing for a straight-line form, propagating uncertainties, and checking the conclusion is actually supported. During the weeks when measurements are being taken there is very little a tutor can usefully add.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of my child's physics report?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor can question the research design, point out that a method will not produce analysable data, explain what each of the four criteria rewards, mark a draft against them and teach uncertainty convention and referencing. A tutor cannot write any part of the report, rewrite the student's prose, supply a research question as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit a draft to completion. One operator in this market was found selling completed Internal Assessments; buying one is malpractice and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Which four habits cost physics candidates the most marks?
faqs.answer: Four places, none of them conceptual. Units and significant figures: a numerically correct answer with a missing unit loses the mark, and figures copied straight from a calculator get marked down. Direction: velocity, force and field strength are vectors and students treat them as numbers. The controlled variable: experiments described without naming what was held constant forfeit marks explicitly available for it. And explanation vocabulary: thermal answers given in terms of temperature where the scheme wants particle behaviour and mean kinetic energy.

faqs.question: Which physics theme needs the most tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Fields, by a clear margin, particularly at Higher Level. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits, electromagnetic induction and the Higher Level extensions into orbital motion and field potential together account for most of the session count we propose. Circuits specifically collapse when a diagram is unfamiliar rather than when the theory is missing. By contrast, nuclear and quantum physics is content-dense but self-contained, which makes it one of the most efficient themes to tutor at four or five focused sessions.

faqs.question: How much does IB physics tuition cost around here?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates for a qualified online subject tutor run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with specialist IB and A-Level provision quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above and one UK agency at AED 270. For physics the useful figure is the block rather than the hour: two or three sessions for data analysis, four or five for nuclear and quantum, ten to fourteen for Higher Level fields taught properly. Those are market rates researched in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices, which follow the free trial.

faqs.question: Does online physics tuition work without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: For the taught parts, yes, and for the practical sense a student develops, no. The school laboratory is where parallax on a metre rule and reaction time against a short interval become real, and nothing over video substitutes for that; we would not claim it does. What video does better than paper is the analysis: a graph built and annotated on a shared screen where both people see it, with uncertainties propagated step by step. The practical work belongs at school and the reasoning around it works well online.

faqs.question: My child takes Applications and Interpretation maths and Physics HL. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It can be, and it is worth planning for rather than discovering. Physics Higher Level assumes comfortable manipulation of indices, logarithms and trigonometric resolution, some of which an Applications and Interpretation student may meet less of elsewhere in their timetable. The practical answer is a short mathematical-fluency block of four to six sessions before the fields theme arrives, which is better value than more physics teaching during it. One marked paper shows clearly whether this is the operating constraint.

faqs.question: Is one physics session a week enough at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: One, in almost every case, with two in the final run-in to the May session. The reason is that a student needs time between sessions to attempt problems unaided, and the unaided attempt is where the learning happens. Two or three weekly slots on top of a full Dubai timetable and training in Dubai Sports City produces attendance rather than progress. The exception is a genuine content backlog in fields, where a short period of two sessions a week can close a gap that one cannot.

faqs.question: Can physics sessions move during Ramadan or exam weeks?
faqs.answer: Yes, and online delivery is what makes it straightforward. Sessions shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan, move within the week when an investigation deadline or a tournament collides, and pause entirely through mock and final examination weeks. Nobody's round trip has to be renegotiated, so it is usually settled in the same week. We also agree a stop date at the start, normally study leave or a named deadline, so a physics arrangement is reviewed deliberately rather than renewed out of habit.

faqs.question: Is there a physics specialist near Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is better to say so. Physics Higher Level teachers are scarce in any school system, and the catchment of a single villa community of a few thousand households is unlikely to contain one who is also free at the hours your child can work. That arithmetic is why we match online by level and theme rather than by distance. Where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, we say so before any payment, including which time zone they teach from.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free for Higher Level physics when we need it?
faqs.answer: You get the realistic wait, not a substitute. Availability is thinnest in the eight weeks before the May session, which is exactly when demand peaks, and for the fields theme specifically. In that situation we will offer a shorter diagnostic block or a data-analysis block that can run with a different specialist, and tell you when the Higher Level teacher becomes free. intro.heading: What a physics specialist knows that a science teacher may not
paragraphs: A capable physics teacher knows physics. A Diploma physics specialist knows four additional things, and those four decide whether a term of tutoring changes a grade. They are: how the components are weighted and what each one actually asks for, how the internal investigation is marked, where this specific course loses marks that have nothing to do with physics, and where Higher Level genuinely separates from Standard.

Take the second of those. The sciences investigation is marked against four criteria on the current published arrangement -- research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation -- for a total of twenty-four marks. Design carries as much as analysis, which means most of the mark is decided before any apparatus is touched. A tutor who has never read those descriptors cannot help with the component students handle worst.

Or the third. Physics students routinely lose marks with the physics entirely correct: a gradient quoted without units, significant figures inconsistent within an answer, a value given to five figures from two-figure data. And in extended response, answering why something happens by describing what happens, or abandoning a four-mark question after one blocked step. None of that is a physics gap.

The fourth is the one that most often goes wrong in hiring. Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra chapters. The additional material in fields, induction and quantum physics changes the character of the questions, which assume a student can combine two or three ideas in one answer with explicit reference to mechanism. A tutor strong at Standard Level can run out of depth about four weeks into Higher Level work.

Supply makes this harder locally. The International Baccalaureate accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum, and Higher Level physics is among the thinnest specialisms within that. Jumeirah Islands has no school inside the gates, so the community's Diploma students are scattered across several schools and there is no local concentration to draw a tutor from.

One more fact changes how a family here should plan. The dates that actually govern a Diploma physics year are mostly set by your child's school rather than by the IB: the investigation deadline, the mock window and the internal milestones. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates on this site, because the IB's own site is the authority and we have not verified them. Ask the coordinator for the school's calendar in September.

IB Gram matches on subject and level and teaches live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For physics the shared screen is a real advantage, because diagrams, derivations and marked papers all live better on it than on a kitchen table.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-islan.subjectsIntro: What a Diploma physics specialist should be able to say about each topic area. Use these as test questions; the answers are specific and checkable.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: A specialist names vector resolution as the failure that matters, because students resolve by remembering which is sine and which is cosine rather than reading the triangle. That error survives two years and reappears in circular motion, inclined planes and fields. It needs geometry, not more formulae.

subjects.name: Circular motion and gravitation
subjects.description: A specialist knows students invent an outward force rather than identifying what provides the centripetal effect, and that the error is conceptual so revision does not touch it. The fix is diagram work in which the student names the real force every time.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, interference, diffraction, standing waves and the Doppler effect. A specialist points at phase and path difference as the marks-loser, because students memorise a condition without being able to draw the situation that produces it, and the drawing is what the question tests.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: A specialist names the potential divider as the single most mishandled topic in the course. Students treat circuits algebraically when the reliable method is to reason about the physical situation first and calculate second. Three sessions usually rebuilds it properly.

subjects.name: Fields and electromagnetic induction
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated together, with flux, induction and Lenz's law. This is where Higher Level separates and where a generalist runs out. A specialist can explain how the three field types are taught as one structure rather than as three topics.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and energy
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, gas laws, energy production and transfer. A specialist knows calculation marks are usually secure and explanation marks are not, because students describe what happens without naming the mechanism the question asked about.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: HL and SL, with HL depth
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, mass defect, and quantum phenomena at Higher Level. A specialist flags unit and order-of-magnitude errors in mass-energy calculations, and notes that the quantum material arrives late and is routinely under-revised relative to its weight.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.description: Graph reading, gradients with units, error bars and propagated uncertainty. A specialist calls this the best-value topic in the subject, because it earns marks in the written papers and again in the investigation. Students skip it because it feels like mathematics.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: Long answers combining two or three ideas with explicit reference to mechanism. A specialist can describe the difference between describing an outcome and explaining a cause, and can show it on a mark scheme. It is trainable with marked past papers and nothing else.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A specialist names the four criteria and says that design carries as much as analysis, then explains that a tutor may teach criteria and comment on drafts and may never write any part of it. Any other answer ends the conversation.

sections.heading: Six things to ask a physics tutor before you hire them
paragraphs: These questions have specific answers, which is why they work better than reading a CV. Ask them in the trial session, before price comes up, and listen for whether the answer is precise or general. A tutor who says they will confirm a detail with the school and then does so is fine; one who glides past it will be guessing for a term.

First: which components does this course have at my child's level, and roughly how are they weighted? Second: how is the investigation marked, and what are the criteria called? Third: where does this course lose marks when the physics is correct? Fourth: what changes between Standard and Higher Level, specifically?

Fifth: what will you ask us for before the first session? The right answer is a marked paper and the school's assessment calendar, because the deadline that matters for the investigation is set by the school rather than the IB. Sixth: what will you not do? The right answer includes not writing any part of the investigation and not promising a grade.

The answers to the third and fourth questions are the most diagnostic. A specialist names unit and significant-figure discipline, describing rather than explaining, and abandoning multi-step questions. On the level question they name fields, induction and quantum depth rather than saying Higher Level covers more material.

On exam dates, note what a careful tutor will not do: state a specific IB session or results date as fact. The IB's own site is the authority and we do not publish those dates here. A tutor who quotes exact IB dates confidently without reference to the school's own calendar is working from something they have not verified.

sections.heading: Where Higher Level actually separates from Standard
paragraphs: This is the question that most often produces a mis-hire. The Higher Level course extends the same topics rather than adding separate ones, which sounds like a difference of quantity and is actually a difference of kind. The extension changes what questions ask for: synthesis and justification where Standard Level asks for recall and a clean calculation.

Concretely, the separation happens in fields and electromagnetic induction, in the quantum and nuclear depth added at Higher Level, and in the mathematical treatment running through all of it. A Higher Level extended-response question frequently requires two or three ideas combined, with the mechanism named explicitly, rather than one relationship applied correctly.

That is why a tutor can be genuinely effective at Standard Level across two sciences and out of their depth at Higher Level in either. It is not a criticism of the tutor; Higher Level depth takes sustained specialist teaching to maintain. It is, however, the most common mismatch in Dubai physics tutoring and it is invisible for about four weeks.

The test is specific rather than general. Ask how the three field types are taught together, or what Lenz's law actually lets a student predict, or how an induction question differs from a magnetic force question. A Higher Level specialist answers immediately. A Standard Level tutor hedges, and that hedge is worth more to you than any amount of stated experience.

sections.heading: The investigation, and what 'design' means in physics
paragraphs: On the current published arrangement the sciences investigation is marked against four criteria -- research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation -- for twenty-four marks. Criterion names and allocations are set by the IB and revised between syllabus cycles, so confirm them against your school's copy of the current subject guide rather than against this page.

The fact that changes behaviour is that design carries as much weight as analysis. A student who collects excellent data for a badly framed question has already lost marks that no amount of careful graphing recovers. The single most valuable hour of tutoring in the whole investigation happens before any apparatus is booked.

In physics a workable research question has four properties. The variable being changed can be controlled with school equipment. The quantity measured can be measured precisely enough that the change exceeds the uncertainty. The apparatus is actually available. And the expected relationship connects to accepted physics, so the conclusion can be discussed rather than merely reported.

Most failures breach the second property. A student measuring a small effect with an instrument too coarse to detect it produces data that cannot support anything, and discovers it in week three. That is a planning conversation, not a physics problem, and it is exactly what a specialist earns their fee on.

Evaluation is where the remaining marks go. Students write a conclusion and label it an evaluation, restating the result rather than assessing which source of uncertainty dominated, which control was weakest, and what a different approach would have improved. That is two or three sessions of writing practice and several marks.

sections.heading: Reading a marked physics paper properly
paragraphs: Hand a tutor a marked paper at the start of the trial and watch what they do with it. In physics the categories are unusually clean, and a specialist sorts them quickly. There are three, and they need different responses over different timescales.

The first is conceptual: vector resolution done by habit rather than geometry, an invented outward force in circular motion, a potential divider treated algebraically. These are few in number, findable from one paper, and once corrected they stay corrected. They are the best use of early sessions.

The second is presentation of correct physics: units missing from a gradient, significant figures inconsistent across an answer, a derived value quoted to five figures from two-figure data. This is examiner-level discipline and it recovers marks on every paper. It costs very little to teach and is the cheapest improvement in the subject.

The third is extended-response technique: answering why by describing what, abandoning a four-mark question after one blocked step, naming the right physics without connecting it to the specific situation in the question. This needs marked past papers and a conversation about each decision rather than more content.

There is a fourth category that looks like physics and is not: the mathematics. A student who cannot rearrange a formula with the subject on both sides, or who resolves vectors by recalling which ratio to use, fails physics questions for mathematical reasons. A session or two of algebra inside a physics hour often moves more marks than more physics would.

sections.heading: Practical work when the tutoring is online
paragraphs: This is the honest limitation and the question families here ask most. Your child's practical physics happens at school, with the school's apparatus, under the teacher's supervision, and no tutor substitutes for that. What a tutor does is everything either side of the laboratory, which is where most of the investigation marks actually sit.

Before: narrowing the research question, choosing a measurable variable, identifying what must be controlled, checking that the instrument's precision is finer than the effect being measured, and planning the range and number of readings so the data can support a conclusion. All of that is paper work and it determines most of the research design mark.

After: processing the data, plotting with error bars, finding a gradient with units, propagating uncertainty, and writing an evaluation that assesses the method rather than restating the result. Again paper work, and the part students handle worst. A shared screen with the spreadsheet open is a better environment for it than two people over a printed table.

What online delivery does not do is hands-on apparatus coaching. If your child specifically needs someone beside them handling equipment, in-person provision is better and we will say so rather than taking the booking. IB Gram has no home-visit service and no centre in the UAE, so for that requirement you need a local provider.

For everything else the format is at least neutral and often better, because a free-body diagram can be redrawn five times in a minute and the student keeps the written record of the session instead of losing a loose sheet by Thursday.

sections.heading: What we can honestly staff, and when
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, so here is ours. Standard Level physics is reasonably covered and usually matched within the same week. Higher Level physics is scarce, and scarcest of all in a weekday slot between 17:00 and 19:00 during the spring term, which is when every Diploma family in Dubai wants the same hour.

That scarcity is structural rather than tactical. Teaching Higher Level physics well needs depth in fields, induction and quantum phenomena, the mathematics to support it, and familiarity with how the investigation is marked. A tutor with four Higher Level students already has a full early evening, and insisting they also drive to a gated community removes most of the remainder.

The leverage available to you is timing, and it costs nothing. A weekly Higher Level slot booked in September costs the same per hour as one booked in March and gets a materially better tutor, because in September the specialist's calendar is still open. That is simply how a calendar of one-to-one appointments fills.

That scarcity has a consequence most providers leave you to discover later. Where a Higher Level physics specialist covering a UAE family is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book rather than after the first lesson - and in this subject the disclosure is needed more often than in anything else we staff, because the pool able to teach fields, induction and quantum phenomena at Higher Level is not deep enough inside the Emirates to fill that 17:00 to 19:00 ring on its own. A parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it at all, which turns a perfectly workable arrangement into something that feels concealed.

If a combination is not free you are told, with a date, and offered a choice: an off-peak or weekend slot with the specialist, an interim tutor with a stated handover, or a wait. The table sets out where supply currently sits.

sections.heading: Scheduling physics from a community with no school
paragraphs: Jumeirah Islands has no school inside the gates, so every student travels out and back. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30, and a bus route serving this community usually calls at two or three others first, putting arrivals home between about 15:40 and 16:50 depending on the school and the route order.

The dependable weekday start is therefore 17:00, and 17:30 for children returning from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. A 16:30 slot is nominally available and loses its first twenty minutes to settling, which in a cumulative subject means the arrangement feels less effective than it is and gets dropped.

For physics the slot splits by work type. Quantitative work and derivations belong earlier, because arithmetic and algebraic accuracy are the first casualties of tiredness. Conceptual discussion and investigation planning tolerate a later slot, and second-year students frequently do better at 19:30 for that kind of work than at five o'clock.

Use the weekend for long work. A Saturday morning slot is the only ninety-minute block in a Jumeirah Islands week, which makes it the right place for a full timed paper or for processing investigation data properly, with Sunday used to review what came out of it.

During Ramadan the pattern shifts: shortened school hours, later households, and a post-Iftar or late-morning weekend session working better than anything at five in the afternoon. We reschedule rather than cancel, and because nobody travels a change is a slot swap rather than a negotiation.

sections.heading: Rates, limits and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200. Specialist IB tuition sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65, which buys supervision rather than Higher Level physics.

In-home visits run AED 180-350 on Bestimate's figures, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500. For monthly planning, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All are the providers' own figures, read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram price.

On coursework the limit is absolute. A tutor may explain the four criteria, help narrow a research question, teach uncertainty treatment and graphical analysis, and read the student's draft and name which descriptor band it meets. A tutor may not write, part-write, rewrite or supply any part of it. Operators in this market sell completed internal assessments at four-figure prices, and the consequence falls on the student.

We do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; they are cited and linked, and your child's school holds licensed access. We publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage, because a statistic without its sample size, date and method cannot be checked.

One approval claim circulates in physics more than in any other subject - that a tutor is a current IB examiner, which would conveniently explain how anybody knows where investigation marks go - and we make neither that claim nor any other we cannot hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit. What a physics specialist covering a Jumeirah Islands family does need is the individual permission: a MoHRE private tuition work permit, free and valid for two years. Ask to see it, because it costs the tutor nothing to hold and nothing to mention, and a provider that answers a question about approval with a logo has answered a different question.

faqs.question: What would a real Diploma physics specialist know that a science teacher might not?
faqs.answer: Four things. How the components are weighted at your child's level and what each asks for. How the internal investigation is marked, which on the current arrangement is four criteria for twenty-four marks with research design carrying as much as data analysis. Where this course loses marks when the physics is correct, meaning units on gradients, significant figures and describing instead of explaining. And where Higher Level separates from Standard, which is fields, induction and quantum depth rather than simply more content.

faqs.question: How do we test whether a tutor can handle Higher Level rather than Standard?
faqs.answer: Ask something specific rather than general. How are the three field types taught together? What does Lenz's law actually let a student predict? How does an induction question differ from a magnetic force question? A Higher Level specialist answers immediately and in detail. A Standard Level tutor hedges or answers at a level of generality that could apply to any course, and that hedge is the most useful information you will get in the whole trial session.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor come to our house in Jumeirah Islands?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. Physics tuition for families inside these gates is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared surface for free-body diagrams and derivations. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel if presence in the room is essential for your child, and for hands-on equipment work it genuinely may be.

faqs.question: How does the investigation work if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The laboratory work happens at school with the school's apparatus and supervision, as it would in any case. The tutoring covers everything either side, which is where most of the marks sit: narrowing the research question, checking that the instrument's precision is finer than the effect being measured, confirming the apparatus is available, then processing data, plotting with error bars, propagating uncertainty and writing an evaluation that assesses the method rather than restating the result.

faqs.question: What makes a physics research question actually workable?
faqs.answer: Four properties. The variable you change can be controlled with school equipment. The quantity you measure can be measured precisely enough that the change exceeds the uncertainty. The apparatus is genuinely available. And the expected relationship connects to accepted physics, so the conclusion can be discussed rather than merely reported. Most failures breach the second: a small effect measured with a coarse instrument produces data that cannot support anything, and the student finds out in week three.

faqs.question: Our child's physics is right but the marks are low. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Presentation and technique, almost certainly. Units omitted from a gradient, significant figures inconsistent within an answer, a value quoted to five figures from two-figure data. Then extended-response habits: answering why something happens by describing what happens, or abandoning a four-mark question after one blocked step. These are examiner-level discipline rather than physics, they are visible on any marked paper, and they are the cheapest marks in the subject to recover.

faqs.question: Is some of our child's physics problem actually a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is worth checking early. A student who cannot rearrange a formula with the subject appearing on both sides, or who resolves vectors by recalling which ratio to use rather than reading the triangle, will fail physics questions for mathematical reasons. A session or two of algebra inside a physics hour often moves more marks than more physics would. A specialist spots this from a marked paper rather than from a conversation about topics.

faqs.question: When should physics support start for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: The autumn of the first Diploma year, one hour a week, rising to two or three per week in the final weeks. Physics compounds in a specific chain: mechanics underpins fields and fields underpin induction, so an unresolved misunderstanding multiplies rather than sitting still. Starting in the spring of the second year means more sessions at the scarcest time, competing for the fullest calendars, which is the highest cost per unit of improvement available.

faqs.question: How long does the potential divider take to fix?
faqs.answer: About three sessions, and it is worth doing properly because it is the single most mishandled topic in the course. The problem is that students treat circuits algebraically, applying relationships without a model of what the circuit is doing, so anything non-standard defeats them. The fix is to reason about the physical situation first and calculate second, which takes rebuilding rather than revision. Electricity as a whole is usually the best use of early sessions.

faqs.question: Which topics tend to be under-revised before the papers?
faqs.answer: Quantum phenomena at Higher Level, because the material arrives late in the course, and data analysis with uncertainties, because students classify it as mathematics and skip it. Both are unusually trainable: the quantum content is finite, and data analysis is a procedure that earns marks in the written papers and again in the investigation. Together they are the best-value revision target in the subject and they are routinely left until there is no time for them.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take physics and chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: We generally advise against it. Genuine depth in Higher Level physics and Higher Level chemistry is rare in one person, and a tutor stretched across both tends to be strong in one and adequate in the other, which you will discover in about a month. Two tutors on two fixed evenings is also easier to protect in a household where everyone travels to school. Ask directly which level they have taught each subject to, then ask a specific question in each.

faqs.question: Why is Higher Level physics harder to book than other subjects?
faqs.answer: Because the specialism is thin and the demand is concentrated. Teaching it well needs depth in fields, induction and quantum phenomena plus the mathematics and knowledge of how the investigation is marked, and a tutor with four Higher Level students already has a full early evening. Every Diploma family in Dubai wants a weekday slot between 17:00 and 19:00 in the spring term. Booking in September costs the same per hour and gets a materially better tutor.

faqs.question: What time should a physics session be from these gates?
faqs.answer: 17:00, or 17:30 if your child travels back from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, because with no school inside Jumeirah Islands every pupil travels out and arrives home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50. Split by work type: quantitative work and derivations earlier, when accuracy is best, and conceptual discussion or investigation planning later, where 19:30 often suits a second-year student. Keep Saturday morning for a full timed paper or for processing investigation data.

faqs.question: Do you publish the IB exam dates we should plan around?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own site is the authority for session and results dates and we have not verified them independently, so we will not restate a date a parent might act on. What we will say is that Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session and that the dates governing your year are mostly the school's internal ones: investigation deadlines, Extended Essay milestones and mock windows. Ask the IB coordinator for the school's calendar in September.

faqs.question: Our child may drop physics from Higher to Standard Level. Can you advise?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic session will tell you more than a term of worrying, and the decision belongs with the school. What we can say is that the drop is usually possible early in the first Diploma year and rarely sensible once the second has started, and that some degree routes specify the Higher Level course. Read the published entry requirements for the programmes your child is considering before anyone reduces a level to relieve workload, because the relief is immediate and the cost arrives later.

intro.heading: What IB physics support costs, and why
paragraphs: Physics sits at the expensive end of the Dubai tutoring market for a straightforward reason: the supply of people who can teach Higher Level physics well is much smaller than the demand for them. Published rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, and specialist IB work at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's Dubai survey, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270. At the premium end BartyED publishes AED 650.

So the first thing worth saying to a Jumeirah Park family is that the budget end of the market is not a cheaper version of the same thing. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. That buys homework supervision, which has real value for a student who will not start without company, and almost none for a student who cannot interpret a Paper 2 extended-response question about induction.

The second thing is to plan monthly rather than hourly. Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 a month for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support in one subject. Physics sits in the upper two bands if the tutoring is going to do anything, and that number decides whether the arrangement survives a term.

The third, and the one that saves the most money, is timing. Physics compounds: mechanics underpins fields, fields underpin induction, and a student who never properly understood vector resolution in the first term will struggle with everything that rests on it. A weekly hour from the autumn of the first Diploma year costs more in total hours and far less in total money than an emergency programme in the spring of the second.

On delivery, IB Gram matches your child to a physics specialist and teaches live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For physics this is less of a compromise than parents assume, because the work is diagrams, derivations and marked past papers, all of which live better on a shared screen than on a kitchen table.

For household context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. That stabilises one line in the budget while you plan this one, which is a better starting position than families here have had for several years.

What it does mean is that you are not paying a travel premium. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180-350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. The difference against the online specialist band is a commute across Al Khail Road at half past five, and in physics the tutor you most want is the least likely to make it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: What physics tutoring actually works on, topic by topic, with the place each one costs marks. These double as test questions for any tutor you are considering.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws, momentum and energy. The failure that matters is vector resolution: students who resolve on autopilot rather than from the geometry get inclined-plane and circular-motion questions wrong for two years. Fixing it early pays for itself across the whole course.

subjects.name: Circular motion and gravitation
subjects.description: Centripetal acceleration, orbital motion and gravitational fields. Students confuse the force providing the centripetal effect with a separate force acting outward, and the error survives revision because it is conceptual rather than computational. It needs diagram work, not more formulae.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, interference, diffraction, standing waves and the Doppler effect. Phase and path difference questions are where marks disappear, usually because the student has memorised a condition without being able to draw the situation that produces it.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. The potential divider is the single most reliably mishandled topic in the course. Students treat circuits algebraically when the reliable approach is to reason about the physical situation first and then calculate.

subjects.name: Fields and electromagnetic induction
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated together, with induction, flux and Lenz's law. This is where Higher Level separates from Standard Level, and where a generalist tutor usually runs out of depth about four weeks in. It needs a specialist and it needs time.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and energy
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the gas laws and energy production and transfer. Calculation marks are usually secure; explanation marks are not, because students describe what happens without naming the mechanism the question asked about.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, mass defect and, at Higher Level, quantum phenomena. Mass-energy calculations are a frequent source of unit and order-of-magnitude errors, and the quantum material arrives late in the course and is routinely under-revised.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.description: Reading graphs, gradients with units, error bars and propagated uncertainty. It appears both in the written papers and in the investigation, which makes it the best-value topic to tutor in the whole subject: one skill, marks in two places.

subjects.name: Extended-response technique
subjects.description: Long answers that require combining two or three ideas, with explicit reference to the physical mechanism. Students lose marks by describing the outcome rather than explaining the cause, and by abandoning a multi-part question after one blocked step. Trainable with marked past papers.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, marked against published criteria. A tutor may teach the criteria, help narrow a research question, teach uncertainty treatment and comment on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write, part-write or supply any of it.

sections.heading: Why Higher Level physics costs more to staff
paragraphs: This is the supply side of the price, and it is rarely explained. Teaching Higher Level physics well requires someone comfortable with fields, induction and quantum phenomena at the level the extended-response questions probe, plus the mathematics to support it, plus familiarity with how the investigation is marked. That combination is scarce everywhere and particularly scarce in any one city neighbourhood.

Demand is also concentrated. Across Dubai, physics tutoring requests cluster in the same weeks, around mocks and the final term, and in the same hours, weekday 17:00 to 19:00. A tutor with four Higher Level students already has a full early evening. Insisting that the same person also drive into Jumeirah Park eliminates most of the remaining candidates.

The consequence for a family here is that timing is leverage. Booking a weekly Higher Level physics slot in September costs the same per hour as booking one in March and gets a materially better tutor, because in September the specialist's evening is not yet full. That is not a scarcity tactic; it is how any calendar of one-to-one appointments fills.

sections.heading: How physics is assessed, and what that means for spending
paragraphs: Knowing the structure stops you buying the wrong hours. On the current published arrangement, physics is examined by written papers that combine multiple-choice and data-based questions with extended response, alongside an internally assessed scientific investigation worth around a fifth of the grade at both levels. Structures and weightings are set by the IB and revised between syllabus cycles.

The spending implication is that about a fifth of the mark is coursework with an internal deadline, and it is the most coachable fifth in the course. A block of sessions on the investigation, bought in the term the school sets it, is better value per dirham than the same hours spent on content revision in the final weeks. Almost nobody sequences it that way.

The second implication concerns data analysis. Graph reading, gradients with units, error bars and propagated uncertainty appear both in the written papers and in the investigation. One skill, marks in two places, which makes it the single best-value topic in physics to tutor. It is also routinely skipped because it feels like mathematics rather than physics.

A third implication is about the multiple-choice section, which rewards breadth with no gaps. A student who understands fields deeply and has never properly revised energy production will drop marks that a weaker but more evenly prepared candidate collects. That argues for coverage auditing late in the course rather than more depth in the topics the student already enjoys, and it is a cheap thing to do well.

Confirm the current paper structure and weightings with your child's teacher or the school's copy of the subject guide rather than from any tutoring page, this one included. The table sets out the components as commonly published, with that caution attached, and what each demands.

sections.heading: The investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: This is the part of the course where money is best spent and most often wasted. On the current published arrangement the sciences investigation is marked against four criteria -- research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation -- for a total of twenty-four marks. Criterion names and allocations are set by the IB and change between syllabus cycles, so confirm them against your school's copy of the current guide.

The distribution explains the common failure. Research design carries as much as data analysis, which means a student who collects excellent data for a poorly framed question has already lost marks they cannot recover later. The single most useful hour of tutoring in the whole investigation happens before any apparatus is touched, narrowing the research question until it can genuinely be answered.

Evaluation is the second place marks disappear. Students write a conclusion and call it an evaluation: restating the result rather than assessing the method, the sources of uncertainty, and what a different approach would have improved. That is a writing and reasoning skill, teachable in two or three sessions, and worth several marks.

What a tutor may do here is explain each criterion, help narrow the question, teach uncertainty treatment and graphical analysis, and read the student's draft and name which descriptor band it currently meets. What a tutor may not do is write, part-write, rewrite or supply any of it. We publish that limit because operators in this market do not observe it, and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: Where physics marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Three categories, and they need different money spent on them. The first is conceptual: vector resolution done by habit rather than geometry, the belief in an outward force in circular motion, potential dividers treated algebraically instead of physically. These are few in number, identifiable from one marked paper, and once corrected they stay corrected.

The second is presentation of correct physics. Units omitted from a gradient, significant figures inconsistent across an answer, a derived quantity quoted to five figures from two-figure data. Examiner-level discipline here recovers marks on every paper and costs very little to teach, which makes it the cheapest improvement available in the subject.

The third is extended-response technique. A question asking why something happens, answered by saying what happens. A four-mark question abandoned after the first blocked step. An answer that names the right physics without connecting it to the specific situation in the question. This is trainable with marked past papers and a conversation about each decision.

There is a fourth thing that looks like a physics problem and is not: the mathematics. A student who cannot rearrange a formula with the subject on both sides, or who resolves vectors by remembering which is sine and which is cosine rather than reading the triangle, will fail physics questions for mathematical reasons. A session or two of algebra inside a physics hour often moves more marks than more physics would.

A physics tutor should be able to tell you in the first session which of the three dominates for your child, from a marked paper. If the answer is a plan to revise the syllabus from topic one, the paper has not been read. That distinction is worth more to your budget than any hourly rate negotiation.

sections.heading: Practical work when the lessons are online
paragraphs: This is the honest limitation and the question Jumeirah Park parents ask most. Your child's practical physics happens at school, with the school's apparatus, under the teacher's supervision, and no tutor substitutes for that. What a tutor can do is everything around it, which turns out to be where most of the investigation marks actually sit.

Before the laboratory: narrowing a research question, choosing a measurable variable, identifying what has to be controlled, and planning the range and number of readings so that the data will support a conclusion. These decisions are made on paper, they determine most of the research design mark, and they are made better with a specialist on a screen than alone at a desk.

After the laboratory: processing the data, plotting with error bars, finding a gradient with units, propagating uncertainty, and writing an evaluation that assesses the method rather than restating the result. Again entirely paper work, and the part students handle worst. A shared screen with the spreadsheet open is a better environment for it than two people over a printed table.

If your child needs hands-on equipment coaching specifically, that is one of the genuine cases where in-person provision is better and we will say so. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and has no centre here, so for that requirement you need a local provider and should expect the published in-home premium of AED 180-500 an hour.

sections.heading: Scheduling physics from a Jumeirah Park address
paragraphs: Physics needs a slot where the student can concentrate for a full hour on something cumulative, which in this community means working around the school run. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30, and a Jumeirah Park bus route serving Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village returns most students between 15:20 and 16:40 depending on district.

There is no metro station inside Jumeirah Park, so the nearest Route 2020 stations at Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens have no bearing on a tutoring timetable. The practical window is roughly 16:30 to 21:00 on weekdays. Students at the school inside the community can hold 16:00; second-year Diploma students frequently do better at 19:30, after dinner, because derivation work needs a settled mind more than an early one.

For long work use the weekend. A Saturday morning slot is the only ninety-minute block in a Jumeirah Park week, and it is the right place for a full timed paper or for processing investigation data properly. Marking the paper together on Sunday is where the improvement happens rather than in the sitting of it.

Ramadan moves all of that. School hours shorten, so the bus returns well before the usual window, and households run later; a post-Iftar session or a late-morning weekend slot works better than anything at five in the afternoon, which during Ramadan is the least useful hour of the day for cumulative work. The Saturday block stays the right place for a timed paper, it simply starts later. We reschedule rather than cancel, and because nobody drives to a Jumeirah Park address a reschedule is a slot swap rather than a negotiation about somebody's evening.

One last scheduling point that applies to physics more than to other subjects: protect the week before a school assessment rather than the night before it. A session three days out can still change the method a student uses; a session the evening before changes nothing except anxiety. Families who plan around their child's internal assessment calendar rather than the exam date get noticeably more from the same number of hours.

sections.heading: What we will not sell, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: On a page about cost it matters to say what is not for sale. We do not write, part-write, rewrite or supply any part of a scientific investigation, Extended Essay or other assessed work. A tutor teaches the criteria and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments at four-figure prices; that is a malpractice trigger and the risk lands on the student.

We do not sell grade guarantees, promised score improvements or money-back schemes, because nobody can honestly deliver one. We publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage, because a statistic without its sample size, date and method is a liability rather than a credential, and several providers in this market publish two conflicting ratings on a single page.

We do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They are cited and linked; your child's school holds licensed access to what it needs. Anyone offering a folder of exam material is offering a copyright problem rather than an advantage.

And we claim no approval we do not hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit. Individual tutors in the UAE need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge and valid for two years.

faqs.question: Why is physics tutoring more expensive than most other subjects here?
faqs.answer: Because the supply of tutors who can teach Higher Level physics well is much smaller than demand, and demand concentrates in the same weeks and the same early-evening hours. Published Dubai figures put specialist IB tuition at AED 200-450 or more, with TutorChase around AED 270 and a premium tier at AED 650 on BartyED's figures. A qualified online subject tutor sits at AED 150-300. The budget band of AED 33-65 buys supervision, which does not teach induction.

faqs.question: Can we reduce the cost by starting physics support later?
faqs.answer: Usually it increases it. Physics compounds: mechanics underpins fields and fields underpin induction, so a misunderstanding from the first term multiplies. Starting in the spring of the second Diploma year means more sessions per week, at the scarcest time, competing for the fullest calendars, which is the highest cost per unit of improvement available. One weekly hour from the first year is both cheaper in total and more effective, and it secures a better tutor.

faqs.question: Does a physics tutor come to the villa in Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. Physics tuition for Jumeirah Park families is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared surface for diagrams and derivations. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and the premium buys the commute rather than more physics. If presence in the room is essential, hire locally.

faqs.question: How does my child do practical physics if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The practical work happens at school with the school's apparatus and the teacher's supervision, as it would anyway. What a tutor adds is the paperwork around it, which is where most investigation marks sit: narrowing the research question, deciding what to control, planning the range of readings, then processing data, plotting with error bars, propagating uncertainty and writing an evaluation. All of that is better done on a shared screen than alone. Hands-on equipment coaching is the genuine exception, and for that you need a local provider.

faqs.question: What are the four marks allocations in the sciences investigation?
faqs.answer: On the current published arrangement, four criteria share twenty-four marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with six marks each. Criterion names and allocations are set by the IB and revised between syllabus cycles, so confirm against your school's copy of the current subject guide. The practical consequence is that design carries as much as analysis, so the most valuable hour happens before any apparatus is used, narrowing the question until it can genuinely be answered.

faqs.question: Where does my child lose physics marks if the physics is right?
faqs.answer: Presentation and technique. Units omitted from a gradient, significant figures inconsistent within an answer, a value quoted to five figures from two-figure data. Then extended-response habits: answering why something happens by describing what happens, or abandoning a four-mark question after one blocked step. These are the cheapest marks in the subject to recover and the least often taught, because they feel too obvious to spend a session on. They are visible on any marked paper.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics genuinely harder, or just longer?
faqs.answer: Genuinely different in character. The additional material in fields, induction and quantum physics is not simply more content; the extended-response questions assume a student can combine two or three ideas in one answer with explicit reference to mechanism. That is where the marks separate. It is also why a tutor who is strong at Standard Level can run out of depth about four weeks into Higher Level work, which is the most common mismatch in Dubai physics tutoring.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week does a Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: One a week from the start of the first Diploma year, rising to two or three per week in the final weeks before the May session. More than that early in the course is usually wasted, because the student needs time to work between sessions and the school is still covering content. The pattern that costs least overall is weekly and early; the pattern that costs most is three a week from February, which is also when the scarcest tutors are least available.

faqs.question: Could the physics tutor also pick up the mathematics?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level often yes, and the overlap is useful because many physics errors are mathematical. At Higher Level we usually advise two tutors, because genuine depth in both Physics HL and Analysis and Approaches HL is rare and a tutor stretched across both tends to be strong in one. Two fixed evenings is also easier to protect in a Jumeirah Park household than one long combined session after a late bus. Ask directly which level they have taught each subject at.

faqs.question: After six physics sessions, what evidence should we be looking at?
faqs.answer: Specific question types that previously failed now scoring on timed work, and your child able to explain a mechanism without prompting rather than describing an outcome. Not a predicted grade. If the marked evidence has not moved in six sessions, the match, the frequency or our diagnosis is wrong and one of those should change rather than more hours being bought. No honest provider will promise a grade, a mark or a percentage improvement.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying premium rates for an examiner-led physics tutor?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, with caution. For a scarce Higher Level subject in the final weeks, genuine expertise can justify the top of the market, which reaches AED 650 an hour on BartyED's published figures. But current examiner status is hard to verify, it must never be used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content, and it is not a substitute for teaching skill. Ask what evidences the claim. For most students the AED 200-450 specialist band does the work.

faqs.question: Our child is moving from IGCSE into Diploma physics. What should we buy?
faqs.answer: A short bridging block in the summer, focused on the mathematics rather than the physics. The gap into Diploma physics is usually vector resolution, rearrangement, graph interpretation and confidence with uncertainties, not unfamiliar content. Six to eight sessions with nothing else in the diary removes most of the first-term difficulty that otherwise needs weekly support to fix. It is the cheapest useful physics tutoring available to a family in this community.

faqs.question: Do you cover MYP sciences for a younger child?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is both cheaper and more valuable than most parents expect. MYP sciences is marked against criteria covering inquiry and design, processing and evaluating, and reflection, and marks are lost on process rather than content: a method that cannot be repeated, an uncontrolled variable, an evaluation that reports success. Those are exactly the habits Diploma physics assumes. A tutor needs the school's own task sheet and descriptors, which screen sharing handles well.

faqs.question: What happens if the Higher Level specialist we want is fully booked?
faqs.answer: You get told, with a date rather than a reassurance. The options are an off-peak or weekend slot with the specialist you wanted, an immediate start with a strong generalist and a stated handover date, or a wait. In the spring term, weekday 17:00 to 19:00 Higher Level physics can run to two weeks. Where a tutor is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time we say so before you book, because you are entitled to know who is teaching your child.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during exams or shift during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes to both. Many families pause in the fortnight when written papers are actually running and resume afterwards if a resit or the next year is in view. During Ramadan school hours shorten and households run later, so a post-Iftar slot or a late-morning weekend session usually works better than anything at five in the afternoon. Because no tutor travels, a reschedule is a slot swap rather than a renegotiation, and the weekly slot is held either way.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.closingHeading: Sequence the spending, then book early
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.closingBody: If you are pricing an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah Park, three decisions matter more than the hourly rate. Start in the first Diploma year rather than the second, because physics compounds and late help costs more for less. Spend a block on the investigation in the term the school sets it, because around a fifth of the grade sits there and it is the most coachable fifth. And buy data analysis early, because it earns marks in the papers and the investigation both. Our lessons are live online, one to one, with a free trial session first.

intro.heading: The comparison families make, and the one that matters
paragraphs: Jumeirah Village Circle sits in a ring of communities that feel like alternatives to each other. JVT is next door. Al Barsha South holds much of the school provision this whole cluster uses. Motor City is eight to fifteen minutes along Hessa Street. Families compare them for rent, for schools and for the commute, and when they start looking for a physics tutor they compare them for that too.

That comparison will not resolve, and the reason is worth understanding rather than asserting. Physics teachers who have taught the IB Diploma to examination standard are scarce in absolute terms. The International Baccalaureate accounts for about 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, only a portion of that cohort takes physics, and only a portion of those take it at Higher Level. The resulting population across the whole emirate is small and almost entirely employed full time. Those people live wherever they happen to live, and no mechanism concentrates them in one of these four communities rather than another.

So the useful comparison is not between areas. It is between subjects, and it explains a great deal about why finding a physics tutor feels harder than finding a mathematician. Mathematics is taught to every student in every school, so the teacher population is large. Biology has the deepest supply of the three sciences. Chemistry is thinner. Physics is thinnest, and Higher Level physics in the eight weeks before the May session is the single tightest request in this market.

The second comparison worth making is within physics itself: Higher Level against Standard Level, which are routinely described as the same course at different depths and behave as different subjects. The Higher Level extensions in fields and in quantum physics are substantial, the mathematical demand is materially higher, and a tutor who handles Standard Level comfortably may not be the right person for Paper 2 extended responses at Higher Level.

A third comparison is worth flagging early because it changes what you should buy first. A large share of students described as weak at physics have intact physical reasoning and failing mathematics: they know which relationship applies and cannot rearrange it under time pressure. Those two failures look different on a script, they cost roughly the same marks, and they have completely different fixes. One marked paper distinguishes them in twenty minutes, which is why we ask for the script rather than proposing to start at the beginning of the syllabus.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, matched by level and theme. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Confirm every weighting and criterion below against your school's subject guide, because science guides are periodically revised and your child's cohort version is the only one that counts.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.subjectsIntro: Physics divides into parts that fail in different ways and that differ sharply in how easy they are to staff. These are the ones Jumeirah Village Circle families ask for.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum and, at Higher Level, rotational dynamics. The characteristic error is treating velocity and force as plain numbers, which loses the vector mark while the magnitude is right.

subjects.name: Energy and power transfer
subjects.description: Work, energy, efficiency and conservation arguments. Marks are lost by producing numbers without naming the energy stores involved, which is explicitly what the extended-response scheme asks for. Three sessions corrects the habit.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, specific heat capacity, latent heat and the gas laws, with thermodynamic extension at Higher Level. Explanations given in terms of temperature where the scheme wants particle behaviour and mean kinetic energy are the standard loss.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Superposition, standing waves, interference, diffraction and the Doppler effect. Standing waves on strings and in pipes is the most commonly muddled item in the theme and is efficient to tutor, because the rules are finite and diagrammatic.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, substantial HL extension
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits, electromagnetic induction and, at Higher Level, orbital motion and field potential. The heaviest Higher Level theme and where most of the session count goes. Circuits collapse on unfamiliar diagrams rather than on missing theory.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, the photoelectric effect and, at Higher Level, further quantum phenomena. Content-dense and self-contained, so four or five focused sessions usually secures it — the most efficient theme in the subject.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.levels: SL and HL, assessed in the first paper
subjects.description: Gradients, error bars, uncertainty propagation and linearising a relationship. Assessed as its own skill, taught unevenly because it falls between the physics and mathematics departments, and frequently worth a grade boundary for two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Experimental technique and the investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: Research design, variable control, data collection and honest evaluation, marked out of 24 across four criteria. Valuable support sits before the data exists and then again at analysis, always as feedback on the student's own work.

subjects.name: Mathematical fluency for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging equations, indices, standard form, unit conversion and trigonometric resolution of vectors. Not a syllabus topic and very often the actual problem, particularly for a student taking Applications and Interpretation mathematics alongside Higher Level physics.

subjects.name: Extended response technique
subjects.description: Structuring a multi-mark explanation so each mark-scheme point is separately creditable. Students who know the physics lose marks by tangling three correct ideas into one sentence, of which an examiner can credit one.

sections.heading: Why physics is harder to staff than any other Diploma subject
paragraphs: Start from how teacher supply is produced. Mathematics is taught to every student in every school, so the mathematics teacher population in Dubai is large and a reasonable share of it has taught the Diploma. Biology is the most commonly chosen of the three sciences and has the deepest supply. Chemistry is thinner. Physics is thinnest, and the gap is not marginal.

Then narrow it to the IB. The International Baccalaureate accounts for about 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment, against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, out of 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25. A physics teacher in Dubai is far more likely to have taught A Level or a national curriculum than the Diploma. Narrow again to Higher Level and the population is very small, and nearly all of it is employed full time at the handful of campuses offering it.

That is the honest answer to a parent comparing Jumeirah Village Circle with JVT or Al Barsha South. You are comparing samples of the same small emirate-wide population, distributed by where individuals happen to rent. Moving house changes the school run and does not change which physicists can teach your child. It is also why a provider claiming a local Higher Level physics tutor for any community should be asked which school they teach at and which papers they have marked.

The practical response is to stop treating distance as a constraint and treat availability as the real one. The table compares the three sciences on how they actually staff, which is information no competitor page in this market publishes and which should change how early a family books.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, compared properly
paragraphs: Physics Higher Level and Standard Level are commonly described as the same course taught to different depths, which understates the difference. The Higher Level extensions sit within each theme rather than as separate options, and two of them are substantial: fields, which gains orbital motion and field potential, and nuclear and quantum physics, which gains further quantum phenomena. Rotational dynamics appears in the motion theme.

The mathematical demand is the other real difference. Higher Level physics assumes comfortable work with indices, logarithms, trigonometric resolution of vectors and, in places, rates of change. A student taking Analysis and Approaches alongside it meets that content in parallel; a student taking Applications and Interpretation may not meet some of it at all. That is a planning question for Year 11, not a discovery for Year 13.

The teaching consequence is that the two levels are not interchangeable staffing problems. A tutor who handles Standard Level comfortably — explaining circuits, kinematics and waves clearly — may be out of their depth on Higher Level field potential or on a Paper 2 extended response requiring four separately creditable points about induction. Asking which level somebody actually teaches is a fair and non-confrontational question.

For a family choosing between the levels in Year 11, the honest guidance is to check the published entry requirement for the degrees under consideration. Engineering and physics degrees commonly specify Higher Level physics; many other degrees do not require physics at all. Students sometimes carry Higher Level physics through two difficult years for a plan that never needed it.

sections.heading: Is it physics, or is it mathematics?
paragraphs: This is the most useful diagnostic comparison in the subject and it is settled by one marked script. A substantial share of students described as weak at physics have intact physical reasoning and failing mathematics. They know that the component of weight along the slope accelerates the block, and then cannot rearrange the resulting expression under time pressure.

The two patterns look different on paper. Physics-reasoning weakness appears as a blank, or as a wrong starting equation — the student did not know which relationship applied. Mathematical weakness appears as the correct starting equation followed by an algebraic slip, an unconverted unit, or a rearrangement performed in the wrong order. The second is cheaper to fix and the fix transfers straight into the student's mathematics course as well.

At Higher Level the overlap widens. Fields, orbital motion and quantum content all assume comfortable manipulation, and a student taking Applications and Interpretation mathematics may not be meeting that elsewhere in their timetable. Where that is the case, four to six sessions of mathematical fluency before the fields theme arrives is better value than more physics teaching during it.

So the instruction to a Jumeirah Village Circle parent is concrete: send the marked paper before asking for a quote, and ask the prospective tutor which of the two patterns they see, with examples from the script. A specialist will tell you. Somebody who proposes starting at the beginning of the syllabus has not looked at it.

sections.heading: Data analysis: the block nobody buys and everybody needs
paragraphs: The first physics paper assesses data analysis separately from content, and it is the single most reliably underprepared part of the course. The reason is structural rather than anybody's fault: it sits between the physics department and the mathematics department, so each assumes the other has covered it, and in many schools neither has done so explicitly.

What it requires is specific and learnable. Reading a gradient correctly from a graph with awkward axes. Drawing and interpreting error bars. Propagating an uncertainty through a calculation rather than quoting it and moving on. Recognising when a relationship can be linearised, and knowing what the gradient and intercept of the linearised form physically represent. None of that is conceptually hard and all of it has to be shown once.

Two or three sessions on real past-paper data sets usually covers it, which makes it the cheapest grade movement available in physics. It also pays twice, because the same skills are assessed again in the internally assessed investigation, where the data analysis criterion carries marks of its own and where uncertainties stated but never propagated is the standard loss.

This is also a point of comparison between the sciences worth knowing. Chemistry and biology both assess data handling, but physics leans on it hardest and expects the most formal treatment of uncertainty. A tutor who proposes a data analysis block before proposing content teaching has probably read the script properly.

It is also the one block whose availability is reliably good, because it does not require a Higher Level fields specialist. That makes it the sensible thing to run while waiting for a tighter match, rather than leaving a student idle for three weeks.
