sections.heading: Laboratory access, and what online tuition cannot replace
paragraphs: A comparison worth making honestly, because physics is a practical subject and we are not going to pretend otherwise. The school laboratory is where a student develops measurement sense: the parallax on a metre rule, the way reaction time dwarfs a short interval on a stopwatch, the drift on a thermometer that has not settled. Nothing delivered over video substitutes for that, and the investigation data has to be collected there on the school's timetable.

What video does better than paper is the work either side of it. Before the laboratory session, a tutor can interrogate the research question, estimate whether the expected range of readings is measurable with the available equipment, and spot that a variable cannot in practice be controlled — which saves laboratory time, a rationed resource in every school in this cluster. After the session, raw data can be plotted and annotated on a shared screen, uncertainties propagated step by step, and the student's intended conclusion tested against what the data actually supports.

Simulations are sometimes offered as an equivalent and they are not. They are useful for seeing a relationship cleanly and useless for learning that real measurements are noisy, which is half of what the evaluation criterion is assessing. A tutor who leans on simulations instead of asking what equipment the school has is working around a gap rather than addressing it.

One rule on materials. We do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. Tutors work from the copies the school provides and link to the official source. A provider offering a complete folder of everything is describing something they should not be doing.

sections.heading: The investigation: 24 marks and four criteria
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation carries 20 per cent of the physics grade and is marked out of 24 across four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Confirm the current criteria with your school, since the science guides were restructured relatively recently and schools work from the version their cohort sits.

In physics the design criterion is where projects are usually decided, and it is settled before any measurement. A question that cannot generate enough readings across a usable range, or where the controlled variable cannot genuinely be held constant with school equipment, produces a capped mark that no later writing recovers. Three sessions at that stage is a small block with a disproportionate effect, and it is the one families buy least often.

The evaluation criterion is where otherwise strong physicists lose marks. It asks for specific, honest limitation of the method — that the timing method introduced a systematic error of roughly a known size, and what that does to the conclusion — rather than a list of generic improvements. Writing that more repeats would have helped earns very little. That distinction is taught, not intuited.

The boundary is firm. A tutor may question the design, point out that a method will not produce analysable data, explain what each criterion rewards, mark a draft against the criteria, and teach uncertainty convention and referencing. A tutor may not write any part of the report, rewrite the student's prose, supply a research question as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit a draft to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line. One operator in this market was found selling completed Internal Assessments outright, which is malpractice with consequences that fall on the student.

sections.heading: What it costs, and when to book it
paragraphs: Rates are set by format and tutor category rather than by subject, so physics costs roughly what any specialist subject costs. Published Dubai figures: a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level provision at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, one UK-based agency at AED 270, premium named or examiner-led provision as high as AED 650, and budget online tuition from AED 45 to AED 150. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to AED 500.

What differs in physics is not the rate but the availability, and that is the comparison a family should actually plan around. Higher Level physics in the eight weeks before the May session is the tightest request in this market, because every Diploma family in Dubai wants the same very small group of people at the same two evening hours. A family that books in September chooses; a family that books in March accepts.

In blocks the figures are modest. Data analysis is two or three sessions. Nuclear and quantum physics is four or five. Wave behaviour is five or six. Higher Level fields is ten to fourteen, which is where most of the spend goes. Investigation support is three sessions plus two. A mathematical fluency block, where the script shows that is the real issue, is four to six.

Every figure here was read from the provider's own published page in October 2026 and describes the market rather than IB Gram, whose fee follows a free trial lesson. We make no examiner claims about any tutor, because current examiner status cannot be evidenced from a website and should never be implied to confer access to marking or grade boundaries.

sections.heading: Where a physics session fits in this cluster
paragraphs: The commute genuinely differs across these communities, and this is the one place the area comparison pays off. Most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South, or eight to fifteen to Motor City, and are home by about 3.45pm. Students commuting from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square are home after 4.30pm.

That short run looks like it should open an early slot and it usually does not, because Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take students out between four and six. So physics sessions work around 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for the many with one, with the later end for the outer belt.

Physics in particular should not be scheduled early and tired. It requires holding a physical model, applying mathematics to it, and tracking units and vector directions at the same time, which a student cannot do well at five o'clock after a full day. Mathematics tolerates fatigue better, because a familiar procedure can run on autopilot; physics does not.

Place the session after a first attempt at the school's problem set. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which is what forty minutes with a specialist resolves. Weekend mornings are the right slot for whole timed papers. Online delivery keeps it flexible: sessions move within the week when an investigation deadline or a fixture collides, shift post-Iftar during Ramadan, and stop at study leave, agreed on day one.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to teach physics privately here
paragraphs: Because the specialist pool is so small, families in this situation sometimes consider approaching the school directly, which makes the permit position worth knowing precisely. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

The eligible list is wider than most parents assume, and in a cluster where the physics pool is this thin it is worth reading properly: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category explains the cheapest cards pinned to JVC community boards, and a sixth-former is not disqualified from drilling kinematics even though they are plainly not the person for Higher Level fields and quantum phenomena. The penalty side is where honesty runs out. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted and we do not quote one - where a figure appears on a page serving JVC, JVT or Al Barsha South, somebody has supplied it from nowhere.

The boundary matters here more than in most subjects. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as exact wording. Whatever the precise text, scarcity is not a reason to engage your child's own physics teacher privately.

And what nobody in any of these communities holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IB physics tutor in Jumeirah Village Circle or in Al Barsha South?
faqs.answer: Neither, and physics is the clearest illustration of why. Physics teachers who have taught the Diploma to examination standard are scarce in absolute terms: the IB is about 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment, only a portion of that cohort takes physics, and fewer take it at Higher Level. The resulting population across the whole emirate is small and almost entirely employed full time. Those people live wherever they live, so both communities are drawing from the same small pool by accident of where individuals rent.

faqs.question: Why is physics harder to staff than chemistry or biology?
faqs.answer: Because the supply chain is narrower at every step. Biology is the most commonly chosen of the three sciences and has the deepest teacher supply; chemistry is thinner; physics is thinnest. Then the IB filter applies: a physics teacher in Dubai is far more likely to have taught A Level or a national curriculum than the Diploma. Then the Higher Level filter. Higher Level physics in the eight weeks before the May session is the single tightest request in this market, which is an argument for booking in September rather than March.

faqs.question: How different is Physics HL from SL, really?
faqs.answer: Different enough to need a different tutor. The Higher Level extensions sit within each theme rather than as separate options, and two are substantial: fields gains orbital motion and field potential, and nuclear and quantum physics gains further quantum phenomena, with rotational dynamics added to motion. The mathematical demand is materially higher, assuming comfortable work with indices, logarithms and trigonometric resolution. A tutor who explains Standard Level circuits clearly may be out of their depth on a four-point extended response about induction.

faqs.question: How do I tell physics reasoning from failing algebra on a script?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and one marked script settles it. Physics-reasoning weakness appears as a blank or a wrong starting equation — the student did not know which relationship applied. Mathematical weakness appears as the correct starting equation followed by an algebraic slip, an unconverted unit, or a rearrangement done in the wrong order. The second is cheaper to fix and transfers into the student's mathematics course too. At Higher Level the overlap widens, particularly for students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level physics.

faqs.question: What is the best-value short block in IB physics?
faqs.answer: Data analysis and uncertainties, at two or three sessions. The first paper assesses it separately from content, and it falls between the physics and mathematics departments at school, so each assumes the other covered it and often neither did explicitly. It requires reading gradients from awkward axes, drawing and interpreting error bars, propagating uncertainty through a calculation, and recognising when a relationship can be linearised. It also pays twice, because the same skills carry marks in the internally assessed investigation.

faqs.question: Which physics theme takes the most tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Fields, by a wide margin, and especially at Higher Level. Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits, electromagnetic induction and the Higher Level extensions into orbital motion and field potential together account for most of the session count we propose — typically ten to fourteen sessions against five or six at Standard Level. Circuits specifically collapse when a diagram is unfamiliar rather than when the theory is missing. Nuclear and quantum physics is the opposite: content-dense, self-contained and usually secure in four or five sessions.

faqs.question: Can online physics tuition work without laboratory access?
faqs.answer: For the taught parts yes, and for measurement sense no, and we would not claim otherwise. The school laboratory is where parallax on a metre rule and reaction time against a short interval become real, and investigation data has to be collected there on the school's timetable. What video does better than paper is the work either side: interrogating the research question before laboratory time is spent, then plotting and propagating uncertainties on a shared screen afterwards. Simulations are not a substitute, because they remove the noise the evaluation criterion assesses.

faqs.question: When should we get help with the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Twice, in two short blocks, and barely at all in between. Three sessions before the laboratory work, because the design criterion is settled before any reading is taken and a question that cannot generate enough readings across a usable range caps the mark permanently. Then two sessions after collection, on processing, uncertainty propagation and the evaluation — where strong physicists lose marks by listing generic improvements instead of naming a specific systematic error and its effect on the conclusion.

faqs.question: Would moving to a different community improve our physics options?
faqs.answer: No, though it might improve two other things. A move to JVT or Al Barsha South shortens the school run by ten or fifteen minutes each way, which is real time in a teenager's week, and a move to Dubai Hills Estate or Motor City may change school provision — including whether the school offers the Diploma at all rather than A Level. What it does not change is which physicists can teach your child, because that pool is emirate-wide and very small.

faqs.question: How does IB physics compare with A Level physics?
faqs.answer: A Level physics is narrower and deeper with a separate practical endorsement; IB physics is broader, carries a compulsory internal investigation worth a fifth of the grade, and sits inside a six-subject diploma with core components. Several schools in this cluster offer A Level rather than the Diploma, so it is a genuine choice for families weighing a move. Tutor supply for A Level physics in Dubai is a separate and somewhat deeper pool, because the UK curriculum is 37 per cent of private enrolment against the IB's 7 per cent.

intro.heading: Eight weeks is enough for some things and not others
paragraphs: The call usually comes with a deadline attached. A mock has come back at a 4, there are eight or ten weeks until the next assessment that matters, and the question is whether a physics tutor can do anything about it. The honest answer depends entirely on which component is losing the marks, and that is why this page is organised as a calendar instead of a syllabus summary. Some physics problems are eight-week problems. Others are not, and a provider who will not say which is which is not giving you information.

Start with the weightings, because they decide where eight weeks should go. In IB Physics, Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and splits into Paper 1A, which is multiple choice, and Paper 1B, which is data analysis. Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response: calculation, explanation and application across the syllabus. The scientific investigation, internally assessed in school and externally moderated, carries the remaining 20% and is marked out of 24 across four criteria. Those three numbers tell you that extended response is where most of the grade lives, and that the investigation is the single largest controllable block.

Now the triage. Multiple-choice performance on Paper 1A responds quickly, often within three weeks, because the loss is usually recall and misread stems rather than deep misunderstanding. Data analysis on Paper 1B responds quickly too, because it is a defined set of techniques — gradients, error bars, uncertainty propagation, linearising a relationship — and a student can be taught all of them in four sessions. Extended response on Paper 2 is slower, six to eight weeks, because it requires both content security and a structural habit: name the physics, then apply it, then evaluate. A student two grades short on content across the whole syllabus is not an eight-week project at all, and saying so is more useful than taking the booking.

The investigation is the component where a late start costs the most and where a tutor's legitimate role is narrowest. A student can control the research question, the method and the timeline, and the four criteria reward design, analysis, conclusion and evaluation in equal measure at six marks each. What a tutor may do is interrogate the research question, check the method can generate data that supports the planned analysis, explain what each criterion credits, and give feedback on the student's own draft. What a tutor may not do is write it, rewrite it, or supply the analysis.

What follows is the week-by-week plan, the component detail behind it, the uncertainty treatment students most often get wrong, the Dubai rate bands with their sources, a comparison of formats for a Jumeirah Village Triangle household, and the regulator and honesty footnotes that belong on every page in this set. No IB examination or results date appears anywhere on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and a date a family reorganises a term around has to be right.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-jumeirah-villa.subjectsIntro: The physics topics and components most often requested from the Jumeirah Village Triangle area, listed by where marks are actually lost rather than by syllabus order. Each entry says what the examination does with the topic.

subjects.name: Paper 1A, multiple choice
subjects.description: Recall, quick reasoning and the ability to read a stem precisely. Most loss here is not conceptual: it is misread wording, forgotten definitions and sign errors. It is the component that responds fastest to work, often within three weeks of daily short question sets.

subjects.name: Paper 1B, data analysis
subjects.description: Gradients, intercepts, error bars, uncertainty propagation and linearising a relationship to test it. A closed set of techniques, which makes it unusually teachable: four focused sessions normally covers all of them, and students who have never been taught them lose marks they could hold.

subjects.name: Paper 2, extended response
subjects.description: Forty-four per cent of the grade and the slowest component to improve. Marks are lost describing what happens instead of naming the law and applying it. The structural fix — state the principle, apply it, then evaluate — takes six to eight weeks to become automatic.

subjects.name: Mechanics and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum and energy. Sign conventions cause more loss than the physics does, particularly in momentum questions involving a reversal of direction. Graph interpretation of displacement, velocity and acceleration is assessed repeatedly.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance in combination, internal resistance and power. Students reproduce rules without applying them to the circuit in front of them, and lose marks reasoning about what happens when a component is changed in a network.

subjects.name: Fields and gravitation
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, potential and potential energy. The recurring error is confusing field strength with potential, and treating potential as a vector. Orbital questions require combining circular motion with the field law rather than recalling a single formula.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, superposition, interference, diffraction and standing waves. Phase relationships are where marks go, along with path-difference reasoning in interference questions where students substitute before deciding which condition applies.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the gas laws and the kinetic model. Marks are lost on unit conversion between degrees Celsius and kelvin, and on heating curves where a student applies a specific heat capacity across a phase change.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, mass defect and the photoelectric effect. Binding energy per nucleon questions require careful unit handling between electronvolts and joules, which is a high-frequency source of avoidable loss.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Internally assessed, 20% of the grade, 24 marks across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. Weak evaluations cost more than weak data: the criterion rewards discussion of methodological limitations and specific realistic improvements.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks have to achieve, week by week
paragraphs: A revision plan that says 'cover the syllabus' is not a plan. A plan says what each week produces and how you will know. The schedule below is the one we build for a DP2 student arriving with a marked mock, roughly eight weeks out, whose main loss is on Paper 2 extended response with secondary loss on Paper 1B. It is adjusted after the diagnostic session, but the shape holds for most students in this position.

The first two weeks are diagnostic and structural. Week one reads the mock and names the error patterns; week two installs the Paper 2 answer structure — name the physics, apply it, then evaluate — on questions the student already knows the content for, so the only new thing being learned is the structure. Weeks three and four add the data analysis technique set, because it is closed and fast and banking it early removes a worry.

Weeks five and six are content repair on the two or three topics the mock showed as weakest, worked through past questions rather than through notes. Weeks seven and eight are full timed papers, one a week, marked against the published scheme with the error log updated afterwards. The point of ending with timed papers rather than content is that by then the limiting factor is almost always time allocation and question selection, not knowledge.

Two honest caveats. If the diagnostic shows content weakness across most of the syllabus rather than in two or three topics, eight weeks does not fix it and the written diagnosis will say so, proposing a realistic target instead of the one you asked for. And if the scientific investigation is still unfinished, it takes priority over examination technique, because it is 20% of the grade with a hard internal deadline and the examination technique can still be worked on afterwards.

sections.heading: Where the grade actually lives: the component arithmetic
paragraphs: Physics students and their parents routinely misallocate revision because they think in topics rather than components. The grade is a weighted sum: Paper 1 at 36%, split between multiple choice and data analysis; Paper 2 at 44%; the scientific investigation at 20%. A student who revises content evenly across the syllabus is implicitly treating all three as equally improvable, which they are not.

Paper 2 is the largest single share and the slowest to shift, which means it should get the longest run rather than the most intensive one. The reason it is slow is that the loss is structural as well as factual: a student who writes a paragraph describing a phenomenon when the question asked them to explain it with reference to a named law has produced correct physics and scored at the bottom of the band. Installing the structure takes repetition over weeks, not a single explanation.

Paper 1 divides into two components with very different improvement curves. The multiple-choice section rewards recall and precise reading and responds quickly to daily short sets. The data-analysis section is a closed technique list and can be taught in about four sessions. Together they are over a third of the grade and they are the fastest third to move, which is why a compressed window should usually bank them before turning to extended response.

The investigation is 20% and is the only component where the student sets the timeline. It is marked out of 24 over four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion, evaluation. A strong investigation and a weak Paper 2 produces a very different grade from the reverse, and in a short window the investigation is frequently the better place to spend time precisely because it is not an examination.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: the marks almost nobody is taught to collect
paragraphs: Uncertainty treatment appears in the data-analysis section of Paper 1, in the investigation's data analysis and evaluation criteria, and incidentally in Paper 2 wherever a result has to be quoted sensibly. It is a small, closed and entirely learnable body of technique, and it is the most reliably neglected part of IB Physics teaching in any school system, because it does not feel like physics and it is not in the exciting part of the syllabus.

The content is short. Absolute uncertainty is the raw spread; fractional uncertainty is that divided by the value; percentage uncertainty is the fractional one expressed as a percentage. When quantities are multiplied or divided, fractional or percentage uncertainties add. When a quantity is raised to a power, its percentage uncertainty is multiplied by that power. When quantities are added or subtracted, absolute uncertainties add. The final answer is quoted to a precision consistent with its uncertainty, and the uncertainty itself to one significant figure in most cases.

Beyond propagation there is graphical uncertainty: error bars drawn from the absolute uncertainty, a line of best fit and lines of maximum and minimum gradient, and the uncertainty in the gradient inferred from those. Students who can do propagation algebraically often cannot do the graphical version, because it requires drawing carefully and reading values honestly rather than substituting into a formula.

And then linearising, which is the skill that makes a data question tractable: rearranging a proposed relationship into the form of a straight line so that a graph can test it, then identifying what the gradient and intercept physically represent. Four sessions covers all of this. For a student with secure content and a weak Paper 1B, it is the highest-yield block available in the subject.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the grade, 24 marks, four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion, evaluation. The symmetry matters. A student who collects excellent data and writes a thin evaluation has thrown away a quarter of the component, and evaluation is the criterion most often treated as a closing paragraph rather than as six marks of assessed work.

Research design credits a clear research question with defined independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a method described well enough to be repeated. The common failure is a research question that is not actually a question, or a method whose controlled variables are listed but not explained. Data analysis credits processing that is appropriate and complete, including uncertainty treatment and clear presentation — this is where the uncertainty work above pays off directly.

Conclusion credits an answer to the research question that is justified by the processed data and compared with accepted scientific context. Students lose marks here by restating the data rather than interpreting it, or by comparing with no literature value at all. Evaluation credits discussion of the method's specific limitations and realistic, targeted improvements. 'Human error' and 'more time' score nothing; 'the thermometer's resolution limited the temperature precision to half a degree, which propagates to a four per cent uncertainty in the specific heat capacity' scores.

On the honesty line, which matters more here than anywhere else in the subject. A tutor may interrogate the research question until it is answerable, check that the method will generate data capable of supporting the planned analysis, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, teach uncertainty treatment as a skill, and read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion a passage fails. A tutor may not design the investigation, process the data, write any part of the report, or edit prose to a standard the student cannot produce. Every submitted word is the student's own.

sections.heading: What a physics specialist costs in Dubai, and what a short window changes
paragraphs: A compressed calendar changes the pricing question. Over two years, hourly rate dominates total cost and it is worth optimising. Over eight weeks, the total is bounded — sixteen sessions at most on a twice-weekly block — and what matters is whether the person teaching has marked the component you are trying to fix. Paying AED 100 less an hour for somebody who has never taught Paper 1B uncertainty propagation saves perhaps AED 1,600 across the block and spends the component.

Published Dubai figures, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IB and IGCSE specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 including travel; TutorChase at AED 270 for specialist work; BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly, Bestimate estimates roughly AED 240-600, AED 600-1,200 and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for one weekly hour at the three tiers.

For an eight-week physics block the practical arithmetic is simple. One session a week at the specialist band is eight sessions; two a week is sixteen. Published packages in this market sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which maps onto exactly this kind of short intensive programme. IB Gram does not publish a fixed hourly rate on this page because level, component and urgency move it, and a quote follows the free diagnostic lesson rather than preceding it.

One piece of context worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat; a tutoring block is the variable decision in front of you.

sections.heading: Two sessions a week from Jumeirah Village Triangle, practically
paragraphs: An eight-week block at two sessions a week needs sixteen slots in the diary, and that is where the format decision becomes concrete rather than philosophical. From the Triangle, a Diploma physics student is commuting out of the community to school, so the realistic earliest start is about 17:30. Two sessions a week at that time, every week for eight weeks, is achievable online and very difficult with a visiting tutor.

The reason is travel. A tutor driving in from elsewhere in Dubai is spending forty to sixty minutes each way in term-time traffic, which normally requires a two-hour minimum booking and caps the latest workable start at roughly 18:30. Two two-hour visits a week in the late afternoon is a large imposition on a student who has already done a full school day and a commute, and the physics on offer in hour two of such a session is not usually the physics that moves a grade.

Online sessions can be 45 or 60 minutes, which is the right length for a focused component, and can run to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time, which means the second session of the week can sit after a sports fixture or a music lesson rather than displacing one. Every session is recorded, which in physics specifically matters: a student can rewatch the uncertainty propagation session three times during revision week at no additional cost.

A home visit still has genuine advantages for some students, and they are worth naming. A younger student who needs an adult present works better in person; apparatus handled physically helps some learners; a parent in earshot is easier to arrange. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE regardless, so the table below is there to let you compare the market honestly rather than to argue you out of something.

sections.heading: The calendar you can actually verify, and the one you cannot
paragraphs: A calendar-driven page has a duty to be straight about which dates are known. For the Diploma, UAE candidates sit the May session. That is as specific as this page goes, because ibo.org returns an error to automated checking and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. A family reorganises a term around an examination date, so publishing an unverified one would be worse than publishing none. Your school's Diploma coordinator has the real dates, and ibo.org is the authoritative source.

What can be verified are the deadlines your school sets, and for a physics student those are the ones that bite first. The scientific investigation has an internal submission deadline, usually preceded by a method approval point and a draft feedback point. The mock window is fixed by the school. So is the date by which any Higher Level content must have been taught. Ask the physics teacher for those four dates and the eight-week plan builds itself around them.

For students on the British route before the Diploma, the awarding bodies' positions are published and usable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not a UAE route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than trusting a restatement.

One Cambridge administrative rule applies to every Dubai candidate: centres are allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Get the zone from the examinations officer.

sections.heading: Starting inside a short window, and the footnotes that belong here
paragraphs: If the window is short, the sequence has to be fast. Send the level, the marked mock and the four school dates. A physics specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson, usually within a working day or two at this notice, and the written plan follows within a working day of that with a target against each week. Nothing is charged before you have read it, and if eight weeks cannot reach the grade you want, the plan says so and names what it can reach.

Availability for IB Physics is good at both levels for UAE evening slots, with a match normally inside one to three working days. The constraint when a family calls six weeks out is usually the slot rather than the specialist, particularly for twice-weekly blocks at 17:30. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking rather than afterwards.

Two footnotes that belong on every page in this set. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here.

And the claims we do not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the authorisation a Dubai training institute with premises requires, and we have no UAE office or centre. We do not describe tutors as current IB examiners, because examiner status for an individual cannot be evidenced here, and we would not use it to imply access to marking or paper content if it could.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent reading the student's own errors rather than teaching a topic. For physics the output is usually two or three patterns: describing instead of applying, uncertainty rules half-remembered, and time lost on the long questions at the end of Paper 2.

process.title: A written plan with a target per week
process.description: Within a working day, a plan naming what each week of the block has to achieve and how you will know it happened. If the honest assessment is that the window is too short for the target, the plan says that and proposes a reachable one instead.

process.title: Checked against the week-one diagnosis
process.description: At week four and week eight the error log is compared with the original diagnosis. Patterns that are closing confirm the plan; patterns that repeat mean the work between sessions is not happening or the diagnosis was wrong, and both are better found at week four than afterwards.

whyPoints.title: A calendar, not an open-ended commitment
whyPoints.description: The block has eight weeks, a target for each one, and a defined endpoint. You can see at week four whether it is working rather than discovering at the session that it was not, and the plan is in writing before any payment is taken.

whyPoints.title: Triage by component, not by topic
whyPoints.description: Paper 1A moves in about three weeks, Paper 1B in about four sessions, Paper 2 in six to eight weeks, and whole-syllabus content gaps not at all inside a term. Knowing which of those you have is the difference between a short block that works and one that disappoints.

whyPoints.title: Uncertainty treatment taught properly
whyPoints.description: Propagation, error bars, gradient uncertainty and linearising form a closed technique set that most students have never been taught systematically. It is four sessions of work and it pays into Paper 1B, the investigation's data analysis and the evaluation criterion simultaneously.

whyPoints.title: The investigation treated as 20%
whyPoints.description: Twenty-four marks across four criteria at six marks each, with evaluation carrying as much as data analysis. Where the investigation is unfinished, it takes priority over examination technique in a short window because it has a hard deadline and the technique work can follow.

whyPoints.title: Dates stated only where they are verified
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the awarding bodies and are quoted with their sources. No IB session or results date appears, because none could be confirmed at source, and a family reorganises a term around an exam date.

whyPoints.title: Sixteen sessions in eight weeks is actually schedulable
whyPoints.description: Twice-weekly 45-minute sessions from 17:30, with slots to 21:00 when the early evening is taken, and a recording of each one. A travel-based model with a two-hour minimum cannot offer that shape, which is the practical reason the format matters in a short window.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the physics mock. Is that enough?
faqs.answer: It depends on the component, which is why the first session reads the marked script. Paper 1A multiple choice usually moves within three weeks because the loss is recall and misread stems. Paper 1B data analysis is a closed technique set and takes about four sessions. Paper 2 extended response takes six to eight weeks because the fix is structural — name the physics, apply it, evaluate — and structure needs repetition. Content weakness across most of the syllabus is not an eight-week problem, and the written plan will say that rather than take the booking.

faqs.question: How are the marks split across IB Physics components?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 carries 36% of the grade and divides into Paper 1A, which is multiple choice, and Paper 1B, which is data analysis. Paper 2 carries 44% and is extended response across the syllabus. The scientific investigation, assessed internally and moderated externally, carries 20% and is marked out of 24 across four criteria at six marks each. That arithmetic should drive revision: Paper 2 is the biggest share and the slowest to shift, while Paper 1 is over a third of the grade and the fastest third to move.

faqs.question: Why does my child describe the physics instead of explaining it?
faqs.answer: Because describing is what most school answers reward until the papers start asking for more. An IB Physics extended-response question wants the named principle, then its application to the specific situation, then an evaluation where asked. A student who writes a fluent account of what happens has produced correct physics and will score at the bottom of the band. The fix is a structure applied to every answer, practised on questions where the content is already secure so the only new thing is the shape. It takes six to eight weeks to become automatic.

faqs.question: What exactly is in the Paper 1B data analysis technique set?
faqs.answer: Gradients and intercepts read from a graph; absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty; propagation through addition, multiplication and powers; error bars drawn from absolute uncertainties; lines of maximum and minimum gradient and the gradient uncertainty inferred from them; and linearising a proposed relationship so a straight-line graph can test it, with the gradient and intercept interpreted physically. That is the whole list, which is why four focused sessions normally covers it. For a student with secure content and a weak Paper 1B it is the highest-yield block in the subject.

faqs.question: How do the four investigation criteria divide the 24 marks?
faqs.answer: Evenly: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each, and the whole investigation is 20% of the grade. The even split is the thing students miss. Excellent data with a thin evaluation discards a quarter of the component, and evaluation is routinely written as a closing paragraph rather than as six marks of assessed work. Evaluation credits specific methodological limitations and realistic targeted improvements, so 'human error' and 'more time' score nothing while a resolution limit propagated into a percentage uncertainty scores well.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help design the physics investigation?
faqs.answer: A tutor can interrogate the research question until it is answerable, check whether the proposed method will generate data capable of supporting the planned analysis, explain what each criterion credits from the published descriptors, teach uncertainty treatment as a transferable skill, and read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion a passage fails. A tutor cannot design the investigation, process the data, write any part of the report, or edit the prose to a standard the student could not produce. The test after each session is whether every submitted word is still the student's own.

faqs.question: Should the investigation come before exam technique in a short window?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if it is unfinished. The investigation is 20% of the grade, has a hard internal deadline set by the school, and cannot be revisited once submitted. Examination technique can still be worked on in the weeks that follow. The exception is a student whose investigation is already submitted or essentially complete, in which case the whole window goes to components. Ask the physics teacher for the method approval date, the draft date and the submission date before planning anything, because those three dates constrain everything else.

faqs.question: Is twice a week better than once for a physics block?
faqs.answer: For a compressed eight-week window, generally yes, and for a specific reason: a single weekly session leaves six days for a misconception to set, and the structural work on Paper 2 needs more frequent correction than that. Two 45-minute sessions a week is a better shape than one ninety-minute session, because physics attention fades and the second half of a long session after a school day is rarely productive. Sixteen short sessions in eight weeks is routine online and difficult to arrange with a visiting tutor, who normally needs a two-hour minimum.

faqs.question: Does an IB physics tutor travel to Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do, at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE. For a short physics block the online format also fits the calendar better: 45-minute sessions, twice-weekly scheduling, starts up to 21:00 after a fixture, and a recording the student can rewatch during revision week. A visiting tutor's two-hour minimum and roughly 18:30 latest start make sixteen sessions in eight weeks hard to arrange from this postcode.

faqs.question: What will eight weeks of IB Physics tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At published market bands, eight weekly sessions with an IB specialist comes to roughly AED 1,600-3,600 or more, and sixteen sessions twice weekly to roughly AED 3,200-7,200 or more, using Bestimate's 2026 specialist band of AED 200-450 and above. A qualified non-specialist online tutor at AED 150-300 gives AED 1,200-2,400 for eight sessions. Published packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' figures read in October 2026; we quote after the free diagnostic lesson rather than before it.

faqs.question: How much harder is Higher Level Physics than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level carries additional syllabus content and greater depth in the same components, rather than a wholly different paper type. The practical effect in a short window is that an HL student short of a grade may need content taught as well as technique repaired, which doubles the work in the available time. That is why the written plan after the diagnostic lesson is explicit about what eight weeks can and cannot do: for an HL student with gaps across several topics, the honest answer is often a revised target rather than the one the family arrived with.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools near JVT teach IB Physics?
faqs.answer: None inside Jumeirah Village Triangle. Sunmarke School and Arcadia Global School are British-curriculum, so Diploma physics students from the Triangle commute. The nearest cohorts are at JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, North London Collegiate School Dubai, Greenfield International School and Emirates International School Meadows. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three on the IB curriculum, creating 16,846 places. We name schools as market context and hold no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell me the May exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified at source. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an examination date is something a family rearranges travel and a revision plan around. UAE candidates sit the May session; for the window, the results date and the candidate release time, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly. The dates that constrain an eight-week physics plan first are internal anyway: method approval, draft, mock and submission.

faqs.question: Can a block run through Ramadan or a mock week?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timings adjusted. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar slots, typically 20:30 to 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time, often at 45 minutes, which suits twice-weekly technique work well. Through a school mock week most families pause the teaching and keep one session to read the marked scripts, which in an eight-week block is usually the most valuable hour in it. Because every session is recorded, a pause costs nothing in content: the uncertainty session from week three can be rewatched in week eight at no charge.

Send the marked mock and the four dates your school has set, take the free diagnostic lesson, and get a written plan with a target against each of the eight weeks before you commit to anything.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-karama.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB Diploma Physics at Higher and Standard Level on the current subject guide. Each works from the themes as the school teaches them, marks against the published assessment criteria, and reports in marks rather than impressions.

intro.heading: Physics marks go missing in predictable places
paragraphs: Physics is the Diploma subject where the gap between understanding and marks is widest. A student in Karama can explain projectile motion at the kitchen table and still lose half the marks on a projectile question, because the question asked them to deduce rather than to describe, or because the answer needed a unit, or because the gradient they calculated came from two points they read off a graph instead of from the line of best fit. None of that is a physics problem. All of it is examined.

That is why a physics tutor earns their fee differently from a maths tutor. Much of the work is forensic. A specialist reads your child's last script question by question against the published mark scheme and names where each mark went: content not known, command verb misread, working not shown, unit missing, significant figures wrong, graph read badly, uncertainty ignored. Those seven categories cover the large majority of lost marks in Diploma physics, and five of the seven need no new physics taught at all.

The current IB physics syllabus is organised into five themes rather than the older topic list, which matters practically because revision material bought from the wrong era does not map onto what your child is taught. The themes run from space, time and motion, through the particulate nature of matter, wave behaviour, fields, and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level carries additional content within those themes rather than as a separate block. Ask your child's school for its own copy of the current guide and plan from that, not from a second-hand revision book.

Assessment is two papers plus the scientific investigation. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section, Paper 2 is structured and extended response, and the investigation is internally marked against four criteria and carries twenty per cent of the final grade. The investigation is the component a student controls most and neglects most, and it is where the boundary between coaching and malpractice has to be explicit before any work starts.

The hidden prerequisite is mathematics. Rearranging an equation where the subject appears inside a square root, handling standard form, working in radians when a wave question needs them, reading a logarithmic scale, propagating an uncertainty: these are mathematics skills marked inside a physics paper. A student taking Physics HL alongside Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation often finds this harder than one taking Analysis and Approaches, and it is a fixable gap rather than a verdict.

What follows is the content of that work: the five themes and what each demands, the paper structures, the seven places marks disappear, the data booklet, the investigation criteria by name, and what the Dubai market charges. Lessons are delivered one to one, live online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

sections.heading: The five themes, and what each one actually demands
paragraphs: The current IB physics syllabus is built around five themes, and a tutor planning work for a Karama student needs to know which theme the school is in and which themes are still ahead. The themes are space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level content sits inside the themes rather than in a separate block, which is a change from older syllabuses and the reason second-hand revision guides mislead.

Each theme fails in its own way. Space, time and motion is where graph interpretation is established, and students who never learn to read a gradient as a physical quantity carry that weakness through every later theme. The particulate nature of matter is arithmetic-heavy: specific heat capacity, latent heat and gas law calculations, where the marks go to unit conversion and to the substitution being written before the answer. Wave behaviour punishes students who cannot work confidently in radians or handle a phase relationship, and the superposition questions reward a sketch before any algebra.

Fields is the theme most students name as the hardest, partly because gravitational and electric fields are taught in parallel and the analogies invite confusion, and partly because the questions ask for deductions about direction and sign that a memorised formula cannot supply. Nuclear and quantum physics has less mathematics but more precise language, and it is where command-verb errors are most expensive: a question asking a student to explain a decay process will not award marks for a description of it.

The practical consequence is that revision cannot be uniform. A student weak in fields and strong in waves should not be revising in syllabus order, and a student whose graph reading is unreliable needs that fixed before any theme is revisited, because it affects all five. Our tutors audit the themes against marked work, then set the order by marks available. Confirm the current theme structure and content against your child's school's own copy of the subject guide, since the IB revises guides on a cycle.

sections.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2 and the investigation: what each component rewards
paragraphs: Diploma physics is assessed by two papers and one internally marked investigation. Paper 1 has two sections: a multiple-choice section and a data-based section. Paper 2 is structured and extended response. The investigation carries twenty per cent of the final grade and is marked by the school against four criteria, then moderated. Confirm the current weightings against your school's own copy of the subject guide, because the IB revises them on its publication cycle and an out-of-date figure misdirects revision.

The multiple-choice section is the most mechanical and the most neglected. It rewards elimination, order-of-magnitude checks and a willingness to leave a question and return. Students lose marks here to time rather than to physics: four minutes spent fully solving a question that could have been settled by ruling out two impossible options is four minutes taken from the end of the paper. This is coachable in two sessions and it is almost never taught.

The data-based section is the part that distinguishes prepared candidates. It asks a student to read a table or a graph, process the numbers, consider uncertainty, and comment on whether the data supports a claim. Marks are available for plotting correctly, for drawing a best-fit line that actually fits, for calculating a gradient from widely separated points on that line rather than from data points, for stating units, and for discussing whether an anomaly matters. Each of these is a specific taught skill.

Paper 2 is where command verbs decide everything. State, describe, explain, outline, deduce, determine, show that, compare and discuss each define the shape of a creditable answer, and a student who writes a good paragraph in the wrong shape loses marks they understood the physics for. The remedy is unglamorous: take twenty real past-paper stems, identify the verb, write the required shape of answer without doing the physics, then check against the scheme. Two sessions of that is worth more than a theme revisited.

sections.heading: Seven places physics marks disappear, in order of how much they cost
paragraphs: A diagnostic that names categories is more useful than one that names topics, because five of the seven categories below are fixed without teaching any new physics. Our tutors mark a student's own script and allocate every lost mark to one of these seven, then plan from the proportions. In this belt the pattern is consistent enough to predict before the script arrives.

First, command verbs. A student who describes where the question said explain, or who gives one reason where the mark scheme wanted a comparison, loses marks on content they knew. Second, unshown working. Diploma physics mark schemes award method marks for a correct substitution even where the arithmetic then fails, and a bare answer forfeits them. Third, units. A numerical answer with no unit, or with a unit that does not match the quantity, loses the mark however correct the number. Fourth, significant figures and premature rounding, which accumulate quietly across a paper.

Fifth, graph handling. Reading a gradient from two adjacent data points, drawing a line that passes through the first and last point rather than fitting the data, failing to label axes with quantity and unit, ignoring error bars entirely. Sixth, the data booklet: students who do not know what is in it waste minutes searching or, worse, try to recall a constant they could have read. Seventh, uncertainty, which is the category most often skipped by schools under time pressure and therefore the one most reliably available as a source of recovered marks.

The sequence matters. Fix command verbs and shown working first, because they are quick and affect every question on both papers. Then units and significant figures, which are habits rather than knowledge. Then graphs and uncertainty, which take longer and need repeated practice on real data sets. Content gaps come last in the ordering not because they do not matter, but because a student who fixes the first six categories typically recovers more marks in four weeks than a student who revisits a theme does in eight.

sections.heading: The data booklet and uncertainty: two short skills worth a grade band
paragraphs: The data booklet is supplied in the examination and most students treat it as a formula sheet they will glance at if stuck. Treated properly it is a working tool, and knowing it well is worth minutes on every paper. A student should be able to find a constant without hunting, know which equations are given and therefore need not be memorised, and know which relationships are not given and therefore must be. That last distinction is the useful one: the memorisation burden in Diploma physics is smaller than students assume, and misplacing effort on recall of supplied equations is a waste.

Using it well also changes how a question is read. If the equation is on the page, the examiner is not testing recall; they are testing whether the student can select the right relationship and substitute correctly, which means the marks are in the selection and the substitution. Teaching a student to find and quote the relationship explicitly before substituting earns method marks and slows them down at exactly the point where speed causes errors.

Uncertainty is the second short skill, and it is the one most often compressed out of a crowded school year. The examinable content is bounded: absolute and percentage uncertainty, propagating uncertainty through sums, products and powers, representing uncertainty with error bars, and drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines to estimate the uncertainty in a gradient. That is a small body of technique with a predictable question style, and it appears reliably in the data-based section.

Because it is bounded and predictable, uncertainty is the best-value tutoring topic in Diploma physics. A student who cannot touch these questions at the start of a block can usually answer them competently after three or four focused sessions with real past-paper data. The same cannot be said of fields. Our tutors therefore front-load uncertainty and graph work in a short run-in, and only then move to whichever theme the diagnosis flagged.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: four criteria, twenty-four marks, and a firm boundary
paragraphs: The internally assessed scientific investigation is a single piece of independent experimental work, written up within a word limit set by the current guide and marked by the school against four criteria before IB moderation. It carries twenty per cent of the final physics grade. For a student who finds examinations difficult, it is the most controllable fifth of the grade available; for a student who leaves it late, it is the fifth most easily thrown away.

The four criteria are research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each carrying six marks. Research design is where most investigations are lost before any data is collected: a question that is too broad, variables that cannot be controlled in a school laboratory, or a method that will not generate enough data points to support a gradient. A tutor can add enormous value in one or two sessions here simply by asking whether the proposed question can be answered with the equipment that actually exists.

Data analysis rewards correct processing, honest treatment of uncertainty and graphs that are genuinely informative. Conclusion rewards an answer to the stated question that is supported by the data and placed in the context of accepted physics, not a restatement of the result. Evaluation rewards specific, physics-based criticism of the method and realistic improvements, and it is where generic sentences about human error cost marks that specific observations about systematic effects would have earned.

The boundary is not negotiable and should be stated in writing before any session. An IB Gram tutor will interrogate the research question, teach the physics involved, check whether the method can produce usable data, explain what a criterion requires and mark a draft against it. An IB Gram tutor will not supply the research question, write any part of the report, rewrite the student's prose or produce the analysis the student then submits. The supervisor at the school remains the supervisor and the authenticity declaration remains the student's.

sections.heading: The mathematics inside physics, and why it ambushes students in DP1
paragraphs: Diploma physics assumes a level of algebraic fluency that IGCSE physics does not. At IGCSE a student can often survive with a formula triangle and a calculator. In DP1 the questions expect rearrangement as a routine step, including rearranging for a variable inside a square root or a reciprocal, and they expect it done quickly because the physics is the point of the question rather than the algebra.

The specific skills are nameable. Rearranging an equation where the subject appears in a denominator or under a root. Handling standard form and prefixes, including converting between them under time pressure. Working in radians rather than degrees as the default for wave and circular-motion work. Reading and interpreting a logarithmic scale. Manipulating proportionality statements to predict the effect of doubling one quantity. Propagating percentage uncertainty through a product or a power. None of these is advanced mathematics; all of them are examined inside physics papers.

Which mathematics course a student takes alongside physics changes the size of this gap. A student on Analysis and Approaches is drilled in exactly this kind of manipulation, often to a higher level than physics requires. A student on Applications and Interpretation is drilled in data, modelling and calculator work, and may be a strong mathematician who has simply not practised symbolic rearrangement to the same depth. That combination is entirely viable, but it needs recognising in DP1 rather than in DP2.

The fix is a short, front-loaded block rather than a running theme. Four or five sessions of rearrangement, standard form, radians and proportional reasoning, drilled on physics equations rather than abstract ones, removes most of the friction. It is also the clearest example of why a physics tutor should read a script before teaching anything: a student whose physics looks weak may simply be losing marks to algebra, and the two problems have completely different remedies.

sections.heading: What Diploma physics tutoring costs in this market, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: Take the in-home premium first, because it is the figure Karama families question most. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one tutoring at AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The difference between those bands is, in substance, the tutor's travel. In Karama, where the schools and the tutors are both minutes away, that premium buys a short drive rather than better physics teaching.

Below both bands sits budget online tutoring, advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour: EdFlik publishes AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya quotes from AED 33 to AED 52. At that level a tutor can supervise practice and re-explain something already taught. What it does not reliably buy for Diploma physics is someone who can mark a data-based question against the published scheme or tell you whether a proposed investigation question is answerable. Above the mid-band, IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards; premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED.

Monthly, the same market looks like this: Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Packages advertised in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of these are other providers' published figures, not IB Gram's prices.

What a parent can test independently is worth more than any band. Ask a prospective physics tutor to mark one data-based question from your child's last paper and explain where each mark went. Ask which themes they have taught at Higher Level and when. Ask them to name the four investigation criteria without looking them up. A tutor who can do those three things is worth more at the middle of the band than one who cannot at the bottom of it. For IB Gram's own arrangements, start with the free trial lesson and the consultation.

sections.heading: Why a physics specialist is harder to find locally than a maths one
paragraphs: Hiring someone who can physically attend a flat in Karama means hiring from the set of tutors who live within a short drive and are free at the hour your child is free. For IGCSE mathematics that set is large. For Diploma physics at Higher Level, with current-guide theme knowledge and the ability to mark a data-based question properly, it is small, and the overlap between small and free-at-5pm-on-a-Tuesday is smaller still.

This is the structural reason online delivery wins for this subject rather than a marketing preference. Removing geography from the match changes the constraint from postcode to diary, and for a scarce specialism that is the difference between the right tutor and a near-enough one. A near-enough physics tutor is specifically expensive: they will teach the content competently and miss the mark-scheme detail that was costing your child the marks, so the sessions feel productive and the grade does not move.

The practical side favours online too. Physics tutoring needs a shared surface where graphs can be drawn, annotated and kept, a way to send a script for marking and get it back annotated, and the data booklet open on screen alongside the question. A tablet and a shared whiteboard do all of that better than two people and one exercise book. Sessions can also run at 3:45pm, because the schools in the Oud Metha belt finish early, which matters for a subject that needs an alert student.

The honest exception is a much younger or very distractible student, where a person in the room helps in a way video does not. For a DP1 or DP2 physics student it almost never decides anything. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE — home tutoring is a service we provide only in India — so where a family's child genuinely needs someone physically present, we will say so rather than sell an online session as a substitute.

sections.heading: Permits, claims and the lines we will not cross
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, any specific amount quoted to you is unverified.

A permit is a legal status rather than a teaching qualification, and it is nobody's endorsement. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes operating premises in Dubai; we do not operate premises in the UAE and make no such claim. Nor are our tutors IB examiners unless an individual's current status can be evidenced, and examiner status in any case gives nobody access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or unseen papers.

Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which on the UAE government's own description is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students and instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. That matters to a physics tutoring plan mainly as timetable arithmetic: the free hours in your child's week are fewer than the curriculum brochure suggests.

On materials and outcomes the limits are firm. We will not supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because they belong to the board; a tutor references them, teaches from them in the session and points you at the official source. We will not predict a grade, and nobody should. A specialist can tell you which of the seven mark-loss categories is costing your child marks today and what looks reachable from there, which is a useful statement and a different one from a promise.
