faqs.question: What are the five themes in the current IB physics syllabus?
faqs.answer: Space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. Higher Level content sits inside those themes rather than in a separate options block, which is a change from older syllabuses. The practical consequence is that second-hand revision guides written for the previous topic list do not map cleanly onto what your child is taught. Ask the school for its own copy of the current subject guide and plan revision against that, confirming the structure and assessment weightings there rather than relying on any figure quoted online.

faqs.question: Which physics theme do Diploma students find hardest?
faqs.answer: Fields, in most cohorts. Gravitational and electric fields are taught in parallel and the analogies between them invite confusion, and the questions ask for deductions about direction and sign that a memorised formula cannot supply. Wave behaviour comes second, usually because students are working in degrees when the physics expects radians, or attempting algebra before drawing a diagram. Neither difficulty is about intelligence; both respond to being taught to reason in words before reaching for an equation, which is a habit rather than a body of knowledge.

faqs.question: How does the data-based section of Paper 1 differ from the rest?
faqs.answer: It asks a student to work with real data rather than recall physics. Marks are available for plotting accurately, drawing a line that genuinely fits the points, calculating a gradient from two widely separated points on that line rather than from raw data points, stating units, handling absolute and percentage uncertainty, and judging whether an anomaly matters. Each of those is a specific taught skill with a predictable question style, which makes this section unusually responsive to tutoring compared with content-heavy parts of the course.

faqs.question: Why does my child's physics answer get part marks when the answer is right?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the method was not written down. Diploma physics mark schemes award marks for a correct relationship quoted and a correct substitution made, independently of whether the final arithmetic succeeds. A bare answer forfeits those marks even when it is correct. The habit to build is mechanical: quote the relationship from the data booklet, write the substitution line with units, then give the answer to a sensible number of significant figures. It takes one session to explain and several weeks of marked practice to become automatic.

faqs.question: How much does the scientific investigation count, and what is it marked on?
faqs.answer: It carries twenty per cent of the final physics grade and is marked by the school against four criteria before IB moderation: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six marks. Most investigations are lost in research design, before any data is collected, because the question is too broad or the variables cannot be controlled with the equipment available. Confirm the current word limit and criterion weightings against your school's own copy of the subject guide, since the IB revises guides on a publication cycle.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the physics investigation without breaching IB honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor can interrogate the research question, teach the physics involved, check whether the proposed method will generate data the criteria reward, explain what a criterion requires and mark the student's own draft against it. A tutor cannot supply the research question, write any section, rewrite the student's prose or produce the analysis. The school's supervisor remains the supervisor and the authenticity declaration remains the student's. Any service offering to produce an investigation is offering malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Is Physics HL much harder than Physics SL, or just longer?
faqs.answer: Both, and the difference is more than volume. Higher Level adds depth inside each theme, so the questions demand reasoning chains rather than single-step application, particularly in fields and in nuclear and quantum physics. The mathematical demand rises alongside: more rearrangement, more proportional reasoning, more work with logarithmic relationships. A student coping comfortably at Standard Level will not automatically cope at Higher, and the usual limiting factor is algebraic fluency rather than physics interest. Audit the Higher Level content specifically before revising anything.

faqs.question: My child takes Applications and Interpretation maths with Physics HL. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is workable, with one gap to manage deliberately. Applications and Interpretation drills data, modelling and calculator work; Diploma physics assumes routine symbolic rearrangement, including rearranging for a variable under a root or in a denominator, plus confident standard form and radians. A strong Applications student may simply not have practised those to the depth physics expects. Four or five front-loaded sessions on rearrangement and proportional reasoning, drilled on real physics equations rather than abstract ones, removes most of the friction in DP1.

faqs.question: How well should a student know the physics data booklet?
faqs.answer: Well enough to find a constant without hunting and to know which equations are supplied and which must be recalled. That second distinction is the useful one, because it shrinks the memorisation burden considerably and students routinely waste effort learning relationships that are printed in the examination. Using it properly also changes how a question is read: if the equation is given, the marks sit in selecting the right relationship and substituting correctly, so quoting the relationship explicitly before substituting earns marks and slows a student down where speed causes errors.

faqs.question: What does Diploma physics tutoring cost around Karama?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates split by tier rather than by neighbourhood. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to AED 300, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors as high as AED 650. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is inside the rate. Those figures come from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED. For IB Gram's own arrangements, begin with the free trial lesson and the consultation.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level physics tutor harder to find nearby than a maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is genuinely smaller. Plenty of tutors can teach IGCSE mathematics; far fewer can teach current-guide Higher Level fields, mark a data-based question against the published scheme and advise on an investigation's research design. Hiring someone who can attend a Karama flat restricts that already small group to those living nearby and free at your hour. Online removes the geography from the match, which matters most precisely for a scarce specialism, and a near-enough physics tutor is expensive: the sessions feel productive while the grade stays still.

faqs.question: Can one session a week genuinely move a physics grade?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the work between sessions is marked. The session itself is where diagnosis and teaching happen; the marks move because of practice done afterwards and corrected before the next session. One well-used session a week with submitted and annotated work usually outperforms two sessions a week with nothing in between, because the limiting factor is corrected practice rather than contact hours. In a short run-in before the May examinations that changes, and twice weekly with full timed papers becomes the sensible shape.

faqs.question: Does the school's KHDA band tell us anything about its physics department?
faqs.answer: Very little on its own. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a whole-school band from Outstanding to Very Weak, which can conceal a strong department beside a weak one and cannot reflect a teacher who left in August. More useful questions for physics: whether the school offers Physics at Higher Level every year, how many students sat it last session, whether the same teacher carries it across DP1 and DP2, and what laboratory equipment is actually available for the investigation.

faqs.question: Can physics sessions run in the afternoon given school finishing times here?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this belt is one of the better parts of Dubai for it. Schools around Oud Metha finish early enough that a 3:30pm or 3:45pm slot is genuinely available, which suits physics because graph handling and uncertainty work need an alert student rather than a tired one. Online delivery is what makes that slot usable, since nobody is driving anywhere. During Ramadan the same session usually shifts earlier or moves to a post-Iftar slot, and holiday weeks are often the most productive in a run-in.

faqs.question: Will you tell us if no suitable physics specialist is available?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is worth asking of anyone. Higher Level physics at a specific hour in Gulf Standard Time is a narrow requirement, and the honest answer is sometimes that nobody suitable is free. We would rather say that than place a tutor who nearly fits, because a term spent with the wrong specialist costs more than a fortnight spent waiting for the right one. Where a child genuinely needs a person physically in the room, we will also say so; IB Gram provides home visits only in India, not in the UAE.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-knowledge-park.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma physics to students at schools around Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and the Marina. Each works on one level at a time, because Higher Level physics is not Standard Level with extra chapters bolted on.

intro.heading: Physics fails in a particular way, and it is rarely about physics
paragraphs: Diploma physics produces a distinctive kind of struggle. A student can describe a concept accurately, explain it out loud, and still lose most of the marks on a question about it. That is because the subject is examined through algebra, through graphs and through precise written reasoning, and a student can hold the physics while failing all three. Parents in this catchment usually notice the symptom - a grade dropping from a 6 to a 4 across one term - without the diagnosis, and the diagnosis is what decides whether tutoring is worth buying.

The current subject guide organises the course into five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics. The options and the old Paper 3 are gone, which matters because revision material written for the earlier guide is still circulating widely and still being sold. Assessment is Paper 1, split into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section, carrying 36 per cent; Paper 2, carrying 44 per cent; and the scientific investigation, carrying 20 per cent.

The three failure modes are separable and each needs a different response. Algebraic failure shows as marks lost whenever an equation has to be rearranged under time pressure, and it is usually a maths problem that happens to be sitting in a physics paper. Graph failure shows as marks lost on gradients, intercepts and the uncertainty work in Paper 1B. Written-reasoning failure shows as answers that are correct but score in the lower band, because the command term asked for an explanation and received a description.

The scientific investigation is the fourth failure mode and it is the one families see coming least. It carries twenty per cent of the grade, is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria, and is finished months before the papers against a school deadline that sits well ahead of the IB's own. Most of the marks lost here are lost at the design stage, weeks before any data is collected, because the chosen method cannot produce a measurable relationship with enough range to analyse.

Knowledge Park itself is an education free zone off Al Sufouh Road, holding university campuses and training institutes rather than homes, so families searching for a physics tutor near it live in Al Sufouh, Media City, Barsha Heights, The Greens or the Marina towers. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor attending a UAE address is a service we run only in India. For a subject this narrow that is an advantage: the number of people in this emirate who have taught the fields theme at Higher Level is small, and it does not overlap much with the number free to drive to Barsha Heights at 5pm.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-knowledge-park.programmesIntro: Physics does not begin in Year 12, and what a student can manage at Higher Level is largely set by the mathematics they bring. These are the stages a Knowledge Park family is usually planning across.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria - knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science - each on a 1 to 8 scale. The inquiring and designing criterion is the direct ancestor of the Diploma investigation, so a student who scored poorly there will struggle with investigation design two years later unless it is addressed deliberately.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within reach of Al Sufouh run the Middle Years Programme before the Diploma. The criterion scores are more informative than the overall grade for predicting physics readiness: a strong score in knowing and understanding with a weak one in processing and evaluating points at exactly the data-handling gap that Paper 1B and the investigation expose.

programmes.name: IGCSE physics as the other entry route
programmes.description: Most students entering Diploma physics in this catchment come from Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 rather than from the Middle Years Programme. Extended or Higher tier is effectively a prerequisite. Students who took combined or coordinated science instead of separate physics arrive with roughly half the content coverage, and the first term of Standard Level physics closes that gap at speed.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools around Al Barsha and The Greens send a steady flow of students into Diploma sciences elsewhere in the city, so a curriculum change at sixteen is common here. The practical check is whether the student did separate physics and whether they took Additional Mathematics, because the second predicts Higher Level survival better than the physics grade does.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme physics
programmes.description: Two years at Higher or Standard Level, sat in the May session that UAE schools use, with a November session also available. The scientific investigation is designed and carried out in Year 12 and written up early in Year 13. Higher Level adds depth across all five themes rather than extra topics at the end, which is why a late switch down from Higher to Standard is cleaner than a switch up.
programmes.countryNote: Physics at Higher Level is a common requirement for engineering and some medical and architectural routes, and it is frequently paired with Analysis and Approaches. Check each target university's own published entry page, because requirements are set course by course and are revised between admission cycles rather than following a general rule.

programmes.name: After the Diploma: what the physics grade opens
programmes.description: Engineering faculties commonly expect Higher Level physics, often with Higher Level mathematics alongside. The pairing is the real requirement rather than the physics grade alone, and students who take Higher Level physics with Standard Level Applications and Interpretation sometimes find the combination closes doors they assumed were open. That is worth checking in Year 12, not Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: No IB points threshold for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency has been verified from the Ministry's own pages, so no figure appears here. The British-track rules are sourced; the IB figure is not. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority, and treat equivalency as separate from any university's academic offer.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-knowledge-park.subjectsIntro: Physics rarely fails alone. These are the subjects Knowledge Park families most often ask about alongside it, with the component that usually decides the grade named.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two papers and a scientific investigation. Fields and circuits are the reliable mark drains at both levels, and the data-analysis section of Paper 1 is where students who were never taught uncertainties lose marks they could have had.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The subject that most often determines a physics grade. Rearranging an equation under time pressure, handling logarithms and reading a gradient are maths skills examined inside physics questions. Fixing algebraic fluency usually lifts both grades.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A common pairing with Standard Level physics and an awkward one with Higher Level, because the algebraic density of Higher Level physics assumes more manipulation practice than this course provides. Worth checking against university requirements early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the investigation structure and the uncertainty work, so skills transfer directly between the two. Energetics and kinetics draw on the same graph-reading ability that physics tests, which makes joint support unusually efficient.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Popular in this catchment, where many parents work in technology roles around the free zone. Algorithmic thinking and systematic debugging transfer into physics problem solving, particularly on multi-step questions where the method has to be planned before anything is calculated.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Overlaps with physics on materials, forces and energy, and its coursework culture makes students noticeably better at investigation design. Students taking both often produce their strongest investigation in physics because of the transfer.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Shares the sciences investigation criteria and the statistics. A student who has learned standard deviation and error bars properly for one subject collects marks in the other, which is worth knowing when deciding where tutoring hours go.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The natural sciences are an area of knowledge, and physics students frequently write their strongest Theory of Knowledge work on measurement, models and the limits of observation. Support here is on argument structure and the student's own examples only.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in physics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece. Physics essays fail most often on a research question that cannot be answered with the equipment available, which is the same design failure that costs marks in the investigation.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support has to match the pathway the school has placed the student in.

sections.heading: The five themes and what each paper actually asks for
paragraphs: The current physics guide runs on five themes rather than a core-plus-options structure, and the Paper 3 that older revision guides discuss no longer exists. That is worth stating plainly, because material written for the previous guide is still sold and still recommended in parent groups, and a student revising from it will spend hours on content that is not examined while missing content that is.

Paper 1 carries 36 per cent and has two parts. The first is multiple choice, and it rewards speed, confident elimination and a willingness to move on - the single commonest error is spending four minutes on one item and losing three later ones to the clock. The second part is data analysis, and it is a different examination altogether: graphs, gradients, uncertainties and the physical interpretation of a line. Students who treat Paper 1 as one thing prepare badly for both halves.

Paper 2 carries 44 per cent and is extended response. This is where command terms decide the band. 'State' wants one line. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why, in causal steps, and an explanation delivered as a description sits in the lower band however accurate it is. 'Compare' wants both sides in the same sentence structure, not two separate paragraphs. These are learnable in about three sessions and they are worth more marks than any single theme.

The table sets the components against what each demands and where marks are typically lost. It is worth reading alongside a marked script: if the marks went in Paper 1B, the fix is uncertainty work, and if they went in Paper 2 extended responses, the fix is command-term discipline. Those two plans share almost nothing, which is why diagnosing before buying hours matters.

sections.heading: Where physics marks drain away, theme by theme
paragraphs: Mark loss in physics is theme-specific in a way that makes planning straightforward once a marked script exists. Fields is the reliable worst case at both levels: students confuse field strength with potential, lose signs on work done, and cannot explain why a quantity is negative. The fix is conceptual rather than procedural, and it takes two or three sessions on definitions and sign conventions before any question practice is worthwhile.

Circuits within the fields theme is the second drain and it fails differently - students know the rules but cannot apply them to an unfamiliar network, because they learned worked examples rather than the method of reduction. Wave behaviour fails on superposition and on the difference between path difference and phase difference. The particulate nature of matter fails on the distinction between heat, temperature and internal energy, which sounds like vocabulary and is actually the whole topic.

Nuclear and quantum physics fails last in the course and least in the examination, because it is taught close to the papers and revised while fresh. Space, time and motion fails early and then stops, because its content gets re-used constantly. That pattern has a practical consequence: a Year 12 physics problem is usually a motion or matter problem, and a Year 13 physics problem is usually a fields problem, so the same student needs different support in different years.

Underneath all of it sits algebra. A student who cannot rearrange an equation with three terms under time pressure will lose marks in every theme, and will interpret that as being bad at physics. Testing this is simple: give the student an unfamiliar formula and ask them to make a given symbol the subject, with no physics attached. If that is slow or uncertain, the first few sessions are maths sessions, and they will show up as a physics improvement.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: twenty-four marks and where they are really won
paragraphs: The investigation carries twenty per cent of the physics grade and is marked out of twenty-four across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, six marks each. Almost no page in this market names one of them. The practical consequence of the mark split is that two of the four criteria - conclusion and evaluation - are about what the student says once the data exists, and those twelve marks are frequently the ones a strong experimentalist leaves behind.

Research design is where the damage is done, though, and it is done early. A method that cannot generate a measurable relationship across a decent range will cap every criterion that follows, because the data will not support analysis and the conclusion will be weak by necessity. The questions worth asking before anything is set up are simple: what exactly is being varied, over what range, what is being held constant and how, and how many repeats are realistic in the laboratory time available. A method that survives those four questions will usually produce a workable investigation.

Data analysis rewards processed data rather than raw data - uncertainties propagated, a graph with error bars, a gradient with its own uncertainty. The conclusion criterion asks the student to state what the data supports and compare it against accepted physics with a source. The evaluation criterion asks for specific, prioritised weaknesses and realistic improvements, and this is where generic phrases about human error score nothing. A weakness worth marks is quantified and tied to the data.

A tutor's role here has a clear boundary. We test the research question, interrogate variable control, explain what each criterion rewards, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. The design, the data, the analysis and the words are the student's own, and the school signs an authentication saying so. A provider offering to produce an investigation is transferring the entire risk to the candidate, who is the only person the board can sanction.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: the skill nobody teaches and Paper 1B keeps testing
paragraphs: Uncertainty handling is the clearest example of a skill that is examined repeatedly and taught almost nowhere systematically. Students pick up fragments - add absolute uncertainties when adding quantities, add percentages when multiplying - without ever seeing the system behind them, so under time pressure they guess. It appears in the data-analysis section of Paper 1 and in the data analysis and evaluation criteria of the investigation, which between them account for a substantial share of the grade.

The system is small enough to teach in two sessions. Absolute uncertainty is the size of the doubt in the same units as the measurement. Fractional and percentage uncertainty are that doubt relative to the measurement, which is what makes different measurements comparable. Adding or subtracting quantities adds absolute uncertainties; multiplying or dividing adds percentage uncertainties; raising to a power multiplies the percentage uncertainty by that power. That last rule is the one most consistently missed.

Graph work is the other half. A gradient has an uncertainty, found from lines of best and worst fit, and a student who draws one line has no way to produce it. An intercept carries physical meaning that is often the point of the question. Error bars are drawn from the uncertainty in the measurement rather than chosen for appearance. Doing this by hand, on paper, a few times is what makes it stick; doing it in a spreadsheet hides the mechanics that the examination asks about.

The reason this is worth prioritising is arithmetic rather than pedagogy. It is a small, closed body of technique that recurs in two components, and it is not entangled with any particular theme, so it can be fixed in isolation at any point in the two years. For a student eight weeks from the papers, it is usually the highest-yield block available, and it is almost never the thing they came asking for.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level: what the extra depth actually demands
paragraphs: Higher Level physics is not Standard Level with additional topics at the end. The current guide adds depth across all five themes, which changes what the whole two years feels like rather than adding a block that can be dropped. That has a practical consequence families should know early: moving down from Higher to Standard mid-course is usually manageable, while moving up is not, because the additional depth was embedded in teaching the student did not receive.

The algebraic density is the real difference. Higher Level questions chain more steps together, use logarithms and exponentials more freely, and expect a student to carry symbolic expressions rather than substitute numbers at the first opportunity. A student comfortable with Analysis and Approaches handles this; a student taking Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level alongside Higher Level physics often finds the maths, not the physics, is the binding constraint. Checking that pairing in Year 12 is worth the ten minutes it takes.

The investigation is marked on the same twenty-four-mark scheme at both levels, which surprises families. A Higher Level student is not given a harder criterion set; they are expected to design something that genuinely merits the level, and markers do notice when a Higher Level investigation measures something trivial. That means topic choice at Higher Level carries more weight than at Standard, and it is the part of the investigation a tutor can most legitimately help stress-test.

For a student weighing the two, the useful question is not whether they can cope with the content but whether they can cope with the content alongside everything else on a six-subject timetable. Higher Level physics taken with Higher Level mathematics and a Higher Level third subject is a genuinely heavy load, and the grade that suffers is rarely the one the student expects. Deciding that honestly in Year 12 beats discovering it in the spring of Year 13.

sections.heading: What a parent can actually verify about a physics tutor
paragraphs: Rates in this market are published inconsistently and credentials are published loosely, so it is worth separating what can be checked from what cannot. Published online rates in Dubai start at roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik, which generally means a university student. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work, Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above, and BartyED sits at around AED 650 for examiner-led sessions. In-home visiting rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price.

The permit is checkable and most parents never ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here.

What is not checkable is most of what gets advertised. An examiner claim cannot be verified by a parent, and we do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners for individuals whose current status cannot be evidenced. A star rating that a provider published about itself is not evidence either: competitor pages in this market show ratings of 4.92 from 480 reviews and 4.93 from 850 reviews on the same page, and one shows five out of five from twenty reviews next to a student-numbers claim in the thousands. Figures that contradict themselves are the signal.

So the verifiable tests are these. Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition permit. Ask which subject guide edition they teach from, because the answer separates current knowledge from outdated. Ask them to explain uncertainty propagation in the trial lesson. And ask what happens if the match does not work. IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, because a number quoted without knowing the level and frequency is not information; the trial lesson and consultation are free.

sections.heading: Practical work, online delivery and the limits worth naming
paragraphs: Physics is the subject where online delivery has a genuine limit, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest. Apparatus cannot be handled together. A student cannot be shown how to clamp a pendulum properly, how a micrometer feels when it is over-tightened, or why a particular ammeter reading is drifting, on a video call. Those are real skills and they are learned in the school laboratory, which is where they belong.

What can be done over video is most of what the examination actually assesses about practical work. The design of an investigation is a thinking task. The processing of data, the propagation of uncertainty, the drawing and interpretation of graphs, the evaluation of a method - all of that is analysis, and analysis is better on a shared screen than on a bench, because the work is visible, annotated and saved for the student to return to. Paper 1B tests the analysis, not the dexterity.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. So the comparison is not between our online lessons and our in-home lessons, but between a specialist on a screen and a generalist in the room. For a Higher Level fields problem or an investigation design question, that comparison favours the specialist. For a fourteen-year-old who needs a person present to stay on task, it may not, and that is worth saying plainly rather than selling around.

The practical gains of video delivery are specific rather than rhetorical. The whiteboard is saved and revisited, which matters in a subject where a derivation needs re-reading. Two siblings can be taught in one evening without a second journey. No session is lost to Sheikh Zayed Road at 5pm, which in this catchment is the difference between thirty sessions a year and twenty-four. And the tutor is chosen for having taught the theme rather than for living in Al Barsha.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, materials and who is allowed to teach
paragraphs: The investigation is coursework, which makes it the point where academic honesty is tested in physics. The boundary is clear. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each criterion rewards, interrogate a research question, model an analysis technique on different data, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not design the experiment, produce the data, write the analysis or draft the text.

The reason this matters is where the consequence falls. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if that is untrue the sanction lands on the student, not on whoever helped. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price; that transaction transfers the whole risk onto a sixteen-year-old. Any provider willing to do the work for your child has told you something about how they treat your child's interests.

Materials follow the same logic. We reference the IB physics subject guide, past papers and mark schemes, cite them and point to the official source. We do not reproduce them or distribute them as downloads, because they are the board's copyright and, in the case of unreleased material, a malpractice exposure in themselves. We also do not publish IB session or results dates, because ibo.org blocks automated access and nothing in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself - the May session is the one UAE schools sit, and exact dates come from the school's Diploma coordinator.

There is a question about who teaches, too. Abu Dhabi's ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct barring the same arrangement. Those are press-reported positions and should be verified against the current policy document, but the principle travels across the UAE: paying your child's own classroom teacher privately is the arrangement most likely to put that teacher in breach.

faqs.question: Is there an IB physics tutor near Dubai Knowledge Park who has taught the fields theme at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Some, but not many. Plenty of competent science tutors live within fifteen minutes of Al Sufouh; the number who have taught Higher Level fields and circuits on the current guide is small across the whole emirate. Require them also to be free at your preferred hour and willing to drive to Barsha Heights or The Greens at 5pm, and the overlap gets very thin. Delivering over live video takes geography out of the match, which is why we work this way rather than by home visit.

faqs.question: My daughter understands the physics but her marks keep dropping. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things, and a marked script separates them. If marks went on questions where an equation had to be rearranged, it is an algebra problem wearing physics clothing. If they went in the data-analysis section of Paper 1, it is uncertainties and graph interpretation, which are rarely taught systematically. If they went on extended responses in Paper 2, it is command terms - an explanation delivered as a description sits in the lower band however accurate it is. Each needs a different plan.

faqs.question: Does the current physics course still have Paper 3 and the options?
faqs.answer: No. The current subject guide runs on five themes - space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; and nuclear and quantum physics - and the options and Paper 3 are gone. Assessment is Paper 1, which splits into multiple choice and data analysis and carries 36 per cent, Paper 2 at 44 per cent, and the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Check the edition of any revision guide you buy, because material written for the earlier structure is still widely sold.

faqs.question: How are the twenty-four investigation marks split in Diploma physics?
faqs.answer: Four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Research design is where the damage is done, because a method that cannot produce a measurable relationship across a usable range caps everything downstream. Conclusion and evaluation together carry twelve marks and are about what the student says once the data exists, which is where strong experimentalists most often leave marks behind. Generic statements about human error score nothing in evaluation; a quantified, prioritised weakness does.

faqs.question: Why does nobody seem to teach uncertainties properly?
faqs.answer: Because it falls between topics, so no single lesson owns it, and students collect fragments instead of the system. The system is small: add absolute uncertainties when adding or subtracting, add percentage uncertainties when multiplying or dividing, and multiply the percentage by the power when raising to a power. Gradient uncertainty needs lines of best and worst fit, so one line is never enough. It appears in Paper 1B and in two investigation criteria, which makes two sessions on it unusually good value.

faqs.question: Can online physics tutoring work when so much of the subject is practical?
faqs.answer: For the parts the papers assess, yes. Apparatus handling cannot be taught over video and belongs in the school laboratory, and we say so rather than claiming otherwise. What the examination actually tests about practical work is analysis: designing an investigation, processing data, propagating uncertainty, drawing and reading graphs, evaluating a method. All of that works better on a shared screen, because the work is visible, annotated and saved for the student to return to later.

faqs.question: Should my son take physics at Higher Level if his maths is Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It is a pairing worth examining rather than assuming. Higher Level physics chains more algebraic steps, uses logarithms and exponentials more freely, and expects symbolic expressions to be carried rather than substituted early. Applications and Interpretation provides less of that manipulation practice than Analysis and Approaches does, so the maths often becomes the binding constraint rather than the physics. Check the target university requirements too, because engineering faculties frequently expect both subjects at Higher Level and the pairing is the real requirement.

faqs.question: My child moved from combined science to Diploma physics. How big is that gap?
faqs.answer: Material. A student who took combined or coordinated science rather than separate physics at IGCSE arrives with roughly half the content coverage, and the first term of Standard Level physics closes that at speed while also introducing new material. It is recoverable with a term of targeted support on motion, forces and energy, taken alongside the course rather than instead of it. The bigger predictor of how it goes is the mathematics the student brings, not the science grade they arrived with.

faqs.question: Which theme is worth spending money on if we can only afford a few sessions?
faqs.answer: Fields, including circuits, at either level - it is the reliable worst case. Students confuse field strength with potential, lose signs on work done, and cannot reduce an unfamiliar network because they learned worked examples rather than a method. Three or four sessions there usually shows up in the next timed paper. If the marked script instead shows losses in the data-analysis section, spend the money on uncertainties and graphs, which is a smaller body of technique and faster to fix.

faqs.question: How much does a specialist physics tutor cost in Dubai, and what should we expect to pay monthly?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this city run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end, which usually means a university student, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, up to AED 200 to 450 and above for specialist work and around AED 650 for examiner-led sessions. Monthly, a weekly session at the specialist end sits around AED 1,000 to 2,000. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. Our trial lesson and consultation are free.

faqs.question: How can I check whether a physics tutor is legally allowed to teach here?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published. Any provider suggesting private tutoring is unregulated in the UAE is wrong, and that is worth noticing.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at the investigation before my son starts collecting data?
faqs.answer: That is the single most useful time to involve one. Most of the twenty-four marks are decided at the design stage: whether the research question is answerable, whether the independent variable can be varied across a usable range, whether the controls are real, and whether enough repeats fit the laboratory time available. A method stress-tested in week one avoids a rescue attempt in week six. The design, the data and the writing remain the student's own throughout, which is both required and the reason the marks hold.

faqs.question: When do Dubai students sit IB physics papers, and where do I get the exact dates?
faqs.answer: Schools in the UAE sit the May session, with a November session also available. We do not publish IB examination or results dates on these pages, because ibo.org blocks automated access and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the current dates, including the internal deadline for the investigation, which usually sits well ahead of the IB's own submission window and is the one that actually governs your child's term.

faqs.question: What happens if no physics specialist is free at the level we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Some requirements are genuinely thin - Higher Level fields work at short notice, or investigation design help in the two weeks before a school deadline. When that happens you get three straight answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist can cover part of the need, and whether the school's own department is the better route for now. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: Fitting IB Physics into a LA Mer school week
paragraphs: Most pages about physics tutoring describe the subject. The constraint for a family living at LA Mer is not the subject, it is the clock. Schools in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster end the teaching day between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm. Add the exit onto Jumeirah Beach Road or Al Wasl Road and a student is home between 3:15pm and 4:15pm. After that there is a window of perhaps four hours before concentration on quantitative physics stops being productive, and that window has to hold food, sport, Arabic homework, four other Diploma subjects and the investigation.

Physics has a particular claim on that window because it does not reward short sessions. A worked Paper 2 question with a multi-stage calculation, a graph to linearise and an uncertainty to propagate takes twenty minutes to do properly and another ten to mark against the scheme. A thirty-minute slot produces a conversation about physics rather than physics. The practical floor is a full hour, and for a Higher Level student in the second year the useful unit is two separate hours on different days rather than one long block.

The second feature of the LA Mer week is sport and co-curricular scheduling. Swimming, football and the school activity programme in this cluster cluster between 4pm and 6pm, which pushes academic work after 6:30pm for a lot of students. That is workable for physics provided the session is the first thing after the break rather than the last thing before bed. Diploma physics at 9:30pm is money spent on a tired student.

The third is the investigation. The scientific investigation is 20 per cent of the Physics grade, it is marked against four criteria, and it has a 3,000-word limit. It does not fit into the weekly teaching hour, because it needs blocks: one to choose and narrow a research question, one to design the method, one to work through data analysis. Families who plan the year leave two or three deliberately longer sessions in the calendar for it rather than trying to graft it onto a Tuesday evening.

What that leads to in practice is a simple arrangement. One fixed hour a week in a slot that survives the school run and the activity programme, a second hour added in the second year or ahead of a mock, and two or three longer blocks reserved for the investigation. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are offered only in India. The practical gain for a LA Mer family is that a 6:45pm start is a 6:45pm start, with nobody stuck on Al Wasl Road.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-la-mer.programmesIntro: LA Mer sits close to several schools running the IB continuum alongside the British-curriculum majority. These are the programmes a physics timetable has to accommodate.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Standard Level runs to 150 teaching hours and Higher Level to 240. Both are assessed through Paper 1, split into a multiple-choice section 1A and a data-based section 1B, plus Paper 2, with the scientific investigation carrying 20 per cent. The Higher Level extension is not a separate course but extra depth inside the same five themes, which changes how a tutoring week should be shaped.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in the Jumeirah cluster commonly take Physics Higher Level alongside Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, which is the heaviest quantitative pairing on offer. In a week that ends at 3:30pm and already contains Arabic and Social Studies as KHDA mandatory subjects, that pairing is what makes session timing a real constraint rather than a preference.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: MYP sciences are assessed against four criteria rather than papers, with strong emphasis on investigation design. Students arriving in Diploma Physics from MYP 5 are usually confident designing an experiment and less practised at timed quantitative questions under a mark scheme, which is a specific and fixable gap.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within a fifteen-minute drive of LA Mer run MYP to 16 rather than IGCSE. For those students the step into Diploma Physics in September of Year 12 is the moment the weekly hour matters most, and starting it in the first term rather than after the first report is the cheaper sequence.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the route in
programmes.description: Most LA Mer students reach Diploma Physics through Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Pearson Edexcel 4PH1. Both leave a student fluent in substitution into formulae and much less practised at algebraic rearrangement before substitution, which is exactly what Diploma Paper 2 demands.
programmes.countryNote: A student moving from 0625 Extended into Physics Higher Level in a Dubai school meets uncertainty propagation and graph linearisation as new skills in the first term. Booking the weekly hour for September rather than November is what keeps that transition from becoming a grade problem by the first report.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: Diploma Physics is five themes plus the investigation. These are the blocks that generate the most tutoring hours among LA Mer students, with the specific demand each makes on a weekly slot.

subjects.name: Theme A: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum, work and energy, with rigid body mechanics and relativity at Higher Level. The reliable loss is sign convention in momentum problems. Needs a full hour because the questions are multi-stage.

subjects.name: Theme B: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, the gas laws, current and circuits. Students handle numbers confidently here and lose marks on explanation questions that ask why rather than how much. Short, frequent sessions work well on this theme.

subjects.name: Theme C: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, standing waves and the Doppler effect, with diffraction and interference extended at Higher Level. Graph interpretation dominates, so this is the theme where screen-shared annotation earns its keep.

subjects.name: Theme D: Fields
subjects.levels: SL and HL, heaviest HL extension
subjects.description: Gravitational and electric fields, motion in a field, and induction. This is the theme where Higher Level diverges most sharply, and the one that most often prompts a second weekly hour in the second year of the Diploma.

subjects.name: Theme E: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, nuclear binding energy, fission and fusion, with the photoelectric effect and quantum ideas extended at Higher Level. Taught late in the course, which means it collides with mock season and needs calendar planning.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: Marked against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with a 3,000-word limit. Needs reserved longer sessions rather than a slice of the weekly hour, and the student must do the work themselves.

subjects.name: Uncertainties and error propagation
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty bars on graphs. Examined across Paper 1B and the investigation, and almost never taught thoroughly inside normal class time.

subjects.name: Graph linearisation and gradient analysis
subjects.description: Turning a non-linear relationship into a straight line and extracting a physical quantity from the gradient. The single most transferable skill in the course and the one most often missing when a student arrives at a first session.

subjects.name: Mathematical technique for physics
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting, handling standard form, trigonometry in resolving vectors, and small-angle approximations. Students taking Mathematics Applications and Interpretation often need this explicitly taught alongside the physics.

subjects.name: Command terms and extended response
subjects.description: Distinguishing state, outline, explain, discuss and justify, and writing to the mark allocation. A four-mark explain question needs four distinct points, and students who know the physics still lose these marks routinely.

sections.heading: When a physics session actually fits after the Jumeirah school run
paragraphs: A Diploma physics session in LA Mer realistically starts at 4:30pm, 6:45pm or 7:30pm, and which of those three it is depends on the activity programme rather than the school bell. The table sets out the shape of the afternoon from a senior-school finish to the point where quantitative work stops being productive.

The 4:30pm slot works for students who are home by 3:15pm and whose sport sits later in the evening or not at all. It is the best slot available because the student is not yet tired, and it is the hardest to protect because it is the one activities colonise first. Families who want it generally have to decide in September rather than negotiate in January.

The 6:45pm slot is the workhorse. It sits after the activity programme and after food, it leaves time afterwards for the student to attempt something unsupervised, and it survives the whole year without collapsing. For Higher Level students taking two sessions a week, one at 4:30pm and one at 6:45pm on a different day is the arrangement that holds up best in this cluster.

The 7:30pm slot is viable and the 9pm slot is not. Physics is the subject where tiredness shows first, because a student who is tired can still read a history chapter but cannot carry a four-stage calculation with an uncertainty attached. Booking late on a school night produces an hour of explanation that does not stick, and the honest advice is to move the slot rather than buy more of them.

sections.heading: What the papers are worth, and which hour should be aimed at which
paragraphs: Session planning is easier once the weightings are on the table. Diploma Physics is assessed through Paper 1 and Paper 2 plus the scientific investigation. Paper 1 divides into section 1A, multiple choice, and section 1B, data-based questions. The investigation carries 20 per cent at both levels, which means a fifth of the grade is decided by work done in reserved blocks rather than in the weekly hour.

That split tells a family where to point the paid hours. Paper 1A rewards fluency and breadth, which is best built by frequent short retrieval rather than by teaching. Paper 1B rewards exactly the two skills schools have least time for: handling uncertainties and extracting physics from a graph. Paper 2 rewards extended multi-stage calculation and writing to the mark allocation. Those are three different tutoring tasks, and a tutor who treats the hour as generic revision is spreading effort across all three without improving any.

Higher Level does not add papers; it adds depth, longer papers and more teaching hours, 240 against 150. The consequence for a LA Mer student in the second year is that Theme D and the extension content land in the same term as the investigation deadline and the mock window. That collision is the argument for the second weekly hour, and it is predictable enough to plan in September rather than discover in January.

The practical rule that comes out of all this is to name the paper at the start of each session. An hour aimed at Paper 1B looks nothing like an hour aimed at Paper 2: the first is graphs, gradients and uncertainty arithmetic, the second is long questions marked to the scheme. Saying which one the hour is for turns a session into teaching.

sections.heading: Why the Fields theme is the one that breaks a LA Mer timetable
paragraphs: Every Diploma Physics cohort hits a point where one weekly hour stops being enough, and in this cluster it is almost always Theme D. Gravitational and electric fields, motion within a field, and electromagnetic induction arrive in the second year, carry the heaviest Higher Level extension of the five themes, and depend on mathematics the student may be meeting simultaneously in Analysis and Approaches.

The specific difficulty is not conceptual, it is compounded. A field question asks the student to identify the field, apply an inverse-square relationship, handle a vector direction, and often integrate or differentiate a relationship they learned three weeks earlier in a different subject. A student who is fine on each step individually fails the combined question, and the failure looks like not understanding fields when it is actually not having practised the combination.

That shapes the session. Fields work needs a question attempted alone, then marked, then the same question type attempted again, which is a two-session cycle rather than a one-hour explanation. Families in LA Mer who add a second weekly hour almost always add it during this theme, and the ones who plan for it in September pay the same total as the ones who panic in February while getting a better outcome.

The other practical point is sequence. Theme D sits close to the investigation deadline and the mock window in most Dubai schools, so the term in which it is taught is the term with the least slack. Reserving the investigation blocks earlier in the year, during the lighter Theme B and Theme C term, is the single most useful piece of calendar planning available to a Diploma physics family here.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: criteria, word limit and what a tutor may do
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is 20 per cent of the Physics grade and it is marked against four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. There is a 3,000-word limit. For a LA Mer family budgeting evening hours, the useful fact is that it is the one component where the work cannot be done inside a weekly hour, because each stage needs a block long enough to finish a thought.

Where students lose marks is consistent. Research questions are too broad to be answered by the data collected, so research design suffers. Data is recorded without uncertainties, so data analysis cannot reach the top band. Conclusions restate the trend rather than comparing it against accepted physics. Evaluation lists limitations without saying how any of them would be addressed. None of those is a physics failure; all four are design failures that show up at marking.

The boundary on tutoring here is firm and it is worth stating in plain terms. A tutor can explain what each criterion is asking for, teach the physics the student has chosen to investigate, show how uncertainty propagates through the particular calculation involved, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write any part of it, does not redraft it, and will not supply a research question for the student to adopt. Submitting work that is not the student's own is a malpractice risk that falls on the student.

The honest version of investigation support is therefore slower than the version sold by an essay mill, and it is the only version available here. Two or three reserved blocks across the first year, placed before the Theme D term, is what the component actually needs.

sections.heading: Online delivery and the Jumeirah drive, in plain numbers
paragraphs: Home tutoring is what many LA Mer parents search for, and it deserves a direct answer. In-home one-to-one physics tuition in Dubai exists and is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. A qualified subject tutor working online is published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB rates from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Those are market figures from the providers named, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

The timetable argument matters more here than the price argument. A tutor who must physically reach LA Mer for a 6:45pm start has to leave Al Barsha or Business Bay around 6pm, which on a school night is a gamble. Sessions lost or started late to traffic are the cost nobody quotes, and across a Diploma year they are more disruptive than the hourly rate, because a physics session missed in the Theme D term is not easily recovered.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. LA Mer families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past papers and session recordings. For physics specifically that format has a concrete advantage: graphs can be annotated live and kept, and a linearisation worked on screen in October is still there to look at in April.

The second advantage is the pool. Requiring a tutor to be within driving distance of the Jumeirah coast at 6:45pm on a Tuesday reduces the available set to those who live nearby and are free then. Requiring instead that they have taught Physics Higher Level and marked the investigation criteria is a different filter, and it is the one that affects the grade.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects sitting inside the same week
paragraphs: A physics timetable for a Dubai student is not competing only with sport. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA set these requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Those lessons occupy real timetable space and generate real homework.

The detail is more specific than most families realise. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects, and the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is not allowed.

For a LA Mer Diploma student the consequence is arithmetic. The week already contains a mandatory subject load on top of six Diploma subjects, the investigation and an activity programme. That is the real reason a single well-placed physics hour outperforms three badly placed ones, and the reason the slot has to be chosen around the whole week rather than around the subject.

sections.heading: The Diploma year counted forwards from September
paragraphs: Physics is a two-year course and the pressure is not spread evenly across it. Setting out the shape in advance is what lets a family place the hours where they do the most good, instead of buying more of them later.

The first year is the cheap year. Themes A, B and C are taught, the mathematics is still manageable, and the investigation can be started properly. A single weekly hour through this period, plus two or three reserved investigation blocks, is usually the whole requirement. Families who use the first year well spend less in total than families who treat it as the easy year and start in Year 13.

The second year is where the collision happens. Theme D and Theme E arrive, the Higher Level extension deepens, the investigation reaches its deadline, mocks are sat, and the final papers follow. A second weekly hour in this period is a sensible plan rather than an escalation. In the final weeks the sensible move is the opposite of escalation: fewer paid hours, more unsupervised timed practice, because at that stage technique sets through the student's own repetition.

On dates, one caution belongs on every page in this set. IB exam and results dates are not published here because they have not been verified from the IB directly; the correct source is the school's Diploma coordinator or ibo.org. For the IGCSE qualifications many of these students sat on the way in, UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June and November series, since the February/March series is offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

process.title: Send us the week, not just the subject
process.description: The first thing we ask for is the shape of the afternoon: school finish time, activity days, and what time the student is genuinely able to think. A physics slot chosen around that survives the year. One chosen around tutor availability collapses by December.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session over live video at no charge, taught rather than pitched, with the student. The tutor looks at recent marked work and starts teaching. If the match is wrong, say so and nothing is owed; one trial lesson per student, before any booking.

process.title: Name the paper each hour is for
process.description: Each session is aimed at a component: Paper 1A retrieval, Paper 1B graph and uncertainty work, Paper 2 extended questions, or an investigation criterion. Saying which one at the start is the difference between teaching and general revision.

process.title: Reserve the investigation blocks early
process.description: Two or three longer sessions are placed in the calendar during the lighter first-year terms, before the Fields theme and the mock window arrive together. The student does the work; the tutor teaches the criteria and responds to drafts.

process.description: The marked mock script is the honest diagnostic. It sets the topic list for the following weeks, which are the highest-value hours of the course. In the final stretch the paid hours reduce on purpose so the student practises alone under timed conditions.

whyPoints.description: Physics Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra pages; the Fields theme in particular diverges sharply. Tutors are matched on whether they have taught the level and marked the investigation criteria, not on how close they live to the Jumeirah coast.

faqs.question: What time can an IB Physics session realistically start for a LA Mer student?
faqs.answer: Three slots work in this cluster. A 4:30pm start suits students home by 3:15pm with no early activity, and it is the strongest slot because nobody is tired yet. A 6:45pm start after activities and food is the one that survives the whole year. A 7:30pm start is workable with care. After 9pm, quantitative physics stops holding, and buying more hours at that time of night is money spent on a tired student. Pick the slot around the activity timetable rather than around the school bell.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough for IB Physics Higher Level?
faqs.answer: For the first year of the Diploma, usually yes, provided it is well placed and the student practises between sessions. In the second year the Fields theme, the Higher Level extension, the investigation deadline and the mock window arrive close together, and that is when most LA Mer families add a second hour on a different day. Two separate hours allow work to be set, attempted alone and then marked, which a single long block cannot. Planning for the second hour in September costs the same as panicking in February and works better.

faqs.question: Why is the Fields theme harder than the rest of IB Physics?
faqs.answer: Not because the ideas are harder, but because the questions combine. A field question typically asks a student to identify the field, apply an inverse-square relationship, resolve a direction, and use calculus met recently in a different subject. Each step is manageable alone; the combination is not, until it has been practised. The failure looks like not understanding fields when it is actually not having rehearsed the sequence. That is why Fields work needs an attempt, a marking, and a second attempt rather than an explanation.

faqs.question: What share of a LA Mer student's Physics grade is decided outside the exam hall?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Standard and Higher Level. It is marked against four criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, with a 3,000-word limit. The practical consequence for scheduling is that a fifth of the grade cannot be earned inside the weekly teaching hour, because each stage needs a block long enough to finish properly. Families here usually reserve two or three longer sessions during the lighter first-year terms, which keeps the investigation away from the Fields theme and the mock window.

faqs.question: Where do IB Physics students in Dubai usually lose investigation marks?
faqs.answer: In four predictable places. The research question is too broad for the data actually collected, which damages research design. Raw data is recorded without uncertainties, which caps data analysis. The conclusion restates the trend instead of comparing it with accepted physics. The evaluation lists limitations without saying how any would be addressed. None of those is a physics failure; all four are design failures visible at marking. They are also all fixable in advance, which is why the planning blocks matter more than the writing ones.

faqs.question: What exactly can a physics tutor do for the investigation, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should offer to. A tutor can explain what each assessment criterion is asking for, teach the physics the student has chosen to investigate, show how uncertainty propagates through that particular calculation, and give feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor does not write, redraft or supply any part of it. At least one operator appearing in this search sells completed Internal Assessments; submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk that falls on the student, not the seller.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to homes in LA Mer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. LA Mer families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, screen-shared past papers and session recordings. For physics that format earns its place: a linearised graph annotated live in October can be reopened in April. It also means a 6:45pm start is not at the mercy of traffic on Al Wasl Road.

faqs.question: What does in-home physics tuition cost in Dubai compared with online?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. Qualified online subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IB rates from AED 200 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Those are market figures from the named providers, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. The timing risk matters as much as the money on a school night.

faqs.question: My child takes Maths Applications and Interpretation. Will that hold back Physics?
faqs.answer: It can, and the fix is to name it rather than work around it. Diploma Physics expects rearranging before substituting, confident standard form, trigonometry for resolving vectors, and comfort with gradients. Analysis and Approaches covers more of that incidentally. A student on Applications and Interpretation often needs the mathematical technique taught explicitly alongside the physics, which is a specific and short piece of work rather than a general weakness. It is worth raising at the trial lesson so the first few hours target it directly.

faqs.question: How does practical work get taught if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: The practical skills the papers actually assess are data skills, and those travel well. Paper 1B asks students to read and process data, linearise a relationship, extract a quantity from a gradient and handle uncertainty, and all of that is done better on a shared screen than on paper because the working is kept. The hands-on apparatus work happens at school, where it belongs. A tutor's job is the analysis, the uncertainty arithmetic and the evaluation reasoning, which is where marks are actually lost.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools near the Jumeirah coast run IB Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: Several schools in and around this cluster run the IB Diploma, including Jumeirah Baccalaureate School on the Jumeirah strip and Raffles World Academy, Dubai American Academy and Dubai International Academy Al Barsha a short drive west. Others nearby run A Level instead, so the first question for any family is which post-16 route their school offers. Those schools are named as context for the local market only; no affiliation or endorsement is implied, and the school's own admissions page is the right place to confirm current programmes.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory UAE subjects affect a Diploma physics schedule?
faqs.answer: They occupy real timetable space. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA requiring implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory subject lesson. Added to six Diploma subjects, the investigation and an activity programme, that is why one well-placed physics hour beats three badly placed ones.

faqs.question: When are IB Physics exams and results, and can you confirm the dates?
faqs.answer: No specific IB session or results date is published on this page, because those dates have not been verified directly from the IB. The right sources are your school's Diploma coordinator and ibo.org. What can be said reliably is that UAE schools sit the May session, with a November session also running. For the IGCSE qualifications students sat on the way in, UAE candidates take Cambridge in the June and November series, since the February/March series is offered to India only.

faqs.question: We are starting physics tutoring in Year 13. Is that too late?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but it changes what the hours can achieve. Starting in the second year means the Fields theme, the extension content, the investigation and mocks are all live at once, so the sensible pattern is two hours a week aimed at a diagnosed list from a marked mock rather than general revision. What cannot be rebuilt in that window is a shaky mathematical foundation, which is why the first session should be diagnostic. Starting in Year 12 costs less in total and allows the investigation to be done properly.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-la-mer.closingHeading: Pick the slot first, then the tutor
dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-la-mer.closingBody: For a LA Mer family the useful first step is not comparing hourly rates. It is deciding which evening the physics hour will live on, given a school day that ends around 3:30pm and an activity programme that runs to 6pm. Once that slot exists, a tutor can be matched to it and to the level, and the hour can be aimed at a named component rather than at physics in general. Take the free trial lesson, which is taught rather than pitched, and ask for the paper each session will target. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so nothing in the hour is spent on the drive.
