Availability is listed by hour as well as subject, because for physics the hour is part of the teaching decision.

intro.heading: Physics, a long commute and the energy that is left
paragraphs: Physics asks a student to hold several quantities in mind at once, choose a route through a problem, carry units through every line and then judge whether the answer is physically sensible. None of that survives exhaustion. In a community where every Diploma student commutes, that makes the energy budget of the week a teaching question rather than an administrative one, and it is the first thing worth getting right.

Living Legends is a single gated community of villas and apartment towers off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, between Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Remraam, with no secondary school inside the gates. Diploma students travel out, most often to Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate or the Al Khail Road corridor. School finishes between half past two and half past three, the journey runs twenty to thirty minutes in free traffic and longer on a bus serving several communities, and the student is home between four and half past four. By the time they have eaten, the clock reads five or later and the mental energy available is not what it was at nine in the morning.

What makes physics different from most subjects here is that the damage is uneven across the course. Recalling the stages of nuclear decay tolerates a tired hour. Working a multi-step mechanics problem does not. Processing uncertainty through a calculation and then writing an evaluation requires sustained attention of exactly the kind a commuting student has least of on a Tuesday evening. So a physics plan that does not distinguish between those tasks spends its best hour on the wrong thing.

There is also the pairing with mathematics, which families underestimate. IB Physics at Higher Level assumes a level of algebraic comfort that Mathematics Applications and Interpretation does not emphasise, and students taking Higher Level physics alongside Applications often find the physics mathematics harder than the physics. That is a diagnosable situation with a specific remedy, and it is far cheaper to address in the first Diploma year than the second.

IB Gram removes travel from the arrangement so the hour becomes a choice. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so a session can start minutes after arrival, move to a Saturday morning for the heavy work, and be matched on level rather than on who will drive to a gated community at six. Nobody is sent to a Living Legends address; home visits are a service we operate only in India. What follows is the physics detail: which tasks need which hour, the maths pairing, the uncertainty block, the internal assessment, and what the market charges. The order is deliberate, because a family that fixes the week first and the teaching second gets both, while one that books a convenient slot and hopes usually ends up changing tutors when the slot was the problem all along.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-living-legends.subjectsIntro: Physics is best planned topic by topic, because each topic needs a different amount of concentration and therefore a different slot in a commuting week.

subjects.name: Kinematics and dynamics
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws, momentum and impulse. Taught early and relied on throughout, so a gap resurfaces for two years. Marks go missing when a student starts from an equation rather than from a free-body diagram that was never drawn. Needs a sharp hour.

subjects.name: Work, energy and power
subjects.description: Energy transfer, efficiency and conservation arguments. The recurring failure is a correct calculation with no statement of which energy went where, which is what the longer questions pay for. Moderately demanding; suits a good weekday slot.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, internal resistance and circuit analysis. Jointly with mechanics this holds the largest share of marks. Losses come from circuits worked from the formula sheet instead of redrawn, which is a habit fixable in a few sessions.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Superposition, standing waves, diffraction and simple harmonic motion. Phase relationships are described loosely and lose marks because the language has to be precise. Content-heavy rather than calculation-heavy, so it tolerates a later slot.

subjects.name: Fields, gravitation and electromagnetism
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Field lines, potential, orbital motion and induction. Sign conventions and direction rules are the standard loss and they are drillable rather than conceptual, which makes this an efficient block for a short weekday session.

subjects.name: Thermal physics and gases
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the gas laws. Questions usually pair a calculation with an explanation of particle behaviour, and candidates answer one half. A compact block of three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.levels: SL and HL, extended at HL
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy, mass-energy equivalence and quantum phenomena. Heavier on precise vocabulary than on calculation, which makes it the best physics topic to place in a tired slot after training.

subjects.name: Data analysis and uncertainties
subjects.levels: SL and HL, and the internal assessment
subjects.description: Error propagation, gradients with uncertainty and significant-figure discipline. Where strong candidates leak marks on both the papers and the internal assessment, and the most reliably recoverable area in the whole course. Needs a long, undisturbed session.

subjects.name: The internal assessment
subjects.levels: SL and HL, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: An individual investigation assessed against published criteria and moderated by the IB. The band is largely decided by whether the research question produces data with measurable variation, which is settled before apparatus is touched.

sections.heading: The energy budget of a commuting physics week
paragraphs: Think about the week as an energy budget rather than a timetable, because that is what physics actually spends. A student has perhaps one genuinely sharp study window, one moderate one and one depleted one after travel, training, mandatory subject homework and everything else. Matching physics tasks to those three windows is the cheapest improvement available to a family in this community, and it costs nothing but planning.

The sharp window, which for most students here is a weekend morning, should carry the problem-solving. Multi-step mechanics, fields and electromagnetism problems, uncertainty propagation and full timed papers all require a chain of reasoning held for twenty minutes or more without interruption. Attempting them at six on a Thursday produces a partial version of each and a student who concludes they are bad at physics when they are simply tired.

The moderate window handles consolidation. The school taught a topic; the student works examples and has a misunderstanding corrected before it hardens. Electricity circuit practice fits here, as does drilling sign conventions in fields, because both are procedural and benefit from frequency rather than length. This is the standard weekday slot and it is genuinely productive when used for the right work.

The depleted window, typically after training, still has a use, and knowing that prevents a family from writing it off. Nuclear and quantum physics is heavier on precise vocabulary than on calculation. Command-term work, going through model answers and tidying definitions all survive a tired hour. So does reviewing a marked paper, because the thinking is being guided rather than generated. The table below assigns the course accordingly.

sections.heading: The maths pairing: why Higher Level physics sometimes feels like maths
paragraphs: This is the diagnosis families most often miss, and it is worth checking before any physics content is retaught. IB Physics at Higher Level requires comfortable algebraic manipulation: rearranging relationships with several variables, handling powers and reciprocals confidently, reading and producing gradients from non-obvious plots, and working with proportionality rather than with numbers. A student who can do the physics and not the algebra looks like a student who cannot do the physics.

The route taken in mathematics matters here. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches emphasises exactly the algebraic fluency Higher Level physics assumes. Applications and Interpretation emphasises statistical and modelling work, which is valuable in its own right and less directly aligned. A student taking Higher Level physics alongside Applications is not in trouble, but they are carrying a gap the course will not close for them, and it shows up first in the longer calculation questions rather than in the conceptual ones.

Diagnosing it is straightforward. Give the student a physics question whose physics they can explain verbally and watch where the attempt breaks down. If the reasoning is sound and the manipulation fails, the work needed is algebraic rather than physical, and it is a faster fix than reteaching the topic. Three or four sessions on rearrangement, powers and proportional reasoning often moves more marks than a term of content revision.

The practical advice for a family in this community is to check the pairing early in the first Diploma year rather than in the second. Subject combinations are hardest to adjust later, and where a combination stays as it is, the algebra can be supported deliberately instead of being discovered as a mystery in the spring. sections.heading: Uncertainty and data: the most recoverable marks in the course
paragraphs: If a family has budget for one physics block and no diagnosis to guide it, uncertainty and data analysis is the safest choice. It appears in the written papers, it carries real weight in the internal assessment, it is rarely taught as its own topic, and it is almost entirely procedural, which means it responds quickly to direct instruction.

The component skills are specific. Distinguishing absolute from fractional and percentage uncertainty. Propagating uncertainty through a sum, a product and a power. Plotting with error bars and drawing maximum and minimum gradient lines to obtain an uncertainty in a gradient. Quoting a result to a number of significant figures justified by the uncertainty rather than by the calculator display. Distinguishing random from systematic error, and knowing which one a repeated measurement addresses. Writing an evaluation that names a specific error and its specific effect on the result.

Students who have done the laboratory work frequently cannot do any of this, because school practical time is spent on apparatus and procedure while the data treatment is set as homework and never fully taught. That is not a criticism of schools; it is a predictable consequence of limited laboratory time. It does mean the gap is widespread and therefore worth targeting.

This block also suits online delivery unusually well, which matters in a community where a visiting tutor is expensive and loses minutes at the gate. Both people annotate the same data table and graph in real time, maximum and minimum gradients can be drawn and redrawn on screen, and the most valuable session of all is one where the student brings messy data from their own school practical and watches it processed properly. What a screen cannot replace is handling the apparatus, and that stays with the school.

sections.heading: The internal assessment is the first thing a commuting week drops
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the physics grade sits in an individual investigation, and in a household where the student commutes an hour a day it is the piece of work most likely to be postponed. It has no weekly lesson defending its place, its deadline is set by the school rather than the board, and that deadline falls in a term already crowded with subject assessments. So it gets left, and then it is done in a rush.

The structural problem is that the part which most determines the band happens first. A research question that produces data with no measurable variation, or a variable range too narrow to show a trend, caps the mark however carefully the report is written afterwards. A specialist can see that in one session; a student working alone usually cannot see it until the data has been collected and the time is gone.

So the sequence that works is testing before doing. Is the variable range wide enough to produce a visible effect? Will the uncertainty in the measurement swamp the quantity being measured? Is there something that can be plotted to give a meaningful gradient? Does the physics behind the question go beyond a standard school experiment? Those four checks take one session and protect a term of work, which is why the block should start well before the deadline rather than near it.

The boundary is absolute and worth stating plainly. A tutor may test a research question, explain what each criterion rewards, teach uncertainty propagation and graphing, read a draft the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, and demonstrate an analysis on different data. A tutor must never conduct the investigation, write the report, or redraft it until the work is no longer the student's own. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is an IB malpractice trigger and the penalty falls on the student, whose diploma can be withheld.

sections.heading: What the school's laboratory does, and what a tutor does
paragraphs: The honest division of labour answers the objection every physics parent raises about online tuition, and it is not a compromise.

The school runs the practical programme. It has the equipment, the technician, the safety framework and the internal assessment arrangements, and nothing about online tutoring substitutes for any of that. The student handles apparatus, takes measurements and encounters the ordinary frustrations of real experimental work in the laboratory, which is where that learning belongs.

What a tutor teaches is the part of practical physics that is assessed in writing, and it is a substantial part. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables precisely. Criticising a given method. Reading an instrument scale and recording to an appropriate precision. Processing data into a table that makes the relationship visible. Plotting with error bars. Extracting a gradient and its uncertainty. Writing an evaluation that distinguishes random from systematic error and proposes an improvement that would genuinely change the result.

Those skills are better taught on a shared screen than at a bench, because both people can annotate the same table and graph live, and because a tutor can display a deliberately flawed method and ask what is wrong with it, which is exactly the format the written papers use. On materials the position is firm: IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, data booklets and grade boundary tables are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source and works from what the school has legitimately issued.

sections.heading: What a physics specialist costs from this community
paragraphs: Physics has fewer specialists than mathematics and fewer again at Higher Level, which shows up in both rate and availability. The sourced bands first, since three of the six most visible pages competing for these searches publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

Read the Dubai bands from the top down, because Higher Level physics is bought at the top. Bestimate places examination-year specialist support at AED 200 to 450 plus and TutorChase quotes AED 270, so a single weekly specialist hour across a twelve-week Living Legends term sits somewhere between AED 2,400 and AED 5,400. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. Below that, qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300 and Unitors publishes IB from AED 200. The floor is budget online provision at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, which for a villa community set back from the main Dubailand arteries is the line where somebody else absorbs the journey instead of your evening.

For Higher Level physics the budget band is rarely the right purchase, because diagnosing a combined multi-topic loss or a maths-pairing problem requires somebody who has worked the syllabus. The sensible pattern is the qualified or specialist band for Diploma physics, with the budget band reserved for MYP science fluency where frequency matters more than depth.

The in-home premium deserves specific scrutiny in a gated community. A tutor booked for six who clears the gate at ten past has delivered fifty minutes of a paid hour, and across a school year at two sessions a week that is a serious quantity of teaching bought and not received. Monthly, four two-hour in-home sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. None of these figures is an IB Gram price list, and the MoHRE private tutor permit is free of charge, so no licensing cost belongs in any quote.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators, dates and availability
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published.

There is a conduct rule worth knowing alongside it. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. That reporting is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy text, so verify against the current ADEK document before relying on the exact wording.

On dates, this page publishes nothing it has not verified. IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session; no specific IB examination or results date appears here, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification and an unsourced date a family plans around is a genuine harm. Confirm with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications a sibling may be taking, the UAE series are June and November and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with its November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026.

On availability, Standard Level physics matches quickly and Higher Level matches well but not instantly, with the contested half past five to seven weekday window usually the limiting factor rather than the subject. The narrowest request is a Higher Level specialist for a short-notice pre-session block, and where none is free we give a date rather than a near-fit. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval or accreditation and operates no UAE office, and specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates.

faqs.question: When should a physics session happen for a Diploma student in Living Legends?
faqs.answer: The main session is usually best on a weekend morning, with a shorter weekday slot around six for consolidation. There is no secondary school inside this community, so every Diploma student commutes to Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills or the Al Khail corridor. School finishes between half past two and half past three, the journey runs twenty to thirty minutes or longer by bus, and the student is home between four and half past four. Physics problem solving needs a sharp hour, which that chain does not leave on a weekday.

faqs.question: Which physics topics can survive a session after training?
faqs.answer: Nuclear and quantum physics work well, because they are heavier on precise vocabulary than on extended calculation. So does command-term practice with model answers, tidying definitions, and reviewing a marked paper, since the thinking is being guided rather than generated. What does not survive a depleted hour is multi-step mechanics, fields and electromagnetism problems, uncertainty propagation or a full timed paper. Knowing that distinction lets a family use the after-training slot productively instead of writing it off.

faqs.question: Why does my child find Higher Level physics harder than the physics itself?
faqs.answer: Often because the difficulty is algebraic rather than physical. Higher Level physics assumes comfortable rearrangement of relationships with several variables, confident handling of powers and reciprocals, and reasoning about proportionality rather than numbers. A student who can explain the physics verbally and whose written attempt breaks down at the manipulation has a maths gap, not a physics gap. Three or four sessions on rearrangement and proportional reasoning frequently moves more marks than a term of content revision.

faqs.question: Does the IB maths route affect Higher Level physics?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than families expect. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches emphasises exactly the algebraic fluency Higher Level physics assumes, while Applications and Interpretation emphasises statistical and modelling work, which is valuable and less directly aligned. A student taking Higher Level physics with Applications is not in difficulty, but they carry a gap the physics course will not close for them, and it surfaces first in the longer calculation questions. Check the pairing in the first Diploma year rather than the second.

faqs.question: What is the single best physics block to buy with a limited budget?
faqs.answer: Uncertainty and data analysis, if there is no diagnosis to guide the choice. It appears in the written papers, carries real weight in the internal assessment, is almost entirely procedural and is rarely taught as its own topic because school laboratory time goes on apparatus and procedure. The component skills are specific and quick: propagation through products and powers, error bars and gradient uncertainty, significant figures justified by the uncertainty, and distinguishing random from systematic error.

faqs.question: How is the physics internal assessment protected in a commuting week?
faqs.answer: By testing the research question well before the school's deadline and placing the drafting in a holiday or weekend block. The band is largely decided at the design stage: a question producing data with no measurable variation, or a variable range too narrow to show a trend, caps the mark however well the report is written. Four checks take one session, and they protect a term. Leaving the work until it is urgent reliably produces a rushed investigation and a disappointed student.

faqs.question: How are laboratory skills handled if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: By dividing the work honestly. The school runs the practical programme, with the equipment, the technician, the safety framework and the internal assessment arrangements. The tutor teaches the part assessed in writing: identifying variables precisely, criticising a method, reading scales, processing data, plotting with error bars, extracting a gradient and its uncertainty, and writing a specific evaluation. Those are taught better on a shared annotated screen than at a bench, and the most useful session is one processing the student's own school data.

faqs.question: Which physics topics cause the most trouble for students here?
faqs.answer: Electricity and fields, for different reasons. Circuits go wrong because students work from the formula sheet instead of redrawing the circuit, so potential dividers and internal resistance questions collapse. Fields and electromagnetic induction go wrong on sign conventions and direction rules, which are drillable rather than conceptual. Mechanics underlies everything and is taught first, so a weakness there resurfaces for two years. Waves cause trouble through imprecise language about phase, which is a vocabulary problem with a vocabulary fix.

faqs.question: My child came from Cambridge 0625 and the Diploma feels much harder. Normal?
faqs.answer: Entirely. The step is in mathematical fluency and in the expectation that an answer is reasoned in precise physical language rather than recalled. International GCSE rewards reliable recall and procedure; the Diploma asks for a visible chain of reasoning. A student who did well on recall finds the first Diploma term harder than their grade predicted. That transition term is where most ground is lost and where work is cheapest, because the second year has no room to rebuild a mechanics foundation.

faqs.question: What does an IB physics specialist cost from Living Legends?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. Budget provision at AED 45 to 150 is rarely right for Higher Level physics. In-home visits are AED 180 to 500 including travel, and in a gated community they also lose minutes at the gate on every visit.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week make sense here?
faqs.answer: One well-placed long session plus one shorter weekday slot is the pattern that survives a full year, rather than three weekday evenings. Length serves problem solving and data work; frequency serves consolidation. In the final months before the session the frequency usually rises for technique drilling, where repetition matters more than session length. Three weekday evenings fails in this community because the journey home and the training calendar guarantee at least one of them collapses within a month.

faqs.question: Which exam session does a Living Legends physics candidate sit?
faqs.answer: IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification and an unsourced date a family plans around is a real harm; confirm with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications a sibling may be taking, the UAE series are June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, its November 2026 timetable running to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Do you provide the IB physics data booklet or past papers?
faqs.answer: No. The data booklet, syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure in addition. A tutor cites the official source, works from material the school has legitimately issued to the student, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. A provider advertising a paper library has an unresolved copyright problem, and a family using it would be participating in that rather than benefiting.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect physics specifically?
faqs.answer: More than it affects content-light subjects, because physics needs concentration and school days shorten across the Emirates while energy moves to the evening. Sessions typically shift later, often after Iftar, and shorten while holding frequency. Heavy new content is better front-loaded before the month begins, with the Ramadan weeks used for consolidation, command-term work and discussion that tolerates a shorter attention span. Non-fasting students in the same household are affected too, since the shortened school day changes the whole week's rhythm.

Check the maths pairing early, and protect the internal assessment before it becomes urgent. Then book a free trial lesson at the hour you actually intend to use, and judge it on whether the tutor names the loss pattern.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-meydan.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are Diploma Physics specialists who teach the current five-theme syllabus, the data-based paper and the scientific investigation. Each one works online, one-to-one, in a slot that fits a Meydan weekday. You see who is teaching before you pay anything.

intro.heading: Price the work before you price the tutor
paragraphs: Most Meydan parents start this search with a number in mind and no idea what the number buys. The Dubai market will quote you anything from AED 45 an hour to AED 650 an hour for something described as physics tutoring, and the descriptions barely differ. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65. Tutopiya's comparison panel starts at AED 33. Unitors publishes an IB rate from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650 for a named examiner. Those are five different products wearing one label, and a parent paying AED 450 an hour for the wrong one has not bought a better tutor, only a more expensive misunderstanding.

Diploma Physics makes the problem sharper than most subjects, because the grade is built from parts that respond very differently to paid help. Paper 1 is worth 36% and splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-based section that reward two unrelated skills. Paper 2 is worth 44% and is mostly long-answer physics where marks are given for the reasoning line, not the final number. The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20% and is marked by the school against four criteria out of six marks each. An hour spent on the investigation in week three of DP1 does something an hour spent on it in April of DP2 cannot. The same AED 250 produces a different return depending only on when you spend it.

The other thing a Meydan address changes is who is physically available. Meydan has no secondary school inside it. The school belt is Nad Al Sheba, a short drive south, where North London Collegiate School Dubai, Repton School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Kent College Dubai sit within minutes of each other. Sobha Hartland and Al Jaddaf take the rest. That means a Meydan weekday ends somewhere other than Meydan, and an in-home tutor's quote has to absorb a drive through the Ras Al Khor interchange between half past three and five o'clock. The travel is in the price whether or not it is itemised.

IB Gram does not sell home visits anywhere in the UAE. Tutoring for Meydan families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and the reason is the one that matters for a Higher Level physics grade: the pool of people who can teach the current scientific investigation criteria properly is small, and restricting it to whoever can reach Meydan by six o'clock shrinks it further. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. Saying that plainly costs us nothing and saves a parent a phone call.

What follows is a cost argument rather than a brochure. There is a rate table drawn from what Dubai providers actually publish, with the publisher named. There is a breakdown of which part of the physics grade each hour should be attacking. There is a section on the three ways families here reliably waste money on physics tutoring, because knowing the waste is worth more than knowing the rate. Everything about the regulator, the permit and the academic-honesty line is stated too, since those are the questions that arrive after the first invoice rather than before it.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-meydan.programmesIntro: Physics sits inside a programme, and the programme decides what a tutor can usefully do. A Meydan family may be anywhere on the continuum, from an MYP sciences class at an IB school in Nad Al Sheba to a DP2 student eight weeks from a paper.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: The two-year course assessed on Paper 1, Paper 2 and a scientific investigation. Paper 1 splits into 1A, a multiple-choice section, and 1B, a set of data-based and practical-skills questions. Paper 2 is structured long-answer physics. Standard Level is timetabled for 150 hours of teaching and Higher Level for 240, and the extra ninety hours are not evenly spread: they load onto fields, nuclear and quantum physics, and the harder end of wave behaviour.
programmes.countryNote: In Meydan this is the version most families are paying for, because the Nad Al Sheba IB schools run the full continuum and students arrive in DP1 from their own MYP sciences classes. Cost per month is usually set by how many Higher Level sciences a student is carrying, not by the hourly rate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Sciences in the MYP is marked against four criteria, each out of eight: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. There is no external physics paper. A student can hold a 6 in MYP sciences and still arrive in DP1 Physics without the algebraic fluency the Diploma assumes, because criterion A rewards explanation while Paper 2 rewards a working line.
programmes.countryNote: Meydan families at the IB continuum schools in Nad Al Sheba often meet this gap in the September of DP1. Spending four hours in MYP 5 on rearranging formulae and handling units is the cheapest physics tutoring available to a Dubai family, and almost nobody buys it then.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the route in
programmes.description: Several Meydan students reach Diploma Physics from Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1 rather than from the MYP, usually after an IGCSE at Repton School Dubai or Kent College Dubai. The IGCSE course is content-heavy and formula-driven; the Diploma is derivation-driven. A student who scored well by memorising equations frequently stalls in DP1 when asked to justify why an equation applies.
programmes.countryNote: If your child is on this route, the useful spend is a short block in the summer between Year 11 and DP1 rather than a longer block in October when the first Diploma test has already gone badly. Dubai providers charge the same rate in July as in October for materially easier work.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme and single-subject study
programmes.description: A smaller number of students take Diploma Physics as a certificate course rather than inside the full Diploma, or alongside a Career-related Programme. The subject assessment is identical, including the scientific investigation, but the student carries no Theory of Knowledge or Extended Essay load, which changes what a sensible weekly commitment looks like.
programmes.countryNote: For a Meydan family this usually means one subject needs attention rather than a timetable needing rescue, and the monthly cost is correspondingly closer to the lower end of the Dubai bands than the upper.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-meydan.subjectsIntro: Physics is one paid hour among several in most households. These are the Diploma subjects Meydan families most often buy alongside it, with a note on what each one actually costs in effort rather than in dirhams.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes, two papers and a 24-mark scientific investigation. The expensive part is not content recall but the long-answer reasoning on Paper 2, where a correct number with no stated principle earns part of the available credit and nothing more.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The course Higher Level Physics quietly assumes. Calculus, logarithms and the manipulation of indices turn up inside physics questions long before the maths class has finished teaching them, which is why these two subjects are so often tutored together.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistically weighted and modelling-led. A student taking Applications and Interpretation alongside Higher Level Physics usually needs explicit algebra practice that their maths timetable will not supply, and that practice is cheaper bought early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares the scientific investigation structure and the same four criteria, so a student taking both sciences can prepare one methodology and apply it twice. Families paying separately for two investigation reviews are usually paying twice for one conversation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-handling overlaps strongly with Physics Paper 1B. Students who can read an uncertainty on a physics graph tend to score better on biology data questions, and the transfer runs in both directions.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Chosen often by Meydan students heading for engineering. The logic and systems content is independent of Physics, but the two subjects compete for the same problem-solving evenings, which matters when you are scheduling.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Carries its own substantial internal assessment load. Students taking Design Technology with Physics face two long coursework pieces in the same window, and the scheduling cost of that is larger than the tutoring cost.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Taken by some students instead of a second science. The quantitative demand is lower than Physics but the essay demand is higher, so a household budget often shifts from calculation support to structured writing support.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An assessed essay and exhibition that sit outside subject teaching and still consume DP2 evenings. Worth knowing about when you plan a physics schedule, because the TOK deadline usually lands in the same month as the investigation deadline.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece. Students who write it in physics need supervision on method and scope rather than content, and that supervision is a different purchase from weekly subject tutoring.

sections.heading: What Dubai providers actually charge for physics, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market and work up, because that is the order in which a parent should eliminate options rather than the order a sales page presents them. The cheapest published physics tutoring available to a Meydan family is a university-student tutor working online, advertised by EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 an hour and by Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. At that price the tutor is almost certainly working from the textbook rather than from the assessment criteria, which is fine for revising content a student has already met and close to useless for a Paper 2 reasoning problem.

The next band up is a qualified subject tutor teaching online, which in Dubai runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. Unitors publishes an IGCSE rate from AED 150 and an IB rate from AED 200, which is the only hourly figure any competitor in this market states openly. This band is where most Diploma Physics work actually belongs. Above it sits the specialist band, AED 200 to 450 and upwards, where TutorChase lists AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts exam-year specialists between AED 200 and 450. At the top, BartyED quotes AED 650 an hour for a named examiner.

In-home one-to-one in Dubai is quoted separately, at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate putting the usual range at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. The difference between that band and the online band is not teaching quality. It is a car, a driver and forty minutes of Dubai traffic, and in Meydan's case a drive that crosses Ras Al Khor Road at the worst hour of the day. Monthly packages circulate too: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly price list on these pages, and a parent should treat any figure above as the market rather than as our quote. What we do instead is give the first lesson free so the comparison is made on teaching rather than on copy, and state the delivery model before anyone pays: one-to-one, live video, Gulf Standard Time.

sections.heading: Which part of the physics grade each paid hour should be attacking
paragraphs: A physics grade is not one thing, so an hour of tutoring is not one thing either. Paper 1 carries 36% of the final mark at both Standard and Higher Level, and it is two separate problems in one paper. Section 1A is multiple choice, where the loss pattern is almost always speed and misread stems rather than ignorance. Section 1B is data-based and practical, where students lose marks on uncertainty, graph gradients, unit prefixes and the difference between precision and accuracy. Those two sections need different lessons, and a tutor who treats Paper 1 as a single revision block is charging for one hour and delivering half of one.

Paper 2 carries 44% and is the largest single pot of marks in the subject. It is structured long answer, and the published mark schemes award credit for the stated principle, the substitution and the conclusion separately. A student who writes the right final number with no working visible can lose most of the available marks on a six-mark item. This is the most tutorable part of Diploma Physics and the part cheap tutoring touches least, because marking a long answer properly takes longer than teaching the content did.

The scientific investigation carries the remaining 20% and is marked by the school against four criteria of six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Twenty-four marks, a 3,000-word ceiling, and a deadline the school sets rather than the IB. The return on a paid hour here is the highest in the subject in DP1 and close to zero in the last fortnight before submission, because by then the data exists and the design cannot be changed. A family that buys investigation support in April of DP2 has bought proofreading they are not permitted to accept.

Put those three together and the spending plan writes itself. DP1 money goes on content plus one or two investigation reviews. The mock window pays for diagnosis. DP2 money goes on timed Paper 2 work and on Section 1B data skills. Nothing in that sequence requires the top of the market, and a household following it will usually spend less in total than one buying a steady weekly hour for two years without changing what the hour does.

sections.heading: The three ways Meydan families reliably waste physics money
paragraphs: The first is paying a premium rate for content delivery. A tutor at AED 400 an hour re-explaining Newton's second law is doing work a textbook, a school teacher and a free video all do adequately. The premium bands exist for diagnosis and for marking, which are the two things nothing free can supply. Households that buy at the top of the market and then ask for content revision are buying the most expensive version of the cheapest service, and it is the single most common pattern we see in this corridor.

The second is buying a steady weekly hour and never auditing it. A sixty-minute slot that was correctly aimed in October of DP1 is frequently pointed at nothing by February of DP2, because the student's gap has moved from content to timing and the format has not. The fix costs nothing: ask for the written note after each session, and if three consecutive notes describe the same gap, the format is wrong rather than the student. A parent who does that audit twice a year spends materially less than one who does not.

The third is paying for travel without knowing it. An in-home quote in Meydan has to cover a drive in from Al Quoz or Al Khail Road through the late-afternoon interchange, and that drive is priced into the hourly figure rather than itemised beneath it. The published Dubai gap between online and in-home one-to-one runs from roughly AED 30 to over AED 200 an hour depending on which end of each band you compare. For a weekly session across an exam year that is a real sum, and what it buys is proximity rather than subject depth.

There is a fourth pattern worth naming even though it is less common: buying three subjects at once in a panic after a bad DP1 report. Three weekly hours is a large monthly commitment and it usually diagnoses nothing, because the household cannot tell which subject improved for which reason. One diagnostic block in the worst subject, then a decision, costs less and produces information.

sections.heading: Online against an in-home physics tutor in Meydan, priced honestly
paragraphs: The honest comparison is not online versus in-person as a philosophy. It is what each format gives a Meydan household in return for the money, on a Tuesday in November, with a student at a Nad Al Sheba school and a parent returning from Business Bay. An in-home tutor arrives with presence and with a car, and for a younger student who will not settle without someone in the room, presence is worth paying for. A Diploma Physics student eight weeks from a paper usually needs something else: a person who has marked that paper's scheme many times and can show why four of six marks went missing.

Those two needs pull in opposite directions in Meydan specifically, because of geography. The specialist pool for Higher Level physics anywhere is small. The specialist pool that can also reach a Meydan villa by six o'clock, having left Al Quoz at five, is smaller again, and the tutor who meets both conditions is being selected on their commute as much as on their subject. Online delivery removes the commute from the selection criteria entirely. That is the whole argument, and it is a practical argument rather than a technological one.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in India. So the comparison below is between what the Dubai in-home market quotes and what we actually sell, which is one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time. A screen share with a shared whiteboard, a past paper open on both sides and a recording the student can rewatch does things a kitchen table cannot. A kitchen table does one thing a screen cannot, which is sit a reluctant fourteen-year-old down. Both of those are true and a parent should weigh them rather than be sold one.

On timing, the online slot wins in this community for a reason specific to it. Meydan's school run ends in Nad Al Sheba, and a parent frequently is not home when the student is. An online lesson can start at quarter past four with the student alone and the parent still on Al Khail Road. An in-home lesson at that hour requires the tutor to arrive while nobody is back, which most families reasonably decline.

sections.heading: Counting a Diploma Physics year backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Working forwards from today produces a plan that runs out of time. Working backwards from the assessment produces one that does not, and in physics the critical date is usually not the examination at all. It is the school's internal deadline for the scientific investigation, because that deadline is set locally, sits in DP2 or late DP1 depending on the school, and cannot be moved. Every Meydan school on the list above runs a different one. The first thing a family should do is ask the science coordinator for it in writing.

From that date, count back. The evaluation and conclusion need a draft to exist, so a draft deadline sits several weeks earlier. The data analysis needs data, so collection sits earlier again. The research design needs questioning before a single measurement is taken, which puts the highest-value tutoring conversation months before the deadline a parent is worrying about. This is why investigation support is the cheapest useful purchase in DP1 and an expensive irrelevance in DP2.

On the written papers, UAE candidates sit the May session, which is the one Dubai schools enter. We do not publish an IB examination or results date on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date in this project has been confirmed from the source, and a wrong date is worse than no date. Ask your school's IB coordinator and treat their answer as the authority. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications, the published timetables are the reference, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own version of the timetable, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one.

The rest of the calendar is local and predictable. Mocks land in the winter term at most Nad Al Sheba schools. Ramadan shortens the school day and moves tutoring to a post-iftar slot for many families here. The weeks either side of a mid-year break are when revision quietly disappears. A family that marks those four things on a calendar in September is making better decisions in March than one that discovers them.

sections.heading: What a physics tutor may and may not do with the scientific investigation
paragraphs: The scientific investigation must be the student's own work, and the line is not a matter of taste. Twenty-four marks and a fifth of the grade depend on it, the school authenticates it, and a breach is an academic-honesty matter that falls on the student rather than on the tutor. So it is worth stating exactly what is bought when a family buys investigation support, because two competitors in this market sell something else entirely and one of them advertises completed assessments at a set price.

A tutor may teach the physics the investigation needs. A tutor may ask whether a research question is answerable with the equipment available, whether the independent variable can actually be controlled, and whether the proposed range will produce a gradient worth analysing. A tutor may explain what criterion B expects from uncertainty treatment, show how the published criteria are worded, and read a student's own draft and say which criterion is not yet being met. A tutor may point at a paragraph and say that the evaluation names a limitation without explaining its effect, which is the most common way criterion D marks go missing.

A tutor may not choose the research question, write any part of the report, supply data, redraw the student's graphs, rewrite a conclusion, or edit a draft to completion. IB Gram does not provide any of those things, and a tutor who offers them is creating an expulsion risk for the student. If you have been quoted a price for a finished investigation anywhere in this market, that is the service being sold, and it is worth knowing what it exposes your child to before the invoice.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and to Theory of Knowledge. Supervision, questioning and feedback on the student's own work are legitimate and valuable. Production is not. Saying so plainly is a genuine differentiator in a search results page where it is not always said at all.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and what a Meydan parent can check alone
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Every school a Meydan family uses sits under KHDA and is inspected on a published band scale. Elsewhere in the country the map differs: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah under the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages in this market, which is odd given how many of their readers live in Abu Dhabi.

For tutoring specifically, the relevant authority is not KHDA but the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services system. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

This is also where a parent can do their own verification cheaply. Ask any prospective tutor, including ours, whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit and ask to see it. It costs nothing to issue, so there is no reason for a legitimate tutor to be without one. Ask separately whether a provider with premises holds a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the specific thing a training institute in Dubai needs and which has its own initial-approval and renewal steps.

IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here will suggest otherwise. We are an independent platform that matches families with subject specialists and delivers lessons online. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is useful to a parent. Implying it endorses us would be the single most misleading thing these pages could say.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside Diploma Physics
paragraphs: Every Meydan family running a Diploma timetable is also running a second, mandatory one, and it changes the arithmetic of a tutoring week more than most parents expect. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of which international curriculum the school is licensed for, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. These lessons occupy real timetable space that a Diploma student has to find alongside six subjects, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay.

The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic must be the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies for Arab students is taught primarily in Arabic; non-Arabs are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold the appropriate KHDA approval.

Instructional time is counted in 40-minute lesson units. Schools may vary the actual lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. There is also a content restriction worth knowing before you buy any help here: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That rules out the sort of supplementary workbook approach a family might reasonably take in physics.

The practical consequence for a physics budget is simple. A DP1 student at a Nad Al Sheba school who is already struggling to fit six subjects into a week is also sitting several mandatory-subject periods, and the evening available for paid physics work is narrower than the school day suggests. Families who map the whole week before booking a slot tend to pick a slot that survives the term.

sections.heading: Getting started from a Meydan address, with the limits stated
paragraphs: The first step is a conversation rather than a purchase. Tell us the school, the level, the subjects, the current grades and the time of day that actually works, and we will say whether we have a Diploma Physics specialist free in that window. If we do not, we say so rather than offering a generalist at a specialist rate, which is the point in this process where most of the market quietly substitutes.

Then there is a free trial lesson with the specific person who would teach your child. It is genuinely free: no card, no commitment, no automatic enrolment afterwards. The trial exists because every provider's copy reads the same and the only honest comparison is sixty minutes of actual teaching. A parent is welcome to sit in on it, and a parent of a DP2 student is usually better off reading the written note afterwards instead.

What happens if nobody suitable is free is worth stating plainly, because no competitor in this market states it. Higher Level physics specialists are a small group, and the four-to-seven window on Gulf Standard Time is the most requested in the UAE. Sometimes the answer is a different hour, sometimes a different day, and sometimes it is a wait. We will tell you which, with a date. We will not fill the slot with somebody who last taught the subject under a previous syllabus.

From there, the working pattern is weekly sessions with a written note each time, a format review twice a year, and an explicit decision point after the mock window about whether to switch from content work to timed paper work. The money follows the plan rather than the calendar. That sequence is the whole of our method, and it is deliberately boring.

faqs.question: What does an IB Physics tutor cost per hour for a Meydan family?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and exam specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards. Unitors states an IB rate from AED 200, TutorChase lists AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai table puts exam-year specialists in the 200 to 450 band. Budget online tutoring advertises much lower, from around AED 33 to 65. In-home one-to-one is quoted separately at AED 180 to 500 because the travel sits inside the figure. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our price list. We give the first lesson free so the comparison is made on teaching.

faqs.question: Is a cheap physics tutor a false economy or a sensible starting point?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the hour is for. A tutor at the bottom of the Dubai market, advertised from AED 33 to 65, is usually working from a textbook, and for revising content a student has already met that is adequate. For a Paper 2 long-answer problem it is not, because diagnosing why four of six marks went missing requires familiarity with how the mark scheme awards credit for the stated principle. Buy cheap for content consolidation and specialist for diagnosis and marking. The expensive mistake runs the other way: paying a premium rate for someone to re-explain Newton's second law.

faqs.question: How much should a Meydan household budget per month for Diploma Physics?
faqs.answer: Work in months rather than hours, because that is how the money actually leaves the account. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for an exam-year specialist. Packages in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. One Higher Level science taught weekly through DP2, with a few ninety-minute past-paper blocks near the papers, usually lands in the middle to upper range. Two Higher Level sciences roughly doubles it.

faqs.question: Does an in-home physics tutor in Meydan justify the extra cost?
faqs.answer: The published gap between online and in-home one-to-one in Dubai ranges from about AED 30 to over AED 200 an hour depending which ends of the bands you compare, and what it buys is a person in the room rather than deeper subject knowledge. For a younger student who will not settle alone, that presence is worth money. For a DP2 student eight weeks from a paper, the better purchase is someone who has marked that scheme repeatedly. Meydan makes it starker: an in-home tutor crosses Ras Al Khor Road at the worst hour, so you are also selecting on their commute.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a villa in Meydan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Physics tutoring for Meydan families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard, a past paper open on both sides and a recording the student can rewatch. The reason is practical rather than ideological. The pool of people who can teach the current Diploma Physics course properly is small, and narrowing it to those who can reach a Meydan address by six o'clock narrows it much further.

faqs.question: Which part of the physics grade gives the best return on tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Paper 2, by a clear margin, because it carries 44% of the grade and the marks are awarded for the reasoning line rather than the final answer. A student writing correct numbers with no visible working can lose most of a six-mark item, and that is fixable in a way content gaps often are not. Second is the scientific investigation, worth 20% across four criteria, but only if bought in DP1 while the research design can still change. Paper 1A multiple choice is the weakest purchase; it responds to timed practice the student can do alone.

faqs.question: When is scientific investigation support worth paying for, and when is it too late?
faqs.answer: The high-return window is early DP1, before data collection begins, when a tutor can ask whether the research question is answerable with the available equipment and whether the proposed range will produce a gradient worth analysing. A second useful point comes once a first draft exists, for criterion-by-criterion questioning. By the last fortnight before the school's deadline there is almost nothing legitimate left to buy, because the design is fixed and the only remaining help would be editing, which a tutor must not provide and a student must not accept.

faqs.question: What is Paper 1B and why do Meydan students lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: Paper 1B is the data-based and practical-skills section that sits alongside the multiple-choice section inside Paper 1, which together carry 36% of the grade. Marks disappear on uncertainty treatment, gradient calculation from a graph, unit prefixes and the distinction between precision and accuracy. These are procedural skills rather than content, which makes them unusually tutorable and unusually neglected, because a revision block aimed at Paper 1 as a single entity tends to drill content and leave the data skills untouched. Ask for them to be timetabled separately.

faqs.question: My child is coping at Standard Level but Higher Level Physics looks unreachable. What changes?
faqs.answer: Higher Level is timetabled for 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard, and the additional ninety hours are not spread evenly. They concentrate on fields, on nuclear and quantum physics, and on the harder end of wave behaviour. The other change is mathematical: Higher Level questions assume comfort with manipulating indices, logarithms and rates of change, often before the maths course has formally covered them. That is why Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are so frequently tutored together, and why the algebra, not the physics, is often the real gap.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or finish my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering it is creating an expulsion risk for your child. The investigation is the student's own work, authenticated by the school, and worth a fifth of the subject grade across four criteria of six marks each. A tutor may teach the underlying physics, question whether the research design will work, explain what criterion B expects of uncertainty treatment and read a draft to say which criterion is not yet met. A tutor may not choose the question, supply data, redraw graphs, write any section or edit to completion. IB Gram provides none of those.

faqs.question: Which schools do Meydan physics students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Meydan has no secondary school inside it, so the cohort is set elsewhere. The nearest belt is Nad Al Sheba, where North London Collegiate School Dubai, Repton School Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Kent College Dubai all sit within a short drive. Across Ras Al Khor Road the alternatives include Hartland International School, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, Deira International School and Dubai English Speaking College. Each sets its own internal deadline for the scientific investigation, which is the date that should shape your spending. These schools are named as context; no affiliation is implied.

faqs.question: How early can a physics session start on a Meydan weekday?
faqs.answer: Around quarter past four is realistic for most Meydan addresses once the Nad Al Sheba school run is done, and that assumes the student can begin without a parent present. Many Meydan parents work in Business Bay or DIFC and are not home until five or later, which is one of the real advantages of the online format: the lesson can start on time with the student alone. If a parent wants to be in the room, the practical earliest moves to half past five, and that slot is the most contested one in the UAE.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor promise a particular grade by the exams?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who does. No tutor controls the paper, the mark scheme, the grade boundaries or how much work the student does between sessions, so a promised score is a sales device rather than a professional judgement. What a tutor can do is name the specific gap, show the evidence from a marked script, and describe what closing it would take in hours. Several providers in this market publish outcome claims with no sample size, date or method behind them. Ask for the method and watch what happens.

faqs.question: Does an online physics tutor still need the MoHRE private tuition permit?
faqs.answer: The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing to obtain, there is no sensible reason for a tutor working with UAE families to be without one, so ask to see it. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can we pay my child's own school physics teacher for private lessons instead?
faqs.answer: It is not a shortcut we would help arrange. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document before relying on the exact wording. Beyond the rules, the arrangement puts the person who marks your child's internal work in a paid relationship with you, which is a poor position for everyone.

faqs.question: Can you confirm the IB examination and results dates for physics?
faqs.answer: No, and we will not publish one. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the source, and a wrong date is something a family acts on. UAE schools enter the May session; that much is safe to say. For the actual dates, ask your school's IB coordinator and treat their answer as authoritative. Where Cambridge or Pearson qualifications are involved, their published timetables are the reference, and Cambridge warns that every centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level physics specialist has a Meydan-friendly slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date. The pool of people who can teach the current five-theme Diploma Physics course and mark its papers properly is small, and the four-to-seven window on Gulf Standard Time is the most requested in the UAE. Sometimes the answer is a different hour, sometimes a different weekday, sometimes a wait of a fortnight. What we will not do is seat a generalist in the slot and charge a specialist rate, which is the substitution most of this market makes silently. No competitor page we examined discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: Compare physics against maths, not Mirdif against Al Mizhar
paragraphs: There is a comparison every eastern-suburb family makes and it is the wrong one. Looking for an IB physics tutor in Mirdif, finding thin results, then trying Al Mizhar, Al Warqa and Al Khawaneej in turn - as though the next neighbourhood holds a Diploma physicist who has simply not been found. It does not, and the reason is structural rather than local: the IB accounts for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, so Diploma physics teachers are scarce in every part of the emirate including the western school belt.

The comparison that actually changes outcomes is internal to the subject. Physics at Diploma level is taught in two languages at once: the physics and the mathematics that expresses it. A very large share of students who appear to be failing physics are failing the algebra inside it - rearranging a formula under time pressure, handling indices and standard form, converting units, taking a gradient from a graph. Their physics is fine. Their arithmetic is costing them a mark a question, which is a grade across a paper.

Those two problems look identical on a report and completely different on a marked script. The physics problem shows as a question not attempted, or an explanation that describes rather than explains. The maths problem shows as a correct formula, a correct substitution, and then a wrong value - or a question abandoned two lines in. Hiring a physics specialist to fix an algebra problem is the most common misdirected spend in this subject, and it is expensive because physics specialists sit at the top of the Dubai rate card.

Mirdif has one further comparison worth dismissing explicitly, because it comes up here and nowhere else in Dubai. Dubai Silicon Oasis and Dubai International Academic City are a short drive south-east, full of engineers, technologists and university physics teaching. None of that is IB Diploma physics. The Diploma has HL-only content, an internally assessed investigation marked against published criteria, command terms that carry mark-scheme consequences, and an uncertainty treatment that costs strong candidates a whole band. Somebody who uses physics professionally may know the subject perfectly and have never seen a criterion descriptor.

So this page gives you the diagnostic, the syllabus detail to test a tutor with, and the Dubai market in AED with every figure attributed. Named IB specialists are quoted AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table showing 200-450+; a qualified subject tutor online is AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200; in-home visits are quoted AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Mizhar family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is how a scarce subject at a specific level becomes reachable from the eastern suburbs at all.
