dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: A Mirdif physics enquiry can sit at several points in the continuum, and the useful work differs sharply between them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Physics
programmes.description: Available at Higher and Standard Level, with written papers plus the internally assessed scientific investigation, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Higher Level adds content and depth, and its extended-response questions reward command-term discipline as much as content knowledge. Uncertainty treatment appears in both the papers and the investigation.
programmes.countryNote: The bulk of Mirdif physics enquiries, usually prompted by the first substantial Year 12 assessment. The pattern repeats whichever eastern suburb the family lives in: a student who did well in IGCSE physics meets Higher Level and finds that the mathematics has stopped being incidental.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences into Physics
programmes.description: Integrated sciences before the subjects separate, assessed against four criteria scored 0-8: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating are the skills the Diploma investigation assumes, introduced several years earlier and at a lower rate tier.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Mirdif family can prevent the Year 12 problem entirely, and at mid-market rather than specialist prices. Uncertainty handling and method design with controlled variables are both introduced here and both assumed later, which makes this the cheapest effective physics spending in the whole pathway.

programmes.name: IGCSE Physics as the foundation
programmes.description: Cambridge 0625, tiered Core and Extended, or Pearson 4PH1 as a single tier. Electricity and waves absorb most lost marks at this level, and the failure is usually arithmetic rather than conceptual. The step up to Diploma physics is built on exactly the algebraic fluency the IGCSE only begins to demand.
programmes.countryNote: Relevant because most of the local teaching experience in the eastern suburbs sits at this level and in other curricula. That is genuinely useful for Years 10 and 11 and insufficient for Higher Level Diploma work, where the mathematical demand is the difficulty.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with Physics
programmes.description: CP students take at least two Diploma courses, which may include Physics, assessed exactly as a Diploma student's would be with the same papers and the same investigation. Offered by a small number of UAE schools and frequently confused with the Diploma when post-16 options are being compared.
programmes.countryNote: Worth distinguishing because a CP certificate is not the Diploma, and engineering destinations in particular ask for specific qualifications. For any UAE university, check the Ministry of Education equivalency position directly with the authority rather than relying on a secondary source.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: Below, the physics a Mirdif family is actually buying help with, with the mathematics each topic hides and where the marks go.

subjects.name: Mechanics and kinematics
subjects.description: Motion, forces, momentum and energy. Conceptually the most accessible part of the course and the place where algebraic weakness shows first, because almost every question requires rearrangement before anything physical is decided. Marks go on signs, on units left unconverted and on vector directions assumed rather than stated.

subjects.name: Circular motion and gravitation
subjects.description: Where Standard Level students most often lose confidence. The physics is a small number of relationships applied carefully, and the difficulty is holding several substitutions in order. HL extends into orbital reasoning and field treatments that reward algebraic comfort rather than extra memorisation.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat and the gas laws, with calculation-heavy questions that punish unit inconsistency - kelvin against celsius, kilojoules against joules. Explanations lose marks when a particle-level account is replaced by a restatement of the observation.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Superposition, standing waves, diffraction and interference, with HL extending into more demanding treatments. Marks go on diagrams drawn without labelled quantities, and on calculations where the period and frequency relationship gets inverted under time pressure.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The most heavily examined area across every level of physics and the one where arithmetic failure is most costly, because circuit questions chain several calculations together and an early slip propagates. A systematic approach to circuit analysis is teachable in two sessions and rarely taught.

subjects.name: Fields and electromagnetic induction
subjects.levels: HL and SL, HL extends substantially
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields treated together, with HL adding depth and more demanding induction problems. Conceptually the hardest part of the course for most students and the place where a specialist is least substitutable, because the reasoning is unfamiliar rather than merely difficult.

subjects.name: Atomic, nuclear and particle physics
subjects.description: Decay, binding energy and particle interactions, with HL adding depth. Calculation marks go on standard form and on energy unit conversions; explanation marks go on accounts that name a process without describing the mechanism behind it.

subjects.name: Energy production and transfer
subjects.description: Sankey reasoning, efficiency and the physics of energy sources. Often treated as the easy topic and often a source of lost marks, because efficiency calculations are straightforward and the explanation questions demand precise comparative reasoning rather than general comment.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error treatment
subjects.description: Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through calculations, and uncertainty on a gradient. The quiet grade killer: it appears on the written papers and again inside the investigation, and it is rarely taught explicitly in a crowded Year 12 timetable.

subjects.name: Graph and gradient technique
subjects.description: Choosing what to plot to linearise a relationship, taking a gradient from large intervals, reading an intercept and relating both to the physics. Appears in the papers and is central to the investigation, which makes it the most transferable few hours available in the subject.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: The internally assessed component, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, and banked before the papers. Must be entirely the student's own work; a tutor teaches the method and the uncertainty treatment, marks practice work and comments on the student's own draft.

subjects.name: The algebra inside the physics
subjects.description: Rearrangement, indices, standard form, unit conversion and multi-step substitution under time. Not a physics topic and frequently the actual problem, which is why the first session should diagnose it rather than assume the physics is at fault.

sections.heading: Is it physics or is it maths? The diagnostic
paragraphs: This takes ten minutes with a marked script and it determines everything that follows, including which rate tier you should be paying. The two problems produce different kinds of lost mark, and once you know what to look for the distinction is unmistakable.

A physics problem looks like this: a question left unattempted because the student did not know where to start. An explanation that restates the observation instead of giving a mechanism. A field or induction question where the reasoning direction is wrong. A diagram drawn without the quantities labelled. These are content and reasoning failures, and they need a physics teacher.

A maths problem looks like this: the formula written correctly, the substitution correct, and then a wrong value. A question abandoned two lines in. A unit left unconverted - kelvin against celsius, millimetres against metres, kilojoules against joules. A standard-form slip in a nuclear calculation. A gradient taken from two points that are too close together. These are fluency failures, they are not fixed by more physics, and they cost a mark a question which is a grade across a paper.

The financial consequence is direct. Named IB specialists in Dubai are quoted AED 200-450 an hour and above, while a qualified subject tutor is AED 150-300 - and the algebra work sits comfortably in the lower band. A family who hires a physics specialist to fix an arithmetic problem pays the premium and sees no movement, because the specialism is not being used. A tutor who reads the script and says so is reducing your bill rather than protecting it, which is the single most useful signal available in a first conversation.

sections.heading: Why the engineers next door do not solve this
paragraphs: Mirdif sits a short drive from Dubai Silicon Oasis and Dubai International Academic City, which between them hold a technology free zone and a cluster of university campuses teaching engineering and the physical sciences. Eastern-suburb families notice this and reasonably conclude that physics expertise must be abundant nearby. The physics is abundant. The Diploma teaching is not, and the difference is specific enough to be worth setting out.

The Diploma has four things that professional or higher-education physics experience does not supply. Grades run 1-7 with no intuitive mapping onto other systems. Every subject carries an internally assessed investigation marked against criteria - research design, data analysis, conclusion, evaluation - with published descriptors. Command terms are specified and mark schemes act on them, so explain, describe, outline and deduce ask for different things and answering the wrong one caps the response. And Higher Level content differs from Standard Level in ways a non-teacher cannot be expected to know.

There is also a subtler mismatch. Somebody who uses physics professionally solves problems with the tools they prefer and often with software. A Diploma student solves them under timed conditions, by hand, with a specified data booklet and a mark scheme awarding method credit in particular places. Expert knowledge sometimes makes that harder to teach, not easier, because the expert's route is not the route the marks follow.

None of which is an argument against hiring somebody with a strong physics background - it is an argument for testing. Ask them to name the investigation criteria. Ask what Higher Level adds to the fields topic. Ask where uncertainty treatment costs a band. Across the entire competitor corpus researched for this market, not one page names a single IB assessment criterion, which tells you how rarely this knowledge accompanies physics knowledge.

sections.heading: What Higher Level physics adds
paragraphs: Parents are often told Higher Level is Standard Level with more topics, which understates it in a particular way. Higher Level physics adds depth where the mathematics gets harder, and it adds reasoning in the areas students already find least intuitive. The additions are not evenly distributed across the course, which matters for planning.

Fields and electromagnetic induction take the largest share. This is where a Higher Level student meets reasoning that has no Standard Level equivalent in difficulty - relating field strength, potential and energy across gravitational, electric and magnetic cases, and handling induction problems that require tracking several relationships at once. It is also the area where a non-specialist is least able to help, because the difficulty is unfamiliarity rather than volume.

Elsewhere the pattern is mathematical intensification. Circular motion and gravitation gain orbital treatments, waves gain more demanding analysis, and atomic and nuclear physics gain depth in binding energy and particle interaction. A Higher Level student struggling in these is frequently not struggling with physics they have never met - they are struggling with calculations whose Standard Level version they handled, which returns the diagnosis to the question this page opened with.

Confirm the current content and weightings for your child's level with the school or the subject guide rather than with any summary, including this one, because the IB revises syllabuses between cycles and the school holds the version your child is assessed against. The table sets out the shape of the difference so you can hear whether a prospective tutor is describing the course or describing physics in general.

sections.heading: The uncertainty chain, and where it costs a whole band
paragraphs: Physics is the subject where uncertainty treatment is most consequential, because it appears twice: on the written papers and inside the internally assessed investigation, which is worth roughly a fifth of the grade and is marked months before the papers are sat. A student who has never been taught it explicitly loses marks in both places, and the loss is invisible on a report because it looks like general weakness.

The chain has distinct links and each has its own failure. Raw uncertainty on a measurement, taken from the instrument rather than guessed. Absolute converted to fractional or percentage. Propagation through addition and subtraction, which behaves differently from multiplication and division. Propagation through a power. Uncertainty on a gradient, taken from the steepest and shallowest plausible lines rather than asserted. Then a final result quoted to a precision the measurements actually support rather than to whatever the calculator produced.

None of it is conceptually difficult, and almost none of it fits into a crowded Year 12 timetable alongside the content. That combination - high consequence, low difficulty, rarely taught - makes it the highest-return few hours available in Diploma physics, and it is the first thing a specialist will ask about when reading an investigation draft.

The boundary on investigation support is absolute and it protects your child. A tutor may explain each criterion, interrogate the research question, teach the uncertainty chain on the student's own data, explain what a specific limitation looks like, mark practice work, and give written questions and comments on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph to demonstrate register, supply data or edit to completion. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the malpractice consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller.

sections.heading: Practical physics when nobody is in the room
paragraphs: A straight answer is more useful than a reassurance here. A tutor over live video cannot set up a trolley and light gate with your child, and apparatus familiarity belongs in the school laboratory. Anybody claiming otherwise is overselling, and a family should be sceptical of a provider who does not draw the line themselves.

What transfers completely, and is where almost all the marks sit, is the thinking around the apparatus. Deciding what to vary and what to control. Choosing a range wide enough to show a trend. Deciding what to plot so that the relationship linearises and a gradient means something physical. Recording raw data with uncertainties taken from the instrument. Propagating them. Reading an intercept. Writing an evaluation specific to this method rather than to all methods.

On a shared screen, with the student's own data table and graph open, that work is arguably better than across a kitchen table, because both parties are looking at the same numbers and the same line of best fit. For a physics investigation in particular - where the deliverable is a document containing a graph, a gradient and an uncertainty - that is the natural working environment.

Where a student genuinely needs apparatus time, the honest advice is to ask the school for laboratory access rather than to pay anybody for something they cannot provide. Schools run the practical sessions, that is where the equipment is, and a tutor who says so is giving better value than one who quietly takes the booking.

sections.heading: Physics, maths and the engineering destination
paragraphs: A large share of Higher Level physics students are taking it for a destination rather than an interest, and in the eastern suburbs - with Academic City's engineering provision nearby - that destination is frequently engineering. That changes what the two years should optimise for, and it brings a second subject into the decision.

Competitive engineering, physics and mathematics programmes generally expect Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, alongside physics. That is the algebra, calculus and proof route rather than Applications and Interpretation, which is modelling and statistics led. A student who took Applications to protect a grade may find engineering courses closed that nobody mentioned when the choice was made in Year 11 - and the physics grade will not compensate for it.

Requirements are set by each university and change between cycles, so the only source worth acting on is the institution's own published admissions page. Treat grade thresholds as cliffs rather than slopes: a student one grade below a stated requirement may be ineligible rather than disadvantaged, which puts particular weight on the components still open to influence - and reinforces why the investigation, banked months before the papers, should not be left to chance.

On UAE destinations, two cautions. Ministry of Education equivalency is a regulatory process run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, not something any tutoring provider performs, guarantees or accelerates, and tutoring is not required for it. And no IB points threshold for equivalency appears anywhere in the sourced guidance used for this project, so any figure quoted by a tutoring company should be checked on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

sections.heading: What it costs, and whether you need two tutors
paragraphs: Every figure here carries the name of whoever published it. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Named IB specialists run AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table showing 200-450+ and BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently.

Now the question this page's diagnostic raises: does a physics problem that is really a maths problem need two tutors? Usually not, and that is the saving. A physics-literate tutor drilling rearrangement, units and standard form on physics questions does both jobs in one hour, and does them better than a separate maths tutor working on abstract algebra - because the context is the thing the student is struggling to hold. Two parallel weekly subscriptions is the default answer and rarely the right one.

Where two are genuinely justified is a student taking Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Physics at Higher Level, both with real content problems rather than a shared fluency problem. That is an expensive year by any standard - Bestimate's monthly estimates run AED 1,000-2,000 and above per subject for specialist exam-year work - and it deserves a deliberate decision rather than an accumulation of separate ones.

Two honesty notes. Examiner framing often carries the top of this market: current examiner status should be evidenced before it is charged for, and never presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. And no IB Gram price appears on this page, because what a block costs depends on level, component and weeks remaining - the free trial lesson and the consultation after it are where a real figure is given. Household context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Permits, boundaries and claims to refuse
paragraphs: Two free checks and a short list to reject. The permit: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you by anybody.

MoHRE's own service page is "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Because it is free and fast, a working tutor without one has chosen not to have one - which is worth asking about when a tutor has come from a professional or academic background rather than a teaching one.

The second check is the arrangement. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat it as press-reported and verify against current policy, but decline the arrangement where your child's own physics teacher is paid privately.

And the claims to refuse. No individual tutor in Dubai is KHDA-approved, because that status does not exist for individuals - KHDA regulates schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. Nobody holds IB accreditation as a private tutor. Nobody should be described as an IB examiner without evidence of current status, and examiner status must never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. No provider should supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; those get referenced and linked. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and operates no premises in the UAE.

sections.heading: A first month that answers the question it opened with
paragraphs: Four sessions with a shape, and the shape follows the diagnostic. Session one teaches nothing: the marked paper and, if there is one, the investigation feedback are read together, and the lost marks are sorted into arithmetic fluency, content gaps, conceptual reasoning in fields, uncertainty treatment and command-term misreading. Those are five different problems with different teachers and different price tiers, and a plan proposed before any marked work has been read is guesswork.

Sessions two and three attack whichever the diagnosis named, on the student's own next piece of work rather than on a generic exercise. For arithmetic that means drilled rearrangement and unit conversion inside real physics questions, in short bursts rather than whole lessons. For fields it means building the reasoning from a small number of relationships until it holds on an unfamiliar configuration. For an investigation it means the uncertainty chain applied to the data the student actually collected, with the criteria open alongside.

Session four is a measurement rather than a lesson, and the instrument belongs to the school, not to us. Either the next marked physics paper moved or it did not; either the next investigation criterion band moved or it did not. Those are the only two readings that count, which is a distinction a physics student of all people should recognise - a provider reporting progress only against its own internal tests has calibrated the apparatus against itself, and no university will ever see a number from that scale. Mirdif's schools issue the marks; our job is to change them, not to grade our own work.

Then a decision gets made rather than a subscription continuing. Some students need a second block on the other problem. Some need the investigation block and nothing else this term. Some turn out to have an IGCSE-level algebra gap, which is cheaper work at a lower rate tier - and a tutor who says so is reducing the bill. The free trial lesson means the diagnostic session costs nothing, and it works identically from Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Khawaneej.

sections.heading: When no Higher Level physicist is free
paragraphs: Availability transparency is a gap nobody in this market fills, and for Higher Level physics it is a genuine constraint. Fields and induction teaching combined with investigation marking experience is a narrow population, and in the weeks before the May session the right person may not have a slot at the hour a Mirdif family needs. Several competitors conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking phone number rather than saying anything at all.

What happens here instead is a disclosure and a choice. Where the exact match is unavailable at your preferred time, the options are named: a different hour with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date attached, or an adjacent specialist - a chemistry or mathematics teacher with strong uncertainty and data-analysis experience taking the investigation work, say - who can address the component you need now, with the limits of the match stated so you can judge.

Because delivery is online the specialist may sit outside the UAE, which is stated rather than disguised. Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the eastern-suburb school run, which varies enormously depending on whether your child attends a school inside Mirdif or travels to Festival City, Silicon Oasis or further west. A family paying specialist rates for a narrow subject is entitled to know exactly what they are buying and from where.

The free trial lesson converts it all from a promise into a check. One lesson at no cost, with the marked paper or the investigation draft on screen. Ask the tutor what Higher Level adds to the fields topic, name the investigation criteria back to you, and say where uncertainty costs a band. If the fit is wrong, nothing is owed and no block has been bought.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child is failing physics or failing the maths inside it?
faqs.answer: Read the marked script rather than the report. A maths problem shows as the formula written correctly, the substitution correct, and then a wrong value - or a question abandoned two lines in, or a unit left unconverted, or a standard-form slip in a nuclear calculation. A physics problem shows as a question not attempted at all, an explanation that restates the observation instead of giving a mechanism, or field reasoning in the wrong direction. The distinction matters financially: the arithmetic work belongs in the AED 150-300 band, not the AED 200-450 specialist band.

faqs.question: Would searching Al Mizhar or Al Warqa find more IB physics tutors?
faqs.answer: No, and knowing that saves a fortnight. The IB accounts for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, so Diploma physics teachers are scarce in every neighbourhood including the western school belt. What changes between eastern suburbs is the drive time, which raises in-home quotes and shrinks the pool willing to travel without widening the expertise available. Matching on level and component rather than on postcode is the move that actually changes the answer.

faqs.question: Can an engineer from Silicon Oasis tutor IB physics?
faqs.answer: The physics, certainly; the assessment, often not. The Diploma runs grades 1-7, carries an internally assessed investigation marked against research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, specifies command terms that mark schemes act on, and has Higher Level content that differs from Standard Level in uneven ways. There is also a subtler mismatch: a professional solves problems with preferred tools and often software, while a Diploma student solves them by hand under time with a specified data booklet. Test by asking for the investigation criteria and what Higher Level adds to fields.

faqs.question: Which part of Higher Level physics is genuinely new rather than deeper?
faqs.answer: Fields and electromagnetic induction. Most Higher Level additions are intensifications - more demanding calculations in mechanics, circular motion, waves and nuclear physics - where a student's difficulty is usually mathematical rather than conceptual. Fields is different: relating field strength, potential and energy across gravitational, electric and magnetic cases, and handling induction problems that require several relationships tracked at once, is reasoning with no Standard Level equivalent. It is also the area where a non-specialist helps least, because the difficulty is unfamiliarity rather than volume.

faqs.question: Why does uncertainty treatment matter so much in physics specifically?
faqs.answer: Because it is marked twice. Uncertainty appears on the written papers and again inside the internally assessed investigation, which is worth roughly a fifth of the grade and is marked months before the papers. The chain has distinct links - raw uncertainty from the instrument, conversion to fractional or percentage, propagation that differs between addition and multiplication, propagation through a power, uncertainty on a gradient from steepest and shallowest plausible lines, and a final precision the measurements support. High consequence, low difficulty, and rarely taught explicitly in a crowded timetable.

faqs.question: Can physics practical work be prepared over video?
faqs.answer: The thinking yes, the apparatus no, and the honest division matters. No tutor can set up a trolley and light gate with your child - apparatus familiarity belongs in the school laboratory. What transfers completely is where almost all the marks sit: deciding what to vary and control, choosing a range that shows a trend, deciding what to plot so the relationship linearises, recording raw data with instrument uncertainties, propagating them, reading a gradient and intercept, and writing an evaluation specific to this method. On a shared screen showing the same graph, that is arguably easier than across a table.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a physics tutor to a house in Mirdif?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For a Mirdif, Al Warqa or Al Mizhar family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked paper, the graph being plotted and the investigation data table are visible to both sides, and the annotated work stays with the student. For a scarce subject reached from the eastern suburbs, that is the mechanism rather than a compromise - and it removes the longest drive in the city from the price.

faqs.question: Do we need separate tutors for Physics HL and Maths AA HL?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and that is the saving. Where the physics marks are going on arithmetic, a physics-literate tutor drilling rearrangement, units and standard form inside real physics questions does both jobs in one hour, and does them better than a maths tutor working on abstract algebra - because the context is what the student is struggling to hold. Two tutors are justified where both subjects have genuine content problems rather than a shared fluency problem, and that is an expensive year: Bestimate's monthly estimates run AED 1,000-2,000 and above per subject for specialist exam-year work.

faqs.question: What does an IB physics tutor cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures with their publishers, not ours. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Named IB specialists run AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. In-home visits are quoted AED 180-350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 independently, and from the eastern suburbs that sits near the top because the drive is longest.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level physics for an engineering degree?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and usually alongside Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level rather than Applications and Interpretation - which is the detail that catches families out, because a strong physics grade does not compensate for the wrong maths route. Competitive engineering, physics and mathematics programmes set their own requirements and change them between cycles, so the only source worth acting on is each university's own published admissions page. Treat thresholds as cliffs rather than slopes: one grade below a stated requirement can mean ineligible rather than disadvantaged.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with my child's physics investigation?
faqs.answer: They may explain each criterion and what separates one band from the next, interrogate the research question, teach the uncertainty chain on the student's own data, explain what to plot and why, show what a specific limitation looks like, mark practice work, and give written questions and comments on a draft the student wrote. They may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph to demonstrate register, supply data or edit to completion. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Can a weak investigation be made up for in the written papers?
faqs.answer: No, and that arithmetic should drive the plan. The investigation is internally assessed, worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and completed and marked months before the written session - so the band is banked and travels into the exams with the student. Strong paper performance does not retrieve marks lost there. That is why a short block while the research question is still being chosen is worth more than a larger one spent on a finished draft, and why the uncertainty work should be taught before the data is collected rather than after.

faqs.question: How many physics hours a week can a Diploma student realistically take?
faqs.answer: Usually one protected weekly hour, rising to two during a specific phase such as an investigation block or the weeks after a disappointing mock. More than that competes with five other Diploma subjects, the core, and the practice a tutor sets between lessons, which also has to fit somewhere. A student doing four hours of physics tuition a week is usually a student whose other subjects are about to slip. Buy the phase the diagnosis points at rather than a standing commitment across two years.

faqs.question: Should I pay a premium for a tutor described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence, and never for what the title implies. Premium rates in this market reach AED 650, with BartyED publishing that figure, and examiner framing is frequently what justifies it. Current examiner status should be evidenced before it is charged for, and it must never be presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it is not. Ask what the evidence is and what concretely changes in the lesson. A specialist who has taught and marked physics at your child's level is the thing you actually need.

faqs.question: Why does this page carry no IB exam or results dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified. ibo.org returns an error to automated fetching, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and handing an unverified date to a parent who will plan around it does real harm. UAE candidates sit the May session, which is a pattern rather than a date. Confirm every specific date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates are sourced from the boards and used elsewhere on this site with their framing intact.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-r.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach DP Physics at Standard and Higher Level. Each one works to the themes and command terms of the current subject guide, and each one is scheduled into a slot that survives a Dubai school run rather than one that looks neat on paper.

intro.heading: Why physics tuition in MBR City is a scheduling question first
paragraphs: Mohammed Bin Rashid City is not one neighbourhood. It is a band of districts — District One, Sobha Hartland, Meydan, Nad Al Sheba — stitched together by Al Khail Road and Ras Al Khor Road, with a school inside the boundary in some districts and a twenty-minute drive to one in others. That geography is the whole reason a physics tutor search here behaves differently from the same search in a dense older area. The parent typing it is rarely short of candidates. They are short of a slot in the evening when a specialist is awake, free, and able to teach the Higher Level fields topic rather than general science.

Work the day backwards and the problem is obvious. A secondary school in Sobha Hartland releases students at roughly 15:00 to 15:30. A bus serving the villa plots in District One or the Meydan side adds twenty to forty minutes, longer on a weekday when the Al Khail interchange is slow. Co-curricular commitments — a match, a rehearsal, an MYP service project — push the real arrival home to 16:30 on at least two evenings a week. A physics session booked at 16:00 does not exist in practice. A session at 17:00 or 19:00 does, and it is the one that survives a full term.

Then there is the subject itself. DP Physics is not a subject a generalist can hold. The current guide is organised into five themes, running from space, time and motion through to nuclear and quantum physics, with additional Higher Level content folded inside each theme rather than bolted on at the end. A tutor who is comfortable with mechanics and uncomfortable with fields will carry a student happily through the first year and then stall in exactly the term that matters. A Higher Level student needs someone who can move between an induced-emf question and a radioactive-decay calculation without changing register.

The honest position on delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to houses in Mohammed Bin Rashid City, or anywhere else in the UAE. Visiting tutors are an India-only service. Physics support here is delivered as one-to-one live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard for working and screen sharing for past-paper questions. That is a limit stated plainly, and it is also what makes the subject match possible: the pool a MBR City family draws from is not the set of physics teachers who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of District One.

What follows is built around the clock. Which schools this area actually feeds and when they finish; what time a physics session can realistically start on each weekday; how the DP Physics assessment is weighted so the hours go where the marks are; what the Dubai market charges for the alternatives; and what a tutor may and may not do with a Scientific Investigation under IB academic-honesty rules.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-r.programmesIntro: Physics appears in three different shapes across the IB continuum, and a family in MBR City may be dealing with any of them depending on which district school their child attends. The notes below say what the programme asks of a physics student and what that means for the week.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics sits in Group 4 and is taken at Standard or Higher Level. Both routes share the same five themes and the same Scientific Investigation; Higher Level adds depth inside each theme and a longer, more demanding Paper 2. Students also carry Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS alongside six subjects, which is why a physics session that drifts into coursework triage rarely helps anyone.
programmes.countryNote: In the MBR City catchment, DP Physics is taught at the IB continuum schools on the Sobha Hartland side and at IB schools a short drive out towards Nad Al Sheba and Al Jaddaf. Dubai sat roughly 7% of its private-school pupils on an IB curriculum in 2024-25, so a physics cohort in a single Dubai IB school is often small — twelve to twenty students — and a child who falls behind has few peers at the same point to work with.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Physics is taught inside MYP Sciences rather than as a separate subject until the later years, assessed against four criteria covering knowledge and understanding, inquiry and design, processing and evaluating, and the impact of science. A student arriving in DP1 from MYP5 has usually written more about method than about mechanics, which is a predictable and fixable gap.
programmes.countryNote: The continuum schools inside MBR City run MYP straight into DP, so a Sobha Hartland student may never sit an external examination until DP1 mock season. The first timed physics paper they attempt under exam conditions is frequently their DP1 November internal assessment, and the shock of that is a common reason families in District One start looking for a tutor in Year 12 term one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study. Where a CP student takes DP Physics as one of their Diploma courses, the physics requirement is identical to a full Diploma student's — same themes, same papers, same Scientific Investigation — but the surrounding workload is shaped differently.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered by a minority of Dubai IB schools, so an MBR City family on this route often has fewer local peers and relies more heavily on subject-specialist support outside school. Confirm with the school's IB coordinator which DP courses their CP cohort is permitted to combine before planning a physics programme around it.

programmes.name: A Level Physics, for comparison
programmes.description: Several British-curriculum schools in and around MBR City run A Level Physics instead of DP. The content overlaps heavily — mechanics, waves, fields, nuclear physics — but the assessment model does not. A Level places more weight on externally assessed practical skills; DP places 20% of the grade on a single student-designed investigation.
programmes.countryNote: This matters for MBR City families choosing between a British school in Sobha Hartland and an IB continuum school two minutes away. If your child prefers one long self-directed project to a series of practical examinations, the DP model suits them better. We tutor both routes, but a tutor should know which one your child's school actually enters them for before the first lesson.

dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-r.subjectsIntro: Physics is rarely the only subject in play. Below are the Group 4 and Group 5 courses MBR City families most often pair with physics support, with a note on what each one assesses and where marks reliably leak away.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Five themes: space, time and motion; the particulate nature of matter; wave behaviour; fields; nuclear and quantum physics. Marks are lost less on recall than on unit handling, significant figures, and failing to read the command term. 'Deduce' and 'state' are not the same instruction and are not marked the same way.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The usual partner to HL Physics. Calculus fluency, trigonometric manipulation and vector work underpin half the physics syllabus; a student weak in AA often reads as weak in physics when the actual gap is algebraic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Taken by physics students at some Dubai schools where AA is oversubscribed. The statistics and modelling content helps with data analysis in the Scientific Investigation, but the lighter calculus load leaves gaps in the fields and quantum themes that need closing deliberately.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Shares energetics, bonding and the data-and-measurement strand with physics. Students who sit both often reuse one laboratory habit across two investigations; the criteria reward it in one subject and penalise it in the other.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The third Group 4 option, chosen by physics students aiming at biomedical engineering or medicine. Statistical treatment of data is more central than in physics, and students cross-contaminating the two styles of conclusion lose marks in both.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: A frequent fourth-subject pairing in the MBR City continuum schools. Overlap with physics is thin on content but thick on logic; students who can trace an algorithm usually handle multi-step physics derivations better than their grade suggests.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Group 4 alternative with a design cycle rather than an experiment at its centre. Where a school offers both, a physics-minded student sometimes finds the DT project easier to control and the physics paper harder to time.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Physics students draw heavily on TOK when asked about the limits of a model. The essay and exhibition are assessed separately from physics, but a physics tutor who can explain why a model is useful rather than true makes the TOK essay less abstract.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Physics
subjects.description: A physics EE needs a researchable question with a measurable variable, not an interesting topic. Most failures happen at the question stage, months before any data is collected, and that is where supervision earns its keep.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Counts for Group 3 or Group 4 and appeals to students who want a science without the mathematical load of physics. Worth knowing about if a physics choice is proving to be the wrong fit in DP1 term one, while a change is still permitted.

sections.heading: What the MBR City school day actually leaves you
paragraphs: An IB Physics tutor in Mohammed Bin Rashid City has to fit into a window that is narrower than most families expect. Secondary schools in and around the district release students between 15:00 and 15:45. Add a bus route and the arrival home lands between 15:40 and 16:30 depending on the district. Add one co-curricular commitment and two evenings a week collapse entirely. The usable slot for serious physics work, for most students in this area, is 17:00 to 19:30 on three or four weekdays, plus a weekend morning.

That constraint is worth naming because it changes what good scheduling looks like. A tutor who offers 16:00 to a District One family is offering a slot the student will miss or arrive at exhausted. A tutor who offers 20:00 is offering a slot where retention falls off for a fifteen-year-old who started at 07:00. The sessions that hold for a full term, in our experience across the Dubai corridor, start between 16:45 and 18:30 and run sixty minutes on a school night, ninety at weekends.

There is a second constraint most families only notice in week three. Thursday evening is the weakest slot in the Dubai week, because the weekend starts on Friday and a student who knows it is in no state to work through a fields derivation at 18:00 on Thursday. Monday and Tuesday are the strongest. If you can only hold one weekly session, put it early in the week and keep Saturday morning free for timed paper practice.

sections.heading: How DP Physics is assessed, and where the hours should go
paragraphs: A DP Physics grade is built from two external papers and one internally assessed investigation. Paper 1 splits into a multiple-choice section and a data-analysis section. Paper 2 is short and extended response. The Scientific Investigation is a single student-designed report. Higher Level and Standard Level share this structure; what differs is the depth of content and the length of the papers.

The weightings matter for how a family spends its tuition hours. Paper 2 carries 44% of the grade, which is more than Paper 1 and more than twice the investigation. Yet the investigation is the component families most often buy help for, because it has a deadline and a visible document, while Paper 2 technique has neither. A tutor who lets the whole programme become coursework supervision is spending your money on a fifth of the grade.

Students lose marks on Paper 2 in patterns that are diagnosable rather than mysterious. Command terms are ignored — a question asking the student to 'deduce' is answered as though it asked them to 'state'. Units are dropped in the final line of a multi-step calculation. Significant figures are carried through inconsistently. Graph gradients are read off without checking the axis scale. None of that is a knowledge gap, and all of it is cheaper to fix than a syllabus theme.

Weightings and durations below reflect the current DP Physics guide. The IB revises subject guides on a cycle, and ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm the structure your child is entered for with their school's IB coordinator or the current guide itself before planning around it.

sections.heading: The five themes, and which ones break students
paragraphs: The current guide organises physics into five themes rather than a long list of topics, with Higher Level content sitting inside each theme instead of in an appendix. Theme A covers space, time and motion. Theme B covers the particulate nature of matter. Theme C covers wave behaviour. Theme D covers fields. Theme E covers nuclear and quantum physics.

In the Dubai cohorts we see, the failure points cluster. Theme A goes well, because mechanics is what students arrive from MYP or IGCSE already able to do. Theme C is manageable with practice. Theme D is where a Higher Level student either consolidates or comes apart: gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are taught as three analogous structures, and a student who learns them as three unrelated topics triples their revision load and still misreads the questions. Theme E compounds the problem, because it arrives late in DP2 when revision for everything else is already underway.

This has a practical consequence for an MBR City family deciding when to start. A tutor engaged in DP1 term two can teach fields properly the first time. A tutor engaged in DP2 February is repairing fields while also running Paper 2 technique and finishing an investigation, in the same ten weeks. Both are possible. One is considerably cheaper and less unpleasant for the student.

A useful test before committing to a tutor: ask them to explain, in the trial lesson, why the inverse-square form appears in both gravitation and electrostatics and what that similarity does and does not let a student assume. A physics specialist answers that in two minutes with a diagram. A generalist changes the subject.

Theme B: thermal and gas behaviour, where unit errors concentrate
Theme C: waves and superposition, fixable with timed practice
Theme D: fields, the single largest HL failure point
Theme E: nuclear and quantum, taught late and revised in a hurry

sections.heading: What physics tuition costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure, because that is the number a family actually budgets. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. For a Higher Level physics student in DP2, the top band is the honest one to plan against, because the tutor you need is a subject specialist and specialists are not priced like generalists.

The hourly figures behind those monthly bands are published across the Dubai market, unevenly. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour for budget online tutoring and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist IB or A Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 or more. BartyED, at the premium end, publishes AED 650.

Those are market rates from the providers' own published pages, not IB Gram prices. We do not publish a physics rate card on this page, because the right answer depends on level, session length and how many weeks are left before the examination session. The free trial lesson exists so you can judge the teaching before any of that is discussed. What the table does is let you check whether a quote you have been given sits inside the market or outside it.

One figure worth holding alongside the tuition numbers: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private-school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. School fees are flat. Tuition spending is the variable a family still controls, which is an argument for spending it deliberately rather than early.

sections.heading: Online physics versus a visiting tutor in MBR City
paragraphs: The comparison a parent in District One is really making is between two different things that both get called tutoring. One is a person who drives to the villa. The other is a subject specialist on a video call. On physics specifically, the second wins for reasons that have nothing to do with price.

Physics teaching is drawing. A field diagram, a free-body diagram, a ray path, a graph with its gradient marked — these are the medium of the subject. A shared digital whiteboard records all of it, keeps it after the session, and lets the student scroll back to the derivation they half-followed three weeks ago. A paper notebook on a kitchen table does not. For a subject assessed partly on data analysis, a screen that can hold a spreadsheet, a graph and a past-paper question simultaneously is a working advantage, not a compromise.

The pool argument is the stronger one. A visiting tutor must live within a drivable radius of MBR City and be free at 17:00. That intersection, for Higher Level Physics specifically, is small. Online, the constraint is only the clock. A family in Sobha Hartland can work with a physics specialist who teaches fields and quantum at Higher Level every week, rather than the nearest available science graduate.

To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. We are not quietly arranging them. Visiting tutors are an India-only service, and the figures in the in-home column below are what the Dubai market charges for something we do not sell.

sections.heading: The physics year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session. Working backwards from it is the only way to tell whether a physics plan has enough weeks in it, and it is the exercise almost no tutoring page performs for a parent.

The fixed points are not the examination dates. They are the school's internal deadlines: the investigation draft deadline, the final investigation submission, the DP2 mock window, and the school's own deadline for predicted grades. Those are set by your child's IB coordinator and they differ between Dubai schools by several weeks. Ask for them in writing at the start of DP2 and build the physics plan around them rather than around a generic revision calendar.

IB session and results dates are not published on this page. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a wrong date is worse than no date. Confirm every IB deadline with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates — relevant where a sibling is sitting IGCSE Physics — Cambridge runs June and November series in the UAE, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

The practical shape of a physics year, then, looks like this. DP1 term one is content and laboratory habits. DP1 term two and three is where fields should be taught properly and where the investigation question should be settled. DP2 term one is the investigation and the first full timed papers. DP2 term two is Paper 2 technique and theme E. The final weeks are timed papers and nothing else.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with your child's investigation
paragraphs: The Scientific Investigation is worth 20% of the DP Physics grade and it must be the student's own work. That is not a soft expectation. IB academic-honesty rules make submitting work that is not the student's own a malpractice matter, and the consequence falls on the student, not on whoever helped.

A tutor may do a great deal inside that boundary, and the useful ones do. They can interrogate a research question until it is narrow enough to control. They can teach uncertainty propagation as physics rather than as arithmetic. They can read the student's own draft and say which of the four criteria is underserved. They can explain why an evaluation section that lists limitations without weighing them scores poorly. They can teach the student to graph their own data properly.

A tutor may not write any part of the report, rewrite sentences into their own prose, supply a research question wholesale, process the student's data for them, or produce the evaluation. IB Gram does not offer any of that, and a provider that does is selling your child an expulsion risk. The essay mills in this market are explicit about it — one Dubai-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments outright — and the distinction between them and a tutor is the entire point of asking the question.

The practical version for a parent: if the finished document contains a sentence your child could not have written and cannot explain, the line has been crossed. Ask them to talk you through their own evaluation section. If they can, the help was teaching.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally allowed to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a question MBR City parents ask less often than they should, and it has a clear answer. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18.

MoHRE's own service page for it is titled 'Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee, and states a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source.

Two further points specific to this area. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction — so the arrangement some families reach for, their child's own class teacher privately, is the one to avoid. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute. IB Gram does not hold one and does not describe itself as KHDA approved.

What this means in practice for a physics engagement: ask any individual tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition permit, and verify what you are told. It costs nothing to hold, so there is no good reason not to have one.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects sitting alongside physics
paragraphs: A physics plan that ignores the rest of the timetable will fail on contact with the week. Every private school in Dubai, whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies. KHDA's own mandatory-subjects guidance confirms this and required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisational detail matters because it eats timetable space. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and it is advised that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

For an MBR City family, the consequence is arithmetic. A DP student carrying six subjects plus TOK plus the mandatory UAE subjects has fewer free periods than the timetable suggests, which is why after-school hours are contested and why a physics slot booked at the wrong time gets dropped first. It is also why some students arrive at a physics session having had no break since 07:00 — worth knowing before you book 16:00 and wonder why nothing lands.

One further constraint on content: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. Where a family wants Arabic support alongside physics, it has to be support with the school's own prescribed material, not a parallel course.

sections.heading: Starting physics support from MBR City, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The process is short and the first lesson costs nothing. You tell us the school, the year group, the level — Standard or Higher — and the two or three evening windows that genuinely work after your district's school run. We match a DP Physics specialist to the level and to the slot. The trial lesson runs as a real lesson on a real topic, usually whatever your child is stuck on that week, and you decide afterwards.

The part most providers leave out: sometimes the match is not immediate. Higher Level Physics in a specific evening window is a narrow request, and if no specialist is free in your slot we say so rather than offering a general science tutor and hoping. The options then are a different slot, a short wait, or a weekend session. We would rather tell you that in the first conversation than three weeks into a programme that is not working.

Three things are worth having ready before the first conversation, because they shorten it considerably. The most recent marked physics assessment, with the marks per question still visible. The school's scheme of work for the year, which the science department will usually send on request. And the internal deadline dates for the Scientific Investigation draft and final submission, which differ between Dubai schools by several weeks and which no generic revision plan can account for.

If the match is wrong after the trial, say so and we change the tutor. There is no argument to be had about it; a physics student who does not trust their tutor will not ask the question they are embarrassed about, and that question is usually the one holding the grade down. The point of the trial is to find that out before money changes hands.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB Physics tutor in Mohammed Bin Rashid City who fits around the school run?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the slot matters more than most families expect. Secondary schools serving MBR City finish between 15:00 and 15:45, and a bus from District One or Meydan adds twenty to forty minutes. A session starting at 16:45 or 17:00 is realistic on a school night; one at 16:00 generally is not unless your child walks home from Sobha Hartland. Lessons are one-to-one live video scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so there is no travel at either end. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; visiting tutors are an India-only service.

faqs.question: Which schools near MBR City does an IB Physics tutor usually work with?
faqs.answer: The district itself contains British and IB continuum provision on the Sobha Hartland side, with further IB and British schools a short drive out through Nad Al Sheba and across Ras Al Khor into Al Jaddaf. Students we support attend schools including Hartland International School, North London Collegiate School Dubai, Kent College Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. These are named as local context only; no affiliation is implied. The first thing a tutor should confirm is whether your child sits DP Physics or A Level Physics, because the assessment models differ substantially.

faqs.question: What time of day do physics sessions actually work for a District One family?
faqs.answer: Between 16:45 and 18:30 on three or four weekdays, plus a weekend morning if you want ninety-minute Paper 2 practice. District One has no secondary school inside the plot boundary, so students travel out and back, and the arrival home lands around 16:15 to 16:30 on a bus day. Add a co-curricular commitment and two evenings disappear entirely. Sessions that start after 20:00 tend to lose retention for a fifteen or sixteen-year-old who began the day at 07:00, which is why we recommend fewer, better-placed sessions over more frequent ones.

faqs.question: How is DP Physics weighted between the papers and the investigation?
faqs.answer: Paper 1, which combines multiple choice with a data-analysis section, carries 36% of the grade. Paper 2, short and extended response, carries 44%. The internally assessed Scientific Investigation carries 20%. Those proportions hold at both Standard and Higher Level; what changes is content depth and paper duration, with HL papers running longer. Because Paper 2 is the largest single component, a tuition programme that becomes coursework supervision is spending most of your money on a fifth of the grade. Confirm the current structure with your child's IB coordinator, since the IB revises subject guides on a cycle.

faqs.question: Why do so many Higher Level physics students struggle with fields?
faqs.answer: Because gravitational, electric and magnetic fields are taught as three analogous structures, and a student who learns them as three unrelated topics triples the revision load while still misreading the questions. Theme D also arrives when the DP2 workload is already heavy, so there is little slack to fix it. The diagnostic question is whether a student can say why an inverse-square relationship appears in both gravitation and electrostatics, and what that similarity does not let them assume. A physics specialist answers that with a diagram in two minutes. It is a reasonable thing to ask in a trial lesson.

faqs.question: What does a specialist IB Physics tutor cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates for an IB or A Level subject specialist in Dubai run roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table showing AED 200 to 450 or more. Qualified online subject tutors sit lower, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Budget online options start much lower, from AED 33 to 65 at EdFlik and Tutopiya, but rarely cover Higher Level Paper 2 technique. Those are the providers' own published figures, not IB Gram prices. We quote after a free trial, because the right answer depends on level and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Is online physics tuition really as good as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For physics specifically, the screen is an advantage rather than a compromise. The subject is taught through diagrams, graphs and derivations, and a shared digital whiteboard keeps all of it after the session so a student can scroll back to a derivation they half-followed weeks earlier. A spreadsheet, a graph and a past-paper question can sit open together, which matters for a component assessed on data analysis. The stronger argument is the tutor pool: online, your child works with a Higher Level physics specialist rather than the nearest available science graduate free at 17:00.

faqs.question: Can your tutors help with the IB Physics Scientific Investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can stress-test the research question until it has one controllable variable, teach uncertainty and error propagation properly, and give feedback on your child's own draft against the four assessment criteria, each worth six marks. What a tutor must never do is write, rewrite or edit any part of the report, supply the research question, or process the data. The work must be the student's own under IB academic-honesty rules, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student. If the finished report contains a sentence your child cannot explain, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: My child has six weeks until the physics exam. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the plan has to change shape. Six weeks is not enough to teach theme D from scratch and also fix Paper 2 timing, so the first session should be diagnostic: a marked mock paper, read for patterns rather than scores. In most cases the quickest gains are technical rather than topical — command terms, units carried through the final line, consistent significant figures, reading a gradient off a scaled axis. Those are worth marks across every theme. Content gaps get triaged by weighting, with Paper 2 topics prioritised because that paper carries 44%.

faqs.question: Do private physics tutors in Dubai need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted online with suspicion. Ask a tutor to show you their permit.

faqs.question: Is it a problem if the physics tutor also teaches at my child's school?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the regulatory position, it puts your child's class teacher in the position of marking work they were paid to prepare. A separate specialist with no stake in the internal grade is a cleaner arrangement and usually a more candid one about where the student actually is.

faqs.question: How many physics sessions a week does a DP2 student in MBR City usually need?
faqs.answer: One well-placed weekly session through DP1 and most of DP2, rising to two or three a week in the final revision block. The reason is that physics gains come from repeated contact with examiner-style questions rather than from volume. A single ninety-minute weekend session often outperforms two rushed weekday hours for a student whose school day ends at 15:30 and who gets home at 16:30. Families who start in DP1 term two consistently need fewer total hours than families who start in DP2 February, because fields can be taught properly the first time rather than repaired under deadline.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai school calendar change when physics revision should happen?
faqs.answer: It does, in two ways. The mandatory UAE subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies — occupy timetable space in every Dubai private school whatever curriculum it is licensed for, so a DP student has fewer free periods than the published timetable suggests. And where the pre-examination revision block overlaps Ramadan, session timing usually has to move, commonly to a post-Iftar slot. We schedule around both. The fixed points to plan from are your school's own internal deadlines for the investigation, the mocks and predicted grades, which differ between Dubai schools by several weeks.

faqs.question: Are IB exam dates and results dates published on this page?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and a date a parent acts on has to be right. UAE IB schools sit the May session; confirm the exact window, the upload deadlines and the results date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For a sibling sitting IGCSE Physics, the position is clearer: Cambridge International runs June and November series in the UAE, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Will a physics tutor follow my child's school scheme of work or their own?
faqs.answer: Your child's. The topic order in a Dubai IB school is set by its own science department and the sequence varies between schools, so a tutor working to a generic plan will teach fields in February when the class covered it in October. We ask for the school's scheme of work, the internal deadline dates and the most recent marked assessment at the start, then set the session sequence against those. Where a student is clearly behind the class rather than ahead of it, catching up on the taught sequence takes priority over revision of material not yet reached.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level physics specialist is free in our window?
faqs.answer: We tell you. Higher Level Physics in one specific evening slot is a narrow request, and if nobody suitable is available we would rather say so than offer a general science tutor and let you discover the gap in week four. The realistic options at that point are a different weekday, a weekend morning, or a short wait for a slot to open. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is why it is worth asking directly before you commit, of us or of anybody else.

intro.heading: Four comparisons that decide how physics goes
paragraphs: Physics is the Diploma subject most often chosen for the wrong reason and abandoned for the right one. Students take it because it sounds like the serious science, or because an engineering degree was mentioned once, and then discover in DP1 that the limiting factor is not their grasp of mechanics but their algebra. Families in Motor City usually arrive at this page having already made one of four comparisons badly, and the page is organised around putting them right before any hours are bought.

The first comparison is IB Physics against A Level Physics, which is a live choice here because GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs a British curriculum to IGCSE and then a sixth form, while the Diploma schools sit across the Dubailand corridor. The two qualifications assess differently: the IB spreads assessment across a 36% paper of multiple choice and data analysis, a 44% extended-response paper and a 20% internally assessed investigation, while A Level concentrates it in terminal papers with a separate practical endorsement. Neither is harder in the abstract; they reward different students, and a family that knows which kind of student they have can make the choice in an afternoon rather than regretting it in DP2.

The second is physics against the other sciences, which should be decided by degree requirement rather than by preference. Engineering and physics routes generally want Physics with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. Medicine, dentistry and pharmacy generally want Chemistry and often Biology, with physics optional. A student who takes Physics HL for a medical application and Biology SL has frequently got that the wrong way round, and no amount of tutoring afterwards recovers a subject that was not taken at the level the course wanted.

The third is Higher against Standard Level, which is a time-budget question rather than an intelligence test. Higher Level carries additional content and deeper application in the same components, and a student taking three Higher Level sciences has three internally assessed investigations with overlapping school deadlines plus the Extended Essay and the TOK essay in the same period. That is a scheduling load rather than an intellectual one, and it is invisible on a timetable until DP2.

The fourth, and the one almost nobody makes deliberately, is the mathematics course underneath. IB Physics assumes a specific set of mathematical techniques, and the two mathematics courses supply them differently. A student on Applications and Interpretation taking Physics HL will meet mathematical demands their mathematics course does not drill, and that is a predictable, fixable and usually unanticipated problem. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, sessions run 45 or 60 minutes to 21:00, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.
