dubai/ib-physics-tutor-in-motor-city.subjectsIntro: The physics topics and components most requested from the Motor City area, with the mathematical technique each one leans on. The mathematics column is the part most revision plans omit.

subjects.name: Mechanics and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, Newton's laws, momentum and energy. Leans on simultaneous equations, quadratics for projectile timing and vector resolution. Sign conventions cause more loss than the physics, particularly in momentum problems involving a reversal of direction.

subjects.name: Circular motion and gravitation
subjects.description: Angular quantities, centripetal force, gravitational fields and potential. Leans on algebraic rearrangement of inverse-square relationships and on comfort with ratios. Confusing field strength with potential, and treating potential as a vector, are the standing errors.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance in combination, internal resistance and power. Leans on simultaneous equations and on reciprocal arithmetic for parallel resistance. Students reproduce rules without applying them to the specific network in the question.

subjects.name: Fields and electromagnetism
subjects.description: Electric and magnetic fields, induction and alternating current. Leans on trigonometry for flux through an angled area and on gradient interpretation. Direction conventions and the sign of an induced effect are where marks are routinely conceded.

subjects.name: Waves and oscillations
subjects.description: Simple harmonic motion, superposition, interference, diffraction and standing waves. Leans heavily on trigonometric functions, radians and phase relationships — the clearest example of a topic where a weak mathematics course shows up as a physics problem.

subjects.name: Thermal physics
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, the gas laws and the kinetic model. Leans on proportional reasoning and unit conversion between degrees Celsius and kelvin. Heating-curve questions where a specific heat capacity is applied across a phase change are the recurring error.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactive decay, binding energy, mass defect and the photoelectric effect. Leans on exponentials and logarithms for decay, and on careful unit handling between electronvolts and joules, which is a high-frequency source of avoidable loss.

subjects.name: Paper 1B, data analysis
subjects.description: Gradients, intercepts, error bars, uncertainty propagation and linearising a relationship to test it. Leans on straight-line algebra and on rearranging a proposed law into linear form — a closed technique set that four focused sessions normally covers.

subjects.name: Paper 2, extended response
subjects.description: Forty-four per cent of the grade. Leans less on mathematics and more on structure: name the principle, apply it to the situation, then evaluate where asked. Students who describe what happens rather than naming the law have written correct physics and scored low.

subjects.name: The scientific investigation
subjects.description: Internally assessed, 20% of the grade, 24 marks across four criteria at six marks each. Leans on uncertainty propagation and graphical analysis. Weak evaluations cost more than weak data, because the criterion wants methodological limits and specific realistic improvements.

sections.heading: IB Physics or A Level Physics?
paragraphs: For a Motor City family this is a real choice rather than an academic one, because GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs the British curriculum through to sixth form while the Diploma schools sit across the corridor. Staying put means A Level; moving means the Diploma. The decision is usually made on school preference and then the subject consequences are discovered afterwards, which is the wrong order.

The assessment models differ in a way that suits different students. IB Physics spreads the grade across a 36% paper of multiple choice and data analysis, a 44% extended-response paper, and a 20% internally assessed investigation marked in school and moderated externally. That 20% is coursework in effect: planned, executed and written over weeks, with a school deadline. A Level Physics concentrates assessment in terminal written papers with a separate practical endorsement that is reported rather than graded into the subject result.

So a student who performs well on sustained work with a deadline and less well in a three-hour hall gains from the IB structure. A student who revises hard, performs under pressure and finds extended coursework a grind gains from A Level. That is a more useful basis for the decision than any general claim about which qualification is more rigorous.

The breadth difference matters too. A Level Physics is one of three or four subjects, so depth per subject is greater and the timetable is narrower. IB Physics is one of six subjects plus the core, which means less time per subject and the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service competing for the same evenings. A student who wants to specialise early is poorly served by six subjects; a student whose university list is unsettled is well served by them.

sections.heading: What physics assumes from your child's mathematics course
paragraphs: This is the comparison nobody makes deliberately and the one that causes the most avoidable difficulty. IB Physics assumes a set of mathematical techniques, and the two Diploma mathematics courses supply them to different depths. Analysis and Approaches builds algebraic manipulation, trigonometric functions and calculus. Applications and Interpretation builds modelling, statistics and interpretation, with less drilled algebra and lighter trigonometric work.

The result is predictable. A student taking Physics Higher Level alongside Applications and Interpretation will meet waves and oscillations questions needing fluent trigonometric manipulation in radians, decay problems needing exponentials and logarithms, field problems needing confident rearrangement of inverse-square relationships, and mechanics needing vector resolution — and their mathematics course will not have drilled several of those. The physics is not the obstacle; the technique underneath it is.

This is entirely fixable and it is cheapest to fix in DP1. Six to eight sessions teaching the specific techniques inside physics problems rather than as abstract mathematics closes most of it, and teaching them in context matters because transfer from a mathematics lesson to a physics question is exactly what does not happen reliably. A student who can solve simultaneous equations in a mathematics class and cannot apply them to a two-loop circuit has a transfer problem, not a knowledge one.

The practical advice for a family choosing subjects is simply to make the pairing deliberately. If physics is the priority and the degree list includes engineering or physics, Analysis and Approaches is the natural partner and several degree routes specify it anyway. If Applications and Interpretation is the right mathematics course for other reasons, take it — and budget for the technique gap in DP1 rather than discovering it in DP2.

sections.heading: Physics against the other sciences, by destination
paragraphs: Subject choice should be read backwards from the degree, and physics is the science where that discipline is most often skipped. Students take Physics Higher Level because it signals seriousness, and then apply to courses that never asked for it while omitting something that did. The table below gives the usual pattern as a starting point for reading each university's own admissions page, which is the only reliable source and a thirty-minute job for a shortlist of six.

The broad shape is this. Engineering of most kinds wants Physics with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, often both at Higher Level, and chemical or materials engineering adds Chemistry. Physics and astrophysics degrees want Physics and Mathematics at Higher Level. Computer science usually wants Mathematics and treats Physics as optional. Architecture varies widely and is worth checking individually. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary medicine want Chemistry, usually at Higher Level, often with Biology, and treat Physics as optional or irrelevant.

The practical consequence for a Motor City family is a sequencing instruction rather than a recommendation. Build the shortlist of likely degree routes first, even loosely. Read the admissions requirements for each. Then choose the three Higher Level subjects to satisfy the union of those requirements, and only then think about preference. A student with an unsettled list should favour the combination that keeps the most routes open, which is usually Mathematics Analysis and Approaches plus two sciences at Higher Level.

One caution that belongs here. No amount of tutoring is a requirement for admission to anything, and any provider implying that a degree route depends on buying lessons is manufacturing urgency. Equally, tutoring cannot substitute for a subject that was not taken, which is why the subject-choice conversation is worth more than any number of sessions afterwards.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level Physics
paragraphs: Higher Level Physics is more content and deeper application within the same components rather than a different style of paper. The additional material raises the volume substantially and the expectation of depth raises it again, which makes the decision a question of available hours rather than of ability. A student capable of a 6 at Standard Level is usually capable of the Higher Level material given the time; the question is whether the time exists alongside five other subjects and the core.

The load that families underestimate is the internally assessed one. Every Group 4 subject carries a scientific investigation worth 20% of its grade, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. A student taking three Higher Level sciences carries three of those, and schools tend to set their deadlines in overlapping windows during DP2, with the Extended Essay and the TOK essay in the same period. That is a real timetable problem that does not appear on a timetable.

The decision should therefore be anchored to the degree requirement. Where a target route requires Physics at Higher Level, as most engineering and physics degrees do, the decision is made. Where it does not, Standard Level Physics with a stronger overall point total is frequently the better outcome, and a 7 at Standard Level reads better on an application than a 4 at Higher Level.

If a mismatch has already happened, raise it early. A move from Higher to Standard Level is generally possible in the first term of DP1 and progressively harder afterwards, and the school decides. What helps is marked evidence across the Higher Level-only material, because that is what the school is judging. A few sessions of real Higher Level questions, marked honestly, give the Diploma coordinator something concrete to work from rather than a parental impression.

sections.heading: The investigation, compared with an A Level practical endorsement
paragraphs: This is the clearest single difference between the two routes and the one that most often decides which suits a student. The IB scientific investigation is worth 20% of the physics grade, marked out of 24 across four criteria at six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is planned, executed and written by the student over weeks, submitted to a school deadline, marked in school and moderated externally. It is, in effect, graded coursework.

An A Level practical endorsement works differently: practical competence is assessed and reported, but it does not carry a percentage of the subject grade in the same way. The written papers carry the grade. For a student who finds extended independent work difficult, that difference is worth real points; for a student who works steadily and writes well, the IB structure hands them a fifth of the grade on terms they can control.

Within the IB investigation, the symmetry of the four criteria is what students miss. Excellent data with a thin evaluation discards a quarter of the component, and evaluation is routinely written as a closing paragraph rather than as six marks of assessed work. It credits specific methodological limitations and realistic targeted improvements: an instrument resolution limit propagated into a percentage uncertainty scores, while human error and a shortage of time score nothing.

The honesty line is strict and this market does not always respect it. At least one site ranking for UAE IB searches sells completed Internal Assessments; submitting purchased work is academic misconduct under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. A tutor may interrogate the research question, check the method's feasibility against the apparatus actually available, teach uncertainty propagation, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, and read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion a passage fails. A tutor may not design the investigation, process the data, write or rewrite any part of the report, or edit prose to a standard the student could not produce.

sections.heading: Costing physics and mathematics together
paragraphs: Because physics problems are so often mathematics problems, the sensible unit of cost for a family in this position is the pairing rather than the subject. A student on Physics Higher Level with Applications and Interpretation frequently needs a technique block in DP1 and then physics support in DP2, and planning for both from the start is cheaper than discovering the second halfway through.

The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IB and IGCSE specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240-600, AED 600-1,200 and AED 1,000-2,000 or above across the tiers.

The pairing can often be covered by one tutor, which is worth asking about directly. A specialist who teaches both Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches can diagnose a physics script and treat the technique gap in the same session, which is more efficient than two separate relationships and removes the transfer problem entirely. Where one tutor cannot cover both to a high standard, splitting is still the better outcome, but it costs a second slot in an already congested evening.

IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate on this page, because level, component and urgency move it, and a quote follows the free diagnostic lesson rather than preceding it. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat; the tutoring decision is the variable one.

sections.heading: Scheduling physics from Motor City
paragraphs: Diploma Physics students from Motor City commute out of the community, because GEMS Metropole School runs the British curriculum through IGCSE and into sixth form while the IB schools sit across the Dubailand corridor. Students are generally home between 16:30 and 17:30, which makes about 18:00 the earliest realistic session start and puts the busiest physics bookings at 18:00 and 19:00.

That matters for physics specifically because of the two session shapes the subject needs. A technique or data-analysis session works well at 45 minutes and benefits from frequency. A past-paper session with extended-response marking wants a full hour. Online, those two can sit on different evenings in the same week; with a visiting tutor they have to be combined into one long appointment, because forty to sixty minutes of travel each way requires a two-hour minimum booking and caps the latest workable start at roughly 18:30.

There is also a format advantage particular to physics, which is the shared whiteboard. Uncertainty propagation, free-body diagrams, circuit redrawing and graph work all have to be seen to be corrected, and a surface both parties can write on produces a record of the working that the student keeps. Every session is recorded, which matters most for the technique sessions a student will want to watch again during revision.

Home visits are nonetheless the right purchase for some students, and the honest cases are a younger student who needs an adult present or one whose written method needs correcting as it is produced. IB Gram does not offer them anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — and we have no UAE office, centre or branch. The comparison here is informational rather than persuasive.

sections.heading: Starting, and the footnotes that belong on every page here
paragraphs: Send the level, the mathematics course the student is taking alongside, a marked physics paper and the school's investigation dates. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day separating the physics problem from the mathematics problem, with a session estimate against each. Nothing is charged before you read it, and where the honest answer is that the Higher Level target is not reachable in the time left, the note says so and proposes what is.

Availability for IB Physics is good at both levels for UAE evening slots, with a match normally inside one to three working days. A tutor who covers both Physics and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches to a high standard is a narrower pool but routinely available, and worth asking for where the diagnosis points at the technique gap. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

On dates, briefly. UAE candidates sit the May session. This page publishes no IB examination or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself; a family reorganises a term around an examination date, so your Diploma coordinator is the right source. For students on the British route first, Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series with the February/March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November — the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The claim this page refuses first is the one a physics parent hears most often. We do not describe any tutor as a current IB examiner, because that status cannot be evidenced from Motor City or anywhere else, and a page comparing Diploma physics with A Level physics would be the obvious place to smuggle it in. The remaining refusals follow from the same rule: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, is not an examination centre, and has no UAE office. On the tutor's own side there is a licence that does exist and can be shown to you: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Say which mathematics course goes with it
process.description: Physics Higher Level with Applications and Interpretation is a different proposition from Physics Higher Level with Analysis and Approaches, and the diagnosis depends on knowing which. It is the single most useful piece of information in a first message about physics and the one most often omitted.

process.title: Read the degree list before the subject list
process.description: Build even a loose shortlist of likely degree routes and read each university's own admissions requirements. Most engineering and physics routes want Physics with Analysis and Approaches, often both at Higher Level; medicine generally wants Chemistry instead. Thirty minutes of reading settles a two-year commitment.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent on the student's own marked physics work, specifically to separate the physics problem from the mathematics underneath it. A student who can state Newton's second law and cannot resolve a vector has a technique gap, and that is a different purchase.

process.title: Put the technique block in DP1
process.description: Six to eight sessions teaching the specific mathematical techniques inside physics problems — vector resolution, simultaneous equations, radians, exponentials, inverse-square rearrangement. Taught in context, because transfer from a mathematics lesson to a physics question is exactly what does not happen reliably.

process.title: Review on the school's own marks
process.description: Progress is judged on the next internal assessment or mock, read against the original diagnosis. If the physics score has not moved but the technique work has landed, the next block is content; if neither has moved, the between-session work is the thing to examine first.

whyPoints.title: The mathematics pairing diagnosed first
whyPoints.description: Physics problems are frequently technique problems: vector resolution, radians, exponentials, inverse-square rearrangement. We read the physics script to find out which, because teaching more physics to a student with a technique gap is the commonest waste in this subject.

whyPoints.title: Both routes compared honestly
whyPoints.description: IB Physics spreads the grade across two papers and a graded 20% investigation; A Level concentrates it in terminal papers with a reported practical endorsement. We set out which student each suits rather than claiming one qualification is more rigorous.

whyPoints.title: Degree requirements described, then verified
whyPoints.description: Engineering and physics routes generally want Physics with Analysis and Approaches; medicine generally wants Chemistry. We give the usual pattern and then tell you to read each university's own admissions page, because requirements differ and change.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level framed as a time budget
whyPoints.description: Higher Level is more content and deeper application, not harder questions on the same content. The real constraint is three internally assessed investigations with overlapping deadlines plus the Extended Essay and the TOK essay in the same period.

whyPoints.title: The investigation treated as 20%
whyPoints.description: Twenty-four marks across four criteria at six each, with evaluation carrying as much as data analysis. We check the method's feasibility against the apparatus actually available before data is collected, which is the one hour that cannot be bought back later.

whyPoints.title: One tutor for both subjects where possible
whyPoints.description: A specialist who teaches Physics and Analysis and Approaches can diagnose a physics script and treat the technique gap in the same session, which removes the transfer problem and saves a slot in an already congested Motor City evening.

faqs.question: Should my child take IB Physics or A Level Physics?
faqs.answer: It depends on how they perform rather than on which qualification is harder. IB Physics spreads the grade across a 36% paper of multiple choice and data analysis, a 44% extended-response paper and a 20% internally assessed investigation planned and written over weeks to a school deadline. A Level concentrates the grade in terminal written papers with a separate practical endorsement reported rather than graded in. A student who works steadily to deadlines gains from the IB structure; a student who revises hard and performs under pressure gains from A Level.

faqs.question: Can my child take Physics HL with Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth doing with open eyes. Physics assumes a set of mathematical techniques that Analysis and Approaches drills more heavily: trigonometric functions in radians for waves and oscillations, exponentials and logarithms for decay, vector resolution for mechanics and fields, and confident rearrangement of inverse-square relationships. Applications and Interpretation covers less of that ground at the same depth, while being stronger on statistical treatment of data, which helps the investigation. Budget six to eight technique sessions in DP1 rather than discovering the gap in DP2.

faqs.question: Why is my child good at maths but losing marks in physics?
faqs.answer: Usually a transfer problem rather than a knowledge problem. A student who can solve simultaneous equations in a mathematics lesson and cannot apply them to a two-loop circuit has both pieces and no bridge between them. The same pattern shows up with trigonometry in flux questions and with exponentials in decay problems. The fix is to teach the technique inside physics contexts rather than abstractly, which is why the technique block is diagnosed from physics scripts and not from mathematics ones.

faqs.question: Does an engineering degree need Physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Most engineering routes want Physics, commonly at Higher Level, with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches alongside and often also at Higher Level. Chemical and materials engineering add Chemistry. Physics and astrophysics degrees want Physics and Mathematics at Higher Level. But requirements differ by country and institution and they change, so the only reliable step is reading each university's own admissions page for the year of entry. For a shortlist of six that is about thirty minutes of work and it settles a two-year commitment.

faqs.question: Is Physics worth taking for a medical application?
faqs.answer: Usually not as a priority. Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary medicine generally require Chemistry, often at Higher Level, frequently with Biology, and treat Physics as optional or irrelevant. A student who takes Physics Higher Level and Biology Standard Level for a medical application has often got the levels the wrong way round. Check each institution's own requirements, because this is the pattern rather than a rule, and a small number of programmes do name a second science without specifying which.

faqs.question: How much more work is Physics HL than SL?
faqs.answer: Substantially more content and a deeper expectation of application within the same three components, rather than harder papers on the same material. The load families underestimate is the internally assessed one: every Group 4 subject carries an investigation worth 20% of its grade, so three Higher Level sciences means three of them, usually with overlapping school deadlines during DP2 and the Extended Essay and TOK essay in the same period. That is a timetable problem that does not appear on a timetable.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Physics HL to SL partway through?
faqs.answer: Often in the first term of DP1, and progressively harder after that, with the school deciding rather than the family. What helps the conversation is marked evidence on the Higher Level-only material specifically, because that is what the school is judging. A few sessions of real Higher Level questions, marked honestly, give the Diploma coordinator something concrete. Where the move is not possible, a revised target grade with the hours redirected to another subject is usually a better plan than more hours at the same level.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the IB investigation and an A Level practical?
faqs.answer: The IB scientific investigation is worth 20% of the physics grade and is marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation at six marks each. It is planned, executed and written by the student over weeks, submitted to a school deadline, marked in school and moderated externally — graded coursework in effect. An A Level practical endorsement assesses and reports practical competence without carrying a percentage of the subject grade in the same way; the written papers carry the grade.

faqs.question: Where do the investigation marks actually go missing in physics?
faqs.answer: Evaluation most often, because students write it as a closing paragraph rather than as six marks of assessed work. It credits specific methodological limitations and realistic targeted improvements, so an instrument resolution limit propagated into a percentage uncertainty scores while human error and a shortage of time score nothing. Research design is the second: a question whose variables cannot be controlled to the precision the analysis needs, or whose apparatus the school does not have, produces data that cannot support a conclusion however well written.

faqs.question: Is the Paper 1B data analysis section worth a separate block?
faqs.answer: For a student with secure content and a weak Paper 1B, it is the highest-yield short block in the subject. The whole component is a closed technique set: gradients and intercepts, absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, propagation through products and powers, error bars, maximum and minimum gradient lines, and linearising a relationship to test it. Four focused sessions normally covers all of it, and the same work feeds directly into the investigation's data analysis criterion, so it pays twice.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and IB Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Many can cover Physics with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches to a high standard, and where that is the case it is worth asking for. A single tutor can diagnose a physics script, identify the technique gap underneath it and treat both in the same session, which removes the transfer problem entirely and saves a slot in an already congested Motor City evening. Where one tutor cannot cover both properly, splitting is still better than compromising on either, but it costs a second appointment.

faqs.answer: About 18:00 for Diploma students, because GEMS Metropole School inside the community runs the British curriculum through IGCSE and into sixth form, so IB students commute out across the Dubailand corridor and are generally home between 16:30 and 17:30. Online sessions run to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time, which allows a 45-minute technique session and a full-hour paper session on different evenings in the same week. A visiting tutor's two-hour minimum and roughly 18:30 latest start forces those into one long appointment.

faqs.question: Does a physics tutor visit homes in Motor City?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do, at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE. For physics there is also a format point worth making: free-body diagrams, circuit redrawing, graph work and uncertainty propagation all have to be seen to be corrected, and a shared whiteboard both parties write on produces a record of the working that the student keeps and can rewatch.
